sections.heading: What the UAE market charges for resit hours, with the publisher named
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. The figures below were read in October 2026 from each provider's own published page, plus Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They are the market, not an IB Gram price list. We do not publish an hourly rate on this page because the honest answer depends on the subject, the component and the window, and a number invented to fill a table is worse than no number.

Read the bands as a description of supply rather than of quality. The budget tier is occupied largely by university students and recent school leavers, a group the UAE private tuition work permit explicitly covers: the permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years and its eligible applicants include unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. A lawful AED 60 hour is therefore entirely possible. What it is unlikely to include is a reading of your child's component marks, a plan written against the board's assessment objectives, or experience of the specific variant sat.

At the other end, a premium named figure such as the AED 650 an hour BartyED publishes buys scarcity, and on a resit scarcity sometimes is the product: a thin-supply subject like Computer Science 0478 inside a six-week window is a genuinely hard booking. The band that most resits actually settle in is the qualified-to-specialist range of roughly AED 150 to 450, and the decision inside that range should be made on whether the person can name where the marks went, not on where they sit in the table.

sections.heading: Cost per grade: the arithmetic that decides whether to resit at all
paragraphs: A resit is worth buying when the grade change it produces is worth more than the total of the four bills. That sounds obvious and it is almost never written down. Write it down. Name the grade you need and why you need it, because the answer is usually one of four things: a sixth-form or college entry requirement, a conditional university offer, a Ministry of Education equivalency count that is one subject short, or a subject the student intends to continue at A-Level and cannot currently cope with. Each of those has a different tolerance for a near miss, and some of them do not need the resit at all.

Then size the hours against the component rather than the subject. A single weak component inside an otherwise sound performance is the cheapest thing in this whole market to fix, because the content is already there and what is missing is a technique. A syllabus that was never properly taught is the most expensive, because you are buying a year of teaching in a term and the honest number of hours is large enough that repeating the year starts to compete on price. The planning figures in the table below are planning figures: they are how we size a block, not a measured outcome, and no tutor can promise a grade.

Finally, put a stop condition on the spend before it starts. Agree at the midpoint review what evidence would say the plan is working, usually a marked paper on the target component showing a specific movement in marks. If the evidence is not there, the right decision is to change the plan or stop, not to add hours. Families who skip this step tend to discover in the last fortnight that they have bought twenty hours and still have the original problem, which is the single most common way resit money is wasted in this market.

sections.heading: Repeating Year 11 against resitting the subject
paragraphs: This is the comparison UAE families actually make, and it is almost never laid out with the numbers facing each other. Repeating a year means a full year of published school fees, and in Dubai that figure is unusually knowable right now: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. So the comparison is a known annual fee at a frozen rate against an entry fee plus a block of hours.

On price the resit wins overwhelmingly in almost every case, which is why the decision should turn on what each route actually fixes. A resit fixes a grade. A repeated year fixes an education, and sometimes that is the thing that is broken: a student who arrived mid-year from another curriculum, who missed a long stretch through illness, or who was placed in a tier that never suited them may need the teaching rather than the second entry. A repeated year also costs twelve months of a young person's life, and that cost does not appear on any fee schedule.

There is a third route families forget to price, which is accepting the grade and making the case. A sixth form, a college or a university admissions office may take a lower grade in one subject alongside strong results elsewhere, particularly where the subject is not a prerequisite for the intended course. Asking the admissions office before buying anything costs one email. It is, measured against every other row in the table below, the cheapest option on this page, and the one nobody in this market has any commercial reason to recommend to you.

sections.heading: The resit calendar, counted forward from the day the result landed
paragraphs: Nobody in this search cluster publishes a date. The word November returned no hits on every competitor page we could fetch, which means a UAE parent researching a resit online is given rate cards and no calendar. The calendar is the part that decides whether a plan is possible at all, because every meaningful deadline on a resit sits months before the paper and the entry closes while the family is still deciding whether to resit.

The published anchors are worth memorising. Pearson's International GCSE runs in a May/June series and a November series; its November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Its June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. That last date is the single most useful fact on this page for a family weighing a November entry, because it tells you precisely when a November resit grade becomes a document you can send to anybody.

Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and for a resit that pairing is the whole decision. June is the main sitting with results in August; November is the fast resit route, sat in October and November with results in January. The February/March series that appears on some tutoring sites is offered to India only and is not available to a UAE candidate, so a plan built on it collapses at the entry stage. Pearson gives the same choice with dates you can hold: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, the November 2026 timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Confirm every date against the board's live timetable, since Pearson publishes provisional timetables that are later revised.

sections.heading: Sitting the resit as a private candidate when the school says no
paragraphs: A school is under no obligation to re-enter a former pupil, and plenty do not. That is the moment many UAE families discover the private candidate route exists, usually with less time left than they would like. A private candidate entry is made through an examination centre that accepts candidates it does not teach. The centre sets and publishes its own fee, makes the entry with the board, hosts the papers and issues the statement of results. Nothing about it is unusual; it is simply administered by somebody other than a school.

The question that catches families out is components. A syllabus is not only written papers. There may be an alternative-to-practical component, a coursework component, or a speaking endorsement, and not every centre can host every one of them. Ask a shortlisted centre three things in writing: whether it accepts private candidates for your exact syllabus code, which components of that code it can host, and what its published fee is per subject. If a centre cannot host a component your syllabus requires, the entry is not viable there no matter how convenient the location.

The second question is carry-forward. Some syllabuses allow a previously awarded coursework or component mark to be carried into a later series, and some do not; it is a syllabus-specific rule rather than a general one. The exams officer at the centre can confirm the position for your code against the board's own syllabus page, and the answer changes the plan materially, because a carried mark removes a whole component from the revision timetable. Settle it before you buy hours, not after.

sections.heading: The five grades a UAE resit is usually chasing
paragraphs: A great many UAE resits are not about an A at all. They are about reaching a count. For the British track of Ministry of Education equivalency, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also show either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for that count.

Read what that does to the maths of a second attempt. A student with four qualifying subjects and a fifth below the threshold needs one grade, in one subject, to move one step. That is the single cheapest and most consequential resit in this market, and it is the one families most often misunderstand, because they assume more subjects or higher grades are required. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the published clarification says five, and the difference is an entire unnecessary entry plus a block of hours.

Two cautions. The American track has its own requirements, including a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT for English, and at least 450 in SAT Math before applying. And no IB points threshold for equivalency should be taken from any tutoring website, including this one, without reading it on moe.gov.ae. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee any part of an equivalency or attestation process, and tutoring is not required for it; we describe it, cite the source and point you to the official channel.

sections.heading: Why the right resit tutor is probably not within driving distance
paragraphs: Everything a resit needs works against hiring locally. You need one board, one syllabus code, one tier and often one named component, available in a window that may be eight weeks wide, for a student who has stopped believing the subject is learnable. The pool of people who satisfy all of that within a twenty-minute drive of your address is small in Dubai and very small in Ajman, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain. Widen the pool to anyone who can teach over live video and the constraint disappears, which is why online IGCSE resit tuition is not a compromise on this particular purchase but the obvious form of it.

Be clear about what we do and do not sell. IB Gram does not make home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India, and we do not provide in-person tuition in the UAE at all. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. The query that brought you here may well have been for a visiting tutor, and the honest answer is that the market for visiting tutors is real, it charges roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced in, and on a component-specific resit it usually buys you a generalist close by instead of a specialist in your syllabus.

The practical gains are specific rather than rhetorical. A screen-shared past paper means both people are reading the same mark scheme at the same time, which is how answer-structure work actually gets done. A session can be recorded for the student to re-watch before a paper. Nobody loses forty minutes of a sixty-minute slot to the Sheikh Zayed Road at five o'clock. And when a result has already gone badly once, being taught by the person who knows that exact variant matters more than being taught by the person who lives nearby.

sections.heading: Where a tutor stops on a second attempt
paragraphs: A resit raises the temptation, because the stakes are higher and the window is shorter. The line does not move. A tutor teaches, questions, marks and gives feedback. Everything the board assesses has to be the student's own, from first note to submission, and nobody at IB Gram will produce assessed material on a student's behalf or supply finished text for a student to submit. One page ranking in this market sells finished Internal Assessments outright. That is an academic-integrity breach that puts the student's qualification at risk, and it is the clearest available example of what to refuse to buy.

Where a component mark is being carried forward from the first attempt, the position is stricter rather than looser: that mark belongs to work already submitted and assessed, and it is not something to be revisited or improved after the fact. Where a coursework component is being sat again, the student starts again, with a tutor who may discuss method, question an argument and mark a draft against the published criteria, and who may not supply the content. Say this out loud to any provider you are considering, and listen carefully to how they answer it.

Two more boundaries worth knowing. Past papers, mark schemes, grade-threshold tables and syllabus documents belong to Cambridge and Pearson; we link to the boards' own sites and we do not redistribute their material as a download, no matter how convenient a revision pack would be. And the person teaching your child in the evening needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years; those offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. You can ask a tutor to confirm their permit before the first paid hour.

sections.heading: The dead months, Ramadan, and when resit hours actually fit
paragraphs: A resit year has a strange shape. The result lands in the middle of August, when a large part of the country is out of the UAE, and the next set of papers may not sit until late October or February. Those weeks in between are where resit plans quietly die. The family decides to resit in August, nothing is arranged while people are away, September goes on settling back into school, and by the time anybody books an hour the entry deadline is close and the useful preparation window has halved. The fix is unglamorous: make the entry decision and the first diagnostic booking in the same fortnight as the result.

The UAE calendar then sits on top of the examination calendar. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA calculates their instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, so a resit candidate in school is carrying those periods alongside the subject being resat. They cannot be dropped to make room, and the resit timetable has to be built around the week the school actually runs rather than the week a revision guide assumes.

Ramadan deserves planning rather than improvisation. Shortened school days, altered family routines and later evenings change when a sixty-minute session is genuinely useful, and for many UAE families post-Iftar is the most productive slot of the day rather than a concession. Because lessons run over live video, the slot can move without anybody renegotiating a commute, and sessions can follow a family that travels between emirates or out of the country mid-block. Build the Ramadan weeks into the plan at the diagnosis, and decide then whether the hours drop in number or simply move in the day.

process.title: Send the statement of results, not a description of it
process.description: Share the document itself, with the component marks, the syllabus code and the variant digits. Add the forecast grade the school submitted if you have it. Nothing useful can be planned from a subject name and a grade letter, and any provider willing to quote hours without seeing the breakdown is quoting a package rather than a plan.

process.title: Take the free diagnostic trial lesson
process.description: One free trial lesson per subject, with no payment details taken and nothing payable before or after it. The student works a timed section of a real past paper while the tutor watches the process. The session is a diagnosis, not a sales call, and it ends with a written note of the target component and the hours it needs.

process.title: Get the resit plan in writing, with the deadline at the top
process.description: The plan names the board, the syllabus code, the series, the final entry date, the component being targeted and the evidence that will show progress at the midpoint. If a private candidate entry is needed, it also names the shortlisted centres and what each one has confirmed it can host. Then you can compare it against any other quote.

process.title: Buy a block, with a stop condition agreed in advance
process.description: Hours are bought by the hour against the plan, not as a monthly subscription, because a resit changes shape once the diagnosis is in. Agree at the start what the midpoint review has to show and what happens if it does not. Hours can be moved between two subjects where a child is resitting more than one.

process.title: Review at the midpoint, before the window closes
process.description: A marked paper on the target component, compared against the first diagnostic. If the marks have moved, the block continues as planned. If they have not, the plan changes or the spend stops. Adding hours to a plan that is not working is the most common way resit money disappears in this market.

process.title: Hand back for the paper, and disclose any gap
process.description: The final sessions belong to timed practice under exam conditions on the component that failed first time. If no specialist is available for a thin-supply subject or an unusual syllabus code in your window, we say so rather than substituting a generalist, and we say it before anything is paid for.

whyPoints.title: The component, not the subject
whyPoints.description: A resit is the one point in a student's school career where the evidence already exists. Every plan starts from the component marks on the statement of results rather than from the subject name, because teaching a whole syllabus again to fix one structured paper is the most expensive mistake available in this market.

whyPoints.title: AED figures with the publisher attached
whyPoints.description: Every rate on this page is a market figure read in October 2026 from the provider that publishes it, named in the table. We do not print an IB Gram hourly rate here because the honest answer depends on subject, component and window, and a number invented to fill a column is worse than an empty column.

whyPoints.title: Deadlines linked, never remembered
whyPoints.description: Entry dates, timetables and results dates come from cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com, with the published position and the date we read it stated. Pearson revises provisional timetables, so every resit plan links the live official document rather than trusting a figure copied into a planner.

whyPoints.title: One specialist, chosen from the whole pool
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so the tutor is selected for your syllabus code, tier and component rather than for proximity to your address. On a second attempt in a thin-supply subject, that difference is frequently the difference between a booking and no booking.

whyPoints.title: A stop condition, not an open-ended package
whyPoints.description: Hours are sized to a target, reviewed at a midpoint against a marked paper, and stopped or changed if the evidence is not there. Nobody can promise a grade, and we do not. What can be promised is that you will be told what the hours bought while there is still time to spend them differently.

whyPoints.title: Independent, and plain about what that means
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. It holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, occupies no UAE office, and performs no part of the equivalency or attestation process. Named schools and centres on this page are context, not relationships.

faqs.question: The grade came back one band below the forecast. Should we ask for a review or go straight to a resit?
faqs.answer: Ask about the review first, because it is time-limited and a resit is not. A results enquiry is filed by the examination centre's exams officer, not by a parent, and the centre prices it per candidate per component. Ask the officer for the deadline, the price and whether the fee is returned when a grade changes. A review is most worth filing where the result is inconsistent with every mock and every piece of coursework, and least worth filing where the component marks match what the school already saw all year. Either way, note the entry deadline for the next series while you wait, because the review timetable can run close to it.

faqs.question: Does a resit grade replace the original one, or does the lower result stay visible?
faqs.answer: Each series produces its own statement of results, and the earlier result is not deleted from the record. What a particular institution sees depends on what is submitted to it and on that institution's own rule about which attempt it considers. Some admissions offices take the highest grade, some ask for every result, and some care only that a threshold was met. The only reliable way to find out is to ask the sixth form, college, university or attestation authority directly before you make the entry, and to get the answer in writing. It costs one email and it occasionally makes the whole resit unnecessary.

faqs.question: Can our son resit only the paper he failed, or does the whole subject have to be sat again?
faqs.answer: In most cases the whole subject is entered again and every written component is sat again, because an IGCSE grade is awarded on the complete syllabus rather than paper by paper. The partial exception is carry-forward: some syllabuses permit a previously awarded coursework or component mark to be carried into a later series, and some do not. It is a syllabus-specific rule, so the exams officer at your school or centre should confirm the position for your exact code against the board's own syllabus page. Settle that question before hours are bought, because a carried component removes a whole chunk of the revision timetable.

faqs.question: Our daughter has left school and nobody will re-enter her. Can she still resit in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes, through a private candidate entry at an examination centre that accepts candidates it does not teach. The centre makes the entry, hosts the papers and issues the statement of results, and it sets and publishes its own fee. Ask any shortlisted centre three things in writing: whether it accepts private candidates for your exact syllabus code, which components of that code it can host, and what the published fee is per subject. Dubai carries most of the UAE centres that take private candidates; Al Ain, the northern emirates and the east coast carry fewer, so paper-day travel belongs in the plan from the start.

faqs.question: How many one-to-one hours does a one-grade resit usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the component marks show, and any provider who answers this before seeing them is guessing. As planning assumptions rather than measured outcomes: a single weak component inside an otherwise sound paper is usually sized at six to twelve hours, two or three weak topics at twelve to twenty, and a syllabus that was never securely taught at thirty or more, at which point repeating the year starts to compete on price. Those are the figures we use to size a block, reviewed at the midpoint against a marked paper. Nobody can promise a grade from any number of hours.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to resit three subjects or to repeat the whole of Year 11?
faqs.answer: Three entries plus a shared block of hours is far cheaper than a year of school fees in almost every case, and in Dubai the fee side is unusually knowable: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for 2026-27. The real question is not price but cause. Resits fix grades; a repeated year fixes an education, which is the right purchase for a student who arrived mid-curriculum, missed a long stretch, or sat the wrong tier throughout. Also weigh the twelve months, which appears on no fee schedule and is the largest cost in the comparison.

faqs.question: Will a November resit result arrive in time for a September university start?
faqs.answer: Usually, but check the admissions deadline rather than assuming. Pearson's International GCSE runs a November series, and its November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026; its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. So an autumn resit grade becomes a document you can send in late January, which is comfortable for a September start and tight for anything earlier. Confirm the current dates on qualifications.pearson.com, because provisional timetables are revised, and tell the admissions office before you enter that a result is pending so the file is not closed in the meantime.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE resit entry cost, and why is there no figure for it on this page?
faqs.answer: Because the amount is not ours to publish. The entry fee is set and published by the school making the re-entry or by the examination centre accepting the private candidate, and it varies by centre, by subject and by whether the entry is made before or after the board's final deadline. We would be inventing a number, and an invented number on a resit page is worse than none. Ask for the centre's published fee list in writing, ask whether it is charged per subject or per component, and ask for the late-entry scale that applies after the final entry date for your series.

faqs.question: Does a coursework mark from the first attempt carry forward to the second?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is decided by the syllabus rather than by general policy. Certain syllabuses allow a previously awarded component or coursework mark to be carried into a later series under defined conditions; others require every component to be sat again. The exams officer at your school or centre can confirm the position for your syllabus code against the board's own published page. The answer changes the plan materially, because a carried mark removes a component from the revision timetable and reduces the hours needed. A carried mark also belongs to work already assessed, and is not something to be revisited or improved afterwards.

faqs.question: Our son was entered at Core tier and the grade still disappointed. What does a resit change?
faqs.answer: Possibly nothing, until the tier question is settled. The Core tier is examined on its own component set and its grade range is narrower at the top than the Extended tier's, so a student aiming above that ceiling cannot reach it on a Core entry however many hours are bought. Confirm the current grade range for your syllabus on cambridgeinternational.org, then ask the school or centre in writing which tier a re-entry would use. If the answer is Core again, the honest conversation is about what that grade can do for the next step rather than about tutoring.

faqs.question: How do we read the component marks on a statement of results?
faqs.answer: Start with the structure: the statement shows the overall grade plus a mark for each component the board set, identified by the syllabus code and a component or variant number. Compare the components against each other rather than against a pass mark. A strong multiple-choice mark beside a weak structured paper points at written answers under timing. A theory paper holding up beside a weak alternative-to-practical component points at a specific skill nobody taught explicitly. Then set the whole picture against the forecast grade the school submitted: a large gap between forecast and outcome moves the hours from content towards exam conditions.

faqs.question: Do UAE universities treat a resit grade differently from a first-attempt grade?
faqs.answer: Institutions set their own rules and they genuinely differ, so this is a question for the admissions office rather than for a tutoring site. Some consider the highest grade achieved, some ask to see every result, and some are concerned only that a stated threshold is met in named subjects. Ask directly, in writing, before you make the entry, and ask the same question of any sixth form or college involved. For Ministry of Education equivalency the published British-track rule is about grades and subject counts rather than attempts, but verify the current position on moe.gov.ae rather than relying on any third party.

faqs.question: Does a resit help or hurt a Ministry of Education equivalency file?
faqs.answer: For most families it is the thing that completes it. The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. A student sitting at four qualifying subjects needs one grade in one subject, which is the cheapest consequential resit in this market. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae; IB Gram performs no part of the equivalency process and tutoring is not required for it.

faqs.question: The resit window falls across Ramadan. How should the hours be arranged?
faqs.answer: Deliberately, at the diagnosis, rather than week by week once it starts. Shortened school days and later family evenings change when a sixty-minute session is actually productive, and for many UAE families a post-Iftar slot is the most useful of the day rather than a compromise. Because lessons run one-to-one over live video, moving a slot costs nobody a commute, and sessions can follow a family travelling between emirates or abroad mid-block. Decide at the start whether the Ramadan weeks drop in number of hours or simply shift in the day, and write that into the plan alongside the entry deadline.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle resits in two different subjects for the same child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, within a related pair such as two sciences or maths and physics, and it is worth asking because a single tutor sees the whole timetable and can move hours to whichever subject needs them. More often a second attempt is better served by two specialists, because the value on a resit lies in knowing one syllabus and one component deeply rather than covering a wide range adequately. Where two tutors are involved, ask for one shared plan with both entry deadlines on it, so the hours are allocated against the grades you actually need rather than split evenly out of fairness.

faqs.question: Nobody in the UAE covers the syllabus we need to resit. What happens then?
faqs.answer: You get told, before anything is paid for. Thin-supply subjects such as Computer Science 0478, unusual syllabus codes and very short windows are the cases where availability genuinely runs out, and the dishonest response is to substitute a generalist and hope. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the alternatives are a specialist elsewhere teaching one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, a later series with more preparation time, or a frank conversation about whether the resit is the right route at all. No competitor page we measured in this market discloses a coverage limit anywhere.

faqs.question: What does the free trial lesson cover before we commit to a block of resit hours?
faqs.answer: One free trial lesson per subject, with no payment details taken and nothing payable before or after it. The statement of results is open on screen, the student works a timed section of a real past paper, and the tutor watches how the work is produced rather than only what the answers say. The session ends with a written note naming the component the block should target, the hours it needs and what the midpoint review should show. You are free to stop there and use that note wherever you like, including with another provider.

igcse-resit-tutor.closingHeading: Settle the entry deadline first, then buy the hours
igcse-resit-tutor.closingBody: A second attempt is won or lost on two dates and one document. The dates are the final entry deadline for the series you are aiming at and the day the result will reach you. The document is the statement of results already sitting in your email, with the component marks that say which paper actually failed. Get those three things in front of a specialist before anybody quotes you a rate. Book the free trial lesson in the subject being resat, ask for the plan in writing with the deadline at the top, and decide on the hours once you know what they have to change. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, anywhere in the UAE.

intro.heading: Who is allowed to run the revision class you are about to pay for
paragraphs: A revision class is not one product. In the UAE it is four, and the difference between them is regulatory rather than educational. A school's own revision club runs inside the licence the school already holds from its emirate authority. A tuition centre with a shopfront in Dubai needs an Educational Services Permit of its own. An individual charging for private lessons needs a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. A tutor teaching your child one-to-one over live video is a fourth case again. Most families pay for one of the four without ever asking which.

That matters because the authority behind a provider decides what it can be held to. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the emirate authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods — so a school's revision programme has passed a regulator's desk, and a commercial course sold beside it has not. In Dubai, KHDA oversees the quality of private education and issues the separate permit a training institute needs before it opens its doors. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate.

Underneath all of it is one federal rule that shapes every IGCSE timetable in the country: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Your child therefore sits nine or ten IGCSE subjects and the mandatory UAE subjects in the same week, on the same body, with one set of evenings left over. A revision plan that ignores the second group is planning around a week that does not exist.

There is a second arithmetic problem nobody mentions at the point of sale. For British-track Ministry of Education equivalency, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Nine subjects, five that count towards the file, three that are compulsory and excluded from it, and a fixed number of revision hours between now and the first paper. That is a resource-allocation question before it is a teaching one.

IB Gram teaches IGCSE revision classes as one-to-one lessons over live video. We do not send a tutor to an address in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The honest case for the screen is not convenience, it is supply: a family in Fujairah or Khor Fakkan gets a Chemistry 0620 specialist rather than whoever is willing to drive. The first lesson is free — one subject, one hour, booked after a short consultation, with no payment details taken beforehand.

Read the tables rather than the prose if you are short of time. The regulator map tells you whose rules your child's school runs on. The permit table tells you what to ask any provider to show you. The rate table tells you what the UAE market charges, with each figure attributed to the provider who published it, read in October 2026.

igcse-revision-classes.programmesIntro: Four programmes matter to a UAE family searching for revision classes: the two IGCSE boards your child is actually entered for, the stage underneath that sets up Year 10, and the Diploma or A-Level route the grades are being spent on. Each is regulated differently and each has its own calendar.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The board most UK-curriculum schools in the Emirates enter. Subjects carry four-digit syllabus codes — 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology — and most are offered at two tiers, Core and Extended, sat on different papers. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Revision has to be planned against the code and the tier, because the paper your child sits is decided by both.
programmes.countryNote: Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential that you use the correct version of the timetable for your zone — it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your exams officer which zone the school sits in before you build a revision calendar from a PDF you found online.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other board widely entered across the UAE, with codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics A and 4PH1 Physics. Exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Results behave differently from Cambridge: June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes a provisional timetable before each May/June and November series and then revises it, sometimes more than once, before the final version reaches centres. Work from the live official timetable on qualifications.pearson.com rather than from a date a revision course quoted you in September. A November entry changes the whole shape of a UAE revision year, because the pressure lands in the first term rather than after the spring break.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE sets are chosen, ending in Checkpoint tests in March, May or October. Revision at this stage is not exam revision; it is closing the gaps that decide whether a child is placed on Core or Extended in Year 10. Fractions, rearranging formulae, writing a conclusion that answers the question asked — the Year 9 weaknesses reappear verbatim in a Year 11 mock.
programmes.countryNote: Families arriving mid-year from CBSE, an American system or a UK school land here more often than at IGCSE itself, and the UAE's school year makes the timing awkward: a January arrival meets a set-placement decision already half made. A term of one-to-one work before Year 10 is cheaper in hours than a crash course in Year 11, and it changes a tier decision rather than working around one.

programmes.name: IB Diploma and A-Level, the routes IGCSE grades buy
programmes.description: IGCSE revision is spent on something. In Dubai in 2024-25, 37 per cent of private-school pupils followed a UK curriculum and 7 per cent the International Baccalaureate, so the two destinations sit side by side in the same neighbourhoods. HL Chemistry and A-Level Chemistry both assume Extended-tier fluency with moles and algebraic rearrangement, not a Core pass. The grade your child needs is therefore set by the sixth-form door, not by the IGCSE certificate.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools — four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate — creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. More places means more transfer applications read against IGCSE predictions, and a prediction is built from mock scripts. That is the practical reason mock season, not exam season, is when revision classes earn their keep here.

igcse-revision-classes.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects UAE families book IGCSE revision classes for most often, with the Cambridge code first and the Edexcel equivalent where it is commonly entered. The note on each one is about where marks actually go, because that is what a revision hour has to target.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 Cambridge · 4MA1 Edexcel)
subjects.description: The subject that gates most sixth-form and degree routes, and the one where Core or Extended changes the entire revision plan. Marks disappear in rearranging formulae, in non-calculator arithmetic, and in multi-step problems where the first line is right and the fourth is copied wrong. Revision here is timed past-paper work with every error classified, not more worked examples.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 Cambridge · 4PH1 Edexcel)
subjects.description: Electricity and waves are where UAE students most often stall, partly because the practical paper rewards a kind of writing nobody practises. Describing a method precisely, identifying the variable to control, reading a value off a graph to the right precision — these are separable skills. A revision class that only re-explains circuits leaves the practical marks exactly where they were.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 Cambridge · 4CH1 Edexcel)
subjects.description: Moles sit underneath half the Extended paper, and a student who is shaky there loses marks in titration, yield and formula questions that look unrelated. Organic chemistry is memorisable and usually is not. Revision works best as a short diagnostic on quantitative chemistry followed by paper-by-paper rehearsal, rather than a sweep through the syllabus in order.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 Cambridge · 4BI1 Edexcel)
subjects.description: The highest-content IGCSE science, and the one where command words decide the mark. Describe, explain, compare and suggest ask for different shapes of answer, and a correct fact in the wrong shape scores nothing. Revision should be built around marked scripts: what the student wrote, what the mark scheme wanted, and the gap between them named out loud.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences (0653 · 0654)
subjects.description: Two or three sciences compressed into one or two certificates, usually chosen to free a block for another subject. The risk is a student who is strong in one science and carried by it, with the weak third never diagnosed. Revision has to be split by science and by paper, and the hour allocation is rarely even.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: Reading response and directed writing reward structure over vocabulary. Many UAE students read well and write in the wrong register for the task, or run out of time on the longer response. Revision is drafting under the clock against a mark scheme, then redrafting one paragraph — not a reading list and not a vocabulary sheet.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 · 0511)
subjects.description: The syllabus number matters: 0510 and 0511 differ in how speaking is treated, and a family often does not know which the school entered. Marks go in summary writing and in listening questions where the answer is a precise word. Revision is best split into short, frequent sessions, which is also why it survives Ramadan better than a two-hour block.

subjects.name: Economics (0455) and Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Popular with UAE families aiming at business degrees, and deceptively easy to under-perform in. The content is readable; the marks are in applying a diagram or a chain of reasoning to an unfamiliar case study. Revision should be case-study practice with the mark scheme visible, because a student who can define elasticity still loses the four-mark application.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Two very different halves: theory that can be learnt and algorithmic problem-solving that cannot be crammed. Pseudocode and trace tables are where marks move fastest in a revision block, because they are mechanical once practised. Revision classes that stay on theory inflate confidence without moving the paper that decides the grade.

subjects.name: Geography (0460) and History (0470)
subjects.description: Source and case-study subjects where a revision hour pays for itself through structure. Geography rewards named, numbered case studies; History rewards knowing what each source question is actually testing. Both are badly served by group revision, because the fix is almost always specific to how one student is organising an answer.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508) and Arabic as a Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.description: Entered as IGCSE subjects by many UAE schools and simultaneously governed as a mandatory UAE subject, which is a combination nobody explains to parents. Revision here has to work from the school's own scheme of work, because the material used for the mandatory stream is not freely interchangeable with a tutor's workbook.

igcse-revision-classes.regionsIntro: Which authority holds your child's school changes what you can look up, who approves a course, and who to ask when a revision provider will not answer a question. These are the seven emirates as the regulator map actually divides them, not as a marketing page divides them.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA oversees the quality of private education in the emirate and issues the Educational Services Permit a training institute needs. 387,441 students attended 227 private schools in 2024-25 across 17 curricula. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in private school fees for 2026-27.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules describes a prohibition on school staff giving paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school — worth verifying against the current ADEK policy document before relying on it.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK rather than by a separate authority, which surprises families who move inland and assume a different rulebook. Centre choice is thinner than in Abu Dhabi city, so Al Ain is where online one-to-one revision changes the subject list available rather than merely the commute.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That last clause is why a school's revision programme in Sharjah has been through a regulator and a commercial course sold next door has not.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, alongside Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Families here often commute to Sharjah or Dubai schools, which means evening revision has to be timed around a school run that ends well after 4pm.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah, approves curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Named by essentially none of the competing tutoring pages, which is also roughly how much local IGCSE revision provision exists on the ground.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. The practical reality is a short list of schools and a shorter list of subject specialists, so a Fujairah family looking for Chemistry 0620 Extended revision is choosing between a screen and nothing at all.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under the federal Ministry of Education. The smallest private-school market in the country, and the clearest case for live online one-to-one: the tutor pool stops being a function of who lives within a 25-minute drive and starts being a function of who teaches the syllabus code.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai and the northern corridor
schoolClusters.note: British-curriculum schools here enter large IGCSE cohorts and most run their own revision sessions in the weeks before a series. Ask which subjects are covered and at what tier before paying for anything external — the overlap is often total in Maths and nil in Computer Science or Economics.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: ADEK-regulated schools, with the professional-ethics position on staff tutoring making the school's own free revision club the first thing to use rather than the last. Al Ain families in particular find the external market thin beyond Maths and English.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the northern emirates
schoolClusters.note: SPEA in Sharjah and the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah approve courses and assessment methods, so the school is the better-regulated starting point. Travel between these emirates at 4pm is the single biggest reason a 5pm in-room class gets missed.

This is the format that changes a tier decision, because a Core-or-Extended conversation in Year 10 is still a real choice. It also survives a busy UAE term better than a long block.

The plan is built backwards from the board's live timetable for your centre's zone and from the school's internal deadlines, so the last fortnight is paper rehearsal rather than content.

sections.heading: Four things sold as IGCSE revision classes, and who stands behind each
paragraphs: Start by naming what you are being offered. A school revision club is provision from an institution that already holds a licence from its emirate authority and is inspected against it. A tuition centre course comes from a business with premises, which in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. An independent tutor running a small group needs a private tuition work permit from MoHRE. A one-to-one tutor on live video is the fourth case, and the permit question still applies to them wherever they are resident in the UAE.

These four differ in accountability before they differ in teaching quality. A school answers to an authority that can inspect it and, in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah, has approved its programmes and assessment methods. A centre answers to the authority that issued its permit. An individual answers to MoHRE and to the code of conduct attached to the permit. Nobody answers to a company that cannot tell you which of the four it is, which is the first question worth asking and the one most often deflected.

They also differ in what one hour can physically do. In a room of eighteen, an hour is a sweep: the teacher covers the topic most of the cohort got wrong. In a group of three, it is a compromise between three different error patterns. One-to-one, the hour belongs to one error pattern, which is why it is the format that moves a stuck student and the most expensive per hour. None of that is a reason to skip the school club — that provision is already paid for and often good.

sections.heading: Five authorities, one school year: whose rules your revision plan runs on
paragraphs: The UAE does not have a single schools regulator, and the differences are not cosmetic. Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah's Private Education Authority regulates private education in that emirate, as does the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah. The Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

Two of those five go further than inspection. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. If you live in those emirates, the programme your child sits at school has been through an approval process, and a privately sold revision course has not. That is not an argument against the course. It is an argument for asking the course the same questions the authority would have asked.

What a parent can do with this is practical. You can look up which authority holds your school and read what it publishes about it. You can ask the school which of its revision sessions are part of its approved provision. You can ask an external provider which authority it answers to and expect a document, not an adjective. And you can stop treating a national-sounding brand name as evidence: none of the five authorities endorses a tutoring company, and any page claiming otherwise is making a claim it cannot support.
The final column is the one to use. It turns the regulator map into a question you can ask on the phone before you pay a deposit.

sections.heading: The permit question, asked about a revision class rather than a tutor
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you — if a provider names one, treat it as marketing. The permit itself is granted free of charge for two years, which removes the usual excuse that licensing is too expensive for a working tutor.

The eligible categories are broader than most parents assume. They include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. That last pair explains a large part of the budget end of the market: a bright undergraduate can legitimately hold a permit, and that is a different proposition from an experienced subject teacher at the same hour. Both can be the right choice. They should not cost the same.

The application route is public. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. A tutor telling you the permit is slow, expensive or optional is telling you something checkable and wrong. A centre is a separate case: a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry.

IB Gram is not approved, licensed or endorsed by any of these bodies, and no tutoring company should tell you it is. What we can do is answer the question honestly when you ask it, and tell you which document to ask any provider for.

sections.heading: Your child's own teacher, the free revision club, and the line Abu Dhabi drew
paragraphs: The cheapest IGCSE revision in the country is the session the school already runs, and it is routinely skipped in favour of something paid. Before booking anything, get the list: which subjects run revision sessions, in which weeks, at which tier, and with which teacher. Then compare that list with where the mock marks actually went. Families frequently discover that Maths and English are covered twice over while the subject that cost them a grade — Computer Science, Economics, the Physics practical paper — has nothing scheduled at all.

The adjacent temptation is to pay your child's own subject teacher privately. In Abu Dhabi that runs into a specific barrier: press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct is described as barring serving students affiliated with their own school. Verify the current wording against the authority's own policy document before acting on it, but do not treat the arrangement as routine simply because somebody offered it.

There is a plainer reason to avoid it even where it is permitted. The teacher who wrote the mock, who will submit the forecast grade and who marks the coursework should not also be the person you are paying for the result. That is a conflict a parent cannot manage from the outside, and it puts a teacher in a position no professional wants. An external tutor who has never met the school is a weaker option on context and a much cleaner one on incentives.

Use the school for what it is uniquely good at — entries, tiers, access arrangements, forecast grades and the subjects it has staffed for revision — and buy outside help only for the gaps that remain.
bullets: Get the school's revision timetable in writing before paying for anything external
Compare it against the mock marks, subject by subject, not against a general worry
Treat paying your child's own teacher as a question for the school, not a convenience
Ask the exams officer about access arrangements early; only the centre can apply for them

sections.heading: A UAE revision year, and who controls each date in it
paragraphs: Revision planning fails on ownership, not on effort. Some dates belong to the board, some to the school, some to the emirate authority, and only a few to you. Writing down which is which is the fastest way to stop arguing about things nobody in the house can change and start working on the things they can. The dates below are the ones a UAE IGCSE family actually runs on, taken from what Cambridge and Pearson have published.

The entry deadlines are the ones that catch families out, because they sit months before the paper. Read the revision year forwards from the autumn and the sequence is plain: Pearson's November 2026 series sits from late October to 19 November 2026, with entries long closed by then; Cambridge's June entries close in the spring term, months before the papers, and the school's internal cut-off lands earlier again. A tier change or a subject withdrawal is therefore a first-term conversation, not an April one. Note too that Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only, so no UAE candidate is sitting in February whatever a timetable found online suggests; the Checkpoint tests in March, May and October belong to Primary and Lower Secondary, not to IGCSE. By the time revision feels urgent, the paper your child is sitting has already been decided.

Results day starts two more clocks. Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. After that come reviews of marking, retake entries and, for families staying in the Emirates, the Ministry of Education equivalency file. None of those belong to a tutor, and all of them have deadlines held by somebody else.

Ramadan sits across this calendar differently each year, shortening the school day and compressing lesson units. Plan for shorter, more frequent sessions rather than cancelling a block, and expect the useful hours to move to the evening.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies: the revision nobody budgets for
paragraphs: Every IGCSE revision plan in the UAE competes with a second curriculum that is not optional. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies. These subjects are the floor, not an extra.

The rules around them are unusually specific, and they constrain what any outside revision provider can honestly offer. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies for Arab students runs primarily in Arabic; non-Arabs take Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two further details decide what a tutor may do. Schools are required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach these subjects — so ask any provider offering Arabic revision who is teaching it and on what basis. And for the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the MoE, is strictly prohibited. A revision class for Arabic cannot simply import a workbook; it has to work from the school's own material.

The time budget is where this bites. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, with schools allowed to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advice that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Those units are inside the school week your child also has to revise nine IGCSE subjects around.

sections.heading: Nine subjects, five grades: how the equivalency rule should split revision hours
paragraphs: If your family intends to use UAE universities or to have the certificate recognised here, the Ministry of Education equivalency rule changes how revision hours should be allocated. On the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Verify the current wording on moe.gov.ae before relying on it.

The detail that reshapes a revision plan is which subjects are excluded. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. One page currently ranking for these searches tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects; the sourced position is five, with those two excluded. Your child still has to sit Arabic and Islamic Education — the school and its authority require it — but those grades are not the ones carrying the equivalency file.

For families on the American track the requirements are different again: English proficiency via a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and at least 450 in SAT Maths before applying. For the IB there is no points threshold in the sourced material, so no figure should be published without reading it on the Ministry's own site. Nobody should be quoting you an IB number from a tutoring page.

None of this means tutoring is required for equivalency. It is an administrative process run by the Ministry, not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or expedites. What the rule does is tell you which five subjects are load-bearing, and that is a far better basis for allocating twelve weeks of revision hours than a general sense that everything needs work.

sections.heading: What IGCSE revision classes cost across the UAE market
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible pages in this search publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote US dollars — a currency UAE families do not transact in. So here is the market in AED, with every band attributed to the provider who published it, read in October 2026. These are other people's rates, not ours. Treat them as a sense of the spread, then ask any provider for a written hourly figure rather than a package headline.

The spread is the useful information. The same hour of IGCSE revision is sold from under AED 50 to over AED 600, and the variable is not mostly quality — it is who is teaching, at what tier, in what format, with how much preparation and marking time included. A university student with a valid MoHRE permit at the bottom of the range is a legitimate option for consolidating Core-tier content. They are not the same purchase as an experienced Extended-tier subject teacher in the last eight weeks before a paper.

Monthly packages are where comparison breaks down. Published examples include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Divide any package by the number of hours before comparing, and ask what happens to sessions you do not use.

Two costs sit outside every quote: exam entry fees if your child sits as a private candidate, and the marking time a tutor spends on papers between sessions. Ask whether the second is included and whether the quoted figure is inclusive of VAT. IB Gram does not publish a rate card on these pages; the first lesson is free, one subject and one hour, and the rate comes out of a short consultation once we know the board, the code and the tier.

sections.heading: A room of fifteen, a group of three, or one child and one screen
paragraphs: The format argument in the Emirates is usually framed as online against a visiting tutor, which skips the two formats most revision classes actually are: a large school session and a centre course of eight to twenty. Each of the four does something the others cannot, and the honest comparison is about what one hour delivers rather than about which is modern. A large session is excellent at coverage and poor at diagnosis. One-to-one is the reverse.

Travel is the hidden term in the equation. A 5pm start in a room means somebody crosses an emirate at the worst hour of the day: Ajman or Sharjah into Dubai, or Al Ain to anywhere. Whether the tutor bills the travel or absorbs it, you pay for it, and in exam term the session that gets cancelled is the one with a commute attached. Online removes that term for both sides, which is why a plan of three short sessions a week survives a UAE April and a plan of one long visit often does not.

The supply argument matters more than the convenience one. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address — home visits are a service we offer only in India — and the reason the online model is the right one here is the subject list. A family in Fujairah looking for Chemistry 0620 at Extended tier, or ESL 0511, or Computer Science 0478, is not choosing between a local specialist and a screen. They are choosing between a screen and a generalist who happens to be nearby.

What online gives up is real and worth naming: no shared workspace in the room, no incidental supervision of a teenager's phone, and a dependence on a stable connection. Screen-sharing a past paper and annotating it live covers most of the first; a parent in the next room covers the second.

sections.heading: What a revision class may hand your child, and what it must not touch
paragraphs: This search contains providers that sell completed assessed work. One of them lists finished Internal Assessments at a price. That is academic malpractice under the boards' own rules, and the student carries the consequence, not the seller. So the boundary needs stating in plain words rather than implied: a tutor teaches, explains, questions, reviews and gives feedback on work the student has produced. The student writes every word that is submitted. Coursework, practical reports and controlled assessments stay the student's own throughout.

In practice that distinction is workable and specific. A tutor can teach the skill a coursework task assesses, talk through a plan the student has drafted, point at a paragraph and ask what it is for, mark a practice attempt against the published criteria, and explain why an answer that contains the right fact scored nothing. A tutor cannot take the pen, rewrite a submission, supply text to be handed in, or sit beside a student during an assessment that must be unaided. If a provider is vague about which side of that line it works on, that vagueness is the answer.

Materials have their own rule and it is a copyright one. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. A provider should be pointing you at cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com, or working from the copies the school has legitimately given your child, not distributing photocopied bundles or a shared drive of scanned mark schemes. Unreleased material is worse again: a tutor offering advance sight of a paper is describing malpractice.

No provider can promise a particular outcome either, and the ones that do are telling you something about themselves. Revision changes the probability of a grade by changing what a student can do under timed conditions. That is worth paying for. A promised number is not a product.
bullets: A tutor teaches and gives feedback; the student produces everything that is submitted
Ask for the honesty policy in writing before the first paid session
Official board sites and the school's own copies, not photocopied mark-scheme bundles
Treat any offer of advance paper content as a reason to walk away

sections.heading: Six questions to ask a revision provider, and the document that settles each
paragraphs: Most of what goes wrong with paid revision in the Emirates is settled in one phone call, if the right six questions get asked. None of them is about teaching philosophy. All of them have a document behind them, and a provider who cannot produce the document is giving you useful information by failing to.

The first two are regulatory: which authority permits or licenses you, and which board and syllabus code is my child entered for. The second is answered by the school's statement of entry, not by the provider, and it is worth getting before you book anything — it carries the board, the code, the tier and the components, and a revision plan built on a guess about any of those wastes hours. Families routinely discover at this point that the school entered 0511 rather than 0510, or Core rather than Extended.

The next two are operational: which zone timetable applies to our centre, and who teaches Arabic or Islamic Education revision and on whose material. The zone matters because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong timetable version. The Arabic question matters because KHDA requires school teachers of those subjects to hold its approval, and because substituting content needs prior MoE permission.

The last two are commercial: what happens to coursework and practical work, and what is the hourly price and what is excluded. Ask for the honesty policy, the session length, whether marking time between sessions is included, and whether the figure includes VAT. Then compare like with like across providers, which is only possible once everybody has given you a number per hour.
