process.title: Send us the three things that decide everything
process.description: Board, syllabus code and tier, taken from the statement of entry rather than from memory, plus the series your child is sitting. Those three facts decide which papers matter, which timetable applies and which specialist can help. A subject name on its own is not enough to match against.

process.title: A short consultation, then a free first lesson
process.description: Twenty to thirty minutes on the phone or over video to establish where the marks are going and what the school already covers. Then one free lesson: one subject, one hour, no payment details taken beforehand. If the match is wrong, say so afterwards and we will try a different tutor.

process.title: A diagnosis built from marked work, not a placement test
process.description: The first paid session works through your child's own marked mock script or homework. The output is a ranked list of topics and techniques with the mark cost of each, which becomes the plan. This is also where a Core or Extended mismatch usually surfaces, while there is still time to raise it with the school.

process.title: A fixed weekly slot on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video at a time that survives the school run and, during Ramadan, usually after Iftar. Shorter and more frequent beats long and occasional through a UAE exam term. You get short written feedback after each session naming what was covered and what comes next.

process.title: If no specialist is free, we tell you that
process.description: Some combinations are thin — a particular Extended-tier science in a narrow evening window, or an Arabic first-language stream tied to a school's own scheme of work. When nobody suitable is available we say so and give you a realistic date, rather than putting a generalist in the slot.

whyPoints.title: The rates on this page are the market's, and each one is attributed
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names the provider that published it and the month it was read. Three of the most visible pages in this search publish no price at all. You can disagree with our reading of the market, which is the point of showing where the numbers came from.

whyPoints.title: Revision planned around the authority your school answers to
whyPoints.description: A plan for a Sharjah family where SPEA approves programmes and assessment methods is not the same as a plan for an ADEK school in Al Ain or a KHDA school in Dubai. Knowing which authority holds the file changes what you can look up and who you can ask.

whyPoints.title: One hour belongs to one error pattern
whyPoints.description: A school session covers what most of the cohort got wrong, which is the right job for a school session. One-to-one covers what your child got wrong. That is the whole difference, and it is why the hour costs more and why fewer of them are usually needed.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line is written down before you pay
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions, reviews and gives feedback. The student produces everything that is submitted, and coursework and practical work stay the student's own. We will put that in writing, and we point at the boards' own sites for syllabus material rather than circulating copies.

whyPoints.title: Timed to the UAE week, including Ramadan and study leave
whyPoints.description: Sessions sit in Gulf Standard Time around a school day that shortens during Ramadan and disappears during study leave. No travel at 5pm in either direction, which is the main reason an exam-term session gets cancelled here.

whyPoints.title: Delivered online, stated plainly, with no UAE premises implied
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video. We do not operate a centre, a branch or a visiting-tutor service anywhere in the Emirates, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. That is also why the tutor pool is a function of the syllabus code rather than of the postcode.

faqs.question: Is a revision class in the UAE allowed to be run by anyone who can teach the subject?
faqs.answer: No. Private tutoring here is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any figure quoted at you as marketing. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. A business running classes from premises in Dubai needs something different again: a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute.

faqs.question: Which authority licenses the revision centre my child would attend?
faqs.answer: It depends on the emirate. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. Elsewhere the emirate authority applies: ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Ask any centre for its permit number and expiry date in writing. No tutoring company is approved or endorsed by these authorities, and one claiming otherwise is making a claim it cannot support.

faqs.question: Can we use the free revision club at my child's school instead of paying for classes?
faqs.answer: Usually you should use it first. It is provision from an institution that already holds a licence from its emirate authority, it costs nothing beyond fees you have paid, and in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves the school's programmes and assessment methods. Ask for the revision timetable in writing: which subjects, which weeks, which tier, which teacher. Then compare it with where the mock marks actually went. Families often find Maths and English covered twice while the subject that cost a grade has nothing scheduled. Paid one-to-one work is then aimed at a short, specific list rather than at everything.

faqs.question: Is my child's own teacher allowed to take our money for private revision?
faqs.answer: Treat this as a question for the school rather than a convenience. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct is described as barring serving students affiliated with their own school. Verify the current wording against the authority's own policy document before acting on it. There is a plainer reason to avoid the arrangement even where it is permitted: the person who writes the mock, submits the forecast grade and marks the coursework should not also be paid by you for the result.

faqs.question: How large is too large for an IGCSE revision class?
faqs.answer: It depends what you need the hour to do. A session of fifteen to thirty is good at coverage, because the teacher works on the topic most of the cohort got wrong. A centre course of eight to twenty delivers a fixed syllabus sweep on a fixed schedule. A group of three is a compromise between three different error patterns, and somebody is always waiting. One-to-one is the only format where the whole hour goes to one student's errors. If your child is stuck on something specific, group size is the variable that decides whether the hour touches it at all.

faqs.question: Is Arabic revision something an outside provider can legally plan for us?
faqs.answer: Only within limits, and the limits are specific. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so a revision class cannot simply import its own Arabic workbook — it has to work from the school's material. KHDA also requires schools to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach these subjects, and that separate classes are organised for Arabs and non-Arabs, with combined classes strictly prohibited. Ask any provider offering Arabic revision who is teaching it and whose scheme of work they are using.

faqs.question: Should revision hours go first to the subjects that count for equivalency?
faqs.answer: If UAE recognition matters to your family, that is a sensible way to rank them. On the British track, the sourced rule requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. Your child still sits them, because the school and its authority require it, but those grades are not carrying the file. Verify the current requirements on moe.gov.ae before building a plan around them.

faqs.question: Do revision classes in the UAE run through Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Ours do, and the shape changes rather than the quantity. The school day shortens and lesson units compress, so three short sessions a week work better than one long block, and the useful hours usually move to the evening after Iftar. This is one of the clearer practical arguments for live video over a visiting tutor in exam term: there is no commute to abandon when a timetable shifts at short notice. If a series falls near Ramadan, build the plan backwards from the first paper and accept that the fortnight before it will be paper rehearsal rather than new content.

faqs.question: What do revision classes cost per hour across the UAE market?
faqs.answer: The published spread in AED per hour, read in October 2026, runs roughly like this: budget online from AED 33-65 at the bottom, where Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise; qualified subject tutors online from AED 150, as Unitors publishes; a visiting tutor at AED 180-500 including travel, per Bestimate and home-tutor listings; specialist IGCSE or IB tuition at AED 200-450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270; and premium named tutors at AED 500-650, where BartyED sits. Those are their figures, not ours. Divide any monthly package by its hours before comparing, and ask what the rate excludes.

faqs.question: How do I check whether a revision tutor holds the MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Ask to see it, and ask when it expires. The permit runs for two years and is granted free of charge, so there is no cost reason for a working tutor not to hold one. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. A tutor who tells you the permit is expensive, slow or optional is telling you something checkable and wrong. For a centre rather than an individual, ask instead for the educational services permit number issued by the emirate authority.

faqs.question: Can a revision class hand my child mark schemes and past paper bundles?
faqs.answer: It should not be distributing them. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and reproducing them is a copyright matter. A provider should be pointing you at cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com, or working from the copies the school has legitimately given your child. A shared drive of scanned mark schemes is a warning sign rather than a resource. Anything described as advance sight of an unreleased paper is worse: that is malpractice, and the student carries the consequence rather than the seller.

faqs.question: Why does the statement of entry matter before we book revision classes?
faqs.answer: Because it is the only document that tells you what your child is actually sitting. It carries the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the components, and a revision plan built on a guess about any of those wastes hours. Families regularly discover at this point that the school entered English as a Second Language 0511 rather than 0510, or Core rather than Extended, or a different board for one subject than for the rest. Get it from the exams officer before the first paid session. The same conversation is the moment to ask which administrative zone timetable applies to the centre.

faqs.question: We are in Fujairah and no centre runs IGCSE revision classes nearby. What now?
faqs.answer: This is the situation live online one-to-one exists for. Fujairah is supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, the private-school market is small, and the list of local subject specialists is shorter still, so a family looking for Chemistry 0620 at Extended tier is not choosing between a local expert and a screen. Teaching over live video makes the tutor pool a function of the syllabus code rather than of who is willing to drive to you. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses — home visits are a service we offer only in India — so what we can offer here is the specialist, on Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: Does my child need revision classes to get Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: No. Equivalency is an administrative process run by the Ministry, and no tutoring provider performs it, guarantees it or speeds it up. What the rule does is tell you which grades carry weight: on the British track, five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus an Advanced Level or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Anybody implying that tutoring is required for a regulatory process is manufacturing urgency. Verify the requirements on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate, and use the rule to rank revision priorities.

faqs.question: Can one revision class cover both Cambridge and Edexcel candidates?
faqs.answer: Content overlaps; assessment does not. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 cover much the same mathematics, but the papers, the tiering, the command-word conventions and the mark schemes differ, and in the last eight weeks that is where the marks are. A mixed group spends its time on the overlap, which is the part your child probably already has. For maintenance work across Year 10 a mixed setting is survivable; for pre-series revision, match the board and the code. Cambridge runs June and November series; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November.

faqs.question: Is eight weeks before the first paper too late for revision classes to change anything?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks is enough to change technique and triage content, and not enough to rebuild a subject from the start. What moves in that window is specific: command-word discipline, timing across a paper, the mechanical marks in pseudocode or trace tables, quantitative chemistry, graph-reading precision, and the structure of an extended answer. What does not move is a tier decision, because the entry closed months earlier: a June entry closes in the spring term and a November entry mid-year, both well before the eight weeks begin. So spend the eight weeks on marked scripts and timed papers, one component at a time, and ignore any plan that proposes a syllabus sweep.

igcse-revision-classes.closingHeading: Start with the statement of entry, then the permit, then the price
igcse-revision-classes.closingBody: IGCSE revision classes in the UAE are easier to buy well once you know which of the four kinds you are buying, which authority stands behind it, and what the market charges per hour rather than per package. Get the statement of entry from the exams officer. Ask the provider which authority permits or licenses it. Ask for an hourly figure and what it excludes. Then book the free first lesson — one subject, one hour, no payment details taken beforehand — and judge the match on how precisely the tutor reads your child's marked work. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time.

igcse-summer-tuition.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE at syllabus level: Cambridge 0580 and 0625 and Pearson 4MA1 and 4PH1 are different documents with different papers, and a summer block is too short to find that out in week three. Each works from the code on your child's statement of entry.

intro.heading: Ten weeks, a fixed calendar, and the decisions that cannot wait for September
paragraphs: A UAE summer is not a blank page. Most private schools in the Emirates close somewhere between the last week of June and the second week of July, and reopen in the last week of August or the first days of September. Your school publishes the exact dates, and it publishes them under a calendar its regulator has signed off on: KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. That is why two families living four kilometres apart, with children in schools licensed by different authorities, can break on different Thursdays.

Strip out the travel. Most families we speak to spend four to six weeks of the break outside the country, which leaves four to six usable weeks, and they are rarely contiguous. A plan that assumes ten clear weeks will fail in week two. A plan written against your actual departure and return dates will not. That is the first thing IGCSE summer tuition in the UAE has to get right, and it is the thing most providers skip because it is easier to sell a fixed twenty-hour package than to build around a family's flights.

What ten weeks can genuinely do is narrower than the marketing suggests and more valuable than parents expect. It can close a tier decision before it hardens - a Year 10 student sitting Cambridge Core when Extended is still reachable has until the entry window to change that, and the summer is when the argument gets made with evidence rather than hope. It can rebuild one broken topic properly: electricity in 0625, moles in 0620, algebraic fractions in 0580. It can convert a student who writes acceptable answers into one who reads command terms. What it cannot do is replace two years of taught lessons, and nobody should sell you that.

The second thing a summer plan has to respect is the board calendar, because entry windows do not pause for the holidays. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series; the February/March series is offered to India only, so it is not an option from the UAE, and the Checkpoint tests that appear in March, May and October are Primary and Lower Secondary papers rather than IGCSE. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and in November, and the November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. That autumn window is the one a summer decision reaches: entries for it close well before the papers, and the exams officer who processes them is often the person least available in late August. A decision about a November resit or a fresh November entry is therefore a July conversation, not an October one.

Third: results. Pearson sent June 2026 International GCSE results to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026 - inside the break, for most UAE schools, while a good proportion of families were abroad. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge releases June-series results on Direct in August as well, with certificates following, and November-series results in January. If a grade is going to be queried, a subject repeated, or an A-Level choice revisited, that happens in a fortnight that overlaps with airport queues. Knowing in June who will be where, and who can log in, is worth more than an extra hour of revision.

Finally, the system your child sits inside does not go on holiday either. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and the federal baseline says private schools must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies whatever else they offer. Those subjects carry their own language-of-instruction and class-organisation rules, and the Ministry's position is that using different or additional content without prior permission is prohibited. A summer plan that quietly ignores a third of the September timetable is not a plan.
bullets: The break is roughly ten weeks; four to six of them are usually travel, so build the plan around flight dates, not around a package size

igcse-summer-tuition.programmesIntro: Four stages of the British-curriculum route turn up in summer enquiries, and each one wants a different use of the weeks. A Year 9 student has room to choose; a Year 11 student has a date. The stage, not the subject, decides what a ten-week block should attempt.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and the year before IGCSE
programmes.description: The year before IGCSE is where option choices are made and where the gap between a strong Year 9 and a comfortable Year 10 opens. Cambridge offers Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and many UAE schools use them to stream. Summer work at this stage is about arithmetic fluency, algebraic manipulation and scientific notation - the mechanical skills that make Extended tier survivable rather than the content, which has not been taught yet.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools often set the IGCSE option form in the spring of Year 9, which means the summer before Year 10 is the last unhurried window to test whether triple science or Additional Mathematics is realistic. Families moving into the Emirates in August face the same decision with no school history behind it, and a diagnostic hour is usually more useful than a term of guessing.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE is sat in a June series and a November series, and every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version. Cambridge's own guidance is blunt about this: it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Core and Extended are separate papers with separate grade ceilings, and the tier is an entry decision.
programmes.countryNote: A UAE family's practical question in July is which zone their centre sits in and which series the school has entered, because those two facts change the whole revision shape. Cambridge IGCSE 0580 summer tuition for a Year 11 student entered in the November series is a different job from the same subject aimed at June, and the first session should establish which it is from the statement of entry rather than from memory.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year. The codes look similar to Cambridge but the papers are not: 4MA1 Mathematics, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology and 4EA1 English Language each have their own assessment pattern, and Pearson publishes a provisional timetable well ahead of each May/June and November series, then issues a final version closer to the papers themselves. Those provisionals can be revised, so a plan should check the live official timetable rather than a figure copied from a blog.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE summer tuition in the Emirates most often involves a November entry, because the November series gives a Year 11 student who underperformed in June a route that does not cost a full academic year. The decision has to be made while the school's exams officer is still contactable, which in UAE terms means before the office closes for the break.

programmes.name: The summer after results: AS, IB Diploma, or a repeat
programmes.description: The weeks after August results are the busiest part of the UAE tutoring year and the least planned. A student who missed a grade needed for AS Mathematics, or for Higher Level Chemistry in an IB Diploma, has days rather than weeks to decide between a review of marking, a November repeat, or a change of subject. Each route has a different deadline and a different cost, and schools are reopening while the clock runs.
programmes.countryNote: UAE sixth forms and IB Diploma schools generally confirm Year 12 subject places in the week schools return, so the August gap between results and enrolment is where the real decisions sit. A tutor's job here is diagnostic and fast: establish whether the gap was content, exam technique or a tier that was always too low, and say which of the three a term of lessons can actually move.

igcse-summer-tuition.subjectsIntro: Summer requests cluster tightly around the same twelve subjects, and in almost every case the useful work is one or two named topics rather than the whole syllabus. Each entry below names the Cambridge and Pearson codes, because the code changes the paper and the paper changes the lesson.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 Cambridge, 4MA1 Pearson)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The single most requested IGCSE summer subject in the Emirates. Extended tier loses marks in algebraic fractions, functions, bounds and vectors far more than in number work. Pearson's Higher tier paper structure differs from Cambridge Extended, so past-paper practice has to match the code on the entry.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606 Cambridge, 4PM1 Pearson Further Pure)
subjects.description: Taken alongside Mathematics by students heading for AS Mathematics or IB Higher Level. Calculus, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities are where the grade is decided. A summer block before Year 11 is the sensible time to add it, because adding it in January rarely works.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 Cambridge, 4PH1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Electricity and magnetism account for most lost marks in UAE classrooms, followed by anything requiring a rearranged formula under time pressure. Practical skills are assessed on a written paper rather than in a laboratory for most international candidates, which makes apparatus-description questions a teachable, scoreable target over a summer.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 Cambridge, 4CH1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry are the hinge topic: a student who cannot convert confidently will lose marks across the whole paper, not just in one question. Organic chemistry and electrolysis come next. Both are closed-loop topics that respond well to concentrated work in a short block.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 Cambridge, 4BI1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Biology marks are usually lost to imprecise language rather than to missing knowledge - describing instead of explaining, naming a process without its location, or omitting the unit. Summer work here is mostly answer discipline against the command terms the board actually uses.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences (0653, 0654 Cambridge)
subjects.description: The route for students taking two science awards rather than three separate ones. Content overlaps the single sciences but the paper allocation does not, and students who revise from triple-science materials routinely cover topics they will never be asked about. Checking the syllabus against the entry saves wasted summer hours.

subjects.name: English Language (0500 and 0990 Cambridge, 4EA1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading-response questions carry the grade, and both are technique rather than content. A summer block can realistically move a student up a band on the writing paper by fixing structure, register and the habit of answering the question asked instead of the one practised.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510, 0511 Cambridge)
subjects.description: Common in UAE schools where English is an additional language for a large part of the cohort. The listening and speaking components reward rehearsal, and the summer is the only unpressured period in the two-year course when speaking practice can happen without a timetable fighting it.

subjects.name: Economics (0455 Cambridge, 4EC1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides the longer questions: an unlabelled axis or a shifted curve in the wrong direction costs the mark regardless of the prose around it. Data-response technique is the other target, and both are short, mechanical and well suited to a ten-hour summer block.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450 Cambridge, 4BS1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Case-study application is where UAE candidates lose marks - correct theory applied to a generic firm rather than to the business in front of them. Summer work means practising against unseen cases and learning to spend the evaluation marks, which most students leave on the table.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478 Cambridge) and ICT (0417 Cambridge)
subjects.description: Two different qualifications that parents frequently conflate. Computer Science carries algorithm and pseudocode work that rewards summer practice; ICT carries practical software tasks assessed against a specification. A summer block should confirm which one is on the entry before it starts teaching.

subjects.name: Arabic (0508 First Language, 0544 Foreign Language, Cambridge)
subjects.description: Arabic sits in two places at once for a UAE family: as an IGCSE entry and as a subject the school is separately required to teach. The two have different content and different expectations, and summer work should be explicit about which of the two it is serving.

igcse-summer-tuition.regionsIntro: Where a family lives changes which authority approves the school calendar, which schools are within reach in September, and how a July schedule behaves. Lessons themselves are delivered online across all seven emirates, so the constraint is the calendar and the time zone rather than the drive.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA licenses the schools and oversees the quality of private education here, across 227 private schools serving 387,441 pupils in 2024-25 on seventeen different curricula. UK-curriculum provision is the largest single block, so IGCSE summer demand is heaviest in Dubai and slots in the 4pm to 8pm band fill first.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. That shapes who can legitimately teach your child over the holidays here more than it does in some emirates.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, with a smaller British-curriculum cohort than Abu Dhabi island and fewer specialist tutors living within driving distance. This is where online delivery changes the answer most sharply: a 4PM1 Further Pure specialist does not need to be in Al Ain to teach in Al Ain.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A Sharjah school's term dates and assessment pattern therefore sit with a different authority from a Dubai school's, which matters when siblings attend across the border.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, alongside Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. The practical effect for a summer plan is that the calendar and the mandatory-subject requirements come from the federal level rather than an emirate-specific authority with its own published guidance.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. British-curriculum provision is concentrated in a small number of schools, so Year 11 cohorts are small and a missing subject specialist is a real constraint locally.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education territory on the east coast, and the emirate with the thinnest published coverage in competitor tutoring content - most national providers name it nowhere. Live online lessons remove the geography question entirely; what remains is confirming which board the school has entered.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: The smallest private-school market in the country and also Ministry of Education territory. Families here frequently travel to Sharjah or Dubai for schooling, which means a summer plan often has to work around a September change of school as well as a change of year group.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai
schoolClusters.note: The densest IGCSE cohort in the country, and the emirate adding seven new private schools for 2026-27 - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 new places after a 6% enrolment rise in 2025-26. Summer enquiries from these schools cluster around Extended-tier Maths and the three separate sciences.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: Schools here answer to ADEK, with strong British-curriculum provision on the island and in Khalifa City, and a thinner spread inland. Families here ask more often about the ethics rules around a serving teacher tutoring privately, because ADEK's guidance on that is specific and widely discussed locally.
schools: GEMS Cambridge International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the Northern Emirates
schoolClusters.note: Smaller cohorts, a different regulator in each emirate, and a real shortage of subject specialists for Additional Mathematics, Computer Science and Further Pure. This is the cluster where online one-to-one stops being a convenience argument and becomes the only way to reach the right teacher.

igcse-summer-tuition.modesIntro: Three shapes of summer block account for almost every workable plan, and the right one depends on how much of the break the family is actually in the country. Each runs as live one-to-one video lessons on Gulf Standard Time, with written notes after every session.

modes.title: The compressed intensive, two or three weeks
modes.description: For families with one solid block at home and the rest of the summer abroad. Four to five sessions a week on one or two subjects, aimed at a named topic rather than a syllabus sweep. This is the shape that works best for a repair job: electricity in 0625, moles in 0620, algebra in 4MA1. It burns a lot of attention in a short time, so it suits a student who already knows what is broken.
bullets: 4-5 sessions a week, 60 or 90 minutes, one or two subjects only
A diagnostic first hour that produces a written topic list
Past-paper work matched to the syllabus code on the statement of entry
A closing session that hands the school something readable in September

modes.title: The travel-tolerant weekly hour
modes.description: One or two sessions a week that follow the family rather than the calendar. Lessons continue from London, Mumbai, Nairobi or wherever the summer takes you, scheduled against local time rather than Gulf Standard Time for those weeks and switched back on return. Progress is slower per week but the habit survives, which matters more for a Year 10 student than for a Year 11 facing a November entry.
bullets: 1-2 sessions a week, rescheduled to the family's actual time zone
Short written tasks between sessions, sized for a holiday not a term
A pause option for weeks with no reliable connection
A step-up in late August without restarting from scratch

modes.title: The late-August bridge
modes.description: A concentrated fortnight in the two or three weeks before schools reopen, for students who have genuinely rested and now need to re-enter a timetable. The most common uses are a Year 10 to Year 11 handover, a Year 11 November-series run-up, and a post-results repair after Pearson or Cambridge grades land in August. Short, specific and aimed at the first fortnight of term rather than at the exam.
bullets: 8-12 sessions over two to three weeks
Built from the actual results or the last school report, not a generic baseline
Explicit targets for the first two weeks of term
A written handover note the family can share with the subject teacher

sections.heading: What a UAE summer actually gives you, counted in teachable days
paragraphs: A UAE private-school summer break runs roughly ten weeks. That is the number parents start from, and it is almost never the number they end up with. Subtract the decompression week nobody can teach through, the travel weeks, the Eid or family-visit weeks where a schedule simply cannot hold, and the pre-term week when uniform shopping and medicals eat the afternoons, and a realistic figure is four to six teachable weeks. At two sessions a week that is eight to twelve hours. At four sessions a week in a compressed block it is sixteen to twenty-four.

The honest consequence is that a summer plan has to pick one or two things. Eight hours will not cover a Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics syllabus, and no amount of scheduling discipline changes that. Eight hours will fix algebraic fractions, bounds and the function notation that a Year 11 student has been guessing at for a year, and those three things might be worth a grade. The plan that names its targets in week one and refuses to widen them is the plan that produces something visible in September.

This is also where the difference between a package and a plan shows. A twenty-hour package sold in June assumes twenty hours exist. A plan written against your departure date assumes nothing and schedules around the flights. Before the first lesson, we ask for three dates: when school closes, when you leave, when you return. Everything else is derived from those, and the week-by-week table below is the shape most UAE families end up with.

One more subtraction worth making deliberately: the student's own rest. A fifteen-year-old who has just finished a UAE academic year with internal exams in it is tired in a way that a timetable cannot argue with. Two weeks of nothing at the start of July costs you two of your ten weeks and buys back attention for the other four. Families who skip it tend to lose those weeks anyway, to arguments.

sections.heading: Who decides when your summer starts, and why three emirates do not break together
paragraphs: Private schooling in the UAE is regulated emirate by emirate, and the regulator is not a formality - it approves the things a summer plan runs on. In Dubai, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge does so in Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education plays the supervising role for private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

Two of those authorities go further in a way parents rarely notice. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is curriculum and fee approval, not just inspection. So when a Sharjah school's internal assessment pattern differs from a Dubai school's teaching the same Cambridge syllabus, that is not an accident or a quality difference - it is two different approval regimes producing two different school-level decisions on top of one board specification.

For a family, the practical consequence is a short list of things to look up rather than assume. Which authority licenses the school. What the school's published calendar says about the last day of term and the first day back, because that is where your ten weeks is actually defined. Whether a sibling's school, under a different authority, breaks on a different date - which determines whether you have one summer or two overlapping ones. And, in Abu Dhabi, what the local ethics rules say about who may teach your child privately, because ADEK's rules on that are more specific than most families expect.

None of this requires a parent to become an expert in education law. It requires knowing which door to knock on. The KHDA private school calendar is published by the school under KHDA's framework rather than invented by the school, and the same holds in each emirate. If a tutoring provider cannot tell you which authority licenses your child's school, it does not know the system it claims to work inside.

sections.heading: The three summers of an IGCSE, and the one job each of them has
paragraphs: Parents ask for IGCSE summer tuition at three distinct moments, and the three have almost nothing in common. Treating them as one service is how twenty hours get spent on the wrong thing. The summer before Year 10 is a choosing summer: nothing is entered, nothing is fixed, and the job is to make sure the tier and option decisions ahead are made from strength rather than from a fear of Extended. The useful work is mechanical fluency, not content, because the content has not been taught.

The summer between Year 10 and Year 11 is the leverage summer, and it is the one most often wasted. A student arriving in Year 11 with a repaired foundation topic and a working habit of reading command terms has a materially different year ahead from one who arrives having forgotten June. This is also the last comfortable window for a tier change, because a Core entry that becomes an Extended entry needs the school convinced before the entry window, and conviction is built with evidence over weeks. A summer block here should produce something a subject teacher will actually read.

The summer after Year 11 is a decision summer, and it is short. Results land in August, the sixth form or Diploma place depends on them, and the options - a review of marking, a November repeat, a change of subject, a different post-16 route - all carry different deadlines. The job in those weeks is not teaching. It is establishing fast and honestly whether a gap was content, technique or a tier that was always too low, and saying which of the three a term of lessons can move. The fourth case, a student repeating a subject in a later series, is really a continuation of that decision summer with a date attached.

Saying which summer you are in changes the first question a tutor asks. A choosing summer starts with a diagnostic on arithmetic and algebra. A leverage summer starts with the June report and the last internal exam paper. A decision summer starts with the statement of entry, the results slip, and a calendar. Any provider that offers the same opening session to all three is selling hours rather than a plan.

sections.heading: Entry windows that open or close while the family is away
paragraphs: The most expensive thing a UAE family can do over the summer is miss a date that was never going to wait. Board deadlines are set months ahead of the papers, and several of them sit in or immediately after the break, when the school's exams officer is unreachable and the parent is in another country. The pattern is worth knowing in outline even if the school handles the mechanics, because the school handles them on the school's timetable and not on yours.

Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and the gap between an entry and a paper is what makes this a summer job. A June entry closes in the spring term, roughly four months before the first paper, with the school's own cut-off earlier again; a November entry closes mid-year, before the autumn papers. Read backwards from either and a decision taken in September is already late, while a decision taken in July is comfortable. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, which is the single most useful date to hold in your head over the break. Ask the exams officer for the exact entry date in writing before the office closes, because that is the number the plan is built on.

There is a second Cambridge detail that catches UAE families specifically. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge's guidance states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam when the wrong zone timetable has been used. A revision plan built off a timetable found online, rather than the one the centre issued, is a real risk and not a theoretical one. Pearson, for its part, publishes a provisional timetable ahead of each May/June and November series - and marks it provisional because those dates can be revised - so the live official timetable is the only one worth planning against, whichever series your child is entered for.

The practical move is small. Before the school office closes for the summer, settle three things in writing: which series your child is entered for, which tier in each subject, and who at the school will action a change if August results make one necessary. Then put the board's own timetable page in a bookmark rather than a screenshot. That is twenty minutes of work in June that removes the most common summer failure entirely.

sections.heading: Results arrive in August, and two clocks start the same morning
paragraphs: For most UAE schools, results day falls inside the holiday. Pearson sent June 2026 International GCSE results to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge releases its June-series results on Direct in August too, with certificates following, so both boards land their main result in the same few weeks of the break. In practical terms that means a significant number of UAE families receive the single most consequential document of the two-year course while in transit or abroad, with the school closed and the sixth-form place pending.

Two clocks start on that morning. The first is the enrolment clock: UAE sixth forms and IB Diploma schools generally confirm Year 12 subject places in the days around reopening, so a grade that falls short of a Higher Level or AS prerequisite has to be addressed before the term timetable hardens. The second is the review clock: boards operate defined windows for a review of marking or an enquiry about results, requested through the centre rather than by the parent, and those windows are measured in weeks from results day, not from the day the family gets home.

This is where a summer plan earns its money without teaching anything. Knowing in June who will be where in late August, who has the login, and which named person at the school is monitoring email, converts a panic into a sequence. If a review is worth requesting, it is requested through the centre quickly. If a November entry is the better route, the entry is made rather than discussed. If the honest answer is that the subject was always the wrong tier, that conversation happens before a Year 12 timetable is built on a false premise.

A tutor's role across that fortnight is narrow and useful: read the paper breakdown with the family, say where the marks went, and give a straight view on whether a repeat is likely to move the grade or whether the gap sits somewhere a repeat will not reach. That is a diagnostic judgement, not a promise, and no tutor who has not seen the script should pretend otherwise.

sections.heading: What a summer block costs in the UAE market
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking tutoring pages for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars - a currency UAE families do not transact in. So here are the AED bands, attributed to whoever published them, as read in October 2026. These are market rates, not IB Gram's rate card. Our own position is simpler: a free trial lesson first, one per subject, booked through the site with no payment taken beforehand, and a quote after the tutor has seen what the work actually is.

The spread is wide and it is informative. At the bottom, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52, which in practice buys a university student or a generalist. In the middle, Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. Specialist IGCSE, IB and A-Level rates run from roughly AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table putting the specialist band at AED 200 to AED 450 plus. A visiting tutor costs more because travel is inside the price: Bestimate puts in-home at AED 180 to AED 350, and independent home tutors at AED 200 to AED 500. At the top, BartyED advertises AED 650 an hour for a named premium tutor.

Multiply those by a realistic summer. Sixteen hours - four weeks at four sessions - costs about AED 720 at the budget end, AED 2,400 in the mid band, AED 4,320 at a specialist AED 270, and AED 10,400 at AED 650. Monthly packages in the market sit around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 plus for specialist exam-year work.

Two cautions on reading any of this. First, an hourly rate tells you nothing about what happens inside the hour; a cheaper tutor who teaches the wrong syllabus code is not cheaper. Second, be wary of a provider whose advertised band and whose quote differ, or who will not say which tier of that table they sit in. Summer IGCSE tuition rates in AED are not a secret, and a provider that treats them as one has told you something.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor in July against live one-to-one online
paragraphs: The home-tutor question deserves a straight answer rather than a sales pitch. A visiting tutor in the UAE market charges roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, and that number carries the travel inside it. In July, travel in the Emirates is a real cost: a cross-city journey in peak heat, two of them per session, and a schedule that constrains the tutor to whoever lives within a reasonable drive. That last point is the one that matters most, and it is the one no price list shows. Within a twenty-minute radius of a villa in Khalifa City or Al Khan, the pool of people who can teach Pearson Further Pure 4PM1 is very small. Nationally, it is not small at all.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition to UAE families as live online video lessons. We do not send a tutor to an address in the Emirates; home visits are something we offer only in India. That is stated plainly here because the alternative - implying a service we do not run - would be the kind of thing this page spends several sections warning parents about. What we do instead is match on syllabus code rather than postcode, which is why a family in Fujairah and a family in Jumeirah can be taught by the same 0625 specialist on the same afternoon.

The summer sharpens the comparison in both directions. Online wins on continuity: when the family flies to Manchester or Kochi for five weeks, the lessons continue, rescheduled to local time, and resume on Gulf Standard Time when you land. It wins on tutor pool and on scheduling, because a 7am session before a flight or a 9pm session after Iftar is a calendar entry rather than a drive. It loses nothing on practical science for an international candidate, because practical skills are assessed on a written paper for most of these entries. Where a visiting tutor genuinely wins is with a much younger child, or a student whose attention does not hold on a screen - and for a Year 10 or Year 11 IGCSE student, that is a judgement a parent should make honestly rather than a thing to be sold either way.

sections.heading: Who is legally permitted to teach your child over the holidays
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated, not informal. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and MoHRE's own service listing for it is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system with a stated two-working-day completion time. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone telling you a permit costs money, or that it is optional for summer work, is wrong on both counts.

The eligible categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. That breadth explains the bottom of the rate table - a university student advertising AED 60 an hour may be perfectly entitled to do so. It also explains why the permit alone is not a quality signal. It tells you someone is permitted to tutor. It tells you nothing about whether they have taught Cambridge 0580 Extended.

The position on your child's own teacher deserves care. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and notes that teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than as ADEK's exact wording, and check the current policy document before relying on it - but the direction of travel is clear enough that a parent should not arrange it casually over the summer. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are, on the federal guidance, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any specific figure you see quoted online is not sourced.

One further distinction matters because it is the most abused phrase in this market. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: it needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram does not hold that permit, does not operate premises in the Emirates, and makes no claim to regulator endorsement of any kind. Any provider describing its tutors as carrying a regulator's seal of approval is making a claim you are entitled to ask it to evidence.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies do not leave the September timetable
paragraphs: Families planning a summer around Maths and the sciences routinely forget that a third of their child's September week is spoken for. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. At federal level the same principle holds: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

The rules around how these subjects run are specific, and they constrain what any tutor can honestly offer. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; and for non-Arabs, Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies run in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two further details decide what summer work in these subjects can look like. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. And the content question is settled: for the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Schools are also required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

So the honest offer is narrow and still worth having. Over the summer, a tutor can build vocabulary and reading fluency in Arabic, work on the language skills that make a Social Studies assessment legible, and practise written expression - all of which sit alongside the school's programme rather than substituting for it or introducing alternative material. Where a family's goal is an Arabic IGCSE entry, 0508 as a first language or 0544 as a foreign language, that is a board qualification with its own content and should be planned as a separate thing from the school's mandatory provision. Conflating the two is the most common mistake in this corner of the market.

sections.heading: The Ministry of Education equivalency file is a summer job, not a Year 13 job
paragraphs: Equivalency is the step that converts a foreign school certificate into something a UAE authority recognises, and it is the step families discover late. For the British track, the requirements as reported from the Ministry's July 2026 clarification are specific: a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That last sentence is where a competitor page already gets it wrong. One ranking provider states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The sourced rule is five accredited subjects, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count - which in practice means a student taking nine subjects including Arabic has more headroom than the six-subject claim implies, and a student taking six including Arabic has less. Counting the subjects correctly in Year 10, during a summer when options can still change, is worth considerably more than finding out in Year 12.

For the American track the published requirements are different again: English proficiency via a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT; and mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the International Baccalaureate, there is no figure on this page, deliberately. No IB points threshold for UAE equivalency has been read on an official Ministry source for this project, and publishing an unsourced number would be worse than publishing nothing. Check it on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority.

Equivalency is a process the authority performs, not something a tutor or a platform does or guarantees, and tutoring is not required for it. What the summer is good for is the arithmetic: counting which subjects will be on the certificate, confirming which of them are accredited and which are excluded from the five, and identifying now whether a subject needs adding, strengthening or repeating. That is a one-hour conversation in July that occasionally changes an entire option block.
