sections.heading: Coursework, past papers and the line a tutor does not cross over a summer
paragraphs: Summer is when the academic-honesty line gets tested hardest, because deadlines are far away, supervision is light, and a tired family is susceptible to an offer that sounds like help. One provider found in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is not tutoring. For an IB student it is a malpractice trigger with expulsion consequences, and the equivalent for board coursework is no better. A tutor's work is teaching, review and feedback on the student's own material, and a student who submits work that is not theirs carries the risk personally.

In practice the boundary is easier to hold than it sounds, because the useful work sits well inside it. A tutor can teach the skill the task assesses. A tutor can read a draft the student has written and say which paragraph does not answer the question, where the evidence is thin, and which command term has been ignored. A tutor can model a worked example on a different question entirely, then watch the student attempt theirs unaided. A tutor can set a schedule so a piece due in October is not started in October. What a tutor may not do is supply the text, edit a piece to completion, or hand over anything the student then submits as their own.

The same caution applies to materials. Board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. We reference them, cite the official page, and link out. We do not reproduce them, host them or offer them as downloads, and a provider that advertises a complete past-paper archive as a bundled benefit is telling you something about how it treats other rules too. Your child's school can provide centre-appropriate material through the proper channel.

There is one more thing worth stating plainly for the summer specifically. If a tutor's summer plan requires work the student cannot plausibly have produced, the plan is wrong regardless of who wrote the words. The test a parent can apply in September is simple: ask your child to explain, unaided, one paragraph of anything handed in. If they can, the summer did its job. If they cannot, it did not, whatever the grade says.
bullets: Teaching the skill, reviewing a draft and giving feedback are inside the line
Supplying text, editing to completion or handing over finished work is outside it
Board papers and mark schemes are referenced and linked, never reproduced or supplied as downloads
The September test: can the student explain one paragraph of their own work unaided?

sections.heading: Starting in July: the honest version, including what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: The first step is a free trial lesson, one per subject, booked through the site with no payment taken beforehand. It is a diagnostic hour rather than a sample lesson: the tutor works from the school report, the last internal exam paper and the syllabus code on the statement of entry, and ends it with a written list of named topics in priority order. Families who do nothing else with us still leave with that list, which is deliberate - a plan a parent can read is the only way to judge whether the hours that follow are aimed at anything.

The second step is a calendar built from your dates. We ask for the last day of term, your departure and your return, and we write the block against those rather than against a package size. Ten weeks becomes a specific number of sessions in specific weeks, with the travel period either paused or rescheduled to your local time. Nothing is billed for weeks when no lesson happens, and an unused slot does not quietly expire while you are abroad.

The third thing is the part most providers do not put in writing. Summer is when tutors take their own holidays, and in minority subjects - Pearson Further Pure 4PM1, Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 - the UAE-resident pool is genuinely thin in July. If no specialist is free at the time you need, we say so rather than filling the slot with a generalist. The options we put to you are a different time slot, a tutor from our India-based pool teaching online at the same standard, a later start date, or nothing at all if the honest answer is that the window has closed. Three of those four involve us earning less, which is the point.

After that it is routine. A written note goes out after every session, with what was covered, what was set and what is not yet fixed. A fortnightly summary is short enough that a parent on holiday will actually read it. At the end of the block you get a handover note written for the subject teacher rather than for us, naming what changed and what did not. Whether you continue into the autumn is a decision taken on that evidence, and we would rather you took it coldly.

process.title: Send the three dates and the syllabus code
process.description: The last day of term, your departure and your return, plus the code from the statement of entry - 0580, 4MA1, 0625. Those four facts decide the whole shape of a summer block. Without the code, a tutor is guessing which paper your child sits, and in July there is no time to discover that in week three.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson as a diagnostic
process.description: One free trial lesson per subject, booked through the site, with no payment taken beforehand. It runs on the school report and the last internal paper, and it ends with a written list of named topics in priority order. The list is yours whether or not you book anything further, because a plan you cannot read is not a plan.

process.title: Get the block written against your calendar
process.description: Specific sessions in specific weeks, with the travel period paused or rescheduled to your local time zone. Weeks with no lesson are not billed, and a slot you cannot use while abroad does not expire. This is the step that separates a plan from a twenty-hour package, and it takes about ten minutes to settle.

process.title: Read the notes, not the reassurance
process.description: A written note after every session says what was covered, what was set and what is still broken. A fortnightly summary stays short enough to read on holiday. If a note never says anything is still unfixed, something is wrong with the note rather than right with the progress.

process.title: Take the September decision on the handover note
process.description: At the end of the block you get a note written for the subject teacher: what changed, what did not, and what the first fortnight of term should target. Whether you continue into the autumn is a decision taken on that evidence. We would rather you decided coldly in September than warmly in July.

whyPoints.title: The syllabus code sets the lesson, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are both called IGCSE Mathematics and they are not the same qualification. Tier, paper structure and formula provision differ. Every summer block starts from the code on the statement of entry, which is also why we ask for it before the first lesson rather than after the third.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the subject, not on the driving distance
whyPoints.description: Lessons run live online, one-to-one, so the pool is national rather than whoever lives within twenty minutes of your villa. For Additional Mathematics, Further Pure or Computer Science in Al Ain, Ras Al Khaimah or Fujairah, that is the difference between the right teacher and the available one.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling that survives a UAE summer
whyPoints.description: Sessions are set on Gulf Standard Time and rescheduled to your local time when you travel. A 7am slot before a flight or a 9.30pm slot after Iftar is a calendar entry rather than a drive across the city in August heat. Weeks with no lesson are not billed.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published, our quote given after the trial
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are attributed to the providers and rate tables that published them, read in October 2026. They are the market, not our price list. Our own number comes after a free trial lesson, when a tutor has seen what the work actually is, and it arrives in writing.

whyPoints.title: The coursework line is stated before the first lesson
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the skill, reviews the student's own draft and gives feedback. A tutor does not supply text or hand over finished work for submission. Saying that out loud is a differentiator in a market where at least one provider sells completed Internal Assessments, and it protects the student rather than us.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated honestly, including when it is nil
whyPoints.description: In July, specialists in minority subjects are often unavailable. We say so and offer a different slot, an online tutor from our India-based pool, a later start, or nothing. Three of those four mean we earn less, which is why no competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: Our school closes in early July and reopens in late August. How many teaching weeks is that really?
faqs.answer: On paper about ten. In practice four to six. Take out the first fortnight, when a student who has just finished a UAE academic year with internal exams in it cannot absorb anything. Take out the four to six weeks most families spend abroad. Take out the pre-term week of uniforms and medicals. What is left is eight to twenty-four usable hours depending on intensity. That is enough to repair one or two named topics properly, settle a tier argument with evidence, or run a post-results decision. It is not enough to cover a syllabus, and a plan that pretends otherwise will fail in week two.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a MoHRE permit if the lessons only run through the summer holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and there is no seasonal exemption in the federal guidance. It is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service listing shows a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you see quoted online as unsourced. Ask any tutor for their permit position before a summer block starts, including ours.

faqs.question: Who decides the summer dates for my child's school, and where are they published?
faqs.answer: The school publishes them, under a framework set by whichever authority licenses it. In Dubai that is KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain it is ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. The practical point is that two children in schools under different authorities can break on different dates, so check each school's own published calendar rather than assuming one national summer.

faqs.question: We travel for five weeks in July. Is there any point starting IGCSE summer tuition at all?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the plan has to be built around the flights rather than in spite of them. Two realistic shapes work. The first is a compressed block in the weeks you are in the country, four or five sessions a week aimed at one named topic. The second is a single weekly hour that follows you, rescheduled to your local time wherever you are, then stepped up on return. What does not work is a fixed twenty-hour package bought in June on the assumption of ten clear weeks. Send us your departure and return dates and the block gets written against them.

faqs.question: Is the November IGCSE series a sensible target if the work starts in July?
faqs.answer: It can be, and July is the right month to decide. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November; the Pearson November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. The constraint is rarely the teaching time, it is the entry: confirm with the school's exams officer that your centre offers the series and that an entry can still be made, before the office closes for the break. A November entry is the route that avoids losing a full academic year after a disappointing June.

faqs.question: Our son's IGCSE results land in August while we are out of the country. What cannot wait?
faqs.answer: Three things. First, access: know who has the login and who at the school is monitoring email in August, because the office may be closed. Second, enrolment: UAE sixth forms and IB Diploma schools generally confirm Year 12 subject places around reopening, so a grade short of an AS or Higher Level prerequisite needs addressing immediately. Third, any review of marking, which is requested through the centre and sits inside a defined window measured from results day, not from the day you get home. Pearson released June 2026 International GCSE results to students on 20 August 2026, firmly inside most UAE breaks.

faqs.question: Can my daughter's own class teacher tutor her privately over the holidays?
faqs.answer: Be careful with this one. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi describes a prohibition on teachers giving paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and notes that the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. That is press-reported rather than verbatim policy, so check the current document before relying on it. The direction is clear enough that an informal summer arrangement with your child's own teacher is not something to set up casually.

faqs.question: Does summer work count towards the Arabic and Islamic Education the school has to deliver?
faqs.answer: No, and it should not try to. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with their own language-of-instruction rules and a requirement that classes for Arabs and non-Arabs are organised separately. Instructional time is counted on a 40-minute lesson unit. Crucially for tutoring, using different or additional content for these subjects without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited. Summer work can build Arabic vocabulary, reading fluency and written expression alongside the school's programme. It cannot substitute for it or introduce alternative material.

faqs.question: What does the UAE market charge for an IGCSE hour in July and August?
faqs.answer: The published bands, read in October 2026, run wide. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase publishes AED 270, and Bestimate's Dubai table puts specialist IGCSE, IB and A-Level work at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. A visiting tutor runs AED 180 to AED 500 because travel sits inside the price. BartyED advertises AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Those are market figures, not ours; our quote follows a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: How many hours a week in July is sensible before a fifteen-year-old stops absorbing anything?
faqs.answer: For a compressed repair block, four or five sessions of 60 to 90 minutes across one or two subjects is about the ceiling, and only for two or three weeks. Beyond that, attention falls faster than content accumulates and the sessions turn into supervision. For a travel-tolerant plan, one or two hours a week sustains the habit without fighting the holiday. The variable that matters more than the hours is narrowness: two subjects worked properly beats five touched lightly, every time. Widening the target list mid-block is the most common way a good summer plan quietly stops working.

faqs.question: We move from Sharjah to Dubai in September. Does the IGCSE course carry across?
faqs.answer: The board qualification does; the school-level arrangements may not. Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, and Dubai's schools sit under KHDA's framework, so two schools teaching the same Cambridge syllabus can differ on tier entries, internal assessment timing and option blocks. Check three things before term: which board and series the new school enters, whether the tier matches what your child has been taught, and which option subjects actually run. A summer block is well spent closing a gap that a tier or option mismatch creates, if you find it in July rather than October.

faqs.question: Is a summer intensive better value than the same hours spread across the autumn term?
faqs.answer: For repairing one broken topic, the intensive usually wins, because the topic is held in working memory across consecutive sessions rather than rebuilt weekly. For exam technique and command-term discipline, spread hours win, because the habit needs repetition against school work that is actually happening. The practical answer for most Year 11 families is both: a compressed summer block on content, then a weekly hour through the autumn on technique. Market monthly figures for a weekly one-hour session sit around AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 plus for specialist exam-year work.

faqs.question: Can the summer be used to open the Ministry of Education equivalency file?
faqs.answer: The file itself is the authority's process, not something a tutor or a platform performs or guarantees, and tutoring is not required for it. What the summer is genuinely good for is the arithmetic behind it. The British-track rule as reported from the Ministry's July 2026 clarification is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at E. Count your child's subjects against that in July, while options can still change, and verify on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: My child is repeating a subject in the March Cambridge series. What should the summer look like?
faqs.answer: Count backwards from the series your child is actually entered for. In the UAE that is Cambridge's June or November series, or Pearson's May/June or November - not the February/March series, which Cambridge offers to India only. For a June sitting the entry closes in the spring term and the papers run across May and June, so the summer before is three clear months ahead of any timed-paper season. For a November sitting the papers are close behind the break; Pearson's November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. So the summer is not the revision period, it is the diagnosis and foundation period: establish from the previous script where the marks went, rebuild the two or three topics underneath that, and leave the timed-paper work for the autumn. Confirm with the exams officer which series the entry is for before you plan around either.

faqs.question: Can a tutor work on IGCSE coursework with my child during the holidays?
faqs.answer: On the student's own work, yes, within clear limits. A tutor can teach the skill the task assesses, read a draft the student has written and say which paragraph misses the question, model a worked example on a different task, and set a schedule so an October deadline is not started in October. A tutor may not supply text, edit a piece to completion, or hand over anything the student submits as their own. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright; that is malpractice and the consequences land on the student, not the seller.

faqs.question: Our tutor will be in another time zone in July. How do the lessons actually run?
faqs.answer: They run as live one-to-one video lessons, scheduled to whichever time zone you are in that week rather than fixed to Gulf Standard Time. Families travelling to the UK, India or East Africa usually keep the same tutor and the same slot shifted by the time difference. On return the schedule moves back to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in the Emirates at any point in the year; home visits are offered only in India. Weeks where no lesson happens are not billed, and an unused slot does not expire while you are away.

faqs.question: What should a summer plan have produced by the first week of term?
faqs.answer: Three things you can hold. A written topic list from the diagnostic hour, with what has been closed marked off and what remains named. A handover note addressed to the subject teacher rather than to us, saying what changed, what did not, and what the first fortnight should target. And a student who can explain, unaided, one paragraph of anything they produced over the break. If that last test fails, the summer did not work regardless of how many hours were booked, and the autumn plan should be built on that rather than around it.

igcse-summer-tuition.closingHeading: Start with the three dates, not with a package
igcse-summer-tuition.closingBody: Send the last day of term, your departure and your return, plus the syllabus codes from the statement of entry. The first lesson is a free trial, one per subject, booked through the site with no payment taken beforehand, and it ends with a written list of named topics in priority order rather than a sales call. From there the block is written against your calendar, weeks with no lesson are not billed, and if the right specialist is not free in July we will tell you that instead of filling the slot. Lessons run live online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time across all seven emirates.

igcse-to-ib-transition-course.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma subjects and have taught students through the Year 11 to DP1 move, which is a specific skill: knowing which IGCSE habits help and which have to be unlearned. Ask for the subject your child is least confident carrying forward. Sessions run online, one to one.

intro.heading: Eight IGCSEs become six subjects, and the assessment changes underneath them
paragraphs: The usual description of this move is that the Diploma is harder. That is not quite the problem. A student who sat eight or nine IGCSEs is dropping to six subjects, which sounds like relief, and then discovers that three of those six are Higher Level courses carrying 240 recommended taught hours each, that the grade is built partly from an independent piece of work they have never produced before, and that the two-year arc has no public examination in the middle of it to tell them where they stand.

The content gaps are real but narrower than families fear, and they are specific rather than general. IGCSE mathematics ends before formal calculus; Diploma mathematics assumes it almost immediately in one route and uses it casually in the other. IGCSE sciences assess practical skills through a paper or an alternative-to-practical; Diploma sciences require a designed investigation the student scopes themselves. IGCSE English rewards accurate response to a question; Diploma English rewards sustained argument about unseen non-literary text. Each of those is a few weeks of focused work if it is identified early, and a term of confusion if it is not.

The timing is what makes the move difficult in the UAE specifically. Cambridge and Pearson results reach students in August, days or weeks before a late-August or early-September DP1 start, and Pearson's own published pattern has June series results going to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. That leaves almost no window between knowing the grades and starting the course they were supposed to inform. Families who wait for results to plan the bridge have already lost the summer that was the bridge.

There is also a paperwork tail that nobody raises in Year 11 and everybody meets in Year 13. Ministry of Education equivalency for the British track is specific about what IGCSE students must show: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among the five, alongside one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. A student moving into the Diploma rather than A-Levels needs to check the current Diploma requirement directly with the Ministry, because no Diploma points figure has been read on a Ministry source for this project.

What follows is the bridge as a calendar: what to do in which week, what each subject actually assumes on day one of DP1, what IGCSE grades predict and what they do not, the four Diploma components that are genuinely new, and the board dates that are published and verifiable. Teaching for UAE families is delivered one to one over live video; IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE.

igcse-to-ib-transition-course.programmesIntro: Three qualifications are in play in this move, and the differences between them are structural rather than a matter of difficulty. Reading them side by side is what makes the gap visible.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses in eight or nine separate subjects, tiered in several of them into Core and Extended or Foundation and Higher, assessed almost entirely by terminal written papers. Cambridge runs June and November series with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October; Pearson runs May and June and November series. The structure rewards accurate, bounded answers to set questions, and the student is rarely asked to decide what the question should be.
programmes.countryNote: UK curricula account for the largest share of enrolment in Dubai's private schools, so most UAE students arriving in DP1 come from this background. That also means a whole cohort arrives with the same strengths and the same two or three gaps, which is why a bridge can be planned rather than improvised.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, each graded 1 to 7, with internal assessment contributing a fifth to a quarter of the grade in most subjects. Higher Level carries 240 recommended taught hours against 150 at Standard Level, and in most subjects adds an extra examination paper. The two-year arc has no public mid-point examination.
programmes.countryNote: In UAE schools the Diploma runs alongside mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies, which are required in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. A DP1 week is therefore fuller than a Year 11 week was, not emptier, despite having fewer examined subjects.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge is assessed by an exhibition and an essay; the Extended Essay is an independent research piece with a strict word limit; CAS is completed rather than graded. The essay and Theory of Knowledge together contribute up to three points to the Diploma total. None of the three has an IGCSE equivalent, which makes them the single largest change in the move.
programmes.countryNote: The Extended Essay lands in DP1, in the same term as the first serious internal assessments. Students who come from an IGCSE background where every deadline was set and policed by a teacher find the self-managed timeline harder than the research, and that is a planning skill a bridge can teach.

igcse-to-ib-transition-course.subjectsIntro: What follows is the handover point for each subject: what IGCSE finished with, and what the Diploma course assumes in its opening weeks. The gap, not the subject, is what a bridge should cover.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: IGCSE ends with algebraic manipulation, trigonometry and a first look at gradients. Analysis assumes fast, accurate manipulation and begins calculus early, with one paper sat without a calculator. Students arriving from a calculator-permitted IGCSE route need by-hand fluency built deliberately, which takes weeks of practice rather than a few sessions.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: IGCSE statistics stops at descriptive measures and simple probability. Applications assumes comfort with distributions, correlation and regression, and a graphical display calculator in every paper. The gap is calculator technique and statistical vocabulary rather than algebra, and it is usually quicker to close than the Analysis gap.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: IGCSE physics is formula-led with structured questions. Diploma physics expects algebraic rearrangement under time pressure, multi-step reasoning from unfamiliar starting points, and a scientific investigation the student designs. The uncertainty and error treatment is the part with no IGCSE equivalent at all.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: IGCSE chemistry covers reactions, moles and basic organic families. Diploma chemistry rebuilds bonding and energetics on a more quantitative footing and treats organic mechanisms as a system rather than a list. Students who memorised IGCSE reactions find the mechanism approach disorienting for about a month.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content overlap is the largest of any subject, which is why Biology lulls students. Diploma biology asks for application of named processes to unfamiliar data and for precise command-term discipline, and the volume of exact terminology roughly doubles. The investigation requires an independently scoped experiment.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: IGCSE English Language and Literature reward accurate, bounded response. Diploma English A assesses unseen non-literary texts, a spoken individual oral on a global issue, and at Higher Level a formal essay on a studied work. The step is in sustained independent argument, which cannot be revised for by content.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Most students arrive with no IGCSE Economics at all, which is an advantage: there is nothing to unlearn. The genuine demand is diagram fluency and the three commentaries on published articles, which require reading the financial press rather than a textbook. Higher Level adds a quantitative paper.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: IGCSE Business Studies, where taken, transfers reasonably well in content terms. What changes is the internal assessment, which at Higher Level is a research project on a real organisation. Choosing that organisation early in DP1 is the difference between a comfortable project and a rushed one.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: IGCSE history teaches source handling in a tightly structured format. Diploma history expands it into a source paper, world history topics, a historical investigation, and at Higher Level a regional option with a third timed essay paper. The reading load is the change, roughly doubling at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Students who met Arabic only through mandatory school periods frequently overestimate their starting point for Arabic B, because the mandatory stream and the Diploma language acquisition course have different purposes. An honest placement conversation before DP1 saves a difficult term of catching up on productive skills.

igcse-to-ib-transition-course.regionsTitle: Where the Year 11 to DP1 move happens, across the UAE
igcse-to-ib-transition-course.regionsIntro: Some students move into a Diploma sixth form inside the same school; others change school entirely at the end of Year 11. Which of those it is changes what the bridge has to cover, because a new school means new teachers, new deadlines and a new option-block structure as well as a new qualification.

regions.name: Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and the Greens, Dubai
regions.note: A dense corridor of British-curriculum schools, several with Diploma sixth forms attached and several without. Families here often move school at the end of Year 11, which means the bridge covers a new timetable and new internal deadlines on top of the qualification change.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Established schools with mature sixth forms offering both A-Levels and the Diploma. The decision here is frequently two-stage, and students who choose the Diploma over A-Levels do so alongside friends taking the other route, which makes the workload difference visible by October.

regions.name: Dubailand, Arabian Ranches and the southern communities
regions.note: Villa catchments with long school-bus routes, which matters for a summer bridge because it determines what time a session can realistically start once term begins. Many families here run the bridge intensively in July and August and then taper to weekly.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi city, Al Bateen and Al Mushrif
regions.note: Capital schools with British-curriculum intakes feeding Diploma sixth forms at a smaller number of institutions. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and a change of school means a change of regulator contact point too.

regions.name: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Al Shamkha, Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Growing communities where sixth-form provision is still filling out, so a Year 11 student may find the Diploma available only at a school some distance away. The bridge conversation here often starts with whether the move is happening at all.

regions.name: Sharjah and Ajman
regions.note: Diploma provision is concentrated in a few schools. The Sharjah Private Education Authority approves curricula, programmes and assessment methods, so a sixth form cannot add a Diploma subject late because a cohort asked for it. Plan the subject conversation in term two of Year 11.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Private schools here are regulated by the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and the federal Ministry of Education in Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain. Students moving into the Diploma frequently do so at a school in another emirate, and online bridging is the practical way to prepare.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai schools where Year 11 feeds an in-house Diploma
schoolClusters.note: Where a school runs both an IGCSE programme and a Diploma sixth form, the subject teachers on both sides usually know each other, which makes the handover conversation possible. Ask the Year 11 teacher to speak to the DP1 teacher directly.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sixth forms taking IGCSE students
schoolClusters.note: Several capital schools admit external Year 11 students into a Diploma sixth form, which means a student arrives with no history at the school and a syllabus that started without them. The bridge matters most in this configuration.

schoolClusters.city: Northern emirates
schoolClusters.note: Fewer Diploma sixth forms, and smaller cohorts within them, so option blocks are tighter and a chosen Higher Level may not run. Establish what is available before the bridge is planned, because the bridge should cover the subjects the student will actually sit.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE to IB transition course actually has to fix
paragraphs: Three things change in this move and they are not equally difficult. The first is content, and it is the smallest. Specific gaps exist, they are known in advance, and each one is a few weeks of focused teaching: calculus in mathematics, uncertainty treatment in the sciences, unseen non-literary text in English. A list of those gaps can be written before a student has finished Year 11, which is what makes a summer bridge plannable.

The second change is assessment, and it is much larger. IGCSE is predominantly terminal: the papers decide the grade and revision is the lever. The Diploma puts a fifth to a quarter of each subject grade into internal assessment, which means a piece of work the student scopes, carries out and writes up over weeks, with no fixed question handed to them. A student who was excellent at IGCSE because they revised well has not yet demonstrated anything about this, and it will be a quarter of their result.

The third change is time management across a two-year arc with no public examination in the middle. Year 11 had a visible finish line and a teacher setting weekly deadlines. DP1 has an Extended Essay, two or three internal assessments and a Theory of Knowledge exhibition arriving in overlapping windows, with the school's internal deadlines being the only pressure. Students who are organised by habit cope; students who were organised by their teachers struggle, and it shows in February of DP1 rather than September.

A bridge that only covers content therefore fixes the easiest third of the problem. The useful version covers the content gaps in one or two subjects, introduces command terms and mark schemes early so that the new assessment language is familiar, and maps the DP1 year backwards from its deadlines so the student has seen the shape of it before they are inside it.
bullets: Content gaps: narrow, known in advance, a few weeks each
Assessment change: a quarter of the grade in work the student scopes themselves
Time management: overlapping deadlines with no public mid-point examination
A content-only bridge solves the smallest part of the move

sections.heading: Subject by subject: where IGCSE ends and DP1 begins
paragraphs: The transition map below is the most useful single object in this page. Each row names where an IGCSE course leaves a student, what the Diploma course assumes in its opening weeks, the specific gap between those two, and a realistic number of bridge weeks. The final column is an estimate from teaching experience rather than a published figure, and it assumes one session a week alongside normal school work.

Two rows deserve flagging before you read them. Mathematics has the widest gap in the Analysis route and a different, narrower gap in the Applications route, which is why the route decision and the bridge plan have to be made together rather than in sequence. And Biology has the smallest content gap of any subject while producing some of the most surprised students, because the overlap conceals a change in what is being assessed: application of named processes to unfamiliar data, under strict command-term discipline.

Where a row says the gap is a skill rather than a topic, that is a deliberate distinction. A topic gap closes by being taught. A skill gap closes by being practised, which takes longer and cannot be compressed into a holiday week however many hours are booked into it.

The bridge-weeks column also assumes the student is doing nothing else academic at the time, which is true in July and false in October. A gap estimated at six weeks over the summer is realistically a term's work once DP1 has started and five other subjects are competing for the same evenings. That is the real argument for running the bridge early: the same gap costs roughly twice as long to close once school is in session, and it is being closed while new content keeps arriving on top of it.

sections.heading: The bridge calendar, counted backwards from the first week of DP1
paragraphs: The whole argument of this page is in this table. DP1 begins in late August or early September in most UAE schools. Results arrive days or weeks before that. Every useful preparatory action therefore has to be taken before the information that would have informed it exists, which feels wrong and is simply how the calendar falls.

The practical answer is to plan from predicted grades and the Year 11 teachers' views, both of which are available in May or June, and to accept that the plan may need one adjustment in late August. That is a far better position than arriving at DP1 with a plan that has not been made yet. Families who treat the summer as a reward for IGCSEs rather than as the bridge lose the only uncommitted time in the two years either side of it.

The deadlines in the right-hand column are set by different people, and knowing which is which saves arguments. The school sets the option-form date, the internal level-change cut-off and the internal assessment deadlines. Cambridge and Pearson set the examination and entry dates for IGCSE, and those are published: Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with entries closing well ahead of it, and Cambridge's two series close their entries in the spring for June and mid-year for November. Neither board offers a UAE candidate a February sitting; Cambridge's February/March series is for India only. The IB sets the candidate registration date through the school. Nobody sets the summer bridge, which is why it does not happen unless a family decides it will.

sections.heading: What IGCSE grades predict about Higher Level, and what they do not
paragraphs: Families treat IGCSE grades as a readiness score for Higher Level and they are a weaker signal than that. A grade 8 or 9 says the student handled the content of a tiered two-year course accurately under examination conditions. Higher Level asks for something adjacent but different: sustained work on extension content that has no IGCSE equivalent, and an independent piece of assessed work the student scopes alone. Neither of those was tested.

What does predict well is narrower and more useful. How a student performed on the least structured questions in their IGCSE papers is informative, because unstructured extended questions are where Higher Level marks are won and lost. Whether they chose the extended or higher tier, and whether they took an additional mathematics qualification, says something about appetite as well as ability. And the Year 11 subject teacher's answer to the question of what this student does when they get stuck is better evidence than any grade, and costs nothing to obtain.

Board differences complicate the comparison in the UAE, where a single Diploma cohort will contain students from Cambridge and Pearson qualifications with different tiering conventions and different paper structures. Two students holding the same letter in the same subject from different boards have not necessarily demonstrated the same thing, and a sixth form admitting from several feeder schools knows this even when a parent comparing children in the same year group does not.

The practical conclusion is to treat a strong IGCSE grade as necessary rather than sufficient, and to generate the missing evidence directly. One session on a genuine piece of DP1 extension content, attempted without the method being given first, tells you more than a grade profile and takes an hour.
bullets: A high IGCSE grade shows accuracy on a tiered course, not readiness for extension content
Performance on the least structured questions is the predictive part
Cambridge and Pearson tiering differ, so the same letter is not the same evidence
One session on real DP1 extension content generates the evidence a grade cannot

sections.heading: The four components with no IGCSE equivalent
paragraphs: Internal assessment is the first and the largest. In most Diploma subjects a student scopes, carries out and writes up an independent piece of work worth a fifth to a quarter of the subject grade. Nothing at IGCSE resembles this. The common failure is not poor execution but poor scoping: a question too broad to answer within the limit, or an experiment whose data cannot support any conclusion. Both are fixable in planning and almost unfixable once the work is written.

The Extended Essay is the second. An independent research piece with a strict word limit, usually in a subject the student studies, chosen and managed by the student across DP1. The research is rarely the difficulty. The scoping and the self-managed timeline are, and students from an IGCSE background where every deadline was teacher-enforced find that genuinely hard rather than merely unfamiliar.

Theory of Knowledge is the third, and it is the one students enjoy once they stop looking for the right answer. It is assessed by an exhibition and an essay, and it rewards precise thinking about how knowledge claims are justified rather than accumulation of content. Its difficulty for an IGCSE student is that there is no syllabus to revise, which removes the strategy that got them through Year 11.

CAS is the fourth and is not graded, which is exactly why it gets neglected until it becomes an administrative problem in DP2. It has to be completed. The honest advice is to treat it as a fixed weekly commitment from September of DP1 rather than something to catch up on, because the catching up always collides with examinations.
bullets: Internal assessment: a quarter of the grade in a piece the student scopes alone
Extended Essay: the timeline and the scoping, not the research, are the difficulty
Theory of Knowledge: no syllabus to revise, which removes the IGCSE strategy
CAS: ungraded, therefore deferred, therefore a DP2 problem

sections.heading: Command terms, mark schemes and the language change nobody mentions
paragraphs: IGCSE and the Diploma both use command terms and they do not use them identically. A Diploma question that says evaluate is asking for something specific and marked against specific criteria, and a student who writes a strong IGCSE-style describe answer to it will lose most of the marks while believing the answer was good. This is the cheapest gap to close in the whole transition and the one least often addressed, because it reads as a study-skills point rather than a content one.

The fix is mechanical. Work through the command terms for each of the six subjects, with a real past-paper question for each and the mark scheme alongside it, and have the student write one answer per term rather than reading about them. Two or three sessions covers the terms that carry the most marks across a subject. Doing it in the summer, before the first DP1 assessment, is worth considerably more than doing it in February after two disappointing marks have already arrived.

There is a related constraint worth stating plainly. Boards publish past papers, mark schemes and subject guides, and the right way to use them is to reference and link the official source rather than to reproduce or redistribute it. Nobody should be supplying a student with a package of copied syllabus documents or mark schemes, and a tutoring service that offers downloads of board material is handling someone else's copyright. The official Cambridge, Pearson and IB sites are where those documents belong, and a school's subject teacher can point to the right version for the current syllabus cycle.
bullets: The same command term can carry different expectations at IGCSE and in the Diploma
One written answer per term with the mark scheme alongside, not a reading exercise
Two or three sessions covers the highest-value terms in a subject
Board material should be linked from the official site, never redistributed

sections.heading: Equivalency and attestation: the paperwork that follows the certificates
paragraphs: A student moving from IGCSE into the Diploma in the UAE accumulates certificates from two systems, and at the end of school those certificates have to satisfy the Ministry of Education's equivalency process if a UAE university place or certain employment routes are in view. This is a process the family completes with the authority, not something a school or a tutoring service performs on their behalf, and no provider should present it as a service they deliver or guarantee.

The British-track requirements are published and specific. A student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Alongside them the requirement names one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. For the American track, English proficiency is specified as a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying.

For the Diploma itself, this page publishes no figure. No Diploma points threshold has been read on a Ministry of Education source in the course of this project, and at least one ranking competitor page publishes an IGCSE subject count that disagrees with the Ministry's own published five. Check the current Diploma requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority directly, early rather than in the final term, because document attestation has its own lead time and the certificates come from two different boards.

sections.heading: The board dates that are published, and why entries close months early
paragraphs: One of the few genuinely useful things a transition page can do is show a family how far ahead of an examination its administration closes, because the same pattern governs the Diploma even though the Diploma's own dates are not reproduced here. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October.

Pearson's November 2026 series is the clearest worked example of the lead time, because the whole window is published: the papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026, entries closed well before that, and November 2025 results had reached students on 22 January 2026, which tells you when an autumn retake grade actually becomes a usable document. Cambridge's June series behaves the same way in a different part of the year - entries in the spring term, papers across May and June, results on Direct in August - and its November series closes entries mid-year for papers sat in October and November. In every case the entry closes months before the first paper, so a family that first thinks about a retake once DP1 has started is thinking about the series after the one they wanted.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May and June and in November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why any table on this subject should link the live official timetable rather than restating dates that can be revised. There is one further Cambridge administrative point worth knowing: every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, it is essential that the correct version of the timetable for that zone is used, and Cambridge states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable has been used.

process.title: Ask the Year 11 teachers before study leave ends
process.description: Two questions per subject: which part of this course does my child rely on being structured, and what would you want them to practise before DP1. Written down in May, those answers are the bridge plan. Asked in September, they are no longer available, because the teachers have moved on to a new cohort.

process.title: Pick one or two subjects, not six
process.description: A bridge covering everything covers nothing. We pick the subjects with the widest gap on the transition map, which for most UAE students means mathematics and one science or English. The topic list is written down before the first session and the block closes when the list is done.

process.title: A free trial on DP1 content, not IGCSE revision
process.description: One online session pitched at what the Diploma course assumes in week one, with the method not given first. It produces evidence about level readiness while the option form or the school's change window is still open, which a revision session cannot do.

process.title: Two sessions on command terms and mark schemes
process.description: Each of the six subjects uses command terms the student will be marked against from the first assessment. One written answer per high-value term, with the official mark scheme alongside, closes the cheapest gap in the whole transition before it costs a mark.

process.title: Map DP1 backwards before it starts
process.description: Extended Essay, internal assessments and the Theory of Knowledge exhibition arrive in overlapping windows set by the school. Putting them on one page in August, counted backwards from submission, is the single most effective piece of DP1 preparation that involves no subject content at all.

whyPoints.title: The bridge is planned from the calendar, not from results
whyPoints.description: Results reach UAE students days before DP1 starts, so a plan that waits for them has no summer left to run in. We build from predicted grades and the Year 11 teachers' views in May or June, then adjust once in August if the grades land differently.

whyPoints.title: The transition map is subject-specific, not generic
whyPoints.description: Each subject has a different gap and a different realistic number of weeks, and mathematics has two different gaps depending on the route chosen. A generic transition course that treats all six subjects as one problem spends most of its time where there is no gap.

whyPoints.title: Board dates quoted from the boards
whyPoints.description: The Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page come from their own published key-dates and timetable documents, with the series named. No IB examination or results date appears, because the IB's assessment pages block automated checking and an unverified date on a planning page misleads.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency described, never performed
whyPoints.description: The Ministry of Education sets what each track must show, and this page states the sourced British and American track requirements and sends you to moe.gov.ae for the Diploma figure. Equivalency is a process your family completes with the authority; no tutoring provider delivers or guarantees it.

whyPoints.title: Official board material linked, not redistributed
whyPoints.description: Past papers, mark schemes and subject guides belong on the Cambridge, Pearson and IB sites, and the current version for your child's syllabus cycle is the one their teacher can point to. A provider offering downloads of board documents is handling someone else's copyright.

whyPoints.title: Delivered online across the UAE
whyPoints.description: Teaching is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE, which is how a student in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain reaches a Diploma subject specialist for the exact subject and level they are about to start.

faqs.question: How long before DP1 should an IGCSE to IB bridge actually start?
faqs.answer: Six to eight weeks before the first DP1 lesson, which in most UAE schools means starting in early July. The reason is arithmetic rather than preference: results arrive in August, days before term, so a bridge that begins after results has almost no time to run. Plan it in May or June from predicted grades and the Year 11 teachers' views, run it through the summer, and adjust once in late August if the grades landed differently from expectation. Families who treat the summer as a reward for IGCSEs lose the only uncommitted weeks on either side of the move.

faqs.question: Which subjects need the most bridging work from IGCSE to the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Mathematics in the Analysis route and English A, for different reasons. The mathematics gap is both a topic gap, calculus, and a skill gap, by-hand fluency for the non-calculator paper, and it typically needs six to ten weeks. English A moves from accurate bounded response to sustained independent argument about unseen non-literary text, which is a skill and takes longer than a topic would. Physics and chemistry need four to eight weeks each, mostly on uncertainty treatment and mechanistic thinking. Biology looks like the easiest and surprises students, because a large content overlap hides a change in what is assessed.

faqs.question: Does a grade 9 at IGCSE mean my child is ready for Higher Level?
faqs.answer: It means they handled a tiered two-year course accurately under examination conditions, which is necessary and not sufficient. Higher Level adds extension content with no IGCSE equivalent and an independent piece of assessed work the student scopes alone, and neither of those was tested. The better evidence is how they performed on the least structured questions in their papers, whether they took an extended tier or an additional mathematics qualification, and what their Year 11 teacher says they do when they get stuck. One session on real extension content generates what the grade cannot.

faqs.question: What is the hardest part of moving from IGCSE to the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Not the content. It is internal assessment, which in most subjects puts a fifth to a quarter of the grade into a piece of work the student scopes, carries out and writes up with no set question. Nothing at IGCSE resembles that task, and the usual failure is scoping rather than execution: a question too broad for the word limit, or an experiment whose data cannot support a conclusion. The second hardest part is managing overlapping deadlines across two years with no public examination in the middle to mark progress.

faqs.question: Can my child retake an IGCSE while starting DP1?
faqs.answer: It is possible and it has a cost. A Cambridge November series or a Pearson November series retake sits in the middle of the first Diploma term, and Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so the result arrives mid-DP1. The examination preparation competes directly with early Diploma deadlines, including the Extended Essay question and the first internal assessments. Where a retake is genuinely needed, for example to meet a specified entry condition, plan it deliberately with the school and reduce something else. Confirm entry deadlines and the correct zone timetable with the examination centre.

faqs.question: Do Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE students face different gaps entering the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes, and UAE sixth forms see this constantly because they admit from both. The two boards tier and structure papers differently, so two students with the same letter in the same subject have not necessarily demonstrated the same thing. Pearson's modular options in some subjects produce a different examination experience from Cambridge's linear ones. In practice the differences matter less than the individual student's performance on unstructured questions, but they are a reason not to compare children across feeder schools and conclude anything from the letters alone.

faqs.question: Which of my child's IGCSE certificates will the Ministry of Education actually count?
faqs.answer: Five. The published British-track requirement names five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Alongside them a student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. At least one ranking tutoring page in this market publishes a different subject count. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority rather than from any tutoring site.

faqs.question: After switching to the Diploma, what points total will UAE attestation expect?
faqs.answer: Not one this page will state. No Diploma points threshold has been read on a Ministry of Education source during this project, and publishing an unsourced figure on a page families plan around would be worse than publishing none. The sourced requirements are the British track and the American track, both of which this page sets out in full. For the Diploma, check moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority directly, and start early, because document attestation has its own lead time and Diploma students may also hold IGCSE certificates needing separate handling.

faqs.question: What are command terms, and why do they catch IGCSE students out?
faqs.answer: They are the instruction words that tell a student what kind of answer earns marks: describe, explain, evaluate, justify, discuss. Both IGCSE and the Diploma use them, and they do not use them identically. A strong IGCSE-style description written in answer to a Diploma evaluate question loses most of the marks while feeling like a good answer. The fix is mechanical and cheap: one written answer per high-value term with the official mark scheme alongside, two or three sessions in total, done before the first DP1 assessment rather than after two poor marks.

faqs.question: Should we do the bridge in one intensive week or spread across the summer?
faqs.answer: Spread, for anything that is a skill rather than a topic. Topic gaps such as introductory calculus or statistical vocabulary respond reasonably well to concentrated teaching. Skill gaps such as by-hand algebraic fluency or sustained argument in English need repeated practice over weeks, because they are habits rather than knowledge, and an intensive week produces the feeling of progress without the habit. A workable shape is two or three sessions a week through July and August in one or two subjects, with practice between them.

faqs.question: My child is changing school as well as curriculum. Does that change the bridge?
faqs.answer: It widens it. A new school means new teachers who have no history with your child, a new option-block structure, and internal deadlines set by people you have not met. The content bridge is the same, but two additions help: get the names and dates of the new school's internal assessment deadlines in writing before term starts, and ask whether the sixth form expects any preparatory work over the summer. External entrants to a Diploma sixth form are the group for whom a bridge pays off most clearly, because nothing else is familiar.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay during the transition?
faqs.answer: With the scoping and the planning, yes, and within a clear boundary. A tutor may discuss whether a proposed question can be answered within the word limit, explain what the assessment criteria reward, teach the underlying subject content and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not supply text, hand over finished work or edit a draft to the point where it is no longer the student's. The essay is submitted with the student's declaration of authorship and a breach is handled as malpractice, with the consequence landing on the student.

faqs.question: Does the Diploma leave time for the mandatory UAE subjects?
faqs.answer: It has to, because they are required. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a DP1 student that means a week with very little slack. Counting those periods into the workload plan at option-form stage is what prevents a crisis in November.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE to IB bridge cost in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Market rates rather than a package price are the honest answer. Published figures in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors advertising IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, while Bestimate's Dubai 2026 table placed specialist support at AED 200 to 450 and above. A bounded summer block in one or two subjects is a defined number of sessions in that range rather than an open commitment. Those are market figures from the providers named; IB Gram's own numbers follow a free trial lesson and a consultation.

faqs.question: Is online bridging as useful as in-person for this move?
faqs.answer: For this particular job it has a structural advantage. The bridge needs a tutor who teaches the specific Diploma subject at the specific level your child is about to start, and that combination is scarce in the UAE outside Dubai and Abu Dhabi. Live video one-to-one puts a student in Fujairah, Ras Al Khaimah or Al Ain in front of that specialist rather than the nearest generalist. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service available only in India, and teaching here is online by design rather than by compromise.

igcse-to-ib-transition-course.closingHeading: Plan the bridge in June, not in September
igcse-to-ib-transition-course.closingBody: The summer between Year 11 and DP1 is the only uncommitted time in four years of school, and the calendar makes it impossible to plan with full information. Ask the Year 11 teachers two questions each before study leave ends. Pick the one or two subjects with the widest gap on the transition map. Run a bounded block through July and August, and put the DP1 deadlines on one page before term starts. A free trial lesson is online, one to one, and pitched at DP1 week-one content rather than IGCSE revision.

igcse-tuition.heroSubtitle: IGCSE tuition in the UAE is a scheduling problem before it is a teaching problem. Your child sits a dated series — Cambridge in June or November, Pearson Edexcel in May or June and November — and the entry that fixes that date closes months earlier. This page counts the year backwards from the first paper: what the month you start still buys, what the entry form locks shut, what results day opens and what it closes a fortnight later. Lessons are one-to-one and live online, timed to Gulf Standard Time around a UAE school day.

igcse-tuition.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE at both tiers. Each profile names the syllabus codes that person has actually taught and the series they have taken candidates through. Tell us the subject, the board and the date of the first paper, and we will say plainly who is free at your hour.

intro.heading: The date is already fixed. Everything else is still a choice.
paragraphs: An IGCSE course in the UAE ends on a day somebody else chose. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series. Pearson runs Edexcel International GCSE in May or June and again in November. Your child's school picked one of those, entered them for it, and most families find out by accident halfway through Year 11. Every useful decision about tuition sits downstream of that date: how many subjects, how many hours a week, which tier, whether to begin now or wait for the mock results in January.

So this page is organised around the calendar rather than around subjects. Each section answers one question with a date attached. When does the entry close? When does the tier stop being reversible? How many teaching weeks are left if you begin in February? When do results arrive, and what shuts fourteen days later? UAE families lose more marks to a closed window than to a weak topic, because a weak topic can be taught in four sessions and a closed entry cannot be reopened at any price.

The dates below come from the boards themselves. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series for UAE centres - its February/March series is offered to India only - so the year has two entry points, with June entries closing in the spring term and November entries mid-year, both months ahead of the papers and both earlier again at the school's internal cut-off. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026; its June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 and its November 2025 results on 22 January 2026. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after reading the wrong zone's timetable, which is why the first thing to confirm is a centre and a zone, not a tutor.

Verifiability is not the same across boards. Cambridge and Pearson publish their dates openly and revise them in public. We restate no IB examination or results date anywhere on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date here would be worse than no date at all. Where your child sits IB components alongside or instead of IGCSE, confirm every window with the school's programme coordinator and work from that.

Lessons from IB Gram are delivered one-to-one over live video. Nobody arrives at a UAE address; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. That is a deliberate trade rather than a limitation. A family in Khalifa City gets the tutor who has taught Cambridge Physics 0625 Extended through four series, instead of whoever happens to be free inside a twenty-minute drive at five in the afternoon. Working through a marked script on a shared screen is also better than working across a kitchen table, because both people are looking at the same line of the same answer at the same moment.

What this page will not do is quote you our hourly rate dressed up as market research. The AED figures here are market figures, each attributed to the provider that published it and read in October 2026. IB Gram's own commercial conversation happens after a trial lesson and after someone has read your child's last set of marks, which is the only point at which a number means anything.
bullets: Confirm three things before buying any hours: the board, the series and the centre's Cambridge zone.
