sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line between coaching and producing work
paragraphs: Internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay must be the candidate's own work. The IB treats breaches as malpractice, with consequences that fall on the student rather than on whoever supplied the help. In a market where some providers openly sell finished assessments, a family is entitled to know exactly where a tutor's involvement stops.

What a tutor may properly do is substantial. Teaching the subject content the assessment rests on. Discussing whether a research question is answerable with the data available. Explaining what each criterion descriptor is asking for in plain language. Reading a draft the student has written and saying which criterion is underserved and why. Teaching data handling, referencing conventions and academic style as skills.

What a tutor may not do is equally clear. No supplying text to be submitted. No rewriting a draft into its final form. No choosing the topic on the student's behalf. No supplying data the student has not gathered. No sitting beside a student during an assessed oral or a timed component. These boundaries are stated in every session where coursework is on the table, and they are the reason feedback is given against criteria rather than as corrections on a page.

Two related rules are worth knowing. Official syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are referenced and linked rather than reproduced and distributed, because reproducing them is a copyright matter. And no tutor should be described as an examiner for a board unless that status can be evidenced, nor should it ever be presented as access to marking or grade boundaries.

process.title: Diagnose with marked work, not a conversation
process.description: Send the most recent mock paper, the marked homework and the last report. A diagnostic built from real marked answers locates six or seven recoverable topics in an hour, which is more useful than a general discussion about how a subject feels.

process.title: Agree what the sessions are for
process.description: Content repair, timed paper technique and internal assessment coaching are three different programmes with different durations. Deciding which one a family is buying prevents the common outcome where sessions drift into homework supervision and the grade does not move.

process.title: Trial lesson before any commitment
process.description: One session with the matched tutor, after which the family decides. The thing to watch is whether your child speaks and holds the pen. A student who is silent after forty minutes is not matched yet, and that is worth finding out in week one rather than in March.

process.title: Fix the slot and the review point
process.description: A fixed weekly slot for the term, plus a named next assessment to measure against: a mock, a timed paper or an internal deadline. Progress is judged against that, not against a feeling, and the tutor changes if it is not moving by the second review.

process.title: Hand the independent plan to the student
process.description: The gap this page describes is closed by the student, not by the tutor. Each session ends with a written list of what is still insecure and what to practise before the next one, so the independent hours have a target rather than being filled with rereading.

whyPoints.title: The work outside class is the work we plan
whyPoints.description: Sessions are built around what a student must do alone: timed papers, mark scheme literacy, criterion work and the topics the scheme of work rushed. That is where a grade is actually decided, and it is the part no class of twenty can individually supervise.

whyPoints.title: Papers marked to the board's own scheme
whyPoints.description: Self-assessed practice teaches very little. Papers are marked against the official mark scheme and reviewed line by line, which is how a student learns where credit is awarded rather than guessing from a total.

whyPoints.title: Specialists rather than whoever is nearby
whyPoints.description: One causeway serves Al Marjan Island, and the local pool of Higher Level subject specialists willing to drive it weekly is tiny. Live video replaces geography with syllabus expertise, which is the whole point for a Diploma student.

whyPoints.title: Clear coursework boundaries, stated up front
whyPoints.description: Internal assessments and the Extended Essay remain the student's own work. Sessions give criterion feedback on drafts the student has written and never supply text, data or a finished product. That protects the student from a malpractice finding.

whyPoints.title: Written record after every session
whyPoints.description: Notes go out listing what was covered, what was set and what is not yet secure. A parent can see the picture without interrogating a teenager, and a replacement tutor can take over mid-term without restarting the diagnosis.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what IB Gram is
whyPoints.description: An independent tutor-matching platform with no premises in the UAE, no accreditation from the Department of Knowledge, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and no relationship with the schools named on this page.

faqs.question: How many hours a week outside class should an IGCSE student actually be working?
faqs.answer: In normal term time, budget forty to sixty minutes of independent work for every taught hour in each exam subject. For a Year 11 student with three or four periods a week in nine subjects, that is roughly three to four hours per subject across the week, and it rises steeply in the eight weeks before a terminal series. The figure is uncomfortable, which is why it is worth calculating in September rather than discovering in March. Homework alone does not reach it, because homework is set to be marked rather than to build retrieval.

faqs.question: The school says the syllabus is covered, so why is my daughter still short of her target?
faqs.answer: Because coverage and security are different measurements. A scheme of work delivers content at a single pace to a whole set, and every student is left with a residue: the topics taught in the week of a trip, the ones rushed before a holiday, the ones they were unwell for. A mock grade is best read as a map of six or seven recoverable topics rather than a verdict on the subject. A diagnostic built from the marked mock paper will locate them in about an hour, and most are repairable in a term.

faqs.question: Is a set of twenty too large for Higher Level Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Set size matters less than what is left to the student. A large set reduces individual attention and makes it harder for a teacher to notice that one student's multi-step calculations are drifting. A very small set, which is more common on this coast, brings the opposite risk: no second set to absorb students if staffing changes, and a thin practical programme. In both cases the fix is the same, and it is independent practice with real marking against the official scheme rather than a change of school.

faqs.question: Can my son move from Core to Extended IGCSE maths part-way through Year 10?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the question to ask is what content the Core set has not seen. Moving up means covering the extended material that was never taught, and doing it alongside the normal course. It is realistic early in Year 10 with consistent support and much harder by the spring. The honest advice depends on marked work rather than confidence: a student fluent on core topics and merely untested on harder ones can usually move, while one still slow on core arithmetic will do better securing a strong Core grade.

faqs.question: Which pieces of Diploma core work should be done before the DP1 summer holiday?
faqs.answer: A research question and a reading list for the Extended Essay, chosen topics for the science and maths internal assessments, and at least a first attempt at one internal assessment draft. Students who reach the summer with the core untouched spend the autumn of DP2 writing three pieces of assessed work in the same fortnight as their first serious revision. The school's own deadlines will be later than this; the point of working ahead of them is to buy two rounds of feedback rather than one.

faqs.question: How can a tutor support the Extended Essay without breaking the IB's rules?
faqs.answer: By teaching and giving feedback, never by producing text. A tutor can discuss whether a research question is answerable with the sources available, explain what each assessment criterion is asking for, teach referencing and academic style, and read a draft the student has written to say which criterion is underserved. A tutor must not choose the topic, supply passages for submission, rewrite a draft into its final state or provide data the student has not gathered. The essay must be the candidate's own work from first notes to final submission.

faqs.question: My son's mock came out two grades below his predicted grade. What does that usually mean?
faqs.answer: Most often it means technique rather than knowledge. Mocks are frequently sat on shortened papers under lighter conditions, so the real paper is the first time pacing, command-term reading and the discipline of attempting the final question are properly tested. Pacing is the single largest loss and the quickest to repair, usually in two to four weeks of timed papers with a mark-per-minute target. Insecure prerequisite topics take longer, six to twelve weeks, and the marked mock will show which of the two is actually the problem.

faqs.question: Do you teach students living on Al Marjan Island, and how are lessons delivered?
faqs.answer: Yes. Students across Ras Al Khaimah, including the island, are taught one-to-one over live video with shared screen working so a tutor can write and annotate while talking. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address, and home visits are a service offered only in India. The practical reason this matters here is the specialist pool: one causeway serves the island, and the number of Higher Level subject specialists willing to drive it weekly is very small, so matching on video widens the choice enormously.

faqs.question: What does IB and IGCSE tuition cost for a family on Al Marjan Island?
faqs.answer: No rate table has been published for Ras Al Khaimah, so the honest answer uses Dubai figures as a ceiling. Named providers publish AED 45-150 an hour for budget online tuition, AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 180-500 for in-home visits with travel priced in, and AED 200-450 or more for an IB or IGCSE specialist, with one premium provider at AED 650. Monthly packages of AED 799 online and AED 1,599-1,799 in-home have also been published. IB Gram quotes after a consultation.

faqs.question: Will a video lesson work from an apartment where the family is at home?
faqs.answer: It works with two adjustments that are worth making in the first week. Headphones, so the student can speak without feeling overheard, and a position where the screen is not visible from the main living area. A child who stops speaking has stopped having a one-to-one lesson, and that is a room problem rather than a technology problem. A wired connection or a seat near the router removes most of the remaining issues, since shared screen work is more demanding than video quality.

faqs.question: How do we find out which exam board our child has actually been entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for the entry statement, which lists each subject with its syllabus code. Cambridge codes look like 0580 or 0625; Pearson International GCSE codes look like 4MA1 or 4PH1. The code matters because the papers, the tiering and the practical arrangements differ between boards even where the subject name is identical. Bring it to a first session: past-paper practice drawn from the wrong board teaches the wrong structure, and it is a mistake that can run for a whole term unnoticed.

faqs.question: How many past papers should a Year 11 student complete before the June series?
faqs.answer: Eight to twelve full papers per subject, sat to time and marked against the official mark scheme rather than self-assessed. Schools typically manage two or three in class, which is enough to show students the format and nowhere near enough to build pace. The marking is the part that cannot be skipped: a student who marks their own paper generously learns nothing about how credit is awarded, and a student who marks it harshly learns only to be discouraged.

faqs.question: Should my daughter drop a subject to protect the others?
faqs.answer: Occasionally yes, and the decision should be made on evidence and timing rather than stress levels in the moment. For a British-track student, Ministry of Education equivalency requires five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, so the arithmetic of what can safely be dropped is checkable. Confirm the current requirement with the Ministry before acting, and discuss university prerequisites with the school, because a dropped subject can quietly close a degree route.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody covers my child's Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: You are told, rather than matched to the nearest approximation. Some Diploma combinations are genuinely thin: Higher Level Music, Film, certain second languages and some Group 3 options have few specialist teachers anywhere in the region. Where no specialist is available, the realistic options are a tutor who can support the transferable skills, such as essay structure or data analysis, with the subject content handled at school, or a wait until a specialist slot opens. Being told honestly is more useful than a mismatched match.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start in January of the exam year?
faqs.answer: No, but what is achievable narrows, and anyone who tells you otherwise is selling something. Starting in January leaves time to repair technique, to work through timed papers with real marking, and to target the specific topics where marks are being dropped. It does not leave time to rebuild two years of insecure foundations across several subjects. The sensible plan at that point is narrow and deliberate: one or two subjects, the components with the most recoverable marks, and no promises about a particular grade.

intro.heading: One district, four different tutoring conversations
paragraphs: Al Nakheel is the working centre of Ras Al Khaimah: the banks, the clinics, Al Naeem Mall, the older apartment blocks along the main roads and the villa streets behind them. It is also where most of the emirate's tuition centres sit, which is why families from Al Dhait, Khuzam, Al Qusaidat and the southern coast drive here. The district's defining feature for tutoring is not geography. It is the sheer mixture of curricula inside a small radius.

Four distinct households ask for help here, and they want different things. Apartment families on the Indian curriculum, often with children at the Indian School or Our Own English High School, usually ask about Year 9 or Year 10 and the step into IGCSE. Villa families at the British and IB campuses on the coast ask about Higher Level sciences and the Diploma core. Emirati and Arabic-speaking households ask about Arabic as a first language and Islamic Education running alongside an international programme. And a smaller group of families commuting to Sharjah or Dubai schools ask about scheduling before anything else.

Treating those as one market produces the thing that frustrates parents most: a tutor who is competent and is teaching the wrong course. A child on Cambridge Mathematics 0580 Extended and a child on Pearson 4MA1 are sitting different papers with different structures. A child moving from CBSE Class 9 into Year 10 IGCSE has a content map that overlaps only partly with the course they are entering. A child in MYP 5 has no past papers at all.

The second thing Al Nakheel families run into is the limit of the local pool. A general subject tutor is findable here. A Higher Level Chemistry specialist, an Economics internal assessment supervisor or an Analysis and Approaches teacher who has taught the exploration criteria is a different matter, and in the whole of the northern emirates there are very few. That is the structural argument for teaching over live video rather than a preference about technology.

The sections that follow do the work district by district: who lives here and what they request, the curriculum mix inside one postcode, how to establish which board your child is actually entered for, what the Indian-curriculum step into IGCSE really involves, what the market charges in AED, how the mandatory UAE subjects sit alongside an international programme, and what the Ministry of Education requires for equivalency. Tuition is delivered as one-to-one lessons over live video; IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address and offers home visits only in India.

One regulatory note that matters for every household here. Private schools in Ras Al Khaimah are regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. KHDA governs Dubai and ADEK governs Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, so guidance written for those emirates does not automatically apply in Al Nakheel.

ras-al-khaimah/al-nakheel.programmesIntro: Al Nakheel children are spread across more programmes than any other district in the emirate. The four below account for almost all local requests, and each has a different relationship with the exam that ends it.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Eight to ten subjects examined terminally. Cambridge runs June and November series with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October; Pearson runs May/June and November. Some subjects are tiered, and the entry tier chosen in Year 10 sets a grade ceiling before revision begins.
programmes.countryNote: The practical issue in Al Nakheel is that neighbouring children sit different boards. One campus enters Cambridge, another Pearson, and a few run a mixture by subject. Ask the school for the entry statement with syllabus codes rather than relying on the subject name, because past-paper practice from the wrong board teaches the wrong paper structure and the error can run undetected for a term.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internally assessed components contribute a substantial share of each subject grade, and terminal papers are sat in the May session at virtually every UAE school.
programmes.countryNote: Al Nakheel families mostly reach the Diploma by sending children to the coastal campuses rather than locally, which means a long school day before any tuition. Cohorts are small, so a Higher Level subject may run as a single set. Ask in September how many students are in each HL set: that number is the best available predictor of how much independent support the two years will need.

programmes.name: CBSE and Indian-curriculum schooling
programmes.description: A significant share of Al Nakheel children follow the Indian curriculum through the local Indian-curriculum campuses, with board examinations at Class 10 and Class 12. The assessment culture is different from IGCSE: more frequent internal testing, a different style of question, and a stronger emphasis on prescribed solutions.
programmes.countryNote: Families switching from this route into IGCSE or the Diploma are the most common transition case in Al Nakheel. The content overlap in mathematics and the sciences is high; the examination technique overlap is low. Students arrive able to solve problems and unused to command terms, extended written reasoning, and coursework they design themselves.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked out of eight and reported on a 1-7 scale. There is no external examination before the optional eAssessment, so progress is judged entirely from criterion descriptors and teacher judgement.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP reporting style confuses parents arriving from an examination-led system, which in Al Nakheel is most of them. A 5 looks reassuring. The useful question for the school is which of the four criteria that 5 is built from, because a student strong on knowledge and weak on communicating will struggle with Diploma paper answers while the single number says nothing is wrong.

ras-al-khaimah/al-nakheel.subjectsIntro: The requests from this district split along curriculum lines. Indian-curriculum families ask most about mathematics and the sciences at IGCSE entry; coastal IB families ask about Higher Level sciences and the Diploma core; Arabic-stream households ask about the mandatory subjects.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE)
subjects.description: The most requested subject in the district. Students arriving from an Indian-curriculum background are usually fluent in procedure and unfamiliar with the way marks are awarded for method and for interpreting a worded problem. The tier decision in Year 10 matters more than any single topic.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism stall most IGCSE students. The practical and uncertainty strand is rarely taught explicitly and carries real marks. Pearson and Cambridge handle the practical component differently, which is one of the clearest reasons to check the code before starting.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry are the gateway: a student insecure there loses marks across energetics, equilibria and electrochemistry regardless of how well those topics were taught. Organic mechanisms reward precision in drawing rather than recall.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: The highest content volume of the sciences. Extended-response marks go to named mechanisms and exact terminology, so students who revise by rereading plateau around the middle grades. Data-handling questions are the other reliable loss.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof and calculus route. Higher Level adds complex numbers and vectors. Marks are lost in unstructured later questions where the topic is recognised but no method is prompted, and in the exploration where the mathematics is fine and the reflection is thin.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the three internal assessment commentaries decide most grades. Evaluation that does not refer back to the diagram just drawn stops earning marks at the top band. Al Nakheel students often take this subject in a set of three or four.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study command terms do most of the work. Answering 'evaluate' as if it were 'describe' loses the top band without anything being factually wrong. The Higher Level research project needs a real organisation and a tightly bounded question.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Reading at speed and the summary task separate the grades. Register control earns more than vocabulary range in the writing papers. The speaking endorsement arrangements differ between the 0510 and 0511 variants, so the code on the entry form matters.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language
subjects.description: Mandatory for Arab students in UAE private schools, taught in Standard Arabic and assessed to the Ministry's prescribed content. Schools are required to run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ.

subjects.name: Islamic Education
subjects.description: Required in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. Standard Arabic is the language of instruction for Arab students, while non-Arab students are taught in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Teachers of the subject need the relevant authority's approval to teach it.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode discipline and trace tables account for a large share of IGCSE marks. The Higher Level internal assessment needs a genuine client and a bounded problem; students who code before scoping lose criterion marks that are hard to recover.

ras-al-khaimah/al-nakheel.regionsIntro: Families taught from this part of the emirate come from the city districts around Al Nakheel and from the coastal communities whose children often cross the city for school or tuition. The notes record the local detail that changes a plan.

regions.note: Older established districts next to the creek, largely Indian, Egyptian and Emirati households. School days tend to finish earlier here, which opens late-afternoon tutoring slots that coastal families cannot use.

regions.name: Khuzam
regions.note: Residential district south of the centre with a RAK Academy campus. A mix of villas and apartment blocks, and the usual school destination for families living in and around Al Nakheel who want a British or IB route.

sections.heading: Who lives in Al Nakheel, and what each household actually asks for
paragraphs: The requests that arrive from this district sort cleanly into four groups, and knowing which one a family belongs to answers most of the early questions before they are asked. The largest group is Indian-curriculum apartment households, usually with children at the Indian School or Our Own, and their question is almost always about the move into IGCSE or about Class 10 mathematics and science.

The second group is villa families on the British and IB routes, whose children travel out to the coastal campuses. Their requests arrive later in a child's schooling and are more specific: Higher Level Chemistry, Analysis and Approaches, an Economics internal assessment, a Theory of Knowledge essay. These are the families most likely to find the local pool unable to help, because a general tutor cannot supervise a Diploma internal assessment.

The third group is Emirati and Arabic-speaking households with children in international programmes, asking about Arabic as a first language and Islamic Education running in parallel with an English-medium curriculum. These are mandatory subjects, prescribed in content, and a tutor has to work inside the school's own scheme rather than importing material.

The fourth and smallest group commutes out of the emirate for school, to Sharjah, Ajman or occasionally Dubai. For them the subject is almost a secondary question: the first constraint is that a child is not home until early evening, and anything booked before that will fail. The table sets out the four with what each typically needs.

sections.heading: Four curricula inside one postcode, and why that matters
paragraphs: The UAE private school market runs seventeen different curricula, and Ras Al Khaimah's city centre carries an unusually dense slice of that variety for its size. Within a few kilometres of Al Nakheel a child may be sitting Cambridge IGCSE, Pearson International GCSE, an Indian board examination, the IB Middle Years Programme or the Diploma, alongside the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education strands that apply regardless of the licensed curriculum.

For a parent this creates a specific problem that does not exist in a single-system city. Advice from a neighbour is frequently about a different qualification. A recommended tutor may be excellent and may have never taught the board your child is entered for. Published guidance online is overwhelmingly written for Dubai under KHDA, and the regulator here is the emirate's own Department of Knowledge, which approves curricula, programmes, courses, activities, assessment methods and fees.

For a tutor it creates a matching problem that has to be solved before the first lesson rather than during it. The subject name is not enough. Mathematics could mean Cambridge 0580 at Core tier, 0580 at Extended, Pearson 4MA1, a Class 10 board syllabus, MYP mathematics assessed against four criteria, or Diploma Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. These are six different courses.

The federal position underneath all of this is worth knowing: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That single rule is why a child on a British or IB route in Al Nakheel still has mandatory subjects on the timetable.

sections.heading: Establishing which board your child is actually entered for
paragraphs: This is the first question asked of any new IGCSE family in Al Nakheel, and a surprising number of parents cannot answer it. The school knows, and the document that states it is the entry statement, which lists each subject with its syllabus code. Cambridge codes are four digits, such as 0580 for Mathematics or 0625 for Physics. Pearson International GCSE codes begin with a digit and letters, such as 4MA1 or 4PH1.

The codes are not cosmetic. The two boards structure papers differently, assess practical science differently, and tier different subjects. Cambridge publishes separate Core and Extended papers in several subjects; Pearson's structure differs. A student who has spent a term on Cambridge past papers for a Pearson entry has practised the wrong paper, and will discover it in a mock at the point when there is least time to adjust.

There is a further operational detail from Cambridge worth knowing in this emirate. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask the school which zone its centre sits in before building any revision plan around published dates.

sections.heading: The Indian-curriculum step into IGCSE and the Diploma
paragraphs: This is the single most common transition in Al Nakheel, and it is consistently misdiagnosed. Families expect the difficulty to be content, and it rarely is. A student arriving from Class 9 into Year 10 IGCSE mathematics has usually met most of the topics and often met them in more procedural depth. What they have not met is the way marks are awarded.

Three specific habits have to change. First, command terms: an IGCSE or Diploma paper asks the student to state, describe, explain, compare or evaluate, and each of those wants a different quantity and type of response. Second, method credit: showing working earns marks even where the final answer is wrong, which is not how every system treats it. Third, worded problems, where the mathematics is straightforward once the question has been translated and the translation is the assessed skill.

The science transition adds a fourth: practical and data-handling questions that expect precise language about variables, uncertainty and reliability. These are rarely taught explicitly in any system, and a student who can perform an experiment may still not be able to write about one in the way a mark scheme credits.

Going the other way, from IGCSE into the Diploma, the shock is different again: internally assessed work the student designs themselves, a 4,000-word Extended Essay with a supervisor rather than a teacher, and Theory of Knowledge, which has no content to revise. sections.heading: What tutoring costs in and around Al Nakheel
paragraphs: Al Nakheel has more tuition provision than the rest of the emirate combined, which makes price comparison easier here than anywhere else in Ras Al Khaimah and also more confusing, because group classes and one-to-one hours are quoted in the same conversation. No published rate table exists for this emirate. Every AED figure in circulation comes from a Dubai source, so the bands below carry the provider that publishes them and should be read as a ceiling.

The format matters more than the headline rate. A group class at a centre is cheaper per hour and divides the teacher's attention by the number of students; a one-to-one hour is dearer and is entirely the student's. Neither is automatically better value. A confident student who needs structured revision does well in a group; a student with specific topic gaps or an internal assessment to design does not.

In-home visits carry a travel premium that is real and is mostly the car journey rather than the teaching. That premium rises with distance from the city centre, which is why the published in-home bands sit above the online ones for the same calibre of teacher. For families in the outlying districts it is the dominant cost.

IB Gram does not publish a fixed hourly rate on these pages. The honest figure depends on subject, level and frequency. A consultation establishes the plan, a trial lesson tests the match, and a quote follows. For wider context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for 2026-27 under the emirate's second economic incentives package; fee policy is set emirate by emirate, so confirm the local position with your school.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies alongside an international programme
paragraphs: Every child in a UAE private school carries mandatory subjects regardless of which international curriculum the school is licensed to teach. The federal position is explicit: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. In Al Nakheel, where households run across four curricula, this is the one timetable element every family shares.

The clearest published statement of how this works in practice comes from KHDA's mandatory subjects guidelines for Dubai schools, and the structure it describes is instructive even though Dubai is a different emirate. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ.

The language rules follow from that. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. Social Studies is taught in Arabic for Arab students. Non-Arab students take Islamic Education and the moral, social and cultural studies strand in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Schools must also ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the relevant authority's approval to teach those subjects.

For tutoring there is one firm constraint. Using different or additional content for these subjects without prior Ministry permission is prohibited, so support has to work inside the school's own prescribed scheme rather than importing material from elsewhere. That makes these sessions unlike any other subject: the task is fluency and confidence within a fixed syllabus, not enrichment around it.

sections.heading: A tutor near Al Nakheel is not the same as a tutor for your subject
paragraphs: Searching for a tutor by location is a reasonable instinct and a poor filter. The pool within driving distance of Al Nakheel is mostly generalist: capable teachers who can support mathematics or science across a range of ages, which is exactly right for a Year 8 student and insufficient for a Diploma candidate who needs someone who has supervised an Economics commentary or marked an Analysis and Approaches exploration.

The scarcity is structural rather than a comment on anyone local. Ras Al Khaimah has a small private-school set, so there are few Higher Level sets, which means few teachers with Higher Level experience, which means a tiny pool of people who could tutor it even in principle. The same holds in Fujairah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain. Across the whole northern belt a student sitting a less common Diploma subject may have no local specialist at all.

That is the argument for live video, and it is a supply argument rather than a claim about teaching quality. Matching on syllabus instead of geography changes the pool from whoever is within a twenty-minute drive to anyone who teaches that course. For a Year 8 maths student the difference is marginal. For a Higher Level Chemistry candidate it is the entire question.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Tuition for Al Nakheel families is delivered one-to-one over live video with shared screen working; home visits are a service offered only in India. Where no specialist covers a subject, a family is told that rather than matched to an approximation, because a mismatched tutor costs a term before anyone admits it.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency and the route into UAE universities
paragraphs: A qualification earned at a private school in Ras Al Khaimah needs an equivalency certificate from the Ministry of Education before it can be used for admission to UAE universities or for many government processes. This is one of the least covered topics in the local tutoring market and one of the most consequential, because the requirements shape subject choices made two years earlier.

On the British track the published requirements are specific. A student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which is a detail at least one ranking competitor publishes incorrectly as six subjects.

On the American track the requirements are different in kind. English proficiency is shown by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB there is no points threshold published in the source read for this page, so no IB figure is quoted here: confirm it on the Ministry's own site or with the emirate attestation authority.

Two cautions. Equivalency is a process the family completes with the Ministry; it is not something a tutoring platform performs, guarantees or expedites, and nobody should imply otherwise. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, admission or progression. The table summarises what each track must show and where to verify it.

process.title: Name the board and the level first
process.description: Send the entry statement with syllabus codes, or the school's subject list if entries have not been made yet. Cambridge 0580 Extended, Pearson 4MA1 and Diploma Analysis and Approaches are three different courses, and matching on the subject name alone is how a term gets wasted.

process.title: Send marked work, not a description
process.description: The most recent mock paper, a marked homework and the last report. A diagnostic built from real marked answers identifies the specific topics and techniques losing marks, which is more useful than a conversation about how the subject feels at home.

process.title: Pick a slot that matches the school day
process.description: City school days in Al Nakheel finish earlier than on the coast, so late-afternoon slots that fail for a coastal family often work here. Families commuting to Sharjah or Dubai need an evening slot. Fixing the right one at the start is what keeps the arrangement alive past November.

process.title: Trial lesson, then decide
process.description: One session with the matched tutor before any term commitment. Watch whether your child speaks and whether the tutor can describe the paper structure in the first ten minutes. A tutor who cannot is a generalist being asked to do a specialist's job.

process.title: Review against the next real assessment
process.description: Progress is measured against a named upcoming assessment: a mock, a timed paper, an internal deadline. If it is not moving by the second review point, the match changes rather than the student being told to try harder.

whyPoints.title: Board-specific matching, every time
whyPoints.description: A tutor is matched to the syllabus code on the entry statement rather than to a subject name. In a district where neighbouring children sit Cambridge, Pearson, an Indian board and the IB, that single step prevents the most common and most expensive mismatch.

whyPoints.title: Transition work treated as its own job
whyPoints.description: Moving from an Indian-curriculum classroom into IGCSE, or from IGCSE into the Diploma, is a technique problem rather than a content problem. Those blocks are scoped with an end point and target command terms, method credit and self-designed coursework explicitly.

whyPoints.title: Access to specialists the district does not have
whyPoints.description: There are very few Higher Level sets anywhere in the northern emirates, so there are very few teachers with Higher Level experience. Matching over live video changes the pool from whoever is nearby to anyone who teaches the course your child sits.

whyPoints.title: Mandatory subjects handled inside the rules
whyPoints.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and the social and moral studies strand are supported using the school's own prescribed scheme, because different or additional content for these subjects requires Ministry permission. Streams are kept separate as the published rules require.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency explained, never performed
whyPoints.description: The Ministry of Education requirements are set out with the figures that are actually published, including the five-subject British-track rule and the exclusion of Arabic and Islamic education. The process belongs to the family and the Ministry, and no IB points figure is quoted without an official source.

whyPoints.description: An independent tutor-matching platform. No premises in the UAE, no accreditation from the Department of Knowledge, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no relationship with any school named on this page.

faqs.question: Which schools do children living in Al Nakheel usually attend?
faqs.answer: Most attend the city-centre campuses: the Indian School Ras Al Khaimah, Our Own English High School, Scholars Indian School and Little Flower English School are the main Indian-curriculum and British options within a short drive. Families wanting an IB continuum route generally travel out to the RAK Academy campuses at Al Hamra and Khuzam, or to RAK English Speaking School. A minority commute to Sharjah, Ajman or Umm Al Quwain for a particular subject combination. Those schools are named as local context only; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: We are moving our son from the Indian curriculum into Year 10 IGCSE. How big is the jump?
faqs.answer: Smaller in content than most families fear and larger in technique. Students arriving from Class 9 have usually met most IGCSE mathematics and science topics, often with more procedural practice. What is new is how marks are awarded: command terms that each demand a different depth of answer, credit for showing method even when the final answer is wrong, and worded problems where translating the question is the assessed skill. One term at two sessions a week closes it for most students, concentrated on past-paper technique rather than new content.

faqs.question: Is there an IB World School inside Al Nakheel itself?
faqs.answer: The IB provision in this emirate sits on the southern coast rather than in the city centre, principally at the RAK Academy campuses at Al Hamra, with a further campus at Khuzam. Families living in Al Nakheel who want an IB route are therefore making a daily journey out and back, which is why a tuition slot for those households sits later in the evening than for a child at a city-centre school. Check current programme authorisation with the school and with the emirate's Department of Knowledge before enrolling.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my daughter sits Cambridge or Pearson papers?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's examinations officer for the entry statement, which lists every subject with its syllabus code. Cambridge codes are four digits, such as 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics or 0620 Chemistry. Pearson International GCSE codes combine digits and letters, such as 4MA1 or 4PH1. The distinction matters because the boards structure papers differently, assess practical science differently and tier different subjects, so a term of practice on the wrong board's past papers trains the wrong exam.

faqs.question: Does my child still study Arabic at a British curriculum school in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Yes. The federal rule is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. So a child on a British or IB programme still carries those subjects. KHDA's published guidelines for Dubai set out the structure most clearly: separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups, Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Arabic as a first language, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arab students in some strands.

faqs.question: Will a UAE university accept IGCSEs and A-Levels taken in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: They are recognised qualifications, but admission usually requires a Ministry of Education equivalency certificate rather than the certificates alone. On the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at E. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. Verify the current wording with the Ministry, since the figures are updated, and treat equivalency as a process your family completes directly rather than something a tutor arranges.

faqs.question: If we drop a subject in Year 11, does that put equivalency at risk?
faqs.answer: No. The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are explicitly not included among those five. This matters when a family is deciding whether a subject can safely be dropped, because the arithmetic changes depending on what counts. At least one competitor page in this market publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong. Confirm the current rule on the Ministry's own site before making a decision.

faqs.question: How much do IB and IGCSE tutors charge around Al Nakheel?
faqs.answer: No rate table has been published for Ras Al Khaimah, so the available figures are Dubai ones and should be read as a ceiling. Named providers publish AED 45-150 an hour for budget online tuition, AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 180-500 for in-home visits where travel is priced into the fee, and AED 200-450 or more for an IB or IGCSE specialist, with one premium provider at AED 650. Centre group classes are usually quoted per course rather than per hour. IB Gram quotes after a consultation.

faqs.question: There are tuition centres in Al Nakheel. How do they compare with one-to-one?
faqs.answer: They solve different problems. A centre group class is cheaper per hour, provides structure and works well for a confident student who needs a revision timetable imposed. The teacher's attention is divided by the size of the group, so a student with specific topic gaps, an internal assessment to design or a technique problem gets less from it. One-to-one costs more per hour and is entirely the student's. Many families use both: a centre for structured revision, one-to-one for the subject that is actually failing.

faqs.question: Can live video lessons work in a busy Al Nakheel apartment?
faqs.answer: Yes, with two adjustments worth making in the first week. Headphones, so the student will speak freely rather than go quiet with family within earshot, and a seat where the screen is not visible from the main living area. A student who stops talking has stopped having a one-to-one lesson, and that is a room problem rather than a technology one. A wired connection or a position near the router handles the rest, since shared screen working is more demanding than video quality.

faqs.question: My daughter is one of four students taking Economics at Higher Level. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It has two effects worth planning for. A very small set gets more teacher attention, which is genuinely good. It also means no second set to absorb students if staffing changes mid-year, fewer peers to compare work against, and less classroom discussion to sharpen evaluation, which is where Economics marks are won. For the internal assessment commentaries it also means a supervisor spread across several different topics. Independent practice with marked work against the official scheme is the practical answer rather than moving school.

faqs.question: Which subjects do Al Nakheel families ask about most often?
faqs.answer: Mathematics first by a wide margin, at both IGCSE tiers and in both Diploma routes. Then the sciences, with Physics requested most for electricity and electromagnetism and Chemistry for moles and organic mechanisms. Economics and Business Management follow at Diploma level, usually because of the internal assessment rather than the content. English as a Second Language is requested steadily across the district. Arabic as a first language and Islamic Education come mainly from Arabic-speaking households whose children are in English-medium programmes.

faqs.question: How is Islamic Education assessed if my child is in an English-medium programme?
faqs.answer: It is a school-assessed subject taught to the Ministry's prescribed content, not an external examination like IGCSE. KHDA's published Dubai guidelines describe the structure clearly: separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for the Arab stream, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for the non-Arab stream. Schools must ensure teachers of the subject hold the relevant authority's approval. Because the content is prescribed, tutoring has to work within the school's own scheme rather than importing other material.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor be matched for a student living in Al Nakheel?
faqs.answer: For mathematics, the sciences, English and the common Diploma subjects, matching is usually quick because the pool teaching those syllabuses is large once geography is removed from the filter. For a less common Higher Level subject it can take longer, and occasionally no specialist is available at all. In that case you are told rather than matched to an approximation. The information that speeds everything up is the syllabus code, the level and the specific topics the last marked paper flagged.

faqs.question: Would it help to have a tutor who speaks our home language?
faqs.answer: For most subjects it makes little difference to the outcome, because the examination is in English and the technique being taught is in English. It helps in two situations. For a younger child still building English fluency, a shared home language speeds up explanation of a concept before it is practised in English. And for Arabic as a first language or Islamic Education, the language of instruction is Standard Arabic for Arab students, so a tutor working in that stream has to teach in it.

Send the syllabus code from the entry statement, the last marked paper, and the time your child is actually home. We will match a tutor who teaches that exact course, arrange a trial lesson before any commitment, and tell you honestly if the specialist you need is not available. ras-al-khaimah/al-qusaidat.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the IB Diploma, the Middle Years Programme and both main IGCSE boards. Before a first paid lesson, any individual tutor should be able to show their MoHRE private tuition work permit and name the syllabus code they will be teaching to.

intro.heading: The crossing decides the hour, and verification decides the tutor
paragraphs: Al Qusaidat sits north of the Ras Al Khaimah creek, an established residential district of older villas and low-rise apartment blocks, with a largely Indian, Egyptian and Emirati population and several generations of settled families. Children here attend the city-centre campuses across the water, the Khuzam campus inland, or in a smaller number of cases the coastal schools at Al Hamra, which is the longest run available inside the emirate.

The crossing is the fact that governs an afternoon in this district. Everything south of the creek is reached by one of the bridge routes, and at school-run times that is a constraint rather than a formality. A journey that takes twelve minutes at ten in the morning takes considerably longer between half past one and three, which is precisely when children are being collected. Families here do not need a lecture about traffic; what they need is an honest statement of which session times actually survive it.

The second thing that shapes tutoring here is less visible and more important. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. Most parents have never seen one, do not know it is free, do not know how long it lasts, and have no idea whether the person teaching their child in a weekly session holds it. That is a gap the market has been content to leave open.

It matters for a reason beyond compliance. The same market that leaves the permit question unanswered also contains providers selling finished coursework, self-published star ratings nobody can audit, promises about specific grades, and UAE-facing websites whose only contact route is a foreign phone number. A family in Al Qusaidat comparing options online has no obvious way to tell a legitimate teacher from a liability.

So this page does two jobs. It works through the practical timing of a session from this side of the creek, including prayer times and the northern school day, and it sets out how to verify a tutor properly: what permit applies to which category of person, what to ask in the first ten minutes of a trial lesson, which market practices are genuine warning signs, and what a tutoring service should be telling you about your child's personal data. Tuition for Al Qusaidat families is delivered as one-to-one lessons over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service offered only in India.

One orientation point. Private schools in Ras Al Khaimah are regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Tutoring permits are a separate federal matter handled by MoHRE, and the two should not be confused: no tutoring platform, including this one, holds an education regulator's accreditation.
bullets: One creek crossing governs the afternoon for most of this district
The MoHRE private tuition work permit is free and lasts two years
Most parents have never been shown a tutor's permit
School regulation and tutoring permits are two separate systems
Lessons are one-to-one over live video, not in person

ras-al-khaimah/al-qusaidat.programmesIntro: Al Qusaidat households span the Indian curriculum, the British route and the IB, so the verification question applies across three different sets of qualifications. The programmes below are the ones that appear in this district.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Eight to ten subjects examined terminally, with Cambridge running June and November series and Pearson running May/June and November. Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers, and tiered entries in some subjects cap the available grade.
programmes.countryNote: When checking whether a tutor is right for an IGCSE student in this district, the useful test is specific rather than general. Ask which board, which syllabus code and how the practical component is assessed for that code. A tutor who answers in generalities about the subject has probably not taught the paper, whatever their qualifications say.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internally assessed work carries a real share of each subject grade and is marked against published criteria before moderation.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma is where the integrity question becomes concrete. Internally assessed work must be the student's own, and providers that offer to supply finished pieces are creating a malpractice exposure that falls on the student rather than on them. A legitimate tutor explains criteria and gives feedback on the student's own drafts, and says so without being asked.

programmes.name: CBSE and Indian-curriculum schooling
programmes.description: A substantial share of children in this district follow the Indian curriculum at the city-centre campuses, with board examinations at Class 10 and Class 12 and a more frequent internal testing cycle than IGCSE.
programmes.countryNote: Families on this route are the most likely in the emirate to be offered informal tutoring arrangements through community networks, which are often excellent and are also where the permit question is least likely to be asked. The permit applies regardless of how the arrangement was found, and asking for it is normal rather than impolite.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria marked out of eight and reported on a 1-7 scale, with no external paper before the optional eAssessment.
programmes.countryNote: Because there is no exam mark, an MYP parent has less independent evidence than at any other stage, which makes a tutor's claims harder to test. The practical substitute is to ask the tutor to name the four criteria in the subject and say which one the student is weakest against. A tutor who cannot do that is not working from the assessment framework.

ras-al-khaimah/al-qusaidat.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones requested most from the northern districts, listed with the specific detail a parent can use to test whether a prospective tutor actually knows the course.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE)
subjects.description: Ask which tier the student is entered for and what the grade ceiling is on the lower tier. A tutor who does not raise the tier question within the first conversation has not thought about the entry, which is the decision that caps the outcome.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Ask how the practical component is assessed for that specific code, since Cambridge and Pearson route it differently. Electricity and electromagnetism are the usual IGCSE blockers, and the uncertainty strand is the fastest available recovery.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Ask what gates the rest of the course. The right answer is moles and stoichiometry: a student insecure there loses marks across energetics, rates and electrochemistry regardless of how those topics were taught.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: Ask why students who revise by rereading plateau in the middle bands. Extended-response marks go to named mechanisms and exact terminology, and a tutor who talks about content volume without mentioning terminology has missed the mark allocation.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Ask which criteria the exploration is marked against and which ones students lose. Personal engagement and reflection are the usual answers; a tutor who only discusses the mathematics is not equipped for the internal assessment.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Ask how much of the course assumes the graphic display calculator. A real share of lost marks are calculator operation errors in statistical tests, and a tutor who has taught the course will say so unprompted.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Ask the difference between the 0510 and 0511 variants. The speaking endorsement arrangements differ, and a tutor who does not know which one the student is entered for cannot prepare them for it.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.description: Ask what Paper 1 actually is. Unseen textual analysis under time pressure rewards a repeatable paragraph structure, and the Individual Oral needs a tightly scoped global issue rather than a broad theme.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Ask how many internal assessment commentaries are required and what they are marked on. Diagram accuracy and evaluation anchored to the diagram decide most grades, and a tutor should be able to say that in one sentence.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language
subjects.description: Mandatory for Arab students in UAE private schools, taught in Standard Arabic to prescribed content. Schools must ensure teachers of Arabic hold the relevant authority's approval, which is a separate credential from a tutoring permit.

subjects.name: Islamic Education
subjects.description: Required regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate streams and different languages of instruction. Content is prescribed, so support works within the school's own scheme rather than importing material.

sections.heading: What the creek crossing does to an afternoon
paragraphs: Al Qusaidat sits on the wrong side of the water from almost every school its children attend. That is not a complaint about infrastructure; it is a fixed planning constraint, and the families here who get tutoring to work are the ones who plan around it rather than hoping it will not matter on a given Tuesday.

The arithmetic is straightforward. A crossing that is a few minutes at midday absorbs significantly more between half past one and three, when the school runs for every campus on the southern side are happening at once. A parent collecting a child from a city-centre school is therefore back in Al Qusaidat somewhere between a quarter past two and three o'clock, later if there are two schools involved. A second crossing to reach a tuition centre later the same afternoon means the same traffic twice more.

The consequence for scheduling is a narrower usable window than families in Khuzam or Al Nakheel have. Mid-afternoon sessions, which work well for primary children living close to their school, are much less reliable here because the child may still be in the car. Early-evening slots work. Late-evening slots work for secondary students. The window in practice runs from around five o'clock to a quarter to nine.

The version of this that actually ends arrangements is the tuition-centre drive. A family who books a centre in Al Nakheel for two afternoons a week is committing to four crossings a week at the worst possible times, on top of the school runs. It is sustainable in September and it is typically abandoned by November, which is why removing the journey is the most useful thing a format can do in this district.

sections.heading: Session timing around prayer times and the northern school day
paragraphs: Prayer times move through the year, and in a district with a large Emirati and Arab population they are a real scheduling input rather than an afterthought. The two that interact with tutoring are Asr, which falls in the late afternoon, and Maghrib at sunset, which in the UAE moves across roughly an hour and a half between the shortest and longest days.

The practical approach families here use is to anchor the session to a prayer rather than to a clock time. A slot agreed as starting after Maghrib stays correct all year without renegotiation, where a slot fixed at 18:15 drifts into the wrong part of the evening by December. Tutors matched for this district are told which anchor applies so the booking reflects it.

The northern school day adds its own pattern. City-side campuses finish earlier than the coastal ones, so a northern child at a city-centre school may be home earlier than a Khuzam child at a coastal school, despite the crossing. That is worth checking rather than assuming: the useful number is not the distance but the time the child actually walks through the door, measured over a normal week rather than on a quiet day.

The third column is the honest one: several of the windows that look available on a calendar are not available in practice, and booking them is how a family ends up with a cancelled slot and the impression that tutoring does not work for them.

sections.heading: How to verify that a tutor is legally permitted to teach here
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are deliberately broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18.

Two facts in that paragraph are worth repeating because they are routinely misstated. It costs nothing, so anyone telling you a permit fee needs to be passed on is wrong. And it covers a wide range of people, so a tutor being a university student rather than a schoolteacher is not in itself a compliance problem, though it is a relevant fact about what they can teach.

The application route is MoHRE's own service, listed as 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days and no fees listed. Anyone providing private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any specific amount quoted to you as the penalty is somebody's invention.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: in Dubai that requires a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and no regulator accreditation, and should never be described as holding one. The table below is the parent's version of all of this.

sections.heading: What to ask in the first ten minutes of a trial lesson
paragraphs: Qualifications on paper and competence in a specific paper are different things, and the trial lesson is where the gap becomes visible if anyone is watching for it. Ten minutes of specific questions tells a parent more than a page of credentials, because a tutor who has actually taught the course answers them instantly and one who has not answers them generally.

The questions are all of the same type: specific to the syllabus code, not to the subject. Which paper carries the practical component for this code. How many marks is the internal assessment worth and against which criteria. What is the difference between the two tiers in this subject. Which topic in this syllabus do students most commonly lose marks on, and why. A tutor fluent in the course has a fast, concrete answer to every one.

There are two further signals worth noticing, and neither is about knowledge. Does the tutor get the student talking, or do they lecture for forty minutes? A one-to-one session in which the student speaks very little is not working, however impressive the explanation was. And do they ask to see the student's own marked work rather than starting from a generic plan? Beginning from the marked paper is the single clearest indicator of a tutor who intends to diagnose rather than deliver.
The table gives each question with what a good answer sounds like and the corresponding warning sign. It is written to be used, so take it to a trial lesson rather than reading it once.

sections.heading: What the market charges, and what the travel premium pays for
paragraphs: No rate table has been published for Ras Al Khaimah, so every AED figure available in this market comes from a Dubai source. The bands below carry the provider who publishes them and should be read as a ceiling rather than a local quote. Families in this emirate commonly report paying at or below the Dubai mid-band for a comparable teacher.

The in-home premium is the figure worth understanding in a district like this. Published in-home bands sit above online bands for the same calibre of teacher, and the difference is mostly travel. For Al Qusaidat that premium is larger than average, because any tutor coming here from the city side is making the crossing at exactly the time it is slowest, and that hour is priced into the fee whether or not it appears as a line item.

Monthly packages are the other thing to read carefully. Published examples in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are not comparable products: one is eight contact hours and the other is eight contact hours plus eight journeys, and the per-hour arithmetic looks very different depending on which number you divide by.

IB Gram does not publish a fixed hourly rate on these pages, and does not pass on any permit fee, because the permit is free. Pricing is quoted after a consultation and a trial lesson is arranged before any commitment. For wider budget context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for 2026-27 under the emirate's second economic incentives package; fee policy is emirate-specific, so confirm the local position with your own school.

sections.heading: Genuine warning signs in the UAE tutoring market
paragraphs: Comparing providers online from Al Qusaidat is harder than it should be, because several practices that look like credentials are in fact liabilities. These are not hypothetical; each was found on pages currently competing for exactly the searches a family here would run, and each is worth recognising on sight.

The most serious is the sale of finished assessed work. At least one provider in this market sells completed internal assessments outright. Submitting work a student did not produce is malpractice under the IB's rules, and the consequence lands on the student, not on the seller. Any provider willing to supply assessed work is also telling you what they think of your child's long-term interests. A legitimate tutor teaches, explains criteria and gives feedback on the student's own drafts, and will say so without being asked.

Next is review markup nobody can audit. Competitor pages in this market display star ratings of 4.9 or higher with hundreds of reviews, in at least one case alongside figures that contradict each other on the same page, and in another a self-published rating embedded in structured data. Self-serving review markup breaches Google's structured data policies and, as a commercial representation, is a consumer-protection exposure. A rating you cannot click through to individual dated reviews is not evidence.

Then there are three smaller but reliable signals. Promises about a specific grade or a specific improvement, which no honest teacher can make and which carry no mechanism of redress. Statistics with no sample size, date or method, such as satisfaction percentages or average tutor scores. And UAE-facing pages whose only conversion route is a foreign phone number, or which show a Dubai address on a page about another emirate. Each of those tells you something true about how carefully the provider operates.

sections.heading: Your child's data: what is collected and how to have it removed
paragraphs: Every tutoring enquiry involves personal data about a minor: a name, a year group, a school, sometimes a marked paper with a teacher's comments on it. The UAE has a federal data protection framework, Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data, and a family is entitled to know what a provider holds, why it holds it, and how to have it deleted. Almost nobody in this market says anything about it.

The honest minimum is short. A tutoring enquiry needs a contact for the parent, the student's year group, the subject, the board and level, and ideally the marked work that shows where the marks are going. It does not need a photograph, a full academic history, a school identification number or a copy of a passport, and a form that requests those without stating a purpose should be treated with suspicion.

Marked work deserves specific mention, because it is the most useful thing a family can send and the most sensitive. A mock paper carries a student's name, a grade and a teacher's written comments. It should be used for the diagnosis, held only while the arrangement runs, and deleted on request. A family is entitled to ask for that in writing before sending anything.

Two related points. A privacy link should be on every page a family can submit information from, not buried on a separate policy page nobody reaches. And nothing about a child should be published, quoted in testimonials or used as a case study without explicit permission from the parent, which includes anonymised results. If a provider cannot tell you what it holds and how to delete it, that is itself an answer about how it operates.

sections.heading: A schedule that survives from September to May in the northern districts
paragraphs: Most tutoring arrangements in this district end rather than conclude, and they end in October or November for reasons that are entirely predictable in August. Too many sessions booked, booked at times that depend on traffic, with no plan for Ramadan, exam leave or the weeks when the student's own deadlines collide.

The pattern that lasts is smaller than families first want. Two sessions a week in one subject, anchored to Maghrib rather than to a clock time, with one weekend long block if there is a timed-paper programme running. One evening deliberately left empty as a buffer for deadline weeks. That is four or five hours of commitment a week including the student's own preparation, which a northern household can genuinely sustain.

Ramadan is planned before it starts, not after the first missed lesson. Private schools shorten the day, so children are home earlier, and fasting teenagers are least alert in the late afternoon. Post-iftar slots work well for secondary students; late-morning sessions on the shortened day work for primary. Agreeing the variation in advance saves the three cancelled sessions that usually precede the renegotiation.

Exam leave is the other foreseeable disruption. When the school day disappears, the whole day becomes available, which produces less work rather than more unless it is timetabled. Two fixed sessions plus one timed full paper per subject per week, with the rest of the day written down before leave begins, is the pattern that holds. The table sets out the year as a plan rather than as a hope.
