process.title: Ask for the permit before anything else
process.description: Any individual tutor should show their MoHRE private tuition work permit without hesitation. It costs nothing to obtain and lasts two years, so there is no legitimate reason for it to be missing. A tutoring centre with premises should be able to give you its own permit number instead.

process.title: Give us the syllabus code and the marked paper
process.description: The code from the entry statement and the most recent marked mock. Those two documents let a tutor arrive at the trial lesson already knowing the paper structure and the specific topics losing marks, rather than spending the first session finding out.

process.title: Anchor the slot to a prayer, not a clock time
process.description: A slot agreed as starting after Maghrib stays correct across the year. A slot fixed at a specific time drifts into the wrong part of the evening by December and gets renegotiated or quietly dropped, which is the most common way an arrangement in this district ends.

process.title: Use the trial lesson as a test, not a formality
process.description: Take the seven questions from the trial-lesson table and use them. Watch whether your child speaks, whether the tutor asks for the marked work, and whether written notes arrive afterwards naming specifics rather than saying the session went well.

process.title: Agree the variations before the term starts
process.description: Ramadan timing, exam leave, the empty buffer evening and the summer slot. Each of those is foreseeable in September, and every one of them ends arrangements that were not planned for it. Fifteen minutes at the start saves a term.

whyPoints.title: The crossing is treated as a real constraint
whyPoints.description: Session times are built from when a child in this district actually gets home, not from when a calendar looks free. Removing the journey to a tuition centre removes four peak-time crossings a week, which is the difference between an arrangement that lasts and one that stops in November.

whyPoints.title: The permit question answered, not avoided
whyPoints.description: The private tuition work permit is free, lasts two years and covers a broad set of categories. Any individual tutor should show it before a first paid lesson, and no fine amount should ever be quoted to you, because none has been published.

whyPoints.title: Verification you can run yourself
whyPoints.description: Seven specific questions, each tied to the syllabus code rather than the subject, that distinguish a tutor who has taught the paper from one who has not. They work in ten minutes and need no prior subject knowledge from the parent.

whyPoints.title: No promises about grades, ever
whyPoints.description: No honest teacher can commit to a particular score, and a provider that does is offering something with no mechanism of redress. Timescales for specific repairs are given instead, because those can be judged against evidence at the next assessment.

whyPoints.title: Clear boundaries on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Internal assessments, the Extended Essay and TOK essays are the student's own work throughout. Sessions explain criteria and give feedback on drafts the student has written, and nothing is supplied for submission. Official papers and mark schemes are referenced and linked, never reproduced and distributed.

whyPoints.title: Straight about data and about status
whyPoints.description: What is collected, why, and how to have it deleted, under the UAE's federal data protection framework. And plainly: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no UAE premises and no accreditation from any education regulator or examination board.

faqs.question: How long does the crossing from Al Qusaidat to the city-side schools actually take?
faqs.answer: A few minutes at midday and considerably longer between half past one and three, when every southern-side school run is happening at once. In practice a parent collecting from a city-centre campus is back in Al Qusaidat somewhere between a quarter past two and three o'clock, later with two schools involved. That is why mid-afternoon tutoring slots are unreliable here even though they work well for a family living beside their school, and why the usable window runs from about five o'clock.

faqs.question: Can a session be scheduled around Maghrib prayer?
faqs.answer: Yes, and anchoring it that way is the better arrangement in this district. Maghrib moves across roughly an hour and a half between the shortest and longest days in the UAE, so a slot fixed at a clock time drifts into the wrong part of the evening by midwinter and gets renegotiated. A slot agreed as beginning after Maghrib stays correct all year. Tutors matched for northern households are told which anchor applies, so the booking reflects it from the start.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor holds a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Ask to see it before the first paid lesson. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years, so there is no legitimate reason for it to be unavailable or for a fee to be passed on. The application route is MoHRE's own service for private tutor licensing, through its smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days.

faqs.question: Who is actually eligible to apply for a private tutor permit?
faqs.answer: The categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in both the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. So a tutor being a university student rather than a schoolteacher is not a compliance problem in itself, although it is a relevant fact about what they are equipped to teach. What is not permitted is tutoring without the permit at all, which carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: What should I ask a prospective tutor in the first ten minutes?
faqs.answer: Seven things, all specific to the syllabus rather than the subject. Which syllabus code will you teach to. How is the practical component assessed for that code. What is the internal assessment marked against. Which topic loses students the most marks on this paper, and why. Can I see an example of the notes you send after a session. Will you work from my child's marked papers. And do you hold a MoHRE permit. A tutor who has taught the course answers all seven instantly and concretely.

faqs.question: Should I consider a tutor who promises a specific grade improvement?
faqs.answer: No. No honest teacher can commit to a particular score, because the outcome depends on the student's own work, the paper that happens to be set and the grade boundaries for that series. A promise of that kind comes with no mechanism of redress, and in this market it often sits alongside other practices worth avoiding. What a good tutor will give you instead is a realistic timescale for a specific repair, such as two to four weeks for pacing, which can be judged against evidence at the next assessment.

faqs.question: A tutoring site shows 4.9 stars from hundreds of reviews. Should I trust it?
faqs.answer: Only if you can click through to individual dated reviews. Pages competing in this market display ratings above 4.9 with large review counts, in at least one case with figures that contradict each other on the same page, and in another with a self-published rating embedded in the page's structured data. Self-serving review markup breaches Google's structured data policies and, as a commercial representation in the UAE, is a consumer-protection exposure. A number you cannot audit is decoration rather than evidence.

faqs.question: Someone offered to supply a completed internal assessment. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It is a serious one, and the consequences fall on your child rather than on the seller. Submitting work a student did not produce is malpractice under the IB's rules and can end a Diploma. At least one provider in this market sells finished assessments outright. A legitimate tutor teaches the subject content the assessment rests on, explains what each criterion descriptor is asking for, and gives feedback on drafts the student has written themselves. Anything beyond that is not help, whatever it is described as.

faqs.question: What information do you hold about my child, and can I have it deleted?
faqs.answer: An enquiry needs a parent contact, the student's year group, the subject, the board and level, and ideally the marked work that shows where marks are going. It does not need a photograph, a passport copy or a full academic history. Marked papers are the most useful and most sensitive item, since they carry a name, a grade and a teacher's comments, and you can ask in writing how long they are held and request deletion. The UAE's framework is Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data.

faqs.question: Is it a concern if a tutoring company only lists a foreign phone number?
faqs.answer: It is a reasonable thing to weigh. Two pages ranking for these searches route UAE parents to numbers outside the country, and one displays a Dubai address on a page about a different emirate. Neither is illegal in itself, but both tell you how carefully the provider handles its own representations, and an address a company does not occupy is a misrepresentation. Ask where the business is actually established and who you would be contracting with. IB Gram has no UAE premises and does not claim one.

faqs.question: What does tutoring cost from Al Qusaidat, and why is in-home dearer?
faqs.answer: No rate table has been published for this emirate, so the figures are Dubai ones and should be read as a ceiling: AED 45-150 an hour for budget online tuition, AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 180-500 for in-home visits and AED 200-450 or more for a specialist. In-home is dearer because the tutor's travel is priced into the fee, and from this district that travel includes the crossing at the slowest time of day. The permit itself is free and no permit fee should ever be passed on.

faqs.question: Does the private tutor permit cover lessons delivered over video?
faqs.answer: The permit is a work permit for providing private tuition rather than a licence tied to a particular room, and the published eligibility and conditions do not turn on the delivery format. The scope and conditions are nonetheless set by MoHRE and are the sort of detail that gets updated, so the authoritative answer is MoHRE's own service page for private tutor licensing rather than any tutoring website. Ask the individual tutor to show the permit and read what it covers rather than accepting a summary of it.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week actually survive a full school year here?
faqs.answer: Two in one subject, plus a weekend long block if a timed-paper programme is running. That is the pattern that lasts from September to May in the northern districts. Three or four sessions a week booked in September are usually abandoned by November, because the week has less room than it appeared to in the summer. Keep one evening deliberately empty as a buffer for the fortnights when school deadlines collide, and add a second subject only once the first has visibly moved.

faqs.question: Can we pause during Ramadan and pick up afterwards?
faqs.answer: Pausing works, and retiming usually works better. Private schools shorten the day, so children are home earlier, and fasting teenagers are at their least alert in the late afternoon. Post-iftar slots suit secondary students, while primary children often do better with a late-morning session on the shortened day. Agree the variation before Ramadan begins rather than after the first missed lesson, since the renegotiation itself tends to cost three sessions. The schedule then reverts to the term pattern.

faqs.question: Do you use past papers and mark schemes, and can you send them to us?
faqs.answer: Past papers and mark schemes are central to the work, and they are referenced and linked from the boards' own sites rather than reproduced and distributed. Cambridge, Pearson and the IB hold copyright in their syllabus documents, papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables, so a provider circulating them as downloads is infringing it, and for unreleased material there is an additional malpractice exposure. What you will get is the official link, plus the tutor's own marking of your child's attempt against the published scheme.

ras-al-khaimah/al-qusaidat.closingHeading: Check the permit, anchor the slot, then start
ras-al-khaimah/al-qusaidat.closingBody: Two things make tutoring work from this side of the creek. A session time anchored to Maghrib rather than to a clock, so it is still correct in December, and a tutor whose permit and syllabus knowledge you have actually verified rather than assumed. Send us the syllabus code and the last marked paper, and we will match a tutor who can answer the seven trial-lesson questions on the spot. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, which removes four peak-time crossings a week from your schedule.

ras-al-khaimah/best-ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB subjects to Ras Al Khaimah students over live video at Higher and Standard Level. Which of them suits a given student depends on the starting position and the weeks available, so the trial lesson exists to settle both before any money moves.

intro.heading: There is no ranking, but there is a right answer for your child
paragraphs: Searching for the best IB tutor in Ras Al Khaimah is a reasonable thing to do and a poorly specified question, because the thing being ranked does not have a single scale. A tutor who moves a student from a 3 to a 5 in chemistry is doing a different job, requiring different skills, from one who moves a capable student from a 6 to a 7. The first needs patient reconstruction of missing foundations. The second needs precision about where two marks disappear in a Paper 2 extended response. Very few people are excellent at both, and nobody is excellent at both for every subject.

So the useful reframing is this: best means the closest fit between three things you can actually establish. Where your child is now, measured in marks rather than in impressions. Where they need to be, defined by the next step rather than by ambition. And how many usable weeks sit between the two, counted from your school's real calendar rather than from a notional year. Fix those three and the choice of tutor becomes a matter of matching rather than of ranking.

Most families skip the first one, and it is the one that determines everything. A parent arrives knowing that chemistry feels hard and that the last report said effort was good. Neither statement identifies a problem a tutor can work on. A marked Paper 2 script, by contrast, shows whether marks were lost to missing content, to command words, to arithmetic, to timing, or to a complete absence of working. Those five diagnoses lead to five different plans, and four of them are wrong for any given student.

The second thing families underestimate is the arithmetic of weeks. A Ras Al Khaimah school year looks long in September. Subtract the autumn internal assessment deadlines, the mock window, the public holidays, the Ramadan weeks where the evening study slot moves, the fortnight of exam leave and the two weeks either side of a family trip, and a Year 13 plan often has fewer than twenty usable weeks in it. A plan built for thirty-five weeks fails not because it was wrong but because the weeks were never there.

The third is honesty about what a tutor cannot be the fix for. A student sleeping five hours, carrying three Higher Levels that were never the right combination, with an Extended Essay untouched in February, has a scheduling and triage problem rather than a teaching problem. Buying hours in that situation makes the week worse. We would rather say so in a free trial lesson than take a term's fees. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video; IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, because visiting tutors are an India-only service.

ras-al-khaimah/best-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: Ras Al Khaimah IB students arrive from two directions: up through a continuum campus, or across from an examined route at sixteen. The starting point differs sharply between them, which is why the same target grade needs a different plan.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subject groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, with the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and creativity, activity, service alongside them. Each subject combines internally assessed work moderated by the IB with externally marked examinations, and subjects are graded one to seven. The internally assessed component is the part of the grade settled before any examination room.
programmes.countryNote: A Ras Al Khaimah Diploma cohort is small, so a student's starting position is often shaped by the timetable rather than by ability: a Standard Level entry where Higher Level was needed, or a set with one teacher and no second specialist. Establishing which of those applies changes the plan more than knowing the current grade does.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years assessed against four published criteria per subject on a one to eight scale, with no past papers and no published mark schemes. The starting point here is a criterion pattern rather than a mark total, and the most useful diagnostic is a criterion that scores low across several subjects at once rather than one subject scoring low overall.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students on Ras Al Khaimah continuum campuses move into Year 12 with the same staff and buildings, which hides how much the assessment changes. The twelve months before that move are where written volume and independent scheduling get built, and where a tutor's time has the longest reach.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: The examined route most of the emirate's schools run into sixteen, assessed by papers in a June or November series. Students crossing from here into the Diploma arrive with strong timed-paper technique and no experience of internally assessed investigation work, which is a very specific starting position with a very specific first-term plan.
programmes.countryNote: The Core or Extended tier chosen in Year 10 at a Ras Al Khaimah school reaches into the Diploma: a Core mathematics candidate entering Year 12 is poorly placed for Higher Level mathematics, and that gap is best addressed in the summer before Year 12 rather than discovered in October.

ras-al-khaimah/best-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones Ras Al Khaimah families most often ask about, described in terms of where the marks sit rather than what the syllabus contains, because the location of lost marks is what decides which tutor fits.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: A student stuck at a 4 is usually missing algebraic fluency from before the course started. A student stuck at a 6 is usually losing the last marks of extended-response questions by stopping at an answer without interpretation. The same subject, two unrelated repairs, and a tutor strong at one is often ordinary at the other.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Marks concentrate in modelling and statistics, and the common failure is treating the graphical calculator as a last resort rather than as the intended tool. Students who chose this route expecting it to be lighter typically meet the statistics content late, which is a sequencing problem with a predictable fix.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Three distinct failure patterns: mole arithmetic with units dropped, organic mechanisms treated as memorisation rather than pattern, and practical write-ups where uncertainty is ignored. Diagnosing which of the three applies takes one marked script, and the plans for each are entirely different in shape and length.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Students who can rearrange equations and cannot say what a result means lose marks across every paper. Graph gradient interpretation and explanations that name a principle instead of describing an outcome are the two highest-yield repairs, and both respond to technique work within weeks rather than terms.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term discipline decides the grade more than content recall does. An answer that describes a trend when an explanation was asked for collects part of the credit at best, and students repeat that error for two years unless someone names it from a marked script. Data analysis is the second reliable source of lost marks.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams drawn accurately and labelled fully carry marks that go unclaimed with surprising regularity. Evaluation questions need a judgement that follows from the analysis rather than a two-sided list. The internally assessed commentaries have a hard word limit, so editing to length is part of the assessed skill.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral is the component students prepare least and worry about most. Marks attach to a global issue stated precisely and extracts chosen because they evidence it. A student at a 5 is usually summarising texts; a student at a 6 is usually analysing without a clear line of argument running through the response.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application is where the marks are. Describing an organisation earns little; applying a named tool to the evidence supplied and reaching a supported recommendation earns the band. Calculation questions in the finance content are predictable marks that students leave behind because they were never drilled.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay combine with the Extended Essay for additional points, and they are the elements most often left too late. Marks attach to knowledge questions handled with real examples and a counter-position taken seriously, which is coachable in a short defined block rather than across a year.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Lost marks are structural almost every time: a research question too broad for four thousand words, no method section, and a conclusion that summarises instead of answering. A student in February with nothing written has a triage problem rather than a research problem, and the honest plan says so.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The documentation is marked, not the program, which reorders a student's priorities the moment it is explained. A working solution with a thin design record and no testing evidence scores poorly, and recovering those marks is a writing job that can be done in a handful of sessions if the deadline has not passed.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: Language B or ab initio, plus mandatory provision
subjects.description: Arabic runs alongside the Diploma for UAE students as a federal requirement, with separate provision for Arabic speakers and non-Arabic speakers, and it may also be taken as a Diploma language subject. Support only works when it matches the stream the school has placed the student in, so confirm that in writing first.

ras-al-khaimah/best-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in Ras Al Khaimah changes the number of usable hours in a week more than it changes anything else, which is why it belongs in a page about timelines.

regions.name: Al Hamra and Al Hamra Village
regions.note: Closest to the emirate's IB provision. Short school run, but core activity commitments often run to 16:30, so a realistic weekly slot is 17:30 and the early-evening hour is the one that holds across a full term.

regions.name: Mina Al Arab and Hayat Island
regions.note: The bus adds thirty to forty minutes at the far end of the development. Students here reliably sustain an 18:00 session and reliably lose a 16:30 one by half-term, which matters when a plan assumes thirty consecutive weeks.

regions.name: Al Nakheel
regions.note: The city side, with the shortest journeys to the main campuses. Students transferring into the Diploma from an examined route often live here, and their first-term gap is internal assessment technique rather than subject content.

regions.name: Al Dhait North and South
regions.note: Inland districts with several tuition centres. Families here have usually tried a group class already, so the starting point conversation includes what that class did and did not move over the previous term.

regions.name: Khuzam and Al Uraibi
regions.note: Central districts with minimal travel. The limiting factor is a quiet room rather than a commute, so the usable hour is often later in the evening than a parent first proposes, and planning for that keeps the plan intact.

regions.name: Al Marjan Island
regions.note: Longer internal drives and parents frequently returning from Dubai at lesson time. A session requiring no adult to be present works here in practice, and the week audit usually shows fewer free evenings than expected.

regions.name: Digdaga and the inland belt
regions.note: Semi-rural areas with no campus nearby and long bus journeys. Weekday capacity is genuinely short, so weekend mornings carry the heavier work and any plan built on five weekday evenings will not survive October.

sections.heading: Fixing the starting point: three documents and a week audit
paragraphs: A starting point is not a feeling and it is not a report comment. It is evidence, and three documents produce almost all of it. The first is the most recent marked script: a mock paper, a class test, anything where a marker wrote on the page. The second is the latest school report, read for the gap between attainment and the teacher's comments rather than for the headline grade. The third, for a Diploma student, is the most recent internally assessed draft with the supervisor's feedback on it.

Those three take a specialist ten minutes and tell them things no conversation will. The marked script shows whether marks went to absent content, to misread command words, to arithmetic, to timing or to working that was never written down. The report shows whether the picture is one subject or five. The internally assessed draft shows whether the research question was ever answerable in the available length, which is the commonest reason an otherwise strong student scores badly on their own work.

The fourth input is one families almost never bring and is the one most likely to change the plan: an honest audit of the week. Write down every hour that is already committed between Sunday and Thursday. The school day, the commute, the activity programme, religious commitments, family obligations, the hours spent on homework that is actually set. Then count what remains. In Ras Al Khaimah, where a bus journey can take forty minutes and Year 13 activity commitments run into the early evening, the answer is regularly four or five genuinely free weekday hours.

That number is a constraint, not a complaint. A plan asking for two tutored hours plus six hours of independent work in a week containing five free hours is not ambitious; it is arithmetic that does not close. Knowing it up front produces a plan that survives contact with October, and it frequently redirects the decision away from a second tutored subject and towards making the first one count.

sections.heading: The gap in marks, not in grades
paragraphs: Parents talk in grades and papers are marked in marks, and the translation between the two is where realistic planning begins. A move from a 4 to a 5 is not a vague improvement in understanding; it is a specific number of additional marks across a specific set of components, and the number is usually smaller than people fear and larger than they hope. Schools can often tell you roughly what a band step cost in the last cohort, and the question is worth asking directly.

Thinking in marks also exposes where the cheapest marks are. On almost every paper there is a set of questions a student is losing not because the material is hard but because the answer was the wrong shape: a description where an explanation was wanted, a calculation with no working, a graph gradient computed and not interpreted, a question abandoned because the clock ran out. Those are recoverable quickly. The marks that sit behind two years of missing algebra are not, and no amount of weekly technique work pretends otherwise.

The practical move is to take the most recent marked script and sort every lost mark into one of five categories: content absent, content known but misapplied, command word misread, arithmetic or units, and time. Add the totals. A student losing twenty marks of which fourteen fall in the last three categories has a technique problem and a short, high-yield plan. A student losing twenty marks of which sixteen are absent content has a reconstruction problem and needs a year.

This sorting exercise is the single most useful hour a parent can spend, and it does not require a tutor. It also protects you from buying the wrong thing: the difference between those two students is invisible in a report and obvious in a script. Any tutor worth hiring will do this in a trial lesson, and will tell you which of the two situations you are in before asking for a commitment.

sections.heading: Three starting positions, three different people to hire
paragraphs: Once the starting point is evidence rather than impression, the choice of tutor narrows sharply, because the three common positions call for three genuinely different sets of skills. Treating them as one job is why families sometimes hire a strong tutor and see nothing move for a term.

A student at a 3 heading for a 5 needs reconstruction. The skill required is patience with foundations, a willingness to go back two years in a syllabus and sequence forward, and the honesty to say the plan is a year rather than a half-term. The wrong hire here is a brilliant specialist who starts from this week's topic, because the student will keep nodding and keep failing. Progress shows as earlier material re-tested successfully, not as this week's homework improving.

A student at a 5 heading for a 6 usually has the content and is losing the marks elsewhere. The skill required is forensic: reading a marked script, naming the pattern, and drilling the shape of the answer until it becomes automatic. This is the shortest and most reliable of the three plans, frequently six to ten sessions, and it is measurable in marks recovered on a comparable paper. It is also the position where group classes do least, because the diagnosis is individual.

A student at a 6 heading for a 7 needs precision, and the hardest thing about this hire is that the gains are small and specific. It is extended-response structure, evaluation that commits to a judgement, the two marks per question that separate the top bands, and in the internally assessed work the difference between a competent draft and one that answers its own question. Four to eight narrow sessions, then it stops, because beyond a point the student's own practice is what adds marks and more tutoring crowds it out.

sections.heading: A Ras Al Khaimah term as a budget of usable weeks
paragraphs: The calendar is the part of planning that families treat as background and that actually decides outcomes. A school year contains far fewer weeks a plan can use than the number of weeks it contains. The exercise is simple: print your school's published calendar, mark the weeks that are genuinely available, and plan only inside those. Everything on this page about marks and starting positions is academic if the weeks are not there.

Four things remove weeks in this emirate. Internal assessment deadlines in the autumn term of Year 13 absorb almost all the slack a student has, and a family planning subject revision through that period is competing with the school's own schedule. The mock window in January or February removes a fortnight and produces the most valuable data of the year, which most students then ignore. The Ramadan period moves the usable study evening, so sessions need rescheduling in advance rather than cancelling week by week. Exam leave starts earlier than parents expect and is not a revision bonus; it is when a plan either pays off or does not.

Where boards publish dates, use them rather than estimates. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE series is a clean example of how far administration sits ahead of papers: the final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and the entry that put a candidate in that room had closed months before the first of those papers. Cambridge's two UAE series, June and November, work the same way, with the June entry closing in the spring and the exact day printed on the centre's statement of entry rather than published as a single national date. Pearson publishes provisional timetables that can be revised, so the live official timetable is the only reliable source. IB session and results dates are deliberately not published on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and we will not restate a date we have not verified; confirm those with your school's coordinator.

The output of this exercise is a number, and the number changes the plan. Twenty usable weeks supports one subject taken properly with independent work in between. It does not support three subjects, a neglected Extended Essay and a new activity commitment. Writing the number down is what converts a wish into a plan, and it is also what makes the honest conversation about priorities possible rather than awkward.

sections.heading: What the weeks cost, and why the hourly rate is the wrong first question
paragraphs: Published market rates in dirhams are rare in this market, so here they are with sources, and then the more useful framing. Budget online and university-student tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online sits roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutoring runs AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 table giving 200 to 450 and above. In-home visiting tutors run AED 180 to AED 500 with travel inside the number. Premium named tutors go higher, with BartyED publishing AED 650. These are market figures, not an IB Gram price list.

The reason the hourly rate is a poor first question is that it prices the wrong unit. What a family is buying is a plan of a certain length aimed at a certain number of marks, and two plans at identical hourly rates can differ by a factor of three in total cost because one needs thirty sessions and the other needs eight. A student at a 5 needing technique work is a cheap problem at any rate. A student at a 3 needing reconstruction is an expensive one even at a modest rate, and pretending otherwise at the point of sale is how families end up stopping halfway through something that only works if finished.

So the question worth asking a prospective tutor is not what they charge per hour but how many sessions they think this will take, what the measurable target is, and what evidence will show at the halfway point. A tutor who answers those three precisely is demonstrating the diagnostic skill you are actually hiring. A tutor who cannot is quoting on hope. Bestimate's monthly estimates give useful shape here, running roughly AED 240 to 600 for budget weekly sessions, 600 to 1,200 mid-range and 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year support.

Worth placing beside the rest of the bill. School fees dominate the education line in any UAE household, and in Dubai the Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for 2026-27 under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Our own arrangement starts with a free trial lesson, no card required, and a plan quoted after it, because quoting before the starting point is established would mean guessing at the number of sessions.

sections.heading: The signals in week two that say the match is wrong
paragraphs: Families usually discover a poor match in week eight, when a term has gone and a report has not moved. The signals are available in week two, and knowing them is worth more than any amount of care at the point of hiring, because no selection process is reliable enough to skip the check.

The clearest signal is that the tutor has not seen the student's marked work. If two sessions have passed and nobody has asked for a script, the teaching is being aimed at a subject rather than at a student, and it will keep being aimed there. The second is that the student cannot say what the session was for. A fifteen-year-old who says it was useful but cannot name what changed has had a pleasant hour. Ask them what the tutor said they were getting wrong, and listen for whether it is specific.

The third is the absence of a measurable target. If nobody has said what this block is aiming at, in marks or in a named component, then there is no point at which anyone will discover it is not working. The fourth is work not increasing between sessions: tutoring that does not generate independent work is entertainment, because the hours between sessions are where the learning happens and a good tutor is deliberately loading them.

The fifth is specific to our format and worth naming honestly. If a student will not write on the shared document, keeps the camera off and answers in single words, live video is not working for that student in that term. That is a legitimate finding rather than a failure, and the right response is to say so and recommend a local visiting tutor or a group class in Al Dhait instead. All five of these checks take one conversation with your child and one question to the tutor, and they are far cheaper in week two than in week eight.

sections.heading: When a tutor is not the constraint, and what to do instead
paragraphs: Some of the enquiries we take from Ras Al Khaimah describe situations where buying tutoring would make the week worse, and saying so is part of the job. The most common is sleep. A Year 13 student finishing homework at one in the morning, travelling forty minutes to school and carrying three Higher Levels is not short of teaching. Adding two hours of commitment to that week reduces performance across every subject, and the intervention that works is a brutal audit of what gets dropped.

The second is a subject combination that was never right. A small cohort means option blocks are tight, and students end up carrying a Higher Level they did not choose and do not need. Changing a level is a school conversation, it is possible further into Year 12 than most families assume, and it is worth having before buying a year of support to prop up a subject nobody requires. Ask the school what the deadline for a level change is and what the consequences are.

The third is the core. A student in February with an Extended Essay untouched and a Theory of Knowledge essay outstanding has a sequencing emergency, and subject tutoring in that month is spending money on the wrong thing. The correct order is to get the core work to a submittable state against the school's deadlines, because those marks are nearer and the time is shorter. We will say this plainly even when the enquiry was about chemistry.

The fourth is motivation, and it is the one no tutor can purchase. A student who does not want this, in a house where it is being wanted for them, will sit through any number of competent hours without changing. Occasionally a different adult with no shared history changes something, which is why a free trial lesson is worth doing. But if the trial shows a student who is not participating, the honest report says so rather than recommending a block that will be endured for a term and then abandoned.

sections.heading: What progress actually looks like, and when to stop
paragraphs: Progress in IB subjects is not linear and it is not visible weekly, which is why reviews need defined checkpoints rather than general impressions. In the first fortnight the measurable change is diagnostic: the student can state what they were getting wrong and the tutor has written down a target. That is all, and expecting more is what causes families to abandon plans that were working.

By week four there should be evidence in the student's own work: marks recovered on a question type, an earlier topic re-tested successfully, a draft that answers its own research question. By week eight, a comparable paper should show movement in the targeted components even if the overall grade has not changed, because grades lag marks and the components are where the change happens first. By week twelve, if nothing in any of those categories has moved, the plan is wrong and continuing is the expensive choice.

Stopping deliberately is an underrated outcome. A technique block that recovers its target marks in seven sessions should finish at seven rather than roll into an open weekly arrangement, because beyond that point the student's independent practice adds more than another tutored hour and the hour crowds it out. We write a closing note saying what moved and what did not, and a recommendation that is sometimes to stop entirely.

The exception is Year 13 across a whole year, where continuity has value in itself: a tutor who has been with a student since September knows the internal assessment, the mock script and the specific pattern of errors, and that knowledge is worth more in April than a fresh pair of eyes. The decision between the two is a judgement, and the useful rule is that continuity is worth paying for when marks are moving and worth abandoning when they are not.

Week four: marks recovered on a question type, or earlier material re-tested

This single exercise distinguishes a short technique block from a year of reconstruction, and it is the difference between the two plans that changes what a family should buy.

process.title: Free trial lesson, then a written opinion
process.description: Taught by the tutor who would take the course, with no card required. Afterwards you get the diagnosis in writing, a proposed block with a measurable target, an estimate of sessions, and an honest statement if tutoring is not the constraint in this student's week this term.

process.title: Agree a block with a target and an end date
process.description: Blocks rather than open-ended weekly hours, because a block forces a verdict. The target is named in marks or in a component, the checkpoint sits at the halfway point, and the closing note states what moved and what did not alongside the student's own marked work.

process.description: Ask your child what the tutor said they were getting wrong, and ask the tutor what the block is aiming at. If the answers are vague, or no marked script has been requested, say so immediately. Changing tutor in week two costs a fortnight; discovering it in week eight costs a term.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before any hours are sold
whyPoints.description: The trial lesson exists to establish a starting point from marked work rather than from a conversation, and to say which of the three common positions a student is in. Those positions need different tutors, and selling the wrong one is the commonest way a term goes nowhere.

whyPoints.title: Plans sized in weeks you actually have
whyPoints.description: The usable weeks in a Ras Al Khaimah year are fewer than the calendar suggests once internal assessment deadlines, mocks, Ramadan and exam leave are counted. A plan is built inside that number, which is why it is still standing in March rather than quietly abandoned in November.

whyPoints.title: Targets in marks, reported in writing
whyPoints.description: Blocks have a named target and a halfway checkpoint, and progress is reported as marks recovered on comparable work with the student's own scripts attached. When nothing has moved by the checkpoint, the review says so rather than reframing it as a slower start.

whyPoints.title: Matched on subject and level, not distance
whyPoints.description: Removing travel from the match is what makes a Higher Level specialist reachable from the northern emirates. A request is matched against everyone qualified to teach that subject at that level rather than the handful who could drive to Al Hamra by six on a weekday.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you when not to buy
whyPoints.description: Sleep, a wrong subject combination, an untouched Extended Essay in February and a student who does not want this are not teaching problems, and hours spent on them make the week worse. Those findings go in the written opinion after the trial, in plain words.

whyPoints.title: No rankings, guarantees or regulator claims
whyPoints.description: No tutor can be ranked across every subject and starting point, no grade outcome is promised, and IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, the Ministry of Education or any emirate regulator, and operates no UAE office.

faqs.question: Can you actually rank IB tutors, or is that the wrong question?
faqs.answer: It is the wrong question, and the reframing is useful rather than evasive. Moving a student from a 3 to a 5 requires patient reconstruction of foundations from before the course. Moving a student from a 6 to a 7 requires forensic precision about where two marks disappear in an extended response. Those are different skills, and few people are strong at both in the same subject. What you can establish is fit: where your child is now in marks, where they need to be, and how many usable weeks sit between. Fix those three and the choice becomes matching rather than ranking.

faqs.question: Which documents should I gather before I contact anyone about IB support?
faqs.answer: Three, plus one list. The most recent marked script, where a marker wrote on the page. The latest school report, read for the gap between attainment and the teacher's comments. For a Diploma student, the newest internally assessed draft with the supervisor's feedback. Then a list of every hour already committed between Sunday and Thursday: school, commute, activity programme, religious and family obligations, homework actually set. The first three identify the problem; the fourth decides what size of plan can survive contact with a real week in this emirate.

faqs.question: How do I tell from a marked paper whether the problem is content or technique?
faqs.answer: Sort every lost mark into five categories and add the totals. Content genuinely absent shows as blanks or nonsense across a whole topic. Content misapplied shows as the right idea in the wrong context. Command words show as describing when asked to explain. Arithmetic and working show as a correct method losing method marks. Time shows as a strong start and blank final questions. A student losing most marks in the last three categories has a six to ten session problem. A student losing most to absent content needs a year, and any plan that pretends otherwise will fail.

faqs.question: How many usable weeks does a Ras Al Khaimah IB year actually contain?
faqs.answer: Fewer than the calendar implies. Subtract the autumn internal assessment deadlines, which absorb nearly all of a Year 13 student's slack; the mock fortnight; public holidays; the Ramadan weeks where the evening study slot moves; exam leave; and the weeks either side of family travel. A Year 13 plan commonly has under twenty usable weeks in it. Twenty weeks supports one subject taken properly with independent work in between. It does not support three subjects plus a neglected Extended Essay, and writing the number down is what makes that conversation possible.

faqs.question: What should I ask a prospective tutor instead of asking the hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Three questions. How many sessions do you think this will take? What is the measurable target, in marks or in a named component? What evidence will exist at the halfway point? A tutor who answers all three precisely is demonstrating the diagnostic skill you are actually paying for. One who cannot is quoting on hope. The rate matters less than the plan length, because two plans at identical hourly rates can differ threefold in total cost when one needs thirty sessions and the other needs eight.

faqs.question: How soon would I know that we have hired the wrong person?
faqs.answer: Week two, if you check. Five signals: no marked script has been requested; your child cannot name what the tutor said they were getting wrong; no measurable target has been stated for the block; independent work between sessions has not increased; or the student will not write on the shared document and answers in single words. The last one means live video is not working for that student this term, which is a legitimate finding. All five take one conversation with your child and one question to the tutor, and acting in week two costs a fortnight rather than a term.

faqs.question: What does real progress look like at four, eight and twelve weeks?
faqs.answer: At a fortnight, the only honest measure is diagnostic: the student can state what they were getting wrong and a written target exists. By week four there should be evidence in their own work, such as marks recovered on a question type or an earlier topic re-tested successfully. By week eight a comparable paper should show movement in the targeted components even if the grade lags, because grades follow marks rather than lead them. By week twelve, if nothing has moved in any of those categories, the plan is wrong and continuing is the expensive choice.

faqs.question: Our child is at a 6 and wants a 7. Is more tutoring the answer?
faqs.answer: Less of it, applied more narrowly. At this position the gains are small and specific: extended-response structure, evaluation that commits to a judgement rather than listing both sides, the two marks a question that separate the top bands, and in internally assessed work the difference between a competent draft and one that answers its own question. Four to eight narrow sessions comparing model answers against the student's own, line by line, then stop. Beyond that point the student's independent practice adds more than another tutored hour, and the hour crowds it out.

faqs.question: When is buying tutoring the wrong move entirely?
faqs.answer: Four situations we see regularly from this emirate. A student sleeping five hours and finishing homework at one in the morning needs a brutal audit of what gets dropped, not another commitment. A student carrying a Higher Level nobody needs should have a level-change conversation with the school first. A student in February with an untouched Extended Essay needs the core brought to a submittable state before any subject work. And a student who does not want this at all will sit through competent hours without changing. We put those findings in writing after the trial lesson.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our home in Ras Al Khaimah if we pay more?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India, and no payment changes that. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen and a document both sides can write on, which suits marked-script work particularly well because the paper, the mark scheme and the student's own answer can be on screen together. If having an adult physically present is the requirement, a local visiting tutor or a group class in Al Dhait is the right purchase and we will say so.

faqs.question: Should we support two subjects at once, or one properly?
faqs.answer: One properly, almost always, and the week audit usually proves it. A Diploma student in Ras Al Khaimah commutes, carries three Higher Levels plus the core, and typically has four or five genuinely free weekday hours. Two tutored subjects plus the independent work each requires does not fit inside that, and the hours between sessions are where the learning happens, so they get squeezed first. Choose the subject where a grade is both most at risk and most load-bearing for the next step, support that one, and revisit after a defined block.

faqs.question: Does the mock paper matter, or is it just a rehearsal?
faqs.answer: It is the most valuable data in the school year and the most wasted. A mock produces a question-level picture of exactly where marks are going, in the conditions that matter, two or three months before it counts. Most students read the grade on the front and file it. The useful response is to sort every lost mark into the five categories, total them, and build the spring plan from the totals. A tutor who has not asked to see the mock script by the second session is not using the best evidence available to them.

faqs.question: Do you publish the IB examination and results dates for Ras Al Khaimah schools?
faqs.answer: No, deliberately. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, and restating an unverified date across many pages turns one error into hundreds. Confirm every IB date with your school's coordinator or on the IB's own pages. Cambridge and Pearson dates are different: those come from the boards' published key-dates and timetable documents and are attributed, which is why Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE window appears on this page and an IB window does not. Note also that the February and March sitting you may find in Cambridge's own key dates is offered to centres in India only, so it is not a window a Ras Al Khaimah candidate can be entered for; here the series are June and November.

faqs.question: How does a small Ras Al Khaimah cohort change where our starting point came from?
faqs.answer: It often means the starting point is a timetable artefact rather than an ability one, and separating those changes the plan. With a Diploma cohort in the tens, each subject runs one set, so two wanted Higher Levels can fall in the same block and a student ends up at Standard Level in a subject a degree route expects at Higher. A set may also have one teacher and no second specialist. Ask the school for the written option blocks and for who marks and moderates the internal assessment, then decide whether the gap is teaching or timetabling.

faqs.question: Is the first lesson genuinely free, and what do we get from it?
faqs.answer: It is free, no card is required and no condition is attached. It is taught by the tutor who would take the course rather than by a salesperson, and it is a lesson rather than a pitch. Afterwards you receive a written opinion: which of the common starting positions the student is in, what the lost marks are going to, a proposed block with a measurable target and an estimated number of sessions, and a plain statement if tutoring is not the constraint in this student's week. Sometimes that statement is the most useful thing in it.

ras-al-khaimah/best-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Fix the starting point, count the weeks, then choose
ras-al-khaimah/best-ib-tutor.closingBody: The families who get the most from IB support in Ras Al Khaimah are not the ones who searched hardest for a ranking. They are the ones who found a marked script, sorted the lost marks into categories, counted the weeks their school calendar actually leaves available, and then hired for the specific job those three things described. ras-al-khaimah/best-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects at Core and Extended tier. Each is matched against a named syllabus code rather than a subject label, because a student entered for 4MA1 sits a different paper from a classmate entered for 0580, even inside the same year group.

intro.heading: Nobody can hand you a ranked list, so here is the test instead
paragraphs: The phrase assumes a league table exists. It does not. The RAK Department of Knowledge publishes judgements on schools, not on tutors. MoHRE issues a private tuition work permit, which establishes that someone may legally teach for money and says nothing about whether they can teach Extended-tier chemistry. No UAE body ranks individual tutors, and every site that claims to rank them is ranking its own customers. So a parent is left to build the judgement from evidence, in one conversation, before any money changes hands. That is what the rest of this page is for.

The evidence is narrower than most parents expect, and it is checkable. A strong International GCSE tutor can tell you the syllabus code your child is entered for, how many papers that code involves, which tier the entry sits at, and what the last marked script says about where the marks went. A weak one talks about rapport, confidence and experience, and cannot name a paper. That gap shows up inside the first ten minutes and it is the most reliable signal available to someone who does not teach the subject themselves.

Geography makes the question sharper here than it would be in Dubai. Ras Al Khaimah's private school set is small, and the emirate's subject cohorts are smaller still. A Year 11 group sitting Extended-tier Physics may number a dozen students, taught by one teacher who also covers Chemistry and Biology. Dubai, by contrast, enrolled 387,441 private school students across 227 schools in 2024-25 and licensed 17 separate curricula, which is why its tutor market is deep and the northern emirates' is thin. Hiring on the basis of proximity in Al Nakheel or Al Dhait usually means hiring a generalist.

Most families here are quietly choosing between four things rather than searching for one: a tuition centre in the city, an independent tutor who will drive to the address, an agency in Sharjah or Dubai whose tutors would have to make the same drive, and a specialist reached over live video. Those options differ on price, on travel, on the size of the pool they draw from, and on whether the person teaching has ever marked the paper in question. The table in the second section sets the four side by side with published rates and the month they were published.

IB Gram arranges one-to-one tuition delivered live online, over video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Ras Al Khaimah address; visiting tuition is a service offered only in India. That is stated plainly because the alternative is a page that lets a parent assume otherwise. What online delivery buys in this emirate is specific: the pool stops being people within a thirty-minute drive of Al Nakheel and starts being people who teach 0580, 0620 or 4MA1 for a living. On a narrow Extended-tier subject, that is the whole difference.

ras-al-khaimah/best-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Ras Al Khaimah families arrive at this search from three directions: an International GCSE year group heading for the June series, a Middle Years Programme cohort choosing options, and students who will carry IGCSE grades into a Diploma or A-level sixth form. The programmes below are the ones that actually appear in this emirate's schools.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The qualification most British-curriculum schools in the emirate enter. Each subject carries its own four-digit syllabus code, and the code governs the papers, the tier and the practical arrangements. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with centres allocated to one of six administrative zones; the zone decides which version of the timetable applies, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who sit the wrong one.
programmes.countryNote: Because Ras Al Khaimah schools are supervised by the emirate's Department of Knowledge rather than by KHDA or ADEK, parents here will not find a Dubai-style public inspection dashboard. Ask the school directly for the syllabus codes on the entry list and for the zone its exam centre falls into, because both affect what a tutor should be preparing your child for.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other board in regular use locally, with codes in the 4xx1 family: 4MA1 for mathematics, 4CH1 for chemistry, 4PH1 for physics. Pearson examines in a May or June window and again in November, and publishes provisional timetables for future series well ahead of each one. Some Pearson subjects are modular in structure, which changes how a revision plan should be sequenced across two years.
programmes.countryNote: A Ras Al Khaimah family with children at two different schools can easily have one child on Cambridge and one on Pearson, sitting what looks like the same subject. The November Pearson window matters here in particular: it gives a student who underperformed in June a second attempt inside the same academic year, without repeating Year 11 or changing school.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Taught at the emirate's IB continuum campuses on the southern coast. The MYP is assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, and reported on a 1-7 scale that does not map neatly onto IGCSE grades. Students moving from the MYP into an IGCSE year group, or into the Diploma, meet a different assessment language rather than harder content.
programmes.countryNote: Families comparing an MYP campus near Al Hamra with an IGCSE school on the city side are comparing two assessment systems, not two quality levels. If a transfer is on the table, the useful question is which subjects your child would be entered for at the receiving school and at which tier, since that decides whether any catching up is content or technique.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The sixth-form route many strong IGCSE students take next, either locally or in Sharjah and Dubai. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. IGCSE performance matters to it directly: Extended-tier mathematics and triple science are the usual expectation for Higher Level maths and sciences, and a Core-tier maths grade generally closes the Analysis and Approaches route.
programmes.countryNote: This is the main reason tier choice in Year 10 deserves attention in Ras Al Khaimah specifically. Local Diploma provision is concentrated in a small number of campuses, so a student who leaves IGCSE without the prerequisites for Higher Level maths may find the nearest alternative subject combination is in another emirate rather than down the road.

ras-al-khaimah/best-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the International GCSE subjects Ras Al Khaimah families ask about most, with the codes a tutor should be able to name without looking them up. Where Cambridge and Pearson differ in structure, the difference is stated rather than smoothed over.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.description: The tier decision dominates everything else. Cambridge 0580 Core caps the grade available; Extended carries the algebra, functions and trigonometry that a Higher Level maths course later assumes. Marks are lost most often in multi-step algebraic manipulation and in unstructured problem questions where no method is written down.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students aiming at Higher Level maths or engineering. It front-loads calculus, series and advanced trigonometry a year early. Students who cope with 0580 but struggle here are usually short on algebraic fluency rather than on understanding, which is a tractable gap.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry decide the grade more than any other topic, and organic chemistry decides the top band. Extended-tier papers reward precise use of command terms: describe, explain and deduce are marked differently, and treating them as synonyms is the most common avoidable loss.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and waves produce the steepest drops locally. The practical component is assessed through written papers rather than a live practical in most centres, which means students must be fluent in describing apparatus, variables and sources of error in words they have rarely practised.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content-heavy and deceptively easy to revise badly. Students reread notes and score the same mark twice. Gains come from converting recall into the extended-response structure the paper wants, and from the data-handling questions where graph reading beats memorisation.

subjects.name: English Language (0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the summary question carry weight out of proportion to the time students spend on them. Marks go missing in reading-for-purpose tasks, where candidates paraphrase the passage instead of selecting and compressing it against the question's stated audience and form.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Common across the emirate's Indian-curriculum and bilingual intakes. The listening and speaking components are scheduled separately from the written papers, and families regularly discover the dates late. Preparation is technique-led rather than content-led.

subjects.name: Economics (0455) and Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Popular option choices that reward diagram accuracy and evaluation structure. The data-response questions are where grades separate: a candidate who can read a table and quantify a change outperforms one who has memorised definitions, every time.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables are the recurring stumbling block, not programming ability. Students who code confidently in a language still lose marks writing algorithms in the board's own notation, which is a specific and quickly fixable deficit.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language and Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Required study alongside the licensed international curriculum, with first-language and additional-language streams taught separately. Federal rules place Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies outside a school's curriculum discretion, so this runs in parallel with IGCSE whatever board the school uses.

subjects.name: Islamic Education
subjects.description: Delivered in separate classes by group, with the language of instruction differing between streams. Support here is about assessment language and written structure rather than content substitution, since using different or additional material without ministry permission is not permitted.

sections.heading: What this search can return, and what it cannot
paragraphs: A search for the best IGCSE tutor in Ras Al Khaimah returns advertising. That is not a complaint about the advertisers; it is a structural fact. There is no authority in the UAE that assesses individual tutors and publishes the result. The RAK Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah's authority, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods for schools. Its remit is institutional. A tutor working from their own home with four students is outside it entirely.

MoHRE sits closer to the question but answers a different one. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. It establishes legality. It is not a competence test, and it does not distinguish between a chemistry teacher of fifteen years and a first-year undergraduate.

So the word in the search has to be replaced with something testable. For an International GCSE subject, four pieces of evidence do almost all the work: the syllabus code your child is entered for, the number and structure of the papers under that code, the tier the entry sits at, and a reading of the last marked script that identifies where marks went rather than how many were lost. A tutor who can produce all four in a first conversation is demonstrating subject knowledge in the only form a non-specialist parent can verify. One who cannot is asking to be trusted on reputation, which is exactly what a search result already offered.

sections.heading: The four options a Ras Al Khaimah family is really choosing between
paragraphs: Almost nobody arrives at this search with a blank slate. There is usually a tuition centre someone has recommended in Al Nakheel, a neighbour's tutor who drives over on Saturdays, an agency in Sharjah or Dubai that answered an enquiry, and the possibility of teaching over video. Those four are different products. They differ on hourly price, on how much of that price is travel, on how large a pool the tutor is drawn from, and on whether the person teaching has marked the paper your child will sit.

The pool size is the variable that matters most in this emirate and the one least often discussed. A visiting arrangement draws from people who live within a reasonable drive of your address. On the northern strip or on Al Marjan Island, that is a short list in any subject and frequently an empty one in Extended-tier physics or Additional Mathematics. A tuition centre draws from its own staff, who are typically generalists covering a phase rather than specialists covering a code. Online delivery draws from everyone who teaches the code, wherever they are, which is why it is the answer to subject scarcity rather than to cost.

Price moves in the opposite direction to convenience. Published market figures put visiting one-to-one tuition in the UAE at AED 180-500 per hour with travel inside the fee, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The centre looks cheapest per hour until the ratio is counted: a group of eight in a revision class is not one-to-one teaching priced lower, it is a different service. The table sets the four options against each other on the terms a parent actually decides on.

sections.heading: Ten minutes of questions that separate a specialist from a confident generalist
paragraphs: This is the part a parent can do without knowing the subject. The questions below are not a quiz about chemistry; they are about whether the person in front of you works at the level of the paper. A tutor who teaches a code regularly answers them flatly and quickly, the way a mechanic names a part. One who does not will generalise, and the generalisation is the signal.

Run the conversation before any trial session, not after. A trial lesson is a poor filter on its own, because a warm, organised adult who is pleasant with teenagers looks identical in forty-five minutes to a subject specialist. What separates them is whether the plan after the session names topics and papers or names attitudes. Ask for that plan in writing, however short, and read it for specifics.

Pay particular attention to the answer about the marked script. A tutor who asks to see the last two marked pieces before quoting a plan is working from evidence. A tutor who proposes a programme before seeing any of your child's work is selling a programme. The second is not dishonest, but it cannot be targeted, and targeting is the entire economic case for one-to-one teaching over a revision class that costs a fraction as much per head.

Two answers are worth weighing more heavily than the rest. The first is the one about coursework, because it is the only question on the list where the correct answer is a refusal, and a tutor who hedges there has told you how they will behave in an internal assessment week. The second is the exit question. A family that has paid a term's fees up front has lost the ability to change a decision cheaply, which is the main protection a parent has when a match turns out to be wrong. Neither answer requires you to know any chemistry.

sections.heading: Syllabus codes: the fastest filter available to a parent
paragraphs: Subject names are almost useless as a specification. Two students in Al Dhait can both be doing IGCSE chemistry and be sitting different numbers of papers, different practical arrangements and different grading structures, because one school entered Cambridge 0620 and the other entered Pearson 4CH1. A tutor who works at code level knows this without being told. A tutor who works at subject level will teach the overlap and discover the difference in April.

Getting the codes takes one email to the school office or one look at the exam entry statement, and it is the highest-value ten minutes available to a parent in Year 10. The codes also resolve a second question that causes real confusion locally: whether a child can sit a subject the school does not teach. Entry as a private candidate is possible through a registered exam centre, but the centre, the zone and the entry deadline all follow from the code, and the deadlines sit months before the papers.

Cambridge publishes its key dates series by series, and for a UAE candidate the series are June and November - the extra February and March sitting in those documents is offered to centres in India only. Read a June series in order and the sequence is: final entries in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper and on a date the centre prints on the statement of entry; forecast grades on Cambridge's published deadline for that series, close to the window; papers in June on the timetable for the centre's administrative zone; results on Cambridge International Direct in August; certificates later in the year. November shifts the same sequence earlier at the entry end and later at the results end. Pearson's International GCSE November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are the published figures to plan against; always open the board's live timetable rather than relying on a restatement, including this one.

sections.heading: Core and Extended, and the grade ceiling nobody mentions at parents' evening
paragraphs: The tier decision is the one place where a quiet administrative choice sets a hard limit on an outcome. Core-tier entry in Cambridge mathematics restricts the grades available; Extended-tier entry opens the full range and assumes more algebra, more trigonometry and more problem-solving under time pressure. Pearson structures the same decision as Foundation and Higher. The school makes the entry, often sensibly, on the basis of how a student is performing in Year 10. Parents frequently do not realise a decision has been made at all.

It matters beyond the grade on the certificate. Core-tier mathematics generally closes the route into Higher Level Analysis and Approaches in the Diploma, and makes an A-level mathematics course difficult to start. In an emirate where sixth-form options are concentrated in a handful of campuses, closing a route is more consequential than it would be in Dubai, because the alternative is not a different school ten minutes away. A student who wanted engineering and discovers in Year 12 that the maths prerequisite is missing has a problem that is expensive to solve.

The practical consequence for tutoring is about timing rather than intensity. A student who is borderline between tiers in the first term of Year 10 has a real window: the algebraic fluency that separates the tiers is teachable, and it is teachable fastest before the content gets harder. The same student in February of Year 11, after entries have closed, has a different and narrower job to do. If your child is anywhere near that line, the useful question to the school is not how they are doing but which tier they are being entered for, and when that becomes final.

sections.heading: What the northern-emirates market charges, and why the dearest is not automatically the strongest
paragraphs: Published rates in this market are wide and the spread is not primarily about quality. It is about what is inside the hour. A visiting tutor's fee contains a drive. A premium rate frequently contains scarcity rather than skill: a subject that few people teach costs more because few people teach it. An agency rate contains the agency. Reading the band without reading what sits inside it is how families end up paying for travel they could have avoided and calling it quality.

Three of the main competitor sites in this market publish no hourly figure at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Ras Al Khaimah family transacts in. The figures in the table below are market rates published by named providers in October 2026, not IB Gram's price list. For what a specific subject, tier and session length would cost, the honest answer is a short consultation and a first trial session at no charge, one per family, arranged after that conversation.

One useful piece of context when weighing the numbers: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai will not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. School costs holding flat does not mean tutoring costs hold flat, but it does mean a family budgeting for the exam year has one fewer moving part than in previous cycles. Set the tutoring decision against the full picture: two sessions a week across an exam year is a material commitment and worth sizing before it starts.
