sections.heading: The three topics that decide a 0620 grade
paragraphs: Across marked Extended chemistry scripts the same three areas account for most of the loss, and they are not evenly difficult. Moles and stoichiometry come first, not because the arithmetic is hard but because everything downstream depends on it: concentration, yield, limiting reagents, titration calculation and gas volumes all collapse if the mole concept is shaky. A student who cannot move confidently between mass, moles and particles is losing marks in four or five separate places on the paper for one reason.

Electrolysis is second, and the failure there is conceptual rather than computational. Students memorise the products of specific electrolyses and are then asked about an unfamiliar electrolyte, where the reasoning — which ion is attracted where, which is discharged in preference, what happens at each electrode and why — has to be reconstructed rather than recalled. Half-equations are the usual sticking point, and they are learnable in two sessions once the pattern is explicit instead of implicit.

Organic chemistry is third and is the most over-feared. It looks like memorisation and is actually pattern recognition: homologous series behave consistently, functional groups react predictably, and the reaction pathways form a small map that can be drawn on one page. Students who try to learn organic chemistry as a list of facts find it enormous. Students who learn the map find it among the more tractable parts of the syllabus, and that reframing is often a single session's work.

What should not be on this list is the rest of the syllabus. States of matter, atomic structure, the Periodic Table and chemistry of the environment are generally well scored, and spending a deadline-constrained plan on them because they appear early in the contents list is how twelve weeks gets wasted. The sequencing rule is simple: fix what is costing marks, in order of how much it is costing, and verify with a second marked paper at the halfway point.

sections.heading: Switching from Core to Extended chemistry, and what it costs in weeks
paragraphs: Occasionally a strong Core candidate wants to move up, usually because a post-16 science route has come into view. It is a legitimate ambition and the honest answer is that it costs weeks rather than willpower. The Extended tier covers the same twelve topic areas with additional supplement content, and that supplement is where A and A* separate: deeper stoichiometry, more demanding electrolysis, redox in terms of electron transfer, additional organic chemistry and more quantitative work throughout.

In Ras Al Khaimah the practical constraint is the school rather than the content. With one chemistry pathway per year group, moving a student between tiers in Year 11 means asking a teacher to deliver supplement content to a single student outside lesson time, and most schools in this emirate will say honestly that they cannot. So the switch, where it happens, is largely carried privately, and a family should know the size of that commitment before starting rather than discovering it in week five.

The table below gives working estimates for each supplement area, assuming the Core content underneath is already secure and the student does the between-session work. They are estimates, not promises. The decision point is the entry deadline, which falls months before the paper. A Ras Al Khaimah candidate sits either the June series or the November series, and for June the papers run from May into June while the final entry closes in the spring, well before them. That puts the Core-or-Extended conversation in the autumn and winter terms, with the school and supported by marked evidence, rather than in the weeks before the first paper when the tier has already been submitted on the entry. Cambridge's February and March sitting is offered in India only, so its deadlines do not apply to a RAK student; the date that binds you is the one printed on your centre's statement of entry.

The published UAE bands are AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified online subject tutor, with Unitors quoting AED 150 as its IGCSE starting rate, and AED 200 to AED 450 an hour and above for an examined-subject specialist, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table giving the 200 to 450-plus band. At the cheap end of the market, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52; at the named-premium end, BartyED quotes AED 650.

Multiply those by the shape of the plan and the totals are easy to check. Twelve weeks at one session a week is twelve hours. Twelve weeks at two sessions a week is twenty-four. A three-to-five session topic block is what it says. The table below runs those numbers across the qualified and specialist bands so a family can see the range before anybody quotes them anything, and so they can hold another provider's quote against the same published figures. Nothing here is an IB Gram price; our figure is quoted after the free trial lesson.

One comparison worth making. Over a three-month countdown the specialist monthly band and the twenty-four-hour calculation land in roughly the same territory, which is a useful cross-check: if a quote sits far outside both, ask what the extra is buying. And nobody should be quoting a price against a promised grade, because no tutor can promise one.

sections.heading: The first six weeks: what a parent should actually be able to see
paragraphs: Chemistry is not a subject most parents can assess directly, which makes it one of the easiest to be sold badly. The protection is not expertise but evidence, and the evidence should be specified before the first session rather than requested later when something feels wrong. Three checkpoints across the first six weeks are enough, and each one produces an artefact a parent can look at without understanding the chemistry inside it.

Week two produces a marked full paper with topic-level scores. Not a comment, not an assessment summary — a script with marks on it and a table showing how many marks were lost in each of the twelve topic areas. That document is the basis of the whole plan, and if it does not exist by week two the plan does not exist either. Week four produces marked homework on the first repaired topic, with a short timed set showing whether the repair held under pressure.

Week six produces a second full marked paper, and this is the checkpoint that matters. Compared against week two it shows movement or it does not. Movement in the targeted topics with the rest flat is exactly right. Movement everywhere is unlikely and worth a sceptical question. No movement anywhere after six sessions means the plan is wrong, and the honest response is to change the focus, change the tutor, or tell the family that the timeline is shorter than the ambition. The table sets out the checkpoints so they can be agreed up front.

sections.heading: How a Ras Al Khaimah student practises chemistry they cannot run at home
paragraphs: The reasonable objection to online science tutoring is the laboratory, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a reassurance. A student cannot electrolyse copper sulphate over a video call, and nobody should claim otherwise. What they can do, and what the examination actually assesses, is a set of skills that are entirely paper-based: describing a method precisely enough for somebody else to follow, identifying independent and dependent variables, naming sources of error and saying how each would be reduced, reading scales to the correct precision, tabulating results with units and appropriate decimal places, and drawing a conclusion that the data actually supports.

Every one of those is examined in writing, in both practical forms, and every one of them transfers to a shared screen without loss. The sessions use the student's own school practical sheets where they exist and past questions where they do not, and the work is the student's writing being corrected rather than a demonstration being watched. For the alternative-to-practical paper this is the whole of the preparation. For the practical test it is the half that school lab time does not reliably cover, because a school lesson optimises for completing the experiment rather than for exam technique.

There is also a specific Ras Al Khaimah argument here, and it is about who is available rather than about format. The emirate's specialist teaching pool is small, and chemistry at Extended level with a practical component is a genuinely specialist job. Searching within driving distance of Al Hamra Village or Digdaga returns very few people. Searching for someone who has marked 0620 papers returns a national pool. In a twelve-week plan, getting the right specialist in week one matters considerably more than how far away they live.

sections.heading: Starting a 0620 countdown, and the honest availability answer
paragraphs: Two things start a timeline plan: the date of the paper and a photograph of the last marked chemistry script. Send those with the school and the year group, and a 0620 specialist will come back with the topic sequence, the number of sessions, and a direct answer about what is achievable in the weeks available. That answer is sometimes narrower than a parent hoped, and it is better delivered in week one than discovered in week nine. A free trial lesson with the same tutor follows, at no charge.

Scheduling takes the Ras Al Khaimah geography seriously. Families in Mina Al Arab, Al Hamra Village and Al Marjan Island realistically start on a weekday at 7.30pm or later; Al Nakheel, Al Dhait and Khuzam can often manage earlier. Sessions are 60 minutes by default and 90 where a full timed paper is the point of the session. Rescheduling with reasonable notice is free, and during school mock weeks the plan pauses deliberately rather than competing with the school's own assessment schedule.

The availability disclosure matters more in the final term than at any other point in the year. Chemistry specialists at Extended level are in heaviest demand in the eight weeks before a main series, which is exactly when most families start looking. When nobody suitable is free at your hour we say so, and offer a different time with the specialist you asked for, an available tutor whose 0620 experience is described precisely enough to judge, or a dated place on the list. We will not put a general science tutor into a twelve-week Extended chemistry countdown and describe them as a specialist, because with twelve weeks on the clock there is no time to recover from that.

process.title: Send the date and the marked script
process.description: The paper date, the school, the year group and a photograph of the last marked chemistry paper. Those two things are enough for a specialist to sequence the twelve topic areas by mark value and to say what is realistic in the weeks remaining.

process.title: Get the honest timeline answer first
process.description: Before any money is discussed you are told what the available weeks can and cannot cover. A six-week plan that fixes two topics properly beats a six-week plan that touches four, and the choice should be made deliberately in week one.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the same tutor
process.description: Sixty minutes with the 0620 specialist who would run the countdown, working on questions from the marked script rather than a generic diagnostic. Nothing is paid until after that lesson has happened.

process.title: Agree the three evidence checkpoints
process.description: A marked paper at week two, marked homework with a timed set at week four, and a second marked paper at week six. Agreeing these up front is what lets a parent judge progress in a subject they cannot assess themselves.

process.title: Schedule the practical component explicitly
process.description: The practical or alternative paper is worth a fifth of the grade and is the component students ignore. It is timetabled into the plan at weeks four and three rather than left to whatever time remains at the end.

process.title: Reserve the last fortnight for timed papers
process.description: No new content inside two weeks of the paper. The final sessions are full papers under exam conditions with corrections written by the student, because reliability under pressure is a separate skill from knowing the chemistry.

whyPoints.title: The plan is built from the date backwards
whyPoints.description: Topics are sequenced by how many marks each is currently costing, not by syllabus order. That one change is why a twelve-week countdown produces movement where a term of general revision often does not.

whyPoints.title: Three checkpoints a parent can read
whyPoints.description: A marked paper at week two, a timed set at week four, a second marked paper at week six. You do not need to understand stoichiometry to see whether the targeted topics moved, which is the point of specifying the evidence in advance.

whyPoints.title: The practical component is scheduled, not assumed
whyPoints.description: A fifth of the grade comes from the practical or alternative paper and most students allocate it no revision at all. It is the highest-return block available to them and it is written into the plan.

whyPoints.title: Travel time counted as part of the budget
whyPoints.description: From Al Hamra Village or Mina Al Arab, a weekday in-home session costs around two hours of driving a week — roughly three sessions of teaching across a twelve-week plan. Remote delivery puts that time back into the chemistry.

whyPoints.title: Figures you can reproduce
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page names the provider or survey that published it, and the block totals are simple multiplication you can check. Three of six competitor pages reviewed in October 2026 published no price at all.

whyPoints.title: No promised outcome, in writing or otherwise
whyPoints.description: Nobody here will attach a grade to a fee. The honest product is a sequence, marked evidence and a visible trend, and a provider offering a specific score in exchange for a block should be read with real scepticism.

faqs.question: We are twelve weeks from the chemistry exam. Is it too late to start 0620 support?
faqs.answer: Twelve weeks is a workable countdown and it is the most common starting point. What it rules out is covering everything. The plan sequences the twelve topic areas by how many marks each is currently costing, repairs the two or three most expensive, schedules the practical component, and reserves the final fortnight for timed papers with no new content. A specialist should tell you in week one what those weeks can realistically cover, and that answer is sometimes narrower than you hoped. With six weeks rather than twelve the same structure applies, with fewer topics chosen deliberately rather than four attempted badly.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 0620 Paper 5 and Paper 6?
faqs.answer: One is a practical test carried out with apparatus; the other is an alternative-to-practical written paper about experimental work. Both are worth a fifth of the 0620 grade and the school decides which its candidates sit, based on its centre arrangements. The preparation differs: the practical test rewards method discipline, accurate reading of scales and real-time recording, while the alternative paper rewards describing method, identifying variables, naming sources of error and interpreting results tables. Confirm which one your child has been entered for with the exams officer, because a surprising number of families do not know twelve weeks out.

faqs.question: Which 0620 topics should a Year 11 student fix first?
faqs.answer: Whichever is costing the most marks, which a marked paper tells you in ten minutes. At Extended level the usual answer is moles and stoichiometry, because concentration, yield, limiting reagents, titration calculation and gas volumes all depend on it, so one weakness shows up in four or five places on the paper. Electrolysis usually comes second and organic chemistry third. What should not come first is states of matter or atomic structure, which most students already score well on and which only appear early because of where they sit in the contents list.

faqs.question: How long does it take to learn moles properly?
faqs.answer: Four to six sessions for most students, with short daily practice in between, assuming ratio and proportion from mathematics are already secure. The reason it takes that long is not conceptual difficulty but breadth of application: the same idea has to work for mass, particles, gas volumes, solution concentration, titration and percentage yield, and students typically understand it in one context and not the others. The test of whether it has landed is a mixed set of calculation questions in random order. Handling those confidently is what recovers marks across the rest of the paper.

faqs.question: Can my child do 0620 practical work from home in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: No home laboratory is needed and nobody should suggest otherwise. If the alternative-to-practical paper has been entered, no apparatus is required at all: the paper assesses describing method, identifying variables, naming sources of error, reading scales, tabulating results and drawing supported conclusions, all in writing. If the practical test has been entered, the apparatus work happens at school and private sessions add the exam technique that school lab time does not reliably cover, because a lesson optimises for completing the experiment rather than for examination conditions. Both forms of preparation transfer to a shared screen without loss.

faqs.question: How many weeks does a Core to Extended switch in chemistry take?
faqs.answer: Expect it to be carried largely privately and to cost a real block of weeks. The Extended tier covers the same twelve topic areas plus supplement content: deeper stoichiometry, half-equations and preferential discharge in electrolysis, redox as electron transfer, additional organic pathways and more quantitative work throughout. On working estimates that is four to six sessions for stoichiometry, two to three for electrochemistry, two for redox, three to four for organic and two for analysis. In Ras Al Khaimah most schools run one chemistry pathway per year group, so they often cannot deliver supplement content to a single student.

faqs.question: What should we see after the first six weeks of 0620 tutoring?
faqs.answer: A second full marked paper, compared against the one taken in week two, showing movement in the specific topics that were targeted. That is the checkpoint that matters, and agreeing it before the first session is the best protection a parent has in a subject they cannot assess themselves. Movement in the targeted topics with the rest flat is exactly the right result. No movement anywhere after six sessions means the plan is wrong, and the honest response is to change the focus or the tutor rather than to wait and see at week ten.

faqs.question: What does a twelve-week block of chemistry tutoring cost in total?
faqs.answer: At published UAE market bands, twelve weeks at one session a week is twelve hours, costing roughly AED 1,800 to AED 3,600 at the qualified band of AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, or AED 2,400 to AED 5,400 at the examined-specialist band of AED 200 to AED 450. Two sessions a week doubles both. Unitors publishes AED 150 as its IGCSE starting rate and TutorChase quotes AED 270; Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table gives the specialist band. As a cross-check, Bestimate's specialist exam-year monthly estimate is AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above. IB Gram quotes after the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Is organic chemistry really the hardest part of 0620?
faqs.answer: It is the most feared and rarely the most expensive. Treated as a list of facts it looks enormous; treated as a map it is among the more tractable parts of the syllabus, because homologous series behave consistently and functional groups react predictably. The reframing is often a single session's work, after which the reaction pathways can be drawn on one page and revised from it. The genuinely expensive topic at Extended level is usually moles and stoichiometry, because it sits underneath so many other questions. Organic chemistry tends to cost three to four sessions once the pattern is explicit.

faqs.question: How is 0620 electrolysis examined at Extended level?
faqs.answer: Through reasoning about unfamiliar electrolytes rather than recall of familiar ones, which is why memorisation fails here. A question may name an electrolyte the student has never seen and expect them to work out which ion moves to which electrode, which is discharged in preference, what is produced at each electrode and why. Half-equations are the usual sticking point. Once the pattern is made explicit instead of implicit, this is a two-to-three-session repair, and it is frequently the second-largest mark recovery available after stoichiometry. Past questions on unfamiliar electrolytes are the only reliable practice.

faqs.question: Does my child need a lab to score well on the chemistry practical paper?
faqs.answer: Not for the alternative-to-practical paper, which is entirely written and requires no apparatus. For the practical test, the apparatus work happens at school and cannot be replicated at home, but the marks lost there are usually technique marks rather than manipulation marks: results recorded without units, scales read to the wrong precision, methods described too loosely for another person to follow, error sources named in general terms instead of specifically. All of that is correctable in writing, over a shared screen, using school practical sheets and past questions.

faqs.question: How often should 0620 sessions run in the final term?
faqs.answer: Two a week is the usual shape inside twelve weeks where there are gaps across two or three topic areas: one session repairs content, the other applies it to past questions under time pressure. One a week is enough where the student mainly needs sequence and accountability rather than teaching, and it costs half as much. More than two is rarely productive, because improvement comes from attempted questions between sessions rather than from contact time, and a student who is not completing homework converts extra sessions into extra explanation — which is the thing that was not working already.

faqs.question: What does a 0620 revision week actually look like?
faqs.answer: In a countdown plan, one session teaches or repairs the current topic and sets a question set from past papers. The student completes it during the week. It is marked before the next session, so the following hour starts with corrections rather than with new material, and the lost marks are attributed to specific causes rather than to a general comment. Every fourth week a full timed paper replaces the teaching session. The pattern is deliberately repetitive, because reliability under exam conditions comes from repetition and not from variety.

faqs.question: Should we pause 0620 tutoring during school mock exams?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and a good tutor will suggest it before you ask. Mock weeks already consume the student's evenings, the school's own assessment produces exactly the marked evidence a plan needs, and competing with it adds load without adding progress. The sensible pattern is to pause during the mocks and resume with the marked mock papers in hand, which is a far better diagnostic than anything bought separately. Rescheduling with reasonable notice should carry no charge; a provider that penalises a pause during school assessments has designed the arrangement around its own revenue.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover chemistry and biology for the same student?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and in a deadline plan it has a real advantage: one person sequences both subjects so their heaviest demands do not land in the same fortnight. The two share an assessment shape — multiple choice, theory, and a practical or alternative paper worth a fifth of the grade — so the practical technique work transfers directly between them. The trade-off is depth: a specialist in one subject at Extended level is usually stronger in it than a tutor covering both. Where that matters we say so rather than presenting a generalist as a subject specialist.

Send the date, the school, the year group and a photograph of the last marked 0620 script, and a specialist will sequence the twelve topic areas by mark value and tell you plainly what the remaining weeks can cover. A free trial lesson with that tutor follows at no charge, and the three evidence checkpoints are agreed before anything is paid. intro.heading: Where your child is now, and how many weeks are left
paragraphs: Most families arrive at this page with a date in mind and a vague sense of trouble. The date is a series, usually June. The trouble is a mock result, a comment in a report, or a child who says computer science is fine while quietly avoiding the programming questions. The useful first move is not to buy lessons. It is to work out precisely where the student is, precisely what the papers will ask in June, and then to be honest about what the number of weeks between those two points can change.

Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478 makes that arithmetic unusually clear, because the assessment has no hiding places. Two papers, each one hour forty-five minutes, each seventy-five marks, each exactly half the grade. Paper 1 Computer Systems covers the first six syllabus topics: data representation, data transmission, hardware, software, the internet and its uses, and automated and emerging technologies. Paper 2 Algorithms, Programming and Logic covers the remaining four: algorithm design and problem solving, programming, databases, and Boolean logic. There is no coursework and no project, so nothing is banked before the day.

What that structure means in practice is that the two papers have completely different time constants. Paper 1 is largely recall and explanation with a defined body of content; a motivated student can move it substantially in eight weeks of disciplined work, because the questions reward precise knowledge and the precise knowledge is finite. Paper 2 is skill. Writing an algorithm, dry-running it in a trace table, spotting an off-by-one error, completing a truth table under time pressure: these improve with repetition over months, not with revision over weeks. A family with ten weeks and a weak Paper 2 needs to know that before they spend anything.

Ras Al Khaimah sharpens the problem. The emirate's private sector is small and regulated by its own Department of Knowledge, which under the federal framework approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods here. A small sector means computer science is typically one set taught by one person, who may also be covering ICT and running the school network. Parents in Al Nakheel and Khuzam tell us the same story: the teaching is willing, the subject knowledge is real, and there is simply no capacity for one student to get twenty minutes a week of supervised algorithm writing.

So the honest proposition is this. A specialist who has marked hundreds of 0478 scripts is unlikely to live within driving distance of Al Rams or Digdaga, and searching for one locally is searching a list of two or three people. Over live video the same specialist is available on a Wednesday at six, with your child's own pseudocode on a shared screen and the trace table filled in together. The rest of this page is the detail: how to read the mock, what each paper demands, what eight or twenty or fifty weeks can do, and what the market charges for the privilege.

ras-al-khaimah/cambridge-igcse-computer-.programmesIntro: Computing qualifications in the UAE come in versions that look alike and assess very differently. Below are the four stages and variants a Ras Al Khaimah family meets, with what each demands and how it plays out in a small cohort where one teacher usually covers all of them.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science
programmes.description: Ten topics across two written papers of equal weight. Paper 1 Computer Systems examines data representation, data transmission, hardware, software, the internet and its uses, and automated and emerging technologies. Paper 2 Algorithms, Programming and Logic examines algorithm design and problem solving, programming, databases and Boolean logic. Programming skill is developed in class and then examined on paper in pseudocode, which is the single structural fact most families and some students have never been told.
programmes.countryNote: Where it runs in Ras Al Khaimah it is usually a single set. The teacher often also covers ICT and sometimes supports the school's own systems, so sustained one-to-one algorithm supervision is not realistically available in school hours. That is the specific gap one-to-one support fills here, rather than a general claim about teaching quality.

programmes.name: Computer Science, 9-1 graded variant
programmes.description: Cambridge issues a numerically graded version of IGCSE Computer Science alongside the lettered code. The syllabus content, the two papers and the examined skills are identical; what differs is the reported grade scale. Knowing which code is on the statement of entry matters for one practical reason: a target expressed as a grade 6 and a target expressed as a B are not the same statement, and a revision plan built on the wrong one is built on an assumption.
programmes.countryNote: Centres in the UAE use both codes depending on their reporting conventions. A thirty-second question to the exams officer settles which applies, and it is worth asking before any conversation with a school or a tutor about predicted grades.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Information and Communication Technology
programmes.description: The applied neighbour, and a genuinely different subject. ICT assesses practical competence with documents, spreadsheets, databases, presentations and web authoring through practical papers alongside a theory paper, rather than algorithmic thinking through pseudocode. A student who likes building things with software may do far better here; a student who likes working out why a program behaves as it does belongs in 0478. Families regularly confuse the two because both are often taught by the same person.
programmes.countryNote: Several campuses in the emirate offer ICT rather than Computer Science, or offer both in the same option block so only one is possible. If a student has been allocated the subject that fitted the timetable, that is worth discovering in Year 9 rather than in the first Year 10 assessment.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level Computer Science
programmes.description: The post-16 continuation, with substantially deeper theory and a programming project at A Level. Data structures, abstract data types, object-oriented programming, assembly language and computational thinking all arrive at once. Students who reached a good 0478 grade on Paper 1 recall alone find the step severe, because the post-16 course is weighted towards exactly the algorithmic skill that Paper 2 was measuring and they quietly avoided.
programmes.countryNote: Post-16 computer science provision is thin in the northern emirates. For a student likely to continue, the Paper 2 skills built now are the ones that matter in eighteen months, which changes how a Year 10 year should be spent even when the Year 11 grade looks safe.

ras-al-khaimah/cambridge-igcse-computer-.subjectsIntro: The grid below is the set of entries a Ras Al Khaimah computing student and their timetable neighbours actually sit, with codes as printed on a statement of entry. Each is a separate qualification with its own assessment pattern.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Two papers of 1 hour 45 minutes, 75 marks each. Paper 1 is content: data representation, transmission, hardware, software, the internet, emerging technologies. Paper 2 is skill: algorithms, programming in pseudocode, single-table databases with SQL, and Boolean logic. Marks leak on trace tables, on pseudocode syntax drift and on explanations that name a component without saying what it does.

subjects.name: Computer Science, 9-1 graded variant
subjects.description: The numerically graded version of the same qualification. Identical content, identical papers, identical examined skills; only the reported scale differs. Confirm the code on the statement of entry before setting a target grade, because translating between the two scales by guesswork is how a revision plan ends up aimed at the wrong place.

subjects.name: Information and Communication Technology (0417)
subjects.description: Practical papers on documents, spreadsheets, databases, presentations and web authoring alongside a theory paper. Rewards software competence and accuracy under time pressure rather than algorithmic reasoning. A student failing 0478 Paper 2 while enjoying building things is often in the wrong one of these two subjects, and the time to find out is Year 9.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Listed because 0478 Paper 2 leans on number work that the Extended tier reinforces: binary and hexadecimal conversion, place value, logical reasoning and precision with sequences. Extended also keeps A Level Computer Science realistically open, where a Core entry narrows the post-16 route without anyone announcing it.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Relevant where a student is heading towards computer science or engineering at a university that expects strong mathematics. Not required for 0478 itself. Worth considering ahead of a second humanity if the destination is quantitative, because the step into post-16 computing is mathematical as much as it is technical.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: The common pairing for students heading to engineering or computer systems. Shares a specific habit with 0478: precision in units, prefixes and significant figures, where a correct method with a sloppy final line still loses the mark. Students weak at that precision show it in both subjects at once.

subjects.name: Design and Technology (0445)
subjects.description: Included because it is the other subject that attracts students who like building, and because it occupies similar option blocks. A student choosing between 0478 and a making subject should be choosing on whether they enjoy reasoning about systems or producing artefacts, not on which sounds more employable.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Frequently paired with computing by students who imagine a technology career with a commercial edge. Case-based and command-word driven, so the habits it builds are argumentative rather than algorithmic. Worth knowing that it will not reinforce anything on Paper 2.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500)
subjects.description: Relevant to 0478 more than families expect. Paper 1 marks are lost on explanations that identify without explaining, which is a writing failure as much as a knowledge one. A student who cannot develop a point in two sentences loses marks across every topic on the paper.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Another common pairing, included for completeness on a commerce-and-computing timetable. Its eight-mark evaluation questions demand structured judgement, a different skill from the precise technical explanation 0478 rewards, so a student strong in one is not automatically strong in the other.

regions.note: The largest source of 0478 enquiries in the emirate. Short runs home from city-side campuses mean a 4.30pm or 5pm start is genuinely workable, which matters because algorithm practice goes badly after seven in the evening.

regions.note: British-curriculum provision nearby and a noticeably higher share of Year 10 enquiries. That is the better year to start: Paper 2 skill accumulates over months, and a student beginning in Year 10 has the window that a Year 11 starter does not.

regions.note: Larger households, often with siblings on different subjects. Back-to-back evening slots for two children are straightforward to schedule over video and effectively impossible to arrange with two visiting tutors in one evening.

regions.name: Al Hamra Village
regions.note: International and British provision on this side, with more students likely to continue computing post-16. For those students the Paper 2 skills built in Year 10 matter in eighteen months, not only in June.

regions.name: Mina Al Arab and Hayat Island
regions.note: Newer coastal communities with a longer run to the city-side campuses. Timelines here fail for logistical reasons rather than academic ones, which is exactly the failure a fixed video slot removes.

regions.name: Al Marjan Island
regions.note: Smaller resident population with frequent term-time travel. A revision timeline that survives two weeks abroad is worth more here than a nearby tutor, because a missed fortnight in Paper 2 practice is hard to recover.

regions.name: Al Mairid, Al Uraibi and Julphar
regions.note: Older city districts with established campuses. A share of enquiries from here involve students whose school offers ICT rather than Computer Science, and who are sitting 0478 as an additional entry.

sections.heading: Reading the mock as a diagnostic rather than as a grade
paragraphs: A 0478 mock percentage tells you almost nothing useful. The same fifty-two per cent can mean a student who knows the content and cannot write an algorithm, or a student who programmes competently and has never learned how a packet is assembled. Those two children need opposite terms of work, and the only way to tell them apart is to look at which questions lost the marks rather than at how many.

The quickest split is by paper. If Paper 1 is well below Paper 2, this is a content and precision problem: definitions that are nearly right, explanations that name a component without saying what it does, conversions attempted without method. That is the good news, because it is finite and it responds to weeks. If Paper 2 is well below Paper 1, it is a skill problem, and skill problems respond to months. A family that knows which one they have can plan; a family looking at a percentage cannot.

Inside Paper 2 the diagnosis goes further. A student who writes a plausible algorithm and then cannot complete the trace table has a dry-running gap: they are thinking in intentions rather than in steps, which is a specific and trainable fault. A student whose pseudocode drifts into Python syntax has a syntax discipline gap, which is the easiest fault in the subject to fix and one of the most expensive to leave. A student who cannot start a problem at all has a decomposition gap, which is the slowest of the three.

The table below is the diagnostic we actually run, in the form we send to parents. Send one marked mock script and a tutor will place your child on it within about fifteen minutes, with an estimate of how many weeks each gap takes to close. That estimate is the thing worth having before any money changes hands, because it is what determines whether tutoring is the right purchase at all this year.

sections.heading: Where they need to be: what the two papers demand on the day
paragraphs: The destination is specific and it is worth stating precisely, because a student revising towards a vague notion of knowing computer science will revise the comfortable parts. Paper 1 Computer Systems runs one hour forty-five minutes for seventy-five marks and covers six topics. Data representation deals with binary, hexadecimal, character sets, images, sound and compression. Data transmission covers packets, methods of transmission, USB and error detection. Hardware covers the central processing unit, the fetch-decode-execute cycle, input and output devices and storage. Software covers system software, operating systems, high and low level languages, translators and interrupts. The internet and its uses covers the web, cloud, cyber-security threats and countermeasures. Automated and emerging technologies covers automated systems, robotics and artificial intelligence.

Paper 2 Algorithms, Programming and Logic runs the same length for the same marks and covers four topics. Algorithm design and problem solving deals with computational thinking, pseudocode, flowcharts, trace tables, validation and test data, and standard methods such as searching, sorting, counting and totalling. Programming covers sequence, selection, iteration, data types, procedures and functions, arrays and file handling. Databases covers single-table structures, field types and SQL. Boolean logic covers gates, logic circuits and truth tables.

The structural fact that changes how a student should prepare is this: programming skill is developed in class in a real language, usually Python, Java or VB.NET, but the examination tests it on paper in pseudocode. A student who has spent two years writing Python in a code editor, with autocomplete and an interpreter telling them when a line is wrong, has never once done the examined task. They write code that works and lose marks for conventions they did not know existed. This is the single most common avoidable loss in the subject.

The other half of the same point is that nothing can be banked in advance. 0478 has no coursework, no project and no practical paper. Three and a half hours in one series decides the whole grade. That makes timed practice the main preparation rather than an optional extra, and it is why we sit full papers rather than working through question banks that feel productive and never test the clock.

sections.heading: What eight weeks can fix, and what needs a year
paragraphs: This is the section families most need and most pages in this market avoid, because an honest answer sometimes costs a sale. The weeks available determine what can be attempted, and pretending otherwise produces a disappointed parent in August and a student who concludes they are bad at the subject when in fact they were given an impossible schedule.

With six to eight weeks, the realistic targets are Paper 1 content on the topics the mock shows are weak, pseudocode syntax discipline, binary and hexadecimal method, truth tables, and examination timing. That is a genuine grade of movement for many students, and none of it is trivial. What six weeks cannot do is turn a student who freezes in front of an unfamiliar problem into one who decomposes it calmly, because that is a habit and habits do not form in six weeks.

With twelve to twenty weeks, trace tables and dry-running come into range, along with the standard algorithm patterns: linear search, bubble sort, totalling and counting with a running variable, validation loops. A student who can write and dry-run those from memory has most of what Paper 2 asks for in its mid-range questions. Decomposition of genuinely unfamiliar problems starts to improve but is not reliable yet.

With a full year or two, the subject can actually be built. Weekly supervised algorithm writing from Year 10 produces a student who reads a problem, breaks it into steps, writes it, dry-runs it and finds their own errors. That student does not need a revision block in Year 11; they need past papers and a clock. The table sets out the four windows with what each honestly delivers, and we say the same thing to a family in Al Nakheel with four weeks left as we say to one in Khuzam with two years.

sections.heading: Pseudocode against the language the school teaches
paragraphs: A student who has written Python competently for two years can still lose a third of the available marks on the programming questions, and the reason is purely conventional. The examination is answered in pseudocode. Cambridge publishes the conventions it expects, and they are specific: how a loop is opened and closed, how input and output are written, how a declaration looks, how a procedure differs from a function. A student who has never been shown those conventions writes Python, is understood by the examiner, and is marked against a scheme written for something else.

The habits that cause the loss are small and consistent. Colons and indentation carried over from Python. Semicolons and braces carried over from Java. Loop endings omitted because the editor never required them. Variable types left undeclared. None of these reflects a misunderstanding of the algorithm; every one of them costs marks on a paper where seventy-five marks decide half the grade.

The repair is short and it is the highest-return work available in 0478. Two to four weeks of writing short algorithms in pseudocode, by hand, to the published conventions, with a tutor marking the conventions as strictly as the logic. Students resist it for about a week, because they can already code and the exercise feels like a step backwards, and then the marks move and the resistance stops. We do this early in any block, whatever the family's timeline, because it is the cheapest grade improvement in the subject.

The understanding does transfer, and that is worth saying to a student who feels their Python is being dismissed. Sequence, selection, iteration, arrays, file handling and the idea of a function are the same ideas in every language, and a student who genuinely programmes has the hard part already. What they are missing is a dialect, and dialects are learned in a fortnight.
bullets: Loops opened and closed in the published pseudocode form, not Python indentation

sections.heading: Trace tables and the dry run: the skill that is only practice
paragraphs: If one skill separates a middling 0478 grade from a strong one, it is dry-running: taking a piece of code or an algorithm and walking through it line by line with a table of variable values, finding what it actually does rather than what it was meant to do. It appears directly in trace table questions and indirectly everywhere, because a student who can dry-run can check their own work and a student who cannot is guessing.

Students fail at it in a recognisable way. They fill the table with the values they expect rather than the values the code produces. They update a variable in the wrong order within an iteration. They lose track of a loop counter after the third pass and stop writing. They leave the table blank and write a sentence describing what the algorithm is for, which earns nothing. Every one of these is a discipline failure rather than a comprehension failure, and discipline is built by repetition under supervision.

The method is unglamorous. One trace table every session, every week, with the tutor insisting on a row per iteration and a column per variable, and refusing to accept a value that was not derived from the previous row. On a shared screen this works better than on paper, because the tutor can annotate the cell where the reasoning broke and the student keeps the corrected table afterwards. After eight or ten of these, most students start dry-running unprompted when they write their own algorithms, which is the point at which Paper 2 marks begin to move properly.

There is a reason this cannot be compressed. It is the same reason a student cannot learn to sight-read music in a fortnight. The skill is a sequence of small accurate steps performed under mild time pressure, and the only input that improves it is repetitions with correction. A family with eight weeks can start it; a family with a year can finish it. We say which of those applies before taking any money.

sections.heading: Boolean logic, databases and the topics taught last
paragraphs: Two topics on Paper 2 are reliably underprepared across every campus we see, and for the same structural reason: they are taught at the end of the course, in the term when mock examinations are eating the timetable, and nobody comes back to them. Boolean logic is the first. Single-table databases and SQL are the second. Together they are worth enough marks to decide a grade boundary.

Boolean logic is almost pure technique. There is a small set of gates, a small set of truth tables, and a skill in reading a logic circuit from left to right without losing track of an intermediate output. The errors are mechanical: a NAND read as an AND, an intermediate value not written down, a truth table with rows in an inconsistent order so a line is duplicated and another missed. Three to five weeks of short drills, fifteen minutes at a time, converts this from a liability into reliable marks. It is the second-cheapest improvement in the subject after pseudocode conventions.

Databases are similar in shape. The syllabus deals with single-table structures, appropriate field types and primary keys, and a finite set of SQL query patterns: selecting fields, filtering with conditions, ordering results, and simple aggregate functions. A student who has written half a dozen of each will handle anything the paper asks. A student who skipped the topic because it arrived in the last fortnight of teaching meets it cold in the examination and loses the lot.

We front-load both in any revision block, which surprises students who expect to start with programming. The reason is arithmetic rather than pedagogy: these are the topics where the ratio of marks gained to hours invested is highest, and in a short timeline that ratio is the only thing that should decide the running order.

sections.heading: The series counted backwards, and the weeks that vanish here
paragraphs: A timeline is only as good as the dates it is built on, and two sets of dates bind. Cambridge International runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series. Every examination centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. Parents should hold a printed copy of the right one.

The second set is the entry deadlines, which fall far earlier than families expect. Ras Al Khaimah candidates sit the June series or the November series; the February and March sitting belongs to India, so its dates are no use to anyone here. For June, the papers run from May into June and the final entry closes in the spring, months rather than weeks ahead, with forecast grades due to Cambridge before the papers begin and results reaching centres on Cambridge International Direct in August. The November series mirrors that half a year later: entries over the summer, papers in October and November, results in late January. Where the school runs Pearson Edexcel instead, the published November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, which is what an autumn series actually looks like. Whichever board your centre uses, the gap between the entry deadline and the first paper is the number that matters, and it is measured in months.

Then there are the weeks that disappear from a Ras Al Khaimah calendar and never appear in a revision plan written in September. Mock examinations swallow a fortnight. Ramadan shortens the school day and shifts family routines, and it frequently falls close enough to a summer series that pausing for a month is more expensive than it looks; shortened days also free up afternoon slots that are unavailable the rest of the year, so the sensible response is to move the session rather than suspend it. Eid, half-terms and family travel take more. A plan built on twenty calendar weeks usually has fourteen working ones in it.

The table reads the year backwards from the papers. Confirm every date against the official Cambridge timetable for your centre's zone and examination year on cambridgeinternational.org rather than against this page, and ask the exams officer which zone the centre sits in.

sections.heading: What the travel premium buys, and what a specialist costs here
paragraphs: Start with the premium, because it is the part of this market nobody explains. Published market figures put in-home one-to-one tutoring in this country at AED 180 to 350 an hour according to Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, with independent home tutors quoted from AED 200 to 500 inclusive of travel. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The gap between those two bands is the travel premium, and the question worth asking is what it actually purchases.

It purchases a commute and a smaller pool. For a subject like 0478 in the northern emirates, the second part dominates. The number of people within driving distance of Mina Al Arab who teach Cambridge Computer Science, can dry-run an algorithm in front of a student and are free on a weekday evening is very small. A parent who hires the best available tutor from that list has done something quite different from hiring a 0478 specialist, and the difference shows up in whether trace tables improve.

The rest of the market, for context. Budget online tutoring runs from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52; at that level a generalist can supervise homework but will not mark pseudocode conventions. An IGCSE, IB or A Level specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate putting specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. Premium named tutors go further, with BartyED at AED 650. Monthly packages circulate at around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

Those are all other providers' published figures for this market in 2026, named so that you can check them yourself. None is an IB Gram price, and we publish no rate card on these pages, because the honest number depends on the timeline, the gap and how many sessions are genuinely needed, and a figure printed here would be out of date before your child's series. Book the free trial, watch a trace table being worked, and get a number in writing afterwards.

sections.heading: What a tutor can legitimately do, and how to check they may work here
paragraphs: Two boundaries are worth knowing before a family hires anyone, and both are matters of record rather than opinion. The first is what a tutor may do with a student's work. 0478 has no coursework, no project and no internally assessed component, so the academic-honesty questions that surround coursework subjects do not arise in the same form here. Everything a tutor marks is practice, and the only work an examiner ever sees is what the student writes alone in the hall. That is a simpler position than most subjects offer, and it is worth stating.

What a tutor should not do, even in practice work, is supply finished answers that the student copies into a school assignment and submits as their own. Where a campus sets a programming task that contributes to an internal report, support means teaching the technique and reviewing the student's own attempt. The same rule covers past papers and mark schemes: a tutor references and links the official material on cambridgeinternational.org rather than redistributing syllabus documents, papers or mark schemes, because reproducing those is a copyright matter rather than a grey area.

The second boundary is legal and it applies to every private tutor in the country. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from the ministry are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fee schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

The official application route is the ministry's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time. A parent may reasonably ask any tutor whether they hold the permit. Separately, a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs an educational services permit for a training institute from the Knowledge and Human Development Authority; IB Gram occupies no premises in the UAE, holds no such permit and claims no regulator endorsement of any kind.

process.title: Send the mock script, not the percentage
process.description: One marked mock paper tells a tutor which of the six common gaps your child has, and a percentage tells them nothing. We read it question by question, split it by paper, and come back with a placement on the diagnostic table and an estimate of how many weeks each gap needs to close.

process.title: Agree what the available weeks can do
process.description: Before anything is booked we write down what your timeline can realistically achieve and what it cannot. A family with five weeks and a decomposition gap is told plainly that the gap needs a term. That conversation is free and occasionally ends with us recommending nothing.

process.title: Watch a trace table in the free trial
process.description: In the trial lesson, ask the tutor to work a trace table with your child on a shared screen. A tutor who insists on a row per iteration and refuses a value not derived from the row above is teaching the examined skill. A tutor who explains the algorithm's purpose and moves on is not.

process.title: Fix the pseudocode conventions first
process.description: Whatever the timeline, the first two to four weeks go on writing short algorithms by hand in examined pseudocode. Students who already code resist this and then stop resisting when the marks move. It is the cheapest grade improvement available in 0478 and it is almost never covered properly in school.

process.title: Review against timed papers on a fixed cycle
process.description: Every four to six weeks a timed paper is marked and compared with the last. If the gap the plan targeted is not closing, the approach changes or we tell you the hour is not earning its money. If no 0478 specialist is free in your slot, we say so rather than putting a generalist in it.

whyPoints.title: The timeline is stated before the sale
whyPoints.description: We write down what the weeks you have can achieve and what they cannot, and we do it before any payment. A family with four weeks and a dry-running gap deserves to hear that the gap needs a term, not a reassuring sentence followed by an invoice.

whyPoints.title: Pseudocode conventions are treated as the priority they are

whyPoints.title: Dry-running is drilled, not explained
whyPoints.description: One supervised trace table every session, with a row per iteration and no value accepted that was not derived from the row above. On a shared screen the broken cell is annotated in place and the student keeps the corrected table. This is the skill that moves Paper 2 and it responds only to repetition.

faqs.question: What does a weak 0478 mock result actually tell me?
faqs.answer: On its own, very little. The same mark can describe a student who knows the content and cannot write an algorithm, or one who programmes well and has never learned how a packet is assembled. Those two need opposite terms of work. Split the script by paper first: Paper 1 below Paper 2 is a content and precision gap, which responds to six to ten weeks. Paper 2 below Paper 1 is a skill gap, which responds to months rather than weeks. Send the marked script and a tutor will place your child precisely and estimate how long each gap takes.

faqs.question: Is Paper 2 harder than Paper 1 in Computer Science?
faqs.answer: Not harder, but slower to improve. Both papers run one hour forty-five minutes for seventy-five marks and each is half the grade. Paper 1 is a defined body of content across six topics, so disciplined revision moves it in weeks. Paper 2 tests skill across four topics: writing algorithms, dry-running them in trace tables, SQL queries and Boolean logic. Skill accumulates with supervised repetition over months. A family planning a timeline needs that difference, because an eight-week block aimed at Paper 2 fluency will disappoint while the same block aimed at Paper 1 content often succeeds.

faqs.question: My son codes well in Python but loses marks on the programming questions. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the examination is answered in pseudocode and he has been writing Python. Cambridge publishes the conventions it expects for loops, declarations, input and output, procedures and functions, and a student who has never been shown them writes code that works and is marked against a scheme written for something else. Colons, indentation, missing loop endings and undeclared variables all cost marks without reflecting any misunderstanding. The repair takes two to four weeks of writing short algorithms by hand to the published conventions, and it is the cheapest grade improvement available in the subject.

faqs.question: What is a trace table and why does my daughter lose marks on it?
faqs.answer: A trace table is a dry run: walking through an algorithm line by line with a column per variable and a row per iteration, recording what the code actually does rather than what it was meant to do. Students fail it in recognisable ways, writing the values they expect, updating variables in the wrong order, losing the loop counter after three passes, or leaving it blank and describing the algorithm's purpose instead. It is a discipline failure, not a comprehension failure, and the only thing that fixes it is one supervised table a session for eight to sixteen weeks.

faqs.question: Can programming really be taught over a shared screen?
faqs.answer: For this syllabus it is an advantage rather than a compromise. The examined task is writing pseudocode by hand and completing tables, and both sit naturally on a shared screen where the tutor annotates the exact cell where the reasoning broke. The corrected version is saved and sent, so the student revises from their own marked work rather than from a memory of being told. What video cannot supply is the hours of independent practice between sessions, and no delivery format can; that part is a household habit and it is the real variable.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the June series does my child need for Computer Science?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which gap the mock reveals. Pseudocode conventions take two to four weeks. Binary and hexadecimal method takes one or two. Boolean logic takes three to five. Paper 1 content gaps take six to ten. Trace tables as a reliable habit take eight to sixteen. Decomposition of unfamiliar problems takes a full term at minimum. So a family with eight weeks can achieve a great deal and a specific list of things, and cannot achieve one particular thing. We write that list down before anything is booked.

faqs.question: Does 0478 have any coursework or a programming project?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science has no coursework, no project and no practical examination; the entire grade comes from two written papers in one series. Two consequences follow. Nothing can be banked in advance, so timed practice is the main preparation rather than optional revision. And the academic-honesty questions that surround coursework subjects do not arise in the same form, because the only work an examiner sees is what the student writes alone in the hall. Everything a tutor marks is practice by definition.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether my son's class codes in Python, Java or VB.NET?
faqs.answer: Whichever the school teaches, because the examination does not test a language. Centres typically use Python, Java or VB.NET, and the understanding transfers completely: sequence, selection, iteration, arrays, procedures, functions and file handling are the same ideas everywhere. What does not transfer is syntax, and the examined answers are written in pseudocode. A student should be fluent in the class language for developing understanding and separately fluent in examined pseudocode for writing answers. Treating those as the same skill is the commonest avoidable loss in the subject.

faqs.question: Why does my child keep getting binary and hexadecimal conversions wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always because there is no written method, only a half-remembered trick. A student converting by inspection gets most of them right and the rest wrong unpredictably, which looks like carelessness and is actually the absence of a procedure. The fix is one of the quickest in the subject: a single written method, applied to twenty conversions in both directions, checked each time. One to two weeks of short daily practice makes it reliable. Data representation is early on Paper 1 and sets the tone of the paper, so unreliability here costs more than the marks alone.

faqs.question: Should my daughter be sitting 0478 at all, or would ICT suit her better?
faqs.answer: They are different subjects that are frequently taught by the same person, which is why families confuse them. 0478 is algorithmic: pseudocode, trace tables, logic and computer systems, assessed by two written papers. ICT 0417 is applied: practical competence with documents, spreadsheets, databases, presentations and web authoring, assessed through practical papers alongside theory. A student who enjoys building things with software often does much better in ICT; a student who enjoys working out why a program behaves as it does belongs in Computer Science. Several campuses here offer one and not the other, or both in a single option block.

faqs.question: Does 0478 prepare a student for A Level Computer Science?
faqs.answer: It is the right foundation, and the part that matters is Paper 2. The post-16 course adds data structures, abstract data types, object-oriented programming, assembly language and a programming project, and it is weighted towards exactly the algorithmic skill that Paper 2 measures. Students who reached a good IGCSE grade mainly through Paper 1 recall, while quietly avoiding the programming questions, find the step severe. If a student may continue, the weekly supervised algorithm writing in Year 10 is an investment in eighteen months' time as much as in June.

faqs.question: How much do Computer Science tutors charge around Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Published market figures for this country in 2026 run from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour at the budget online end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit inclusive of travel, and AED 200 to 450 and above for an IGCSE or A Level specialist. Monthly packages of around AED 799 for eight online sessions also circulate. Those are other providers' figures, cited with their sources for context. IB Gram publishes no rate card on these pages; book the free trial, watch a trace table worked, and get a number in writing.

faqs.question: Our campus has no computer science specialist. How much does that matter?
faqs.answer: For Paper 1 it matters less than you would think, because the content is defined and a conscientious teacher can cover it. For Paper 2 it matters a great deal, because the skills need supervised repetition that a single teacher covering two subjects cannot provide for one student. This is the specific gap in the northern emirates and it is why we lead with it rather than with claims about teaching quality. The practical answer is a weekly hour of supervised algorithm writing from Year 10, which is what the school cannot resource and what video delivers without a commute.

faqs.question: Does my child need SQL for 0478, and how much?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the quantity is finite, which makes it one of the better returns on revision time. The syllabus covers single-table database structures, appropriate field types, primary keys and a small set of SQL query patterns: selecting fields, filtering with conditions, ordering results and simple aggregate functions. Six worked examples of each pattern is enough for most candidates. The problem is timing rather than difficulty: databases are usually taught in the last fortnight of the course, when mock examinations are swallowing attention, so the topic gets met cold in the paper.

faqs.question: How are logic gate questions marked, and why are they so often wrong?
faqs.answer: Logic questions are nearly pure technique, which is why a few weeks of drills reliably converts them from a liability into marks. Candidates must know every gate's truth table, including NAND, NOR and XOR, and must read a logic circuit left to right while writing down each intermediate output. The errors are mechanical: a NAND read as an AND, an intermediate value held in the head and forgotten, truth table rows written in an inconsistent order so one combination is duplicated and another missed. Fifteen minutes of drills three times a week for a month usually settles it.

faqs.question: What happens to the revision plan during Ramadan and mock season?
faqs.answer: Both eat weeks that a plan written in September did not account for, which is why we count working weeks rather than calendar weeks. Mock examinations typically swallow a fortnight. During Ramadan the school day shortens, which actually frees afternoon slots that are unavailable the rest of the year, and some families move the session to after Iftar instead. Because Ramadan often falls close to a summer series, pausing for a month usually costs more than it saves. We agree the revised slot in advance so the weekly supervised practice continues at a lighter volume rather than stopping.

ras-al-khaimah/cambridge-igcse-computer-.closingHeading: Send the mock, get the timeline in writing
ras-al-khaimah/cambridge-igcse-computer-.closingBody: The useful next step costs nothing. Send one marked 0478 mock script and a tutor will read it question by question, split it by paper, and tell you which of the six common gaps your child has: content and precision, pseudocode conventions, conversion method, trace tables, Boolean logic or decomposition. With that you get an estimate in writing of how many weeks each gap needs, and an honest statement of what your available weeks can and cannot deliver. Sometimes that estimate says the right purchase is two timed papers and a marker rather than a term of lessons, and we will say so. The trial lesson is free and happens before any payment.

intro.heading: The subject choice comes before the tutoring decision
paragraphs: Economics and Business Studies look like neighbours on an options sheet and are marked almost nothing alike. Cambridge IGCSE Economics, code 0455, is an analytical subject built on models: scarcity, demand and supply, elasticity, market failure, the multiplier, exchange rates, trade. Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies, 0450, is an applied subject built on cases: a firm in a situation, a decision to recommend, a judgement to support. A student who thinks in diagrams tends to prosper in one and feel adrift in the other, and the reverse is just as true.

Ras Al Khaimah makes the decision harder than it needs to be, because option blocks in a small cohort are narrow. A campus with one commerce teacher may run Business Studies and not Economics, or run both in the same block so a student can only take one. We regularly speak to families in Al Nakheel and Khuzam whose child was allocated the subject that fitted the timetable rather than the subject that fitted the student, and who discovered the mismatch in the first set of Year 10 assessments.

There is a third option that families rarely consider and a fourth they stumble into. Pearson Edexcel publishes its own International GCSE in Economics, code 4EC1, with a different paper structure, and some centres in the UAE follow Pearson rather than Cambridge. Cambridge also issues a numerically graded variant of Economics alongside the A*-G code, which changes nothing about the content but changes every conversation about target grades. The first thing to do is read the statement of entry and know exactly which qualification is in play.

Once that is settled, 0455 becomes a very tractable subject to support, and more tractable than most. It has no coursework and no practical component. The syllabus is six defined units. The assessment is two papers, one of thirty multiple-choice marks and one of ninety marks split between a compulsory data response and three structured questions chosen from five. The command words that govern the mark ceiling are published. A student who learns the ladder inside a twenty-mark question can usually move a grade on technique alone, without learning any new economics.

That is the honest shape of the opportunity here, and it is why we lead with structure rather than with content coverage. Most 0455 candidates in the emirate know more economics than their grades suggest. They lose marks because a four-mark part gets a two-mark answer, because a diagram is drawn without axes labelled, and because the eight-mark part ends with a summary instead of a judgement. All three are teachable in weeks. Lessons run one to one over live video, timed to the school day here, and the first one is free.
