ras-al-khaimah/cambridge-igcse-economics.programmesIntro: Economics appears at four points in a Ras Al Khaimah student's route, and the versions are not interchangeable. Below is what each stage assesses and what it assumes a student can already do, with notes on how each plays out in a small northern-emirates cohort.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics
programmes.description: Six units covering the basic economic problem, the allocation of resources and market failure, microeconomic decision makers, government and the macroeconomy, economic development, and international trade and globalisation. Assessed by a 45-minute multiple-choice paper worth 30 marks and a 2-hour-15-minute structured paper worth 90 marks. The structured paper opens with a compulsory data-response question worth 30 marks and then asks for three answers from five structured questions worth 20 marks each.
programmes.countryNote: Where it runs in Ras Al Khaimah it is usually a single set, often taught alongside Business Studies by the same teacher. That concentration is the practical reason families here look outside the campus for subject-specific help: a teacher covering two commerce syllabuses cannot give one student sustained attention on diagram technique.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies
programmes.description: The applied alternative, built around case studies of real and invented firms. Candidates are asked to apply business concepts to a situation and justify a recommendation, with command words controlling how far an answer must go. Content covers business activity, people in business, marketing, operations and finance. It rewards students who can read a scenario quickly and write decisively, and it punishes answers that recite theory without touching the case.
programmes.countryNote: More widely offered than Economics across the emirate's campuses, which is why a student who would suit 0455 sometimes ends up here. If both are available in different blocks, the choice is worth making deliberately in Year 9 rather than by timetable accident.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level Economics
programmes.description: The post-16 continuation, with substantially more theory, quantitative work and extended essay writing than IGCSE. AS content revisits price theory and macroeconomic policy at greater depth; A Level adds market failure in detail, labour markets and international economics. The step up that catches students is not the content but the essay: judgement has to be sustained across a page rather than delivered in a final sentence.
programmes.countryNote: Post-16 economics provision is limited in the northern emirates, and some students commute or change campus for it. Knowing that in Year 10 changes what else belongs on the IGCSE timetable, because a strong maths entry matters more for 9708 than most families expect.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Economics
programmes.description: The Diploma alternative to A Level Economics, taught at Standard and Higher Level with a different architecture: nine key concepts, four units, and an internal assessment portfolio of commentaries on published news articles. The Higher Level course adds quantitative content and a policy paper. Students arriving from 0455 recognise the models immediately; what is new is the demand to evaluate within a real published context rather than an abstract scenario.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision in the emirate concentrates on the Al Hamra side. For a student who may end up on this route, the 0455 habit worth building now is reading one piece of economic news a week and writing three sentences of judgement about it, which is most of what the commentary later asks for.

ras-al-khaimah/cambridge-igcse-economics.subjectsIntro: The grid below is the commerce and social-science family a Ras Al Khaimah Cambridge candidate chooses inside, with codes as they appear on a statement of entry. Each is a separate qualification with its own command words and mark ceilings.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Thirty multiple-choice marks in 45 minutes plus a 90-mark structured paper over 2 hours 15 minutes. Marks are lost on diagrams without labelled axes, on four-mark parts answered at two-mark depth, and on eight-mark parts that summarise instead of judging. All three are technique failures rather than knowledge gaps.

subjects.name: Economics, 9-1 graded variant
subjects.description: Cambridge issues a numerically graded version of IGCSE Economics alongside the lettered code. Content, papers and command words are identical; only the reported scale differs. Confirm which code is on the statement of entry before any conversation about a target grade, because a target of 7 and a target of an A are different sentences.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Case-study assessment where command words set the ceiling on every part. Rewards fast reading of a scenario and decisive application. A student who writes textbook theory without referring to the firm in the case will be capped however accurate the theory is, which is the mirror image of the 0455 failure pattern.

subjects.name: Accounting (0452)
subjects.description: Double-entry bookkeeping, financial statements and basic analysis, assessed by two papers. Frequently taken alongside 0455 by students heading towards commerce degrees. The overlap with Economics is thinner than families assume: this subject rewards procedural accuracy, while 0455 rewards explanation of cause and effect.

subjects.name: Global Perspectives (0457)
subjects.description: Research, argument and collaboration assessed through an individual report and a team project rather than timed essays. The transferable skill into 0455 is evidence selection and the habit of weighing two sides, which is exactly what an eight-mark evaluation part needs. Worth considering as the paired humanity if a student is strong on argument and weak on recall.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Physical and human geography with a compulsory skills paper. Shares real content with 0455 on development, trade and population, and shares a mark-scheme habit too: command words control depth, and a student who learns to read them in one subject reads them better in the other.

subjects.name: History (0470)
subjects.description: Source-based questions requiring inference and judgement under time pressure. The closest humanity to 0455 in terms of what the mark scheme rewards, because both demand a conclusion that chooses rather than a paragraph that lists. Students weak at judgement show it in both subjects simultaneously.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Included because 0455 contains calculation and because post-16 economics assumes confident algebra and graph work. Extended is the tier that keeps A Level Economics and Diploma Higher Level Economics realistically open; a Core entry closes doors quietly rather than loudly.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: The stretch mathematics entry for students heading to quantitative post-16 courses. Relevant to a 0455 student only if the plan includes economics at a university that expects strong mathematics, in which case it is worth more than a second humanity on the timetable.

subjects.name: Sociology (0495)
subjects.description: Research methods, social inequality and social institutions, assessed by extended written answers. Listed because families comparing social-science options often have it on the sheet, and because its mark scheme rewards structured argument in the same way the 0455 twenty-mark question does.

sections.heading: 0455, 0450 or 4EC1: the three economics-shaped choices on a timetable here
paragraphs: A parent comparing options is usually looking at three or four things that sound similar and are not. Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 is analytical: the student learns models and then uses them to explain and judge. Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies 0450 is applied: the student reads a case about a firm and recommends a course of action. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Economics 4EC1 is another board's version of the analytical subject, with its own paper structure, and some UAE centres follow Pearson instead of Cambridge. Global Perspectives 0457 is not economics at all but is often on the same options sheet because it occupies the same kind of block.

The table below sets the four side by side on the things that actually differ: what the assessment looks like, what kind of thinking earns the marks, and which student each suits. Read the right-hand column first. A student who enjoys drawing a diagram to explain why something happened belongs in 0455. A student who enjoys deciding what a business should do next belongs in 0450. Those are different pleasures and they produce different grades in the wrong subject.

One further distinction catches families out at results time rather than at option time. Cambridge issues a numerically graded variant of Economics alongside the lettered code, and the content is identical. If the statement of entry carries the numerical code, a predicted grade expressed as a letter means nothing precise, and a tutor who talks in letters is working from an assumption. Thirty seconds with the exams officer settles it.

Where a Ras Al Khaimah campus offers only one of these, the question becomes whether to accept the allocation or to sit the other as a private candidate. That is a real option and we support it, but it is a bigger commitment than families expect: a private entry means covering the whole syllabus outside school hours, arranging entry through a centre that accepts external candidates, and meeting an entry deadline that falls months before the paper.

sections.heading: Thirty marks of multiple choice and ninety marks of everything else
paragraphs: The assessment structure of 0455 is unusually clean, and knowing it precisely changes how a term of preparation is spent. Paper 1 is multiple choice: thirty questions in forty-five minutes, thirty marks, thirty per cent of the qualification. Paper 2 is structured: two hours and fifteen minutes, ninety marks, seventy per cent. There is no coursework, no practical and no internally assessed component, which means nothing can be banked in advance and nothing is carried into the examination room except what the student can do under time pressure.

Paper 1 is where families over-invest. Ninety seconds a question is comfortable for a student who knows the content, and the gains available from practice are real but capped at a few marks. It rewards elimination technique, careful reading of the stem, and resisting the first plausible option. A tutorial hour spent on multiple choice is an hour not spent on the paper that carries more than twice as many marks, and we say so rather than filling sessions with question banks because they are easy to mark.

Paper 2 is where the grade is decided. It opens with a compulsory data-response question worth thirty marks, built on a short source: extraction, calculation, explanation and a judgement part. Candidates then answer three structured questions chosen from five, each worth twenty marks. The choice itself is worth practising, because a student who starts a question on a unit they half-know and abandons it ten minutes in has lost both the marks and the time.

sections.heading: How a twenty-mark structured question is built, part by part
paragraphs: The single most useful thing a 0455 candidate can learn is that a twenty-mark question is not one question. It is a ladder of parts of increasing demand, each governed by a command word that sets a ceiling, and a student who gives every part the same treatment is guaranteed to lose marks at both ends: wasting time on the easy parts and under-answering the hard ones.

The shape is consistent. An opening part asks for a definition or an identification and is worth a couple of marks: two accurate sentences, no example needed, no diagram, thirty seconds. The next asks for explanation and is worth about double: a point and a developed consequence. The third asks for analysis and is worth more again: a chain of reasoning, usually with a diagram where one fits. The final part asks for discussion or evaluation and carries the largest block of marks on its own.

Students lose marks in a pattern so predictable it can be diagnosed from one script. The definition part gets a paragraph, which earns the same two marks a sentence would have earned and costs four minutes. The explanation part gets a definition again, because that is the comfortable move. The analysis part gets a list of three unconnected points where the mark scheme wanted one developed chain. The evaluation part gets a summary of what has already been said, with no side taken and no criterion for taking it.

The repair is a drill rather than a lesson. We write out the ladder, mark the student's own answer part by part against it, and show where the ceiling was hit and where it was nowhere near. After five or six of these, most students start reading the command word before the content, which is the whole trick. sections.heading: Diagrams and the marks most 0455 candidates leave behind
paragraphs: Diagrams are the cheapest marks in the subject and the most reliably wasted. A demand and supply diagram that is drawn correctly, labelled correctly and referred to in the prose supports an analysis chain in a way words alone cannot. The same diagram drawn without axis labels, with curves unnamed or with the new equilibrium left unmarked, earns a fraction of what it should and sometimes nothing at all.

The errors are specific and they repeat across scripts from every campus we see. Axes labelled P and Q with no indication of what price and quantity refer to. A supply curve shifted with no new intersection shown. Curves drawn so close together that the examiner cannot tell which is which. A diagram that appears on the page and is then never mentioned in the written answer, as though drawing it were the task. And the reverse: an analysis that cries out for a diagram, written as three sentences of description because the student finds drawing slow.

Fixing this is mechanical and fast. We build a small standard set that covers most of what the syllabus needs, and the student draws each one from memory until it takes under a minute with every label in place. Market equilibrium and a shift in each direction. A price ceiling and a price floor. An external cost. A production possibility curve. Each drawn, labelled, then explained in two sentences that point at the diagram rather than ignoring it.

Over video this works better than it does across a table, because the student draws on a shared whiteboard and the tutor annotates the same image rather than describing what is wrong with a sheet of paper upside down. The annotated version is saved, so the student has their own corrected set to revise from instead of a memory of being told.

sections.heading: The six units of the syllabus, and the two that decide most grades
paragraphs: The 0455 syllabus is organised into six units, and they are not equally difficult. The basic economic problem is short and conceptual. The allocation of resources, covering how the market works and where it fails, is the analytical core and the source of most diagram questions. Microeconomic decision makers brings in households, workers, trade unions, firms and banks. Government and the macroeconomy covers policy objectives, instruments and conflicts. Economic development deals with poverty, population and living standards. International trade and globalisation closes with exchange rates, protection and the balance of payments.

In our experience of marking scripts from this emirate, two units decide the grade. The first is market failure inside the allocation unit, because it demands a diagram and a judgement at once and most students can do one or the other. The second is the macroeconomy, specifically the conflicts between policy objectives, because it is the unit where an eight-mark evaluation question most often appears and where students default to listing policies rather than weighing them.

Economic development is the unit students find easiest to revise and hardest to score well in, for an interesting reason: the content is accessible, so everyone writes plenty, and the marks go to the candidate who uses specific mechanisms rather than general concern. International trade is the unit most often half-learned, because it sits at the end of the course and gets taught in the weeks when mock examinations are swallowing the timetable.

The practical consequence for a tutoring plan is ordering. We do not start at unit one and work along. We start wherever the mock script says the marks are missing, which is usually market failure or policy conflict, and we come back to the easier units later with multiple-choice sets rather than full lessons. sections.heading: Evaluation: what the eight-mark part is really asking
paragraphs: The final part of a structured question carries the largest single block of marks and is where the difference between a middling grade and a strong one is visible at a glance. It asks the candidate to discuss or to evaluate, and most answers do neither. They explain, at length, both sides, accurately, and then stop. An examiner reading that script has nothing to reward at the top of the mark scheme, because nothing has been decided.

What the part wants is a judgement with a reason for the judgement. Not a preference, and not a hedge. The reason has to be a criterion the student states: it depends on the time period, or on how elastic demand is, or on whether the economy is near capacity, or on what the government's priority currently is. A student who writes that the effect depends on elasticity, and then says which way it goes when demand is inelastic, has done the thing the mark scheme is built around.

We teach this with a fixed sequence that students can lean on when the clock is against them. Two developed points on one side. Two on the other. One sentence naming the criterion that decides between them. One sentence giving the judgement that follows from that criterion. It is formulaic, deliberately, because a formula a tired sixteen-year-old can execute at minute ninety of a paper beats an elegant method they abandon under pressure.

The same structure carries forward. A Level Economics and Diploma Economics both ask for sustained judgement rather than a concluding sentence, so a student who learns to evaluate properly at IGCSE arrives at the post-16 course with the hardest habit already formed. This is the one part of 0455 preparation that pays dividends long after the certificate.

sections.heading: What 0455 tuition costs around Ras Al Khaimah, by the month
paragraphs: Most families budget monthly rather than hourly, so start there. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table estimates monthly outlay for one weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for a specialist in an examination year. Published monthly packages in this market sit alongside those figures: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

Translated into hourly rates, the same market splits into bands. Budget online tutoring runs from roughly AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits between AED 150 and 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An IGCSE, IB or A Level specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270. At the top of the market, BartyED advertises AED 650 an hour. In-home one-to-one visits inclusive of travel are quoted by Bestimate at AED 180 to 350, and by independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500.

For a single analytical subject like 0455, the monthly view makes the decision clearer than the hourly one. A technique block of eight sessions over two months, aimed at the mark ladder and the diagram set, is a bounded purchase with a visible endpoint. A weekly slot held for eighteen months is a different kind of commitment and should be bought only where the subject is genuinely being built rather than polished. Families who treat tutoring as a subscription tend to spend the most and change the least.

Every figure above is another provider's published rate for this market in 2026, named so you can check it. None of them is an IB Gram price, and we do not print a rate card on these pages: the honest number depends on level, subject and how many sessions are actually needed, and any figure here would be stale before your child's series. As household context, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package; the northern emirates set fees through their own authorities.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor or live video, for one subject in a small emirate
paragraphs: This comparison deserves to be made on the numbers rather than on preference, because for a single analytical subject in the northern emirates it is not close. The in-home premium in this market is AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, and the gap is not buying better teaching. It is buying a commute and, more importantly, it is buying from whoever is within driving distance.

That last point is the one that matters in Ras Al Khaimah. Economics is a single-set subject on most campuses here. The number of people in the emirate who teach Cambridge 0455 and are available on a Tuesday evening and are willing to drive to Al Rams is very small. Searching inside that set and then choosing the best available is a different exercise from choosing a 0455 specialist, and a parent who believes they have done the second when they have done the first will be disappointed without understanding why.

There are genuine advantages to a person in the room, and they are worth naming honestly. A younger child benefits from physical presence. A student who will not engage without an adult sitting beside them benefits. Equipment-heavy subjects benefit. Economics at sixteen is none of those cases: the materials are a diagram, a past paper and a mark scheme, all of which live better on a shared screen that saves the annotation than on a sheet of paper that goes into a bag.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and home visits are a service offered only in India. sections.heading: When a 0455 tutor is the wrong purchase
paragraphs: There are situations where we tell a family not to buy. The clearest is the student who is scoring well on Paper 1 style questions and poorly on structured answers but has never sat a full timed Paper 2. That student does not need teaching; they need three timed papers and a marker, and a parent can arrange much of that with the school for nothing. We will say so in the diagnostic session and we will not sell a term of weekly lessons around it.

The second is the student whose economics grade is a symptom of a reading or a writing problem rather than an economics problem. If the four-mark explanations are short because the student struggles to develop any idea in writing, the subject support will underperform until the writing is addressed. In that case the useful purchase is English support, and the economics grade will move as a side effect. Diagnosing this takes one look at a script and saves a family a term of the wrong hours.

The third is the student who has not yet decided whether they are doing this subject at all. Paying for Economics tuition while an option sheet is still open is spending money on a decision rather than on learning. One conversation about 0455 against 0450, with a clear account of how differently the two are marked, is worth more at that moment than six lessons, and it costs the price of a trial.

We publish this because the alternative is a market where nobody says it. A platform that answers every enquiry with a weekly slot is optimising its own revenue, not the student's grade. The free trial exists partly so that this conversation can happen before any money moves, and a recommendation to buy nothing is a legitimate outcome of it.

process.title: Confirm the code and the board
process.description: Send the syllabus code from the statement of entry: 0455, the numerically graded variant, 4EC1 for Pearson, or 0450 if it turns out to be Business Studies after all. If you do not have the statement of entry, a photograph of the last report and the name of the campus is usually enough for us to work it out and check.

process.title: Send one marked structured answer
process.description: Not a report and not a percentage. One twenty-mark answer with the teacher's marks on it tells us which rung of the ladder is failing, whether diagrams are present and labelled, and whether any judgement appears in the final part. That is the whole diagnosis and it takes a tutor about ten minutes.

process.title: Use the free trial to test the marking
process.description: In the trial lesson, ask the tutor to mark an eight-mark answer out loud, part by part, against the command word. A tutor who can explain exactly why an answer sits at four marks rather than six is the one worth booking. A tutor who praises the content and moves on is not, however pleasant the hour is.

process.title: Fix the slot around the real school week
process.description: Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time around the school day and the run home, which for households in Digdaga or Al Rams is the binding constraint rather than an inconvenience. Choose a time that holds on an ordinary week; the weekly marking cycle is what produces the improvement and it only works if the slot survives.

process.title: Measure against timed papers, not impressions
process.description: Every four to six weeks a timed Paper 2 question set is marked to the criteria and compared with the previous one. If the ladder scores are not climbing we change the approach or tell you the hour is not earning its money. If no 0455 specialist is free at your preferred time we say so rather than substituting a generalist.

whyPoints.title: The subject choice gets answered first
whyPoints.description: Most pages in this market sell tuition for whichever subject the parent names. We start by checking that 0455 is the right subject and the right board for that student, because a child in the wrong commerce subject cannot be tutored into the right one and the decision window is Year 9, not Year 11.

whyPoints.title: Marks are taught as a ladder
whyPoints.description: Every structured question is a sequence of parts with command words that set ceilings. Students are drilled to read the command word before the content and to proportion time to marks. This is technique rather than knowledge, it is teachable in weeks, and it is where most 0455 candidates in this emirate are losing grades.

whyPoints.title: Diagrams are drilled to automatic
whyPoints.description: A small standard set drawn from memory in under a minute each, fully labelled, and referred to explicitly in the prose. Drawn on a shared whiteboard, annotated in place and saved, so the student revises from their own corrected set rather than from a memory of being corrected.

whyPoints.title: Rates are other people's, named and dated

IB Gram publishes no rate card here, because an honest number depends on the subject and the number of sessions and would be stale by your child's series.

faqs.question: Should my son take Economics 0455 or Business Studies 0450?
faqs.answer: They reward different kinds of thinking. 0455 is analytical: the student learns models and uses them to explain why something happened, usually with a diagram. 0450 is applied: the student reads a case about a firm and recommends what it should do, with marks for touching the specific situation. A child who enjoys working out mechanisms generally does better in Economics; a child who enjoys deciding does better in Business Studies. Where a Ras Al Khaimah campus offers both in different blocks, make the choice deliberately in Year 9. Where only one runs, the other can be sat as a private candidate, but that is a larger commitment than most families expect.

faqs.question: Is the 0455 multiple-choice paper easier than the structured paper?
faqs.answer: It is shorter and it carries far less weight. Paper 1 is thirty questions in forty-five minutes for thirty marks, which is thirty per cent of the qualification. Paper 2 runs two hours and fifteen minutes for ninety marks and seventy per cent. Families often over-invest in multiple-choice practice because question banks are easy to set and easy to score, but the gains available there are a few marks. The paper that decides the grade is the structured one, and an hour spent on question banks is an hour not spent on the mark ladder inside a twenty-mark answer.

faqs.question: How is the data response question in 0455 Paper 2 structured?
faqs.answer: It is compulsory, worth thirty marks, and built on a short source that candidates must actually use rather than describe. The parts move from extraction and calculation through explanation to a judgement, in the same escalating pattern as a structured question. The commonest errors are paraphrasing the source instead of applying it, skipping a calculation because it looks fiddly, and treating the final part as a summary. After the data response, candidates answer three structured questions chosen from five, each worth twenty marks, and the selection itself is worth practising.

faqs.question: Does IGCSE Economics involve much mathematics?
faqs.answer: Some, and less than families fear. Candidates calculate percentages, index numbers and simple elasticity values, read and interpret data from tables and graphs, and draw diagrams accurately. There is no algebra of the kind an A Level course expects. A student comfortable with Extended 0580 mathematics will find the quantitative content undemanding; a student on the Core tier can still do it, but the post-16 route matters here, because A Level Economics and Diploma Higher Level Economics both assume stronger mathematics than 0455 requires. That is a Year 9 timetable decision worth making with the destination in mind.

faqs.question: What does an evaluate question in 0455 actually want?
faqs.answer: A judgement with a stated reason, not a balanced summary. Two developed points on each side earns marks in the middle of the scheme and no further. The top of the scheme needs a criterion the candidate names, such as the time period, the elasticity of demand, or whether the economy is near capacity, and then a decision that follows from it. We teach a fixed sequence for this: two points one way, two the other, one sentence naming the criterion, one sentence giving the judgement. It is formulaic deliberately, because a formula survives minute ninety of a long paper.

faqs.question: My daughter knows the economics but her grade is stuck. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always it is the mark ladder rather than the content. Give us one marked twenty-mark answer and the pattern is usually visible in ten minutes: a two-mark definition answered in a paragraph, a four-mark explanation that repeats the definition, a six-mark analysis written as three unconnected points, and an eight-mark part that summarises instead of judging. That student is losing marks at every rung while knowing the subject perfectly well. It is technique, it responds to five or six marked drills, and it is why we ask for a script rather than a percentage.

faqs.question: Which parts of the 0455 syllabus cause the most trouble?
faqs.answer: Two units decide most grades in our experience of marking scripts from this emirate. Market failure inside the allocation unit is the first, because it demands an accurate diagram and a judgement in the same answer and most students manage one of the two. The second is government and the macroeconomy, specifically the conflicts between policy objectives, where eight-mark evaluation questions concentrate and where candidates default to listing policies. International trade is the most commonly half-learned, because it is taught last, usually during mock season when nothing is absorbed properly.

faqs.question: Do 0455 candidates have to draw diagrams, and how are they marked?
faqs.answer: Diagrams are not demanded in every answer, but in analysis questions on the market they are the difference between a described answer and a reasoned one, and they are the cheapest marks available. They have to be labelled properly: both axes with what they measure, every curve named, the new equilibrium marked after a shift, and the diagram referred to explicitly in the written answer. A diagram that appears and is never mentioned earns very little. We drill a small standard set until each one takes under a minute with every label in place.

faqs.question: Is there any coursework in Cambridge IGCSE Economics?
faqs.answer: None. 0455 has no coursework, no practical and no internally assessed component, which has two consequences. Nothing can be banked in advance, so every mark is won in two sittings under time pressure, and timed practice is therefore not optional revision but the main preparation available. It also means the academic-honesty questions that surround coursework subjects do not arise here: there is no submitted work for anyone to have helped with. What a tutor marks is practice, and the only thing an examiner ever sees is what the student writes alone in the hall.

faqs.question: Does 0455 prepare a student for IB Diploma Economics?
faqs.answer: The models transfer almost completely, and the habit that does not is judgement sustained across a page. Diploma Economics is taught at Standard and Higher Level around nine key concepts and four units, with an internal assessment portfolio of commentaries on published news articles, and Higher Level adds quantitative content. A student arriving from a strong 0455 recognises the economics immediately. What is new is applying it to real published material and evaluating within it. The habit worth building now is reading one piece of economic news a week and writing three sentences of judgement about it.

faqs.question: What does Cambridge Economics tuition cost per month for a family here?
faqs.answer: Published market estimates for one weekly one-hour session put monthly outlay at roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for a specialist in an examination year, according to Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. Package rates circulating in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are other providers' figures, cited for context. IB Gram does not publish a rate card here; book the trial and get a number in writing.

faqs.question: Our campus does not offer Economics. Can my child sit 0455 privately?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a real option that needs its eyes open. A private entry means covering all six syllabus units outside school hours, arranging entry through a centre that accepts external candidates, and meeting an entry deadline that falls months before the paper rather than weeks. For a Ras Al Khaimah candidate the series is June or November: a June entry closes in the spring for papers that run from May into June, and a November entry closes over the summer for papers in October and November. The teaching workload is heavier than supplementary support, usually two sessions a week rather than one, and the family should agree to that before starting rather than discover it a term in.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover 0455 Economics and 0580 Mathematics together?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and in Ras Al Khaimah it is a common request because the quantitative parts of Economics and the data-handling parts of Mathematics reinforce each other. What matters is that the tutor is genuinely strong in both rather than adequate in one and willing in the other. We would rather split a student across two specialists than place a single convenient tutor on both subjects. Where one person does cover both, we keep the sessions separate in the week, because a combined hour reliably becomes an hour of whichever subject has homework due.

faqs.question: How early before the June series should 0455 work start?
faqs.answer: If the aim is technique, eight to ten weeks of weekly marked structured answers is enough to change how a student reads a command word, which means starting around February for a June series. If the aim is building the subject, because a student has drifted through a unit or joined the course late, start in the autumn term. The deadline nobody expects is the entry deadline: for a June series the centre's final entry closes in the spring, months before the first paper, so every decision that rides on the entry - the tier, the subject list, whether a November resit goes in alongside it - has to be settled while that technique work is still running.

faqs.question: Is a visiting tutor worth the travel premium for a single subject here?
faqs.answer: For Economics at sixteen, the honest answer is rarely. Published market rates put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and the premium buys a commute rather than subject depth. The deeper problem in the northern emirates is the pool: the people who teach 0455 and will drive to Al Rams on a Tuesday are a very short list. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, so what we offer is the specialist over live video, with the annotated work saved.

faqs.question: What if my child only needs help with the eight-mark questions?
faqs.answer: Then buy that and nothing more. A block of six to eight sessions aimed purely at the evaluation part is a bounded purchase: the student writes one eight-mark answer a session, it is marked out loud against the command word, and the fixed sequence of two points, two counterpoints, a criterion and a judgement is practised until it appears without prompting. Most students show a visible change by the fourth or fifth attempt. We would rather sell that block and stop than convert a narrow need into an eighteen-month weekly slot that nobody reviews.

ras-al-khaimah/cambridge-igcse-economics.closingHeading: Send one marked answer and we will tell you what is wrong
ras-al-khaimah/cambridge-igcse-economics.closingBody: The fastest way to know whether 0455 support will help your child is to send a single marked twenty-mark answer with the teacher's comments on it. A tutor will read it against the command words and tell you which rung of the ladder is failing: the definition answered at paragraph length, the explanation that never develops, the analysis written as a list, or the final part that summarises instead of judging. If the answer is that your child needs three timed papers rather than a term of lessons, we will say that. The trial lesson is free, happens before any payment, and is taught by the tutor your child would keep.

intro.heading: Start by checking which English paper your child is actually sitting
paragraphs: Parents in Ras Al Khaimah often arrive at this page certain of one thing and wrong about another. They are certain their child needs English help. They are frequently wrong about which English qualification the school has entered them for, and that single fact changes everything a tutor should be doing. Cambridge IGCSE English as a First Language carries the code 0500. English as a Second Language carries 0510 or 0511. Literature in English is 0475. Pearson Edexcel's International GCSE English Language A is 4EA1. Four qualifications, four mark schemes, four different kinds of lesson.

The confusion is not carelessness on anyone's part. A statement of entry lists codes, not plain descriptions, and a Year 10 report usually says only "English". In a smaller school cohort the same teacher may take a first-language group and a second-language group in adjoining periods, so the vocabulary at the dinner table is identical whichever route a child is on. The first useful thing a tutor can do for a family in Al Nakheel or Al Hamra Village is read the statement of entry and say out loud which syllabus is in play.

It matters because the reward structures diverge sharply. On 0500, a reader who cannot handle implicit meaning in an unseen text will stall in the low grades however neat the writing is, because Paper 1 Reading is half the qualification. On 0510, accurate controlled language earns credit that 0500 simply assumes. On 0475, the texts are set, studied for two years and quoted from memory in the examination. Preparation that works for one is close to useless for the next, and a tutor who never asks the question will spend a term teaching the wrong thing well.

Ras Al Khaimah adds a second complication. The emirate's private sector is small, and its schools are regulated by the Department of Knowledge, which under the federal framework approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods in the emirate. A small sector means fewer parallel groups, fewer specialist English teachers per campus and more mixed-ability classes. Families in Mina Al Arab and Al Dhait regularly tell us the same thing: the school is attentive, but there is one teacher covering both the first-language and the literature entries, and a child who needs close work on inference is not going to get forty minutes of it a week.

That scarcity is the honest argument for one-to-one online work rather than a search for someone nearby. A specialist who has marked hundreds of 0500 summary answers is not necessarily living in the emirate. Over live video she is available on a Tuesday at six, with your child's own script on screen and the annotation visible to both of them. The rest of this page is the detail: what each paper asks, how the three nearest alternatives differ, where the marks actually go, what the market charges and how the Cambridge series counts backwards from the paper your child will sit.

ras-al-khaimah/cambridge-igcse-english-f.programmesIntro: Ras Al Khaimah families meet English assessment at four points: the lower secondary years when reading habits are set, the IGCSE entry itself, the post-16 choice between A Level and the Diploma, and the Ministry of Education equivalency check that follows. Here is what each stage asks of a student's English.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary English
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE entry, where the reading habit that decides a 0500 grade is either built or missed. Lower Secondary English assesses reading, writing, speaking and listening against Cambridge stage objectives, with optional Checkpoint tests. Nothing here appears on a certificate, which is precisely why it gets neglected. A student who reaches Year 10 able to summarise an argument in their own words rather than copying phrases has already banked most of what Paper 1 will later test.
programmes.countryNote: In Ras Al Khaimah the Year 9 to Year 10 handover is often where a parent first hears that English is a concern. Cohorts are small, so a child can sit comfortably in the middle of a mixed group for three years without anyone diagnosing a specific weakness in inference. Checkpoint results, where a campus runs them, are the earliest honest signal available.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a First Language
programmes.description: Two years of work assessed by two written papers of two hours each, weighted equally. Paper 1 Reading presents unseen texts and tests comprehension, summary and analysis of a writer's language and effects. Paper 2 Directed Writing and Composition asks for one piece written to a specified audience, purpose and form in response to reading material, then one original composition chosen from descriptive or narrative options. A separately reported speaking component is available and does not alter the overall grade.
programmes.countryNote: This is the entry most English-medium campuses in the emirate use for students whose schooling has been in English. Centres in Ras Al Khaimah sit the qualification in the Cambridge June series overwhelmingly, with a smaller November cohort covering retakes and private candidates. Confirm the code on the statement of entry with the exams officer rather than assuming from the class name.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language
programmes.description: The alternative entry for students who use English confidently for study but not as a first language. Assessment covers reading and writing, listening and a speaking test, and the mark scheme credits accurate, appropriate language in a way 0500 does not. 0511 is the variant where the speaking component counts towards the overall grade rather than being separately reported. Universities and the UAE equivalency process treat it as an accredited subject, but it is not interchangeable with 0500.
programmes.countryNote: A meaningful share of Ras Al Khaimah candidates sit this route, and the decision is usually taken by the school on the basis of prior attainment rather than by the family. If your child is on 0510 and wants 0500, that is a conversation with the head of English in Year 9, not something a tutor can change in Year 11.

programmes.name: A Level English and IB Diploma English A
programmes.description: Both post-16 routes assume the reading skill that 0500 Paper 1 measures. A Level English Literature works through set texts with unseen comparison; IB Diploma English A Language and Literature adds an individual oral and a comparative essay on non-literary and literary texts. Students arriving from a strong 0500 cope with the volume; students who scraped the grade on strong writing alone tend to struggle first with unseen analysis under time pressure.
programmes.countryNote: Post-16 English provision is thinner in Ras Al Khaimah than in Dubai, and some families commute south or move campus for it. That calculation is worth doing in Year 10, not after results day, because it changes which English entry and which second English subject make sense now.

ras-al-khaimah/cambridge-igcse-english-f.subjectsIntro: The grid below is the Cambridge family a Ras Al Khaimah English candidate actually sits inside, with the codes as they appear on a statement of entry. Every one of these is a distinct qualification with its own papers; none is a tier or a sub-level of another.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500)
subjects.description: Two two-hour papers weighted equally. Paper 1 tests reading of unseen texts including a summary task and analysis of language and effect; Paper 2 tests directed writing against a brief plus one composition. Marks are lost most often on summary selection and on analysis that describes a technique without explaining its effect.

subjects.name: First Language English, 9-1 graded variant
subjects.description: Some centres enter the numerically graded version of First Language English instead of the A*-G code. The teaching, papers and skills are the same; only the reported grade scale differs. Ask the exams officer which code appears on the statement of entry, because grade conversations with a tutor are meaningless until that is settled.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Reading and writing, listening and speaking. The mark scheme credits range and accuracy of language explicitly. In 0511 the speaking test contributes to the overall grade; in 0510 it is reported separately. Students moved from 0500 to this route often improve fastest on the listening component, which rewards a trainable exam technique.

subjects.name: Literature in English (0475)
subjects.description: Set texts in poetry, prose and drama, studied over two years and written about in closed-book or open-book conditions depending on the component chosen by the centre. Rewards close textual knowledge and quotation under pressure. Frequently sat alongside 0500, which is why families assume it is the same subject. It is not.

subjects.name: World Literature (0408)
subjects.description: A smaller literature entry built on texts in translation alongside texts in English, with an essay portfolio element in some routes. Rarely offered in the northern emirates, but worth knowing about if a campus mentions it, because its assessment pattern differs from 0475 in ways that change how revision is spent.

subjects.name: Global Perspectives (0457)
subjects.description: Research, argument and written communication assessed through an individual report and a team project rather than a timed essay paper. Students who find 0500 Paper 2 directed writing difficult often do well here, and the reverse holds too. The transferable skill is evidence selection, which pays back directly into the 0500 summary question.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Listed because English and maths are the two entries that gate most post-16 and university routes, and because a family buying one subject of support usually needs to decide about the other in the same month. Extended is the tier that keeps A Level and Diploma mathematics open.

subjects.name: History (0470)
subjects.description: Source-based questions that reward exactly the inference skill 0500 Paper 1 tests, applied to documents instead of literary extracts. Students who are weak at reading between the lines show it in both subjects at once, which is often the clearest diagnostic a parent gets.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Thirty-mark multiple choice paper plus a structured paper worth seventy per cent of the grade. Included here because its eight-mark evaluation questions demand the same disciplined paragraph construction as 0500 directed writing, and support in one frequently lifts the other.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Case-study questions where command words control the mark ceiling. Another subject where a student who writes fluently but does not answer the question asked loses marks in the same pattern as on Paper 2 Section A. Worth pairing in a single tutoring plan if both grades are soft.

sections.heading: 0500, 0510, 0475 or 4EA1: which English your child is actually entered for
paragraphs: Four qualifications are in play for an English-medium student in Ras Al Khaimah, and the differences between them are structural rather than cosmetic. Cambridge IGCSE English as a First Language, code 0500, assumes English is the student's main language of education and tests reading of unseen material alongside original writing. Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language, 0510 and 0511, assumes English is an additional language used confidently for study, and credits accurate and appropriate language use in its own right. Literature in English, 0475, is a study of set texts. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE English Language A, 4EA1, is a different board's first-language qualification with its own paper structure and an available coursework route.

The table below sets out what each one is and how to confirm which applies to your child. The single document that settles it is the statement of entry issued by the centre, which lists syllabus codes against each subject. A school report will not tell you. Nor will the textbook, since several of the widely used coursebooks cover both 0500 and 0510 in one volume with the distinction buried in the contents page.

Getting this wrong costs a term. A tutor preparing a 0510 candidate with 0500 Paper 1 inference practice is working above the mark scheme and ignoring the listening component that the student will actually be examined on. A tutor preparing a 0500 candidate with 0510 grammar drills is tidying language that the first-language mark scheme largely takes for granted, while the reading half of the qualification goes untouched. Both students make progress at something; neither makes progress at the thing being assessed.

The decision itself is normally the school's, taken on prior attainment at the end of Year 9. It can be discussed, but it is a Year 9 conversation with the head of English, not a Year 11 one. What a tutor can do at any stage is confirm which route is live, read the relevant mark scheme and teach to it.

sections.heading: First language or second language: the decision a school makes for you
paragraphs: Families sometimes read the second-language route as a lesser qualification. It is not a tier of 0500, and treating it as a demotion leads to bad choices. Both are accredited IGCSE subjects. Both count towards the five accredited subjects the Ministry of Education requires on the British track for secondary certificate equivalency. Universities in the UAE and abroad accept either as evidence of English attainment, though a specific department may ask for a particular grade or a separate language test.

What differs is what earns marks. On the second-language route, a candidate who writes accurately, with appropriate register and controlled structures, is rewarded for exactly that. The listening component is a trainable skill with a clear technique: predicting answer types, tracking signposts, managing the gaps between questions. Many students lift that component by a grade with a handful of focused sessions, which is the fastest available improvement in the whole English family.

On 0500 the reward sits elsewhere. Half the qualification is reading unseen material, and the mark scheme asks for selection, inference and explanation of effect. A student who writes beautiful prose and cannot explain why a writer put a particular verb in a particular place is capped. This is the single most common misdiagnosis we see from Ras Al Khaimah families: the child is articulate, the parent cannot understand the grade, and nobody has looked at the reading paper.

There is a practical consequence for how a term of support is spent. A 0510 student who needs the overall grade moved should usually start with listening and with the directed writing task, because both respond quickly. A 0500 student in the same position should start with the summary question and with one analysis paragraph a week, because both are slow-building and leaving them to the final term is how a predicted grade becomes a disappointment in August.

sections.heading: Paper 1 and Paper 2: what each one is worth and what it asks
paragraphs: 0500 is assessed by two written papers, each two hours long and each worth half of the grade. There is no examined coursework in the standard route, which means there is nowhere to bank marks in advance and nothing to carry into the examination room except technique. For a parent weighing whether support is worth buying, that is the relevant fact: every mark is won in four hours in one series.

Paper 1 Reading presents unseen texts and asks a small number of questions across them. One task requires comprehension and selection of material and includes a summary written in the candidate's own words. Another requires analysis of a writer's language and the effects it creates. Another asks for an extended response to reading, in which the candidate writes in a specified form or voice using material from the passage. The common thread is that nothing can be prepared in advance, so what is being examined is a habit rather than a body of knowledge.

Paper 2 Directed Writing and Composition is in two sections. Section A gives reading material and a brief: a specified audience, purpose and form, with marks split between reading the material accurately and writing effectively. Section B offers a choice of composition tasks, descriptive and narrative, and awards marks for content and structure and for style and accuracy. The composition choice is the single most consequential two minutes of the paper, and the most common error we see is a student picking the title that sounds interesting instead of the one they have practised the shape of.

Mark allocations within each paper change between syllabus versions, so the current syllabus document for your child's examination year on cambridgeinternational.org is the thing to check rather than a figure from an older coursebook. What has held steady is the fifty-fifty split between the two papers and the two-hour duration of each.

sections.heading: The coursework portfolio alternative, and why most centres here do not use it
paragraphs: Cambridge offers a coursework portfolio as an alternative to the second written paper in First Language English. Where a centre runs it, the candidate produces a set of assignments during the course, internally assessed by the school and externally moderated by Cambridge. It is a legitimate route and it suits some students very well, particularly those whose writing is strong but whose examination timing is poor.

Most centres in the northern emirates do not offer it, and the reason is administrative rather than pedagogical. A coursework route requires trained internal assessors, a moderation submission, and an authentication process in which the school certifies that the work is the candidate's own and produced under supervision. In a small department running three or four English entries at once, that is a real staffing cost. Ask the exams officer directly; do not assume from the presence of a portfolio folder in the classroom, which is often just coursework-style practice feeding into the examined route.

If your child's centre does run the portfolio route, the tutoring changes shape and the boundaries tighten considerably. A tutor may teach the form, work through published exemplars, discuss structure in the abstract and help a student understand feedback the school has given. A tutor may not draft, rewrite or edit a portfolio piece to completion, and should not be reading successive drafts of a live assignment at all. The centre is certifying authorship; anything that compromises that certification puts your child, not the tutor, at risk.

Our position on this is fixed and we would rather state it early than be asked. On a coursework centre's portfolio, support happens on practice pieces that will never be submitted, built on the same skills. On an examined centre's Paper 2, support happens on timed practice marked against the published criteria. In both cases the work that reaches Cambridge is the student's own, written without a tutor in the room.

sections.heading: Five places 0500 marks go missing, and what each looks like on a script
paragraphs: After reading enough mock scripts from this emirate a pattern becomes visible, and it is almost never a vocabulary problem. The first leak is the summary. The task asks for the candidate's own words, and a student who has been praised for years for quoting accurately will do exactly the wrong thing: reproduce phrasing from the passage, lose the credit for selection and run over length while doing it. The fix is mechanical and takes about four sessions: read, close the text, write from notes, then check back only for accuracy of content.

The second is analysis that stops at identification. A script that says the writer uses a metaphor, names it correctly and moves on has earned very little. The mark is in the effect: what the image makes the reader feel or picture, and why that serves the writer's purpose at that point in the text. Students arrive at this habit honestly, because device-spotting is easy to teach and easy to test in class, and it has a ceiling that most of them hit around a grade C or a 5.

The third is the extended response to reading, where candidates write in a voice from the passage and quietly abandon the passage's content. Marks are awarded for using the material, developing it and staying inside what the text supports. Invention that contradicts the source is a double loss: it fails the reading objective and reads as careless. The fourth is the composition choice, made in panic, at the end of a long paper, by a student who has practised narrative all year and picks the descriptive title because it looks easier.

The fifth is simple timing. Two papers of two hours is a long sit for a sixteen-year-old, and a script that runs out of time on the last task loses more than the task is worth, because the earlier answers were also written at the wrong pace. We time every practice paper and show the student the clock, because a student who has sat four full papers under conditions does not panic in the fifth.
bullets: Summary written from notes with the passage closed, not paraphrased line by line
Every analysis point to name the effect, not only the device
Extended response kept inside what the source text actually supports
Composition title chosen on practised shape, not on apparent ease
Full papers sat to time at least three times before the series

sections.heading: The Cambridge series counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every examination centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge is explicit that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone; it states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. That sentence is worth reading twice, because it is the parent's responsibility as much as the school's.

The deadline that surprises families is the entry deadline, which sits months before the paper. Take the two series a Ras Al Khaimah candidate can actually sit. For the June series the examination period runs from May into June, the centre's final entry closes in the spring, forecast grades go to Cambridge in the weeks before the first paper, and results reach centres on Cambridge International Direct in August. For the November series the entries close over the summer, the papers run in October and November, and results follow in late January. The February and March sitting that a search result may show you is offered in India only, so its deadlines describe a series your child will never enter. Different series carry different dates and the exact day is printed on the statement of entry, but the shape holds either way: entries close months, not weeks, before the first paper.

What this means for a Ras Al Khaimah family buying English support is that the useful decisions are made much earlier than instinct suggests. A decision in September about which English route and which tier of a paired subject is a real decision. The same conversation in February is mostly about damage control, because entries have closed and the room for manoeuvre is technique and timing rather than qualification choice.

sections.heading: What 0500 support costs around Ras Al Khaimah
paragraphs: Start at the cheap end, because that is where most families start and where the disappointment usually happens. Budget online tutoring in this market runs from around AED 45 to AED 150 an hour: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52, both for online sessions typically delivered by university students or generalist teachers. For a Year 8 reading habit that is defensible. For 0500 Paper 1, where the whole task is a trained examiner's eye on an unseen text, a generalist is being asked to do something they have not done, and the hour is pleasant and ineffective.

One step up, a qualified subject tutor working online sits in the AED 150 to 300 band; Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A named IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table putting specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. At the top, premium named or examiner-led tutors are advertised well beyond that, with BartyED at AED 650. Monthly packages circulate too: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

The in-home comparison is the interesting one for a family in Mina Al Arab or Al Qusaidat. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors are quoted from AED 200 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel. The premium over an online rate is not buying better teaching. It is buying a commute, and in the northern emirates it is buying it from a much smaller pool: the tutors willing to drive to Al Rams for a single hour are the tutors who happen to live nearby, not the ones who have marked a thousand 0500 scripts.

All of these are market figures published by other providers, dated to this market in 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram price. Book the free trial, see the tutor teach, and get the number in writing afterwards. sections.heading: English in the Ministry of Education equivalency count
paragraphs: Families planning a UAE university route need to know how the Ministry of Education treats a British-track certificate, and English sits at the centre of it. On the British track, a student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which means the five have to come from elsewhere in the timetable.

That detail has a direct consequence for subject choice. One competitor page ranking for these queries states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced requirement is five accredited subjects excluding Arabic and Islamic education. If a family has planned a timetable around the wrong number, the error surfaces at attestation rather than at results, which is the worst possible moment to find it.

The American track is governed differently and is worth knowing about because many Ras Al Khaimah families hold both options open. There, English proficiency is demonstrated by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. Those are published figures for that track and do not transfer to the British one.

Two cautions. Equivalency is a process run by the Ministry of Education and the emirate's attestation authority, not something a tutoring platform performs, guarantees or accelerates; verify current requirements on moe.gov.ae before making a decision that depends on them. And no International Baccalaureate points threshold appears in the source we are able to cite, so any figure you see published for the Diploma should be checked against the Ministry's own page rather than trusted from a tutoring site, including this one.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the assessed skill is writing
paragraphs: English is the subject where the line between teaching and doing the work is easiest to blur, because the deliverable is a piece of writing and improving writing feels like editing writing. It is worth being explicit about where the line sits, both because a centre authenticates coursework and because a family paying for support deserves to know what they are buying.

A tutor can teach form, structure and technique. A tutor can work through published exemplar scripts and mark schemes, mark practice pieces that will never be submitted, annotate a returned mock, explain a comment the school has made, model a paragraph on a different title, and run timed practice. A tutor can also tell a student, bluntly, that a piece is not good enough and why, which is frequently the most valuable hour in a term.

A tutor does not write, redraft or edit to completion any piece that will be submitted for assessment. On a coursework centre's portfolio that is an authentication breach and the consequence lands on the candidate. On an examined route it is simply useless, because nobody will be in the room during the paper. The services in this market that advertise finished assessed work are selling something that puts a student's qualification at risk, and we say so on every page rather than compete quietly alongside them.

There is one practical rule we give families that settles most questions before they arise. If the piece of writing will be seen by an examiner or a moderator, a tutor's hands stay off it; everything the tutor touches is practice. If a student cannot produce a piece of that quality alone in two hours with a blank page, the support has not worked yet, and the right response is more practice rather than more polish.
