faqs.question: Is my child sitting Cambridge 0500 or English as a Second Language 0510?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry issued by your child's centre is the document that settles it, because it lists syllabus codes against each subject. A school report will usually say only English. The coursebook will not help either, since several widely used texts cover both syllabuses in one volume. If you cannot find the statement of entry, the exams officer can confirm the code in a minute. Ask before buying any support, because preparation for the two routes diverges sharply: 0500 is half unseen reading, while the second-language route credits accurate language use and includes a listening component that 0500 does not have.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 0500 and Literature in English 0475?
faqs.answer: They are separate qualifications, not two halves of one subject. 0500 tests reading of unseen material and original writing, so nothing can be learned in advance. 0475 is built on set texts studied across two years and written about in examination conditions, closed or open book depending on the components your centre offers. Many students sit both, which is why families assume they are related. For tutoring the consequence is practical: revision for 0475 is text knowledge and quotation, revision for 0500 is habit and technique, and merging the two workloads usually means the unseen reading gets squeezed out.

faqs.question: Does the 9-1 graded code change what my child studies?
faqs.answer: No. Where a centre enters the numerically graded variant of Cambridge First Language English rather than the A*-G code, the syllabus content, the papers and the skills assessed are the same; only the reported grade scale differs. What matters is that you know which one applies before having any conversation about target grades, because a target of a 6 and a target of a B are not the same sentence. The code is printed on the statement of entry. If a tutor or a report talks about grades without that being settled, the conversation is built on sand.

faqs.question: How is the 0500 summary question marked, and why does my daughter keep losing marks on it?
faqs.answer: The summary task asks for relevant content expressed in the candidate's own words, and both halves carry credit. The commonest failure is a student who selects accurately but reproduces the passage's phrasing, because years of praise for careful quotation have trained exactly the wrong reflex here. The fix is mechanical rather than conceptual: read the passage, close it, write from brief notes, then check back only to confirm the content is right. Four or five supervised repetitions usually move it. Overlength answers are the second leak, and they are almost always a symptom of the same habit.

faqs.question: My son writes beautifully but his English grade is stuck. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Almost always it is the reading paper, and almost always nobody has looked at it. Paper 1 is half the qualification, and its marks come from selection, inference and explanation of a writer's effects, none of which a strong prose style supplies. An articulate student with a weak reading habit will sit around a middling grade indefinitely while every adult around him is puzzled. Ask to see the mock reading script rather than the composition. If the analysis answers name techniques without explaining their effect, you have found the problem and it is fixable in about a term.

faqs.question: Does 0500 have a speaking test, and does it affect the grade?
faqs.answer: Cambridge makes a speaking component available in First Language English, and in 0500 it is reported separately rather than contributing to the overall grade. In the second-language family the position differs: 0511 counts the speaking test towards the overall grade while 0510 reports it separately. This matters when a family is deciding where to spend limited preparation time. On 0500 the speaking component is worth doing properly for its own sake and for university applications, but an hour spent on it is an hour not spent on the two papers that carry the whole grade.

faqs.question: Can essay writing really be taught properly over video?
faqs.answer: It is one of the subjects where video is a genuine upgrade rather than a compromise. The student's script sits on a shared screen, annotated live, with both people looking at the same sentence and the same mark scheme. Nothing is passed across a table and nothing is lost on the way home, because the annotated version is saved and sent. Timed practice is sat in the student's own study space, which is where the real paper will feel least like a performance. What video cannot supply is reading volume, and no format can; that part is a household habit.

faqs.question: How many weeks of 0500 support does a Year 11 student in Ras Al Khaimah usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends which of the five common leaks is costing the marks. Timing and composition choice respond to six to eight sessions, because they are technique. Summary and analysis take longer: expect a term of weekly work with one marked piece a fortnight before the change holds under examination pressure. Reading volume is slower still and is not solved in a tutorial at all. We read the mock script first and say which category your child falls into, because selling a weekly slot for a problem that needs a reading habit would waste your money and your child's evenings.

faqs.question: Which composition should my daughter choose in Paper 2, descriptive or narrative?
faqs.answer: Whichever shape she has practised, not whichever title sounds more interesting on the day. That choice is made in the last hour of a long paper by a tired sixteen-year-old, which is why it should be decided months earlier and rehearsed. Most students are structurally better at one than the other: narrative rewards shape and restraint, description rewards controlled focus and precise observation. We establish which one she is reliably stronger at, practise that form repeatedly, and agree a rule in advance so the decision in the examination room takes seconds rather than minutes.

faqs.question: Does English First Language count towards Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track a student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five, so those five must come from the rest of the timetable, and an English entry normally forms part of them. One ranking competitor states six subjects are required; the sourced figure is five. Verify current requirements on moe.gov.ae, because equivalency is the Ministry's process and not something a tutoring platform performs.

faqs.question: What does Cambridge English tuition cost for a family in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Market rates in this country, published by other providers in 2026, run from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour at the budget online end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit inclusive of travel, and AED 200 to 450 and above for an IGCSE or A Level specialist. Monthly packages of around AED 799 for eight online sessions circulate too. Those are other people's figures, cited for context. IB Gram does not publish a rate card on these pages; book the free trial, watch the tutor teach, and get a number in writing afterwards.

faqs.question: Is 0500 enough preparation for A Level English or IB Diploma English A?
faqs.answer: It is the right foundation, and the part that transfers is the reading. Both post-16 routes assume a student can analyse unseen material under time pressure, which is exactly what Paper 1 measures. The students who struggle are the ones who reached a decent 0500 grade on strong writing while the reading half stayed weak; that gap closes slowly and it closes in the first term of a two-year course, when there is least room for it. If a student is heading for post-16 English, the reading paper is the thing to fix now rather than later.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's practice essays without breaking Cambridge rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the core of the work. A tutor may mark practice pieces that will never be submitted, annotate a returned mock, work through published exemplars and mark schemes, model a paragraph on a different title and explain the school's own feedback. What a tutor must not do is write, redraft or edit to completion any piece that will go to an examiner or a moderator. The practical rule we give families is simple: if an examiner will see it, the tutor's hands stay off it, and everything the tutor touches is practice.

faqs.question: Our centre runs the coursework portfolio route. Does that change the tutoring?
faqs.answer: It changes the boundaries rather than the skills. Where a centre offers the coursework portfolio as an alternative to the second written paper, the school internally assesses the work, Cambridge moderates it, and the centre certifies that the work is the candidate's own and produced under supervision. Support therefore happens on practice pieces built from the same skills, never on successive drafts of a live assignment. Confirm with the exams officer that the portfolio route is genuinely being used, because portfolio-style folders often turn out to be practice feeding into the examined route.

faqs.question: What happens if no 0500 specialist is free in the evening slot we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than putting a generalist in the slot and hoping. Ras Al Khaimah families often want 5pm or 6pm on Gulf Standard Time, and those hours fill first. The options are usually a different evening, a weekend morning for extended writing practice, or a wait of a week or two for the right tutor. If none of that works for your household, we say so and you lose nothing, because the trial lesson is booked before any payment. A convenient tutor teaching the wrong mark scheme is worse value than no tutor.

faqs.question: Do English lessons continue through Ramadan and the shortened school day?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the timing moved rather than the work paused. Shortened school days free up afternoon slots that are impossible during the rest of the year, and some families move sessions to after Iftar instead. Ramadan often falls close enough to the summer series that stopping for a month costs more than it saves, particularly for a student who needs weekly marked writing to hold a new habit in place. We agree the revised slot in advance so the fortnightly marking cycle keeps running, and reading practice continues at a lighter volume.

ras-al-khaimah/cambridge-igcse-english-f.closingBody: Two things are worth doing this week. The trial lesson is free and happens before any payment, with the tutor your child would keep.

intro.heading: The tier decision, the regulator and the distances: 0580 in Ras Al Khaimah
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is entered at one of two tiers, and in Ras Al Khaimah that choice carries more weight than in a larger emirate. Core is graded C to G. Extended is graded A* to E. A student entered at Core cannot be awarded a B or an A regardless of how well they perform, which closes several post-16 routes before results day arrives. Each tier is assessed by two equally weighted written papers, one taken without a calculator and one with, and the current syllabus covers nine topic areas: number, algebra and graphs, coordinate geometry, geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, transformations and vectors, probability, and statistics.

The reason the tier decision is sharper here is structural. Ras Al Khaimah's private-school set is small and concentrated around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab, so most schools run a single mathematics pathway per year group with limited capacity to move a student between sets mid-year. Where a larger Dubai school might carry three Extended sets and absorb a change in February, a RAK school often cannot. The practical consequence is that a decision taken in Year 10, sometimes on the basis of one set of internal results, follows a student into the series.

Ras Al Khaimah also regulates its own private education. The u.ae private-schools page states that the Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate, and that Ras Al Khaimah's authority — like Sharjah's — approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a broader remit than inspection alone, and it is why a RAK school's curriculum offer is not simply a commercial decision. It also means this emirate is not covered by KHDA, whose reports and guidance documents are specific to Dubai, a confusion that appears constantly in advice written for a national audience.

On cost, start with what the travel premium actually buys, because in this emirate it buys less than anywhere else in the country. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour, and independent home tutors at AED 200 to AED 500 once driving is included. Those numbers were built on a market where a tutor crosses a city. In Ras Al Khaimah a specialist mathematics tutor is often driving from Dubai or Sharjah, an hour or more each way, and a family is paying for that hour at the same rate as the teaching. Online delivery for comparison sits at AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor, with Unitors publishing AED 150 as its IGCSE starting rate, and AED 200 to AED 450 and above for an examined-subject specialist, with TutorChase quoting AED 270. Those are the providers' and the survey's own published figures.

IB Gram delivers 0580 as one-to-one tuition over live video, with a shared whiteboard for working and the mark scheme open alongside the student's script. We do not send tutors to addresses in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service we run only in India. For mathematics the screen is close to neutral in capability and clearly better in access: a RAK family gets a specialist who has taught both 0580 tiers rather than whoever is willing to make the drive north on a Tuesday evening.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580)
programmes.description: Two years, two tiers, two written papers per tier with equal weighting. There is no coursework. The Extended tier covers the same nine topic areas as Core but to greater depth, with additional content in algebra, trigonometry, functions and vectors that does not appear on the Core papers at all. That additional content is the part a student switching tiers late has to acquire from scratch.
programmes.countryNote: Ras Al Khaimah schools generally run one mathematics pathway per year group, so a tier decision made in Year 10 is difficult to reverse in Year 11. Where families here buy private support in Year 10, the purpose is frequently to keep the Extended option open rather than to chase a grade, and that is a legitimate and cheaper use of tutoring than a Year 11 rescue.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level Mathematics (9709)
programmes.description: Requires the Extended tier in practice, and most centres expect a strong Extended grade before admitting a student. Pure Mathematics 1 assumes fluent algebraic manipulation from the first week, with no revisiting of IGCSE content. Students entered at Core who later want this route face a conversion year rather than a smooth transition.
programmes.countryNote: Sixth-form mathematics provision in the northern emirates is concentrated in a few schools, so continuing may mean applying across the emirate boundary. A predicted Extended grade therefore functions as an admissions document in Year 11, which argues for building evidence in the autumn term rather than the spring.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches / Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: The Diploma splits mathematics into two courses. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented and is the usual expectation for engineering, physics and mathematics degrees. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics oriented. Both are offered at SL and HL, and both assume Extended-level IGCSE fluency; AA HL in particular assumes a good deal more than that.
programmes.countryNote: Because Diploma provision in Ras Al Khaimah is limited, students choosing this route are often the ones moving schools at 16. The route choice between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation should be checked against the entry requirements of the specific universities being considered, since they differ by subject and by country.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics (0606)
programmes.description: Taken alongside Extended 0580 by stronger mathematicians, usually in Year 11 only. It introduces calculus, functions, series and more demanding trigonometry, and it bridges the gap into AS Level considerably. It is not a replacement for 0580 and does not substitute for it in any equivalency count.
programmes.countryNote: 0606 runs in only a handful of schools in the northern emirates and often with very small groups, which makes it one of the hardest subjects to find local private support for. Where a RAK school offers it, the teaching set may be fewer than ten students, and individual marking capacity is correspondingly limited.

ras-al-khaimah/cambridge-igcse-maths-058.subjectsIntro: Mathematics sits underneath most of the other subjects a Ras Al Khaimah student is sitting, and weakness in 0580 shows up in their marks before it shows up in the maths grade. Below is what each neighbouring subject assesses and where the 0580 dependency actually bites.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: This page's subject. Two equally weighted papers per tier, one without a calculator. Marks concentrate and disappear in algebraic manipulation, multi-step problem solving and the questions that require a method to be shown rather than an answer stated.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Calculus, functions, series and advanced trigonometry for students already secure in Extended content. Valuable preparation for AS Level and rarely available locally, which makes it a common reason RAK families look beyond the emirate for teaching.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: The subject where weak 0580 algebra does the most damage. Rearranging formulae, handling standard form and reading gradients are maths skills examined inside a physics paper, alongside a practical or alternative-to-practical component worth a fifth of the grade.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, concentration and yield work all depend on ratio and proportion fluency. A student who struggles with 0580 number work loses chemistry marks that look like chemistry gaps and are not.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Lighter on calculation than the other sciences but still requires percentage change, magnification and surface-area-to-volume reasoning, plus a practical or alternative-to-practical paper worth 20 per cent.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Two equally weighted written papers covering computer systems, then algorithms, programming and logic. Number bases and logical manipulation draw directly on 0580 number work.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: A 30 per cent multiple-choice paper plus a 70 per cent written paper with a data-response extract. Percentage, index and elasticity calculations are modest but regularly cost marks for students weak in arithmetic.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Two 80-mark papers, half of it a case study. Break-even, margins and ratio interpretation are the quantitative core, and they are skipped most often by students who are uncomfortable with 0580 number work.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Data interpretation, graph reading and simple statistics appear throughout. The resource-booklet skill overlaps with 0580's data-handling questions more than either syllabus admits.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the 0580 decision Ras Al Khaimah families cannot easily reverse
paragraphs: This is the question that matters most and it is frequently decided by default. The Core tier of Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is graded C to G; the Extended tier is graded A* to E. A student entered at Core who performs superbly is still capped at a C. That cap is invisible until results day and it closes the AS Mathematics route, weakens an engineering or medicine profile, and limits sixth-form options at the schools that ask for a B or better.

In a large Dubai school the decision is comparatively low-stakes because there are several sets and the capacity to move a student in either direction through Year 10 and into Year 11. In Ras Al Khaimah the school is usually running one mathematics pathway per year group. Moving a student up in February means asking a teacher to deliver the Extended-only content — the additional algebra, the functions work, the trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles, the vector geometry — to one student outside lesson time. Most schools cannot, and will say so honestly.

Which is why the most cost-effective tutoring in this emirate is often bought in Year 10 rather than Year 11, and bought to keep an option open rather than to chase a grade. A student who arrives at the tiering conversation with marked evidence of Extended-level algebra is in a completely different negotiating position from one who arrives with a parent's opinion. The table below sets out what actually differs between the tiers, so a family can judge the decision on content rather than on confidence.

One honest caveat. Extended is not automatically the right answer. A student genuinely struggling with Core content will do better with a secure C on the Core tier than with a D or an E on Extended, and some post-16 routes accept a Core grade perfectly well. The point is that the decision should be made deliberately, with evidence, and not inherited from a single set of November results.

sections.heading: The Department of Knowledge, and what regulation in this emirate actually covers
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah is not a KHDA emirate, and advice written for Dubai does not transfer cleanly. The u.ae private-schools page states that Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate, and that Ras Al Khaimah's and Sharjah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Fee and curriculum approval sitting with the emirate regulator is a meaningfully different arrangement from inspection-plus-reporting, and it shapes what a RAK school can and cannot offer.

For a parent, two practical points follow. First, when you ask a school why it does not run Additional Mathematics 0606 or a second Extended set, the answer may involve approvals rather than demand, and asking the question in those terms usually gets a straighter answer. Second, guidance documents published by KHDA — including its mandatory-subjects requirements and its inspection framework — describe Dubai's system. They are useful as the clearest public description of how UAE private schooling works, and they are not the rules your RAK school is working to.

It is worth knowing the full map, because families in the northern emirates move between them. Dubai's KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in that emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall to ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education. Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge. All five are named on the same u.ae page, and ADEK in particular is mentioned by none of the competitor pages reviewed in this market.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from the Department of Knowledge, the Ministry of Education or any other UAE authority, and no tutoring platform should imply otherwise. Naming a regulator and explaining its remit is useful to a parent choosing a school. Claiming its endorsement would be something else entirely.

sections.heading: The two 0580 papers, and the non-calculator problem
paragraphs: Each 0580 tier is assessed by two written papers of equal weight, one sat without a calculator and one with. The non-calculator paper is the one that surprises families, and it surprises them for a straightforward reason: a generation of students learned mathematics with a calculator permanently available, and unaided arithmetic, surd manipulation and estimation are therefore unpractised rather than unknown. Confirm the exact paper numbers, durations and mark totals for your child's series against the syllabus document on the Cambridge International site, because assessment structures are revised periodically and a school's own handbook may lag.

What the non-calculator paper actually tests is not mental arithmetic for its own sake. It tests whether a student can manipulate an expression rather than evaluate it, recognise that a surd can be left in exact form, estimate well enough to notice an implausible answer, and carry a fraction through several steps without converting it to a decimal and losing precision. Those are the skills that AS Mathematics assumes from day one, which is why the paper exists.

The calculator paper has its own failure mode, and it is method marks. Multi-step questions award marks for the working, not only for the answer, and students who type a long calculation into the machine and write down the result lose marks even when the result is right. The habit to build is deliberate and slightly tedious: write the expression, write the substitution, then write the answer. Over a full paper that habit is worth more than any single topic, and it is the easiest thing for a tutor to see in a marked script and the hardest for a student to notice alone.

sections.heading: Where 0580 marks are lost, topic by topic
paragraphs: Mathematics is unusually diagnosable. A marked paper shows not just the score but the precise location of every lost mark, and across Ras Al Khaimah scripts the pattern repeats with a consistency that makes planning straightforward. Four areas account for most of the loss at Extended level: algebraic fractions and rearrangement, trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles, vectors and transformations, and the probability questions that combine conditions.

Underneath those four sits a fifth problem that is not a topic at all. Students lose marks for not showing working, for rounding too early in a multi-step calculation, for answering in the wrong form when exact form was required, and for not reading the units. Those are presentation and discipline faults, they cost several marks a paper, and they are fixed faster than any content gap. A tutor who starts with content before fixing these is spending the family's money in the wrong order.

The table that follows maps the usual losses to what the fix costs in sessions. The estimates assume the student does the between-session work, because mathematics improves through attempted questions rather than through watched explanations. A plan with no homework in it has no mechanism, and a student who watches thirty hours of worked solutions without attempting anything will arrive in the exam hall exactly where they started. One further note on sequencing. Fix the discipline faults first, then the topic with the largest mark loss, then the rest in descending order of cost. Working down a list of topics in syllabus order instead feels tidier and wastes several weeks on areas the student was already scoring well in, which is the commonest way a reasonable plan becomes an expensive one.

sections.heading: The Ras Al Khaimah year, Ramadan, and the series counted backwards
paragraphs: Almost nobody in this market publishes an exam deadline, which is strange, because deadlines constrain a plan more than ambition does. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and the February and March sitting that surfaces in search results is offered in India only, so it is not a date a Ras Al Khaimah family can plan against. Entries close well before the papers. For the June series the centre's final entry closes in the spring, forecast grades follow in the weeks before the first paper, the papers themselves run from May into June on the timetable for your centre's zone, and results land on Cambridge International Direct in August. The November series repeats that sequence half a year later, with entries over the summer and results in late January.

Read backwards, that schedule tells a RAK family when decisions actually happen. The tier is fixed at entry, months before the paper. The forecast grade is submitted from evidence the school already holds. So the conversation about whether a student should be entered at Extended belongs in the autumn term, supported by marked work, and not in the spring when the entry has already gone. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, where a school uses that board, exams run in May/June and November and provisional timetables are published ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is the only one to plan against.

Then there is Ramadan, which no competitor page in this market mentions at all. School days shorten, routines move into the evening, and the practical session slot moves to after Iftar. Because Ramadan shifts earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar it can fall close to a spring series, which is exactly when a Year 11 student needs their heaviest timed-paper work. The approach that holds up is front-loading: put the full papers into January and early February, and use the Ramadan weeks for shorter consolidation and marking review rather than for new content.

One detail that catches families who have moved from another country. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Get the timetable from your school's exams officer rather than from a search result, and get the zone in writing.

sections.heading: What the travel premium buys in this emirate, and what it does not
paragraphs: Across the UAE, in-home one-to-one tuition is quoted at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour by Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, and at AED 200 to AED 500 by independent home tutors once driving is priced in. Those bands were formed in a market where a tutor crosses a city. In Ras Al Khaimah the geography is different in kind. A specialist mathematics tutor serving Al Hamra Village or Mina Al Arab is frequently driving from Dubai or Sharjah, and the return leg after a 7.30pm session is long. A family paying the in-home premium here is buying the same teaching as elsewhere plus considerably more driving.

What the premium genuinely buys is presence: an adult in the room, a phone put away, a younger child who cannot wander off. For some students that is worth paying for and nobody should pretend otherwise. What it does not buy is subject depth, and in mathematics at Extended level with a tier decision pending, subject depth is the thing a family is actually short of. The published online bands for comparison are AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor, with Unitors quoting AED 150 for IGCSE, and AED 200 to AED 450 and above for an examined-subject specialist, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650 at the named-premium end.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Ras Al Khaimah or anywhere else in the UAE, and the reason is the one above rather than a logistical excuse: for this subject, in this emirate, the premium buys the wrong thing. Instead we match a 0580 specialist and run the session over live video with a shared whiteboard, which is where mathematical working belongs anyway — visible, editable, and saved rather than left on a sheet of paper. sections.heading: 0580 in the Ministry of Education equivalency count
paragraphs: Families planning on a UAE university need to know how an IGCSE profile is treated, and equivalency is a subject the competitor pages in this market do not address. Reporting on the Ministry's clarification states that British-track students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

Mathematics 0580 counts as one of those five on the same basis as any other IGCSE, at either tier, provided the grade clears the stated floor. That is a reassuring point for a Core-tier student worried about the equivalency route specifically: a Core C is comfortably above a grade E or 3. The tier question matters for post-16 study and for competitive admissions rather than for the equivalency count itself, and conflating the two is a common source of unnecessary alarm in Year 10.

Three cautions, all of which matter. The American-track requirements are separate, with English proficiency via a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics via at least 450 in SAT Math. No IB points threshold appears in the sourced reporting, so no figure for the IB route is published here. And one ranking competitor in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which the sourced reporting does not support. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority, because equivalency is a process the Ministry performs, not a service any tutoring platform provides, and tutoring is not required for it.

sections.heading: Starting with 0580, and the honest version of availability
paragraphs: The first step costs nothing: send the school, the year group, the current tier if one has been set, and a photograph of the last marked mathematics paper. For this subject the marked paper is close to a complete diagnosis — it shows the topics, the method-mark discipline, the rounding habits and whether the non-calculator work is the problem. A free trial lesson follows with the 0580 specialist who would teach the course, and no fee is taken until after it.

Scheduling is built around a Ras Al Khaimah week, which means acknowledging the drives. For families in Al Hamra Village, Mina Al Arab or Al Marjan Island a weekday session realistically starts at 7.30pm or later; for Al Nakheel, Al Dhait and Khuzam an earlier slot is often possible. Sessions are 60 minutes by default, with 90 minutes available when a full timed paper is the point. Rescheduling with reasonable notice carries no charge, because a plan that penalises a family for one slow evening on the Emirates Road is a plan that quietly ends in March.

Then the disclosure. Mathematics is the deepest coverage we have, so availability is rarely the constraint it is for a minority subject, but the weeks before a main series are tight everywhere and Additional Mathematics 0606 is genuinely scarce. When nobody suitable is free at your hour we say so and offer a different time with the specialist you asked for, an available tutor whose 0580 tier experience we describe precisely, or a dated place on the list. Because tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video, the pool is national rather than limited to whoever will drive north, which is the structural reason a RAK family should not be choosing from three names.

faqs.question: Should my child sit Cambridge IGCSE Maths 0580 at Core or Extended in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: It depends on current attainment, but the decision deserves more deliberation here than in a larger emirate. Core is graded C to G, so a Core entry caps the outcome at a C no matter how well the student performs. Extended is graded A* to E and keeps AS Mathematics and most Diploma routes open. Because RAK schools generally run one mathematics pathway per year group, moving up in Year 11 is difficult. The practical answer is to settle it in Year 10 with marked evidence of Extended-level algebra and trigonometry, rather than inheriting the decision from one internal test.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates private schools in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: The emirate's own Department of Knowledge. The u.ae private-schools page states that it regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah, and that Ras Al Khaimah's authority — like Sharjah's — approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a broader remit than inspection alone. It also means Ras Al Khaimah is not covered by KHDA: Dubai's authority publishes guidance and inspection reports for Dubai schools only, so advice written around KHDA documents does not describe the rules your RAK school is working to.

faqs.question: Does 0580 still have a non-calculator paper?
faqs.answer: The current syllabus assesses each tier through two equally weighted written papers, one taken without a calculator and one with. Confirm the exact paper numbers, durations and mark totals for your child's series against the syllabus document on the Cambridge International site, because assessment structures are revised periodically and school handbooks can lag behind. The practical point is unchanged either way: unaided arithmetic, surd work, exact-form answers and estimation need separate practice from calculator work. Students who learned mathematics with a calculator always available find this paper unfamiliar rather than difficult, which is a fixable problem.

faqs.question: What are the two 0580 papers worth at Extended level?
faqs.answer: Equal weight — half the grade each — with one paper taken without a calculator and one with. There is no coursework and no practical component, so nothing is banked before the series. That symmetry is useful for planning: a student who is strong on one paper type and weak on the other is losing up to half the available marks in a single identifiable skill, which a marked paper reveals immediately. Check the current mark totals and durations for your child's series with the school's exams officer or on the Cambridge International syllabus page rather than relying on any secondary summary.

faqs.question: Which 0580 topics cost Ras Al Khaimah students the most marks?
faqs.answer: At Extended level, four areas account for most of the loss: algebraic fractions and rearrangement, trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles, vectors and transformations, and probability questions that combine conditions. Beneath those sits a fifth problem that is not a topic — unshown working, premature rounding, and decimal answers where exact form was required. Those discipline faults cost several marks a paper and are fixed in one or two sessions, which is why a good tutor addresses them before teaching any new content. A marked paper identifies all five in about ten minutes.

faqs.question: When is it too late to switch a 0580 entry from Core to Extended?
faqs.answer: In practice the limit is the entry deadline, which falls months before the paper: for a June series the centre's final entry closes in the spring, well ahead of papers that run from May into June. But the real constraint in Ras Al Khaimah is teaching capacity rather than paperwork. With one mathematics pathway per year group, a school asked to deliver the Extended-only content to a single student outside lesson time usually cannot. That is why the useful conversation happens in Year 10, with marked evidence, and why support bought then is both cheaper and more effective than a rescue attempted once the entry has gone in.

faqs.question: What grades are available on the Core tier of 0580?
faqs.answer: Core is graded C to G. That is the single most important fact in the tier decision and it is frequently not explained to families until too late: a student entered at Core who performs excellently is still awarded a C. For some post-16 routes a secure C is perfectly sufficient, and a student genuinely struggling with Core content will do better with a confident C than with a D or E on Extended. The point is that the ceiling should be a deliberate choice made on evidence, not something discovered on results day.

faqs.question: Why are in-home maths rates higher in Ras Al Khaimah than in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because the driving is longer and somebody pays for it. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200 to AED 500, bands formed in a market where a tutor crosses a city. A specialist travelling to Al Hamra Village or Mina Al Arab is often driving from Dubai or Sharjah, an hour each way, and that time is recovered through the rate or through a two-hour minimum. Online qualified tuition sits at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing AED 150 for IGCSE.

faqs.question: How far ahead do Cambridge entries close for a 0580 candidate?
faqs.answer: Months ahead, and the deadline belongs to the school rather than the family. For the June series the centre's final entry closes in the spring, forecast grades go to Cambridge in the weeks before the first paper, the papers run from May into June, results reach centres on Cambridge International Direct in August and certificates follow later in the year; the November series repeats the pattern with entries over the summer and results in late January. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct zone timetable must be used, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. Ask your exams officer for the zone and the exact entry date in writing, because those are the only dates that bind you, and the February and March sitting quoted on some sites is India's series rather than yours.

faqs.question: Does Ras Al Khaimah approve school fees and curricula itself?
faqs.answer: Yes. The u.ae private-schools page states that Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, like Sharjah's authority, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That remit is wider than inspection and it has a practical consequence worth knowing: when a school explains that it cannot add a second Extended mathematics set or offer Additional Mathematics 0606, approvals may be part of the answer rather than demand alone. Asking the question in those terms usually produces a straighter response than asking why the subject is not offered.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan affect 0580 revision in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: School days shorten, household routines move into the evening, and the practical session slot shifts to after Iftar — typically 9pm or later, which suits Year 11 students better than younger ones. Because Ramadan moves earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar it can fall close to a spring exam series, exactly when timed-paper work should be heaviest. The approach that holds up is front-loading: complete the full marked papers in January and early February, then use the Ramadan weeks for shorter consolidation and review of corrections. Agreeing that shape in advance works far better than renegotiating it mid-month.

faqs.question: Is Maths 0580 one of the five subjects needed for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track it counts as one of them, at either tier, provided the grade clears the stated floor. Reporting on the Ministry's clarification states that students must pass five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. A Core C therefore clears the equivalency requirement comfortably. The tier matters for competitive post-16 admission rather than for this count. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority.

faqs.question: Can my child in Al Hamra Village get maths lessons without a drive into town?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most families in the southern communities that is the only version that works midweek. Al Hamra Village, Mina Al Arab and Al Marjan Island are a long way from the city's tuition centres, and a round trip in evening traffic consumes more time than the lesson itself. Sessions run one-to-one over live video with a shared whiteboard, so working is visible, editable and saved rather than left on a sheet of paper. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is a service we offer only in India.

faqs.question: Does my child need Additional Mathematics 0606 as well as 0580?
faqs.answer: Not for equivalency and not for most sixth-form entry, but it helps considerably for AS Mathematics. 0606 adds calculus, functions, series and harder trigonometry on top of Extended 0580, usually in Year 11 only, and it closes much of the gap into Pure Mathematics 1. It is offered in only a handful of northern-emirate schools and often to very small groups, which makes local private support for it genuinely scarce. If your child's school does not run it, that is a reason to look beyond the emirate for teaching rather than to assume the route is closed.

faqs.question: What evidence should a 0580 tutor show us each month?
faqs.answer: One full paper marked against the published scheme, with topic-level scores recorded across the nine syllabus areas, and the previous month's weakest topics named alongside what changed. That is the minimum a parent can use to judge whether the money is working without needing to assess mathematics themselves. If the record is flat after six sessions the plan is wrong and should change. Nobody should offer a predicted grade or promise a jump of two grades in exchange for the fee: the honest product is marked evidence and a visible trend, and any promised outcome deserves scepticism.

Send the school, the year group and a photograph of the last marked paper, and a 0580 specialist will say where the marks are going and what the Extended-only content would take. A free trial lesson with that tutor follows, at no charge. The rate bands on this page carry their sources, so any plan can be weighed against the published market. Lessons run one-to-one over live video.

intro.heading: Starting from the mark you have, not the grade you want
paragraphs: Physics is the IGCSE where a student's grade and their understanding most often disagree. A child can explain refraction clearly at the dinner table and still lose half the marks on a question about it, because 0625 does not test whether you understand physics. It tests whether you can state a definition in the words the mark scheme accepts, rearrange a formula under time pressure, read a value off a graph with a unit attached, and describe an experiment in enough detail that someone else could repeat it. Those are separate skills, and each one can be taught.

That is why this page is organised around time rather than around topics. The useful first question is not what your child finds hard, it is how many weeks remain before the paper and what the current script actually shows. A student twenty-four weeks out with a grade D mock has a different plan from one six weeks out with a grade B who keeps losing marks on the practical paper, and a sensible tutor will not offer the same course to both.

Ras Al Khaimah adds its own constraints to that arithmetic. The emirate's private-school set is small and spread between the city side around Al Nakheel, Khuzam and Al Uraibi and the southern coastal provision near Al Hamra, so the nearest physics specialist is often not near at all. Families from Mina Al Arab or Al Marjan Island who drive to a city tuition centre twice a week spend more time in the car than in the lesson, and the group class they arrive at is usually built around the maths and chemistry demand rather than physics.

IB Gram teaches every UAE lesson one-to-one over live video. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. The gain is not convenience, it is match quality: a student in Al Dhait can be taught by a tutor who teaches 0625 all week, rather than by whoever is willing to drive to Al Dhait at five in the afternoon. Physics teaches well in this format because the work is diagrams, graphs and calculations on a shared whiteboard that both people write on, and the whole board is saved afterwards.

What follows is the plan in detail: which papers your child sits at each tier, what twelve, twenty-four and seventy-two weeks of preparation can each realistically achieve, where the marks actually go in electricity, calculation and the practical paper, what the Ras Al Khaimah school year does to a revision timetable, and what the market charges in AED. Every figure quoted is attributed, and none of it is a price list for this platform. Ras Al Khaimah parents also want to know how a physics tutor handles the practical paper when nobody is in the room, and that is answered below with the mark scheme rather than with reassurance.

ras-al-khaimah/cambridge-igcse-physics-0.programmesIntro: Physics at sixteen is a staging post. These are the three stages either side of 0625, and what a tutor is actually doing at each one.

programmes.name: Lower secondary science, before the 0625 course begins
programmes.description: The groundwork that decides how the first 0625 term goes: units and prefixes, rearranging a two-term formula, drawing a line of best fit, measuring with a ruler and a stopwatch and knowing which digits are meaningful. Students who arrive in Year 10 unable to make kilo, milli and mega behave predictably spend the whole course losing marks they understood the physics behind.
programmes.countryNote: Across Ras Al Khaimah campuses the switch from integrated science to separate physics usually happens at the start of Year 10, and families often notice the change only when the first assessment comes back. Support at this stage is short and cheap compared with repairs later; two months of work on calculation habits in Year 9 is worth more than a term of revision in Year 11.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics
programmes.description: Six topic areas: motion, forces and energy; thermal physics; waves; electricity and magnetism; nuclear physics; and space physics. Core candidates sit a multiple-choice paper and a theory paper, Extended candidates sit the harder versions of both, and every candidate adds either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, which carries a fifth of the grade.
programmes.countryNote: Tier is decided by the centre and printed on the statement of entry, and it is the single most consequential piece of paper in the course because it sets the available grade range. In this emirate both tiers are entered, sometimes within the same class, so a parent should read the entry rather than assume the tier from the textbook on the kitchen table.

programmes.name: A Level Physics and IB Diploma Physics
programmes.description: Cambridge A Level Physics 9702 and IB Diploma Physics both assume 0625 content as given and move immediately into deeper mechanics, fields and quantum ideas, with far heavier mathematical demand. The students who struggle in the first term are rarely the ones who found 0625 hard; they are the ones who passed it by memorising answers rather than methods.
programmes.countryNote: Post-16 physics provision in the northern emirates is thinner than in Dubai, and some families move campus or commute for it. A 0625 candidate planning an engineering or medicine route should check the specific entry requirement published by the university for their intake year, because the grade and the subject combination expected differ between institutions.

ras-al-khaimah/cambridge-igcse-physics-0.subjectsIntro: Tutoring 0625 means teaching six topic areas plus two skill sets that cut across all of them. These are the blocks, and what each one costs a student who has not secured it.

subjects.name: Motion, forces and energy
subjects.description: Speed, acceleration, graphs of motion, Newton's laws, moments, pressure, work, power and energy transfer. The largest topic area on the syllabus and the one most students meet first. Graph interpretation here is examined all the way through the paper, so a student who cannot read a gradient loses marks in topics that have nothing to do with motion.

subjects.name: Thermal physics
subjects.description: Particle model, thermal expansion, specific heat capacity, latent heat, conduction, convection and radiation. The explanation questions here are marked on particle-level language, and a student who writes that heat rises rather than that warmer, less dense fluid rises will lose the mark despite understanding the convection current perfectly.

subjects.name: Waves, light and sound
subjects.description: Wave properties, reflection, refraction including ray diagrams and the refractive index, dispersion, lenses, the electromagnetic spectrum and sound. Ray diagrams are drawn marks: a construction line missing an arrow or a normal drawn by eye rather than at ninety degrees costs marks that the physics itself had already earned.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Charge, current, potential difference, resistance, series and parallel circuits, electrical power and energy, and circuit symbols. More 0625 marks are lost here than anywhere else, usually because a student treats a parallel branch as though it were in series, or calculates correctly in a circuit they have misread.

subjects.name: Magnetism and electromagnetic effects
subjects.description: Magnetic fields, the motor effect, electromagnetic induction, transformers and the d.c. motor. The questions reward a student who can state a rule and then apply it to the orientation actually drawn, which is a different skill from reciting the rule, and one that responds quickly to practice with varied diagrams.

subjects.name: Nuclear physics
subjects.description: Atomic structure, isotopes, alpha, beta and gamma radiation, half-life, nuclear equations and safety. A comparatively small topic with a predictable question set, which makes it reliable territory for a student who needs secure marks quickly. Half-life calculations in particular reward a method on paper rather than mental arithmetic.

subjects.name: Space physics
subjects.description: The solar system, orbits, stellar life cycles, the Big Bang and redshift. Often taught last and therefore revised least, which is why it appears disproportionately in the list of topics students say they have never seen. Teaching it takes a few hours and usually converts straight into marks.

subjects.name: Practical skills for Paper 5 and Paper 6
subjects.description: Reading instruments, tabulating results with units in the heading, plotting, drawing a best-fit line, calculating a gradient, identifying anomalies and suggesting improvements. A fifth of the grade sits here and it is examined on method and precision rather than on knowledge, which is why it is teachable in a way the theory papers are not.

subjects.name: Calculation and command-term discipline
subjects.description: Rearranging formulae, handling prefixes and standard form, significant figures, unit conversion, and answering state, describe, explain, calculate and suggest with the response each command term actually wants. This is the fastest-moving part of any 0625 course, because it adds marks across all six topic areas at once.

sections.heading: Where your child is now: reading a 0625 mock properly
paragraphs: A mock percentage is the least informative number on the report. Two students on 48 per cent can need completely different courses: one has learned four topics well and never met the other two, the other half-knows everything and cannot finish a paper. The script tells you which, and it takes about fifteen minutes to read if you know what to look for. That reading is the first thing a tutor does, and it is why we ask for the marked paper rather than the grade.

Look first at whether marks were lost on questions the student attempted or on questions left blank. Blank questions at the end mean pacing; blank questions scattered through mean missing content. Then look at the calculation questions: if the method line is right and the final number is wrong, the problem is prefixes, rearrangement or significant figures, which is a week of work. If there is no method line at all, the problem is that nobody has taught the student to write one, which is cheaper still to fix.

Next, separate the explain questions from the state questions. 0625 explanation marks are awarded for a specific chain of reasoning, and students who write a true sentence that does not contain the chain get nothing for it. A tutor can show the difference in one session using two versions of the same answer side by side, and most students never lose those marks again afterwards. It is the single highest-return hour in a physics course.

Finally, check the practical questions separately from the theory. The practical component carries a fifth of the grade and is marked on method, tabulation, plotting and precision rather than on knowledge, which means a student can be strong on physics and weak on this paper, or the reverse. Scoring those questions on their own gives you a second, more honest grade, and it is usually the one that explains the gap between what you expected and what the report said.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: which papers your child actually sits
paragraphs: Cambridge examines 0625 through three components, and which versions a candidate sits depends on the tier the centre enters them for. Core candidates take a multiple-choice paper and a theory paper built on the core syllabus; Extended candidates take the harder versions of both, covering the supplementary content as well. Every candidate then adds a practical component, either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical written paper, worth a fifth of the grade.

The decision matters because the tiers do not share a grade range. The Core route is capped below the top grades, and the Extended route does not reach the lowest ones, so entering a struggling student for Extended and a strong one for Core both carry a cost. The tier appears on the statement of entry, and it can usually still be changed before the final entry date for the series, which is why reading that document in the autumn is worth the five minutes it takes.

In practice the tier conversation in this emirate happens too late. Classes are sometimes taught with both tiers in the room, textbooks cover both, and the first time a family sees the word Extended in writing is on the entry confirmation. If you are not sure, ask the head of science two questions: which tier is my child entered for, and what mark in the next assessment would change that answer. Both have short, factual answers.

The table sets out the components for each route, with durations and weightings as published for the current syllabus. Confirm the version for your child's exam year on cambridgeinternational.org or with the school's exams officer, because component details and timings are reviewed between syllabus cycles and the entry is the document that governs.

sections.heading: Twelve weeks, twenty-four weeks, two years: what each can do
paragraphs: The honest answer to how much tutoring will help is a function of time. Physics content takes hours to teach and weeks to consolidate, and no amount of intensity compresses that below a floor. What changes with a short runway is the plan: you stop trying to cover the syllabus and start protecting the marks that are still reachable, which usually means securing three topic areas properly and drilling exam technique rather than touching all six.

A two-year runway allows the opposite approach. Topics are consolidated as they are taught, the practical paper is prepared from the first term rather than discovered in April, and calculation habits are built before they harden into errors. Families who start in Year 10 tend to use one hour a week and finish with fewer sessions overall than families who start panicking in February, which is an argument about cost as much as about grades.

The table below is the version of this conversation we have at the consultation. It is deliberately blunt about what gets dropped, because a plan that pretends everything is coverable in six weeks is how students end up thinly prepared across the whole paper rather than solidly prepared on two thirds of it. Grade predictions are not part of it: no tutor can promise a grade, and anyone who does should be treated with suspicion.

One caveat specific to the northern emirates. School mock timetables, half-terms and the Ramadan adjustment to the school day all land inside these windows, so the usable number of weeks is always lower than the calendar suggests. We build the plan around the school's own calendar, which means asking for it at the start rather than discovering a two-week mock block in the middle of the rebuild.

sections.heading: Electricity and circuits: the topic that decides most grades
paragraphs: If a 0625 cohort's marks are broken down by topic, electricity is almost always the weakest column. The physics is not conceptually harder than waves or thermal, but it is unforgiving in a specific way: a student who misreads a circuit diagram does everything else correctly and still scores zero, because the error happens before the calculation starts. Diagnosing that is simple, and the repair is a drawing habit rather than a knowledge gap.

The habit we teach is redrawing. Before any calculation, the student redraws the circuit as a clean sketch, marks which components share a branch, labels the current direction, and writes the known values onto the diagram. It takes forty seconds and it converts a misreading problem into an arithmetic problem. Students resist it because it feels slow, which is why it has to be practised under timed conditions until it is faster than the alternative.

The second cluster of lost marks is conceptual: potential difference described as something that flows, current described as being used up, resistance treated as a property of the circuit rather than of the component. These misconceptions survive because they produce correct answers to easy questions, then fail on the parallel-circuit question worth five marks. A tutor who knows the standard set can find all of them in one session with four well-chosen questions.

The third is practical. Circuit questions on Paper 5 and Paper 6 ask students to describe how to measure a resistance, what to do about a reading that drifts as a component warms, and how to improve the reliability of the result. Those answers are formulaic in the good sense: there is a right way to say them, and a student who has been shown the structure scores on questions they have never seen before.

sections.heading: Paper 5 and Paper 6: practical physics taught over video
paragraphs: A fifth of the 0625 grade comes from the practical component, and it is the part families worry about most when lessons are online. The worry is misplaced for a specific reason: both versions of the component examine recording, tabulating, plotting, analysing and evaluating rather than manual dexterity. The alternative-to-practical paper is written throughout, and even the practical test awards most of its marks for how results are handled rather than for the handling of the apparatus.

Those skills teach well on a shared whiteboard. A tutor presents a set of raw readings, the student builds the table with units in the column headings, plots the points, draws the best-fit line, calculates the gradient with a large triangle, and identifies the anomaly. The tutor marks it against the published criteria while the student watches, which is the part that actually moves the score, because the criteria are specific and nobody meets them by accident.

What online teaching cannot replace is the student's own time in a school laboratory, and we say so plainly. If your child sits Paper 5, their school's practical programme is the preparation and the tutoring complements it: we work on the write-up, the precision language and the evaluation questions, which is where the marks are lost. Ask the head of science which component the centre enters candidates for, because preparation for the two differs enough to matter.

There is one practical advantage to the online format here. Every graph, table and marked attempt from a session is saved rather than left in an exercise book, so a student revising in May has a folder of their own corrected work with the criteria written beside it. In our experience that folder is the single most used revision resource a 0625 candidate ends up with, and it costs nothing extra to produce.

sections.heading: Units, prefixes and significant figures: the quiet mark drain
paragraphs: Across a 0625 paper, a surprising share of lost marks has nothing to do with physics. It is milliamps entered as amps, centimetres used where metres were needed, a density answer given in the wrong unit, an answer written to six digits because that is what the calculator said, or a formula rearranged incorrectly under pressure. Each error is worth one or two marks, and together they routinely account for a grade boundary.

The repair is drill, and it is the least glamorous part of a physics course. Ten minutes at the start of a session on prefix conversion and rearrangement, every week, until it is automatic. Students find this tedious and parents sometimes question why a tutor is doing arithmetic rather than physics, so it is worth stating the logic: these marks are available in every topic area, they require no new understanding, and they are the cheapest marks on the paper.

Command terms belong in the same category. State, describe, explain, calculate, suggest and determine each have a required response shape, and 0625 mark schemes enforce the distinction. A student who explains when asked to state wastes time; one who states when asked to explain loses marks. Teaching the six command terms explicitly, with two examples each, takes one session and pays across both theory papers.

Significant figures deserve a specific mention because the rule is simple and widely misapplied. Give the answer to the same number of significant figures as the least precise value in the question, show more digits in the working, and never round twice. A student who writes their intermediate values in full and rounds once at the end stops losing the accuracy mark, and that is a habit rather than a skill.

sections.heading: The Ras Al Khaimah school year, and where the weeks actually go
paragraphs: Private schools in Ras Al Khaimah are regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, according to the UAE government's own guidance on private schools. One practical consequence is that term dates, assessment calendars and the school day differ between campuses more than parents expect, so a revision plan has to be built from your own school's calendar rather than a generic one.

The predictable interruptions are worth planning around. Mock examinations usually occupy a block of one to two weeks and consume revision time rather than creating it. Half-term and the winter break arrive at the point in the year when a twenty-four week plan is at its most fragile. Ramadan brings a shortened school day, which changes when a student is actually able to concentrate, and for many families an evening slot after iftar works better than an afternoon one during that period.

Cambridge adds its own fixed points. Entries close months before the papers, every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, and Cambridge states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the exams officer for the zone and then work from that timetable only.

Put together, a twenty-four week plan on paper is usually eighteen or nineteen usable weeks in practice. We build that in from the start, which is why the first consultation asks for the school calendar and the mock dates alongside the mark. It is also why we would rather start a plan in September with one hour a week than in February with three.

sections.heading: What 0625 support costs around Ras Al Khaimah
paragraphs: Published tutoring rates in the UAE are set in Dubai, quoted in AED, and rarely broken down. The figures below come from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, with the source named in each row. They are market rates rather than this platform's prices: IB Gram's own rate is given at the consultation, after the trial lesson, because it depends on the subject, the level and the number of sessions.

Two things distort the comparison in the northern emirates. In-person rates look lower here than in Dubai, but the specialist pool is much thinner, so the real choice is often between a general science tutor nearby and a physics specialist online rather than between two physics specialists. And in-home rates always carry travel: a visiting tutor covering twenty-five kilometres between Al Nakheel and Al Hamra is paid for that time whether the invoice itemises it or not.

Monthly packages advertised in this market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, with Bestimate estimating AED 240 to 600 a month for budget weekly tutoring, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Those are useful anchors for a budget conversation, with the date and source attached.

The variable nobody prices properly is the number of sessions actually needed. A student twenty-four weeks out who starts with a diagnostic and a written plan usually needs fewer total hours than one who starts six weeks out at three hours a week, so the monthly rate is a poor guide to the total. Ask any provider what the plan is, how many sessions it assumes, and what happens when the plan changes.
