sections.heading: Getting started from Ras Al Khaimah, and what we will tell you straight
paragraphs: The useful opening move is not a phone call but three documents: the latest report, the most recent marked paper or internal assessment feedback sheet, and the written option blocks the school issued. Those tell a subject specialist what the problem is. A conversation tells them what the problem feels like, which is a different and less reliable thing. Send them and name the subject and level you are worried about.

The trial lesson is taught by the person who would teach the course and it is a lesson, not a sales call. It is free, no card is required, and afterwards you get a written note: what the tutor thinks is actually wrong, what a defined block would target, roughly how many sessions, and whether a tutor is the right purchase at all. Sometimes it is not. A Year 13 student three weeks from exam leave with four subjects in trouble needs triage and sleep more than a new weekly commitment, and we would rather say so.

Availability in the northern emirates is not unlimited and we state limits rather than hide them. A Higher Level science at short notice in a busy term is the request that most often cannot be filled immediately. Where that happens you get a date, an honest alternative, or a recommendation to look elsewhere. No competitor in the researched set discloses a coverage limit, and concealing one costs a family a term they cannot recover.

Everything then runs on Gulf Standard Time with a fixed weekly slot, a named tutor and a written note after each session. If the slot stops working because the school day changed or an activity commitment moved, it gets changed rather than missed. If the criterion levels or paper marks are not moving after a defined block, the review says so as a fact, and changing tutor or stopping are both normal outcomes rather than failures.

A Standard Level entry where a university route expects Higher Level is a different job from a Higher Level student losing marks on paper technique, and the two need different tutors. Naming it precisely saves a wasted first session.

whyPoints.title: Anchored to this emirate, not to Dubai
whyPoints.description: The regulator here is the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge, the Diploma cohorts are small, and the option blocks are tight. Every section of this page is written from those facts rather than from generic UAE copy, because a plan built on a Dubai timeline misses the weeks this emirate actually has.

whyPoints.title: Matched on subject and level
whyPoints.description: Removing travel from the match is what makes a Higher Level chemistry or physics specialist reachable from the northern emirates. A request is matched against everyone qualified to teach that subject at that level rather than against the handful who could drive to Al Hamra by six o'clock.

whyPoints.title: Internal assessment handled properly
whyPoints.description: A large share of each Diploma grade is settled before the examination room. Sessions on an exploration, investigation, commentary or essay coach method and respond to the student's own drafts, and the tutor keeps a written record of what was done so the school can be told exactly what happened.

IB session and results dates are not stated, because they must be confirmed with your school's coordinator or the IB directly, and restating an unverified date across many pages is how errors scale.

faqs.question: Why does a small Diploma cohort in Ras Al Khaimah limit my child's subject choices?
faqs.answer: Because each subject runs once. A Diploma student takes one subject from each of six groups, three at Higher Level, and on a large campus a popular subject appears in two or three timetable blocks so most combinations fit. A cohort in the tens supports one teaching set per subject, so any two subjects sharing a block become mutually exclusive. Ask the school for the written option blocks and for which degree routes the resulting combination closes. Then decide whether to argue for a small set against a study period or to cover the gap deliberately across the year.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates my child's school in Ras Al Khaimah, and what can it actually decide?
faqs.answer: The Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge. The federal portal states that it regulates private education in the emirate, and that the Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That covers fee changes, programme additions and changes to how a year group is assessed, so there is an accountable route beyond the school office. Dubai schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain schools to the Department of Education and Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah schools to the federal Ministry of Education.

faqs.question: My child was put in Standard Level physics but needs Higher Level for engineering. What now?
faqs.answer: Name the gap in content terms and decide early. Ask the school in writing whether a Higher Level set can run against a study period, because small schools sometimes can. Ask each target university what it actually requires, since some accept a Standard Level subject with a strong overall profile. If the Standard Level place stands and the route still matters, the additional Higher Level content has to be covered deliberately across a year rather than crammed in a term. That is one of the commonest pieces of work we take on from this emirate, and it needs a specialist in the subject.

faqs.question: How much of a Diploma grade is decided before the examinations?
faqs.answer: A meaningful share in every subject, and the exact proportion is published in your school's course outline. The mathematics exploration, the sciences investigation, economics commentaries, the English individual oral and the computer science solution with documentation are all marked in school and moderated by the IB. For a student in a small cohort this is the part of the grade least affected by class size and most affected by whether the criteria were explained. It is also where coaching has the highest return, because the usual failures are structural and visible in a first draft.

faqs.question: Can a tutor work on my child's Extended Essay without crossing the IB's honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Within a boundary that has to be kept precisely. A tutor may teach subject content, explain how the criteria are applied, interrogate a research question until it is answerable in four thousand words, point out a missing method section, ask what the evidence supports, and respond in writing to a draft the student has written. A tutor may not supply text or content, rewrite passages to a standard the student could not reach, or produce any part of the essay. Keep dated drafts in the student's own files and tell the supervisor outside support is being used. Declaring it early removes the problem.

faqs.question: Do you publish the IB examination and results dates for the May session?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is specific. The IB's site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and restating an unverified date across many pages is how a single error becomes hundreds. Confirm every IB date with your school's coordinator or on the IB's own pages. Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page are different: they come from the boards' own published key-dates documents and are attributed, which is why the Pearson International GCSE November 2026 window appears here and an IB window does not. The Cambridge series we name are June and November, the two a UAE centre offers, rather than the February and March sitting Cambridge runs for India.

faqs.question: When should the internal assessment work actually be finished?
faqs.answer: Against the school's internal deadlines, which sit months before anything is uploaded, and ideally earlier than those. In a small Ras Al Khaimah cohort one supervisor may be carrying a dozen Extended Essays alongside marking a subject's internal assessment, so an early draft gets real attention and a late one gets less. The autumn term of Year 13 is where this work should land. Treating a school deadline as negotiable spends the only period in the two years with genuine slack, and spring term has none to lend.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan change how a Diploma student should plan revision?
faqs.answer: Materially, and planning for it beats improvising. The school day compresses and the usable evening moves, so families who shift sessions to a post-iftar slot in advance keep their weekly rhythm and families who do not lose a month of it. Shorter and more frequent works better than long sessions in these weeks. Mark the Ramadan period on the school calendar alongside the mock window, exam leave and public holidays before building a plan, because what remains after those four is the capacity the plan can actually use.

faqs.question: What does a Ras Al Khaimah family pay for Diploma tutoring?
faqs.answer: Market rates rather than ours: specialist IB and IGCSE tutoring is advertised at roughly AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 rate table giving 200 to 450 and above. A qualified subject tutor online sits around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Premium named tutors go higher, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Scarcity moves the figure here more than anywhere: a Higher Level science request in the northern emirates draws on a thin pool. We quote after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Does my child need a Ministry of Education equivalency certificate for a UAE university?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is the family's process to complete rather than a school's or a tutor's. Start before results, because attestation takes time and university windows do not wait. The British-curriculum rules were clarified in July 2026 reporting: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. No IB points figure is published here because we have not read one on the ministry's own site. Ask the ministry directly.

faqs.question: Can my child study for the Diploma at a university inside Ras Al Khaimah afterwards?
faqs.answer: Degree options exist within the emirate, which changes the planning for some families. The American University of Ras Al Khaimah, RAK Medical and Health Sciences University and University of Stirling RAK operate here, and each publishes its own admission requirements. The detail worth checking early is mathematics: engineering and health-science routes frequently expect Analysis and Approaches rather than Applications and Interpretation, and that decision is made at the start of Year 12. We name these institutions as context for route planning, with no relationship of any kind implied.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our villa in Al Hamra or Al Marjan Island?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Diploma lessons for Ras Al Khaimah families run one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen and a document both sides can write on. The reason is availability rather than cost. The number of people qualified to teach Higher Level chemistry or physics who are also willing to drive to the southern coast by six o'clock on a weekday is very small, and matching on subject instead of distance is what makes a specialist reachable here.

faqs.question: Our teacher left mid-year and the set has a cover teacher. Is that a tutoring problem?
faqs.answer: It is a continuity problem, and tutoring addresses part of it. Ask the school two questions in writing: who now marks and moderates the internal assessment for that subject, and what the plan is until the set is staffed. Those answers determine the real risk, which is usually the internally assessed component rather than the taught content. Where the gap is genuine, a subject specialist focused on the internal assessment and on the components the cover teacher is least able to mark is the highest-value hour available. A whole parallel course is rarely necessary.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for support in more than one Diploma subject at once?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the arithmetic usually settles it. A Diploma student in this emirate commutes, carries three Higher Levels plus the core, and has a finite number of usable evenings. Two weekly tutored subjects plus homework plus internal assessment work tends to produce worse results than one, because the hours between sessions are where learning happens and they get squeezed first. Pick the subject where a grade is both most at risk and most load-bearing for the university route, support that one properly, and revisit after a defined block.

faqs.question: What happens if you cannot find a tutor for the subject we need?
faqs.answer: You get told, with a date. Higher Level sciences at short notice in a busy term are the requests that most often cannot be filled immediately in the northern emirates. In that case we will either name when a matched specialist becomes available, offer a tutor for an adjacent component where that is honestly useful, or say the request cannot be served well and suggest you look locally. No competitor in the researched set publishes a coverage limit at all, and hiding one costs a family a term that cannot be recovered.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-diploma-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the option blocks and the last marked piece of work
ras-al-khaimah/ib-diploma-tutor.closingBody: A Diploma problem in Ras Al Khaimah is usually a timetable problem wearing a subject's clothes. Before buying any hours, get the written option blocks, find out who marks and moderates the internal assessment in the subject that worries you, and read the last marked paper rather than the report comment. If after that a specific subject at a specific level still needs a specialist, send those documents and take the free trial lesson with the tutor who would teach the course. You will get a written opinion on the cause, a defined block with an end date, and an honest answer if another weekly hour is not what will move the grade.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-biology-hl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma Biology at Higher Level: the four themes at every level of organisation, the statistics the course assumes, command-term discipline, and the scientific investigation. The first lesson is free and runs on a past paper question your child has already lost marks on.

intro.heading: A biology grade is decided by precision long before it is decided by knowledge
paragraphs: Higher Level Biology is 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, and the course content is enormous. That is the first fact a parent needs, because it explains the most common pattern in the subject: a student who can talk fluently about immunity, respiration or inheritance, and whose written answers keep scoring two marks out of four. Biology rewards saying the right thing in the right quantity using the right vocabulary, and a student who has never been shown a mark scheme does not know that the examiner is counting specific points rather than judging an impression.

The second fact is that the guide is structured as a grid rather than a list. Four themes, unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, and continuity and change, are each taught at four levels of biological organisation: molecules, cells, organisms and ecosystems. Sixteen intersections, with the experimental and mathematical tools threaded through all of them. That structure is deliberate and useful, because it means the same idea recurs at different scales, but it also means a student revising by chapter order will revise the same concept four times without ever noticing it is the same concept.

The third is that Higher Level adds depth rather than new themes. Both levels meet all four themes; Higher Level goes further in almost every one, with additional content on metabolism, signalling, immunity, gene expression and population ecology, and with more demanding data interpretation. Because it is depth rather than breadth, the Higher Level additions tend to be taught as extensions inside existing lessons, which is efficient and makes it hard for a parent to tell whether they have actually been covered.

Ras Al Khaimah adds its own constraint. The emirate runs a compact set of private schools under its own Department of Knowledge, and the Diploma groups inside them are small. Higher Level and Standard Level Biology are often taught in the same room for part of the week, which is a reasonable response to small numbers and does mean the Higher Level extensions compete for attention. A parent looking for additional Higher Level teaching inside the emirate is looking for a teacher who is already fully committed.

One-to-one teaching over live video removes the geography from that problem. The tutor is selected because they teach Higher Level Biology, know what each command term is worth, and have supervised investigations against the four published criteria. Sessions run at a fixed time on Gulf Standard Time with no journey from Al Hamra Village or Al Nakheel at either end, and past paper answers are marked and returned with the mark scheme alongside, which is the single most useful thing a biology student can see.

The rest of this page covers the grid in full, the command terms that decide marks, where Higher Level marks actually go missing, what makes a biology investigation work when the material is alive and variable, the last hundred days before a May session, what the UAE market charges with sources you can check yourself, the academic-honesty line on coursework, and the mandatory UAE subjects that run alongside a Diploma timetable here.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-biology-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: Higher Level Biology sits at the end of a longer IB sequence, and where a student joined that sequence changes what the support has to do. These are the programmes Ras Al Khaimah families ask about.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Middle Years sciences are integrated rather than split into separate subjects and are assessed against four criteria, including inquiring and designing. A student who scored well on criterion A but poorly on criterion B in MYP 5 sciences has the knowledge habit and not the method habit, and the Diploma investigation will expose that difference in DP2 rather than in DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Because Middle Years science is integrated, a Ras Al Khaimah student moving into Higher Level Biology has usually had less dedicated biology time than a British Year 11 triple-award student. The gap shows up in cell biology vocabulary and in confidence with genetics notation, both of which a short bridging block resolves early in DP1.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Biology at Higher Level is examined by two written papers and the scientific investigation. Paper 1 combines multiple-choice with data-based questions and carries 36%, Paper 2 is extended response and carries 44%, and the investigation carries 20%. The course is taught across two years with the investigation submitted in the second, and there is no separate options paper in the current guide.
programmes.countryNote: In a small northern-emirate cohort the Higher Level additions are often delivered as extensions within shared lessons rather than as separate teaching. That is a sensible use of a small timetable and it is the main reason parents here find it hard to establish whether the Higher Level content has actually been covered in full.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs Diploma courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. Where Biology appears in a CP timetable the student sits exactly the same papers and the same investigation as a full Diploma candidate, so the teaching requirement is identical even though the overall qualification differs.
programmes.countryNote: Few campuses in the northern emirates offer CP, so a Ras Al Khaimah student taking Biology within it may be the only one in their year doing so. That is the clearest case for subject-specific teaching from outside the emirate, because there is no peer group to learn alongside.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-biology-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Biology at Higher Level is usually one of several demanding subjects in the same two years. These are the Diploma courses Ras Al Khaimah families raise alongside it most often.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Four themes taught across four levels of biological organisation, from molecules to ecosystems, with experimental and mathematical tools threaded through all of them. Higher Level extends the depth in metabolism, signalling, immunity, gene expression and population ecology rather than adding separate topics.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and Reactivity across six themes, with a data booklet supplied in the exams. Students taking both sciences meet the same investigation criteria twice, and the two pieces of coursework need deliberately different timelines or they collide in the same term.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches to behaviour, with research methods and statistics throughout. Biology students usually handle the research methodology well and lose marks on the critical evaluation of studies, which is a writing skill rather than a knowledge one.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: A transdisciplinary course covering ecosystems, biodiversity, pollution, water, soil and climate. It overlaps substantially with the ecosystems level of the Biology guide, which helps a student taking both as long as the differing assessment demands are kept separate.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with technology permitted throughout. Its regression, standard deviation and significance-testing content maps directly onto the data analysis criterion in a Biology investigation, and these students usually find that criterion the easiest of the four.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebra-and-calculus route, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator. Biology does not depend on it, but students aiming at medicine often carry it because specific university programmes ask for a mathematics course at a stated level.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Themes A to E with a combined multiple-choice and data-analysis Paper 1. The uncertainty and graph work is close in character to the data handling in Biology Paper 1B, so a student doing both should learn that technique once rather than twice.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, with a portfolio of three written commentaries. For a science student the demand is the structure of an evaluative argument rather than the quantitative content.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two written papers and an individual oral, with an additional essay at Higher Level. Biology students often write accurately and too briefly, and the marks recovered here come from developing a point rather than from reading more carefully.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects and a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title. The natural sciences are a standing area of knowledge, and a Higher Level Biology student has usable material on evidence, classification and how a model gets revised.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay. A Biology Extended Essay is popular and difficult, because living material is variable and the data has to be defensible, and the supervision line must be clear before the research starts.

sections.heading: Why a student who understands the biology keeps scoring fours
paragraphs: Mark schemes in Biology award credit for specific points, and a four-mark question generally wants four distinct, correctly expressed ideas. A student who writes a well-organised paragraph containing two of them scores two, and comes away believing the answer was good. Nothing in that experience teaches them what went wrong, which is why the pattern persists for terms at a time. The repair begins the first time a student sees their own answer next to the scheme that marked it.

Precision of vocabulary is the second half of the same problem. Biology distinguishes carefully between terms that students use interchangeably: diffusion and facilitated diffusion, allele and gene, species and population, immunity and resistance. Mark schemes frequently require the precise term and will not credit the approximate one. This is not pedantry on the examiner's part; the distinction usually carries the biology. But it does mean a student can be marked down repeatedly for a vocabulary habit rather than for a misunderstanding.

Volume is the third. With four themes taught across four levels of organisation, plus the Higher Level extensions, there is more content here than in most Diploma subjects, and a student who revises by reading cannot retain it. What works is retrieval: answering questions from memory, checking, and returning to the same material at intervals. That is a habit rather than an insight, and it is the single highest-value change a Higher Level Biology student can make in the last six months.
bullets: Four-mark questions want four distinct credited points, not a good paragraph
Approximate vocabulary is marked as wrong, not as nearly right

sections.heading: The grid: four themes across four levels of organisation
paragraphs: The current Biology guide is organised as four themes, each addressed at four levels of biological organisation. The themes are unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, and continuity and change. The levels are molecules, cells, organisms and ecosystems. Every intersection carries content, and the point of the structure is that a concept such as adaptation or signalling is examined at more than one scale.

This has a direct consequence for how a student should revise, and almost nobody acts on it. Revising by chapter means meeting natural selection at ecosystem level in one week and DNA mutation at molecular level in another, without connecting them, even though Paper 2 questions routinely cross levels within a single theme. Revising along a theme, molecules to ecosystems, builds exactly the connections the examiners are testing, and it takes no more time than the alternative.

The table below sets out the grid with representative content at each intersection, so a parent can see the shape of the course on one page and ask about a specific cell of it. It is also the right basis for a first diagnostic: testing all sixteen intersections lightly finds the gaps far faster than working through the guide in order, and in a cohort where Higher Level content is taught as extension work inside shared lessons, the gaps are rarely where anyone expects. One cell of the grid deserves a mention on its own. The molecules row of theme D, covering DNA replication, protein synthesis, mutation and gene editing, is the content students most often report as understood and most often answer imprecisely, because the vocabulary is dense and every term has a near neighbour that means something else.

sections.heading: Command terms, and the marks they decide
paragraphs: Every Diploma Biology question opens with an instruction, and the instruction is not decoration. 'State' wants a single short answer with no reasoning. 'Outline' wants a brief account. 'Explain' wants reasons or causes. 'Compare and contrast' wants both similarities and differences, and an answer giving only similarities loses half the available marks however good it is. 'Suggest' wants a plausible answer the student has reasoned out rather than recalled, which students find uncomfortable because it feels like guessing.

The mark tariff usually follows the command term, so the term also tells a student how much to write. A two-mark 'outline' question that receives a page of writing has cost the student time they needed elsewhere, and a four-mark 'explain' question that receives two sentences has left two marks on the table. Learning to read the tariff and the term together is worth more in the final term than another pass through the content, and it takes about three sessions to become automatic.

The table lists the terms that cause most of the loss, what the examiner is looking for, and what students typically write instead. It works best used actively: take a marked paper, write the command term beside each question where marks were lost, and see which term appears most often. In most scripts one or two terms account for the majority of the loss, and that is a short, specific thing to fix. The habit is worth building in DP1 rather than in the final term, because by then it costs nothing: a student who reads the term and the tariff before writing is simply answering the question that was set. Students who never build it spend two years answering a slightly different question from the one on the paper, and no amount of additional content teaching repairs that.

sections.heading: Where Higher Level Biology marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Genetics notation is the first reliable source of loss. Students who understand inheritance perfectly well write pedigrees and crosses inconsistently, mix up allele symbols, omit the gametes line, or fail to state the phenotype ratio in the form the question asked for. Each of those is a presentation convention rather than a concept, and each is independently marked. Twenty minutes with a correctly set-out cross, repeated across a few session, closes it permanently.

Data interpretation is the second, and it carries disproportionate weight because it appears in Paper 1B and again inside Paper 2. A Biology data question usually asks what the data shows before it asks what it means, and students conflate the two: they explain the biology without first describing the trend, and the description marks go unclaimed. Error bars and significance are the other half of it. A student who says two means are different when the error bars overlap has made a statement the data does not support, which is penalised.

The third is the extended-response question at the end of Paper 2, often worth a substantial block of marks. These reward structure: a plan, sequenced points, correct terminology, and where appropriate an annotated diagram. Students who write continuously without structure cover the content and still lose marks, because the examiner cannot find discrete credited points in the prose. Teaching a student to plan a long answer in ninety seconds before writing is one of the few interventions that reliably moves a Higher Level Biology grade in the final term.

sections.heading: A biology investigation when the material is alive and variable
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is worth 20% of the grade, marked out of 24 across four equally weighted criteria, and capped at 3,000 words. In Biology it carries a problem the other sciences have less of: living material varies, responds slowly, and sometimes dies. A design that would be fine in physics, two variables and five readings, produces data in biology that cannot support a conclusion, because the variation between individuals swamps the effect being measured.

The fix is decided before anything is ordered. Replication and sample size have to be set so that the analysis planned is actually possible, and the statistical test has to be chosen in advance rather than selected afterwards to suit whatever came out. Students who pick their test after seeing the data almost always pick the wrong one, and the data analysis criterion notices. Time is the other constraint: germination, growth and behavioural work need weeks, and a school laboratory booking schedule has to accommodate that.

Honesty about this matters more in Biology than elsewhere. A result that shows no effect is a perfectly good investigation and can score full marks, provided the design was sound and the evaluation is specific about why. What scores badly is a student quietly adjusting data to produce the expected pattern, which is academic malpractice as well as bad science. The table sets out common investigation types with what each one risks. Reading it before a topic is chosen is worth more than reading it afterwards, because the risks listed are not faults in the student's execution. They are properties of the material, and the only point at which they can be managed is the design stage, while the method is still on paper and nothing has been booked.

sections.heading: The last hundred days before a May session
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May session, so a DP2 Biology student has a long final stretch with everything already taught and nothing left but consolidation. The exact session and results dates belong to the IB and should be confirmed with your child's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org rather than taken from a tutoring page. What is reliable is the shape: the last hundred days are for retrieval, timed writing and command-term discipline, and adding new content to them tends to lower the grade rather than raise it.

The plan below is built on a fortnightly rhythm because that suits a content-heavy subject. Each fortnight covers one theme across all four levels of organisation, which is how the guide intends the content to connect, and each fortnight produces written answers that are marked. The targets are deliberately countable: a parent should be able to see how many marked answers came back and what the command-term error log looks like, rather than relying on a report that everything is going well.

The final fortnight is the one families most often get wrong. The instinct is to intensify, and the right move is to reduce: shorter sessions, more frequent, on the specific topics the error log still names, with full papers already behind the student. A student arriving at a Biology exam tired has a worse problem than a student arriving with one theme slightly thin. The other common error in that stretch is doing full papers too late. A full Paper 2 taken four days before the exam produces a score and no time to act on it, which makes it a test rather than a lesson. Full papers belong in the forty-to-twenty-day window, where there is still room to turn what they reveal into practice.

sections.heading: What Higher Level Biology support costs, and how to check the figures yourself
paragraphs: Everything in this section can be verified by a parent in about fifteen minutes, which is the point of writing it this way. The published UAE market bands, read in October 2026, are these. Budget online tutoring runs roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online runs about AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An IB or IGCSE specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase listing AED 270. An in-home visit including travel is quoted at AED 180 to 500. The market's premium tier reaches AED 650 an hour, published by BartyED.

Converted to monthly figures, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 with a budget tutor, AED 600 to 1,200 at mid range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packaged plans seen in the UAE market run about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are market rates from the named sources, not IB Gram prices.

What a parent should do with this is check it. Open the pricing page of any three tutoring providers advertising in the UAE and look for four things: whether a rate is published at all, whether it is in dirhams, whether the figure in the page body matches the figure in any structured data, and whether the page says what the rate includes. The research behind this page found three of six ranking competitors publishing no price whatsoever, two quoting in US dollars, and one whose schema price contradicted its visible text. A provider that will not tell you the number before the call is telling you something.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in Biology coursework, stated plainly
paragraphs: The scientific investigation and any Biology Extended Essay are assessed as the student's own work, and IB academic honesty rules make that an obligation with consequences that fall on the student. A tutor may teach the biology, explain what each of the four criteria rewards, help narrow a research question, teach the statistics before the data exists, respond to a draft the student has written, and say directly that a conclusion is not supported by the data. A tutor supplies no text, no data, no processed results and no diagrams that appear in the submitted work.

Biology has one specific temptation the other sciences have less of, and it should be named. When living material produces a messy result, adjusting the numbers to show the expected trend is easy and feels harmless. It is academic malpractice and it is also the thing most likely to be noticed, because the adjusted data tends to be implausibly clean. A result showing no significant effect can score full marks if the design was sound and the evaluation is specific about why the effect was not detected. That is worth telling a student before they collect anything.

The wider market context is worth knowing. Research into the UAE tutoring search results found at least one operator selling completed Internal Assessments outright. That is an integrity breach that triggers IB malpractice procedures against the student who submits it, and the student carries the penalty, not the seller. If any provider offers to produce coursework, that is a reason to end the conversation rather than to negotiate the scope.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects running alongside a Diploma timetable
paragraphs: A Diploma student in the UAE is not only doing the Diploma. Private schools here are required to teach Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed international curriculum, and that federal requirement sits behind each emirate's own rules. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. For families in Ras Al Khaimah, the emirate's Department of Knowledge regulates private education and, according to u.ae, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

The most detailed published guidance on how these subjects are organised comes from KHDA, which regulates Dubai's private schools, and its mandatory-subjects requirements are a useful reference for understanding the structure even where a different authority applies. KHDA states that for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. It also sets instructional time on the basis of a 40-minute lesson unit and advises that any mandatory subject lesson should be at least 25 minutes.

Why this belongs on a Biology page is simple arithmetic. These subjects occupy timetable hours that a Higher Level science student would otherwise have, and they carry their own assessments and their own deadlines. A Diploma student carrying Higher Level Biology, Higher Level Chemistry, a mathematics course, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the mandatory UAE subjects has a genuinely full week, and any tutoring plan that ignores that will be the first thing to be dropped. Where a family also needs Arabic support, note that KHDA requires teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic in Dubai schools to hold its own approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential question worth asking about separately.

process.title: Send a marked paper, not a report comment
process.description: The most useful opening document is a marked Biology script. It shows which command terms are costing marks and whether the loss is in description, explanation or extended response, which a school report summary cannot show however carefully it is written.

process.title: Free first lesson on a question already lost
process.description: The first session costs nothing and is spent on a question your child has already attempted and dropped marks on, with the mark scheme open. That is a faster diagnostic than any assessment, and you hear exactly how the teaching works before anything is agreed.

process.title: A plan organised by theme, not by chapter
process.description: The written plan that follows works along themes across all four levels of organisation, because that is how the guide connects and how Paper 2 questions are built. It names the number of marked answers per fortnight rather than a vague coverage promise.

process.title: Fixed weekly slots on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Sessions sit at the same time each week, set around pickup reality in your community, with the same tutor. Ramadan timings shift to a post-Iftar slot for the whole month, and the slot survives the change rather than being rebuilt.

process.title: Monthly review against the error log
process.description: Progress is measured by what has come off the error log, counted by command term as well as by topic. If the same term keeps appearing, the plan changes. If the log is shrinking, the hours can usually come down rather than up.

whyPoints.title: Answers marked against the real scheme
whyPoints.description: A student who has never seen their own answer beside the mark scheme that marked it does not know why a good paragraph scored two out of four. Every weekly session includes one answer marked that way, which is what changes the habit rather than the knowledge.

whyPoints.title: Command terms treated as instructions
whyPoints.description: State, outline, explain, compare and contrast, distinguish, suggest and evaluate each demand a different answer and a different length. They are taught with their mark tariffs attached and logged when missed, because in most scripts one or two terms account for most of the loss.

whyPoints.title: Revision along the grid
whyPoints.description: The guide crosses four themes with four levels of organisation, and Paper 2 questions move between levels inside a theme. Sessions follow that structure rather than chapter order, which builds the connections the examiners are actually testing.

whyPoints.title: Investigations designed for living material
whyPoints.description: Replication, sample size, run time and the statistical test are settled before anything is ordered, because biological variation defeats designs that would be adequate in physics. A null result with a sound design can score full marks; a thin design cannot be written around.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on coursework
whyPoints.description: Support is teaching, design advice and feedback on the student's own draft. No text, data, processed results or diagrams are supplied for submission, and adjusting data to fit an expected trend is named as malpractice before any collection begins.

whyPoints.title: Figures you can check without us
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here names the page that published it and the month it was read, so a parent can verify the lot in a quarter of an hour. No results statistic, satisfaction score or tutor headcount appears anywhere on the page.

faqs.question: Why does my daughter understand biology but keep getting half marks on written answers?
faqs.answer: Because Biology mark schemes award credit for specific points, and a four-mark question usually wants four distinct, precisely expressed ideas. A fluent paragraph containing two of them scores two, and the student comes away thinking the answer was good. Vocabulary compounds it: schemes often require the exact term, so allele used where gene was needed is marked wrong rather than nearly right. The repair starts the first time she sees her own answer beside the scheme that marked it, which is why one marked answer per session is more useful than another hour of content.

faqs.question: How is the current Diploma Biology course actually organised?
faqs.answer: As a grid rather than a list. Four themes, unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, and continuity and change, are each taught at four levels of biological organisation: molecules, cells, organisms and ecosystems. The experimental and mathematical tools run through all sixteen intersections rather than sitting in a separate unit. The practical consequence is that Paper 2 questions move between levels inside a single theme, so revising along a theme from molecules to ecosystems builds the connections being examined, while revising chapter by chapter hides them.

faqs.question: Which command terms cost Higher Level Biology students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Compare and contrast, explain and suggest, in roughly that order. Compare and contrast requires both similarities and differences on the same named features, and an answer giving only similarities loses half the marks regardless of quality. Explain requires a causal chain, and students frequently describe what happens without stating why. Suggest asks for a reasoned plausible answer rather than a recalled fact, which students avoid because it feels like guessing. Writing the command term next to every question where marks were lost on a marked paper usually reveals one or two repeat offenders.

faqs.question: What does Higher Level add to Biology compared with Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Depth rather than different themes. Both levels cover all four themes at all four levels of organisation; Higher Level runs to 240 teaching hours against 150 and extends the treatment of metabolism, signalling, immunity, gene expression and population ecology, with more demanding data interpretation throughout. Because the additions are extensions of familiar material rather than separate topics, they are often taught inside shared lessons, which makes it genuinely hard for a parent to tell whether they have been covered in full. A specific question about a named extension is the way to find out.

faqs.question: My son loses marks on graphs and data questions. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always one of two things. A Biology data question normally asks what the data shows before asking what it means, and students jump to the biology without first describing the trend, leaving the description marks unclaimed. The other is error bars: a student who states that two means differ when the bars overlap has made a claim the data does not support, and that is penalised rather than ignored. Both are fixable in a handful of sessions using past Paper 1B questions, annotated live, with the mark scheme visible alongside the answer.

faqs.question: How should a Biology investigation be designed when the material is alive?
faqs.answer: With replication and run time settled before anything is ordered. Biological variation between individuals routinely exceeds the effect being measured, so a design with five readings that would suit physics produces data that cannot support a conclusion here. Sample size has to match the statistical test, and the test has to be chosen in advance rather than selected afterwards to suit the data. Germination, growth and behavioural work need weeks, which means the school laboratory booking has to be arranged early. These are planning decisions, and they decide the data analysis mark.

faqs.question: What happens if the investigation shows no effect at all?
faqs.answer: It can still score full marks. The four criteria assess research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, not whether the hypothesis was supported. A sound design that detects no significant effect, analysed correctly and evaluated with specific reasons why the effect may not have been detected, is a good piece of work. What scores badly, and is academic malpractice as well, is adjusting the numbers to show the expected trend. Adjusted data usually looks implausibly clean, and a student should be told that before they collect anything rather than afterwards.

faqs.question: How do we fix genetics questions where the biology is understood but the marks are not there?
faqs.answer: By treating the layout as examinable content, because it is. Marks are awarded for consistent allele symbols, for showing the gametes line, for setting out the cross to convention, and for stating the ratio in the form the question requested. Pedigree questions add their own notation. None of that is conceptual, and all of it is independently marked, which is why a student who understands inheritance can still lose several marks per paper. Ten correctly set-out crosses across a few sessions generally closes it for good.

faqs.question: Is there a Higher Level Biology teacher available inside Ras Al Khaimah for private work?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the reason is cohort size rather than quality. The emirate has a compact private-school set under its own Department of Knowledge, and Diploma Biology groups here are small enough that Higher Level and Standard Level often share a room. The teachers who do teach Higher Level are fully timetabled. Matching a specialist over live video on Gulf Standard Time makes subject depth the selection criterion instead of who happens to live nearby, which for a course this large is the difference that shows up in the marks.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level Biology work for medicine and dentistry applications?
faqs.answer: It is usually required rather than optional, frequently with a specified minimum grade, but the requirement belongs to each institution and each programme. Locally that includes RAK Medical and Health Sciences University, and regionally Gulf Medical University, the University of Sharjah and others. Many routes also require Higher Level Chemistry alongside it. The only reliable source is each university's published entry requirement for the specific programme in the current admissions cycle, because requirements differ between courses inside one institution and are revised between cycles.

faqs.question: What do the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons mean for a Diploma science timetable?
faqs.answer: They occupy real hours. Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed international curriculum, and those subjects carry their own assessments. KHDA's published guidance for Dubai schools, which is the most detailed available, requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibits combining them. In Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge regulates private education and approves curricula. Any tutoring plan has to fit what is left of the week after all of that.

faqs.question: How much does Higher Level Biology tutoring cost in the UAE, and where can I check?
faqs.answer: Published October 2026 market figures: budget online tutoring runs about AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and the premium tier reaches AED 650 published by BartyED. Check any provider's own pricing page for three things: whether a rate exists, whether it is in dirhams, and what it includes.

faqs.question: What should the final hundred days before the exams actually contain?
faqs.answer: Retrieval, timed writing and command-term work, with no new content. A fortnightly rhythm suits a subject this large: one theme across all four levels of organisation per fortnight, six marked written answers, and a shrinking error log kept by command term as well as by topic. Full papers belong in the middle of that stretch, not at the end. The last fortnight should reduce rather than intensify, covering only what the error log still names, because a student arriving at a Biology exam exhausted has a worse problem than one with a slightly thin theme.

faqs.question: Can sessions fit around Ramadan and continue through the summer break?
faqs.answer: Yes. During Ramadan most families here move the weekly slot to after Iftar for the whole month rather than renegotiating weekly, which keeps a routine in place while everything else is shifting. Over the summer, families usually either pause with a diagnostic in late August or keep a lighter fortnightly pattern. For a student entering DP2, the summer is the only block of weeks in the course without a competing deadline, which makes it the cheapest available window for closing a theme gap or planning investigation logistics.

faqs.question: Is a private tutor working with a UAE family required to hold a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a fair thing to ask about. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published. MoHRE's private tutor licensing service is the official route, through its app, website or e-services system.

intro.heading: The one fact about this course that should shape your plan from the start
paragraphs: Business Management is the only Diploma subject in a typical Ras Al Khaimah timetable where part of the examination is published in advance. Paper 1 is built on a case study released ahead of the exam session, which means a student can read it, research the industry it sits in, map the course theory onto the organisation described, and practise questions on it, all before the exam. Students who do that walk into Paper 1 with an advantage that cannot be obtained in any other subject. Students who treat Paper 1 as something to revise generally are throwing that advantage away.

The second thing to know is that this is not a soft option. Higher Level runs to 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level. The course has five units: an introduction to business management, human resource management, finance and accounts, marketing, and operations management. Four concepts, creativity, change, ethics and sustainability, run through all five, and examination questions are written against them. There is real arithmetic in it: break-even and contribution, cash flow forecasts, final accounts, profitability and liquidity ratios, and at Higher Level investment appraisal, critical path analysis and simple linear regression.

The third is where marks actually go. Business Management rewards applying theory to a specific organisation and reaching a judgement about it. It does not reward describing theory accurately, which is what a diligent student naturally produces. A student who can define economies of scale perfectly and cannot say what they mean for the particular firm in the stimulus will score in the middle band of every question. That gap between knowledge and application is the single most common pattern in the subject and it is diagnosable from one marked paper.

Families in Ras Al Khaimah usually come for one of three reasons. A DP1 student who finds the finance unit genuinely difficult, because it is arithmetic dressed as a business subject. A DP2 student whose research project has no access to an organisation and no usable data four weeks before the internal deadline. Or a student whose marks sit stubbornly at a 4 or a 5 because every answer explains rather than judges.

The local constraint is supply, as it is in every Diploma subject here. The emirate has a compact private-school set regulated by its own Department of Knowledge, and Business Management groups are small. The teacher carrying it often carries Economics as well. That is a reasonable response to a small year group, and it means additional subject-specific teaching has to come from outside the emirate. Over live video it can, at a fixed time on Gulf Standard Time, with no drive from Al Hamra Village, Mina Al Arab or Al Nakheel at either end of the session.

What this emirate does offer a Business Management student is unusual access to real organisations. There is manufacturing, quarrying, a bulk port, a free zone, construction, hospitality on Al Marjan Island and agriculture inland. A research project needs a real business issue facing a real organisation, and a student here can often reach one through a family connection rather than through a corporate press office. The sections below cover the pre-release calendar, the units and concepts, the three components, the research project stage by stage, where application marks are lost, the quantitative toolkit, the two-year timeline, the pricing question, and the honesty line.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme

programmes.description: Business Management is assessed by Paper 1, built on a case study released ahead of the exam session; Paper 2, a data-response paper on unseen stimulus material; and a research project on a real business issue, capped at 1,800 words. sections.heading: The pre-released case study, and how it reorganises the revision calendar
paragraphs: Paper 1 in Business Management is set on a case study published before the examination session. The organisation, its context and its situation are known in advance. The questions are not, but the material they will be asked about is. Nothing else in a Diploma timetable works this way, and the practical consequence is that a meaningful part of Paper 1 preparation can be completed weeks before any other subject's revision has begun.

Doing it properly has four parts. Reading the case closely enough to know the organisation's structure, market, constraints and stated problems. Researching around it, which means the industry, the competitors and the external environment, so the student can bring context the case does not supply. Mapping the course onto it deliberately, asking which theory from each of the five units could be examined through this organisation. And writing practice answers on the case itself rather than on textbook examples.

Students rarely do any of this unprompted, and in a small cohort it is also the task most likely to be set as independent reading. That makes it the highest-value thing an outside tutor can add, because it is defined, time-boxed and entirely within the student's control. A student who has already written six marked answers on the pre-released case is in a different position from one who has read it twice. The window matters too: this work belongs in the weeks after release and before the mock season absorbs everything, and a plan that does not name those weeks will miss them.

sections.heading: Five units and four concepts, with the Higher Level extensions named
paragraphs: The course is built from five units and four concepts. The units are an introduction to business management, human resource management, finance and accounts, marketing, and operations management. The concepts are creativity, change, ethics and sustainability, and they are not a framing device: examination questions are written against them, and an answer that ignores the concept a question raises has missed part of what was asked.

Higher Level extends every unit rather than adding a separate one, which is efficient to teach and hard for a parent to audit. Alongside the unit extensions there is a set of Higher Level-only tools in the business management toolkit, including force field analysis, gap analysis, Hofstede's cultural dimensions, critical path analysis, simple linear regression and contribution analysis. These are the parts most likely to be compressed when a small group shares lessons with a Standard Level set.

Finance and accounts is the unit that causes most difficulty, and the reason is that it is arithmetic wearing business clothing. Break-even, contribution, cash flow forecasts, final accounts, profitability and liquidity ratios, and at Higher Level investment appraisal, all require a student to compute reliably and then interpret what the number means. Students who were told Business Management is a non-mathematical subject arrive unprepared for it, and the repair is mechanical practice rather than further reading. The toolkit is the other thing worth auditing early. Tools such as SWOT, Ansoff, STEEPLE, the Boston matrix and decision trees are expected to be used on a specific organisation rather than described in the abstract, and a student who can name all of them and apply none will lose marks consistently across both papers.

sections.heading: Three components, and what each one actually rewards
paragraphs: Business Management is assessed by two written papers and a research project. Paper 1, built on the pre-released case study, carries 35% of the grade. Paper 2, a data-response paper on unseen stimulus material including quantitative items, carries 40%. The research project carries the remaining 25%. The weightings are the same at both levels; what differs is the length and depth of the papers and the Higher Level content inside them.

Each component rewards a different behaviour. Paper 1 rewards preparation, because the case is known in advance, and rewards recommendations that fit the specific organisation rather than generic good practice. Paper 2 rewards speed and accuracy on unseen material: reading a stimulus quickly, extracting what matters, performing the calculations correctly and reaching a judgement. The research project rewards method and access, and it is decided long before the writing by whether a real organisation and real data were available.

A parent should ask for the mock breakdown by component. If the loss is on Paper 1, the question is whether the case study was actually worked. If it is on Paper 2, the question is usually calculation speed or the judgement band. If it is on the project, the question is almost always access and data rather than writing quality. Three different diagnoses, three different plans, and a single overall grade tells you none of them. It is also worth knowing that the weightings do not change between the levels. Paper 1 is 35%, Paper 2 is 40% and the project is 25% at both Higher and Standard Level, so the difference between the two courses is content and paper length rather than a rebalancing of the components. A plan built for one level transfers more cleanly here than in subjects where an extra paper appears.

sections.heading: The research project, stage by stage, and where it goes wrong
paragraphs: The research project is a report on a real business issue or problem facing one organisation, capped at 1,800 words and supported by a small set of documents the student has selected. It is worth a quarter of the grade. Almost everything that determines its mark is decided in the first three weeks, when the organisation, the issue and the research method are chosen, and almost nothing can be repaired in the last three.

Access is the first failure point. A student who chooses a large multinational because it is interesting will find no route to primary data and no permission to use internal material, and the project becomes a secondary-source essay with weak evidence. A student who chooses a smaller local organisation, often through a family or community connection, can interview a manager, see real figures and write something genuinely evidenced. In this emirate those connections are more available than in a larger city, which is a real advantage.

The second failure point is the issue itself. 'How can this company improve marketing?' is not an answerable question; it has no boundary and no decision in it. 'Should this company open a second outlet in Al Nakheel?' has both, and the course theory maps onto it directly through investment appraisal, break-even and market research. The third failure point is the supporting documents, which students treat as an appendix to be assembled at the end rather than as the evidence base chosen at the start. sections.heading: Why a student who knows the theory still scores in the middle band
paragraphs: Business Management mark schemes separate knowledge from application and from judgement, and they reward them at different levels. A student who defines a concept accurately earns the knowledge marks. To move up, the answer has to say what that concept means for the specific organisation in front of them, using details from the case or stimulus. To reach the top band, it has to reach a judgement: a recommendation or conclusion that follows from the analysis and acknowledges what it depends on.

The usual script looks like this. The student explains the theory well, mentions the organisation's name twice, lists two advantages and two disadvantages, and finishes with a sentence saying it depends on circumstances. That is a middle-band answer and it will stay middle-band however much more content the student learns. The constraint is structural, not informational, which is why re-teaching units does not move the grade and why a few sessions on answer architecture often does.

Judgement is teachable as a structure. State what the analysis implies. Identify the condition it rests on, usually a constraint in the case: cash position, capacity, labour market, regulation, time. Say what would change the conclusion. Then commit to a recommendation with a reason. Students resist committing because it feels risky, and the mark scheme rewards exactly that commitment when it is supported. Practising it on the pre-released case study is the cheapest way to build it, because the organisation is already familiar.

sections.heading: The quantitative tools a Business Management student has to use quickly
paragraphs: This is the part of the course that surprises families who chose it as a non-mathematical option. The arithmetic is not difficult, but it has to be fast and reliable, because Paper 2 presents unseen figures under time pressure and a student who is slow on contribution or on a current ratio loses minutes they need for the written parts. Accuracy matters doubly: a wrong number carried into an interpretation produces a wrong judgement, and both sets of marks go.

The second half of each tool is interpretation, which students practise even less than the calculation. A gearing ratio is a number; what it tells you about a firm's risk position and what follows for a financing decision is the mark. A break-even point is a number; what it implies about the viability of a pricing change is the mark. Teaching calculation and interpretation together, in the same question, is the only efficient way to do it, because splitting them is how students end up able to compute and unable to conclude.

The Higher Level additions deserve separate time. Investment appraisal, including payback, average rate of return and net present value, requires a student to handle discounting and to compare projects on more than one measure. Critical path analysis has its own notation and its own marks for correct network drawing. Simple linear regression needs a calculator technique as well as an interpretation. None of these appears at Standard Level, and in a shared classroom they are the first thing to be compressed.

sections.heading: A two-year timeline with the case-study release in it
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May session, and the exact session dates belong to the IB and should be confirmed with your child's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org rather than taken from a tutoring page. What makes Business Management's timeline distinctive is that it has an extra fixed point nobody else has: the publication of the Paper 1 case study, which creates a defined window of preparation that closes once the mock season starts.

The research project is the other fixed point, and it is set internally by the school. The two interact badly if nothing is planned: a student doing project fieldwork in the same weeks the case study should be being worked will do one of them poorly. Sequencing them is a planning decision that takes twenty minutes and saves a term, and it is the first thing a tutor should ask about rather than the last.

The table below places both against the ordinary rhythm of a Diploma. Its use is to find the current window and check whether the previous one was actually completed. Where it was not, that is what the first month of support is for, whatever topic the class happens to be on. The summer between DP1 and DP2 is the row families overlook most, and in this subject it is the natural window for securing organisation access for the project, which is the single thing most likely to go wrong later. One caution about the final row. Revisiting the case study in the last weeks is worthwhile only if the real work on it was done in its own window; rereading it in the final fortnight is not preparation, it is reassurance. The marks come from the research and the practice answers, and both have to happen while there is still time to mark them.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs here, and the per-hour versus per-session trap
paragraphs: Before the numbers, the unit of pricing, because it is where families are most often caught out. A rate can be quoted per hour, per session of unstated length, per month as a package, or per block of sessions. A monthly package of eight sessions at AED 799 is about AED 100 a session, which looks very different from an hourly rate until you ask how long a session is. Published in-home monthly packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions work out at roughly AED 200 to 225 an hour, which places them inside the in-home hourly band rather than below it. Always convert to an hourly figure before comparing anything.

With that done, the published UAE market bands read in October 2026 are these. Budget online tutoring runs roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online runs about AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An IB specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase listing AED 270. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 500. The market's premium tier reaches AED 650 an hour, published by BartyED. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour are AED 240 to 600, AED 600 to 1,200 and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more by tier.

Three other questions are worth asking of any quote in this market. Whether the figure is in dirhams or converted from another currency, since two of the competitors researched quote in US dollars. Whether a cancelled session is rescheduled or forfeited. And whether marking of written work is inside the hour or expected to happen unpaid between sessions, which for a subject assessed almost entirely through extended writing is not a trivial detail. IB Gram's own position is a free first lesson and a plan agreed afterwards, rather than a rate card for a problem neither side has diagnosed.
