sections.heading: Academic honesty on the project, and the authorities behind the schooling
paragraphs: The research project is assessed as the student's own work. A tutor may teach the course content, explain what each assessment criterion rewards, advise on whether a business issue is answerable, discuss research method and permissions, check that the chosen tools suit the data, and respond to a draft the student has written. A tutor supplies no text, no analysis, no calculations and no supporting documents that appear in the submission. Research into this market found at least one operator selling completed Internal Assessments outright; a student who submits purchased work carries the malpractice finding and the penalty, and that penalty can be the whole Diploma.

There is a second honesty point specific to this subject. A project built on a real organisation may involve information the organisation considers confidential, and interviewing a manager creates an obligation about how their words are used. Getting explicit permission, anonymising where asked, and saying in the report what was and was not disclosed is both good practice and good assessment practice, because the evaluation of sources is part of what is marked. A student who writes that a figure could not be obtained, and explains the consequence, is doing better work than one who invents a plausible number.

On the institutional side, two separate authorities apply and they are frequently conflated. Private schools in Ras Al Khaimah are regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which according to u.ae regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Individual private tutors are a different matter: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ministry of Education equivalency for university entry is a third process, run by the ministry, and no tutor performs or guarantees it.

process.title: Say which component is losing marks
process.description: Paper 1, Paper 2 and the research project fail for different reasons: an unworked case study, slow calculation and weak judgement, or no organisation access. Naming the component tells a tutor what the first session should be and avoids a fortnight of diagnosis.

process.title: Free first lesson on that component
process.description: The opening session costs nothing and runs on something real: a marked answer, a quantitative question, or the project's current state. You see how the teaching works and how the criteria are applied before anything is agreed.

process.title: A plan with both fixed dates in it
process.description: The written plan names the school's project deadline and the window after the case study is published, and sequences them so neither is done badly. That sequencing is twenty minutes of planning that regularly saves a term of repair work.

process.title: Fixed weekly slots on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Sessions sit at the same time each week, set around pickup reality in your community, with the same tutor throughout. Longer weekend slots are available for case study work, and Ramadan timings move to post-Iftar for the whole month.

process.title: Monthly review against marked answers
process.description: Progress is judged on marked extended writing and timed quantitative work, not on how the sessions felt. If answers are still landing in the middle band, the plan shifts to answer architecture rather than to more content.

whyPoints.title: The pre-released case worked, not skimmed
whyPoints.description: Paper 1 is set on a case study published before the exam, which is an advantage no other Diploma subject offers. It gets a defined block: the case read closely, the industry researched, theory mapped onto the organisation, and practice answers written and marked.

whyPoints.title: Judgement taught as a structure
whyPoints.description: Mark schemes separate knowledge, application and judgement. A balanced list with no conclusion stays mid-band however much content the student knows, and the fix is answer architecture: what the analysis implies, what it rests on, and a supported recommendation.

whyPoints.title: Finance treated as arithmetic
whyPoints.description: Break-even, contribution, cash flow, ratios and, at Higher Level, investment appraisal and critical path analysis have to be fast and accurate under time pressure. They are drilled as computation and interpretation in the same question rather than separately.

whyPoints.title: Project access settled early
whyPoints.description: The research project is decided by whether a student can reach a real organisation and real data, which in this emirate is often possible through a local connection. That access is secured in DP1 or the summer, not in the term the report is due.

whyPoints.title: Prices converted before they are compared
whyPoints.description: Rates in this market are quoted per hour, per session, per month and per block. Every figure on this page is converted to an hourly equivalent with its published source named, so a monthly package can be compared with an hourly rate honestly.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on coursework
whyPoints.description: Support is teaching, method advice and feedback on the student's own draft. No text, calculations, analysis or supporting documents are supplied for submission, and confidentiality obligations to a researched organisation are treated as part of the work.

faqs.question: Is it true that part of the Business Management exam is published before the exam?
faqs.answer: Yes. Paper 1 is set on a case study released ahead of the examination session, so the organisation, its context and its situation are known in advance even though the questions are not. No other subject in a typical Diploma timetable works this way. Used properly it means reading the case closely, researching the industry and competitors around it, mapping theory from all five units onto the organisation, and writing practice answers on the real case. Students who do that arrive at Paper 1 in a materially different position from those who read it twice.

faqs.question: When should the pre-released case study work actually be done?
faqs.answer: In the weeks after it is published and before the mock exam season absorbs everything. That window is short and it closes: once mocks in six subjects are running, nobody has time to research an industry properly. A workable target is six marked practice answers on the actual case before mocks begin, plus a written map of which theory from each unit could be examined through that organisation. In a small cohort this task is often set as independent reading, which is exactly why it is the thing most likely to be left undone.

faqs.question: Why does my daughter know the theory and still score 4s in Business Management?
faqs.answer: Because the mark schemes separate knowledge, application and judgement, and reward them at different levels. Defining a concept accurately earns the knowledge marks. Saying what it means for the specific organisation in the stimulus, using details from it, earns application. Reaching a supported recommendation that acknowledges what it depends on earns judgement. The standard mid-band answer explains the theory, names the firm twice, lists two advantages and two disadvantages and concludes that it depends. More content will not move that; answer architecture will, usually in a handful of sessions.

faqs.question: How much mathematics is really in the Business Management course?
faqs.answer: More than families expect when they choose it as a non-mathematical option. Both levels cover break-even and margin of safety, cash flow forecasts, final accounts, and profitability and liquidity ratios. Higher Level adds investment appraisal with payback, average rate of return and net present value, critical path analysis, simple linear regression and contribution analysis. The arithmetic is not hard, but it has to be quick and accurate because Paper 2 presents unseen figures under time pressure, and every calculation carries an interpretation mark that depends on getting the number right.

faqs.question: What makes a good research project topic, and what makes an unworkable one?
faqs.answer: A workable topic names a real organisation the student can actually reach and asks a decision-shaped question with a boundary, such as whether to open a second outlet in a named location. An unworkable one picks a large multinational with no route to primary data, or asks how a company could improve its marketing, which has no boundary and nothing to conclude. The report is capped at 1,800 words and carries 25% of the grade, and almost everything that decides the mark is settled in the first three weeks rather than the last three.

faqs.question: Can my son use a family business for the research project?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and in this emirate it is frequently the most practical route to real data, which is a genuine advantage over students in larger cities. Two conditions matter. The organisation must have a real business issue worth analysing rather than being chosen purely for convenience, because a thin issue caps the analysis marks. And the confidentiality side has to be handled properly: explicit permission for what is used, anonymising where asked, and a clear statement in the report of what could not be disclosed. Explaining a gap honestly scores better than inventing a plausible figure.

faqs.question: How do the four concepts actually affect answers in this subject?
faqs.answer: Creativity, change, ethics and sustainability are not a framing device; examination questions are written against them, and an answer that ignores the concept a question raises has left part of the task undone. A question about a restructuring that treats it purely as a cost exercise, with nothing on how change affects the people in the structure, is incomplete. The practical habit is to read a question twice, once for the unit content and once for the concept, and to make sure the answer addresses both rather than only the familiar one.

faqs.question: What does Higher Level add to Business Management compared with Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Depth in every unit rather than a separate unit, plus a set of Higher Level-only toolkit tools: force field analysis, gap analysis, Hofstede's cultural dimensions, critical path analysis, simple linear regression and contribution analysis. Higher Level runs to 240 teaching hours against 150, and the papers are longer. The weightings are the same at both levels, at 35% for Paper 1, 40% for Paper 2 and 25% for the research project. Because the additions sit inside existing units, they are the first thing compressed when a small group shares lessons with a Standard Level set.

faqs.question: Is there a Business Management specialist available in Ras Al Khaimah for private work?
faqs.answer: Rarely. Diploma groups here are small, and the teacher carrying Business Management frequently carries Economics as well, which is a sensible use of a small timetable and leaves no spare capacity for private teaching. Matching a specialist over live video on Gulf Standard Time makes subject depth the selection criterion rather than who lives within driving distance. For this subject that matters most on the pre-released case study and the Higher Level quantitative tools, the two things a shared classroom is least likely to cover separately.

faqs.question: Should I compare tutoring prices per hour or per session?
faqs.answer: Per hour, always, after converting. Rates in this market are quoted per hour, per session of unstated length, per month and per block, which makes headline figures hard to compare. A published monthly plan of AED 799 for eight online sessions is roughly AED 100 a session, and published in-home plans of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions work out at about AED 200 to 225 an hour, which sits inside the in-home band rather than below it. Ask the session length first, then convert, then compare.

faqs.question: What should I ask before agreeing a tutoring rate in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Four things. Whether the figure is quoted in dirhams or converted from another currency, since two of the competitors researched publish in US dollars. What the session length actually is, so a monthly package can be compared honestly. Whether a cancelled session is rescheduled or forfeited. And whether marking written work sits inside the paid hour, which matters a great deal in a subject assessed almost entirely through extended writing. A provider unwilling to state a figure before a call is telling you something useful.

faqs.question: How late is too late to start Business Management support in DP2?
faqs.answer: It depends which component is failing. Judgement structure can be built in a few sessions and will lift marks across both papers, and quantitative speed responds quickly to drilling, so a late start is often worth making. What a late start cannot do is work the pre-released case study after the exam, or improve a research project that has already been submitted. An honest late plan names the marks still reachable, which are usually the answer-architecture and calculation marks, and leaves out the ones that are not.

faqs.question: Does Business Management count for business and finance degrees?
faqs.answer: Widely yes, and some programmes prefer or require Economics or a named mathematics course alongside it, which is the thing to check rather than assume. Business, management, logistics, hospitality and marketing routes commonly accept it directly. More quantitative finance and economics degrees sometimes specify a mathematics course at a stated level. Read the published entry requirement for each of the three or four programmes your child is actually considering, in the current admissions cycle, since requirements differ between courses inside one institution and are revised between cycles.

faqs.question: Can sessions work around Ramadan and the summer break for this subject?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the summer is unusually valuable here. During Ramadan most families in this emirate move the weekly slot to after Iftar for the whole month rather than renegotiating weekly. The summer between DP1 and DP2 is the only stretch with no competing deadline, and in Business Management it is the natural window for securing organisation access and permissions for the research project, which is the single thing most likely to go wrong later. A fixed video slot also survives family travel, which many households here do over those weeks.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with a family in this emirate need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, so it is a fair question to ask. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. MoHRE's private tutor licensing service is the official route.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-business-management.closingHeading: Name the component and take the free first lesson
ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-business-management.closingBody: Business Management has three assessed components and they fail for different reasons: a case study that was never worked, calculations that are too slow and answers that never reach a judgement, or a research project with no access to a real organisation. Say which one applies, send the exam session and the current grade, and the first lesson is free, worked on something real with a Business Management specialist, live online on Gulf Standard Time. The plan that follows names your school's project deadline and the case-study window, and sequences them so neither gets done badly.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-chemistry-hl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors here teach Diploma Chemistry at Higher Level: the Structure and Reactivity themes, the quantitative work that carries most of the Higher Level additions, organic mechanisms, and the scientific investigation. The first lesson is free and runs on the topic that is currently blocking your child.

intro.heading: The term you are in decides what Higher Level Chemistry support can do
paragraphs: Higher Level Chemistry is 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, and the ninety-hour difference is concentrated rather than spread. It lands in energetics, where Born-Haber cycles and Gibbs free energy appear; in kinetics, where rate equations and the Arrhenius relationship appear; in equilibrium and acid-base chemistry, where the calculations become genuinely demanding; and in organic chemistry, where reaction mechanisms and spectroscopic identification arrive together. A student can be perfectly competent through the first half of DP1 and meet all of that inside two terms.

That shape is why timing matters so much in this subject. The content that decides Higher Level grades is back-loaded, and it collides with the scientific investigation, the Extended Essay and the mock exam season. In a small Diploma cohort the collision is worse, because the teacher carrying Higher Level Chemistry is often carrying the Standard Level group and a Middle Years science class in the same week, and the Higher Level additions get compressed into the weeks that are left.

Ras Al Khaimah makes that concrete. The emirate runs a compact private-school set under its own Department of Knowledge, and a Diploma cohort here may send four or five students into Chemistry at Higher Level. Nobody is short-changing anybody; a group of five cannot justify a second specialist. What it means practically is that a parent looking for additional Higher Level Chemistry teaching inside the emirate is looking for a person who is already fully timetabled, and that searching harder locally does not change the arithmetic.

Teaching one-to-one over live video changes which constraint applies. The tutor is chosen because they teach Higher Level Chemistry, know what Paper 2 rewards, and have supervised investigations against the four published criteria. The session happens at a fixed time on Gulf Standard Time with no drive from Al Hamra Village or Al Nakheel at either end. For chemistry specifically, the screen is an advantage rather than a compromise: mechanisms, energy cycles and titration curves are drawn and annotated live, and the drawing is the explanation.

The investigation is the component where the timeline bites hardest. It is worth 20% of the final grade, marked out of 24 across four criteria, and capped at 3,000 words. It requires data the student has actually obtained, which means laboratory access through the school and a research design agreed before any apparatus is touched. Students who leave it until the school's internal deadline is visible end up with whatever data they could get rather than the data their question needed, and the conclusion and evaluation criteria punish that directly.

What follows is the detail: the six themes with the Higher Level additions named, how the two papers are weighted and what each rewards, the three places Higher Level marks reliably disappear, the investigation criterion by criterion with dates, how practical work is handled when the teaching is remote, the Chemistry year laid against the school calendar, what the UAE market charges and what a travelling tutor's premium actually buys.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-chemistry-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: Higher Level Chemistry sits at the end of a sequence that starts well before the Diploma. These are the IB programmes Ras Al Khaimah families ask about, and what each means for a student heading into Chemistry at Higher Level.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The Primary Years Programme has no chemistry as such, but it establishes the habit of asking a question and designing a way to answer it. Students who arrive in the Middle Years having been asked to plan their own investigations find the scientific investigation at Diploma level far less alien than those who have only followed instructions on a worksheet.
programmes.countryNote: Only a small number of Ras Al Khaimah campuses run the Primary Years Programme, so many local Diploma students join the IB pathway later from a British or Indian curriculum. That matters at Higher Level Chemistry because independent experimental design is the skill those curricula build least, and it is the first criterion the investigation assesses.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Middle Years sciences are assessed against four criteria, one of which asks students to inquire and design. Criterion B and criterion C scores in MYP 5 sciences are the best available predictor of how a student will cope with the Diploma investigation, and they are more useful than an overall science grade because they separate knowledge from method.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Ras Al Khaimah school runs MYP into Year 11, the integrated sciences course gives less separate chemistry time than a British Year 10 and 11 double or triple award would. Students moving from MYP into Higher Level Chemistry commonly need a short bridging block on moles, bonding and basic organic naming before the Diploma content starts.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Chemistry at Higher Level is examined by two written papers and the scientific investigation. Paper 1 combines multiple choice with data-based questions, Paper 2 is extended response, and a data booklet is supplied in both. The investigation is internally assessed and externally moderated, and the whole course is taught across two years with the investigation submitted in the second.
programmes.countryNote: A northern-emirate Diploma cohort may run Higher Level and Standard Level Chemistry in the same room for part of the week. The content overlaps substantially, so that is a sensible arrangement, but the Higher Level additions in energetics, kinetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms are the part that cannot be taught to both groups at once.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-chemistry-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Chemistry at Higher Level is normally one of three sciences or mathematics subjects under pressure in the same timetable. These are the Diploma subjects Ras Al Khaimah families most often raise alongside it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Six themes: Structure 1 to 3 on the particulate nature of matter, bonding and classification, and Reactivity 1 to 3 on what drives reactions, how far and how fast they go, and by what mechanisms. Higher Level adds the quantitative treatment of almost all of it, plus organic mechanisms and spectroscopic identification.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Four themes crossed with four levels of biological organisation, from molecules to ecosystems. Students taking both sciences meet the same investigation criteria twice, which is an advantage if the two pieces of coursework are planned on different timelines and a problem if they are not.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Themes A to E, with a combined multiple-choice and data-analysis Paper 1. The uncertainty and graph-linearisation work is identical in character to the data analysis criterion in the Chemistry investigation, so a student doing both should be taught that technique once and properly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebra-and-calculus route, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator. Higher Level Chemistry leans on logarithms for pH and pKa work and on exponential relationships for the Arrhenius equation, which Analysis and Approaches students handle most comfortably.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling and statistics route with technology permitted throughout. Its regression and significance-testing content maps directly onto the data analysis criterion of a Chemistry investigation, which is where Applications and Interpretation students have a real advantage.

subjects.name: Biology-adjacent health science routes
subjects.description: Students aiming at medicine, pharmacy or biomedical sciences usually carry Chemistry at Higher Level with Biology, and often with Mathematics at Higher Level as well. The practical consequence is three pieces of internally assessed coursework in the same academic year, which has to be sequenced deliberately.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, with a portfolio of three commentaries as coursework. For a science student it is the extended written argument that usually needs work rather than the quantitative content.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two written papers plus an individual oral, with an additional essay at Higher Level. Chemistry students often write precisely but briefly, and the marks lost here tend to be about development of an argument rather than about accuracy.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects and a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title. The natural sciences are a standing area of knowledge, and a Higher Level Chemistry student has concrete material on models, evidence and the limits of a theory.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay. A Chemistry Extended Essay is a common choice and a demanding one, because it needs experimental work or a defensible data source, and the supervision line has to be clear before the research starts.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Algorithms, data structures and systems, with an internally assessed solution. Students who take it alongside Chemistry often use it for data handling in the investigation, which is legitimate as long as the analysis itself is the student's own work.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-chemistry-hl-tutor.regionsIntro: What makes a weekly chemistry session survive a term is whether it sits at a time the student can concentrate. These are the communities Ras Al Khaimah families book from, with what each one does to a timetable.

regions.name: Al Hamra Village
regions.note: Gated housing in the south near the RAK Academy campuses, where a large share of the emirate's Diploma students are enrolled. Short pickup times here make a 4.30pm start realistic, which matters for a subject that needs a full hour of concentration.

regions.name: Al Nakheel
regions.note: The city-centre district on the creek side. Families here can usually manage a weekday session plus a second shorter slot later in the week, which suits chemistry because the quantitative topics reward frequent short practice over one long session.

regions.name: Mina Al Arab
regions.note: Waterfront housing around Hayat Island. The drive back from city-side campuses runs through pickup traffic, so sessions here are better set at 5pm or later than moved every other week.

regions.name: Al Marjan Island
regions.note: Reclaimed islands with a single access route and ongoing construction. Any arrangement requiring somebody to drive onto the island on a weekday evening is the first thing to fail, which is the practical argument for remote teaching here.

regions.note: Served by a RAK Academy campus with a consistent Diploma intake. Weekday sessions around 4.45pm work for most families, and the Ramadan shift to a post-Iftar slot happens across the whole community at once.

sections.heading: Where a Higher Level Chemistry student usually is when a parent first calls
paragraphs: There are three recognisable arrival points and they need different first months. The earliest is the DP1 student who came through an integrated Middle Years science course or a single-award curriculum and is short on the groundwork: moles, concentration, bonding and the naming conventions that organic chemistry assumes. They are not struggling with Higher Level content yet. They are struggling with what Higher Level content is built on, and a short bridging block fixes it cheaply if it happens in term one rather than term four.

The second is the student who was comfortable until the quantitative Higher Level additions arrived. Energetics is usually the moment: Born-Haber cycles, entropy and Gibbs free energy require a student to hold several sign conventions in mind at once, and a single sign error produces an answer that looks plausible and is wrong. Kinetics and equilibrium follow with rate equations, the Arrhenius relationship and equilibrium constant calculations. These students are good chemists with a specific, fixable arithmetic problem, and they often think they have stopped understanding chemistry.

The third arrives in DP2 with a scientific investigation that has no data, or has data that cannot answer the question asked. That is the hardest brief because it has a hard deadline set by the school, and because the data analysis, conclusion and evaluation criteria all depend on what was collected. The honest order of work is to establish what data exists, decide whether the question can be reframed around it, and only then write. A tutor who starts with the report rather than with the data is solving the wrong problem.

sections.heading: The six themes, and what Higher Level adds to each
paragraphs: The current guide is organised into Structure 1 to 3 and Reactivity 1 to 3, with the experimental and mathematical tools threaded through all six rather than taught separately. Both levels meet the same six themes. What Higher Level adds is largely the quantitative and mechanistic treatment, which is why the extra ninety hours do not feel like extra topics so much as a second, harder pass through the same material.

Knowing which additions have been taught in full is more useful to a parent than any general report comment. Three of them are reliably compressed in a small cohort because they sit late: the entropy and Gibbs free energy work in Reactivity 1, the acid-base and buffer calculations in Reactivity 2, and the organic mechanisms and spectroscopic identification in Structure 3 and Reactivity 3. Those three between them carry a large share of the Higher Level marks on Paper 2.

The table names the additions theme by theme, so you can ask a specific question at a parents' evening. 'Has the class finished the buffer calculations and pH curves?' produces an answer you can plan around. A question about whether chemistry is going well does not. It is also the document a tutor should build the first diagnostic from, because testing all six themes evenly wastes sessions on content the student has genuinely met. One further point about the structure of the guide is worth making, because it changes how revision should work. The experimental techniques, technology and mathematics content is threaded through all six themes rather than taught as a separate unit, which means uncertainty treatment and graph work are examinable in any theme and cannot be revised once and set aside.

sections.heading: How Chemistry HL is marked, and why Paper 2 decides the grade
paragraphs: Higher Level Chemistry is assessed by two written papers and the scientific investigation. Paper 1 combines a multiple-choice section with data-based questions and carries 36% of the grade. Paper 2 is extended response and carries 44%. The investigation carries the remaining 20%. A data booklet is supplied in both written papers, which changes what revision should look like: there is no value in memorising constants, and considerable value in being able to find anything in the booklet within seconds.

Paper 2 is where grades are made and lost, and the reason is structural rather than mysterious. It carries the largest weighting, it asks for extended reasoning rather than recognition, and it is the paper where the Higher Level additions appear in full. A student who revises by re-reading notes and answering multiple-choice questions is preparing for the smaller of the two papers. Command terms matter here too: 'outline', 'explain', 'deduce' and 'discuss' ask for different quantities of writing, and marks are allocated accordingly.

The practical step for a parent is to ask the school for the mock breakdown by paper rather than a single grade. If the loss is on Paper 1A, the work is recall and pace. If it is on Paper 1B, the work is data handling, uncertainty and graph reading. If it is on Paper 2, the work is extended reasoning, mechanism drawing and the quantitative Higher Level topics. Those are three different plans, and a single overall grade conceals which one is needed.

sections.heading: The three places Higher Level Chemistry marks reliably disappear
paragraphs: The first is sign conventions in energetics. Enthalpy, entropy and Gibbs free energy each carry their own convention, and a Born-Haber cycle asks a student to apply several in one calculation while keeping track of whether a step is being added or reversed. The result of a sign error is an answer of the right magnitude and the wrong sense, which no amount of checking the arithmetic will catch. The fix is procedural: draw the cycle every time, label every arrow with its direction, and never work from a remembered expression.

The second is mechanism drawing. Marks in nucleophilic substitution, electrophilic addition and electrophilic substitution questions are given for specific features: the position of a curly arrow, the presence of an intermediate, the correct charge on that intermediate, the stereochemistry where it matters. Students who understand the chemistry perfectly well lose these marks by drawing something that communicates the idea without containing the examinable features. This is the clearest case in the whole course where a tutor drawing alongside a student on a shared screen does something that reading a textbook cannot.

The third is the pH and buffer family of calculations. Ka, Kb, pKa, pKb, buffer composition and the shape of a titration curve form a cluster where each piece is manageable and the combination is not. The usual failure is a student who can calculate the pH of a weak acid but cannot say what happens to it when a salt of its conjugate base is added, because the two were taught as separate exercises. Teaching the cluster as one connected system takes four or five sessions and tends to move more marks than anything else available at Higher Level.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, criterion by criterion, and when each part has to happen
paragraphs: The investigation is worth a fifth of the Higher Level grade, marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each, and capped at 3,000 words. Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation are weighted equally, which is the single most useful fact about it and the one students most often miss. Half the available marks sit in the conclusion and evaluation, written after the practical work is over, and those two criteria are the ones most often rushed because by then the student is tired of the project.

Research design is where the piece is decided. A question that cannot be answered with the apparatus the school has, or that produces too few data points to analyse, caps the other three criteria before any data exists. A good research question names the independent and dependent variables, states how the controlled variables will be held, and is narrow enough that the method fits a realistic number of laboratory sessions. Getting that right is an hour's conversation in DP1 and a term's rescue work in DP2.

The dates below are a working schedule rather than an IB requirement; the submission deadline is set internally by your child's school and should be confirmed with the Diploma coordinator. The purpose of putting dates against criteria is to stop the two highest-value written criteria from being produced in a weekend. Evaluation, in particular, rewards specific comment on the limitations of the method actually used, which is far easier to write while the practical work is fresh.

sections.heading: How practical chemistry is handled when the teaching is remote
paragraphs: This deserves a straight answer because it is the first objection most parents raise. Laboratory work for the Diploma happens at your child's school, under its supervision, using its apparatus, and no tutor changes that. What a remote tutor does is everything that sits either side of the bench: designing the investigation so the data will be analysable, teaching uncertainty and error treatment before the measurements are taken, interpreting the results afterwards, and preparing the student for the data-based questions in Paper 1B.

In practice that is where most of the marks are. A student who collects five data points because nobody told them five was too few has lost marks under data analysis that no amount of careful writing recovers. A student who records measurements without their uncertainties has lost the propagation marks permanently. Both are decided in a planning conversation, not at the bench, and both are entirely teachable over video with the method sheet on a shared screen.

Paper 1B is the other half of this. It presents data a student has never seen, from an experiment they did not perform, and asks them to process and interpret it. Preparing for it is reading practice rather than laboratory practice: identifying what was varied, what was measured, where the uncertainty sits and what the graph actually shows. Working through past 1B questions with a tutor annotating the data live is a closer match to that skill than any additional time in a school laboratory would be.

sections.heading: The Higher Level Chemistry year, laid against the school calendar
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May session, so the two Diploma years have a predictable shape even though the exact session and results dates are set by the IB and should be confirmed through your child's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org rather than taken from any tutoring page. What makes Chemistry particular is that its heaviest content and its coursework deadline land in the same stretch of the calendar, alongside the Extended Essay and the mock exams.

That collision is manageable if it is anticipated and brutal if it is not. A student who has the investigation designed and the data collected before the DP2 mock season has a clear run at Paper 2 content. A student who still has data to collect in the mock term is choosing between two things that both carry marks, and usually does neither well. The single most valuable intervention available in Higher Level Chemistry is moving the investigation earlier, and it costs nothing but planning.

The table sets the chemistry milestones against what else is happening in a typical Diploma calendar, so a parent can see which weeks are already full. The sensible use of it is to find the current window and check whether the previous one was completed. Where it was not, that is what the first month of tutoring is for, regardless of what the current topic in class happens to be. The summer row is the one families overlook most consistently. It is the only window in the two years with no competing deadline, it is long enough to close a real gap rather than paper over one, and in this emirate many families are travelling during it anyway, which a fixed video slot accommodates without anyone rearranging a journey.

sections.heading: What Chemistry Higher Level support costs, and what a travelling tutor's premium buys
paragraphs: Begin with the gap between two published bands, because that gap is the whole argument. Online tutoring from a qualified subject tutor is quoted in the UAE market at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An in-home one-to-one visit including travel is quoted at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's figures at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. Monthly packages seen in the market run about AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

What the premium buys is a person in the room. What it costs, beyond the dirhams, is the size of the pool you are choosing from, and in a northern emirate that is the expensive part. Higher Level Chemistry is a specific competence: Born-Haber cycles, buffer calculations, mechanism marking conventions, investigation criteria. A tutor willing to drive to Al Hamra Village or Mina Al Arab on a weeknight is selected by willingness to travel first and by subject depth second, and for this subject that ordering tends to produce the wrong tutor.

The other bands are worth knowing for completeness. Budget online tutoring runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. IB and IGCSE specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with TutorChase listing AED 270, and the market's premium tier reaches AED 650 an hour, published by BartyED. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. All of these are published market figures read in October 2026 and none is an IB Gram price; our own model starts with a free first lesson and a plan agreed afterwards.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, the health-science routes, and the authorities behind both
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is assessed as the student's own work and IB academic honesty rules treat that seriously. A tutor may teach the chemistry, explain what each of the four criteria rewards, help narrow a research question, teach uncertainty treatment, respond to a draft the student has written and say plainly that a conclusion is not supported by the data. A tutor supplies no text, no data and no processed results for the report. If a service offers a finished investigation, refuse it: a malpractice finding falls on the student and can cost the entire Diploma, and this is a SERP where such offers genuinely exist.

Higher Level Chemistry is usually being taken because of what comes after it. Medicine, pharmacy, dentistry, biomedical science and chemical engineering routes commonly require it, and several specify a minimum grade rather than a pass. Locally that includes RAK Medical and Health Sciences University, and regionally the University of Sharjah, Gulf Medical University and Khalifa University among others. The only reliable source for what any of them requires is that institution's own published entry requirement for the specific programme, read in the current admissions cycle, because requirements differ between courses inside one university.

Two separate authorities sit behind all of this and they are frequently confused. Private schools in Ras Al Khaimah are regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which according to u.ae regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Private tutors are a different matter: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws. For UAE university entry, Ministry of Education equivalency is a third process again, run by the ministry, and no tutor can perform or guarantee it.

process.title: Name the topic, not the subject
process.description: The most useful opening message says which chemistry is failing: Born-Haber signs, buffer calculations, mechanism marks, or an investigation without usable data. That tells a tutor which of the three arrival points you are at and what the first session should actually do.

process.title: Free first lesson on that topic
process.description: The opening session costs nothing and runs on real chemistry. A Higher Level specialist teaches the thing your child named, drawing it out on a shared screen, and you hear how it was explained before any commitment exists.

process.title: A plan with the weightings and the coursework date in it
process.description: The written plan that follows names the themes, the number of sessions and where the investigation work sits relative to your child's school deadline. Paper 2 technique appears as its own block, because at 44% of the grade it earns one.

process.title: Fixed weekly slots on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Sessions are booked for the same time each week, set around pickup reality in your community, with the same tutor throughout. Ramadan timings move to a post-Iftar slot for the whole month rather than being renegotiated weekly.

process.title: Monthly review against marked scripts
process.description: Progress is checked against written work that has been marked by theme, not against how the sessions felt. Recurring errors stay on the list and clean themes come off it, and when the pace is wrong the plan changes rather than the hours rising.

whyPoints.title: Higher Level Chemistry, specifically
whyPoints.description: Not general science and not Standard Level with extra reading. The tutor matched to your child teaches the Higher Level additions as taught content: Born-Haber cycles, entropy and Gibbs work, rate equations, the Ka and buffer cluster, mechanisms and spectroscopic identification.

whyPoints.title: Mechanisms drawn, not displayed
whyPoints.description: Mechanism marks are given for arrow positions, intermediates and charges. A shared screen where the tutor and the student draw the same mechanism together, and the student's version is corrected feature by feature, is a closer match to that than any textbook diagram.

whyPoints.title: The investigation planned, not rescued
whyPoints.description: Half the investigation marks sit in the conclusion and evaluation, and all four criteria depend on a research design that produces analysable data. An hour spent on the research question in DP1 prevents a term of repair work in DP2.

whyPoints.title: Paper 1B treated as its own skill
whyPoints.description: Data-based questions present unfamiliar experiments and ask for processing and interpretation. That is a reading and analysis skill rather than a recall skill, and it gets its own practice rather than being folded into general revision.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Investigation support is teaching, design advice and feedback on work the student has produced. No tutor supplies text, data or processed results, because the student carries the malpractice risk and the consequence can be the whole Diploma.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed
whyPoints.description: The AED bands here are attributed to the rate tables and competitor pages that published them, with the month they were read. No results statistic, satisfaction figure or tutor headcount appears, because none of those could be evidenced on request.

faqs.question: Is there a Higher Level Chemistry specialist based inside Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the arithmetic explains why. The emirate has a compact private-school set regulated by its own Department of Knowledge, and a Diploma cohort here may send four or five students into Chemistry at Higher Level. A group that size cannot support a second specialist, so the teachers who do teach it are fully timetabled. IB Gram's answer is to match a Higher Level Chemistry teacher wherever they are and teach one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which makes subject depth the filter instead of driving distance.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level Chemistry topics get compressed most often in a small cohort?
faqs.answer: Three, and they sit late in most schemes of work. The entropy and Gibbs free energy content in Reactivity 1, the acid-base and buffer calculations with pH curves in Reactivity 2, and the organic mechanisms with spectroscopic identification across Structure 3 and Reactivity 3. Between them these carry a large share of the Higher Level marks on Paper 2, and they land in the term when the investigation deadline, the Extended Essay and the mocks are all competing. A specific question to the school is more useful than a general one here.

faqs.question: Why does my son get the right number but the wrong sign in energetics questions?
faqs.answer: Because enthalpy, entropy and Gibbs free energy each carry their own convention, and a Born-Haber cycle asks a student to apply several in one calculation while tracking whether each step is being used forwards or reversed. A sign error produces an answer of the correct magnitude, so checking the arithmetic never catches it. The repair is procedural rather than conceptual: draw the cycle every time, label every arrow with its direction, and never work from a remembered expression. Four or five sessions of deliberate practice usually settles it permanently.

faqs.question: How are marks actually awarded for organic mechanism questions?
faqs.answer: For specific drawn features rather than for the overall idea. Examiners look for curly arrows starting in the right place and pointing to the right place, the presence and correct charge of any intermediate, and the stereochemistry where the mechanism demands it. Students who understand nucleophilic substitution perfectly well lose marks by drawing something that communicates the concept without containing those features. This is the clearest case in the course for working on a shared screen, where the student's own drawing is corrected feature by feature rather than compared with a finished diagram.

faqs.question: How is the Chemistry scientific investigation marked, and where do students lose it?
faqs.answer: It is marked out of 24 across four equally weighted criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, with the report capped at 3,000 words. Half the marks therefore sit in the two criteria written after the practical work is finished, which is exactly when students are tired of the project. The other common loss is earlier: a research design that cannot produce analysable data caps the remaining criteria before any measurement is taken. Both losses are planning problems rather than chemistry problems.

faqs.question: If the tutoring is online, who supervises the laboratory work for the investigation?
faqs.answer: Your child's school does, using its own apparatus and its own supervision, and no tutor changes that arrangement. What remote teaching covers is everything on either side of the bench: narrowing the research question so the data will be analysable, teaching uncertainty and error treatment before measurements are taken, interpreting results afterwards, and preparing for the data-based questions in Paper 1B. In practice that is where most of the available marks are decided, because a student who collects too few data points cannot recover those marks by writing carefully.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Paper 1A and Paper 1B in Diploma Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Paper 1A is multiple choice across the six themes and rewards recall and pace. Paper 1B is data-based: it presents an experiment the student has never seen and asks them to process and interpret the results, including uncertainties and graph work. The two are sat together and share a single weighting of 36%, but they need completely different preparation. A student revising by re-reading notes is preparing for 1A only, and the 1B marks are usually the easier of the two to recover with targeted practice.

faqs.question: How much harder is Chemistry HL than SL in practice?
faqs.answer: The difference is 240 teaching hours against 150, and it is concentrated rather than spread. Both levels meet the same six themes; Higher Level adds the quantitative and mechanistic treatment of nearly all of them, which is why it feels like a second harder pass through familiar material rather than a list of extra topics. The additions that cause most difficulty are entropy and Gibbs free energy, rate equations, the Ka and buffer family, and organic mechanisms. A student can be comfortable through most of DP1 and meet all of that within two terms.

faqs.question: Does my child need Higher Level Chemistry for medicine or pharmacy?
faqs.answer: Frequently yes, and often with a specified minimum grade rather than a pass, but the requirement belongs to each institution and each programme. Medicine, pharmacy, dentistry, biomedical science and chemical engineering routes commonly ask for it. Locally that includes RAK Medical and Health Sciences University, and regionally institutions such as the University of Sharjah, Gulf Medical University and Khalifa University. Read the published entry requirement for each specific programme in the current admissions cycle, because requirements differ between courses inside the same university and change between cycles.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a Chemistry Extended Essay without crossing the honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the line drawn before the research begins. A tutor may discuss whether a research question is answerable, advise on whether a method can generate defensible data, teach the chemistry the essay needs, explain what the assessment criteria reward and respond to a draft the student has written. A tutor supplies no text, no data and no analysis that appears in the essay. Your child's school appoints the official supervisor, and a tutor works alongside that rather than instead of it. Any offer to produce the essay should be refused outright.

faqs.question: What does a Ras Al Khaimah family pay for Higher Level Chemistry help, online versus in-home?
faqs.answer: Using published UAE market figures read in October 2026: a qualified subject tutor online is quoted at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An in-home visit including travel is quoted at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. Monthly packages seen in the market run about AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. None of those is an IB Gram price.

faqs.question: When is the best time to start Higher Level Chemistry support if we have a choice?
faqs.answer: The summer between DP1 and DP2 is the most efficient window in the whole course, because nothing else is timetabled and no deadline is running. It is the right moment to close a groundwork gap, work through the energetics sign conventions properly, or plan an investigation method in detail. Term three of DP1 is the next best, while the research question is still open. The least efficient start is the DP2 mock term, when the investigation, the Extended Essay and five other subjects are all claiming the same weeks.

faqs.question: Can chemistry sessions move during Ramadan, and do they continue over the summer?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. During Ramadan most families here shift the weekly slot to after Iftar, and the change is made for the whole month rather than renegotiated weekly, which keeps the routine intact when the rest of the schedule is moving. Over the summer, families either pause with a diagnostic session in late August or keep a lighter fortnightly rhythm. For a student entering DP2 the summer is worth using, because it is the only block of weeks in the course with no competing deadline attached to it.

faqs.question: Should I ask a chemistry tutor to show a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: It is a reasonable question. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service is the official application route, through its app, website or e-services.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level Chemistry tutor is free when we need one?
faqs.answer: You are told so, with alternatives, rather than matched to a general science tutor who learns the course alongside your child. The usual options are a different weekday at the same hour, a slightly earlier or later slot that an available specialist can take, a longer fortnightly session, or a place in the queue for a slot that frees at the end of term. For a narrow brief such as mechanism technique or investigation design, a short intensive block at an inconvenient hour frequently works better than a weekly session at a convenient one.

intro.heading: Four ways to buy Computer Science help in a three-school emirate, and what each one cannot do
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah has a small Diploma cohort. The emirate's private schools sit mostly around Al Nakheel, Khuzam, Al Hamra Village and Mina Al Arab, and the number of teachers in the whole emirate qualified to examine Diploma Computer Science is in single figures. That scarcity is the reason the search for an IB DP Computer Science Tutor in Ras Al Khaimah behaves differently from the same search in Dubai. In Dubai a parent is choosing between many comparable people. Here a parent is choosing between four structurally different products, only one of which reliably contains a Computer Science specialist.

The first option is the school's own department. It is already paid for, it knows the teaching sequence and it is bound by a timetable that gives a DP1 class a handful of contact hours a week. The second is a programming tutor — often a working developer, often excellent at code, and often unaware that roughly half the written marks have nothing to do with writing a program. The third is a subject specialist based in Dubai or Sharjah who will travel north; this works, and the rate reflects the E311 in both directions. The fourth is a specialist who never leaves their desk and teaches over live video.

The four are not interchangeable, and the useful comparison is not which one is better. It is which one can move the specific marks your child is losing. A student who scores well on structured questions and badly on the extended response in Paper 1 has a writing problem, not a coding problem. A student whose solution documentation is thin has a planning problem that a developer may genuinely not recognise. A student who has never read a pre-released case study on a named computing scenario has a reading problem that three months of Python practice will not fix.

The sections that follow take each option in turn and say plainly what it does well and where it stops. Then they deal with the two decisions that sit before all four — Computer Science or Digital Society, and Higher Level or Standard — because a parent who gets those wrong pays for tutoring to repair a choice rather than a skill. The figures quoted throughout are market rates taken from published competitor pages and rate surveys, with the source named each time. They are not an IB Gram price list.

One thing is settled before you start reading: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and home visits in the UAE are not something we sell. Our in-home service exists only in India. For Ras Al Khaimah, delivery is one-to-one over live video, with screen sharing both ways, which happens to be the natural format for a subject where the student and the tutor need to look at the same code at the same time.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-computer-science-tu.programmesIntro: Ras Al Khaimah schools offer the Diploma Programme in a small number of campuses, with the Middle Years Programme feeding it and the Primary Years Programme below that. The notes below describe what each stage looks like in this emirate rather than in general.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Computer Science sits in Group 4 with the experimental sciences, which surprises families who expect it in a technology group. That placement matters: a student taking Computer Science has used their Group 4 slot, so Physics, Biology or Chemistry has to come from an elective choice or not at all.
programmes.countryNote: In Ras Al Khaimah the Diploma cohort in any one school is small enough that a subject often runs as a single class with one teacher. If that teacher is also the Theory of Knowledge coordinator or the Group 4 project lead, Computer Science contact time is the first thing squeezed in a busy term. A second specialist voice is therefore less of a luxury here than it would be on a four-form-entry Dubai campus.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, with Design covering digital design and the beginnings of programming. A Middle Years student who has done the Design cycle properly arrives in DP1 already able to state a problem, identify a client and justify a chosen tool — which is three of the five Computer Science solution criteria in embryo.
programmes.countryNote: Several Ras Al Khaimah campuses run the Middle Years Programme and then offer a choice of Diploma or a national-curriculum route at 16. Families who take the second path and later change their minds arrive in DP1 having never written a design brief. That gap is visible in the first solution draft and is cheaper to close in MYP 5 than in DP1.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry organised around six themes, with computational thinking appearing as a way of structuring an investigation rather than as a subject. Primary students here meet block-based coding and simple algorithms inside unit work rather than in a timetabled computing lesson.
programmes.countryNote: The Primary Years Programme is the stage where a Ras Al Khaimah family first notices how thin the local pool of computing teachers is: primary computing is usually taught by a class teacher with an interest rather than a specialist. That is fine at this age. It becomes a problem only if nobody checks, around Year 9, whether the student can read an algorithm as well as write one.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-computer-science-tu.subjectsIntro: Computer Science is rarely tutored alone. The subjects below are the ones a Ras Al Khaimah Diploma student taking Computer Science most often needs alongside it, with a note on what each one assesses and where marks go missing.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Core topics on system fundamentals, computer organisation, networks and computational thinking, one taught option, and a developed solution. Marks leak on the extended-response questions, where candidates describe a mechanism instead of explaining or evaluating it, and on option content taught late in DP2.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, functions, calculus and a strong algebraic spine. Computing degrees usually want this rather than Applications. The commonest loss is in the unstructured Paper 2 questions, where a candidate who can perform every technique cannot decide which one the question wants.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-heavy work. It pairs naturally with Computer Science for students heading towards data analytics or information systems, but some computing faculties ask for Analysis and Approaches, so the route should be checked before the choice is locked in DP1.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields, waves, electricity and the scientific investigation. Students who want hardware, robotics or electronic engineering usually need it, and taking it alongside Computer Science means two Group 4 commitments and two internal assessments running in the same term.

subjects.name: Digital Society
subjects.description: An inquiry course about the social impact of digital systems, assessed through written papers and an inquiry project. It is not a programming course and is not a substitute for Computer Science where a degree asks for one; the two are often confused at option-block time.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: The design cycle, materials, production systems and a major design project. Students who like building things often enjoy it more than Computer Science, and the project discipline transfers directly to the Computer Science solution documentation.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisational structure, marketing, operations and finance, with a research project. It gives a Computer Science student the vocabulary to describe a client, a requirement and a success criterion, which is exactly what criterion A of the solution asks for.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy and three commentaries on published news articles. The quantitative Higher Level paper rewards the same disciplined working that Mathematics rewards, and the commentary word limit teaches the concision the Computer Science extended response needs.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two written papers, an individual oral and, at Higher Level, an essay. It is the subject that most often decides whether a Computer Science candidate can write a four-mark explanation that earns four marks rather than two.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects and an essay on a prescribed title, contributing to the diploma's bonus points alongside the Extended Essay. Computer Science students often find the knowledge questions about algorithms and bias the easiest route into the course.

sections.heading: Route one: a programming tutor, and the marks that are not programming
paragraphs: A working developer is the easiest Computer Science tutor to find in the northern emirates and the most frequently mismatched. Diploma Computer Science is examined on paper. Nothing in Paper 1 or Paper 2 asks a candidate to run a program, and a large share of the marks sit in topics a developer may have never studied formally: two's complement representation, the fetch-decode-execute cycle, the difference between a thread and a process, network protocols by layer, and the social and ethical implications the course attaches to each topic.

The pattern is consistent enough to be diagnostic. A student taught by a developer improves on the questions that ask for an algorithm in pseudocode and stays flat on the four-, six- and eight-mark extended responses. Those longer questions are marked against command terms. 'Describe' wants a sequence of statements. 'Explain' wants a causal chain. 'Evaluate' wants judgement supported on both sides. A candidate who writes good technical prose in the style of documentation scores the first mark of a six-mark question and loses the rest.

The second thing a programming tutor rarely covers is the structure of the paper itself. Section A is short, structured and worth consistent marks to a prepared candidate. Section B is extended and is where grade boundaries are decided. Students who run out of time on Section B almost always spent too long polishing Section A. That is a timing habit, trained with a clock and a mark scheme, and it has nothing to do with programming competence.

None of this makes a developer useless. A developer is the right person to sit beside a student debugging their own solution, and the right person to explain why a particular data structure is the wrong shape for a problem. The mistake is assuming that competence covers the paper. Set the assessment weightings out, as the table below does, and the division of labour becomes obvious.

sections.heading: Route two: a specialist who drives up from Dubai or Sharjah
paragraphs: Start with the cheapest thing on the market and work upwards, because that is the order a budget is actually built in. A university-student tutor working online is the floor: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject teacher online is the next step up, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A recognised IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist sits between AED 200 and 450 or more, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table reaching AED 450 and beyond. Premium named tutors go higher again; BartyED publishes AED 650.

Now add the road. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors between AED 200 and 500. Note what the extra money is actually for. The in-home band overlaps the online specialist band almost exactly, so the premium is not buying a better teacher. It is buying the tutor's travel time, and in Ras Al Khaimah it is buying a lot of it. A specialist living in Dubai Marina who takes a 5pm session in Al Hamra Village is committing something close to three hours of their evening to one paid hour, and they will price it accordingly or decline it.

That arithmetic is why the honest answer to 'can you send someone to Al Dhait on Tuesdays' is usually no, from anyone. The pool of Diploma Computer Science specialists within a 30-minute drive of Ras Al Khaimah city is very small; widen the radius to make it bigger and you have added an hour of driving to every session. Monthly packages make the trade visible. Online packages around AED 799 a month for eight sessions have been advertised, against AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

A Ras Al Khaimah family can check all of this themselves in an afternoon. Ring three agencies, ask for a Diploma Computer Science specialist at Higher Level, give an Al Hamra Village address and a weekday evening slot, and write down what each one quotes and how long the match takes. The pattern that comes back is the argument for teaching this subject over video, and it is a stronger argument than anything written here.

sections.heading: Route three: the department your school already runs
paragraphs: The option most families underuse is the one they have already bought. A Diploma Computer Science teacher in a Ras Al Khaimah school knows the scheme of work, set the internal deadlines, and will be the person who authenticates the developed solution. They also know things no external tutor can know: which option the school teaches, how the Group 4 timetable collides with the science practicals, and when the mock window falls. Before paying anyone, ask the subject teacher three questions and write down the answers.

The first is which option is being taught for Paper 2 and when it will be covered. The second is the school's internal deadline schedule for the solution, including when a draft will be read and how many times. The third is what the teacher thinks the student's specific weakness is, expressed as a component rather than a feeling. 'He is behind' is not actionable. 'He scores well in Section A and loses two-thirds of Section B' is a brief an external tutor can work from immediately.

What the department structurally cannot do is also worth stating. A teacher with one Diploma class, a Middle Years Design timetable and an extracurricular commitment has limited capacity for one-to-one time, and in a small school there is often no second Computer Science colleague to give a different explanation when the first one has not landed. IB rules also cap what any supervisor may do with assessed work: feedback on one draft, and no editing to completion. That cap applies to the school and to every tutor equally.

There is one boundary to respect here. Professional-ethics rules in some emirates prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the permit-holder's own school. Asking your child's own Computer Science teacher for paid evening lessons is therefore the one route on this page that should not be taken. Verify the current rule with the school before assuming anything.

sections.heading: Route four: online one-to-one, and what has to be true for it to work
paragraphs: Video tuition is not automatically better; it is better when three conditions hold, and Computer Science happens to meet all three. The first is that the work is already on a screen. A student's solution, their pseudocode, their marked paper as a scan and the case study PDF are all digital artefacts. Sharing a screen in both directions is a closer approximation of sitting side by side than most subjects get, and it leaves a reviewable record of what was discussed.

The second condition is that the subject is scarce enough that geography costs you quality. That is true here in a way it is not true for, say, Mathematics. A Ras Al Khaimah family hiring locally for Computer Science is choosing from a very short list; the same family hiring online is choosing from specialists anywhere in the world who can work a Gulf Standard Time evening. For a Higher Level candidate taking the case study seriously, that difference is the whole decision.

The third condition is that the student can sustain attention without a person physically present. This is where honesty matters more than sales copy. A 17-year-old working on their own solution will usually be fine. A distractible 12-year-old may not be, and IB Gram does not pretend otherwise — but that is an argument about Middle Years students, not about a Diploma Computer Science candidate preparing for Paper 3. Book the free trial and judge it from the session rather than from a claim on a page.

Practically, sessions run on Gulf Standard Time with the lesson scheduled around the school run and, during Ramadan, around Iftar rather than through it. Work is submitted before the session so the tutor has read it. A short written note goes to the parent afterwards naming the topic, the marks discussed and the next task. If a specialist is not available at the hour you want, we say so and offer the nearest slot rather than substituting a generalist.

sections.heading: Computer Science or Digital Society: the decision that precedes all four routes
paragraphs: A recurring and expensive error in small cohorts is a student who wanted computing and ended up in the wrong course. The two subjects look adjacent on an options sheet and are not adjacent at all. Computer Science is a technical course with a programmed product at its centre. Digital Society is an inquiry course about the social, ethical and political effects of digital systems, assessed through written papers and an inquiry project, with no programming requirement. Both are respectable. Only one of them satisfies a computing faculty that asks for prior programming.

Where this bites in Ras Al Khaimah specifically is option blocks. A school running one Diploma cohort may offer only one of the two, or may offer both but in the same block as a Higher Level science. A student who needs Computer Science and Physics may find the timetable does not allow it. That is not a tutoring problem, and no tutor should be sold to fix it; it is a conversation with the Diploma coordinator in the term before options are chosen, and the earlier it happens the more room there is.

The second place it bites is a student who takes Digital Society expecting to learn to code, then needs programming for a degree application two years later. The repair is a self-taught portfolio alongside the Diploma, which is doable but is extra work in the worst possible year. A parent can prevent the whole situation with one question at the options evening: does this course require my child to build and document a working program, and does the degree we are aiming at require that too?

If the choice has already been made and made badly, say so to the tutor at the trial lesson. There is useful work to do either way — Digital Society students need the same discipline with command terms as Computer Science students, and the inquiry project needs the same planning rigour as a solution. What there is not, is a tutoring plan that converts one qualification into the other.

sections.heading: The developed solution: 34 marks, five criteria and a client who must be real
paragraphs: The internal component of Diploma Computer Science is a developed solution: a piece of software the student designs, builds and documents for an identified client with a real need. It carries 34 marks across five criteria, and the thing families consistently misunderstand is that the marks are mostly not for the product. Planning, design reasoning, the record of development and the evaluation carry most of the total. A beautiful program with thin documentation scores worse than a modest program documented properly.

Criterion A asks for the problem, the client, the rationale for the proposed solution and the success criteria. It is worth six marks and it is where the whole project is won or lost, because every later criterion is judged against the success criteria written here. A vague client — 'students at my school' — produces vague criteria, which produce an evaluation with nothing to evaluate against. A named individual with a stated problem produces a project that marks itself.

Criterion B, the solution overview, wants the design: the records, structures, algorithms and the test plan, presented so another developer could build from it. Criterion C, development, is the largest single allocation at twelve marks and is a record of techniques used and justified, not a code dump. Criterion D looks at whether the product works and whether it could be extended, and criterion E asks the student to evaluate against their own success criteria and propose improvements.

What a tutor may do here is narrow and worth stating out loud. A tutor may teach the criteria, question a plan, point at a weak success criterion, explain why a data structure will not scale, and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not write, complete, edit to completion or supply any part of the solution or its documentation. Nobody should offer that, and an agency that does is exposing your child to a malpractice finding, not helping them.
