sections.heading: Higher Level: the pre-released case study, and why April is too late
paragraphs: Higher Level Computer Science carries a third written paper built entirely on a case study released well before the examination series. The scenario names a computing context — a system, an organisation, a technology — and the paper asks questions that assume the candidate has read around it. This is the single most preparable component in the subject and the one most often left until revision season, at which point it has become a reading list the candidate does not have time to read.

The reason it rewards early work is that the case study introduces vocabulary the core syllabus does not cover. A scenario about machine learning, for example, will expect terms like training data, overfitting and supervised learning to be used accurately rather than gestured at. A candidate meeting those words for the first time in April is learning vocabulary when they should be practising extended responses. A candidate who met them in November has had five months of reading, note-making and discussion to make them usable.

A sensible schedule treats the case study as a term-long project running alongside everything else. Read it once for sense. Build a glossary of every technical term, with a definition in the student's own words and a source. Read a small amount of accessible secondary material each week — vendor documentation, a textbook chapter, a reputable technical article — and add to the glossary. Then, in the last two months, practise answering extended questions on the scenario against a clock.

This is also where a Ras Al Khaimah family feels the thinness of the local pool most sharply. A case study on an unfamiliar technology needs a tutor who can discuss it, not merely a tutor who has the syllabus. That person may not live within driving distance of Al Nakheel. They may well be available over video on a Tuesday evening Gulf Standard Time, which is the practical reason this page exists at all. Confirm the current session dates and the case-study release with your school's Diploma coordinator, since the IB sets them and revises them.

sections.heading: Who is legally allowed to tutor your child in Ras Al Khaimah
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted, and it is permitted by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Any person or agency that tells you a permit costs money, or that a permit is optional, is telling you something that does not match the published rule, and that is a useful early signal about everything else they will tell you.

The eligible categories are broad. The published guidance names teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Breadth is not the same as suitability: a permitted 17-year-old is legally able to tutor and is not the person to coach a Higher Level case study. The permit answers a legal question, not a competence question, and the two get conflated in sales conversations constantly.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are, in the words of the official guidance, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any figure quoted to you as the penalty should be treated as invention. The application route is MoHRE's own service, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days.

An operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. A tuition centre in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; the equivalent licensing in Ras Al Khaimah sits with the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods for private schools. IB Gram is an online tutor-matching platform and holds no regulator permit, accreditation or endorsement of any kind, and no page of ours will claim one.

sections.heading: The Department of Knowledge, Al Nakheel and the weeks a Diploma year has left
paragraphs: Private schools in Ras Al Khaimah are regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which regulates private education in the emirate and, along with Sharjah's authority, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a wider remit than inspection alone, and it is worth understanding what it does and does not reach. It reaches the school: its fees, its licensed curriculum, its assessment practices. It does not reach the Diploma mark scheme, which is set by the IB and is identical in Al Nakheel and in Geneva.

This matters because it tells a parent who to ask. Questions about fees, about whether a campus is licensed to run a programme, or about a complaint against a school go to the regulator. Questions about a subject grade, an internal deadline or a predicted grade go to the school. Questions about the assessment rules themselves go to the IB through the school's Diploma coordinator. Families in small emirates often take all three to the same person and get a frustrating answer.

The calendar then does the rest of the work. A Diploma year in this emirate runs from late August or early September to late June, with a winter break in December, a spring break around March and Ramadan moving through the calendar earlier each year. The usable teaching weeks for a DP2 Computer Science candidate between September and the May examination series are fewer than a parent counting months would assume, because the mock window, the solution deadline and the Extended Essay submission all fall inside them.

Count it backwards and the plan writes itself. Work out the school's internal solution deadline, then the mock window, then the point at which Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay take over a student's evenings, and schedule Computer Science work into what remains. Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar slots rather than being cancelled, which in practice preserves two or three weeks of continuity that families often write off in advance. Confirm every IB date with your school's coordinator, because the IB publishes them and we do not.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the assessed work is code
paragraphs: Computer Science makes the honesty boundary unusually tempting, because code is copyable in a way an essay is not and because reusing code is normal professional practice. The Diploma does not forbid using a library, a tutorial or a code sample. It requires that the student's own contribution is distinguishable and that every borrowed element is referenced in the development record. A candidate who uses a sorting routine from a documented source and says so is fine. A candidate who presents it as their own work is not.

The line for a tutor is clearer still. A tutor may teach a technique, explain why an approach will not scale, question whether a success criterion is measurable, read a draft once and give written feedback on it, and talk through a bug the student is looking at. A tutor may not type into the student's project, restructure their documentation, supply code to be pasted in, or draft any section of the evaluation. If a session ever drifts towards the tutor holding the keyboard, the session has gone wrong and should stop.

The same boundary applies to the reflections a student writes about their own process. Those reflections are assessed and they are the student's. A tutor who coaches a student on what to claim in a reflection is coaching a false account. The honest version is slower and better: the student keeps a development log as they go, and the reflection describes what is in the log. A tutor's job is to make sure the log exists, not to improve the story told about it.

This is worth asking about directly before paying anyone, and the answer is diagnostic. An agency selling completed internal assessments exists in this market; one of them publishes a price for finished work. Ask a prospective tutor what they will do with your child's solution and listen for the word 'feedback' rather than 'handle' or 'sort out'. Then ask the school's Diploma coordinator what external support they expect to be declared, and declare it.

process.description: After the trial the tutor sets out what the first four weeks cover: which core topics, which command terms, which solution criteria and in what order. It tracks the school's own sequence rather than running a parallel syllabus, so it needs the school's scheme of work to be useful.

process.description: A fixed Gulf Standard Time slot each week, with the student's work sent before the session so the tutor has read it. whyPoints.description: A Ras Al Khaimah family hiring locally for Diploma Computer Science is choosing from a very short list. faqs.question: Is there an IB DP Computer Science teacher in Ras Al Khaimah we can hire privately?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but the pool is genuinely small. The emirate's private schools are concentrated around Al Nakheel, Khuzam, Al Hamra Village and Mina Al Arab, and the number of people locally who teach Diploma Computer Science is in single figures. Several of them are prohibited from tutoring students at their own school, which shrinks the list further. That is why most Ras Al Khaimah families end up choosing between a travelling specialist, priced with the road included, and one-to-one lessons over live video. IB Gram offers the second: online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE.

faqs.question: My son codes well but scored 4 in Computer Science. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always the extended-response questions. Paper 1 Section A rewards technical knowledge in short answers, which a strong programmer usually handles. Section B asks for explanation, justification and evaluation against command terms, and good technical prose written in the style of documentation scores badly there. The second common cause is option content for Paper 2 that was taught late and revised thinly. Ask the subject teacher for a component breakdown of the mock rather than a single grade. If Section A is strong and Section B is weak, that is a writing and command-term problem, and it is fixable in a term.

faqs.question: Should my daughter take Computer Science or Digital Society at a Ras Al Khaimah school?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether she needs to build and document a working program. Computer Science sits in Group 4 and has a developed solution at its centre, assessed on 34 marks across planning, design, development, functionality and evaluation. Digital Society sits in Group 3, examines the social and ethical effects of digital systems, and requires no programming. Computing faculties usually want the first. In a small cohort the practical constraint is the option block: the school may offer only one, or may timetable it against a Higher Level science. Raise it with the Diploma coordinator before options are confirmed, not after.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Computer Science developed solution without touching the code?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the only version worth buying. A tutor can teach what each criterion asks for, challenge a vague client or an unmeasurable success criterion, explain why a chosen data structure will not scale, read one draft and give written feedback, and talk through a bug the student is looking at. A tutor must not type into the project, restructure the documentation, supply code or draft any part of the evaluation. If a session drifts towards the tutor holding the keyboard, it has gone wrong. Declare external support to your school's Diploma coordinator.

faqs.question: How much does IB Computer Science tutoring cost in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Market rates rather than ours: online university-student tutors start around AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject teacher online runs roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200. An IB subject specialist sits between AED 200 and 450 or more; TutorChase quotes AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 650, as BartyED publishes. Computer Science usually prices at the specialist end because supply is thin. IB Gram's own figure comes from the consultation after a free trial.

faqs.question: Does it cost more to bring a tutor up from Dubai to Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the published bands show what the money buys. In-home one-to-one visits are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors, which overlaps the online specialist band of AED 200 to 450 almost exactly. The premium is not a better teacher; it is travel time. A specialist driving from Dubai to Al Hamra Village spends close to three hours of an evening on one paid hour, so they price it accordingly or decline the booking. Monthly comparison: around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four in-home ones.

faqs.question: Which programming language will my child be examined on?
faqs.answer: None, in the written papers. Paper 1 and Paper 2 use pseudocode, so a candidate needs to read and write algorithms in a neutral notation rather than in a named language. The language only matters for the developed solution, where the student picks a tool appropriate to the client's problem and justifies the choice in the documentation. Java and Python are both common in UAE schools. Ask the subject teacher which the school teaches, because a tutor fluent in a different language can still teach the course but will cost the student time during development.

faqs.question: When should a Higher Level student start the Computer Science case study?
faqs.answer: The week the scenario is released, and not a month later. Paper 3 is built entirely on a pre-released case study, and the scenario introduces technical vocabulary the core syllabus never covers. A candidate meeting those terms for the first time in April is learning words when they should be practising extended answers. A workable schedule is: read it once for sense, build a glossary in the student's own words with sources, add a small amount of reputable reading each week, then practise timed extended responses in the final two months. Confirm the release and session dates with your school's Diploma coordinator.

faqs.question: Does the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge set the Computer Science syllabus?
faqs.answer: No. The emirate's Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods at school level. The Diploma Computer Science syllabus, its mark scheme and its deadlines are set by the IB and are identical everywhere. That split tells you who to ask: fees and school licensing to the regulator, internal deadlines and predicted grades to the school, assessment rules to the IB through your school's Diploma coordinator. Families in smaller emirates often take all three questions to one person and get a frustrating answer.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Ras Al Khaimah need a permit to teach my child?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, free of charge, for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published, so treat any quoted figure as invention. Ask for a permit reference before the first paid session.

faqs.question: Can online lessons work for a practical subject like Computer Science?
faqs.answer: This is one of the subjects where video is the natural format rather than a compromise. The student's solution, their pseudocode, a scanned marked paper and the case study are all already on a screen, and screen sharing in both directions is close to sitting side by side. It also leaves a reviewable record of what was advised, which matters when the work is assessed. The real variable is the student, not the medium: a Diploma candidate working on their own project is usually fine. Book the free trial and judge the match from the session itself.

faqs.question: My child is in DP1 with no mock marks yet. Is it too early for a Computer Science tutor?
faqs.answer: It is the best point to start, for two reasons. Criterion A of the developed solution is drafted in the first year, and a vague client written in DP1 damages every later criterion because the evaluation is judged against those success criteria. Second, the core topics that sink candidates later, such as number representation and the fetch-decode-execute cycle, are taught early and rarely revisited. Send whatever marked work exists, even a unit test. A specialist can read a weakness from a single marked task better than from a conversation about how the term is going.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level Computer Science needed for a computing degree in the UAE?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the faculty, and it should be checked rather than assumed. Some computing programmes ask for prior programming and will accept Computer Science at either level; others care more about Mathematics, and several prefer Analysis and Approaches over Applications and Interpretation. Check the admissions page of each named university your child is considering and write the requirement down before options are locked. Separately, students entering UAE universities with an international qualification go through Ministry of Education equivalency, a process the ministry runs and we do not; verify its current requirements on the ministry's own site.

faqs.question: What happens if no Computer Science specialist is free at our preferred time?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we offer the nearest slot rather than putting a generalist in the room. Diploma Computer Science is a scarce specialism and Gulf Standard Time evenings are the busiest window in it, so a 5pm Tuesday request is sometimes met with a 7pm Wednesday offer. No competitor researched in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, which is why it is written here. If nothing works for your schedule, that is a straight no from us rather than a substitution you discover in week three.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Computer Science and Mathematics AA for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. The overlap is real: algorithmic thinking, logic and the discipline of justifying each step appear in both, and a single tutor saves scheduling effort and keeps one picture of the student. The risk is depth. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches and Higher Level Computer Science are both substantial, and a tutor strong in one may be merely adequate in the other. Ask for the specialism to be named per subject at the trial stage, and take two tutors if the honest answer is that one person cannot cover both well.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-computer-science-tu.closingHeading: Start with the marked paper, not the price list
ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-computer-science-tu.closingBody: If you are weighing an IB DP Computer Science tutor in Ras Al Khaimah against the department your school already runs, a programming tutor, or a specialist who would drive north from Dubai, the fastest way to decide is to put a component breakdown of your child's last marked paper in front of a specialist and see what they say about it. Send that paper, book the free trial lesson, and use the hour on the weakest component rather than on introductions. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a written note to you after each one. If no specialist is free at the hour you need, we will say so.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-economics-hl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors here teach Diploma Economics at Higher Level: the four units, the nine key concepts, the quantitative Higher Level content, the policy paper and the commentary portfolio. The first lesson is free and runs on whichever of those is currently causing the trouble.

intro.heading: Economics taught against this emirate's own institutions, not generic Gulf copy
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah is a working economy with real material in it, and that matters for Economics more than for any other Diploma subject. The emirate has heavy industry, a bulk port, quarrying and cement, an established ceramics manufacturer headquartered here, a free zone, and a tourism development programme on Al Marjan Island. Each of those generates the kind of published news story a portfolio commentary needs. A student here does not have to write about a hypothetical market or borrow an example from Dubai; the examples are local, current and verifiable.

The regulator is local too, and most pages about UAE tutoring do not know this. Private schools in Ras Al Khaimah are regulated by the emirate's own Department of Knowledge, not by KHDA and not by ADEK. According to u.ae, the Ras Al Khaimah authority regulates private education in the emirate, and the authorities in Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a live economics topic in its own right: a regulated price in a market your child's family actually transacts in.

The course itself is substantial. Higher Level Economics runs to 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, covers four units, and threads nine key concepts through all of them. It is assessed by three written papers plus an internally assessed portfolio of three commentaries. The third paper is the one Standard Level never sits, it carries 30% of the Higher Level grade, and it is unlike the other two: a quantitative and policy-focused paper with compulsory questions and no choice.

What usually brings a Ras Al Khaimah family to a tutor is one of three things. A DP1 student who writes well and cannot produce a diagram that earns its marks. A DP2 student whose portfolio commentaries are returned with low application and evaluation marks and who cannot see why. Or a Higher Level student who is comfortable on Papers 1 and 2 and loses the Paper 3 marks because the paper asks for calculation and policy reasoning rather than extended essay writing.

The constraint on fixing any of that locally is supply. Diploma cohorts in this emirate are small, and Economics at Higher Level may be a group of four or five taught by a teacher who also runs the Standard Level set and a business course. Nobody is at fault in that arrangement; it is what a small year group produces. It does mean that additional Higher Level teaching has to come from outside, and over live video it can, at a fixed time on Gulf Standard Time with no drive from Al Hamra Village or Al Nakheel at either end.

The sections below work through the three papers and their weightings, the portfolio criterion by criterion, where local source material actually comes from, the nine concepts with locally anchored examples, the diagram marks students leave unclaimed, how to practise the policy paper, the regulator map across all seven emirates, what tutoring costs set against school fees, and the academic-honesty line on a commentary.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-economics-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: Economics at Higher Level sits inside a wider IB structure, and where a student came from changes what the support must cover. These are the programmes Ras Al Khaimah families ask about.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Individuals and Societies in the Middle Years Programme is assessed against four criteria, including investigating and communicating. There is no economics as such, but the habit of using sourced evidence to support a claim is the skill a Diploma commentary is built on, and students who never acquired it find criterion C the hardest of the five.
programmes.countryNote: Ras Al Khaimah campuses running MYP into Year 11 generally give Individuals and Societies as an integrated course rather than as separate economics or business teaching. Students entering Higher Level Economics from that route usually need the core diagram set built from the beginning in DP1, which is cheap to do early and expensive to do late.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Economics at Higher Level is examined by Paper 1, an extended-response paper; Paper 2, a data-response paper; and Paper 3, a quantitative and policy paper sat only at Higher Level. Alongside these sits the portfolio of three commentaries, each capped at 800 words, written on published news media and marked out of 45 in total.
programmes.countryNote: A Higher Level Economics group in this emirate may be four or five students sharing a teacher with the Standard Level set. The shared content makes that workable; the Higher Level quantitative material and Paper 3 technique are the parts that cannot be delivered to both groups at once, and they carry 30% of the Higher Level grade.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs Diploma courses with a career-related study. Economics is a natural fit alongside business, hospitality and logistics pathways, and a CP student taking it sits identical papers and the identical portfolio to a full Diploma candidate.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Ras Al Khaimah campus offers CP, the career-related study frequently connects to the emirate's own sectors: logistics around the port, construction materials, manufacturing or hospitality. That gives a CP economics student unusually direct access to local source material for the portfolio.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-economics-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Economics at Higher Level rarely arrives alone in a Diploma timetable. These are the subjects Ras Al Khaimah families most often raise in the same conversation.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Four units covering the introduction to economics, microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, with nine key concepts running through all of them. Higher Level adds quantitative content and a third paper focused on calculation and policy recommendation.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Five units with four concepts, and a Paper 1 built on a case study released ahead of the exam. Students taking both subjects should be clear that Economics rewards diagram-based analysis while Business Management rewards applied judgement on a named organisation.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with technology permitted in every paper. Its index number, elasticity and regression work overlaps directly with the quantitative content of Higher Level Economics, which makes the combination efficient to teach.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebra-and-calculus route with a non-calculator Paper 1. Economics does not require it, though students aiming at economics degrees at competitive universities should check whether a specific mathematics course and level is named in the entry requirement.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Core units on population, climate and resource consumption with optional themes. The development and global interactions content overlaps with the global economy unit in Economics, and the fieldwork requirement builds the same sourcing discipline a commentary needs.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Power, sovereignty, human rights, development and peace, with an engagement project. The development content and the Economics global economy unit reinforce each other, and the written style demanded is closer to Economics Paper 1 than to any science subject.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Prescribed subjects, world history topics and, at Higher Level, a regional depth study, plus a historical investigation. The sourcing and evaluation habits transfer well to the commentary portfolio, which asks for exactly that treatment of a news article.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two written papers plus an individual oral, with an additional essay at Higher Level. Economics students usually have the argument and lose marks on textual analysis, which is the reverse of the pattern science students show.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches with research methods throughout. Behavioural economics ideas appear in both courses, and the critical evaluation of a study is the same skill a commentary's evaluation criterion rewards.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects and a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title. The human sciences are a standing area of knowledge, and an Economics student has concrete material on models, assumptions and whether a prediction counts as evidence.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay. An Economics Extended Essay is a strong choice for a student with access to local primary data, and the research question has to be narrow enough to answer with the theory on the syllabus.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-economics-hl-tutor.regionsIntro: Ras Al Khaimah's communities differ in what they do to a weekday evening, and an Economics session needs an uninterrupted hour for extended writing. These are the areas families book from.

regions.name: Al Nakheel
regions.note: The central district near the creek and the older campuses. Short journeys home make an early slot workable, which suits the pattern of one longer writing session a week that Economics benefits from.

regions.name: Al Hamra Village
regions.note: Gated housing in the south by the RAK Academy campuses. Weekend morning sessions are popular here and work particularly well for commentary writing, where an unhurried ninety minutes is worth more than two rushed half-hours.

regions.name: Mina Al Arab
regions.note: Waterfront housing around Hayat Island. Pickup traffic through Al Qusaidat means a fixed later start holds better than an early one that keeps slipping, which matters when the session involves marking a piece of writing.

regions.name: Al Marjan Island
regions.note: Reclaimed islands carrying the emirate's resort development programme. Families here have the tourism and construction economy on their doorstep, which is useful commentary material, and the single access road is why nobody should be driving to a lesson.

regions.name: Khuzam
regions.note: Served by a RAK Academy campus with a regular Diploma intake. Weekday sessions around 4.45pm are standard, and the whole community shifts to post-Iftar timing together during Ramadan.

regions.name: Al Dhait North and South
regions.note: Inland villa districts, often with children at different campuses. Staggered sibling slots are normal, and an Economics session for one child can sit alongside a different subject for another without anyone travelling.

regions.name: Al Qusaidat and Julphar
regions.note: Older city neighbourhoods close to the industrial and port side of the emirate. Students here frequently have family connections to the sectors their commentaries can be written about, which is an advantage for the personal engagement a portfolio shows.

regions.name: Seih Al Uraibi and Al Mamourah
regions.note: Established districts near the ring road. Parents here tend to arrive having tried a general tutor and now asking the more specific question of whether a tutor can mark a commentary against the five criteria.

regions.name: Digdaga and the inland belt
regions.note: The agricultural and low-density inland area, with real primary-sector activity. For a student writing about resource allocation or agricultural markets, the material is genuinely local rather than imported from a textbook.

sections.heading: The Higher Level Economics course as a student in this emirate meets it
paragraphs: Four units carry the content: an introduction to economics, microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy. Nine key concepts run through all four: scarcity, choice, efficiency, equity, economic well-being, sustainability, change, interdependence and intervention. The concepts are not decoration. They structure the course, they appear in the examination questions, and each portfolio commentary must be explicitly built on a different one of them, which is where students most often lose marks without understanding why.

Higher Level runs to 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, and the additional time goes into quantitative content and into a third examination paper. That matters for how a plan is built, because a Higher Level student has both more content and a different kind of assessment to prepare for. A tutoring plan that treats Higher Level as Standard Level plus extra reading will leave the Paper 3 marks, 30% of the grade, substantially unaddressed.

What a student in Ras Al Khaimah has that a student in a larger city does not necessarily have is direct access to the economy being studied. Heavy industry, a working bulk port, quarrying and construction materials, a ceramics manufacturer headquartered in the emirate, a free zone and an active tourism development programme are all within driving distance. For microeconomics and for the global economy unit in particular, that turns abstract theory into something a student can actually observe, and observation is what the personal engagement behind a good commentary is made of.
bullets: Four units: introduction, microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy

sections.heading: Three papers at Higher Level, and the one Standard Level never sits
paragraphs: Higher Level Economics is examined by three written papers plus the portfolio. Paper 1 is an extended-response paper carrying 20% of the Higher Level grade. Paper 2 is a data-response paper carrying 30%. Paper 3 carries a further 30% and is sat only at Higher Level. The portfolio carries the remaining 20%. At Standard Level the structure is simpler and the weightings are quite different: Paper 1 carries 30%, Paper 2 carries 40%, and the portfolio carries 30%.

The practical consequence of those numbers is often missed. At Standard Level the portfolio is worth almost a third of the grade, which makes it the single most valuable thing a Standard Level student does. At Higher Level the portfolio drops to a fifth and Paper 3 arrives at 30%, so the balance of effort should shift accordingly. A Higher Level student spending the same proportion of their time on the portfolio as a Standard Level classmate is misallocating effort, which is an irony worth pointing out in an economics course.

Paper 3 also behaves differently from the other two. Both of its questions are compulsory, so there is no choice to fall back on, and it mixes quantitative work with diagram analysis and a policy recommendation. A student who prepares for it by writing more essays is preparing for Paper 1. The table sets the components out side by side so a parent can see where the Higher Level effort has to go.

sections.heading: The portfolio: three commentaries, 800 words each, 45 marks
paragraphs: The portfolio is three separate commentaries, each written on a published news article, each capped at 800 words, and each assessed against the same five criteria. Every commentary must be based on a different unit of the syllabus and must be built around a different key concept, and the articles must come from published news media rather than from a blog or a textbook. The articles also have to be recent: within one year of the commentary being written.

Marks are distributed across diagrams, terminology, application and analysis, the key concept, and evaluation. Diagrams carry three marks per commentary and are the easiest to secure, provided they are drawn correctly, labelled fully and referred to in the text rather than left floating. Evaluation carries four, the largest single allocation, and is the one students most reliably lose, because they list advantages and disadvantages instead of reaching a judgement that follows from what they have just argued.

The article choice decides a great deal before any writing begins. An article with no numbers, or one that reports an outcome without any mechanism, gives a student nothing to analyse, and the application and analysis criterion cannot be rescued by effort later. Screening three candidate articles against what each would allow a student to do takes under an hour and is the highest-value hour in the whole portfolio process. The word limit is the other thing to plan around rather than discover. Eight hundred words is very little once a diagram has been referred to properly, the mechanism explained and a judgement reached, which means the commentary has to be narrow from the outset. Students who start broad write 1,400 words and then cut, and what gets cut is almost always the evaluation, because it sits at the end.

sections.heading: Where a Ras Al Khaimah student finds commentary source material
paragraphs: This is the part of the portfolio that families in a smaller emirate assume is a disadvantage, and it is the opposite. Ras Al Khaimah has a visible mixed economy: quarrying and cement, a ceramics manufacturer headquartered in the emirate, bulk shipping through its port, a free zone, construction, agriculture in the inland belt and a tourism development programme on Al Marjan Island. Each of those produces reported news with numbers in it, which is exactly what a commentary needs and exactly what a hypothetical example cannot provide.

The microeconomics unit maps onto several of them directly. A quarrying or cement story supports work on costs, economies of scale and externalities. A port or logistics story supports work on markets, derived demand and infrastructure as a public good. A tourism development story supports work on investment, employment and the multiplier, and also on sustainability as a key concept. An agricultural story from the inland belt supports price volatility and government intervention. None of these requires the student to invent anything; they require a published article and the discipline to analyse rather than summarise it.

The regulated-fee question is the local example most directly relevant to a Diploma family, and it is a genuine intervention case. In Dubai, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package the emirate valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. In Ras Al Khaimah, fee approval sits with the emirate's own Department of Knowledge, which u.ae states approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A commentary comparing a price control in one emirate with an approval regime in another is a strong piece of work on intervention and equity, and the sources are public.

sections.heading: The nine key concepts, with examples a student here can actually observe
paragraphs: The nine concepts are the spine of the course and the structuring device of the portfolio. Students treat them as labels to be attached at the end, and the key concept criterion punishes that: a commentary where the concept appears in the opening sentence and never returns scores poorly however good the economics is. Used properly, a concept is the lens that decides which theory the commentary uses and what the evaluation weighs.

The useful discipline is to choose the concept before the diagram. If the lens is efficiency, the commentary is heading towards deadweight loss and allocation. If it is equity, it is heading towards distribution and incidence. If it is sustainability, it is heading towards externalities and the long run. A student who picks the diagram first and then looks for a concept to justify it produces a commentary where the two pull against each other, and the examiner can see that from the first page.

The table pairs each concept with an example from within this emirate's own economy, which also solves the portfolio's planning problem. Three commentaries need three different units and three different concepts, so planning them together in DP1 prevents the common failure of two commentaries quietly covering the same ground. The table is a planning document as much as a teaching one. It is worth saying that the concepts also appear in the written papers, not only in the portfolio, so the work done planning commentaries is not coursework work that vanishes afterwards. A Paper 1 question asking a student to evaluate an intervention is asking for the same reasoning the intervention concept demands, and a student who has already written 800 disciplined words on it has an advantage in the examination that students who treated the portfolio as an administrative task do not.

sections.heading: Diagrams: the marks almost nobody revises
paragraphs: Economics is unusual among Diploma subjects in awarding explicit marks for drawn work in both the examinations and the coursework. In the portfolio, diagrams carry three marks of every fifteen. In Paper 1 and Paper 2, a correct and fully labelled diagram is frequently the difference between a partial answer and a complete one. Despite that, students revise diagrams less than any other part of the course, because drawing feels like something you either can or cannot do rather than something to practise.

The marks are given for specific features. Axes labelled with the correct variables and units. Curves labelled and drawn in the right shape. Any shift shown with a clear arrow and the new curve labelled distinctly. Equilibrium points marked and the relevant price and quantity dropped to the axes. Shaded areas identified where welfare or revenue is being discussed. A diagram that conveys the idea without those features earns a fraction of its available marks, exactly as in chemistry mechanism questions.

The remedy is mechanical and fast. There is a finite set of diagrams in the course: supply and demand with shifts and interventions, elasticity cases, cost and revenue curves, market structures, the aggregate demand and supply family, the business cycle, trade diagrams with tariffs and quotas, and exchange rate diagrams. Drawing each of them from memory against a checklist, repeatedly, for about three sessions, is enough to secure the drawn marks for the rest of the course. It is the cheapest grade movement available in Economics and the most consistently neglected.

sections.heading: Paper 3, and why essay practice does not prepare a student for it
paragraphs: Paper 3 is the Higher Level policy paper and it carries 30% of the grade. Both questions are compulsory, so a student cannot avoid a weak area by choosing around it. The paper mixes quantitative work, calculations using given data, with diagram analysis and with a policy recommendation that has to be argued rather than asserted. In structure and in demand it is closer to an applied problem set than to an essay.

The two failure modes are distinct. The first is arithmetic: a student who is slow or unreliable on index numbers, elasticity calculations, multiplier values, tax incidence or exchange rate conversions loses marks on questions where the economics was understood. These are mechanical skills and they respond to drilling in a way that essay writing does not. The second is the policy recommendation, where students produce a preference rather than an argument: a recommendation with no stated constraint, no acknowledged cost and no reason for preferring one instrument over another earns a fraction of the available marks.

Preparing properly means treating the paper as its own thing. Quantitative techniques get drilled until they are quick. Policy recommendations get a structure: the objective, the instruments available, the expected effect of the chosen one, the costs and the constraint, and a conclusion that follows. Then both compulsory questions get practised under full timing, because the pacing of a paper with no choice is different from the pacing of one where a weak topic can be skipped. In a small cohort this is also the component least likely to have been drilled, because it serves only part of the class.

sections.heading: Who regulates schools in each emirate, and why it belongs on an Economics page
paragraphs: Most pages about UAE tutoring name KHDA and stop. The actual regulator map has five bodies, and getting it right matters here both because your child's school answers to one of them and because regulation is examinable content. According to u.ae, KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai, ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates private education in that emirate, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The economics interest is in what those bodies actually do. U.ae states that the Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, which is a markedly broader remit than inspection alone. A regulator that approves prices is intervening in a market, and a student who can describe that mechanism precisely has a ready-made commentary on intervention using a market their own family participates in.

There is also a scale comparison available. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen different curricula in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum accounting for 37% of enrolment, Indian 26%, US 14% and the International Baccalaureate 7%. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. Setting that against a northern emirate with a far smaller school set is a legitimate economics discussion about market size, entry and provision.

sections.heading: What Economics support costs, set against what a school year already costs
paragraphs: Tutoring is a line in a household budget that already contains school fees, and the only honest way to present it is in that context. The published UAE market bands, read in October 2026, are as follows. Budget online tutoring runs roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online runs about AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An IB specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase listing AED 270. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 500, and the market's premium tier reaches AED 650 an hour, published by BartyED.

Translated into periods a family actually budgets in, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month with a budget tutor, AED 600 to 1,200 at mid range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages seen in the UAE market run about AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. These are market figures from the named sources and none of them is an IB Gram price.

The context worth adding is that fees themselves are a regulated price in this market. KHDA confirmed no fee increase for Dubai private schools for 2026-27, and in Ras Al Khaimah fee approval sits with the Department of Knowledge. A family deciding whether to add tutoring is making a marginal spending decision against a largely fixed cost, which is the sort of calculation the course itself teaches. The practical version of it is to decide what the tutoring is for before deciding what tier to buy: a diagram and terminology problem does not need the specialist tier, and a Paper 3 technique problem will not be solved by the budget one.

sections.heading: Academic honesty on a commentary, and the equivalency question
paragraphs: The portfolio is assessed as the student's own work. A tutor may teach the economics, explain what each of the five criteria rewards, discuss whether a candidate article will support real analysis, check that the three commentaries cover three different units and three different concepts, and respond to a draft the student has written. A tutor supplies no text, no diagrams and no analysis that appears in a submitted commentary. The research behind this page found at least one operator in the UAE search results selling completed Internal Assessments outright; a student who submits purchased work carries the malpractice finding, not the seller.

The other question Ras Al Khaimah families raise is Ministry of Education equivalency, which is a separate process run by the ministry and not something any tutor performs or guarantees. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math.

No IB points threshold appears on this page because none has been verified from the ministry's own material, and one competitor already publishes an incorrect subject count for the British track. Verify the IB route on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority before planning around a number. Tutoring is also not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, and any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a regulatory process.

process.title: Say which component is losing marks
process.description: Economics has four assessed components and they fail differently. Naming whether the loss is on Paper 1 evaluation, Paper 2 calculation, Paper 3 policy reasoning or the portfolio criteria tells a tutor what the first session should be and saves a week of diagnosis.

process.title: Free first lesson on that component
process.description: The opening session costs nothing and works on a real piece: a marked Paper 1 answer, a returned commentary or a Paper 3 question. You see how the teaching works and how the criteria are applied before anything is agreed.

process.title: A plan weighted the way the papers are
process.description: The written plan allocates time in proportion to the Higher Level weightings rather than evenly, which means Paper 3 gets its own block at 30% of the grade and the portfolio is planned across three units and three concepts from the start.

process.title: Fixed weekly slots on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Sessions sit at the same time each week, set around pickup reality in your community, with the same tutor. Ramadan timings move to a post-Iftar slot for the whole month, and longer weekend slots are available for commentary work.

process.title: Monthly review against marked writing
process.description: Progress is judged on marked extended writing and marked diagrams, not on how sessions felt. Criteria that keep costing marks stay on the plan; those that come back clean leave it, and the hours adjust to what the evidence shows.

whyPoints.title: Local source material, not borrowed examples
whyPoints.description: This emirate has quarrying, cement, a port, a headquartered manufacturer, a free zone, agriculture and a tourism development programme. A commentary built on a published local story beats one built on a hypothetical market, and the examiner can tell the difference.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 treated as its own paper
whyPoints.description: Thirty per cent of the Higher Level grade sits in a compulsory paper that mixes calculation with policy reasoning. It gets a dedicated block: quantitative techniques drilled, recommendations structured, both questions practised under full timing.

whyPoints.title: Diagrams drilled against a checklist
whyPoints.description: Axes, curve labels, shifts, equilibrium points and shaded areas each carry marks. The full diagram set in the course is finite, and drawing it from memory against a checklist for a few sessions secures those marks for the rest of the course.

whyPoints.title: The portfolio planned, not assembled
whyPoints.description: Three commentaries need three different units, three different key concepts and three articles under a year old that each support real analysis. Planning that together in DP1 avoids the standard failure of two commentaries quietly covering the same ground.

whyPoints.title: The right regulator named
whyPoints.description: Private schools in Ras Al Khaimah answer to the emirate's Department of Knowledge, not to KHDA. Getting that right matters for a family reading a fee notice, and the regulator map is examinable content in the intervention sections of the course.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on coursework
whyPoints.description: Support is teaching, article screening and feedback on the student's own draft. No text, diagram or analysis is supplied for submission, because a malpractice finding falls on the student and the consequence can be the entire Diploma.

faqs.question: What does Paper 3 in Higher Level Economics actually involve?
faqs.answer: It is a one-hour-forty-five-minute paper carrying 30% of the Higher Level grade, with both questions compulsory, so there is no weak area to avoid. It mixes quantitative work using given data with diagram analysis and a reasoned policy recommendation. The two usual failures are arithmetic, on index numbers, elasticity, multipliers, tax incidence and exchange rate conversions, and recommendations that state a preference rather than argue a case. Preparing for it by writing more essays prepares a student for Paper 1 instead, which is why it needs a dedicated block of sessions.

faqs.question: How are the three Economics portfolio commentaries marked?
faqs.answer: Each is capped at 800 words and assessed against five criteria: diagrams worth three marks, terminology worth two, application and analysis worth three, key concept worth three and evaluation worth four, giving fifteen marks per commentary and 45 across the portfolio. Each commentary must cover a different syllabus unit and a different key concept, and each article must be published news media released within a year of writing. Evaluation is the largest single allocation and the one most reliably lost, because students list advantages and disadvantages instead of reaching a judgement.

faqs.question: Where can a student in Ras Al Khaimah find news articles for the portfolio?
faqs.answer: Locally, which is an advantage rather than a limitation. The emirate has quarrying and cement, a ceramics manufacturer headquartered here, bulk shipping through its port, a free zone, construction, inland agriculture and a tourism development programme on Al Marjan Island. Each generates reported stories with figures in them. Regulated school fees are another genuine case: Dubai's regulator confirmed no fee increase for 2026-27, while in Ras Al Khaimah fee approval sits with the Department of Knowledge, which makes a strong commentary on intervention using a market the family participates in.

faqs.question: Why do my son's commentaries score well on terminology and badly on evaluation?
faqs.answer: Because evaluation asks for something structurally different from the rest of the commentary. Terminology rewards accurate vocabulary, which a diligent student acquires. Evaluation, worth four marks of fifteen, rewards a judgement that follows from the analysis just presented, together with the assumptions and limitations behind it. A list of advantages and disadvantages is not a judgement, however balanced. The fix is a structure: what the analysis implies, what it depends on, what would change the conclusion, and what the student therefore concludes. It is teachable in three or four sessions.

faqs.question: How many marks do diagrams carry in Economics, and are they really worth practising?
faqs.answer: Three marks of every fifteen in each portfolio commentary, plus substantial credit inside Paper 1 and Paper 2 answers. They are worth practising precisely because the marks are given for specific features rather than for general correctness: labelled axes with units, labelled curves, shifts shown with arrows and new curves distinguished, equilibrium points dropped to the axes, and shaded areas identified where welfare is discussed. The diagram set in the course is finite, so drilling it from memory against a checklist for about three sessions secures those marks permanently.

faqs.question: Which of the nine key concepts should a commentary use?
faqs.answer: Whichever one genuinely frames the article, chosen before the diagram rather than attached afterwards. The nine are scarcity, choice, efficiency, equity, economic well-being, sustainability, change, interdependence and intervention. The concept decides the theory: efficiency points towards allocation and deadweight loss, equity towards distribution and incidence, sustainability towards externalities and the long run. A commentary that names a concept in the opening line and never returns to it loses most of that criterion, which is three marks of fifteen, so the lens has to run through the whole piece.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level Economics need a particular mathematics course alongside it?
faqs.answer: The Diploma does not require one, but the quantitative content at Higher Level, and Paper 3 in particular, is noticeably easier for students taking a mathematics course that covers index numbers, percentage change and basic modelling. Applications and Interpretation overlaps most directly. Separately, some university economics programmes name a specific mathematics course and level in their entry requirement, sometimes Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. That is worth checking in DP1 while subject choices can still be changed, rather than discovering it when offers arrive in DP2.

faqs.question: Which of the five UAE school regulators should an Economics student be able to name?
faqs.answer: The emirate's own Department of Knowledge. According to u.ae it regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The full map has five bodies: KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Most tutoring pages name only KHDA, which is wrong for four of the seven emirates.

faqs.question: How does the Higher Level and Standard Level mark allocation change what we should focus on?
faqs.answer: Considerably, and families often miss it. At Standard Level the portfolio carries 30% of the grade, making it the single most valuable piece of work a student does. At Higher Level the portfolio drops to 20%, Paper 1 falls to 20%, Paper 2 holds 30% and Paper 3 arrives at 30%. A Higher Level student allocating effort as a Standard Level classmate would is therefore underweighting the paper that carries the most Higher Level-specific marks. The plan should follow the weightings rather than treating all four components as equal.

faqs.question: Is there a Higher Level Economics specialist available in this emirate?
faqs.answer: Rarely for private work. Diploma cohorts in Ras Al Khaimah are small, and a Higher Level Economics set may be four or five students taught by someone who also runs the Standard Level group and a business course. That teacher is fully committed. Matching a specialist over live video on Gulf Standard Time makes subject depth the selection criterion rather than who lives nearby, which matters most for Paper 3 and portfolio supervision, the two parts a small cohort is least likely to have drilled separately.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write a commentary without breaching academic honesty rules?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the economics, explain what each criterion rewards, discuss whether an article will support genuine analysis, check that the three commentaries cover three different units and concepts, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot supply text, diagrams or analysis that appears in the submission. Research into this market found at least one operator selling completed Internal Assessments; the malpractice finding falls on the student who submits purchased work and can cost the whole Diploma, so such an offer is a reason to end the conversation.

faqs.question: What does Economics tutoring cost here compared with what we already pay in school fees?
faqs.answer: Published October 2026 market rates: budget online tutoring runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65; a qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200; IB specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Bestimate's monthly bands for a weekly hour are AED 240 to 600, AED 600 to 1,200 and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. School fees are a regulated price here, approved by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which makes tutoring the marginal decision against a largely fixed cost.

faqs.question: How late in DP2 is it still worth starting Higher Level Economics support?
faqs.answer: Later than in most subjects, because two of the biggest sources of loss are fast to fix. Diagram technique can be secured in about three sessions and the evaluation structure in another three or four, and between them those cover marks in every component. What a late start cannot do is rebuild the quantitative fluency Paper 3 assumes or improve a portfolio that has already been submitted. The honest version of a late plan names which marks are still reachable and leaves out the ones that are not, rather than promising coverage.

faqs.question: Do tutoring sessions need to stop during Ramadan or over the summer?
faqs.answer: No. During Ramadan most families here move the weekly slot to after Iftar for the whole month rather than renegotiating week by week, which keeps the routine stable while the rest of the schedule moves. Over the summer, families usually either pause with a diagnostic session in late August or hold a lighter fortnightly pattern. For a student entering DP2, the summer is the only stretch with no competing deadline, which makes it the natural window for planning all three portfolio commentaries properly.

faqs.question: Should I ask an Economics tutor for a UAE tutoring permit?
faqs.answer: It is a reasonable question for any tutor working with a UAE family. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule. MoHRE's private tutor licensing service is the official application route through its app, website or e-services.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-economics-hl-tutor.closingHeading: Name the component and take the free lesson
ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-economics-hl-tutor.closingBody: Economics has four assessed components and they fail in different ways, so the quickest route to a useful plan is to say which one is costing marks: Paper 1 evaluation, Paper 2 calculation, Paper 3 policy reasoning, or a portfolio criterion. Send that with the exam session and the current grade, and the first lesson is free, worked on a real marked piece with a Higher Level Economics specialist, live online on Gulf Standard Time. The written plan that follows allocates time in proportion to the Higher Level weightings rather than evenly across the four.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-english-a-language-.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach group one English for the Diploma, which is a narrower job than teaching English well. Paper 1 rewards one thing, the comparative essay rewards another, and the oral is marked against a four-criterion rubric that has nothing to do with confidence.

intro.heading: Four options on the table, and a parent deciding between them in October
paragraphs: A Ras Al Khaimah family usually arrives at this search after a report card rather than after a crisis. The comment says the writing is fluent but descriptive, or that the response to unseen texts lacks analysis, and a grade five has appeared where a six or seven was assumed. From that point a parent is choosing between four things at once, and the choice is often made badly because nobody lays them out side by side.

The first option is to change course. English A: Language and Literature and English A: Literature are different subjects with different reading lists and different papers, and a student who dislikes advertisements, speeches and political cartoons may genuinely be better served by the literature course. The second is to change level, or to move out of group one altogether into English B, which is a language-acquisition course and a different qualification signal to a university. The third is to wait for the school's English department, which in a small Ras Al Khaimah cohort may be one teacher covering both group one courses. The fourth is to bring in outside support.

Each of those has a real cost and a real deadline. Course changes are usually possible only in the first weeks of Diploma year one, and almost never after the Individual Oral has been recorded. A level change from Higher to Standard removes the Higher Level essay but also removes a 20% component the student may have been doing well in. English B looks like relief and can close doors at admission. Doing nothing has a cost too, because the oral is recorded once and the mark does not get a second attempt.

This page is built as that comparison rather than as a sales pitch. Three tables set out the course differences, the level differences and what each delivery option costs in this market, with the published source for every dirham figure. The subject detail that follows is specific to Ras Al Khaimah because the school set here is small: two campuses carry most of the emirate's Diploma students, cohorts of eight or ten are normal, and there is rarely a second group one specialist in the building to give an independent reading of a draft.

On delivery, the position is plain. IB Gram does not run a centre in Ras Al Khaimah and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE — home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons for families in Al Hamra, Al Nakheel, Mina Al Arab or Al Dhait are one-to-one and online, over live video, with the student's own marked script or draft shared on screen and annotated during the session. The argument for that here is availability rather than price: a specialist who has marked these four criteria is not necessarily someone who lives half an hour from your road.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-english-a-language-.programmesIntro: Group one English is a Diploma course, but a Ras Al Khaimah student arrives at it from one of three places, and the alternative a parent should be considering depends on which.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Language and Literature is one of two group one routes. Students study literary works alongside a body of non-literary material — journalism, advertising, speeches, photography, graphic texts — and are assessed on Paper 1, Paper 2, the Individual Oral and, at Higher Level, a written essay. The non-literary half is what distinguishes it, and it is the half most students have never been taught to read closely.
programmes.countryNote: Ras Al Khaimah Diploma cohorts are small enough that a school may run only one group one course. Where both run, the sets may share a teacher, which is why an independent reading of a Paper 2 draft is hard to obtain inside the emirate.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Language and literature in the Middle Years Programme is assessed on four criteria covering analysis, organisation, producing text and language use. A student who consistently scored higher on producing text than on analysing it is already showing the profile that produces a descriptive Diploma essay two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Two campuses in the emirate run the Middle Years Programme to year five. Students arriving into the Diploma from the Indian or British streams instead have usually never met criterion-referenced marking, and read a grade five as a near-miss rather than as a description of what the writing did.

programmes.name: IGCSE English as the route in
programmes.description: Most Ras Al Khaimah students who enter group one English come from Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE English Language and Literature. Those courses reward accurate reading and controlled writing. The Diploma asks for evaluation of how a text positions a reader, which is a different instruction, and the shift catches out students who were comfortable at IGCSE.
programmes.countryNote: An A or A star at IGCSE English is not a prediction of a seven in Language and Literature. The students who struggle most in Diploma year one here are frequently the ones whose IGCSE grade told them, reasonably, that English was already handled.

programmes.name: The Diploma core alongside it
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay sit on top of group one English, and for a student who writes well they tend to be registered in English. That concentrates the writing load into the same terms as the Individual Oral and the Higher Level essay.
programmes.countryNote: In a small cohort the same teacher may supervise the group one course and several Extended Essays. Families here should check in September which term holds the oral recording window, since it rarely moves.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-english-a-language-.subjectsIntro: The components below are what a group one grade is actually made of, listed with the level they apply to. Reading them as a single subject is how students end up strong at one and weak at another without noticing.

subjects.name: Paper 1: guided textual analysis
subjects.levels: SL one text, HL two texts
subjects.description: An unseen non-literary text with a guiding question. Standard Level analyses one in 1 hour 15; Higher Level analyses two in 2 hours 15. Worth 35% at both levels. Marks are lost in the first twelve minutes, when a student decides what the text is doing.

subjects.name: Paper 2: comparative essay
subjects.description: Four unseen general questions; the student answers one on two literary works studied, from memory and without the texts. Worth 35% at Standard Level and 25% at Higher. The common failure is two separate essays stapled together rather than one comparison.

subjects.name: Individual Oral
subjects.description: A fifteen-minute oral on a global issue, using one literary and one non-literary extract of up to 40 lines each. Marked out of 40 across four criteria. Worth 30% at Standard Level and 20% at Higher. Recorded once.

subjects.name: Higher Level essay
subjects.description: A 1,200 to 1,500 word essay on one literary work or one non-literary body of work studied, developed from a line of inquiry. Marked out of 20. Worth 20% of the Higher Level grade and the component students start latest.

subjects.name: The learner portfolio
subjects.description: Compulsory and not assessed, which is why it gets neglected. It is where the lines of inquiry that become the Higher Level essay and the global issue for the oral are supposed to be developed and recorded.

subjects.name: Non-literary bodies of work
subjects.description: Advertising campaigns, political cartoons, speeches, photojournalism, travel writing, infographics. Students who read fiction confidently often have no vocabulary for how a layout or an image argues, and Paper 1 is drawn entirely from this territory.

subjects.name: English A: Literature
subjects.description: The alternative group one course. Literary works only, with a different Paper 1 and a Higher Level essay drawn from literature. It suits a student who reads novels and plays willingly and finds the non-literary material arbitrary.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: A group two language-acquisition course, not a group one course. Appropriate for genuine second-language learners. Moving a strong English speaker into it to protect a grade changes the qualification a university sees, which is why it deserves a conversation rather than a form.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Shares assessment vocabulary with group one English and competes for the same weeks. A student whose Theory of Knowledge essay is going badly is often having the same problem as in Paper 2: claims asserted rather than argued.

sections.heading: Alternative one: Language and Literature, Literature, or English B
paragraphs: These three are not interchangeable and a parent is often presented with them as if they were. Language and Literature studies literary works alongside non-literary material: advertising, journalism, speeches, cartoons, photography. Literature studies literary works only. English B is not a group one course at all — it sits in group two as a language-acquisition subject, and a university reading a transcript can tell the difference.

The reason this matters for a Ras Al Khaimah student is availability. In a cohort of eight or ten, a school may timetable only one group one course, so the choice is sometimes made by the timetable rather than by the student. Where both exist, the decision should turn on what the student can actually do. A reader who engages willingly with novels and plays and finds the analysis of a government poster arbitrary will do better in Literature. A student who is sharp about how media works and finds nineteenth-century prose a slog will do better in Language and Literature.

Moving a competent English speaker into English B to protect a grade is the decision most likely to be regretted. It is designed for second-language learners, and for a student educated in English since primary it will usually produce a high mark that says less to an admissions reader than a six in group one. There are students for whom it is genuinely the right course, and a bilingual household in this emirate is not by itself one of them.

Timing closes these doors quickly. Course and level changes are generally possible in the first weeks of Diploma year one and become impractical once texts have been studied and the oral extracts chosen. If this decision is live for your family, it is a September and October conversation with the Diploma coordinator, not a February one.

sections.heading: Alternative two: Higher Level or Standard Level, and the four real differences
paragraphs: Level is the second decision and it is widely misunderstood as reading more books. The number of literary works does rise — at least four at Standard Level, at least six at Higher — but three other differences matter more to a grade.

Paper 1 changes shape. Standard Level students analyse one unseen non-literary text in 1 hour 15 minutes. Higher Level students analyse two in 2 hours 15, which is not simply double: it demands a reliable method that can be executed twice under time pressure, and it punishes a student who reads slowly before deciding what to say. The paper is worth 35% at both levels, so the Higher Level version carries the same weight for harder work.

The Higher Level essay is the component that appears only at Higher Level, worth 20%, running 1,200 to 1,500 words on a single literary work or non-literary body of work. It is written outside examination conditions, which should make it the most reliable mark on the course. In practice it is the one students start last, because the learner portfolio that is supposed to generate its line of inquiry was treated as optional.

The weightings redistribute rather than increase. At Standard Level the oral carries 30% and Paper 2 carries 35%. At Higher Level the oral and Paper 2 drop to 20% and 25% to make room for the essay. A student who performs well orally and poorly in written examinations is therefore better served, arithmetically, by Standard Level — a point no school option sheet makes.
