sections.heading: Alternative three: the school's own department, and what it structurally cannot do
paragraphs: The cheapest option is the school, and for many problems it is also the right one. A student who has missed lessons, or who has not read the second comparative text properly, needs the teacher and a reading schedule rather than a tutor. Clinic time, departmental revision sessions and a direct conversation with the group one teacher should be used first, and they cost nothing.

There are two things the school cannot structurally provide in a cohort this size, and they are worth naming without criticising anyone. The first is an independent second reading. When one teacher sets the task, teaches the text, approves the global issue and marks the draft, there is no second professional view available inside the building. On a component marked against criteria rather than right answers, a second reading is often what identifies the problem.

The second is unlimited one-to-one time. A teacher with two group one sets, several Extended Essay supervisions and a Theory of Knowledge allocation has a fixed number of hours. Twenty minutes on a Paper 2 draft is a generous slice of a department's week and is not enough to change a student's habit of writing two parallel essays instead of one comparison.

The honest sequence, then, is to exhaust the school first and bring in outside support for the specific thing the school cannot give: an independent marker, working one-to-one, on the student's own script, repeatedly, until the shape changes. That is a narrower claim than most tutoring pages make and it is the one worth paying for.

sections.heading: Alternative four: a visiting tutor in this emirate, priced as it actually is
paragraphs: Published hourly rates for one-to-one tuition in the UAE span a factor of ten, and most pages in this market publish none at all. The table below sets out bands that providers published themselves, with the provider named and the month they were read, so you can see what each figure is. None of them is an IB Gram price: our quote follows the free trial, because it depends on level, frequency and how close the recording window or the May session is.

Two features of Ras Al Khaimah push in-home figures up rather than down. Distance is the first: a tutor driving from the city side to Al Marjan Island or out to Digdaga absorbs close to an hour of unpaid travel, and that is inside the rate whether it appears on the invoice or not. Supply is the second. There is a workable pool of general English tutors in the emirate and a very small pool of people who have marked Diploma group one criteria. Scarcity in a thin market does not produce a discount.

IB Gram does not operate premises in Ras Al Khaimah and does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tuition is something we offer only in India. Lessons for families here are one-to-one and online over live video, with scripts and drafts shared on screen. The case for it in this emirate is access to a specialist rather than cost, although it is usually cheaper as well.

One practical note on paying anyone, including an independent tutor. An individual giving paid private lessons in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and those working without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask to see it; a tutor who holds one will not mind being asked.

sections.heading: Paper 1 in twelve minutes: why strong readers stall on the unseen text
paragraphs: Paper 1 gives a student a non-literary text and a guiding question, and asks for a focused analysis. It is worth 35% at both levels. The students who stall are rarely weak readers; they are usually students who read well and then write a description of what the text says rather than an argument about what it does.

The first twelve minutes decide the mark. In that window a student has to identify the text type and its conventions, work out the intended audience and the effect being sought, and settle on a controlling idea that the guiding question can be answered through. A script that starts writing before that is settled produces a tour of features — a simile here, a statistic there — with no line of argument for the examiner to follow, which is exactly what the analysis and evaluation criterion penalises.

Non-literary conventions are the gap that shows up most in this emirate, because IGCSE English rarely drills them. A political cartoon argues through caricature, juxtaposition, labelling and scale. An advertisement argues through the relationship between image and copy, through what is cropped out, through the register of a single verb. A speech argues through structure and repetition as much as through content. Students who have no vocabulary for these produce literary analysis of a non-literary text and wonder why the mark is mid-band.

At Higher Level the same method has to run twice in 2 hours 15. That makes timing a separate trainable skill rather than a by-product of competence. In lessons it is drilled as such: the twelve-minute planning phase first, against the clock, repeatedly, before any whole paper is attempted.
bullets: Text type and conventions identified before any sentence is written
Audience and intended effect stated explicitly, not assumed
One controlling idea the guiding question can be answered through
Feature-spotting replaced by argument; every device tied to the effect

sections.heading: The Individual Oral: a global issue, two extracts of forty lines, forty marks
paragraphs: The Individual Oral is fifteen minutes long, marked out of 40 across four criteria, and worth 30% at Standard Level or 20% at Higher. The student speaks for ten minutes on a global issue, drawing on one literary work and one non-literary body of work studied, using an extract of no more than 40 lines from each, and then answers five minutes of questions from the teacher.

The global issue is where most of the mark is won or lost, long before the recording. It has to be of genuine wide significance, transnational, and visible in the everyday. It also has to be narrow enough to be argued in ten minutes. Students pick themes rather than issues — identity, power, the environment — and then speak generally for ten minutes because a theme gives nothing to argue. A workable global issue sounds specific enough to be contestable, and the five fields of inquiry in the guide are a starting point rather than a menu to copy.

Extract choice is the second failure. An extract must be rich enough to sustain close analysis for several minutes and must actually show the global issue at work rather than merely mention it. Forty lines is both a limit and a hint: the examiner expects close work on the extract, not a summary of the whole work with the extract as an excuse. Choosing a passage because it is memorable is how students end up with nothing to analyse.

The oral is recorded once, and that single fact should change how a family plans. There is no retake for a weak recording in the way there is for a weak practice essay. Preparation blocks are therefore timed to the school's recording window, and rehearsal is done against the four criteria rather than against nervousness. The student's plan stays the student's; a tutor can question it, test it and mark a rehearsal, and should not supply it.

sections.heading: The Higher Level essay, and the portfolio nobody marks
paragraphs: The Higher Level essay is 1,200 to 1,500 words on one literary work or one non-literary body of work studied, marked out of 20 and worth 20% of the Higher Level grade. It is written away from examination conditions with access to the text, which should make it the most dependable mark on the course. For a large number of students it is the weakest, and the reason is almost always the same.

The essay grows out of a line of inquiry, and the line of inquiry is supposed to grow out of the learner portfolio. The portfolio is compulsory and not assessed, which in practice means it is maintained for the first term and abandoned. A student with no portfolio arrives at the essay with no developed question, invents one in a week, and writes 1,400 words of general commentary on a text they have not reread with a question in mind.

A good line of inquiry is narrow, arguable and answerable within 1,500 words. It names something specific about the work — a technique, a pattern, a structural decision — and asks what it achieves. A bad one asks how a theme is presented, which produces description. The difference is identifiable in a single tutorial, which is why this component responds well to one-to-one work earlier in the year rather than later.

What outside support may legitimately do here is bounded by IB academic honesty rules and we state it rather than leaving it vague. A tutor may teach the criteria, interrogate a line of inquiry, point at a paragraph that asserts instead of arguing, and mark a draft against the rubric. A tutor may not supply the line of inquiry, add sentences to the essay, or edit it to completion. The essay has to be the student's own work, and in a market that contains providers selling finished coursework that boundary is worth stating in plain words.

sections.heading: How lessons actually run for a Ras Al Khaimah household
paragraphs: Sessions are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The student's own marked script, draft or chosen extract is shared on screen and annotated during the hour, which is the part that makes the difference: a student who watches their own paragraph taken apart twice begins doing it themselves before submitting. Sessions are recorded so an annotated script can be re-watched the night before a mock.

Scheduling here is set by geography and the school calendar rather than by preference. Students in Khuzam and Al Mairid can realistically start at 4pm. Students travelling back from the southern campuses to Al Marjan Island or Digdaga cannot, and an evening slot after dinner is both more realistic and more productive. During Ramadan the usable window moves to after Iftar, and a 5pm slot commonly becomes 9pm for the month; essay and oral work adapts to that better than most subjects because it needs concentration rather than equipment.

Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies are mandatory in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated in 40-minute lesson units and minimum weekly totals to be met. That is real timetable space, and for a group one student it often collides with the term that holds the oral recording window, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Extended Essay deadline. Mapping those dates in September is what creates room later.

If no group one English specialist is free in the window you need, we tell you before you pay, with a realistic date. Where the available specialist is based outside the UAE, that is disclosed too, along with what it means for timing. Several providers in this market route UAE families to a contact number that implies local delivery and does not provide it; a thin market is a fact about this emirate and stating it is more useful than concealing it.

process.title: Send one marked script and two facts
process.description: The two facts are level and which component is causing the problem. The marked script matters more than any description of it: a Paper 1 response with a teacher's annotations usually shows the diagnosis directly, whether that is feature-spotting, weak audience awareness or no controlling idea.

It should end with a named problem — the first twelve minutes of Paper 1, a global issue that is actually a theme, a line of inquiry that invites description — not a general impression.

process.description: Every session ends with a short note on what moved and what did not, which makes progress checkable against the school's own marks rather than against impressions. The note names the criterion, not the effort level.

process.description: At six weeks we look at marked school work. If the targeted criterion has not moved, either the plan changes or the tutor does. That conversation is cheaper in November than in April, and the oral recording window is usually the hard deadline that decides which.

faqs.question: Should my child move from Language and Literature to English A Literature?
faqs.answer: Only if the reason is the material rather than the mark. Literature studies literary works only; Language and Literature adds non-literary bodies of work such as advertising, speeches and cartoons, and Paper 1 is drawn from that territory. A student who reads novels willingly and finds the analysis of a poster arbitrary is often better placed in Literature. A student struggling with analysis itself will struggle in both. The window is practically the first weeks of Diploma year one, before texts are studied and extracts chosen, so this is a September conversation with the coordinator.

faqs.question: Is moving my child into English B a reasonable way to protect the Diploma grade?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and it should not be done on a form. English B sits in group two as a language-acquisition course, not in group one, and an admissions reader can see the difference on a transcript. For a genuine second-language learner it is the right course. For a student schooled in English since primary it usually produces a high mark that says less than a six in group one would. A bilingual household in this emirate is not by itself a reason. Discuss it with the coordinator and with whoever is advising on university applications.

faqs.question: How many literary works does my child read at Standard Level compared with Higher Level?
faqs.answer: At least four at Standard Level and at least six at Higher Level, alongside non-literary bodies of work at both. The number is the least important difference. Paper 1 changes from one unseen text in 1 hour 15 to two in 2 hours 15 while staying worth 35%, and Higher Level adds a 1,200 to 1,500 word essay worth 20% that Standard Level does not sit. The extra reading is manageable; the extra component and the longer paper are what decide whether the level was the right choice.

faqs.question: Why does Paper 1 go badly when my child's English is clearly strong?
faqs.answer: Because Paper 1 is not a test of reading well. It gives an unseen non-literary text and a guiding question, and rewards an argument about what the text does to a reader. Strong readers often write an elegant description of what the text says, list several devices, and never commit to a controlling idea. The mark then sits mid-band in the analysis and evaluation criterion. The fix is the first twelve minutes: text type, audience, intended effect and one controlling idea settled before any sentence is written.

faqs.question: What exactly is a global issue for the Individual Oral, and how narrow should it be?
faqs.answer: Narrow enough to argue in ten minutes and significant enough to matter beyond one country. The guide offers five fields of inquiry as a starting point, covering areas such as culture and identity, beliefs and values, politics and power, art and imagination, and science and environment. Students commonly choose a theme instead — identity, power, the environment — and then speak generally, because a theme gives nothing to contest. A usable global issue is specific enough that a reasonable person could disagree with the student's claim about it.

faqs.question: How long can the two Individual Oral extracts be?
faqs.answer: Up to 40 lines each: one from a literary work studied and one from a non-literary body of work studied. The limit is also an instruction. The examiner expects close analysis of the extracts rather than a summary of the whole work, so a passage must be rich enough to support several minutes of detailed work and must show the global issue operating rather than simply mentioning it. Students who choose a memorable passage rather than an analysable one find themselves with ten minutes to fill and nothing in the text to fill it with.

faqs.question: If the oral recording goes badly, can it be done again?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a single attempt. The oral is recorded once and submitted, and it carries 30% of a Standard Level grade or 20% at Higher Level. That one fact should shape how a family plans the year: preparation is timed to the school's recording window rather than spread thinly, rehearsals are run against the four criteria rather than against nerves, and the global issue is settled weeks earlier than most students settle it. Ask the Diploma coordinator in September when the recording window falls, because it rarely moves.

faqs.question: What makes a comparative essay in Paper 2 score well?
faqs.answer: Comparison rather than coverage. The paper gives four general questions and the student answers one on two literary works studied, without the texts in front of them. The commonest mid-band script is two competent essays joined by a paragraph of transition. A strong script runs one argument through both works at once, moving between them inside paragraphs, with quotations held accurately from memory. That is a planning habit rather than a knowledge problem, which is why building plans for four question types beats memorising a model answer.

faqs.question: What should go into the learner portfolio if it is not marked?
faqs.answer: The work that becomes the two components students most often rush. The portfolio is compulsory and unassessed, and it exists to develop lines of inquiry and candidate global issues as the course goes along. A student who maintains it arrives at the Higher Level essay with three possible questions already tested against the text, and at the oral with a global issue that has been narrowed. A student who abandoned it in term one invents both in a single week, which is exactly how a 20% component becomes the weakest mark on the course.

faqs.question: How do I tell a good Higher Level essay line of inquiry from a weak one?
faqs.answer: A good one is narrow, arguable and answerable in 1,500 words. It names something specific in the work — a structural decision, a recurring technique, a pattern in how a campaign addresses its audience — and asks what it achieves. A weak one asks how a theme is presented, which can only be answered with description. The test is whether a reasonable reader could argue the other side. This is usually identifiable in one tutorial, which is why the essay responds better to support in term two than in the fortnight before submission.

faqs.question: What may a tutor legitimately do on the Higher Level essay or the oral?
faqs.answer: Teach the criteria, interrogate a line of inquiry or a global issue, point out where a paragraph asserts rather than argues, and mark a draft or a rehearsal against the rubric. What a tutor may not do is supply the inquiry question, write or rewrite sentences, edit to completion, or script an oral. IB academic honesty rules make that an expulsion risk for the student, and some providers in this market sell completed work outright. We teach it, question it and mark it; your child writes and speaks it.

faqs.question: Can my child's own English teacher in Ras Al Khaimah tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: Assume not. The MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct barring a holder from tutoring students affiliated with their own school, and Abu Dhabi's regulator has published professional-ethics rules prohibiting school staff from paid private tutoring of their own enrolled students. The practical objection matters as much as the rule: the value of outside support on a criterion-marked component is an independent reading, and the person who set the task, taught the text and approved the extract cannot give you one.

faqs.question: Does a visiting English tutor come to Mina Al Arab or Al Hamra Village?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons for Ras Al Khaimah families are one-to-one over live video with scripts and extracts shared on screen. Independent visiting tutors do work in the emirate, and the published market band for an in-home hour runs roughly AED 180-500 including travel, but very few people within driving distance of these communities have marked Diploma group one criteria, which is the thing you are actually buying.

faqs.question: What does group one English tuition cost in this market?
faqs.answer: Published bands, which are not our prices, run roughly: AED 45-150 an hour for general online tutoring, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject teacher online, AED 180-500 for an in-home visit with travel included, and AED 200-450 or more for an IB subject specialist. EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase and Bestimate published those figures themselves. Monthly packages advertised here include AED 799 for eight online sessions. Our quote follows the free trial, because it depends on level, frequency and how close the recording window is.

faqs.question: It is twelve weeks to the May papers. Is the Higher Level essay still worth working on?
faqs.answer: If it has not been submitted, it is the best-value hour available, because it is the one component written with the text open and without a clock. Twelve weeks is also enough to change Paper 1 behaviour, since the twelve-minute planning phase is a drillable habit rather than new knowledge. What twelve weeks will not do is add two literary works to a student who has not read them, or re-record an oral. Spend the time on what is still movable and be honest about what is not.

faqs.question: What happens if no group one English specialist is free when we ask?
faqs.answer: You are told before paying, with a realistic date. We will not put a general English tutor in front of a four-criterion oral problem and describe it as the same service. Where the available specialist is based outside the UAE, that is disclosed too, along with what it means for scheduling against Gulf Standard Time. Several providers in this market imply local delivery through a contact number and deliver from elsewhere. Ras Al Khaimah is a thin market for Diploma group one English, and saying so is more useful than a confident booking.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-extended-essay-tuto.tutorsIntro: The tutors below coach the Extended Essay as a research project: narrowing a question until it is answerable, choosing a method that can actually be carried out from Ras Al Khaimah, and holding the student to the five criteria. The student writes every word.

intro.heading: You already have a supervisor. Here is what the other three options add, and what they cost
paragraphs: Every Diploma candidate is assigned an Extended Essay supervisor by their school, at no extra charge. That supervisor reads one complete draft, holds three recorded reflection sessions and signs the work off. So the honest starting question for a family in Ras Al Khaimah is not 'how do I find an IB DP Extended Essay Tutor in Ras Al Khaimah' but 'what can a paid coach do that the supervisor structurally cannot'. Answer that first and the rest of the decision becomes straightforward.

There are four alternatives on the table and they are genuinely different products, not price points on the same product. The first is the supervisor you already have, whose time and permitted interventions are both capped by IB rules. The second is a subject tutor in whichever subject the essay is registered under, who knows the content but may have never supervised a 4,000-word research project. The third is an editing or polishing service, which is where families in a hurry lose both money and, occasionally, a diploma. The fourth is a process coach working over video, whose job is method rather than content.

The reason the choice matters more in this emirate than in Dubai is supply. Ras Al Khaimah's IB provision sits across a small number of campuses around Al Nakheel, Khuzam and Al Hamra Village, so a student registering an essay in, say, Psychology or Economics may be the only candidate in the school doing so. The supervisor allocated may be a willing teacher from an adjacent subject. That is not a criticism of the school; it is arithmetic. It is also precisely the gap a subject-matched coach fills.

The second reason is geography. In-home visits are quoted in this market at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors, and a specialist driving from Dubai to Al Dhait is pricing three hours of their evening into one paid hour. For a project that needs perhaps eight to twelve hours of guidance spread across nine months, the travel component is a large share of the bill and buys nothing that affects a single criterion.

Two things should be said plainly before the detail. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and home visits in the UAE are not a service we sell; our in-home offering exists only in India. And nobody here writes any part of an Extended Essay. A coach teaches the criteria, questions a research question, challenges a method and comments on the student's own draft. Any provider offering finished work is creating a malpractice finding for your child, not solving your problem. The sections below take the four alternatives one at a time, in the order a parent in this emirate usually meets them, and each one ends with the specific criteria it can and cannot reach.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-extended-essay-tuto.programmesIntro: The Extended Essay belongs to the Diploma Programme, but the research habits it assesses are built earlier. The notes below describe how each IB stage runs in Ras Al Khaimah and what it contributes to a 4,000-word project.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The Extended Essay is an independent 4,000-word research project registered in one subject, supervised rather than taught, and graded A to E. Its grade combines with the Theory of Knowledge grade on a matrix worth up to three diploma points, with a grade E in either acting as a failing condition.
programmes.countryNote: In Ras Al Khaimah a Diploma cohort is small enough that a student may be the only candidate registering an essay in their chosen subject. The school then allocates the closest available supervisor, which is reasonable and is also the structural reason subject-matched coaching is more valuable here than on a large Dubai campus with a specialist in every department.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, finishing with the Personal Project in MYP 5. That project is the first time most students define their own goal, keep a process journal and evaluate their own outcome — three habits the Extended Essay then assesses formally under criteria A and E.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Ras Al Khaimah campus offering the Diploma runs the Middle Years Programme beneath it, and some candidates arrive from Indian-curriculum or national-curriculum routes. Those students have usually never kept a research journal, which shows up immediately in the first reflection, and they need an extra few weeks at the start rather than extra help at the end.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry built around transdisciplinary themes, where students are expected from early on to say where a piece of information came from and why it can be trusted. The exhibition in the final primary year is a first, supported version of an independent inquiry with a presented outcome.
programmes.countryNote: Primary provision in Ras Al Khaimah spans British, Indian and IB World School campuses, and families move between them inside the emirate fairly often. A student who has changed system twice may be strong on content and unpractised at citing sources, which is a cheap gap to close at 11 and an expensive one at 17.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-extended-essay-tuto.subjectsIntro: The Extended Essay is registered in one subject, and the choice changes the method, the sources and the realistic ceiling. The notes below cover the subjects Ras Al Khaimah candidates most often register, with what each demands locally.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Rewards a question with a measurable variable and a method the student can actually run. The mangrove systems at Mina Al Arab and the wadi vegetation inland give genuine fieldwork options, but ethics and permissions have to be settled before data collection, not after.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Needs laboratory access and a question narrow enough to control. Essays registered here fail most often on scope: a student investigates a whole process rather than one variable, and criterion A loses marks for a question that no 4,000-word essay could answer.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Strong when a student can model something and then test the model. Weak when the essay becomes a literature review of a famous experiment. School equipment limits are a real constraint in a small emirate and should shape the question from week one.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A popular registration because local data is reachable: port activity, tourism, construction, the ceramics industry. The commonest failure is an essay that describes a market instead of applying theory to a specific, bounded question about it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Allows primary research with a named organisation, which is easier to arrange in Ras Al Khaimah than in a large city because local firms are approachable. Requires a clear framework rather than a company profile, and informed consent for any interview.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Attractive and risky. Ethical restrictions rule out most experiments a 17-year-old wants to run, so strong essays here are usually critical evaluations of existing studies with a sharply bounded question rather than new data collection.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The most reliable registration for a student who reads well. The National Museum of Ras Al Khaimah and the emirate's pearling, maritime and trading past offer questions with accessible primary and secondary material and a built-in local angle.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: No equipment and no permissions needed, which makes it the lowest-friction option in a small emirate. The difficulty is a question with a genuine critical argument rather than a theme-spotting exercise across two texts.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Rewards a student who can explain as well as compute. Essays registered here need mathematics beyond the syllabus, developed properly, and they lose marks when the writing becomes a sequence of results with no argument connecting them.

subjects.name: World Studies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary registration addressing an issue of global significance through two subjects. Demanding but well suited to a student whose question genuinely sits between two disciplines, such as coastal development and environmental systems in the northern emirates.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-extended-essay-tuto.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in Ras Al Khaimah affects session timing and, for an Extended Essay specifically, what research material and primary-data sites are realistically reachable. Both notes appear below.

regions.name: Al Nakheel
regions.note: The city centre, near government offices, the Chamber of Commerce and the older souq. Short school runs make a 4:30pm session workable, and the institutions here are the most approachable starting points for a business or economics interview.

regions.name: Khuzam
regions.note: Residential and close to several larger private campuses. A 5pm start is normal. Families here often have two children on different programmes, so an Extended Essay slot usually has to be held as a fixed weekly appointment rather than arranged week to week.

regions.name: Al Hamra Village

sections.heading: Alternative one: the supervisor you already have, and the three reflections that cap what they may say
paragraphs: The supervisor is free, assigned and bound. The IB expects a supervisor to give a few hours of support across the whole project, to hold three recorded reflection sessions with the student, and to read and comment on one complete draft. After that draft comment, the supervisor may not give further written feedback on the writing. That cap is deliberate: the Extended Essay is assessed partly on the student's independence, and a heavily shepherded essay would not test it.

The three reflection sessions are not administrative. They are recorded on the reflections form and assessed under criterion E, worth six of the 34 marks, with roughly 500 words of student reflection across the three. The first comes early and should show a question taking shape. The second, the interim, should show a method in motion and problems encountered. The third, the viva voce, comes after submission and should show the student talking honestly about what they learned and what they would do differently.

What this means in practice is that the supervisor's most valuable hours are at the start, and most students use them at the end. A supervisor asked in October whether a research question is answerable will say something genuinely useful. The same supervisor asked in February to fix a 4,000-word essay built on an unanswerable question has almost nothing left to offer, because the one permitted draft comment cannot repair criterion A retrospectively.

Before paying anyone, extract three things from the supervisor and write them down: the school's internal deadline for the complete draft, the dates of the three reflection sessions, and their honest view of whether the research question is answerable in 4,000 words. Those three facts are what a paid coach needs in order to be useful, and getting them costs nothing. One route to rule out: professional-ethics rules in some emirates bar school staff from paid private tuition of students at their own school, and the MoHRE tuition permit carries the same condition.

sections.heading: Alternative two: a subject tutor in the subject the essay is registered under
paragraphs: A subject tutor knows the content, and on some essays that is exactly what is missing. A Physics essay whose model is wrong, an Economics essay applying the wrong framework, a Mathematics essay whose proof does not hold: these are content failures and they are fixed by someone who knows the subject at Diploma level or beyond. In a small emirate where the supervisor allocated may teach an adjacent subject, this is a real gap and worth paying to close.

The limitation is that the Extended Essay is not primarily a content assessment. Criterion C, critical thinking, carries 12 of the 34 marks — more than a third — and it rewards argument, use of evidence and engagement with counter-positions rather than knowledge. Criterion A, focus and method, carries six and is about scope and approach. A tutor who teaches brilliant Physics and has never supervised a research project will improve the physics and leave half the mark scheme untouched.

The other limitation is habit. Subject tutoring is a teaching relationship: the tutor explains, the student follows. Extended Essay coaching has to be the opposite, because the essay must demonstrate the student's own independent work. A tutor who slips into teaching mode starts suggesting what the next paragraph should argue, and at that point the essay is drifting away from the student without anyone intending it. The best subject tutors on this work consciously hold back.

The sensible version of this alternative is narrow and short: two or three sessions on the subject-specific content where the essay is genuinely weak, with the method and argument work done elsewhere. That also keeps the cost sane. Published specialist rates in this market run AED 200 to 450 an hour and higher, and nobody needs twenty hours of that for a project the IB expects to take about 40 hours of student work in total.

sections.heading: Alternative three: an editing or polishing service, and why it is the most expensive option on this list
paragraphs: This is the alternative families reach for when the deadline is close, and it is the one that should be ruled out in every case. The market contains operations that will take a student's draft and return something better written. Some of them describe this as proofreading. Some will supply a finished essay outright; one such operation in this market publishes a price for completed internal assessments. What all of them are selling is a breach of IB academic honesty rules, dressed in the language of a service.

The consequence sits on the student, not on the provider. Work that is not the candidate's own is malpractice, and a malpractice finding on the Extended Essay can cost the Diploma rather than a grade. The supervisor authenticates the work and the student signs a declaration. The three reflections, which are assessed, are supposed to document a real process; a student who did not do the work has to misrepresent it there too, which makes the problem larger rather than smaller.

There is a narrower, legitimate version of the same instinct, and it is worth naming so families can tell the difference. A student may use a spellchecker. A student may ask a parent whether a sentence is clear. A student may be told their referencing is inconsistent and then fix it themselves. What nobody may do is restructure the essay, rewrite paragraphs, supply analysis or produce text that appears in the submission. The test is simple: did the words in the final document come out of the student?

If a provider's sales conversation is about turnaround time and word counts rather than about the research question, that tells you what you are being sold. Ask directly what they will return. 'Written feedback your child then acts on' is a coach. 'A polished version' is not. In a market where one ranking page is an essay mill with no FAQs and a published price for finished assessments, that question is the cheapest protection a parent has.

sections.heading: Alternative four: a process coach over video, and the five things a session can legitimately do
paragraphs: The fourth alternative is a coach whose subject is the project rather than the discipline. Their work is almost entirely questions, and the five legitimate moves are easy to list. First, test whether the research question is answerable in 4,000 words with sources the student can reach. Second, test whether the method follows from the question rather than being bolted on. Third, read the student's own writing and say where the argument does not hold. Fourth, itemise presentation and referencing failures for the student to fix. Fifth, keep the schedule honest against the school's dates.

None of those five involves producing text, and that is what makes the model safe to use alongside a school supervisor rather than in competition with it. It also makes it suited to video delivery: a shared screen with the student's own draft on it, the coach asking why a paragraph is there, the student annotating as they go. The session leaves a written note the student can show their supervisor, which is how external support stays declared and visible rather than hidden.

For a Ras Al Khaimah family the practical appeal is subject matching. A student registering an essay in Psychology or World Studies in a small cohort may be the only candidate doing so in the emirate. Online, the pool of coaches who have actually supervised essays in that subject is national or international rather than local, and the whole travel premium disappears. A specialist driving from Dubai to Al Hamra Village is charging for three hours of their evening to deliver one.

The honest limits are worth stating too. A process coach cannot rescue an essay in the final fortnight; criterion A is set by a question chosen months earlier. They cannot replace a supervisor, who holds the reflection sessions and authenticates the work. And they are not needed by every candidate: a student with a sharp question, a working method and a disciplined calendar may need nothing at all, and a free first session is the cheapest way to find that out.

sections.heading: Research in Ras Al Khaimah: what a student can actually get hold of
paragraphs: A research question is only as good as the sources behind it, and this is where location genuinely matters. A candidate in central London has a dozen research libraries within an hour. A candidate in Al Dhait does not, and an essay that depends on material the student cannot reach will fail criterion A regardless of how interesting the question is. The sequence that works is: question, then source check, then method. Students who do it in the other order lose a term.

What is actually available is more than families assume. Several universities operate in the emirate, including the American University of Ras Al Khaimah, RAK Medical and Health Sciences University and University of Stirling RAK, and school libraries can sometimes arrange reading access or journal access for a sixth-former with a clear request. The National Museum of Ras Al Khaimah holds material on the emirate's pearling, maritime and trading history that no other candidate's bibliography will contain.

For primary data the emirate is unusually good. The mangrove and wetland system at Mina Al Arab supports genuine ecological fieldwork. The abandoned village at Al Jazirah Al Hamra is a documented heritage site. Jebel Jais and the inland wadis offer altitude, geology and vegetation gradients. The ceramics and cement industries, the Al Marjan hotel economy and the port give Economics and Business candidates local, bounded, researchable questions rather than generic market studies.

Three cautions, because primary data is where good projects go wrong. Permissions and ethics come first: an interview needs informed consent, a protected site needs permission, and anything involving people under 18 needs a careful look at the school's own policy. Sample sizes have to be realistic for a project of about 40 hours. And no amount of interesting data rescues an essay whose question was never answerable, which is why the question block comes before the fieldwork block in every sensible plan.

sections.heading: What Extended Essay support costs, and what a parent can check in an afternoon
paragraphs: The most useful thing about Extended Essay pricing is that a parent can audit it themselves without trusting anybody's page, including this one. Ring three providers. Ask for Extended Essay support in a named subject for a candidate in Ras Al Khaimah. Ask for the hourly rate in dirhams, how many hours they think the project needs, what they will return after reading a draft, and whether their support would need to be declared to the school. Write down four answers each. The pattern that comes back is more informative than any rate table.

For reference, here is what this market publishes. Budget online tutoring runs roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject teacher online is about AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB tutoring sits at AED 200 to 450 or more, where TutorChase quotes AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table reaches AED 450 and above. Premium named tutors reach AED 650, as BartyED publishes.

In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors, and monthly packages advertised in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Set that against the project: the IB expects about 40 hours of student work in total. A provider proposing twenty paid hours of guidance on a 40-hour project is proposing something other than guidance.

Every figure above is a market rate attributed to whoever published it, not an IB Gram price list, and that distinction is worth insisting on from anyone you speak to. Three of six ranking pages researched in this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars rather than dirhams. Our own number comes from the consultation after a free first session, and a realistic Extended Essay engagement is usually a short block rather than a weekly commitment across nine months.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the upload, in a Ras Al Khaimah school year
paragraphs: A Diploma year in this emirate runs from late August or early September to late June, with a winter break in December, a spring break around March and Ramadan moving earlier each year. The Extended Essay typically starts in the second half of DP1 and is submitted in DP2, which sounds like a year of runway. It is not, because the usable weeks are shared with six subjects' internal assessments, Theory of Knowledge and mock examinations, and they clump.

The pattern of failure is consistent. A student chooses a question in spring of DP1, does nothing over the summer, returns in September with the question unchanged and unexamined, and starts serious work in November. By then the sources have not been checked, the method has not been tested, and the first reflection session has either not happened or happened without content. Everything after that is compressed into the same weeks as the internal assessment deadlines.

Counting backwards fixes it. Start from the school's internal deadline for the complete draft, not from the IB submission date. Subtract two weeks for the supervisor's one permitted draft comment and the student's response to it. Subtract six weeks for writing. Subtract six for data collection or reading. Subtract four for narrowing the question and checking that sources exist. That puts the honest start date in the spring or summer of DP1, which is earlier than almost any student believes.

Two local adjustments. The summer break is long and is the single best block of uninterrupted research time a candidate will get; a student who reads and narrows their question over it arrives in DP2 months ahead. And Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar slots rather than stopping, which preserves continuity families often write off in advance. Confirm every IB date with your school's Diploma coordinator, because the IB publishes and revises them and we do not restate them here.

sections.heading: The 4,000 words, the formatting, and the marks that leave for free
paragraphs: Four thousand words is a ceiling, not a target, and examiners stop reading at it. Everything after the limit is unmarked, which means a student who puts their best analysis in the final 300 words of a 4,300-word essay has given those marks away for nothing. The fix is structural: plan backwards from the limit, allocate words to sections before writing, and treat the conclusion as something that must exist rather than something that happens if there is room.

Criterion D, presentation, carries four marks and is the easiest block of marks in the Diploma to collect or to lose. It wants a title page, contents, consistent referencing, a bibliography, legible tables and figures with captions, and sensible use of appendices. Every one of those is a checklist item. Students lose marks here not through difficulty but through hurry, and a coach's most mechanical useful act is to itemise the failures and hand the list back for the student to fix themselves.

Referencing is the item that causes the most trouble, and the rule is less complicated than students fear: pick one recognised system, use it consistently, and cite everything that is not the student's own thought. Inconsistency costs presentation marks, and an uncited source is an honesty problem rather than a formatting one. Appendices are not a storage unit for material the essay needed; anything the argument depends on belongs in the body, inside the word count.

Worth stating in plain terms, because it is the question families ask last and should ask first: nobody at IB Gram writes any part of an Extended Essay, restructures one, or returns a rewritten version. A coach teaches the criteria, questions a research question, challenges a method, reads the student's own draft and gives written feedback the student then acts on. We will tell you if a request crosses that line, and we would rather lose the booking than put a diploma at risk.

process.title: Send the question and the school's dates
process.description: Before anything is booked, send the draft research question, the registered subject and the school's internal deadline and reflection-session dates. A coach cannot be useful without those dates, and asking the supervisor for them costs nothing and takes one email.

process.title: Free first session on the question itself
process.description: The first session costs nothing, takes no card details and is taught by the coach who would continue. It is spent testing whether the question is answerable in 4,000 words with sources the student can reach from Ras Al Khaimah. Sometimes the answer is that no further coaching is needed.

process.title: A short written plan with real dates in it
process.description: The coach counts backwards from the school's draft deadline and sets out what the next few sessions cover, in what order. The plan names your school's own dates, which is why we ask for them first rather than offering a generic nine-month schedule.

process.title: Sessions between the reflections, not instead of them
process.description: Coaching is timed to sit between the school's three reflection sessions so the supervisor's permitted draft comment is not wasted. A written note after each session goes to the parent and can be shown to the supervisor, which keeps external support declared.

process.title: One draft reading, then stop
process.description: The coach reads one complete draft and returns written comments on focus, argument, evidence and presentation. The student makes every change themselves. We say when the block has done its work instead of extending it through the spring.

whyPoints.title: The alternatives compared, not a straw man
whyPoints.description: This page sets the school supervisor, a subject tutor, an editing service and a process coach side by side against the actual 34 marks. Competitor pages in this market compare themselves to an unnamed 'other platforms'; a model-level comparison is more useful to a parent deciding.

whyPoints.title: Subject matching instead of local availability
whyPoints.description: A Ras Al Khaimah candidate registering an essay in Psychology or World Studies may be the only one in the emirate. Online coaching draws from people who have actually supervised essays in that subject rather than from whoever is within a 30-minute drive of Al Nakheel.

whyPoints.title: Rates in dirhams, each attributed to its source
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is a published market rate with the publisher named. Three of six ranking pages researched in this market publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: A stated honesty boundary, before you pay
whyPoints.description: A coach teaches, questions and comments on the student's own work. We do not write, restructure, polish or supply any part of an Extended Essay or its reflections. An operation in this market sells completed assessments; that is a malpractice risk sold as convenience.

whyPoints.title: Local research, not a generic bibliography
whyPoints.description: Mina Al Arab's mangroves, Al Jazirah Al Hamra, the National Museum, Jebel Jais and the emirate's industry give Ras Al Khaimah candidates bounded local questions. An essay built on material nobody else used reads differently to an examiner.

faqs.question: What exactly am I paying an Extended Essay tutor for when the school gives us a supervisor?
faqs.answer: For the things the supervisor is capped from doing. A supervisor gives a few hours across the whole project, holds three recorded reflection sessions and reads one complete draft. After that draft comment they may not give further written feedback. A paid coach adds subject matching where the school allocated the nearest available teacher, and adds hours at the start, which is where the question is narrowed and where the 12 marks of criterion C are won or lost. What they must never add is text. Get the school's dates from the supervisor first; that costs nothing.

faqs.question: How many times can my child's Extended Essay supervisor read a draft?
faqs.answer: Once. The IB allows the supervisor to read and comment on one complete draft, and after that comment no further written feedback on the writing is permitted. That makes the timing of the draft critical: a draft handed in too early wastes the comment on problems the student would have fixed anyway, and one handed in too late leaves no time to act on it. The three reflection sessions are separate from the draft reading and are assessed under criterion E, worth six of the 34 marks.

faqs.question: Is an Extended Essay proofreading service allowed under IB rules?
faqs.answer: Be careful with the word. A student may use a spellchecker, and may be told their referencing is inconsistent and then fix it themselves. What is not allowed is anybody restructuring the essay, rewriting paragraphs, supplying analysis or producing text that appears in the submission. The test is whether the words in the final document came out of the student. Operations in this market sell completed work; one publishes a price for finished internal assessments. A malpractice finding on the Extended Essay can cost the Diploma, not a grade.

faqs.question: Where can a Ras Al Khaimah student collect primary data for an Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: More places than families expect. The mangrove and wetland system at Mina Al Arab supports genuine ecological fieldwork. Al Jazirah Al Hamra is a documented heritage site. Jebel Jais and the inland wadis give geology and vegetation gradients. The ceramics industry, the Al Marjan hotel economy and the port give Economics and Business candidates bounded local questions. Settle permissions and ethics before collecting anything, keep the sample realistic for a project of about 40 hours, and check sources exist before committing to the question.

faqs.question: Which Extended Essay subject is easiest to score well in?
faqs.answer: There is no easy subject, only a better or worse fit for a particular student. English A and History are the lowest-friction registrations in a small emirate because they need no equipment and no permissions, and History in particular has strong local material through the National Museum of Ras Al Khaimah. Chemistry and Physics need laboratory access and tight scope. Psychology looks attractive and is constrained by ethics. Register where the student reads well and can describe a method they can actually carry out.

faqs.question: How much does Extended Essay help cost in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Market rates rather than ours: budget online tutoring runs roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified teacher online is about AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and BartyED publishing AED 650 at the premium end. Set any quote against the project: the IB expects about 40 hours of student work in total, so twenty paid hours of guidance is not guidance.

faqs.question: Does the Extended Essay really have to be exactly 4,000 words?
faqs.answer: It has to be no more than 4,000. The limit is a ceiling and examiners stop reading at it, so anything after the limit is unmarked. A student who puts their strongest analysis in the final 300 words of a 4,300-word essay has given those marks away. There is no minimum that rescues a thin essay either; a 2,800-word essay simply has less room to earn criterion C's 12 marks. Plan word allocations by section before writing, and treat the conclusion as compulsory rather than optional.

faqs.question: What are the five Extended Essay criteria worth?
faqs.answer: Thirty-four marks in total. Criterion A, focus and method, is six marks and covers the question, the scope and the approach. Criterion B, knowledge and understanding, is six and rewards accurate subject-specific knowledge in context. Criterion C, critical thinking, is twelve — more than a third of the essay — and rewards argument, evidence and engagement with counter-positions. Criterion D, presentation, is four and is a checklist. Criterion E, engagement, is six and comes from the three recorded reflections written by the student.

faqs.question: Can an Extended Essay coach work over video from outside the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a small emirate that is usually the point. A coaching session is a shared screen with the student's own draft on it, the coach asking why a paragraph is there and the student annotating as they go. Nothing needs to be physically in the room, and the session leaves a written note that can be shown to the supervisor so the support stays declared. It also removes the travel component that drives in-home quotes of AED 180 to 500 an hour in this market.

faqs.question: What happens if my child misses the school's Extended Essay draft deadline?
faqs.answer: The immediate loss is the supervisor's one permitted draft comment, which is the single most valuable piece of free feedback in the project. Schools set internal deadlines well ahead of the IB submission precisely so there is room to act on that comment, so a missed internal deadline usually compresses writing, revision and the final reflection into the same fortnight as subject internal assessments. Talk to the Diploma coordinator immediately rather than quietly working on. Confirm all IB dates through the school, since the IB sets and revises them.

faqs.question: Do Extended Essay tutors in Ras Al Khaimah need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Anyone giving private tuition in the UAE needs the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one brings fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. Ask for the permit reference before the first paid session, and note the permit answers a legal question rather than a competence one.

faqs.question: Should my son pick an Extended Essay subject he is taking at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Usually, but not automatically. Taking the subject at Higher Level means he already has the knowledge criterion B rewards and a teacher in the building who understands the discipline. The argument against is workload: an essay registered in the same subject as a demanding internal assessment puts two major pieces of work in one department's deadline window. The better question is where he reads well and can carry out a method. A student who writes strongly and registers in a laboratory subject without laboratory access has chosen badly whatever his level.

faqs.question: How are the Extended Essay reflections marked?
faqs.answer: They are the evidence for criterion E, engagement, worth six of the 34 marks, and they are written by the student across three recorded sessions with the supervisor — roughly 500 words in total. The first should show a question taking shape. The interim should show the method in motion, including a problem met and a decision taken. The viva voce, after submission, should be honest about what was learned and what would change. Reflections that read as a summary of the essay score poorly; ones that document real decisions score well.

faqs.question: What should I check before paying anyone for Extended Essay support?
faqs.answer: Four questions, asked in one phone call. What is your hourly rate in dirhams? How many hours do you think this project needs, against the roughly 40 hours of student work the IB expects? What exactly do you return after reading a draft? Would your support need to be declared to the school? A provider who talks about turnaround time and word counts is selling something other than coaching. 'Written feedback your child then acts on' is the answer you want; 'a polished version' is the one to walk away from.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-extended-essay-tuto.closingHeading: Start with the question, not with a provider
ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-extended-essay-tuto.closingBody: If you are weighing an IB DP Extended Essay tutor in Ras Al Khaimah against the supervisor your school has already assigned, the cheapest useful step is free: ask the supervisor for the internal draft deadline, the three reflection dates and an honest view on whether the research question is answerable in 4,000 words. Send those answers and the draft question, and the free first session will be spent testing the question against sources your child can actually reach from this emirate. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and your child writes every word of the essay.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level: the no-calculator paper, the Higher Level extension content, the problem-solving demands of Paper 3, and supervision of the exploration. Each profile names the courses taken, so a family weighing Analysis against Applications can ask about both in one conversation.

intro.heading: Analysis HL against the three courses you are also considering
paragraphs: A parent in Ras Al Khaimah reading this page is rarely asking a single question. They are asking whether their child should be in Analysis at Higher Level at all, given that Applications and Interpretation exists, that Standard Level exists, and that the school's maths department may be two or three people with one genuine Higher Level Analysis specialist among them. Choosing badly costs two years; choosing late costs a grade. So the comparison comes first and the tutoring comes second.

The four courses divide on two axes rather than one. The first axis is Analysis against Applications. Analysis and Approaches is built on algebraic fluency, proof and calculus, and it is the only pair of courses in which a student sits a paper with no calculator at all. Applications and Interpretation is built on modelling, statistics and the use of technology, and a graphic display calculator is permitted throughout. These are different subjects wearing similar names, and a student who is quick with a calculator and slow with algebra is often in the wrong one.

The second axis is Higher Level against Standard Level. Higher Level is a 240-hour course against 150 for Standard Level, and the extra ninety hours are not a gentle extension. Analysis HL adds proof by induction, complex numbers in Cartesian, polar and exponential form, vectors and three-dimensional geometry, differential equations and series approximations. Higher Level candidates also sit a third paper worth 55 marks in a single hour, which Standard Level candidates do not sit at all.

Ras Al Khaimah makes the decision harder than it would be in Dubai, and for a reason worth stating plainly. Private education in this emirate is regulated by its own Department of Knowledge, and the private-school set is comparatively small, concentrated around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab. Specialist Higher Level Analysis teaching is genuinely scarce locally. A family here cannot assume a second opinion is available within a short drive, which is precisely why remote one-to-one matters more here than it does further south.

What a tutor actually changes is narrower than most sales pages suggest. A tutor can rebuild algebraic technique for the no-calculator paper, teach the Higher Level extension topics properly rather than in a compressed final term, coach the unfamiliar-problem habits that Paper 3 requires, and read an exploration against the five criteria. A tutor cannot add ninety teaching hours that the school did not deliver, and cannot make Analysis HL the right course for a student whose interest is in data rather than proof. The sections below separate the two, starting with the four-way comparison, because a family that has not settled the course question is buying hours against a decision they have not yet made. Everything after that comparison assumes the course is the right one and the problem is delivery.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: Group five runs through every IB programme, and the step into Analysis at Higher Level is the steepest transition in the Diploma. What follows describes each stage by the gap it leaves, because the gap determines whether a student should be in this course and what the first term of tuition should address.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Middle Years mathematics is marked on criteria A to D, with investigating patterns and communication carrying real weight. Extended mathematics in the final years is the proper preparation for Analysis at Higher Level; standard mathematics generally is not. The missing habit is algebraic manipulation at speed without technology, which Middle Years assessment rarely demands.
programmes.countryNote: Ras Al Khaimah's Middle Years provision sits mainly with RAK Academy, and families here often ask us in the spring of the final Middle Years year whether Analysis HL is realistic. The honest test is twenty minutes of algebraic simplification with no calculator. If that is painful now, the no-calculator paper will be painful in two years, and Applications deserves a serious look.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level covers number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus, each extended well beyond Standard Level. Assessment is Paper 1 without a calculator at 110 marks, Paper 2 with a calculator at 110 marks, Paper 3 at 55 marks, and the exploration. Confirm the weightings against your school's copy of the subject guide.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma candidates are the audience for this page and nearly all sit the May session. In a Ras Al Khaimah school the practical risk is sequencing: the Higher Level extension topics are frequently timetabled into the final two terms, which is also when the exploration is due and the Extended Essay deadline lands. Pulling induction and complex numbers forward is the single most useful free change available.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Where a school runs the Career-related Programme, students take Diploma courses beside a career-related study. Analysis at Higher Level is an unusual choice inside it, because the hour demand is high and the reflective project competes for the same weeks. Applications at Standard Level is the far more common pairing and is often the better one.
programmes.countryNote: Career-related places in the northern emirates are limited, and families in Ras Al Khaimah considering it are generally weighing an engineering foundation route instead. Where a student does take Analysis at Higher Level within the programme, we plan the hours around the reflective project deadlines, which usually leaves January clearer than it would be for a full Diploma student.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: A mathematics Extended Essay is a demanding choice, because 4,000 words need a question that can be developed mathematically rather than a topic that can be described. Students attracted to that should usually put the energy into the exploration, which is assessed. Theory of Knowledge connects usefully to the course's work on proof and axioms.
programmes.countryNote: For a Ras Al Khaimah household the core is mainly a calendar problem. The exploration deadline, the Extended Essay interim submission and the first full mock tend to arrive within six weeks of each other in the second winter term. We book exploration supervision as separate dated hours so that a family can see which deadline each hour is buying.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: A Higher Level Analysis plan is built against topics, not against the subject. Below are the five topic areas with their Higher Level demands, the Higher Level extension content that most often arrives late, Paper 3, and the exploration. Identify which two are costing marks before agreeing to a weekly hour.

subjects.name: Topic 1: Number and algebra
subjects.description: Sequences and series, exponents and logarithms, the binomial theorem with any rational exponent, counting principles, proof by induction, contradiction and counterexample, partial fractions, and complex numbers in Cartesian, polar and exponential form. The single largest block of Higher Level extension content and the one most often compressed into a final term.

subjects.name: Topic 2: Functions
subjects.description: Function notation, composite and inverse functions, transformations, rational functions with oblique asymptotes, polynomial factor and remainder theorems, modulus functions, and solving inequalities analytically. Marks leak here through sketching: a Higher Level candidate who cannot sketch a rational function by hand loses Paper 1 marks they could certainly earn.

subjects.name: Topic 3: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Trigonometric identities and equations, compound and double angle formulae, reciprocal and inverse functions, and the Higher Level addition of vectors: scalar and vector products, lines and planes in three dimensions, and intersections. Vectors are the topic where Higher Level students most often believe they understand more than they can execute under time.

subjects.name: Topic 4: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Data presentation, regression, probability rules, discrete and continuous random variables, the binomial and normal distributions, and at Higher Level conditional probability, Bayes' theorem, expectation algebra and transformations of variables. Less content than in Applications, but what there is carries full Paper 2 marks and is often taught quickly.

subjects.name: Topic 5: Calculus
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration, the chain, product and quotient rules, implicit differentiation, related rates, optimisation, integration by substitution and by parts, volumes of revolution, differential equations including separable variables, Euler's method and slope fields, and Maclaurin series. The heart of the Higher Level course and the usual home of Paper 3.

subjects.name: Paper 1: no calculator, 110 marks
subjects.description: Short and extended response questions sat without any calculator. Exact values, surds, logarithm manipulation, differentiation by hand and algebraic rearrangement decide the mark. The defining feature of Analysis as against Applications, and the paper a student who has leaned on technology will find hardest to recover.

subjects.name: Paper 2: calculator permitted, 110 marks
subjects.description: The same content with a graphic display calculator available throughout. The skill assessed shifts from manipulation to selection: knowing when to solve graphically, when to use a statistical function, and how to show enough working that method marks survive even if the final value is wrong.

subjects.name: Paper 3: 55 marks in one hour
subjects.description: Two extended problem-solving questions that build from a stated idea towards a result, drawing across topics and often into unfamiliar territory. It cannot be revised topic by topic, which is exactly why students neglect it. Preparation means practising the habit of following a mathematical argument that is being constructed as you read.

subjects.name: The exploration
subjects.levels: All four maths courses, marked in school
subjects.description: An individual piece of mathematical writing worth 20 marks across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics. Supervision is feedback on the student's own work. A tutor does not write the exploration, choose its topic or supply its mathematics.

sections.heading: The four courses a Ras Al Khaimah parent is actually choosing between
paragraphs: Group five offers two courses at two levels, and the names do them no favours. Analysis and Approaches is a course about algebra, proof and calculus, in which one paper is sat with no calculator at all. Applications and Interpretation is a course about modelling, statistics and the intelligent use of technology, in which a graphic display calculator is available throughout. A student can be genuinely able at one and genuinely unsuited to the other, and the common error is to treat Analysis as the prestigious version of the same thing.

The level axis is separate. Higher Level is a 240-hour course and Standard Level is 150, and in Analysis the extra hours carry whole topics rather than deeper treatment of the same ones: induction, complex numbers, vectors in three dimensions, differential equations, series approximations. Higher Level candidates also sit a third paper, 55 marks in an hour, which no Standard Level candidate faces. Those are structural differences, not matters of pace.

For a family in this emirate there is a fourth consideration that rarely appears on a national page: whether the school can staff the course it has offered. Where a Higher Level Analysis class has three students and the teacher's own specialism is statistics, the risk is not the syllabus but the delivery. The table below compares all four courses on the axes that actually decide a grade, and the following sections take each alternative in turn, starting with the calculator rule.

sections.heading: The no-calculator paper is the real dividing line
paragraphs: If a family takes one thing from this page, it should be this. In Analysis, Paper 1 is sat without a calculator of any kind, and it carries 110 marks at Higher Level. Every exact value, every surd, every logarithmic rearrangement and every derivative has to be produced by hand. Applications candidates never face that paper. Two students with identical school reports can therefore have entirely different prospects in the two courses, and the difference is visible long before the Diploma starts.

The diagnostic is easy and costs nothing. Sit a student down with twenty minutes of algebraic simplification, logarithm manipulation and differentiation, with no device in the room. If the work is slow and error-prone, Analysis at Higher Level will be a two-year struggle against the largest single block of marks in the course. If it is slow but accurate, tuition can genuinely fix the speed. If it is quick and careless, that is a different and much cheaper problem.

What a weekly hour does here is specific and it works. Manipulation improves with volume and with marking that distinguishes a method error from an arithmetic slip. We take the calculator off the desk, work by hand for the whole hour, and mark in the session so that the student sees where a method mark was available and lost. Students who do this consistently for a term move on Paper 1 in a way they almost never do by revising topics from a textbook.

sections.heading: Alternative one: Analysis at Standard Level, and what it gives up
paragraphs: Standard Level Analysis keeps the character of the course and removes the extension topics. There is no induction, no complex numbers, no three-dimensional vector geometry, no differential equations and no Maclaurin series, and there is no Paper 3. Papers 1 and 2 are each 80 marks over an hour and a half rather than 110 over two hours. The exploration is identical, worth the same 20 marks against the same five criteria.

That makes Standard Level a genuinely good course rather than a consolation. A student who can handle algebra and calculus but has no appetite for proof will often produce a better Diploma total at Standard Level than a strained one at Higher Level, and will have evenings back for their other Higher Level subjects. The grade distribution argument matters too: a 6 at Standard Level is worth more to a Diploma total than a 4 at Higher Level, and considerably more to a student's confidence in the second year.

What Standard Level gives up is admissions reach into the most quantitative degrees, and that is where a family must do its own reading rather than trust a tutoring page. Engineering, mathematics, physics and some economics programmes commonly expect an analysis-based course at Higher Level, but requirements are set programme by programme and are revised. The honest instruction is to read the admissions page of each university your child is actually considering, and to ask the school's university counsellor to confirm it in writing.

sections.heading: Paper 3: 55 marks, one hour, and nothing to revise
paragraphs: Paper 3 is the component Higher Level candidates most reliably neglect, and the reason is structural rather than lazy. It consists of two extended problem-solving questions that build from a stated starting point towards a result, drawing across topics and frequently into territory the student has not met. There is no topic list to revise, no formula to memorise that opens it up, and no textbook chapter that corresponds to it. So it gets postponed in favour of things that can be revised.

The skill it tests is following a mathematical argument that is being constructed as you read, and contributing the next step. Parts (a) and (b) are usually accessible and set up the machinery; later parts require the student to carry that machinery somewhere new. Candidates who treat each part as an isolated question lose the thread and then lose the marks, even where every individual technique involved is one they can perform.

Preparation is therefore practice rather than teaching, which makes it ideal for a dated block in the term before a mock. One full Paper 3 question per session, attempted under time, then worked through with attention to where the argument was dropped rather than where the algebra failed. Students find this the most uncomfortable hour we sell and the most useful. In a Ras Al Khaimah school with a small Higher Level cohort, it is also the component least likely to have been practised in class, because a teacher with three Higher Level students and a full timetable has other calls on the lesson.
