sections.heading: Alternative two: Applications at Higher Level, and who it genuinely suits
paragraphs: Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is not an easier course and it is a different one. It is also 240 hours, it also carries a Paper 3 worth 55 marks, and its statistics content goes well beyond anything in Analysis. What it does not do is ask a student to work without technology, and its centre of gravity sits in modelling: fitting a function to data, interpreting what the model implies, and judging the model's limitations.

It suits a recognisable student. Someone who is strong with data, comfortable with a graphic display calculator, interested in how mathematics describes a real system, and slower at algebraic manipulation than their general ability would suggest. In our experience that student produces a markedly better grade in Applications at Higher Level than in Analysis at Higher Level, and enjoys the two years considerably more.

The decision cannot be made purely on fit, because it interacts with university plans, and this is the point at which a tutoring page must stop making claims. Programmes in engineering, mathematics and physics often specify which group five course they accept, and some specify a level; others treat the two as equivalent. Those requirements are published by each university and they change. Read them yourself on the institution's own admissions pages, and treat any tutoring provider that tells you the answer in general terms with caution, including this one. Record the wording and the date you read it, because a requirement quoted from memory a year later is worth nothing to an admissions office.

sections.heading: Alternative three: moving level, and the week it stops being possible
paragraphs: Families ask about dropping from Higher Level to Standard Level more often than about anything else on this page, and usually too late. The decision has an academic component and an administrative one, and the administrative one is the binding constraint. Schools set their own internal deadlines for level changes, and those deadlines exist because registration for the session has to be submitted and because a student moving down has to be fitted into a timetabled class that may be full.

Academically, the right moment to decide is the end of the first Diploma year, with two pieces of evidence: a Paper 1 style assessment sat without a calculator, and the student's own account of whether the extension topics are frightening or merely hard. A grade 3 in December of the first year is not by itself a reason to move; a grade 3 that is entirely built from Paper 2 marks, with Paper 1 near the floor, usually is. Those two profiles look identical on a report card and need opposite responses.

Practically, ask the Diploma coordinator for the school's own deadline now rather than in February, write it down, and work backwards from it. If tuition is going to be the alternative to moving down, it needs a term to show whether it is working, which means starting a term before that deadline rather than a fortnight before. sections.heading: University routes, and why the admissions page is the only source
paragraphs: This is the part of the decision where tutoring companies cause real harm, by publishing confident general statements about what universities require. Requirements are set per programme, published by each institution, and revised. A page that tells a family in Ras Al Khaimah that a particular course is 'required for engineering' without naming the programme and the year is guessing, and a family that acts on it may make a two-year decision on a sentence written for search engines.

The reliable method is unglamorous. List the programmes your child is actually considering, open each one's own admissions page, and record exactly what it says about group five mathematics: which course, which level, and what grade. Then ask the school's university counsellor to confirm it, and keep the written answer. Where your child is considering UAE institutions, that list typically includes names such as Khalifa University, United Arab Emirates University, the American University of Sharjah, the University of Sharjah, Zayed University and the international branch campuses in Dubai — each of which publishes its own entry requirements.

There is one related matter where the facts are published and worth knowing: the Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements for secondary certificates. For the British track, students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count of five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. No IB points threshold has been published in a source we have been able to read, so we publish none; verify any IB figure on the Ministry's own pages or with the emirate attestation authority.

sections.heading: The exploration: 20 marks that are identical in all four courses
paragraphs: Whichever of the four courses a student ends in, the exploration is the same instrument: an individual piece of mathematical writing worth 20 marks across five criteria — presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics. Use of mathematics carries the largest allocation, and at Higher Level it is judged against Higher Level expectations, which is the one place where the level genuinely changes the task.

The failures are predictable. A topic with no real mathematics in it cannot score on the largest criterion, however well written. Mathematical communication is lost through inconsistent notation, undefined variables and graphs without labelled axes, all of which are free to fix and routinely are not. Personal engagement is lost by students who choose a topic because it looked impressive rather than because they wanted to know the answer. Reflection is lost by students who summarise instead of evaluating what their mathematics actually showed.

Supervision is where a Ras Al Khaimah family gets the clearest value, because a small department often has one teacher reading every exploration in the cohort. An independent reader who has seen many of them can say whether the mathematics sits at Higher Level and whether the reflection is real. The boundary is firm: a tutor does not write the exploration, does not choose the topic and does not supply the mathematics. Our tutors ask questions, mark against the criteria and hand the pen back to the student who has to defend the work at moderation.

sections.heading: Specialist supply in this emirate, what it costs, and how lessons arrive
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah is the clearest case in the country for remote delivery, and supply rather than price is the reason. The private-school set is small and spread between the coastal communities and the inland districts, and a Higher Level Analysis class of three or four students is normal. The number of adults within a twenty-minute drive of Mina Al Arab who have taught induction, complex numbers and three-dimensional vector geometry to Higher Level is, realistically, very small.

Set against that, the published market figures are almost a side issue. Visiting tutors in the UAE are quoted at AED 180–500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150–300 online for a qualified subject teacher and AED 200–450 and above online for an IB specialist. EdFlik publishes from AED 45–65, Tutopiya from AED 33–52, Unitors lists IB subjects from AED 200, TutorChase quotes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650. Every figure belongs to the company that published it, read in October 2026. IB Gram publishes no hourly list; the free first lesson precedes any figure being agreed.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE — visiting tuition is a service we run only in India — and in this subject the online format carries a real advantage: the student works by hand on paper under a document camera or a tablet, the tutor marks the working as it appears, and the whole annotated attempt is saved. One legal point worth adding: an individual providing private lessons in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and asking about it costs nothing.

process.title: Send the course, the level and one no-calculator script
process.description: Which of the four group five courses your child is in, which level, and a recent assessment sat without a calculator. That third item is the one that tells us most. A report-card grade cannot distinguish a student who is slow at manipulation from one who cannot do it, and those need opposite plans.

process.title: Get an opinion on the course, not just the tutoring
process.description: Where the evidence says a student is in the wrong course, we say so before quoting hours. That advice has cost us bookings. It is also the single most valuable thing we can offer a family in the first Diploma year, because no amount of weekly tuition fixes a mismatch between a student and a calculator-free paper.

process.title: A free first lesson before any payment
process.description: A full session with the proposed tutor, at no charge. Ask them to teach one proof by induction and one three-dimensional vector question from scratch. Fifteen minutes of that distinguishes a Higher Level Analysis specialist from a general mathematics tutor more reliably than any profile.

process.title: Fix the block, the slot and the total
process.description: You see the figure, whether marking time is billed, and whether the quote includes tax. We confirm the Gulf Standard Time slot, the holiday pauses, post-Iftar timings during Ramadan, and what happens to hours you do not use. Nothing starts before that is written down.

process.title: Work by hand, mark in the session
process.description: Sessions run with the student writing on paper the tutor can see, so working is annotated as it appears and the whole attempt is saved. Method marks are named explicitly. A short written note after each session says what was covered and what the student owes before the next hour.

process.title: Reassess against the school's deadline
process.description: If a level change is on the table, we review progress against the school's own deadline rather than against the calendar year. A term of support with no movement on Paper 1 is evidence, and we will say so in time for the family to act on it rather than after the window closes.

whyPoints.title: The course choice is addressed before the tutoring
whyPoints.description: Four group five courses, two axes, one free diagnostic with no calculator in the room. We will tell a family that Applications or Standard Level is the better fit when the evidence says so, because selling two years of weekly hours against a structural mismatch is not a service.

whyPoints.title: Extension topics taught, not revised
whyPoints.description: Induction, complex numbers, vectors in three dimensions, differential equations and series approximations usually arrive late in a small department's timetable. We teach them properly and early where a family comes to us in the first year, which is the cheapest intervention available in this course.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 practised the only way that works
whyPoints.description: Fifty-five marks in an hour, no topic list, two constructed arguments to follow. We run one full timed question per session and review where the thread was dropped rather than where the algebra failed. It is the component least likely to have been practised in a small Higher Level class.

whyPoints.title: An independent reader for the exploration
whyPoints.description: Where one teacher reads every exploration in a cohort, a second opinion is genuinely hard to find in this emirate. Our tutors judge whether the mathematics sits at Higher Level and whether the reflection is real, then hand the pen back. They write nothing and choose nothing.

whyPoints.title: Admissions claims left to the admissions pages
whyPoints.description: We tell families to read each programme's own requirements and to get the school counsellor's confirmation in writing, because requirements are set per programme and revised. We publish no IB points threshold for Ministry equivalency, because no figure for it has been read on an official source.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the limits of an hour
whyPoints.description: A tutor cannot replace ninety teaching hours the school did not deliver, cannot make a calculator-free paper suit a student who needs technology, and cannot promise a grade. IB Gram holds no regulator approval, occupies no UAE premises and sends no tutor to a UAE address.

faqs.question: Should my child take Analysis HL or Applications HL in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Start with a diagnostic rather than a preference. Give them twenty minutes of algebraic simplification, logarithm manipulation and differentiation with no calculator in the room. Analysis makes students sit Paper 1 entirely without a calculator, worth 110 marks at Higher Level; Applications allows a graphic display calculator on every paper and centres on modelling and statistics. A student who is fluent by hand belongs in Analysis. One who is strong with data and slow with manipulation usually produces a better grade in Applications, and enjoys two years more. Then check each university programme's own published requirement before deciding.

faqs.question: What exactly is on the Higher Level Analysis paper sat without a calculator?
faqs.answer: The same five topic areas as the calculator paper, examined in a way that demands manipulation by hand: exact trigonometric values, surds, logarithm laws, algebraic rearrangement, differentiation and integration without technology, sketching rational functions, and the Higher Level extension content including induction and complex numbers. It carries 110 marks over two hours. The marks lost are rarely conceptual; they are arithmetic slips and method errors that a calculator would have hidden. Weekly practice with the calculator out of reach, marked in the session, is the only reliable repair we know.

faqs.question: How many teaching hours separate Analysis at Higher Level from Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Higher Level is a 240-hour course and Standard Level is 150, and the ninety-hour difference carries whole topics rather than deeper coverage of the same ones. Higher Level adds proof by induction, complex numbers in Cartesian, polar and exponential form, vectors and three-dimensional geometry, differential equations including Euler's method, and series approximations, and it adds a third paper worth 55 marks. Papers 1 and 2 are each 110 marks over two hours rather than 80 marks over ninety minutes. It is a structural difference rather than a matter of pace.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 and why can it not be revised topic by topic?
faqs.answer: Two extended problem-solving questions, 55 marks, one hour, sat only by Higher Level candidates. Each builds from a stated starting point towards a result, drawing across topics and often into unfamiliar territory, with early parts setting up machinery that later parts require. There is no topic list and no chapter that corresponds to it, which is exactly why students postpone it. The only preparation that works is one full timed question per session, reviewed for where the argument was dropped rather than where the algebra failed. Expect it to be uncomfortable.

faqs.question: My son is on a grade 3 in Analysis HL in December of year one. Move or stay?
faqs.answer: That grade alone does not decide it; the shape underneath it does. If his marks come almost entirely from the calculator paper with Paper 1 near the floor, the structural problem is manipulation by hand and a move to Standard Level or to Applications deserves serious thought. If he is slow but accurate and his errors are arithmetic, a term of weekly hand-practice usually moves him. Ask the coordinator for the school's own level-change deadline today, because the academic decision has to fit inside an administrative one that nobody reminds you about.

faqs.question: Which is actually harder, Analysis at Higher Level or Applications at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: They are hard in different directions, and treating Applications as the easier option is the most common mistake we see. Both are 240-hour courses and both carry a Paper 3 worth 55 marks. Analysis demands algebraic fluency without technology and formal proof. Applications demands statistical depth well beyond anything in Analysis, and a Paper 3 built on modelling that looks nothing like the Analysis version. The right question is not which is harder but which one your child's actual strengths survive, and a calculator-free diagnostic answers it in twenty minutes.

faqs.question: Do universities in the UAE insist on Analysis rather than Applications?
faqs.answer: Requirements are set programme by programme, published by each institution, and revised, so no tutoring page should tell you the answer in general terms. The reliable method is to list the programmes your child is considering, read each one's own admissions page, record exactly what it says about group five mathematics, and ask the school's university counsellor to confirm it in writing. Institutions a Ras Al Khaimah family commonly looks at — Khalifa University, United Arab Emirates University, the American University of Sharjah and the Dubai branch campuses among them — each publish their own entry requirements.

faqs.question: When is the last sensible week to drop from Higher Level to Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families assume, and the school sets the date rather than the IB. Registration for the session has to be submitted, and a student moving down must fit into a timetabled class that may be full, so coordinators set internal deadlines accordingly. Ask for that date now and write it down. If tuition is meant to be the alternative to moving, it needs a full term to produce evidence, which means starting a term before the deadline rather than a fortnight before it.

faqs.question: Is the exploration easier if my daughter moves down a level?
faqs.answer: The instrument is identical in all four group five courses: an individual piece of mathematical writing worth 20 marks across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. What changes is the standard applied to use of mathematics, which carries the largest allocation and is judged against the expectations of the level she is sitting. So a Standard Level exploration can use less advanced mathematics without penalty. The criteria, the pitfalls and the hours it needs are otherwise unchanged by a level move.

faqs.question: How scarce are Higher Level Analysis teachers in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Scarce enough that it should affect your planning. The emirate's private-school set is comparatively small and spread between the coastal communities around Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab and the inland districts, and a Higher Level Analysis class of three or four students is normal. A department of two or three teachers may contain one person who has taught induction, complex numbers and three-dimensional vectors to Higher Level. That is why families here buy a second explanation and an independent reader rather than general maths help, and why remote delivery matters more here than in Dubai.

faqs.question: What does the Department of Knowledge decide about my child's maths course?
faqs.answer: Private education in Ras Al Khaimah is regulated by its Department of Knowledge, and the emirate's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods — so curriculum approval, not only inspection, sits at emirate level here. What it does not do is choose which group five course your child sits or when a level change closes. Those are school decisions, taken by the Diploma coordinator within the IB's own rules. Ask the school, not the regulator, and ask early enough to act on the answer.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to an address in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; visiting tuition is a service we run only in India. Lessons for families here are delivered one-to-one over live video, and for Higher Level maths the format is a genuine advantage: the student writes by hand on paper the tutor can see, working is annotated as it appears, and the whole attempt is saved for review. The local visiting market does exist at a published AED 180–500 an hour including travel if having someone in the room matters more.

faqs.question: What does Higher Level maths support cost in this market?
faqs.answer: Published figures read in October 2026 run from AED 45–65 an hour at EdFlik's entry tier and AED 33–52 at Tutopiya's, through AED 150–300 for a qualified subject teacher online with Unitors listing IB subjects from AED 200, to AED 200–450 and above for an IB specialist, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650. Visiting tutors are published at AED 180–500 including travel. Those figures belong to the companies that published them. IB Gram publishes no hourly list of its own; the free first lesson comes before any number is agreed.

faqs.question: Where exactly does a tutor's help on the exploration have to stop?
faqs.answer: A tutor may ask whether a topic contains real mathematics, whether the mathematics sits at the right level, whether notation is consistent and defined, and whether the reflection evaluates rather than summarises. A tutor may read one full draft and leave questions in the margin. What a tutor must not do is write the exploration, choose the topic, or supply the mathematics, and our tutors do none of those things. Work produced by somebody else is a malpractice finding against the student, which puts the whole Diploma at risk rather than one grade.

faqs.question: Ras Al Khaimah is a small market. What if nobody covers Analysis at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: We say so instead of substituting a general mathematics tutor. This is the thinnest specialism we match for, and the contested hours are weekday evenings, which is when most families here are free. The realistic alternatives are a different evening, a weekend block for Paper 3 practice, or a wait of a week or two for the right person. If the match cannot be made at all we tell you, because an hour from someone who has never taught Maclaurin series or three-dimensional vectors is not cheaper than no hour.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level: the calculator-free paper, the calculator paper, and supervision of the exploration. Each profile names the courses taken and the terms they have availability in, which matters on this page because the plan is built around weeks rather than topics.

intro.heading: Two Diploma years of Standard Level Analysis, counted forwards
paragraphs: Parents rarely arrive at this page at the start. They arrive in November of the first year with a disappointing test, or in February of the second year with an exploration that has not been started, or six weeks before the papers with a grade 3 and a sinking feeling. Each of those is a different problem with a different number of weeks attached, and the first thing worth doing is locating the family on the calendar rather than reaching for an hourly rate.

The shape of the course is fixed and knowable. Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level is a 150-hour course across five topic areas: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. Assessment is Paper 1 at 80 marks over an hour and a half with no calculator, Paper 2 at 80 marks over an hour and a half with a graphic display calculator, and the exploration at 20 marks. Confirm the weightings against the copy of the subject guide your child's school holds before building a plan on them.

Spread across two years, those 150 hours are not evenly distributed in difficulty. The first term is algebra, and almost everything later rests on it, which is why a student who is shaky in October is still shaky in April unless somebody goes back. The second year front-loads calculus and then collides with the exploration deadline and the mock in a single winter term. The final stretch is revision, timed practice and nerves. A plan that treats all twenty-four months as equally worth paying for will spend most of the money in the wrong ones.

Ras Al Khaimah adds two practical facts to that calendar. Private education here is regulated by the emirate's own Department of Knowledge, whose authority covers approval of tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. And the private-school set is comparatively small, concentrated around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab, so a Standard Level Analysis class may be taught by a department of two or three people with limited capacity for a second explanation after school. Scarcity, not distance, is why remote one-to-one matters here.

What follows is the calendar, term by term, with the weeks a paid hour earns its fee marked clearly and the weeks it does not. There is also a section on why examination entries close months before a paper is sat, worked through with Cambridge's and Pearson's own published dates, because that is the deadline families miss most often and it is nobody's fault but it is also nobody's reminder. Lessons for Ras Al Khaimah students run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with working marked as it is written.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-tutor.programmesIntro: Group five runs through every IB programme, and families reach Standard Level Analysis from several directions. Each entry point below is described by the number of weeks it typically costs to settle, because that is the figure a timeline needs rather than a general description of the stage.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Middle Years mathematics is assessed on criteria A to D, and students who took the extended course arrive at Standard Level Analysis in reasonable shape. Those from the standard course usually need six to eight weeks of algebraic consolidation at the start of the first Diploma year, because Middle Years assessment rarely demands manipulation at speed without technology.
programmes.countryNote: Ras Al Khaimah's Middle Years provision sits mainly with RAK Academy. Families here most often ask us in the spring of the final Middle Years year whether Standard Level Analysis is the right landing place. For a student who enjoyed patterns and disliked proof, it usually is, and six weeks of algebra over the summer beforehand removes most of the first-term difficulty.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Standard Level course covers sequences and series, exponents and logarithms, the binomial theorem, functions and transformations, quadratics, trigonometry, probability and distributions, differentiation, integration, kinematics and optimisation. Two papers of 80 marks each and one exploration. There is no third paper and no Higher Level extension content.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma candidates are the audience for this page, and almost all sit the May session. The calendar fact that shapes a Ras Al Khaimah plan is the second winter term, when the exploration deadline, the Extended Essay interim submission and the full mock arrive within a few weeks of each other in households that may have a parent commuting to Dubai.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Where a school runs the Career-related Programme, Standard Level Analysis is a sensible Diploma course to take beside a career-related study, and candidates sit the same two papers and the same exploration. The reflective project replaces the Extended Essay, which moves the heaviest deadline weeks away from the exploration.
programmes.countryNote: Career-related places in the northern emirates are limited, and families in Ras Al Khaimah weighing it usually have a foundation or diploma route in mind as the alternative. The timeline advantage is real: with the reflective project falling elsewhere in the year, January is generally free, which makes it the best month to buy exploration supervision.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: The core does not add mathematics content but it takes the weeks a student would otherwise spend on it. Theory of Knowledge connects to the course through proof and the status of mathematical knowledge. The Extended Essay competes directly with the exploration for the same winter, and students who attempt both in mathematics usually regret it.
programmes.countryNote: For a Ras Al Khaimah household the core is a scheduling cost rather than an academic one. We quote exploration supervision as separate dated hours precisely so a family can see which deadline each hour is paying for, and we recommend fixing the exploration weeks in a calendar before the Extended Essay takes them.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-tutor.subjectsIntro: The five topic areas below are listed in the order most schools teach them, with the weeks each typically takes and the point at which falling behind becomes expensive. Use this to place your child on the timeline rather than to judge the whole course at once.

subjects.name: Topic 1: Number and algebra
subjects.description: Sequences and series, exponents and logarithms, and the binomial theorem for positive integer exponents. Usually six to eight weeks at the start of the first year, and the foundation everything later stands on. A student who leaves this term shaky will be shaky in calculus eighteen months on, which is why early hours are the cheapest hours in the course.

subjects.name: Topic 2: Functions
subjects.description: Function notation, domain and range, composite and inverse functions, graph transformations, quadratics and the discriminant, and rational functions. Marks are lost in sketching rather than in algebra: a student who cannot produce a labelled sketch by hand gives away Paper 1 marks that need no insight at all to earn.

subjects.name: Topic 3: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.levels: SL, first year or early second
subjects.description: Volumes and surface areas, radian measure, arc and sector, the sine and cosine rules, trigonometric identities, graphs of trigonometric functions and the solution of trigonometric equations. Exact values on the calculator-free paper are the recurring loss, and they respond to drilling rather than to teaching.

subjects.name: Topic 4: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Data presentation, measures of central tendency and spread, correlation and regression, probability rules, Venn and tree diagrams, discrete random variables, and the binomial and normal distributions. The most self-containable topic in the course, which makes it the best candidate for independent catch-up without paid hours.

subjects.name: Topic 5: Calculus
subjects.description: Limits and differentiation from first principles, the chain, product and quotient rules, tangents and normals, stationary points and optimisation, kinematics, and integration including definite integrals and areas. The heaviest topic in the Standard Level course and the one that arrives while the exploration is also due.

subjects.name: Paper 1: no calculator, 80 marks
subjects.description: Short and extended response questions with no calculator permitted. Exact values, surds, logarithm manipulation, by-hand differentiation and algebraic rearrangement decide it. This is the paper that separates Analysis from Applications, and the one where a student who has leaned on technology loses most.

subjects.name: Paper 2: calculator permitted, 80 marks
subjects.description: The same content with a graphic display calculator available. What is assessed shifts from manipulation to selection: knowing when to solve graphically, which statistical function to reach for, and how to show enough working that method marks survive an incorrect final answer.

subjects.name: The exploration
subjects.description: An individual piece of mathematical writing worth 20 marks across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. A tutor does not write the exploration, choose its topic or supply its mathematics; supervision is questions and criterion-based feedback on the student's own work.

subjects.name: The graphic display calculator
subjects.description: A skill in its own right and frequently untaught. Solving numerically, finding intersections, using distribution functions and reading a table of values all save minutes in Paper 2. Two sessions on the student's own machine, early in the second year, pay for themselves in the mock.

sections.heading: Where your child is standing now: four starting points
paragraphs: Every useful plan in this subject begins with an honest position, and there are only four of them. A student in the first term of the first Diploma year has the whole course ahead and the cheapest possible repairs available. A student in the first year with weak algebra has a real problem and eighteen months in which to solve it. A student in the second year who has not begun the exploration has a deadline rather than a learning gap. And a student eight weeks from the papers has a triage problem.

Those four need different purchases, and the mistake families make is reading them as degrees of the same thing. The first-year student with weak algebra needs volume and patience; a crash course would be wasted on them. The second-year student with no exploration needs four dated hours and a calendar, not a weekly subject slot. The student eight weeks out needs timed papers and method marks, and will not be rebuilt from the foundations in the time available, whatever anybody promises.

Locating yourself is free and takes one evening. Find the school's exploration deadline and mock week from the Diploma coordinator. Look at the last marked paper and check whether the marks came from the calculator paper, the calculator-free paper, or evenly. Ask the student which topic they would least like to be tested on tomorrow. Those three answers place a family in one of the four rows below, and the row determines the plan far more than the hourly rate does.

sections.heading: The 150 hours, mapped across two years
paragraphs: The subject guide recommends 150 teaching hours for Standard Level Analysis, and schools distribute them fairly consistently: roughly four lessons a fortnight across two academic years, with the exploration folded in rather than timetabled separately. Knowing the usual distribution lets a family see which term their child is in trouble during, and therefore whether the trouble is current content or an older gap resurfacing.

The pattern matters because difficulty is not spread evenly across those hours. Algebra comes first and is foundational. Functions and trigonometry follow and are mark-rich on the calculator-free paper. Statistics is the most self-contained topic and the easiest to catch up alone. Calculus is the heaviest and arrives in the second year, usually in the same term as the exploration deadline and the mock. A student who struggles in calculus is often not struggling with calculus; they are struggling with the algebra underneath it, eighteen months late.

The table below sets out a typical term-by-term distribution with the weeks a paid hour earns most. Two columns there are worth reading together: the term, and whether an hour bought in it compounds. An hour in year one term one compounds for eighteen months. An hour in the final fortnight compounds for nothing and simply converts into marks, which is a legitimate purchase and a much more expensive one per mark gained. Families who understand that one distinction spend less across the two years and see more movement, which is the whole argument of this page in a sentence.

sections.heading: Year one, term one: the term that decides year two
paragraphs: Almost every Standard Level Analysis problem we are asked to fix in the second year began in the first term of the first year. Indices, logarithm laws, algebraic rearrangement and the handling of surds are taught quickly, assessed once, and then assumed for the following eighteen months. A student who comes out of that term at seventy per cent comprehension has a quiet, compounding deficit that will surface as a calculus problem a year and a half later and be misdiagnosed as one.

The diagnostic in October is simple and a parent can run it. Ask the student to simplify a handful of index expressions, solve a logarithmic equation, rearrange a formula for a variable buried inside it, and complete the square, all without a calculator. If the work is slow and right, the gap is speed and will close with practice. If the work is confidently wrong, the gap is understanding and needs re-teaching now, while it costs six weeks instead of a year.

This is the point on the calendar where paid hours are cheapest in real terms. A term of weekly algebra in year one costs the same per hour as a term of panic in year two and buys perhaps five times as much. It is also the recommendation families are least likely to act on, because in October nothing has visibly gone wrong yet and the report card still looks survivable. We say it anyway, and the families who act on it rarely come back for the final-stretch block.

sections.heading: Year one, terms two and three: functions, trigonometry and the first exploration conversation
paragraphs: The middle of the first year is where the course becomes recognisably Diploma mathematics. Functions bring notation, domain and range, composite and inverse functions and transformations; quadratics bring the discriminant and completing the square; trigonometry brings radians, the sine and cosine rules, identities and equation solving. Each of these is heavily examined on the calculator-free paper, and each rewards hand sketching, which many students have never been required to do neatly.

The specific loss in this period is exact values. Standard Level candidates meet radian measure and the exact trigonometric ratios, and on Paper 1 they are expected to produce them without a device. Students who skip the drilling because the calculator paper forgives them lose the same marks every time for two years. Twenty minutes of exact-value practice a week during these two terms removes a predictable and entirely avoidable deficit.

The other thing that should happen in these terms costs nothing: the first exploration conversation. A student who spends the third term noticing mathematics in things they are actually interested in — a sport, a game, a pattern in something they measure — arrives at the second year with two or three candidate topics rather than a blank page in November. Schools often encourage this over the summer; most students ignore it; the ones who do not have a far easier winter. It costs nothing, it needs no tutor, and a parent can prompt it with a single question once a week during the third term.

sections.heading: The summer between the years: the only free gift in the Diploma
paragraphs: There is one block of weeks in the Diploma that costs nothing and is routinely wasted, and it is the summer between the first and second years. The student has finished roughly half the course, has a clear picture of which topics they are weak in, and faces no deadlines for several weeks. It is the only point at which a genuine repair can be made without anything else being sacrificed for it.

What to use it for is specific and short. First, the algebra from year one term one, if the October diagnostic was unflattering: three or four weeks at a relaxed pace, by hand, with no new content. Second, exact trigonometric values, which are pure drilling. Third, reading about two or three candidate exploration topics, far enough to know whether there is real mathematics in them. That is perhaps twenty hours of work spread across six weeks, and most of it needs no tutor at all.

Where a family does want paid hours over the summer, four to six is usually the right number, and they are worth more than the same hours in February. Families in Al Hamra Village and Al Marjan Island often travel during these weeks, which online delivery handles without a change of plan: the slot moves with the time zone and the sessions continue. We say honestly that most students do not need a tutor in the summer; they need six weeks of unglamorous practice and somebody to check it happened.

sections.heading: Year two, term one: calculus, the exploration and the collision
paragraphs: The second winter term is the hardest stretch of a Standard Level Analysis course, and the reason is collision rather than content. Calculus is being taught — differentiation rules, tangents and normals, stationary points, optimisation, kinematics and then integration — while the school's exploration deadline approaches, while the Extended Essay wants an interim submission, and while the full mock is scheduled. A household in Mina Al Arab with a parent commuting to Dubai has perhaps five usable weekday evenings a week to cover all of it.

The planning response is to separate the two purchases. Calculus support is content teaching and belongs in a weekly slot. Exploration supervision is a dated block of four to six fortnightly hours aimed at a specific school deadline. Families who fold both into one weekly hour end up doing whichever feels most urgent that week, which in practice means the exploration devours the calculus time in January and the calculus gap appears in the mock.

The date to build around is the school's own exploration deadline, not any date published nationally. Schools in this emirate set their own, and two students at different Ras Al Khaimah schools can be working five weeks apart. Ask the coordinator in September, write the date in a calendar, and count backwards: one hour for topic testing eight weeks out, one for the mathematics four weeks out, one full read two weeks out, and one for the final cut. That is four hours, placed deliberately, against a deadline that otherwise arrives as a surprise.

sections.heading: From the mock to the papers: the final stretch, week by week
paragraphs: After the mock, the remaining weeks have one job: converting what a student knows into marks on two specific papers. This is the only period in which a crash block is the right purchase, and it is the most expensive per mark gained, because nothing compounds any more. Market rates in this cluster also rise closer to a session as demand rises, which is a reason to book the block early rather than to assume it will be available.

The structure that works is dull and repeatable. One full paper per session, under time, alternating between the calculator-free paper and the calculator paper so that both habits stay live. Marked in the session rather than returned later, with every method mark named so the student learns where partial credit was available. Between sessions, the student reworks the questions they lost rather than starting fresh material. Two sessions a week in the final month is the maximum that produces anything; more than that and the student stops absorbing.

Equally important is what to abandon. A student eight weeks out with a grade 3 cannot rebuild number and algebra from scratch, and anyone promising otherwise is selling hours. What they can do is secure the marks in statistics, which is self-contained; make sure every exact value is known; drill calculator technique for Paper 2, where several minutes can be saved; and practise showing working so method marks survive. That is a realistic plan, and it is honest about the ceiling rather than silent about it.

sections.heading: Why the entry deadline sits months before the paper
paragraphs: This is the part of the calendar families miss, and it is not an academic matter at all. Examination entries close long before the papers are sat, because boards have to allocate centres, print and distribute material, and publish zone-specific timetables. Missing an entry deadline is not something tuition can repair, so the date belongs in the same calendar as the exploration deadline, and the person who holds it is the school's examinations officer.

Cambridge's published key dates show the shape clearly once you read them for the series a UAE candidate can actually sit, which means June or November rather than the February and March sitting Cambridge reserves for centres in India. For a June series the order is: final entries in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper and on a date the centre prints on the statement of entry; forecast grades on Cambridge's published deadline for that series; papers in June; results on Direct in August; certificates later in the year. Pearson puts hard numbers on the same lag from its own side - its November 2026 International GCSE papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and for the equivalent November 2025 series the grades did not reach students until 22 January 2026. Either way the entry closes a term or more before the first paper. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

Pearson's International GCSE series run in May or June and in November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is the only version worth relying on. For the IB itself we publish no session or results dates: the organisation's site blocks automated checking, so confirm every IB date with your child's Diploma coordinator and the IB's own pages rather than with any tutoring site, including this one.

sections.heading: Arranging the weeks: scarcity, cost and how an hour reaches Al Nakheel
paragraphs: Two practical constraints shape a plan in this emirate. The first is supply: the private-school set is small and spread between the coastal communities and the inland districts, and a maths department of two or three teachers has limited capacity for a second explanation after school. The second is the evening itself, since weekday hours after 6.30pm are the contested ones, and a plan that depends on a slot nobody can hold is not a plan.

On cost, the published market gives a family a frame rather than a quotation. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run about AED 240–600 at the budget tier, AED 600–1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000–2,000 and above for specialist support in an examination year. Hourly, EdFlik publishes from AED 45–65 and Tutopiya from AED 33–52; Unitors lists IB subjects from AED 200; TutorChase quotes AED 270; Bestimate puts the specialist band at AED 200–450 and above; BartyED sits at AED 650. Visiting tutors are published at AED 180–500 an hour with travel included. Those are their figures, read in October 2026, and IB Gram publishes no hourly list of its own.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE — visiting tuition is a service we run only in India — and for a course planned by the week the online format has a scheduling advantage that matters: a slot survives a family travelling, a school run that over-runs, and a parent arriving home from Dubai at seven. One further point: an individual providing private lessons in the UAE needs the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through MoHRE free of charge for two years, and it is a reasonable question to put to anybody before the first invoice.

The last thing worth saying about timing is what we do when the weeks do not work. If no Standard Level Analysis specialist is free in the slot a family can hold, we say so and offer a different evening, a weekend hour or a short wait. We do not fill a protected weekly slot with whoever is available, because in a course where the whole argument is about the right hour in the right term, the wrong tutor in the right slot still wastes the term.

process.title: Send two dates and one script
process.description: The school's exploration deadline, its mock week, and a recent marked paper. Those three place a family on the calendar, which decides the plan. We would rather have the two dates than a description of how the term has been going, because the dates are what the hours have to be built around.

process.title: Get a position, not a package
process.description: We say which of the four starting points your child is at and what that position actually needs, including when the answer is that paid hours are premature. A family in October of the first year is frequently told to run a free calculator-free diagnostic and come back if it goes badly.

process.title: A free first lesson before anything is charged
process.description: A full session with the proposed tutor at no cost. Ask them to teach one logarithm rearrangement and one optimisation question with no calculator in use, and to mark a short timed set live. That request separates a Diploma maths specialist from a general tutor quickly.

process.title: Fix the block against the calendar
process.description: Hours, weeks, figure, whether marking time is billed and whether the quote includes tax, plus the Gulf Standard Time slot, holiday pauses and post-Iftar timings in Ramadan. A block is dated to a school deadline rather than left open, and nothing begins until that is written down.

process.title: Work by hand, marked as it is written
process.description: The student writes on paper the tutor can see, so working is annotated as it appears and the whole attempt is saved. Method marks are named explicitly. A short written note after each session records what was covered and what the student owes before the next hour.

process.title: Review at the end of the block, not monthly
process.description: A block ends on its last session. We compare the next school assessment with the plan and propose another block only where the evidence supports one. Standard Level Analysis plans should get shorter as a student improves, and a plan that never shortens was a subscription.

whyPoints.title: Planned against the school's dates, not a generic calendar
whyPoints.description: Ras Al Khaimah schools set their own exploration deadlines and mock weeks, and two students in the same community can be five weeks apart. We ask for both dates before proposing hours, then count backwards from them, because a block aimed at the wrong week is wasted however good the teaching is.

whyPoints.title: We tell families when it is too early to pay
whyPoints.description: A student in October of the first Diploma year usually needs a free calculator-free diagnostic rather than a subscription. We say so. The hours that compound are in year one and the summer between the years, and most families are offered fewer hours than they came expecting to buy.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the ceiling in the final weeks
whyPoints.description: Eight weeks out, year one algebra cannot be rebuilt, and nobody should claim otherwise. What is reachable is statistics, exact values, calculator technique and working discipline for method marks. We name what is out of reach at the start of the block rather than at the end of it.

whyPoints.title: The exploration boundary is explicit
whyPoints.description: A tutor does not write the exploration, choose its topic or supply its mathematics. Our tutors test whether a topic contains real mathematics, check notation and graph labelling, judge the reflection against the criterion and hand the pen back. Completed coursework is sold in this market; the malpractice finding lands on the student.

whyPoints.title: A slot that survives a northern-emirates week
whyPoints.description: Late weekday hours for parents commuting from Dubai, weekend blocks for exploration work, post-Iftar timings during Ramadan at no surcharge, and a slot that moves with the time zone when a family travels in the summer. Sessions pause for school holidays without the slot being lost.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what we are not
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent matching platform with no approval, licence or endorsement from any education authority or examination board, no premises in the UAE, and no tutor sent to a UAE address. We publish no IB session dates and promise no grade, and every AED figure here names its source.

faqs.question: It is October of the first Diploma year. What should Standard Level Analysis look like by Christmas?
faqs.answer: By Christmas a student should be fluent, without a calculator, in indices, logarithm laws, rearranging a formula for a buried variable, completing the square and the basics of sequences and series. That is the term's content and the foundation for the next eighteen months. Run the diagnostic yourself: a handful of each, no device in the room. Slow but accurate means practice will close it. Confidently wrong means re-teaching now, when it costs six weeks instead of a year, and this is the cheapest point on the whole calendar to act.

faqs.question: My daughter is six marks off a 5 in every paper. How many weeks does that take to close?
faqs.answer: Usually a term, if the six marks are method and presentation rather than content. Look at where they are lost: unshown working that forfeited partial credit, exact values guessed on the calculator-free paper, sketches without labelled axes, or arithmetic slips under time. Each of those responds to eight to twelve weeks of weekly timed practice marked in the session. If instead the six marks are missing because a whole topic is absent, the figure is longer and the honest answer depends on which topic and how many weeks remain before the papers.

faqs.question: How are the 150 hours of Standard Level Analysis spread across the two years?
faqs.answer: Most schools run roughly four lessons a fortnight across two academic years. Typically number and algebra comes in the first term, functions and quadratics in the second, trigonometry in the third, calculus in the first term of year two, and statistics with the completion of integration in the second, followed by revision. The exploration is folded in rather than timetabled separately. Ask your school for its own scheme of work, because the order affects the plan: a student struggling in calculus is often struggling with first-term algebra, eighteen months late.

faqs.question: Is the summer between the two Diploma years worth using for maths?
faqs.answer: It is the only block of weeks in the Diploma with no competing deadlines, and most families waste it. Use it for three things: rebuilding year one algebra if the October diagnostic was unflattering, drilling exact trigonometric values, and reading far enough into two or three exploration topics to know whether real mathematics lives in them. That is about twenty hours across six weeks and most of it needs no tutor. Where paid hours help, four to six are usually enough, and online delivery means the slot travels with the family.

faqs.question: When should my son choose his exploration topic?
faqs.answer: Ideas should start in the third term of the first year and the choice should be made early in the second. The school sets the deadline, not the IB, and schools in this emirate set their own, so ask the Diploma coordinator in September and write the date down. Then count backwards: one hour testing whether the topic contains real mathematics about eight weeks out, one on the mathematics four weeks out, one full read two weeks out, and one for the final cut. Four deliberate hours beat a term of vague weekly contact.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the mock should we start tutoring?
faqs.answer: If the aim is to change the mock result, ten to twelve weeks, with one full paper per session under time. If the aim is to change the final grade, the honest answer is earlier than that and in a different shape: a term of weekly algebra in year one does more than twice as many hours bought in the final stretch. A crash block has its place and it is the most expensive purchase per mark gained, because nothing compounds any more. Book it early in any case, since rates in this cluster rise closer to a session.

faqs.question: Why does the examination entry deadline fall months before the paper is sat?
faqs.answer: Because boards have to allocate centres, print and distribute material and publish zone-specific timetables. Cambridge's own key dates make the gap plain for the series available here. A June sitting has its papers in June, its final entries in the spring roughly four months earlier, and its results on Direct in August; a November sitting shifts the whole sequence, with grades landing in the new year. Pearson's documented November 2025 International GCSE results, which reached students on 22 January 2026, show how long that tail can be. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct zone timetable must be used. Missing an entry is not something tuition can repair, so the date belongs with your school's examinations officer and in your own calendar.

faqs.question: Which session do Ras Al Khaimah students sit, and where do I confirm the dates?
faqs.answer: Almost all IB candidates in this emirate sit the May session, with November available in some circumstances. We deliberately publish no IB session or results dates on this page: the organisation's site blocks automated checking, so any date we printed would be second-hand. Confirm every IB date with your child's Diploma coordinator and against the IB's own pages. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications the boards publish their own timetables and key dates, and the live official timetable is the only version worth planning against, since provisional ones are revised.

faqs.question: Can sessions move to later timings during Ramadan in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we agree the change in advance rather than week by week. Post-Iftar slots are standard during Ramadan and carry no surcharge. In practice families here either move the hour later or convert two weekday hours into one longer weekend session, and both work for Standard Level maths as long as the slot is protected. What we try to avoid is scheduling algebra practice very late at night, because tired manipulation teaches habits that then need unlearning in the following term.

faqs.question: We are arriving in Ras Al Khaimah mid-year. How much maths time does a school change cost?
faqs.answer: Usually four to six weeks, and the cause is teaching order rather than content. The syllabus is the same everywhere, but one school may have finished trigonometry and barely started calculus while the next has done the reverse, so a transferring student arrives with a gap in the middle of a topic rather than at the end of one. A single diagnostic hour identifies the gap precisely, then four to six weeks of targeted work closes it. Starting again from the beginning of the syllabus is the expensive mistake here.

faqs.question: Is one hour a week enough for Standard Level Analysis?
faqs.answer: For most students, yes, provided it is in the right term and the student works between sessions. One protected hour a week through year one, with short timed sets in between, outperforms two hours a week bought in the final month. Two hours a week is justified in two situations: the second winter term when calculus and the exploration collide, and the final month of timed practice. Beyond two hours a week, students stop absorbing, and we would rather say that than sell a third hour that produces nothing.

faqs.question: After a month of weekly hours, what should the marked work be showing?
faqs.answer: Three things, in this order. Working that is now laid out well enough for method marks to survive a wrong final answer. Errors that have shifted from method to arithmetic, which is real progress even when the total has not moved much. And a visible change in the calculator-free paper specifically, since that is where the deficits live. If none of those three has appeared after four sessions, the plan is wrong rather than the student, and we would say so and change it rather than ask for another month.

faqs.question: Does a Standard Level maths tutor need a permit to charge us in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes. An individual providing private lessons needs the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation free of charge for two years. The MoHRE service is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing, with a two-working-day completion time and no published fee. Registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18 may apply. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram arrange a Standard Level maths tutor to teach at a Ras Al Khaimah address?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; visiting tuition is a service we run only in India. Lessons here run one-to-one over live video, and for a plan built around weeks that format has a scheduling advantage: the slot survives a family travelling in the summer, a school run that over-runs, and a parent getting home from Dubai at seven. The local visiting market does exist at a published AED 180–500 an hour including travel if having someone in the room matters more than keeping the slot.

faqs.question: It is eight weeks to the papers and my son is on a grade 3. What is realistic?
faqs.answer: Realistic is securing what is still reachable and being honest about the rest. Statistics is self-contained and can be banked. Exact values are pure drilling. Calculator technique for Paper 2 saves real minutes. Working discipline protects method marks on questions he cannot finish. That combination moves grades. What is not reachable in eight weeks is rebuilding first-term algebra from the foundations, and anyone who tells you otherwise is selling hours. We would plan for one full paper per session, marked live, twice a week at most.

Every match opens with a free first lesson on the topic your child cannot currently finish, so you judge teaching rather than a profile.

intro.heading: Start with the date, then work out what the weeks have to carry
paragraphs: A parent in Ras Al Khaimah rarely calls about mathematics in the abstract. The call comes with a deadline attached. The DP1 report has arrived and Applications and Interpretation is two grades below everything else. The exploration draft is due in four weeks and there is no topic. A conditional offer has arrived asking for a 5 in a Higher Level mathematics subject and the current predicted grade is a 4. Each of those is a different problem with a different number of weeks in it, and the first thing a tutor should do is name which one you are in.

That matters more here than in Dubai. Ras Al Khaimah runs a compact private-school set regulated by its own Department of Knowledge, and the Diploma cohorts inside it are small. A year group of thirty Diploma students may send only a handful into Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, and the teacher carrying that class is often carrying Analysis and Approaches, Standard Level and a Middle Years group as well. Nothing about that is negligent. It is arithmetic. One teacher cannot give six hours a week to the five students who sit the hardest version of the course.

So the support usually has to come from outside the emirate, and the honest question is not whether a specialist lives near Al Nakheel but whether a specialist can be in the room at 5pm on a Tuesday. Over live video they can. The tutor your child works with is selected because they teach AI at Higher Level, know what Paper 3 asks for, and have marked explorations against the published criteria. Geography stops filtering the list of people allowed to teach your child.

The structure of the course is what makes the timeline tight. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level runs to 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, and the extra ninety hours are not revision. They are new content: matrices and eigenvalues, graph theory, complex numbers used as a modelling tool, non-linear regression, hypothesis testing, differential equations approached numerically. A student who arrives in DP2 having quietly skipped two of those blocks is not behind on practice. They are missing syllabus, and that is a different repair job.

Then there is the exploration, worth 20% of the final grade and marked out of 20. It is the one component where a parent can see progress week by week, and the one most often left until the school's internal deadline makes the choice for the student. A plan that puts the exploration in the right ten weeks of DP1 removes the single biggest source of DP2 panic. A plan that does not will cost you more hours later, at a worse time of year.

What follows is the whole of it: the five topics and what Higher Level adds, how each paper is weighted and timed, what Paper 3 actually demands, the exploration criterion by criterion with dates against it, thirty weeks counted backwards from a May session, what the UAE market charges by the month, and how online one-to-one compares with the alternatives from a Ras Al Khaimah address.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-math-ai-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level sits at the end of a path that usually starts in the Middle Years Programme. These are the IB programmes Ras Al Khaimah families ask about most, and what each one means for a student heading towards AI HL.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria rather than papers, and the standard and extended routes split in MYP 4 and 5. Students who take the standard route and then choose Higher Level mathematics in the Diploma usually arrive short on algebraic fluency rather than short on ideas. The gap is closable, but it has to be identified in the spring of MYP 5, not in the autumn of DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Several Ras Al Khaimah campuses run MYP through to Year 11 before the Diploma begins, so the MYP 5 mathematics result is the best early signal a parent has about whether AI at Higher Level is realistic. A student finishing on criterion A scores of 5 or 6 is better placed in Standard Level unless the summer is used properly.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Every Diploma student takes one mathematics course, and the four options are AA or AI at Standard or Higher Level. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is the statistics-and-modelling route taken seriously: three written papers, a technology-permitted exam in every sitting, and an exploration. It is assessed over two years with the exploration submitted in DP2.
programmes.countryNote: Ras Al Khaimah Diploma cohorts are small enough that a school may offer AI only at Standard Level, or run Higher Level as a timetabled group of three or four. Families in that position often need outside teaching not because the school is weak but because the group is too small to carry a dedicated specialist.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs two or more Diploma courses with a career-related study, and mathematics is a common choice inside it. A CP student taking AI sits the same papers as a full Diploma student in that subject, so the teaching requirement is identical even though the overall award is different.
programmes.countryNote: CP is less common across the northern emirates than the full Diploma, but where a Ras Al Khaimah school offers it, the mathematics component is usually AI rather than AA because the applied statistics content maps onto business, engineering and hospitality pathways families here are already looking at.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-math-ai-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: AI at Higher Level is rarely the only pressure point in a Diploma timetable. These are the subjects Ras Al Khaimah families most often add alongside it, with what each one actually assesses.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-permitted problem solving across five topics. At Higher Level the course adds matrices, graph theory, complex numbers as a modelling tool and numerical approaches to differential equations, plus a third written paper built entirely from extended problem solving.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof-and-algebra route. Paper 1 is sat without technology, which is the single biggest practical difference from AI. Students transferring between the two courses in DP1 usually find the calculus comparable and the algebraic manipulation a step up.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Themes A to E, with Paper 1A multiple choice and Paper 1B data analysis sat together. Physics HL leans on the same graph-reading and uncertainty work as AI statistics, so pairing the two tutors' diagnostics often saves hours.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure 1 to 3 and Reactivity 1 to 3, with a data booklet supplied in the exam. The quantitative sections reward exactly the calculator discipline AI builds, and the scientific investigation runs on a similar DP1 timeline to the exploration.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Four themes crossed with four levels of biological organisation. The statistics embedded in the course, standard deviation, error bars and significance testing, is the part AI students handle most comfortably and non-mathematicians handle least.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, with an HL-only third paper asking for a costed policy recommendation. The quantitative element of Paper 3 draws on the same elasticity and index-number arithmetic AI students meet in statistics.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Five units and four concepts, with Paper 1 built on a case study released before the exam. The finance and accounts unit is where AI students have a real advantage, and where students without a strong mathematics course lose marks steadily.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Algorithms, data structures and system fundamentals, with an HL extension into resource management and abstract data types. Graph theory in AI HL and graph traversal in Computer Science cover overlapping ground, which is worth telling both tutors.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two written papers, an individual oral and, at Higher Level, an essay on a studied text. Mathematics students often lose marks here on the structure of an argument rather than on reading, which responds quickly to one-to-one work.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects and a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title. Mathematics is one of TOK's standing areas of knowledge, so an AI HL student usually has more to say about proof, modelling and certainty than they realise.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay. A mathematics EE is a genuine option for an AI HL student but a demanding one, and the supervision question is where the academic-honesty line matters most.

sections.heading: Where an AI Higher Level student in this emirate usually is when a parent first calls
paragraphs: There are four starting points, and they need different plans. The first is the DP1 student who was comfortable in MYP mathematics and has hit the modelling content with no idea how to begin a question that does not tell them which method to use. They are not weak. They have never been asked to choose a model before, and nothing in a Middle Years assessment prepares a student for a question that opens with a table of real data and no instruction.

The second is the student who chose Higher Level because the subject combination demanded it and is now carrying a course designed for 240 teaching hours inside a timetable that gives it less. These students usually present as disorganised rather than behind, and the diagnostic nearly always finds two or three HL-only blocks that were covered in a week each. Matrices and graph theory are the usual casualties, because they sit late in most schemes of work and have no Standard Level equivalent to fall back on.

The third is the DP2 student six months from a May session with an exploration still unsubmitted and a predicted grade that will not meet a conditional offer. That is the hardest brief, and the honest version of it involves triage: the exploration first, because it is 20% of the grade and entirely inside the student's control, then Paper 3 technique, then the topics where the error log says marks are actually being dropped. The fourth is a student who is coping and whose parent wants the gap between a 5 and a 6 closed. That is the cheapest brief of the four and the one families leave until it has become one of the other three.

sections.heading: The five topics, and what Higher Level adds that Standard Level never sees
paragraphs: Applications and Interpretation is organised into five topics, and the same five appear at both levels. The difference is not that Higher Level goes faster. It is that each topic carries additional content that Standard Level students simply do not meet, and the ninety extra teaching hours are spent there. A parent reading a DP1 report that says 'coping well with the course' should know which blocks have actually been taught before concluding that the course is under control.

Two of those additions cause most of the trouble in small cohorts. Graph theory arrives with vocabulary a student has never seen, adjacency matrices, minimum spanning trees, routing problems, and it is examinable in full. Matrices arrive with eigenvalues and transformations, and they underpin the Markov chain work that appears later. Both sit near the end of a two-year scheme of work, which means they get taught in the term when mock exams, the exploration deadline and the Extended Essay are all competing for the same weeks.

The table below sets out the five topics with the Higher Level additions named, so you can ask your child's teacher a specific question rather than a general one. 'Have you finished graph theory?' gets a useful answer. 'Is everything on track?' does not. It is also the document a tutor should work from in the first month, because a diagnostic that tests all five topics evenly wastes sessions on content the student has already met. The point of naming the additions is to find out which of them exist only as a title in a folder, and to teach those first while there are still weeks available to do it properly rather than in summary.

sections.heading: How Applications and Interpretation HL is marked, paper by paper
paragraphs: Higher Level AI is assessed by three written papers and one piece of internally assessed coursework. Paper 1 and Paper 2 each carry 30% of the final grade, Paper 3 carries 20%, and the exploration carries the remaining 20%. Every paper in AI permits a graphic display calculator, which is the structural difference from Analysis and Approaches, where Paper 1 is sat without technology. It also means calculator fluency is not a convenience in this course. It is examined content.

The weightings matter for how hours are allocated. A student who is five marks off a grade boundary gains more from twenty concentrated hours on Paper 3 and the exploration, together 40% of the grade, than from another pass through the Paper 2 topics they already half know. Most families arrive having spent their hours the other way round, because Paper 2 is the paper the school sets most often in mocks.

Standard Level sits the same first two papers at shorter length and with lower mark totals, and sits no Paper 3 at all. That single difference is why a mid-DP1 move from Higher to Standard Level is a real option in this course and why it has to be decided early: the Paper 3 preparation a Higher Level student needs is a block of work on its own, and dropping it late wastes the teaching already spent on it. The other practical consequence of the weightings is how a mock result should be read. A school that reports one overall mock grade hides which paper produced the loss, and a parent who asks for the breakdown by paper gets a far more useful number to plan against.
