sections.heading: Paper 3 is a different exam, and it is where the timeline usually breaks
paragraphs: Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level and it is one hour long for 20% of the grade. It contains two compulsory extended-response problems, each one building through its parts so that a wrong turn in part (b) can cost marks in parts (d) and (e). Nothing about the content is new; everything about the format is. A student who has only ever practised Paper 1 and Paper 2 questions has never been asked to hold a single problem in their head for twenty-five minutes.

The failure mode is predictable. Students spend too long on the opening parts, which are usually accessible, and arrive at the later parts with eight minutes and a half-built model. Or they treat each part as independent, re-deriving something already established, and run out of time. Neither is a knowledge problem. Both respond to practice under the clock with the pacing made explicit: a target time per part, written on the script, checked against the clock.

This is also the component a small cohort is least likely to have drilled. A teacher with four Higher Level students and a Standard Level group in the same room will set Paper 1 and Paper 2 questions because they work for everyone. Paper 3 practice has to be set separately, marked separately and discussed separately, and in a timetable under pressure it is the first thing to be deferred. A tutor working one-to-one can make it the explicit focus of six sessions and nothing else, which is usually what moves the grade.

sections.heading: The exploration, criterion by criterion, with the dates a DP1 student should be holding
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria and is worth a fifth of the final grade. The recommended length is 12 to 20 pages, and the examiner is not looking for difficulty for its own sake. Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries six marks and rewards mathematics that is correct, relevant and commensurate with the level of the course. A Higher Level exploration built on Standard Level content loses marks there however neatly it is presented.

The two criteria students most often throw away are C and D. Personal engagement carries three marks and is earned by evidence that the student actually did something: collected their own data, asked their own question, tested something they wanted to know. Reflection carries three marks and is earned by commentary on what the mathematics showed and what its limits were, not by a closing paragraph saying the investigation was interesting. Both are cheap marks that cost nothing but attention, and both are the first casualties of a draft written in a weekend.

The dates in the table below are the ones that keep an exploration out of the DP2 crisis window. They are not an IB deadline, which is set internally by your child's school and varies, so confirm the school's own dates with the Diploma coordinator. They are a working schedule that has the exploration finished before the mock exam term arrives. Working to them has a second benefit a parent can see directly: an exploration developed over ten weeks produces reflection that was written while the work was happening, which is where criterion D marks come from. An exploration written in a weekend produces reflection invented afterwards, and examiners read the difference without difficulty.

sections.heading: Thirty weeks, counted backwards from a May session
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May session, so a DP2 student's working year runs from an August or September start to an exam window in the second quarter. Counting backwards from the exams rather than forwards from the start of term is what turns a vague plan into a schedule, and it is the one thing a parent can hold a tutor to. Each row below names what should be finished, not what should be in progress.

The specific IB session and results dates for your child's year should come from the school's Diploma coordinator or from ibo.org directly, and should be checked rather than assumed; dates for a given session are confirmed by the IB and can be revised. What does not change is the shape of the year: coursework and internal deadlines sit in the first half, mock exams sit in the middle, and the final weeks are for timing and technique rather than for new content.

The practical use of this table is to find the row you are currently in and look at the one above it. If the row above describes work that has not happened, that is the gap the first month of tutoring needs to close, and it should change what the sessions cover. Two rows deserve particular attention in a small cohort. The 25 to 20 week row assumes the Higher Level additions are being taught rather than revised, which in a compressed scheme of work is frequently untrue. The 13 to 9 week row assumes mock scripts have come back marked by paper, which is the evidence any sensible plan for the last three months is built on.

sections.heading: What AI Higher Level support costs a Ras Al Khaimah family, by the month
paragraphs: Parents budget monthly, not hourly, so this starts with the monthly number. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month with a budget tutor, AED 600 to 1,200 with a mid-range qualified tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more a month for specialist exam-year support. Packaged plans circulating in the UAE market sit around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are market figures from published sources, not an IB Gram price list.

Convert them back to an hourly figure and the market bands become clear. Budget online tutoring runs roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online sits around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An IB specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with TutorChase listing AED 270. An in-home visit including travel is quoted at AED 180 to 500. The market's top tier reaches AED 650 an hour, published by BartyED.

Three things move a Higher Level AI figure inside those bands. Level is the first: Higher Level commands more than Standard Level because the content is wider and the tutor pool is narrower. Timing is the second: a three-week block before the exams costs more per hour than a plan started in DP1, and the hours needed are usually greater. The third is the exploration, which is quoted either as part of a weekly plan or as a separate short block, and which families routinely forget to budget for until the school deadline is four weeks away. IB Gram's own model is to start with a free first lesson and agree a plan after it, rather than to publish a rate card against a subject neither side has diagnosed yet.

paragraphs: Home tutoring is a real market in this emirate and the question deserves a real answer. A tutor who drives to Al Hamra Village or Al Nakheel is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour in the UAE market, and that range includes travel. What the travel premium buys is presence in the room. What it costs is twofold: the money itself, and the fact that the tutor pool shrinks to whoever is willing to make the journey on a weeknight.

In Ras Al Khaimah that second cost is the decisive one for a Higher Level AI student. The emirate has a small Diploma teaching population, and a subject as specific as Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, with graph theory, Markov chains and Paper 3, is not something a general mathematics tutor can pick up between appointments. A family trading a specialist for proximity is usually trading away the thing they are paying for.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and this page is not going to pretend otherwise; home visits are a service offered only in India. UAE delivery is one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen for past papers and live annotation. The comparison below is set out so you can judge that on its merits rather than on a claim. The group option deserves its own line in that comparison, because the price looks attractive and the mathematics rarely is. A centre class that mixes Analysis and Approaches with Applications and Interpretation students has to teach the overlap, which means the Higher Level AI additions and Paper 3 technique are precisely the content a group cannot reach.

sections.heading: The two questions parents ask once the plan is agreed
paragraphs: The first is about the exploration and the line a tutor must not cross. IB academic honesty rules make the exploration the student's own work, and a tutor who supplies text, data or mathematical development is exposing the student to a malpractice finding that can cost the whole Diploma. A tutor may teach the mathematics, explain what a criterion rewards, respond to a draft the student has written, point out that an argument does not follow, and refuse a topic that cannot carry Higher Level mathematics. A tutor writes nothing that goes in the document. If a service offers to produce the exploration, that is a reason to walk away, not a convenience.

The second is whether AI at Higher Level was the right choice, usually asked at the worst possible moment. Applications and Interpretation is accepted widely, but some engineering, mathematics and physics degree routes specify Analysis and Approaches, and a few specify Higher Level. The practical step is to read the actual entry requirements for the three or four courses your child is targeting, including the regional options such as Khalifa University and the American University of Sharjah, before deciding anything. Requirements vary by course within the same university, and the published page for the specific programme is the only reliable source.

Running alongside both is the paperwork. Private schools in Ras Al Khaimah are regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which according to u.ae regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. For students heading to UAE universities, the Ministry of Education equivalency process is separate again and is run by the ministry, not by any tutor. Verify what your child's intended route requires on moe.gov.ae and through the school, and treat anyone who claims to secure equivalency for you with scepticism.

process.title: Tell us the date and the gap
process.description: Send the exam session, the current grade, the predicted grade and the one thing your child cannot currently do. That is enough to work out which of the four starting points you are in and roughly how many weeks the plan needs to cover.

process.title: A free first lesson on the stuck topic
process.description: The first session is free and runs on real content, not on an assessment sheet. A Higher Level specialist teaches the topic your child named, and you hear how it was explained. If the fit is wrong, you have lost an hour and no money.

process.title: A written plan with the weightings in it
process.description: After the first lesson you get a short plan: which topics, in what order, how many sessions, and when the exploration work sits. Paper 3 appears as its own block rather than as a line inside revision, because at 20% of the grade it earns one.

process.title: Fixed weekly slots on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Sessions are booked at the same time each week around school-run reality in your community, and the same tutor keeps the student. Ramadan timings shift to a post-Iftar slot by agreement, and the slot survives the change rather than being renegotiated.

process.title: Monthly review against the papers
process.description: Every month the plan is checked against marked scripts rather than against impressions. Topics that keep producing the same error stay on the list; topics that are clean come off it. If the pace is wrong, the plan changes rather than the hours increasing.

whyPoints.title: Higher Level AI, specifically
whyPoints.description: Not mathematics generally and not Analysis and Approaches with the names changed. The tutor matched to your child teaches the Higher Level additions, the matrices, graph theory, non-linear regression and numerical differential equations, as taught content rather than as topics to look up.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 treated as its own exam
whyPoints.description: A one-hour paper worth a fifth of the grade with a format that appears nowhere else in the course gets its own block of sessions. Pacing is made explicit and practised against the clock until a two-part extended problem stops being a surprise.

whyPoints.title: The timeline is the plan
whyPoints.description: Every plan is written backwards from the exam session and the school's internal coursework deadlines, so you can see which weeks carry which work. A plan that cannot be drawn on a calendar is not a plan, and a parent should be able to read it in one sitting.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Exploration support is teaching, feedback and process coaching on work the student has produced. No tutor supplies text, data or mathematical development that goes into the document, and the reason is that the student carries the consequence, not the tutor.

whyPoints.title: Figures with a source attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to the competitor or rate table that published it, with the month it was read. Market rates are presented as the market, and no page here invents a statistic about results, satisfaction or tutor numbers.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what is scarce
whyPoints.description: A Higher Level AI specialist in a particular Gulf Standard Time slot is a narrow ask, and sometimes the honest answer is that the slot you want is not available this term. You get told that, with alternatives, rather than matched with a general mathematics tutor.

faqs.question: Is there an AI Higher Level mathematics specialist actually based in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and that is the realistic answer rather than a sales line. The emirate has a small set of private schools regulated by its own Department of Knowledge, and the Diploma cohorts inside them are modest. A school may run Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level for three or four students, which cannot sustain a dedicated local specialist, let alone a spare one available for private work. IB Gram's answer is to match a Higher Level AI teacher wherever they are and teach one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The filter becomes subject depth rather than driving distance.

faqs.question: How many weeks does my child realistically need before a May session?
faqs.answer: It depends which of four positions you are in. A DP1 student with an unfixed exploration topic and two HL-only topics outstanding needs a plan across 25 to 30 weeks. A DP2 student six months out with an unsubmitted exploration needs triage inside twelve to fifteen weeks, with the exploration taken first because it is a fifth of the grade and fully inside their control. A student who is at a 5 and wants a 6 can often do it in eight to ten focused weeks. The shortest honest answer is that the number of weeks you have determines what the plan can include, and the plan should say so in writing.

faqs.question: What exactly does Paper 3 in AI Higher Level ask for, and why does it matter so much?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is one hour long, exists only at Higher Level, and carries 20% of the final grade. It contains two compulsory extended-response problems, each building through its parts, so an error early in a question propagates. The content is nothing new; the format is entirely new. Students who have only practised Paper 1 and Paper 2 questions have never had to sustain one problem for twenty-five minutes, and they typically overspend on the accessible opening parts. It responds well to six to eight sessions that treat pacing as the skill being taught, with target times written on the script.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level AI topics do students in small Diploma cohorts most often miss?
faqs.answer: Graph theory and matrices, in that order. Both are Higher Level additions with no Standard Level equivalent, both arrive with unfamiliar vocabulary, and both sit late in most two-year schemes of work, which means they land in the term when mock exams, the exploration deadline and the Extended Essay are competing for the same hours. The Markov chain and transition matrix work that follows from matrices then inherits the gap. A useful question for your child's teacher is not whether the course is on track but whether graph theory has been taught in full.

faqs.question: How is the mathematical exploration marked, and how many marks are genuinely winnable?
faqs.answer: It is marked out of 20 across five criteria: presentation (4), mathematical communication (4), personal engagement (3), reflection (3) and use of mathematics (6). Personal engagement and reflection together carry six marks and are the cheapest to win and the most often thrown away, because both depend on the student doing and recording their own thinking rather than on difficulty. Use of mathematics is the criterion that punishes a Higher Level exploration built on Standard Level content. The recommended length is 12 to 20 pages, and the internal deadline is set by your child's school rather than by the IB.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the exploration without breaking IB academic honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a line that should be stated before any work starts. A tutor may teach the mathematics a topic needs, explain what each criterion rewards, respond to a draft the student has already written, point out where reasoning does not follow, and advise that a chosen topic cannot carry Higher Level mathematics. A tutor must not supply text, data or mathematical development that ends up in the document. The exploration is assessed as the student's own work and a malpractice finding falls on the student, not the tutor, so any service offering to produce one should be refused outright.

faqs.question: Is it too late to move from AI Higher Level down to Standard Level halfway through DP1?
faqs.answer: Often it is still possible, and it is a decision for your child's Diploma coordinator rather than for a tutor, because it affects the subject combination and the points structure. Mathematically the move is cleaner in this course than in many: Standard Level sits the same first two papers at shorter length and sits no Paper 3 at all, so the Higher Level additions and the Paper 3 preparation simply fall away. What makes the decision urgent is that Paper 3 work is a block of teaching on its own. Dropping Higher Level late wastes hours already spent on it.

faqs.question: Does AI Higher Level satisfy university entry requirements for engineering or analytics degrees?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and sometimes not, which is why the only safe step is to read the published requirements for the specific courses your child is targeting. Applications and Interpretation is widely accepted, particularly for business analytics, economics, health sciences and many engineering technology routes. A number of mathematics, physics and traditional engineering degrees specify Analysis and Approaches, and some specify it at Higher Level. Requirements differ between courses inside the same university, so check each programme page, including regional options such as Khalifa University and the American University of Sharjah, before changing anything.

faqs.question: How much should a Ras Al Khaimah family budget each month for Higher Level mathematics help?
faqs.answer: Using published UAE market figures rather than our own rate card: Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month with a budget tutor, AED 600 to 1,200 with a qualified mid-range tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packaged plans seen in the market run about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Higher Level sits at the upper end because the tutor pool is narrower, and exploration support is frequently a separate line families forget to budget.

faqs.question: Does an AI student need a particular graphic display calculator, and is technique examined?
faqs.answer: Every paper in Applications and Interpretation permits a graphic display calculator, including Paper 1, which is the structural difference from Analysis and Approaches. Your child's school specifies which models are allowed, so take the model list from the Diploma coordinator rather than from a shop. What matters for the grade is that calculator work is examined content in this course, not a convenience: regression, distributions, chi-squared tests, numerical solutions and graph reading are all expected to be done on the device accurately and quickly. Sessions here audit calculator technique rather than assuming it.

faqs.question: How do live video mathematics sessions work in practice for a student in Mina Al Arab or Al Marjan Island?
faqs.answer: The student joins from home at a fixed weekly time on Gulf Standard Time, with no journey at either end, which matters most in communities where leaving the island or crossing Al Qusaidat at pickup adds half an hour. The tutor shares a screen, works through past paper questions with live annotation, and the student writes on paper or a tablet while talking through the method. Scripts are photographed, marked and returned with the marks shown. A short written note after each session records what was covered and what to practise.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan, and what happens across the long summer break?
faqs.answer: Yes. During Ramadan most families here move the weekly slot to after Iftar, and the slot is rebooked for the month rather than renegotiated each week. Over the summer, families generally choose one of two patterns: a pause with a short diagnostic block in late August, or a lighter fortnightly rhythm that keeps the HL-only topics warm. For a student entering DP2, the summer between the two Diploma years is the cheapest time to close a topic gap and the best window for exploration data collection, because nothing else is competing for the hours.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor working with a family in this emirate need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. A parent can ask any tutor to show their permit.

faqs.question: Who regulates private schools in Ras Al Khaimah, and does that affect tutoring?
faqs.answer: Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate. According to u.ae, the authorities in Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee approval sit with the emirate regulator rather than only with the federal ministry. That does not place private tutoring under the Department of Knowledge; an individual tutor's permit comes from MoHRE. What it does mean is that your child's school answers to a northern-emirate regulator with its own processes, which is worth knowing when you read an inspection report.

faqs.question: What happens if no AI Higher Level tutor is free in the time slot we want?
faqs.answer: You get told, with options, rather than matched with a general mathematics tutor who will learn the course alongside your child. The usual alternatives are a different weekday at the same time, a slightly earlier or later slot that an available specialist can take, a fortnightly rhythm with longer sessions, or a place on the list for a slot that frees up at the end of term. For a narrow brief such as Paper 3 technique or exploration supervision, a short intensive block in a less convenient slot often works better than a weekly session in a convenient one.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-math-ai-hl-tutor.closingBody: If you know the exam session and the one thing your child cannot currently do, there is enough to work with. Send those two facts and the current and predicted grades, and the first session will be a free lesson on that topic with a Higher Level Applications and Interpretation specialist, taught live online on Gulf Standard Time. After it you get a short written plan with the paper weightings and the exploration dates in it, built backwards from the exam window rather than forwards from today. If the teaching is not right for your child, you have spent an hour and nothing else.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level: the modelling, the statistics, the calculator technique the papers assume, and the exploration. The first lesson is free and runs on a question your child cannot finish today, so the judgement is about teaching rather than credentials on a page.

intro.heading: Standard Level is a smaller course, not an easier one, and the clock runs the same
paragraphs: Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level runs to 150 teaching hours over two years and is examined by two written papers and a piece of coursework. There is no third paper. That makes the course narrower than its Higher Level counterpart, and it is where the misreading starts, because narrower is not the same as gentler. Paper 1 and Paper 2 each carry 40% of the final grade, so a single weak paper costs more here than in almost any other Diploma subject. A student who is slow on Paper 1 cannot repair it elsewhere.

The students who need help divide neatly. Some chose Standard Level AI deliberately and arrive in DP1 fluent in arithmetic and lost the moment a question presents a table of data without saying what to do with it. Modelling is a skill that no Middle Years assessment requires, and it has to be taught rather than absorbed. Others are moving down from Higher Level in the middle of DP1, usually for sound reasons, and need the transfer handled as a piece of work in itself rather than as a relief. A badly managed step down leaves gaps in the shared content that nobody goes back for.

A third group arrives late, in DP2, with the exploration unsubmitted and a predicted grade a point short of what a university offer requires. That group has the least room and the clearest priorities, because the exploration is a fifth of the grade, it is entirely under the student's control, and it is marked against five published criteria that can be worked through deliberately. Where the weeks are few, that is where they go first.

Ras Al Khaimah adds a specific constraint to all three. The emirate runs a compact set of private schools under its own Department of Knowledge, and the Diploma groups inside them are small. A mathematics teacher here may be carrying Higher Level, Standard Level and a Middle Years class in the same week, which means Standard Level AI frequently shares a room, and sometimes a lesson, with Analysis and Approaches. The content overlaps enough for that to be workable and differs enough for it to cost marks on the statistics and the calculator work.

Finding a subject specialist locally is therefore not a matter of searching harder. There are only so many Diploma mathematics teachers in the northern emirates, and the ones who exist are already timetabled. Teaching one-to-one over live video removes the geography from the problem: the tutor is chosen because they teach this course and have marked explorations against the criteria, and the session happens at a fixed time on Gulf Standard Time with no journey at either end.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-tutor.programmesIntro: Standard Level AI sits inside a wider IB structure, and which programme a student is in changes what the mathematics support has to do. These are the three Ras Al Khaimah families ask about most often.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Mathematics in the Middle Years Programme is marked against four criteria, with criterion D asking students to apply mathematics in real-life contexts. That criterion is the closest thing in the programme to Standard Level AI modelling, and a student who scored poorly on it in MYP 5 will meet the same difficulty again in DP1. It is the single most useful number a parent can look up before the Diploma starts.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Ras Al Khaimah school runs MYP into Year 11, the standard mathematics route feeds naturally into AI at Standard Level rather than into Analysis and Approaches. Families sometimes push for AA on reputation alone, and the result is a student working at the edge of their fluency for two years when AI would have produced a better grade and the same university options.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Each Diploma student takes exactly one of four mathematics courses. Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level is the applied, statistics-led option at the lighter of the two course sizes: 150 hours, two written papers of ninety minutes each, and an exploration submitted in DP2. Technology is permitted in both papers, which shapes how the course is taught and how it should be revised.
programmes.countryNote: In small northern-emirate cohorts, Standard Level AI is often the largest mathematics group in the year, which is a mixed blessing. The group gets the teacher's attention, but it may also absorb students who should be in Higher Level and students who are barely coping, and a single class cannot serve both ends of that range.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme combines Diploma courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. Where mathematics appears in a CP timetable it is usually Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level, because the statistics and financial mathematics map directly onto business, hospitality and engineering technology pathways.
programmes.countryNote: CP is offered at relatively few campuses in the northern emirates, so a Ras Al Khaimah CP student taking AI at Standard Level may be the only one in the school doing so. That is precisely the case where one-to-one support from outside the emirate stops being a luxury and starts being the only way to get subject-specific teaching.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-tutor.subjectsIntro: A Standard Level mathematics problem rarely travels alone. These are the Diploma subjects Ras Al Khaimah families most often ask about in the same conversation, and what each is actually assessed on.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Five topics taught through modelling and statistics, with technology permitted throughout. At Standard Level the course runs to 150 hours, examines two ninety-minute papers of equal weight, and asks students to fit models to real data rather than to manipulate algebra for its own sake.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebra-and-proof route, with Paper 1 sat without any calculator. Students considering a move between the two Standard Level courses should know that the statistics content shrinks sharply in AA and the algebraic demand rises, which suits some students and defeats others.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Five units covering human resources, finance, marketing and operations, with Paper 1 built on a case study released ahead of the exam. The finance and accounts unit uses exactly the ratio and break-even arithmetic that AI Standard Level students already practise.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, assessed by extended response and data response papers plus a portfolio of three commentaries. Diagram accuracy carries marks of its own, and AI students generally handle the quantitative data response well.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Four themes crossed with four levels of organisation, with Paper 1A multiple choice and Paper 1B data analysis sat in one sitting. The error bars, standard deviation and significance testing in Biology are the same statistical ideas AI teaches, approached from the other direction.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and Reactivity across six themes, with a data booklet supplied in the exam. The quantitative sections reward calculator discipline, and the scientific investigation runs on a DP1 timeline that collides with the mathematics exploration unless both are planned together.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Themes A to E with a combined multiple-choice and data-analysis Paper 1. Uncertainty, gradient work and graph linearisation appear in both Physics and AI statistics, so a student doing both should be taught the shared technique once, properly.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches, with research methods and statistics threaded through. The descriptive statistics and the reading of studies suit AI students, and the extended writing is usually where the marks are lost instead.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two written papers plus an individual oral, with a Higher Level essay in addition. Students strong in mathematics commonly lose marks on the architecture of an argument rather than on comprehension, which is quick to repair one-to-one.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects and a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title. Mathematics is a standing area of knowledge in TOK, and an AI student has concrete material to draw on about models, assumptions and what counts as evidence.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay in a subject the student chooses. An AI Standard Level student can write a mathematics Extended Essay, but the supervision question and the academic-honesty line need to be clear before the research begins.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-tutor.regionsIntro: What determines whether a weekly slot survives the term is when the student is actually home, settled and able to think. These are the Ras Al Khaimah communities families book from and what each one does to the timetable.

sections.heading: What Standard Level AI actually contains, and who ends up taking it
paragraphs: The course has five topics: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. Statistics is the largest of them by teaching time and by examination presence, which is the opposite of what parents expect from a mathematics course and the reason some students flourish here having struggled elsewhere. The calculus is kept deliberately practical: differentiation, tangents, optimisation and the trapezoidal rule for area, with no requirement to prove anything. Technology is permitted in both papers throughout.

Three groups of students take it. The first chose it on advice and is well placed, because the modelling and statistics suit how they think. The second took it because the timetable or the subject combination left no other option, and this group needs the vocabulary of modelling taught explicitly: how to read a context, choose a model, justify the choice and interpret the answer back into the context. The third moved down from Higher Level, and their position is unusual because they have met more content than the course requires while possibly having met some of it badly.

Knowing which group your child is in changes the first month entirely. A student from the first group needs practice and timing. A student from the second needs teaching on modelling as a skill before any past paper is useful. A student from the third needs an audit, because a Higher Level scheme of work that was running behind usually leaves the same gaps in the shared content that Standard Level will examine fully. Treating all three the same is how families spend money without moving a grade.

sections.heading: AI or AA at Standard Level, and why the choice matters more than families expect
paragraphs: The two Standard Level mathematics courses are not a harder and an easier version of the same thing. They examine different mathematics, in different ways, with a different relationship to technology. The decision is usually made in Year 11 on the basis of reputation, and reputation points towards Analysis and Approaches because it sounds more rigorous. For a student whose strengths are data, context and interpretation, that choice can cost two grades for no gain in university access.

The single biggest practical difference is the calculator. In Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 is sat with no calculator at all, which puts algebraic manipulation and recall under direct examination. In Applications and Interpretation, technology is permitted in both papers, so the examined skill becomes choosing the right tool and interpreting what it returns. Neither is easier. They reward different habits, and a student who is accurate under pressure by hand and a student who is strong at reading a context are not the same student.

The table below sets the two courses side by side on the dimensions that actually decide a grade. It is worth reading with your child's Diploma coordinator rather than alone, because a change of course affects the whole subject combination and there is a window inside which it is possible. After that window, the answer becomes making the current course work, which is a legitimate plan but a narrower one. One row of the table is worth more than the others for a family deciding now. The Middle Years criterion breakdown from MYP 5 is free, already exists in the school's records, and separates the two courses more reliably than a general impression of how good a student is at mathematics.

sections.heading: Two papers, no Paper 3: how the Standard Level grade is built
paragraphs: Standard Level AI is examined by two written papers of ninety minutes each, worth 40% of the final grade apiece, and by the mathematical exploration, worth the remaining 20%. There is no Paper 3; that component exists only at Higher Level. The arithmetic of that structure deserves attention, because with only three components and two of them equal, a single weak paper is unrecoverable. A student who consistently runs out of time on Paper 1 is carrying a ceiling on their grade that no amount of content revision will lift.

The two papers reward different behaviour. Paper 1 is a sequence of shorter questions in which pace and accuracy decide the mark, and in which there is no choice of question. Paper 2 is built from longer structured problems where the method has to be sustained and where a context must be read correctly before any mathematics happens. A student can be comfortably good at one and weak at the other, and a school that reports mocks as one grade conceals exactly that.

What follows from this for a plan is simple. Ask for the mock breakdown by paper. If the loss is on Paper 1, the work is timing, calculator fluency and short-question technique. If the loss is on Paper 2, the work is reading contexts, structuring extended answers and holding a method across parts. If it is on the exploration, that is a different kind of work again, and it has a deadline the school sets rather than the IB.

sections.heading: The calculator is examined content, not a convenience
paragraphs: Because technology is permitted in both Standard Level AI papers, the examiners assume it. Questions are written on the basis that a student can run a regression, read a normal distribution both ways, perform a chi-squared test, find an intersection graphically and solve numerically. None of those are rewarded as cleverness. They are expected, and a student who performs them slowly or unreliably loses marks on questions they understand perfectly well.

This is the most common diagnosable fault in the course and the quickest to repair. A student who takes ninety seconds to set up a regression where fifteen would do has lost a minute and a quarter on a paper of ninety minutes, and they will do it four or five times. Over a full Paper 1 that is five or six minutes, which is the difference between finishing and not finishing. The fix is mechanical: identify the operations, practise each one cold until it is automatic, then re-time a paper.

Your child's school specifies which calculator models are permitted, so the model list should come from the Diploma coordinator rather than from a shop or a forum. What a tutor can do is audit the technique in the first two sessions, against the operations the table below sets out, and report back which ones are slow rather than which ones are missing. Students rarely know; they assume everyone else takes as long as they do. The audit also catches a quieter problem, which is a student performing an operation correctly without understanding what it returns. A chi-squared statistic read off a screen with no sense of what the degrees of freedom mean produces a confident sentence that earns no marks, and that is a teaching problem wearing the costume of a technical one.

sections.heading: Where Standard Level marks actually go missing
paragraphs: The error log of a typical Standard Level AI student is not a list of topics they do not know. It is a short list of recurring habits. Rounding is the first: the course asks for three significant figures unless told otherwise, and a student who rounds early inside a multi-step calculation loses accuracy marks repeatedly on questions they solved correctly. It appears in every topic and it is invisible to the student, because the method was right.

Interpretation is the second. An AI question frequently ends by asking what the answer means in context, and that final mark is given for a sentence about the real situation rather than a number. Students trained on procedural mathematics stop when the calculation stops. Across a full paper, those unclaimed interpretation marks add up to more than most topic weaknesses. They are also the cheapest marks in the entire course to recover, because nothing new has to be learned.

The third is the unread context. Paper 2 questions open with a paragraph that defines variables, states units and sets the scenario, and a student in a hurry starts at the first equation. Units then go wrong, or a model is fitted to the wrong variable, and the error carries through every part. Teaching a student to annotate the stem before touching the mathematics takes one session and pays back across both papers. None of these three is a knowledge problem, which is why a plan built purely on re-teaching topics so often fails to move the grade.

sections.heading: Exploration topics that can carry Standard Level mathematics, and ones that cannot
paragraphs: The exploration is worth a fifth of the grade and marked out of 20 against five criteria, with use of mathematics carrying six of those marks. That criterion is where topic choice is decided, because it rewards mathematics that is correct, relevant and commensurate with the level of the course. A topic that only permits averages and a bar chart caps the mark however carefully the piece is written. A topic that demands mathematics well beyond the syllabus produces work the student cannot justify, which costs marks under communication and reflection.

Screening topics early is therefore the highest-value hour in the whole exploration process, and it takes about an hour. The question is not whether the topic is interesting. It is whether the mathematics the topic requires exists inside the five Standard Level topics, whether the data can actually be obtained, and whether the student can explain every step they perform. Where the answer to any of those is no, the topic is better reshaped now than rescued in month three.

The table below takes proposals students in this emirate genuinely bring and shows what each would need. The pattern worth noticing is that the weak version and the strong version of a topic are usually the same subject matter asked more precisely. Nobody has to abandon an interest. They have to find the question inside it that Standard Level mathematics can answer properly. The second thing worth noticing is that the strong versions almost all involve data the student gathered or sourced themselves, which is how criterion C marks are earned. A topic built on a downloaded table nobody chose is harder to write about personally, and the engagement marks quietly disappear.

sections.heading: What the plan can include, depending on when you start
paragraphs: The honest version of a tutoring plan says what it cannot do as well as what it can. The number of weeks available is the constraint that decides everything else, and it is fixed before any teaching starts. A family beginning in the first term of DP1 can plan for coverage, exploration quality and timing all three. A family beginning eight weeks before the exams can plan for timing and for the two or three topics the error log identifies, and should be told plainly that broad coverage is no longer on the table.

UAE schools sit the May session, so the shape of the year is predictable even though the exact dates belong to the IB and should be confirmed through your child's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org rather than taken from any tutoring page. Coursework and internal deadlines sit in the first half of DP2. Mocks sit in the middle. The last stretch is for timing and technique, and adding new content there tends to lower the grade rather than raise it.

The table sets out what each starting point realistically supports. The purpose is not to discourage a late start, which is frequently worth doing, but to make the aim explicit. A student who begins eight weeks out and gains a grade from timing, rounding discipline and claimed interpretation marks has had good value. A student promised full coverage in eight weeks has been sold something nobody can deliver.

sections.heading: What Standard Level support costs here, cheapest option first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market, because that is where most families start looking. A university-student or budget online tutor is advertised in the UAE from around AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at that level at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month. For a student who needs practice and company rather than teaching, that tier can be perfectly adequate, and saying otherwise would be dishonest.

One step up, a qualified subject tutor working online is quoted at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, which corresponds to about AED 600 to 1,200 a month for a weekly hour. An IB or IGCSE specialist sits at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase listing AED 270, and Bestimate's specialist exam-year monthly band runs AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. The market's premium tier reaches AED 650 an hour, published by BartyED. An in-home visit including travel is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, with monthly in-home packages seen at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions against about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions.

Those are published market figures with their sources named, read in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram price. What they are useful for is deciding which tier the problem needs. A rounding-and-timing problem does not need the specialist tier. A student who has never been taught modelling, or who is moving down from Higher Level with gaps in the shared content, is not going to be helped by the budget tier whatever it costs. IB Gram's own approach is to run the first lesson free and agree a plan afterwards, rather than quote a rate for a problem neither side has diagnosed.

sections.heading: Honesty, equivalency and what comes after Standard Level mathematics
paragraphs: The exploration is assessed as the student's own work, and IB academic honesty rules make that an obligation with real consequences. A tutor may teach the mathematics a topic requires, explain what each criterion rewards, respond to a draft the student has written, say that a conclusion does not follow from the data, and refuse a topic that cannot carry the course. A tutor supplies no text, no data and no mathematical development that goes into the document. Any service that offers a finished exploration should be refused; the malpractice finding lands on the student and can cost the whole Diploma.

For families staying in the UAE, the Ministry of Education equivalency process is separate from anything a tutor does. For the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count of five, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. No IB points threshold should be taken from a tutoring page; verify the IB route on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority, and treat anybody who claims to obtain equivalency on your behalf as a warning sign.

The regulator behind the school itself is the emirate's own. Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, according to u.ae, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is useful context when reading a school's inspection report or a fee notice, and it is distinct from the permit question for tutors, which sits with MoHRE under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. Those are two different authorities doing two different jobs, and conflating them is how misleading claims get made.

process.title: Send the paper breakdown, not the overall grade
process.description: The most useful thing a parent can send is the mock result split by paper, plus whether the exploration has been submitted. That single breakdown tells a tutor whether the problem is timing, context reading or coursework, and it changes what the first session does.

process.title: Free first lesson on a question your child cannot finish
process.description: The opening session costs nothing and runs on real content. A Standard Level AI specialist teaches through the question your child named, and you hear how it was explained. If the match is wrong, you have spent an hour and no money.

process.title: A short written plan with a stated aim
process.description: After the first lesson you get a plan naming the topics, the number of sessions, where the exploration sits, and what the plan is not going to attempt given the weeks available. An aim you can check is more useful than a promise you cannot.

process.title: A calculator and rounding audit in the first fortnight
process.description: Two sessions go on device fluency and accuracy discipline, because both are examined in this course and both are invisible to the student. The report back says which operations are slow rather than which are missing, which is usually the surprise.

process.title: Monthly check against marked scripts
process.description: Progress is reviewed against work that has been marked, not against how sessions felt. Errors that recur stay on the list; topics that come back clean leave it. If the pace is wrong the plan changes rather than the hours quietly increasing.

whyPoints.title: Standard Level AI, taught as its own course
whyPoints.description: Not Higher Level with sections removed and not Analysis and Approaches renamed. The tutor matched to your child teaches the two-paper structure, the statistics weighting and the technology assumptions that are specific to Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level.

whyPoints.title: The habits that cost marks get named
whyPoints.description: Early rounding, unclaimed interpretation marks and unread contexts cost more across a paper than most topic gaps. Those are diagnosed from marked scripts in the first month and drilled directly, because they are the cheapest marks available in the course.

whyPoints.title: Step-downs handled as a handover
whyPoints.description: A move from Higher to Standard Level mid-course leaves specific gaps in the shared content. The audit for those gaps is a defined piece of work with a written note at the end, rather than an assumption that less content means less difficulty.

whyPoints.title: Exploration topics screened before writing
whyPoints.description: An hour spent testing whether a topic can carry Standard Level mathematics prevents a term spent rescuing one that cannot. The screening is about the mathematics the topic requires and the data the student can actually obtain, not about whether the subject is interesting.

whyPoints.title: Every figure carries its source
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are attributed to the pages and rate tables that published them, with the month they were read. No results statistic, satisfaction score or tutor headcount appears anywhere, because none of those could be evidenced.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what the weeks allow
whyPoints.description: A plan states what it will not attempt given the time available. A late start is often worth making, and it is worth making with an explicit aim rather than with an implied promise of full coverage that nobody can deliver in eight weeks.

faqs.question: Is AI Standard Level the easy mathematics option in the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: No, it is the smaller one. Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level runs to 150 teaching hours against 240 at Higher Level, and it drops the third paper entirely. What it does not drop is examination pressure: Paper 1 and Paper 2 each carry 40% of the final grade, so one weak paper cannot be offset anywhere. The content is also genuinely different rather than reduced, with statistics as the largest block and modelling as the central skill. Students who find algebra uncomfortable often do better here; students who expect an undemanding course are routinely surprised.

faqs.question: My daughter is moving from AI Higher Level down to Standard Level in DP1. What should the handover cover?
faqs.answer: Three things. First, an audit of the five shared topics, because a Higher Level scheme of work running behind usually leaves gaps in content that Standard Level will examine in full. Second, re-practised timing, since the papers are ninety minutes rather than two hours and the question density differs. Third, the exploration: if it was pitched at Higher Level depth it may now need rescoping, and if it was pitched at Standard Level depth it may be fine as it stands. The move itself is a decision for your child's Diploma coordinator rather than for a tutor.

faqs.question: How many of the two Standard Level papers allow a graphic display calculator?
faqs.answer: Both of them. That is the structural difference from Analysis and Approaches, where Paper 1 is sat without any calculator. In Applications and Interpretation the examiners write questions assuming the device, so regression, distributions, chi-squared tests, graphical solving and numerical integration are expected to be performed quickly and accurately. Calculator work is therefore examined content rather than a convenience, and slow technique costs marks on questions the student understands. Your child's school specifies which models are permitted, so take that list from the Diploma coordinator rather than from a retailer.

faqs.question: Which exploration topics work at Standard Level and which ones waste a term?
faqs.answer: The test is whether the mathematics a topic requires exists inside the five Standard Level topics, whether the data can actually be obtained, and whether the student can explain every step. Comparing ten years of monthly temperatures with means and a line graph is too thin and caps the use-of-mathematics criterion. Modelling one year of temperature with a sinusoidal function and testing the fit against another year is the same interest asked properly. Topics needing formal proof or university-level techniques fail for the opposite reason: the student cannot justify what they did.

faqs.question: What does my child lose by not sitting Paper 3 at Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Nothing in terms of assessment coverage, because the grade is built from two papers and the exploration, and each component is weighted to account for it. What a student loses is the extended problem-solving practice Paper 3 forces on Higher Level candidates, which is a real but indirect benefit. The practical consequence for revision is positive: Standard Level time can go entirely into the two papers and the coursework. For families weighing a step down mid-course, dropping Paper 3 preparation also removes a block of teaching that is otherwise needed on its own.

faqs.question: Why is my son losing marks on questions he says he got right?
faqs.answer: Usually one of three habits rather than a knowledge gap. Rounding early inside a multi-step calculation costs accuracy marks across every topic while the method stays correct. Stopping at the number and never writing the sentence that interprets it in context leaves a mark unclaimed on question after question. Starting the mathematics before reading the stem produces wrong units or a model fitted to the wrong variable, and the error then runs through every linked part. All three are visible in marked scripts and all three respond to a few sessions of deliberate drilling.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both AI Standard Level and another Diploma subject for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. Mathematics and Physics, or mathematics and Economics, are combinations some tutors genuinely teach to Diploma standard. What should not happen is a single tutor stretched across four subjects because it is administratively convenient, since Diploma assessment is specific enough that general competence shows up quickly in the marks. Where two tutors are involved, the useful step is telling each one what the other is covering, particularly where content overlaps, such as uncertainty and graph work in Physics and statistics in AI.

faqs.question: How quickly can a Ras Al Khaimah family get a Standard Level AI tutor started?
faqs.answer: The limiting factor is almost never finding a Standard Level AI teacher; it is finding one free in the slot a family wants on Gulf Standard Time. Early-evening weekday slots between 4.30pm and 6.30pm are the most contested, and term-time demand peaks around mock exams and the weeks before coursework deadlines. Where the preferred slot is unavailable the alternatives offered are a different weekday, a longer fortnightly session, or a short intensive block at a less popular time. You get told what is actually free rather than promised a slot that then moves.

faqs.question: Does a Standard Level mathematics grade limit university options in the UAE and abroad?
faqs.answer: It narrows some routes and leaves most open, and the only reliable check is the published entry requirement for each specific programme. Business, analytics, health sciences, many engineering technology courses and most social sciences accept Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level. Mathematics, physics and traditional engineering degrees frequently require Analysis and Approaches, and some require it at Higher Level. Requirements differ between courses inside the same institution, so read the programme page for each of the three or four courses your child is actually considering before drawing a conclusion.

faqs.question: Is a budget online tutor at AED 60 an hour enough for Standard Level AI?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the problem is. For a student who understands the content and needs practice, accountability and someone to work alongside, the budget tier advertised in the UAE from around AED 45 to 150 an hour can be perfectly reasonable, and EdFlik lists from AED 45 to 65. For a student who has never been taught modelling as a skill, or who is carrying gaps after a step down from Higher Level, that tier is unlikely to help whatever it costs. Qualified subject tutors online are quoted around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200.

faqs.question: How do live video sessions handle written mathematics in practice?
faqs.answer: The student works on paper or a tablet while talking the method through, and the tutor shares a screen with the past paper question, annotating it live. Completed work is photographed and returned marked, with the marks shown against the mark scheme rather than described in general terms. For a family in Al Marjan Island or Mina Al Arab the practical gain is that no part of the arrangement depends on a car journey at pickup time, which is where weekday sessions in those communities most often fall apart.

faqs.question: What happens to the weekly slot during Ramadan and the summer holidays?
faqs.answer: During Ramadan most families here move to a post-Iftar slot, and the change is made for the whole month rather than renegotiated weekly, which keeps the routine intact. Across the summer, families generally choose either a clean break with a diagnostic session in late August, or a lighter fortnightly pattern. For a student entering DP2, the summer is the cheapest window available for closing a topic gap and for collecting exploration data, because nothing else is competing for the hours and no school deadline is running.

faqs.question: Do we need to check that a private tutor is permitted to work in the UAE?
faqs.answer: It is a fair question to ask any tutor. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published. MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service is the official route, applied for through its app, website or e-services.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates my child's school in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: The emirate's Department of Knowledge. According to u.ae it regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That means curriculum and fee approval sit with the emirate rather than only with the federal Ministry of Education, which supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. It is worth knowing when you read a fee notice or an inspection report, and it is a separate matter from the tutor permit, which MoHRE issues.

faqs.question: Is eight weeks before the exams too late to start Standard Level mathematics support?
faqs.answer: No, provided the aim is stated honestly. In eight weeks a plan can fix timing on both papers, repair rounding discipline, train the interpretation sentence that so many students leave unwritten, and work through the two or three topics the error log actually identifies. That is frequently worth a grade. What eight weeks cannot deliver is coverage of a two-year course, and anybody promising it should be treated with scepticism. The useful conversation at that point is which marks are currently within reach, not which topics are missing.

intro.heading: Why a Higher Level Physics specialist in this emirate is usually a remote one
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah has a compact private-school sector. The Diploma is taught on a handful of campuses clustered around Al Hamra, Al Nakheel and the Mina Al Arab side of the city, and the cohorts are small by Dubai standards. That has one consequence parents feel immediately in DP1: the school may have exactly one teacher who takes Physics at Higher Level, and that teacher also covers Standard Level, the Middle Years science classes and often the lab technician's job as well. Nothing about that is negligence. It is arithmetic. A year group of forty students cannot sustain two Physics specialists, and no head of school in the northern emirates would pretend otherwise.

So when a student hits the wall in Physics HL, and almost every student does hit it somewhere between circular motion and induced electromotive force, the help available inside the building is one person's spare period. If that person taught the topic the same way the first time, a second pass in the same style rarely fixes it. The student needs a different explanation, not a louder one.

The local alternative is a private tutor who drives. In the northern emirates that pool is thin and it is rarely subject-specific. A tutor advertising in Al Qusaidat may be an excellent Maths teacher who takes Physics as a second subject, which is adequate for Standard Level and not adequate for the Higher Level additions to fields and nuclear physics. Travel also eats the budget: you are paying for the Emirates Road run as much as for the teaching, and a 5pm start becomes a 5.40pm start when the Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Road is heavy.

An online IB Physics tutor in Ras Al Khaimah removes the geography from the decision. The question stops being who lives within twenty minutes of your villa and becomes who has taught Higher Level Physics to the current guide, marked the scientific investigation against its four criteria, and can explain magnetic flux three different ways. IB Gram delivers all UAE tutoring as one-to-one live video. We do not offer home visits in the UAE at all; tutors attending a residence is an India-only service, and pretending otherwise on a Ras Al Khaimah page would be dishonest.

What you get instead is specificity. A session runs on a shared screen with the student's own problem set, their own graph, their own half-finished uncertainty calculation. The tutor annotates it live, the student does the next one while the tutor watches, and the recording stays available for the revision week in April. For a subject assessed through two papers and one investigation, that is a closer match to how marks are actually won than an hour of talking at a whiteboard in the living room.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: Physics Higher Level is the end of a line that starts years earlier. Below is what each IB programme asks of a student in this emirate, and what the step into DP Physics demands of them.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Middle Years science is integrated and criterion-assessed: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, reflecting on the impacts of science. Students write up investigations against criteria before they ever meet a Diploma lab. What MYP does not do is drill algebraic rearrangement or standard-form arithmetic, and that gap is the single most common reason a capable MYP 5 student struggles in the first term of Physics HL.
programmes.countryNote: In Ras Al Khaimah the MYP-to-DP step is often made inside the same small school, with the same teacher. That continuity helps pastorally and hides the academic jump, because nobody arrives to re-baseline the cohort. Families here usually find the gap in October of DP1, when the first Physics test comes back lower than every MYP report suggested it would.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Physics sits in Group 4 and is examined through Paper 1, which splits into multiple-choice Paper 1A and data-based Paper 1B, Paper 2 of short and extended response questions, and the internally assessed scientific investigation. Higher Level carries 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, and the extra hours are not revision. They are additional content inside each theme, which is why an SL student who moves up mid-year is behind on substance rather than practice.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in this emirate sit the May session with everyone else, but they do it in a school where the Group 4 project, the Collaborative Sciences Project and the individual investigation are often supervised by the same teacher. A tutor who takes the pressure off the investigation timeline frees that teacher to do what only the school can do, which is sign off the work as genuinely the student's own.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs two or more Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and personal and professional skills. A CP student can take Physics as one of those Diploma courses, usually at Standard Level, and is assessed on it exactly as a Diploma candidate is. The reflective project replaces the Extended Essay and carries its own supervision and academic-honesty requirements.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is not widely offered in Ras Al Khaimah, so families considering it are usually weighing a move to a Dubai or Sharjah campus against staying put. If your child is on CP with Physics, the tutoring question is narrower: the course content is the same, but the timetable around it is not, and sessions have to work around the career-related study placement rather than a standard school day.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-physics-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Physics HL is rarely the only pressure point. These are the Diploma courses Ras Al Khaimah families most often ask about alongside it, with what each one actually assesses.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level adds content inside each one. Marks are lost most often in Paper 2 extended response, where a correct method is undermined by a missing unit, an unstated assumption or a graph gradient read without reference to the axis scale.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The usual partner to Physics HL. Calculus fluency decides whether a student can follow the derivations in fields and simple harmonic motion or has to memorise results. Students who take Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level alongside Physics HL cope, but need the differentiation and integration topics taught earlier than their maths timetable delivers them.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistically richer and lighter on algebraic manipulation. It is a legitimate pairing with Physics HL, and it changes what tutoring has to cover: more time spent on rearranging formulae and manipulating indices, because the maths course will not drill those as a matter of course.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The other Group 4 choice taken with Physics by students aiming at engineering or medicine. Shares the same assessment architecture, including the 24-mark scientific investigation, which means a student doing both has two investigations due in the same window and usually needs help sequencing them rather than writing them.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Often chosen as the Group 4 subject by students who want a second science without a second laboratory. The overlap with Physics is real in the logic and the modelling, and thin everywhere else. Students who assume a strong Physics mark will carry Computer Science are usually surprised by the programming component.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Taken with Physics less often, but common in the combination aimed at biomedical engineering. Biology rewards precise terminology in a way Physics does not, and students who carry a Physics habit of short numerical answers into Biology extended response lose marks for underdevelopment rather than error.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: An alternative Group 4 course for students whose Physics HL load is already heavy. It carries its own internal assessment and its own data-handling demands, and families should treat it as a different subject rather than an easier science, because the command terms and the marking are not softer.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Where offered, this sits closest to Physics in its treatment of materials, forces and testing. The assessed design project is substantial and runs on a long timeline, so a student taking it with Physics HL has two major internally assessed pieces competing for the same term.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Physics
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay supervised by a school teacher. Physics essays fail most often on scope: a question that cannot be answered with the apparatus available in a Ras Al Khaimah school laboratory, or a modelling question with no data to test it against. Tutoring here is question-shaping and method review, never authorship.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed through an exhibition and a prescribed-title essay. Physics students often find the exhibition the easier half and the essay the harder, because the subject habit of stating a single correct answer works against an assessment that rewards weighing competing claims.

sections.heading: What a Higher Level Physics timetable in a small Diploma cohort actually looks like
paragraphs: Start with the option blocks, because they explain most of what parents in this emirate find frustrating. A Diploma school builds a timetable by grouping subjects into blocks and running them simultaneously. With a cohort of forty, each block can only hold a few classes, so Physics HL may run against Economics HL or against the second Maths set. A student who wants both has to drop one, and the school is not being obstructive when it says so. It genuinely cannot staff a second Physics HL section for three students.

The second consequence is teacher load. In a small school the Physics HL teacher usually also teaches Physics SL, a Middle Years science class, and sometimes Maths. Add Group 4 project coordination and investigation supervision for every science student in the year, and the spare capacity for one-to-one reteaching is close to zero by February. Parents reading this will recognise the pattern: helpful replies to emails, a genuine offer of lunchtime help, and a diary that has no lunchtimes left in it.

The third is assessment calibration. A teacher marking eight Higher Level scripts has a small sample to calibrate against. In a Dubai school with four parallel HL sections and a department of six, a borderline Paper 2 answer gets a second opinion in the staffroom. Here it often does not, so a student can carry a stable internal grade through DP1 and then meet a different standard in the mock marked to published markschemes.

None of this argues against the school. It argues for a second, external, subject-specific voice, available on a fixed weekly slot that does not depend on anybody's free period. That is the specific job an IB DP physics HL tutor in Ras Al Khaimah is being hired to do, and it is why delivering it over video rather than by road is the practical choice in a small emirate.

sections.heading: The five themes, and what Higher Level adds to each one
paragraphs: The current Physics guide organises the course into five themes rather than the older numbered topic list. Themes A to E run across both levels, and Higher Level is not a separate syllabus. It is additional content inside each theme, taught alongside the Standard Level material. That structure matters for tutoring because it means a Higher Level student cannot simply be given extra past papers. They need the extra content explicitly taught, usually at the point the school is moving on.

The table below sets out what each theme covers and where students in this emirate most often stall. The pattern is consistent across cohorts: the mechanics theme feels manageable because it looks like IGCSE, and the fields theme does not, because it is the first place where the mathematics stops being arithmetic and starts being algebraic manipulation of relationships the student has not seen before.

A tutor working through this list does two things with it. First, diagnose: a short set of questions per theme establishes where the understanding actually stops, which is rarely where the student says it does. Second, sequence: the themes are not independent, and a student who cannot handle vectors in theme A will not handle fields in theme D, so the repair order is dictated by the physics rather than by the school's calendar.

Confirm the exact teaching order with your child's school. Schools sequence the themes differently depending on how they split the two years and whether they teach the sciences in parallel or in blocks.

sections.heading: How Physics HL is assessed, component by component
paragraphs: Physics at Higher Level is assessed through two external papers and one internally assessed investigation. Paper 1 is split: Paper 1A is multiple choice, Paper 1B is a set of data-based and experimental questions drawn from the practical programme. Paper 2 carries short-answer and extended-response questions and the largest single share of the grade. The scientific investigation is marked in school against published criteria and moderated by the IB.

Parents are often surprised by how much hangs on Paper 2. Nearly half the grade is decided by one paper that rewards structured written physics, which is exactly the skill a student who learned the subject through multiple-choice revision apps has not practised. Students who are strong at Paper 1A and weak at Paper 2 are the most common profile we see arriving from a small cohort, because internal tests in a small school lean towards short questions that are quicker to mark.

The tutoring implication is specific. Paper 1A is improved by volume and speed drills, and improves fast. Paper 2 is improved by writing answers out, in full, to a markscheme, and then rewriting them, which is slow and is the thing almost nobody does unsupervised. A plan that spends its hours in proportion to the weightings rather than in proportion to how pleasant each task is will shift the grade more than any additional content coverage.

Always verify the current weightings and durations for your child's cohort with the school's IB coordinator before planning around them, because the Group 4 courses were revised and different cohorts have sat different versions.
