intro.heading: Comparing districts, and finding the same answer twice
paragraphs: People searching for a tutor in a specific district are doing something sensible: they are trying to narrow a confusing market by using the one variable they understand. In most cities that works. In Ras Al Khaimah it does not, and a page that pretends otherwise is wasting a family's time.

Al Dhait is a large residential area south of Ras Al Khaimah city, substantially villa housing, split between its northern and southern sections, with a straightforward run into the city's school cluster. Al Nakheel, the next district over, sits at the centre of that cluster. Khuzam sits inland. The drive differs by ten or fifteen minutes between them. The schools they feed overlap almost entirely. The Diploma cohort available in each is drawn from the same small set of schools, and the number of local teachers who have taught a given Higher Level option is the same number in all three, because it is an emirate-level figure rather than a district-level one.

So the honest comparison between Al Dhait and the next district over produces one conclusion: the geography changes your evening timetable by fifteen minutes and changes nothing about who is qualified to teach your child. What does vary, and varies a great deal, is the provider model, the delivery format and the individual tutor. Those are the comparisons worth making, and most of this page is spent on them.

Delivery is stated plainly. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The phrase in this page's address is what parents type, and it is answered honestly: what in-home tuition is quoted at in this market, what the travel premium consists of, and why removing the district from the equation is the point rather than a workaround.

Every rate quoted is attributed to the provider that published it and dated October 2026. Regulatory statements come from federal and emirate sources. No IB exam or results date appears, because the IB's own site returns an error to automated checking and nothing in this project has been verified from the board itself.

What follows is four comparisons rather than one: district against district, provider model against provider model, this emirate against Dubai, and format against format. The last two are where a family in Al Dhait can actually change the outcome. There is also a fifth comparison, between two individual tutors, which is the one families feel least equipped to make and which turns out to rest on four questions that need no subject expertise to evaluate. Those are set out towards the end, together with the one question about replacement policy that matters more in a thin market than it would in a large one.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-dhait.programmesIntro: Three IB stages reach Al Dhait, and the comparison logic is the same at each: the district is not the variable, the format and the individual are.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external papers and no mark schemes, so there is nothing to compare tutors on except how they handle a young learner. Short sessions on mechanics are the right purchase: number bonds, written method, reading stamina, explaining an answer in a sentence.
programmes.countryNote: At this stage the in-home argument is at its strongest anywhere in the country, because physical presence matters most with young children. In Al Dhait the honest limitation is that the local pool willing to drive out in the evening is small, so reliability becomes the deciding factor rather than preference.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, with strands inside each criterion. Comparing tutors here has one useful test: ask which subject guide they work from and whether they can name the strands. Most generalists cannot, and that single question separates the field faster than any credential.
programmes.countryNote: MYP cohorts in this emirate are small, so an internal position carries little information. An external view against the published criteria is worth more here than a comparison with classmates.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, with external papers plus an internally assessed component in every subject. This is where the district genuinely stops mattering, because the number of people in Ras Al Khaimah who have taught a particular Higher Level option is frequently in single figures.
programmes.countryNote: Several of those few are also contractually unable to tutor students at their own school. The practical result is that for Higher Level work an Al Dhait family and an Al Nakheel family are competing for exactly the same handful of people, or looking beyond the emirate.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-dhait.subjectsIntro: The Diploma subjects most often requested from Ras Al Khaimah, with a note on whether the local supply differs between districts. It does not.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Standard Level is widely taught across the emirate's Diploma schools; Higher Level is not. Paper 1 is taken without a calculator, which is where calculator-fluent students lose a grade's worth of marks on hand algebra.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, with the calculator central. Higher Level adds graph theory and matrices, usually taught late. Supply is identical in Al Dhait and Al Nakheel because it is drawn from the same schools.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the losses, with data questions catching students who state a trend without its cause. Among the hardest Higher Level subjects to source anywhere in this emirate.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Unit errors, gradients read instead of calculated, and explanation questions answered with an equation. Technique responds quickly to timed practice, which makes format a bigger lever than location.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Naming a process earns one mark; ordering its stages earns the rest. Statistics questions catch students who have never calculated a standard deviation by hand. More widely taught locally than the other two sciences.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram marks are the most available and the most commonly dropped. The commentaries need recent articles collected as they appear. Very scarce across the whole emirate rather than in any one district.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the case stimulus is the whole paper. Higher Level adds the pre-released case study, published far enough ahead that early structured reading is unusually valuable.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 rewards argument about how a text constructs meaning rather than summary. Reasonable supply emirate-wide, and the widest quality spread of any subject, which makes individual comparison essential.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic A
subjects.description: Language B assesses reading, writing to a specified text type and a spoken component. Home speakers lose marks on register and convention rather than vocabulary. Strongest local supply in the emirate.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The essay answers a prescribed title against named criteria and rewards one developed line of argument. Breadth is the standard failure, and the component has no timetabled lesson in most schools.

sections.heading: Al Dhait against Al Nakheel: what actually differs
paragraphs: Take the comparison seriously and set it out properly, because a family deserves the real answer rather than a reassuring one. Al Dhait sits south of Ras Al Khaimah city, largely villas, with its northern and southern sections and a straightforward route into the city. Al Nakheel sits in the middle of the city's school and commercial cluster. On a weekday afternoon the difference in drive time is ten to fifteen minutes.

Everything downstream of that is near-identical. The schools the two districts feed overlap almost completely, because the emirate's private-school set is small and concentrated. The Diploma cohorts are drawn from the same institutions. The number of teachers in the emirate who have taught a specific Higher Level option is the same number regardless of which district a family lives in, since it is a feature of the teaching population rather than of the map. And the professional constraint is the same: in Abu Dhabi the regulator's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid tuition of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct barring the same, which is press-reported and worth verifying against the current policy document but consistent across sources.

What genuinely differs is the clock. Al Nakheel's shorter run moves the earliest workable session forward by about a quarter of an hour; Al Dhait's villa housing makes a quiet room for a full timed paper easier to find than it is in the creek-side apartments. Those are real differences and neither of them is about teaching.

sections.heading: Why the answer comes out the same either way
paragraphs: The reason district comparison fails here is structural rather than accidental, and it is worth understanding because it explains why so much tutoring advertising in the Northern Emirates is written at the level of place names.

Supply of specialist teaching is a function of how many people in a population have taught a particular course. In a city with hundreds of international schools, that population is large enough that it spreads across neighbourhoods, and living near a cluster genuinely improves access. In an emirate with a compact private-school set, the specialist population for a given Higher Level option may be a handful of individuals in total, and a handful does not distribute across districts in any meaningful way. Whether they are fifteen minutes away or thirty makes no difference if they are already teaching full time or cannot take students from their own school.

That is why the comparison that actually discriminates is not between Al Dhait and Al Nakheel but between delivery formats and provider models. Those genuinely differ: an agency, a marketplace, an independent tutor and a tuition centre offer different things at different prices with different failure modes, and the choice between them changes the outcome in a way that a district choice cannot.

There is also a comparison upwards, between this emirate and Dubai, which does matter, but not in the direction families expect. It matters because it explains why advice written for a Dubai audience does not transfer, and that is set out in its own section below.

sections.heading: What geography does change, and what it does not
paragraphs: Dismissing geography entirely would be as unhelpful as over-weighting it, so here is the division. Some things in a tutoring arrangement genuinely depend on where a family lives, and they are worth planning around. Most of the things that determine the result do not.

Geography changes the clock: when the school run ends, how much of the evening survives it, and whether a 4:45pm or a 6:30pm start is realistic. It changes the physical setting: a villa in Al Dhait offers a quiet room more easily than an apartment on the creek. It changes the viability of in-home delivery, because the pool of tutors willing to drive to a southern residential district on a weekday evening is smaller than the pool willing to work in the centre. And it changes the practicality of a tuition centre, which requires a journey each way.

Geography does not change which teachers have taught your child's syllabus, what the market charges, what the papers demand, when the exam series runs, what the criteria require, or which regulator oversees the school. Those are all emirate-level or board-level facts, and they are the facts that determine a grade.

The table separates the two lists explicitly, because the most common planning error in this emirate is spending effort on the left-hand column while assuming the right-hand column will take care of itself. The left-hand column is easy to think about, which is most of why it absorbs the attention; the right-hand column decides the grade.

sections.heading: Provider models compared, since districts do not separate them
paragraphs: This is the comparison that replaces the district one. The market reaching Al Dhait contains five or six genuinely different business models, and they fail in different ways. Comparing them on model rather than on brand claims is both fairer and more useful, and it is something no competitor page in this market does: every one of them compares itself against an unnamed set of other platforms.

An agency selects and manages tutors, which usually means a higher rate, a vetted pool and a replacement policy. A marketplace lists tutors and lets a family choose, which means lower rates, more variance and the vetting burden on the parent. An independent tutor offers the keenest rate and the strongest relationship, with no replacement available if the match fails or the tutor's circumstances change. A tuition centre offers group classes at the lowest headline price with a fixed timetable and no choice of teacher. An international platform offers scale, often in a currency a UAE family does not transact in, and sometimes with no UAE presence at all.

Three questions discriminate between them regardless of model. What happens in week three if the match is wrong. Whether the rate can change mid-year. And whether the person teaching has taught the specific syllabus code, recently. Any provider should answer all three in writing, and the willingness to do so is itself informative.

sections.heading: This emirate against Dubai: the comparison that does matter
paragraphs: Most of the tutoring advice a family in Al Dhait will read online was written for Dubai, and it is not transferable. Understanding why is more useful than any district comparison, because it tells a parent which advice to discard.

Dubai's private sector is large: 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26, US at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7. Seven new private schools were added for the 2026-27 intake, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 with enrolment rising 6 per cent. In a market that size a particular Higher Level option is taught across a large number of schools, so specialist tutors are numerous, competitive and locally available.

Ras Al Khaimah is a different market in kind rather than in degree. The private-school set is compact and concentrated around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab, the Diploma presence inside it is small, and specialist supply for an individual Higher Level course can be a handful of people. Advice that assumes choice, competition and local availability simply does not describe this emirate. Nor does the regulatory advice: KHDA governs Dubai, while private schools here are regulated by the Department of Knowledge, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

The practical conclusions differ accordingly. In Dubai, shopping around on price is rational. Here, booking early and holding a reserved slot with somebody who has actually taught the course is rational, and price is the second question rather than the first.

sections.heading: Comparing two tutors properly
paragraphs: Once the district is set aside, the comparison that remains is between individuals, and it is the one families feel least equipped to make. In practice four questions do almost all the work, and none of them requires subject expertise to evaluate.

First: which syllabus code did you last teach, and when? A date and a code is a good answer. A reassurance about long experience with the IB is not, because the IB revises subject guides and a course taught five years ago is a different course. Second: which papers did your students sit, and which topics did that cohort lose marks on? Somebody who has genuinely taught the component will answer with specifics; somebody who has not will generalise.

Third: what will you not do with my child's internal assessment? This is the most discriminating question available in this market, because the honest answer is a short list of refusals and the dishonest answer is an offer. A page found during research for this project sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, so the question is not theoretical. Fourth: do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit?

Then one practical question for the provider rather than the tutor: what happens in week three if it is not working? In Al Dhait this matters more than it would in Dubai, because an in-home tutor who does not fit may be the only one who was willing to drive out, whereas an online arrangement has a bench behind it.

sections.heading: Formats compared: online, in-home, group and school support
paragraphs: The last comparison is the one that changes the outcome most for an Al Dhait family, and it deserves to be made without a thumb on the scale. In-home tuition has genuine advantages. A tutor in the room reads body language, can take a book out of a student's hands, and cannot be muted. For a young or easily distracted student that is worth paying for, and any page that denies it is selling.

What it costs here is reach, reliability and a share of the fee. The published gap is the evidence: a qualified subject tutor working online is advertised at AED 150 to 300 an hour, while in-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by the Bestimate rate survey and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors, all read October 2026. Al Dhait is a southern residential district, so the drive is real and the pool willing to make it is small. A cancelled visit is a cancelled week when there is nobody else to call.

Online one-to-one trades presence for selection and reliability. The student gets the subject specialist rather than the nearest willing teacher, the session starts when the family is ready, past papers are annotated live on a shared screen and kept, and a replacement is a scheduling question rather than a geographic one. For Diploma paper work, where most of the session is a question, a mark scheme and a pen, the shared screen is at least as good as a table.

IB Gram offers only the online format in the UAE, and no page here will tell an Al Dhait parent otherwise. The table compares all four options on the dimensions that differ, including the places where in-home or a centre genuinely wins.

sections.heading: Honesty, materials and the permit
paragraphs: A page built on comparisons has to be comparable itself, so here are the limits that apply to this provider as much as to any other. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain each assessment criterion and what its descriptors demand, help narrow a research question, test whether a topic is viable, review a method, and give written feedback on a draft the student has already written.

A tutor must never write, redraft or complete an Internal Assessment, a Mathematics exploration, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or any assessed coursework, and must not supply text, data or diagrams for submission. The consequence of crossing that line falls on the student rather than on whoever sold the help, which is why it belongs in a comparison of providers rather than in a footnote.

The materials rule is the same for everybody. No tutor should reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads. The official source should be referenced and linked, which is why this page carries no attachments. Reproducing assessment material is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure.

On who may teach: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from the Department of Knowledge, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no tutor can promise a grade.

process.title: Stop comparing districts
process.description: Al Dhait, Al Nakheel, Khuzam and Al Qusaidat feed substantially the same schools and draw on the same emirate-wide teaching pool. The fifteen minutes of drive time between them changes your slot and nothing else, so put the effort into the comparisons that discriminate.

process.title: Compare the model, then the individual
process.description: Agency, marketplace, independent tutor, centre and international platform are genuinely different products with different failure modes. Then compare individuals on four questions: the code they last taught, the papers their students sat, what they will not do with coursework, and their permit.

process.title: Take the free diagnostic session
process.description: The first session is a diagnosis rather than a sales call, with no card details taken. Lost marks are classified into content, method, command term and time, and you keep the written summary naming the first three targets whether or not anything else is booked.

process.title: Set the slot to your own arrival time
process.description: Measure when your child actually walks through the door in Al Dhait rather than when school finishes, then set the session to that. Because lessons run online, nothing is added at either end, and the slot is set to finish before Maghrib rather than against it.

faqs.question: Is it easier to find a tutor in Al Dhait or in Al Nakheel?
faqs.answer: Practically the same, and that is the honest answer rather than a dodge. The two districts feed substantially the same school cluster, their Diploma cohorts come from the same institutions, and the number of teachers in the emirate who have taught a given Higher Level option is an emirate-level figure rather than a district one. What differs is ten to fifteen minutes of drive time, which moves your earliest workable session and changes nothing about who is qualified to teach your child.

faqs.question: So does my address in Ras Al Khaimah matter at all?
faqs.answer: For some things, yes. It sets the length of the school run and therefore how much of the evening survives it, which decides whether a 4:45pm or a 6:30pm start is realistic. It decides whether a quiet room is easy to find, which is simpler in Al Dhait's villas than in creek-side apartments. And it decides whether an in-home visit is viable at all. What it does not decide is which teachers have taught the syllabus, what the market charges, or what the papers demand.

faqs.question: Why is specialist supply an emirate-level figure rather than a local one?
faqs.answer: Because a handful of individuals does not distribute meaningfully across neighbourhoods. In a city with hundreds of international schools, specialists are numerous enough to spread out and living near a cluster genuinely improves access. In an emirate with a compact private-school set, the number of people who have taught a particular Higher Level option may be a handful in total, and whether they are fifteen or thirty minutes away is irrelevant if they are already fully booked or barred from teaching their own school's students.

faqs.question: How do agencies, marketplaces and independent tutors actually differ?
faqs.answer: An agency selects and manages tutors, so the rate is higher and a replacement is usually available. A marketplace lists tutors and puts the vetting burden on the parent, so rates are lower and variance is wider. An independent tutor offers the keenest rate and the strongest relationship with no replacement if the match fails. A centre offers group classes at the lowest headline price with a fixed timetable and no choice of teacher. Each fails differently, which is the useful basis for comparison.

faqs.question: Why does tutoring advice written for Dubai not work here?
faqs.answer: Because it assumes a market that does not exist in this emirate. Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25 with 17 curricula licensed and International Baccalaureate enrolment at 7 per cent, and added seven new schools and 16,846 places for the 2026-27 intake. In that market shopping around on price is rational. Here, where specialist supply for a Higher Level course can be a handful of people, booking early and holding a reserved slot is rational and price is the second question.

faqs.question: What is the in-home premium really paying for in Al Dhait?
faqs.answer: Largely the drive, plus genuine physical presence. The published bands show the gap: a qualified subject tutor working online is advertised at AED 150 to 300 an hour, while in-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent tutors, read October 2026. Al Dhait sits south of the city, so the journey is real and the pool willing to make it is small, which means a cancellation costs the week rather than the session.

faqs.question: Which four questions separate a good tutor from a confident one?
faqs.answer: Which syllabus code did you last teach and when; which papers did your students sit and where did that cohort lose marks; what will you not do with my child's internal assessment; and do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. The third is the most discriminating question available in this market, because the honest answer is a short list of refusals. A page found during research for this project sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, so it is not a theoretical question.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre a reasonable alternative for an Al Dhait family?
faqs.answer: For exam technique at a shared level, it can be, and the headline price is usually the lowest available. The trade is that a group cannot follow one student's specific gaps, you travel to a fixed timetable each way, and you do not choose the teacher. One practical question worth asking a centre: an operation with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, renewed annually with the request at least 30 days before expiry, so ask about permits.

faqs.question: Does living in a villa rather than an apartment change anything?
faqs.answer: Marginally, and it is the one geographic factor that favours Al Dhait. A full past paper under timed conditions needs ninety uninterrupted minutes in a quiet room, which is easier to arrange in villa housing than in a creek-side apartment where siblings share living space. It matters most for weekend blocks rather than for short weekday sessions, and it is worth settling in week one rather than discovering in week five that the arrangement will not hold.

faqs.question: Should I choose a tutor who lives in Ras Al Khaimah if one is available?
faqs.answer: Only if they have taught the syllabus, which is a separate question from where they live. For Mathematics and the sciences at the commonest levels a local option is often credible. For Higher Level sciences, Economics with its commentaries, or a minority language, the local pool thins to almost nothing and some of the best-placed teachers are barred from tutoring their own school's students. Compare on the code last taught and the papers sat, then on everything else.

faqs.question: What does a replacement policy actually need to say?
faqs.answer: That if the match is wrong you get a different tutor, with the notes transferred, at no extra charge, and that you can trigger it early rather than after a paid term. Ask for it in writing before any payment. In this emirate it is worth more than a marginally better rate, because an in-home tutor who does not fit may be the only one who was willing to drive out, whereas an online arrangement has a bench behind it.

faqs.question: Who regulates schools here, and does that affect tutoring?
faqs.answer: Private schools in Ras Al Khaimah are regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods rather than only inspecting. It does not regulate tutoring providers, so no tutoring company can claim its approval. A parent moving from Dubai should note that KHDA reports do not cover schools here, and should request the school's latest inspection outcome directly instead.

faqs.question: Is the budget end of the market ever the right comparison?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the right job. Online tuition advertised from AED 33 to 65 an hour buys a person, a schedule and a routine, which is a real service for a primary child or a teenager who will not start work unsupervised. It does not buy a diagnosis and it will not survive a Higher Level paper. The error is not buying at the budget end; it is buying at the budget end for a job that needs the specialist end, or the reverse.

faqs.question: How should I compare two quotes that look similar?
faqs.answer: Send both providers the same five pieces of information and the same four questions, or the quotes will not be comparable. The information: subject, level, programme, school and the number of weeks you want covered. The questions: which code did the proposed tutor last teach, is travel inside the rate, can the rate change mid-year, and what happens in week three if the match is wrong. The spread in the answers is more informative than the spread in the prices.

faqs.question: Why does this page tell me the district does not matter?
faqs.answer: Because it does not, and a page that pretended otherwise would be optimising for a search term rather than answering a parent. The variables that change a Diploma outcome in Ras Al Khaimah are the provider model, the delivery format and the individual tutor's experience of the specific papers. All three are comparable, and all three are set out here with sources and dates. Drive time is real, and it belongs in a scheduling conversation rather than a decision about teaching.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-dhait.closingBody: If you have been weighing Al Dhait against the next district over, the useful news is that you can stop: the answer is the same and the effort is better spent elsewhere. Compare provider models, compare delivery formats against the published AED bands, and compare individuals on the four questions in this page. Then take a free diagnostic session, with no card details taken, and keep the written summary of where the marks are actually going. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, set to your own arrival time rather than a tutor's drive.

intro.heading: Al Hamra Village, Mina Al Arab, Al Marjan Island: one question, one answer
paragraphs: Al Hamra Village sits on the coast south of Ras Al Khaimah city, a gated mix of villas, townhouses and apartments arranged around a golf course, a marina and a mall, with a British-curriculum campus inside the community itself. Mina Al Arab lies a short drive north along the same coast road, lower density and newer in parts. Al Marjan Island reaches out into the Gulf on reclaimed land, dominated by hotels and resort residences. Three distinct places with three distinct feels, and almost no difference at all in the thing this page is about.

What differs between them is logistics. Gate access and visitor registration vary. Approach roads vary. The share of households who commute into the city or further south towards Umm Al Quwain and Dubai varies, and that in turn moves the earliest realistic session start by half an hour either way. If you are comparing communities for a house move, those differences are worth weighing.

What does not differ is the supply of people who have taught IB Higher Level Chemistry to an examination class. Ras Al Khaimah is a northern emirate with its own regulator and a comparatively small private-school sector, concentrated around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab. The number of adults inside the emirate who have marked Higher Level papers in any given Diploma subject is small, and it is the same small number whether your villa is in Al Hamra Village or on Al Marjan Island. Driving ten minutes north does not change it.

That is the comparison worth making before any money moves. For a Middle Years student who needs homework structure and someone to sit beside them, a competent local generalist is perfectly adequate and proximity is a genuine benefit. For a Diploma student eighteen months from a session, with a Higher Level Chemistry Internal Assessment to plan and an Extended Essay question to narrow, the question is not who is within a ten-minute drive. It is who knows what the criteria pay for. There is also a sibling effect worth naming: a household running a Middle Years student and a Diploma student at once needs two different kinds of help, and buying the same thing for both is how families overspend on this coast.

So here is the honest position. Lessons for Al Hamra Village students are delivered one-to-one over live video, on a shared screen, timed to Gulf Standard Time around the local school day. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in Ras Al Khaimah or anywhere else in the UAE; visiting in person is a service we run only in India. What that trade buys a family on this coast is the pick of the Diploma teaching rather than the pick of the local traffic, and in an emirate this size that is not a marginal gain.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-hamra.programmesIntro: The IB runs as four distinct programmes and a family in Al Hamra Village may meet three of them. Each has a different assessment logic, and mistaking one for another is the most common planning error we see on this coast.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with no external examinations and no grades in the conventional sense. Progress is reported against learning outcomes and the final year culminates in an Exhibition. Tutoring at this stage is almost never about content; it is about reading fluency, number facts and the ability to work independently for twenty minutes. Those three predict how the Middle Years transition goes far better than any PYP report does.
programmes.countryNote: Al Hamra Village families with primary-age children usually have the shortest school run of anyone in this comparison, with a campus inside the community. The useful question at this stage is whether the child can read a question and plan an answer unaided, because the Middle Years Programme assumes both.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed internally against criteria A to D, with published descriptors rather than percentages, plus a Personal Project in the final year. The gap it leaves is timed external examination technique, because many students reach the Diploma having never sat a formal paper under conditions. Interdisciplinary units and criterion-based feedback are excellent preparation for thinking and poor preparation for a clock.
programmes.countryNote: Ask the school in Ras Al Khaimah which programmes it is authorised to deliver and at which year groups, because provision in the northern emirates is thinner than in Dubai and a family may need to plan a move for the Diploma years. That is a Year 10 conversation, not a Year 11 one.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, usually three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay at a 4,000-word limit, and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment marked against named criteria with published mark allocations. The Diploma is scored out of 45, and the gap between a predicted score and a final one is usually explained by the internally assessed components rather than the papers.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, with a November option where the school offers it. This page publishes no specific IB examination or results date, because the IB's own site cannot be checked automatically; your coordinator holds the internal deadline sheet, and that is the document a tutoring plan should follow.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Less common in the UAE than the Diploma but a genuine fit for students who want two or three academic subjects at depth alongside applied study. The reflective project has its own criteria and its own school deadline, and it is routinely underestimated.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Ras Al Khaimah school offers the Career-related Programme, the practical tutoring need is usually in the Diploma courses taken alongside it, most often a language and a mathematics course. Confirm with the school which components are internally and which externally assessed before planning support.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-hamra.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Ras Al Khaimah families most often cannot source locally at Higher Level, with the component that decides the grade in each.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms separate the grades, and the Internal Assessment needs working data before any analysis can begin. Students who leave data collection until the second year are the single most common rescue request on this coast, and it is the hardest one to answer well.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields and circular motion are the recurring content weaknesses, while uncertainty and error analysis decide marks in both the papers and the Internal Assessment. A student who can describe an experiment but cannot propagate an uncertainty is losing marks twice over, which makes that skill unusually good value.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A content-volume subject where the mark scheme pays for precise terminology rather than general understanding. The Internal Assessment rewards a tightly controlled investigation over an ambitious one, and the most useful tutoring intervention is usually narrowing the research question before any data is collected.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency decides the Higher Level grade more than any single topic does. The Exploration carries its own school deadline and its own criteria, and the hardest part is finding a topic with genuine mathematics in it rather than an application dressed up as one.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and technology-led modelling, and a better fit than Analysis and Approaches for many students. The route decision has to be made before the option form goes in, because some university courses specify Analysis and Approaches by name. Check the target course requirements first.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Individual Oral has a school recording window and the Higher Level Essay has internal draft deadlines, both landing while science Internal Assessments are being written. Analytical precision on an unseen extract is the teachable skill here, and it transfers directly to the examination papers.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides the analysis marks, and evaluation paragraphs that actually weigh competing effects decide the top band. The internally assessed commentaries are spread across the course, which means they are also spread across every other deadline the student has.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-led, so the discipline is applying the right framework to the right stimulus rather than listing frameworks. Higher Level candidates meet a research-based component with its own word limit and criteria. Students who write generally about a company rather than answering with data lose the application marks.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Taken by many students as a dual-subject option, which hides how much terminology and systems thinking it demands. Marks are lost on the difference between a named case study and a general example, which is a fixable habit rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the Diploma
subjects.description: UAE private schools teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the licensed international curriculum, as the federal baseline requires. Support here means working with the school's own material and assessment, since using different or additional content without ministry permission is not allowed.

regions.name: Mina Al Arab
regions.note: The nearest comparable coastal community, a short run north on the same road. Lower density in parts, with its own retail and beach frontage. For tutoring purposes the only meaningful difference is that the inbound drive from the city is slightly shorter.

regions.name: Al Marjan Island
regions.note: Reclaimed islands reaching into the Gulf, heavily resort-oriented with a high share of apartments and serviced residences. Visitor access is the most involved of any community in this list, which is precisely the friction an online session removes.

regions.name: Al Nakheel
regions.note: The central district where much of the emirate's private-school and commercial activity concentrates. Families here have the shortest school run and the widest choice of local tuition, which is also where the local pool is already fully committed.

regions.name: Al Dhait
regions.note: Inland residential districts, north and south, with established villa neighbourhoods. The drive out to the coast is real but unremarkable; the subject-specialist shortage is identical to the coast's.

regions.name: Khuzam
regions.note: Another inland residential area close to the city centre with schooling within reach. A family here and a family in Al Hamra Village will receive the same answer to the same Higher Level question, which is the point of this page.

regions.name: Julphar and Al Qusaidat
regions.note: Older districts closer to the creek and the original town. Through-traffic slows the late afternoon considerably, so an in-home session that starts on time here is the exception rather than the rule.

regions.name: Al Jazirah Al Hamra and Al Mamourah
regions.note: The historic village area and the residential districts behind it, low density with small school-age populations. Group revision classes rarely assemble at a single subject and level here, so one-to-one is the practical format.

sections.heading: Al Hamra Village against the next community along: what genuinely differs
paragraphs: Put the three coastal communities side by side and the differences are real but narrow. Al Hamra Village is a mature gated community with a school inside it, a mall, a marina and a golf course, which means a short school run and an evening that is not spent in a car. Mina Al Arab is newer in parts, lower density, with its own beach frontage and a slightly shorter inbound drive from the city. Al Marjan Island is resort-dominated, apartment-heavy, with the most involved visitor access of the three.

For a family weighing a house move those distinctions matter. For a family weighing a tutoring arrangement they almost all collapse into one variable: how late an in-home session has to start, and therefore how tired the student is when it does. The table below sets that out column by column. Read across any row and the differences appear; read down the final column and they disappear entirely, because an online session starts when the student is ready rather than when the traffic allows.

There is one difference worth taking seriously, and it runs the other way from what parents expect. The communities with the easiest access and the best local schooling are also where the local tutoring pool is already fully booked. Al Nakheel has more schools and more teachers within reach, which means the few people in the emirate who have taught Higher Level Physics are already teaching every evening they have free. Being close to the supply does not help when the supply is committed.

So the recommendation for Al Hamra Village is the same as the recommendation for Mina Al Arab or Al Marjan Island. Stop shortlisting by who can reach the gate. Shortlist by subject and level, ask each candidate which Higher Level papers they have actually taught and which Internal Assessment criteria they can recite, and have them respond to a piece of your child's marked work before you commit to a term.

sections.heading: The scarcity problem, stated plainly rather than sold around
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah is a northern emirate with its own education regulator and a private-school sector concentrated in a handful of locations. That is not a criticism of the schools, several of which are well established and long-standing. It is an arithmetic observation about adult supply. A subject taught at Higher Level in a small number of settings produces a small number of teachers experienced in it, and a fraction of those are available for private work after a full teaching day.

Competitors in this market do not say this. The researched pages for the northern emirates either ignore Ras Al Khaimah entirely or imply the same depth of coverage they claim for Dubai. Several route enquiries to numbers outside the UAE without disclosing it. We would rather state the constraint, because a family that understands it makes a better decision and because the constraint is precisely what online delivery exists to solve.

The practical shape of the problem looks like this. Generalist support for Middle Years students is reasonably available locally. Mathematics at Standard Level is usually findable. Higher Level Chemistry, Physics and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches are not, and neither is experienced Internal Assessment supervision in those subjects, which is the thing a second-year Diploma student most needs. Internal Assessment coaching requires someone who knows the criteria and the mark allocations in that specific subject, and generic study support cannot substitute.

This is also why we will tell an Al Hamra Village family when we cannot match a request well. Some narrow combinations - a particular Higher Level science with a particular component deadline close to a session - have thin availability even online. The options then are a different time slot that opens a wider pool, a short diagnostic block with a specialist followed by weekly work with a strong generalist, or a recommendation to wait. None of those is as satisfying as yes. All of them beat discovering a mismatch in week three of a term you have already paid for.

sections.heading: What IB tutoring costs here, read as a monthly number
paragraphs: Hourly rates are how tutors quote and monthly totals are how families actually experience the cost, so start with the month. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session put budget support at AED 240-600, mid-tier at AED 600-1,200, and specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000-2,000 and above. Packaged offers seen across the market sit inside that frame: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. The in-home monthly figure is roughly double the online one for half as many sessions.

Unpack that into hourly terms and the bands are these, all of them providers' own published rates read in October 2026. Budget online tutoring, usually delivered by university students or recent graduates, is advertised from AED 45-65 by EdFlik and from AED 33-52 by Tutopiya. Qualified subject tutors online run roughly AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Named IB and A Level specialists sit at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase listing AED 270. In-home one-to-one visits run roughly AED 180-350 on Bestimate's table and up to AED 500 from independent home tutors. Examiner-led premium work reaches AED 650 at BartyED.

Now stretch it across a Diploma. Two Higher Level subjects supported weekly for the two years of the Diploma, at mid-tier monthly rates, is a four-figure monthly commitment sustained over roughly eighteen teaching months. Most families do not need that and should not buy it. The pattern that works is dense support at the pressure points - the transition into the Diploma, the Internal Assessment planning window, the run-in to the session - and nothing in between. Three well-placed blocks cost a fraction of continuous tuition and usually achieve more.

What IB Gram does not do is publish an invented price list or quote in a currency Ras Al Khaimah families do not transact in. Two of the pages competing for this search quote US dollars; three publish no price at all, and one of those refuses to answer its own pricing question in its own FAQ. Our position is a free trial lesson first, then a consultation that produces a plan with a shape and a finish line, and a quote against that plan rather than against a theoretical hour.

sections.heading: Higher Level or Standard Level, and when that is really decided
paragraphs: A Diploma student picks six subjects and takes three at Higher Level, and that choice is made before the first Diploma term rather than during it. It is the decision with the longest shadow. Higher Level means more teaching hours, more syllabus content, additional assessment components in several subjects, and the possibility of a university offer that specifies it. Standard Level means a manageable load and, in some subjects, a closed door at university level.

The table below compares the two across the dimensions that matter for planning rather than the ones a prospectus mentions. The row families most often skip is the last one: the right-fit signal from prior attainment. A student who found Middle Years science comfortable rather than easy will usually do better taking it at Standard Level and spending the saved hours on a Higher Level subject they are genuinely strong in. Three Higher Levels chosen by ambition rather than by evidence is the most common cause of a mid-Diploma crisis.

There is a second-order effect on Internal Assessments. Higher Level courses frequently carry extra components or a longer, more demanding internally assessed task, and every one of those has a school deadline. A student with three Higher Levels is carrying three heavier internal workloads through the same two terms as the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay. The subject choice therefore decides the calendar as well as the content, and the calendar is what breaks first.

For an Al Hamra Village family the practical move is to have this conversation in the second half of Year 11, with the school, armed with actual marks rather than impressions, and with the target university requirements checked. Where a change is needed after the Diploma begins, it is usually possible early in the first year and increasingly difficult after that. A short diagnostic block with a specialist in the subject under question is a cheap way to get evidence before the decision rather than regret after it.

sections.heading: The Internal Assessment, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an internally assessed component, marked by the school against the IB's published criteria and then moderated. Those criteria are lettered, each carries a stated maximum, and the total is a meaningful share of the subject grade. A student who has read the criteria and written against them is operating with information. A student who writes a good piece of work and hopes is not, and the second student is far more common.

This is the single largest uncontested gap in this search market. Of the competitor pages researched for the UAE clusters, not one names a single assessment criterion by letter with its mark allocation. Parents are told that Internal Assessment support is available; nobody tells them what the Internal Assessment is marked on. The practical consequence is that families cannot tell a tutor who knows the component from one who has heard of it.

The useful work on a component is sequenced. First, read the criteria aloud with the student and translate each one into a question the finished piece must answer. Second, narrow the research question until the investigation is actually doable with the equipment and the time available, which in science subjects is where most marks are won or lost. Third, collect or gather the material. Only then write. Students who write first and fit the criteria afterwards produce work that reads well and scores in the middle.

And the boundary, stated plainly because this market needs it stated. A tutor may explain the criteria, ask questions about the plan, point out that a conclusion does not follow from the data, and give written feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not write any part of it, rewrite prose, supply data, or edit it to completion. Nobody at IB Gram will do those things. A site currently ranking on these searches advertises completed Internal Assessments for sale; that is an academic-honesty breach with consequences that fall on the student, not the seller.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and why it is not a tutoring credential
paragraphs: Private schools in Ras Al Khaimah are regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah's authority, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a broader remit than inspection alone, and it is worth knowing because it means curriculum and fee questions have a local answer rather than a federal one.

The full map matters for families who move within the UAE, which on this coast is common. Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in that emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education, which plays a supervising role in those three emirates. Five bodies, one country, and a different inspection framework in each.

Here is the part that needs saying on a tutoring page. None of those regulators approves, accredits or licenses a tutoring platform by virtue of regulating schools. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the Department of Knowledge, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Department of Education and Knowledge, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson, and has no office in the UAE. Any page implying otherwise is making a claim it cannot evidence.

What is genuinely checkable is the individual tutor's permit. Private tutoring runs through a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, covering school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The ministry lists the service with no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and states that those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so ignore any figure you see quoted.

sections.heading: What a first term of support should actually produce
paragraphs: Tutoring that cannot be judged tends to continue indefinitely, which suits the provider and nobody else. So agree at the outset what the first block is supposed to produce and how you will know. For a Diploma student the honest measures are narrow and checkable: a named topic that was costing marks and no longer is, a research question narrowed from unworkable to doable, a timed paper score that has moved in a specific component.

What is not a measure is the student feeling more confident, or the sessions going well, or the tutor being lovely. Those are necessary and insufficient. A student can enjoy a term of tuition, like the tutor a great deal, and sit the same paper in May having improved nothing, because the sessions never once put them under time pressure and marked the result against the published scheme.

So the structure we propose for an Al Hamra Village family is a block with an end date. Six to eight sessions, a stated target, a written review at the end, and an explicit decision about whether to continue. Where the answer is no, say so; a block that achieved its target and stopped is a success rather than a lost customer. Where the answer is a different tutor rather than a different plan, say that too, early, because the only thing lost by changing at week three is less than what is lost by changing at week twelve.

The review itself takes ten minutes and needs three things in front of you: the marked work from the start of the block, the marked work from the end, and the target you wrote down. If the first and the second look the same, the plan was wrong or the match was wrong, and both are fixable. That discipline is worth more to a family on this coast than any amount of enthusiasm about engagement.

process.description: The deadline sheet tells us where the pressure falls; the marked work tells us whether the problem is content, technique or component understanding. Ten minutes with both produces a better plan than an hour of conversation, and neither costs anything.

process.description: One 45 to 60-minute one-to-one session, no card details, no obligation afterwards. Watch for two things: whether the tutor diagnoses before explaining, and whether your child does most of the talking. A trial in which the tutor lectures is a preview of the term.

process.title: Agree a block with a target and an end date
process.description: Six to eight sessions, a stated goal, a written review at the end and a real decision about continuing. Open-ended weekly bookings drift into subscriptions that nobody evaluates. Blocks with finish lines can be judged, repeated or stopped.

process.title: Review on marked evidence, then decide
process.description: Put the marked work from the start and the end of the block side by side against the target you wrote down. If nothing moved, change the plan or change the tutor, and do it early. We would rather lose a block than carry a mismatch through a Diploma year.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our villa in Al Hamra Village?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We teach Al Hamra Village students one-to-one over live video, and visiting a student at their address is a service we run only in India. Independent tutors and agencies do advertise in-home visits in Ras Al Khaimah, with market rates for in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180-350 on Bestimate's 2026 table and up to AED 500 from some independents. The trade is specialism against presence, and in an emirate with a small pool of Higher Level teachers the specialism is usually worth more.

faqs.question: Is the tutoring situation different in Mina Al Arab or on Al Marjan Island?
faqs.answer: Only in the logistics. Gate access, approach roads and the realistic earliest start time for an in-home session differ by half an hour or so across the three communities. The supply of people who have taught Higher Level Chemistry or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches to an examination class is identical, because it is an emirate-wide pool and it is small. Once lessons are on a screen the community stops mattering entirely and the only remaining question is whether the tutor knows the component your child is being assessed on.

faqs.question: How much should a Ras Al Khaimah family budget each month for IB support?
faqs.answer: Read it monthly rather than hourly. Bestimate's published monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 240-600 for budget support, AED 600-1,200 mid-tier, and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Packages seen in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are providers' own published figures read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices. Our own plan and quote follow the free trial lesson and a consultation.

faqs.question: Why is it so hard to find a Higher Level science tutor in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Arithmetic rather than anything else. The emirate has a comparatively small private-school sector concentrated around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab. A subject taught at Higher Level in a handful of settings produces a handful of teachers experienced in it, and only some of those take private work after a full teaching day. The pool is the same whether you live on the coast or inland, which is exactly why remote one-to-one matters more here than it does in Dubai, where the same subject is taught in a great many schools.

faqs.question: Which body regulates private schools in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: The emirate's Department of Knowledge, which regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a wider remit than inspection, so curriculum and fee questions have a local answer here. Dubai's schools answer to KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to ADEK, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. None of those bodies accredits a tutoring platform, and IB Gram claims no approval from any of them.

faqs.question: What exactly can a tutor do with my child's Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Explain the assessment criteria and the marks attached to each, ask questions about the plan and the method, point out where a conclusion is not supported by the data, and give written feedback on the student's own draft. What a tutor cannot do is write any part of it, rewrite the prose, supply data or edit it to completion. Nobody at IB Gram will. Submitted work has to be the student's own and the consequences of a breach land on the student, which is why any provider selling completed assessments should be read as a warning.

faqs.question: Should my child take three Higher Levels if they are capable of it?
faqs.answer: Capable of it and well served by it are different questions. Higher Level means more teaching hours, additional syllabus topics, extra assessment components in several subjects and a heavier internally assessed workload, all landing in the same two terms as the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay. Three Higher Levels chosen by ambition rather than by evidence of prior attainment is the most common cause of a mid-Diploma crisis. Check the target university requirements first, then choose from marks rather than from aspiration.

faqs.question: Does online one-to-one actually suit a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: For component and paper work it suits it unusually well. A shared screen both people annotate, the student's own draft or marked paper open, and the published criteria beside it is a better working surface than a kitchen table, and the annotations survive the session. Where physical presence genuinely matters is younger children and students who need an adult managing attention in the room. A sixteen-year-old narrowing a research question or working through a timed paper section does not need anyone sitting next to them.

faqs.question: When should we start thinking about the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: In the first Diploma year, while there is slack in the calendar. The Extended Essay runs to a 4,000-word limit and the school sets staged draft deadlines, which collide in the second year with science Internal Assessment write-ups, the Theory of Knowledge essay and oral components in language subjects. Students who enter the second year with a narrowed research question, a supervisor relationship that works and some reading done are in a wholly different position from those who enter it with a title. The topic choice is the part worth slowing down on.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Ras Al Khaimah need a licence?
faqs.answer: Individuals need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years and covers school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The ministry lists the service with no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and states that those tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine amounts are published, so disregard any figure quoted online.

faqs.question: What should six sessions of IB support have produced by the end?
faqs.answer: By marked evidence against a target you wrote down, not by how the sessions feel. Agree a block of six to eight sessions with a specific goal: a named topic no longer costing marks, a research question narrowed to something doable, a timed paper score moving in a defined component. At the end, put the marked work from the start and the finish side by side. If they look the same, change the plan or change the tutor, and do it at week three rather than week twelve.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor take two of my child's Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, but do not optimise for it. A mathematician who also teaches Physics at Higher Level exists and is genuinely useful, because the overlap in mechanics and calculus is real. A single tutor covering Chemistry and English is almost always a generalist wearing two hats, and the Internal Assessment coaching in both will be shallow. Depth in the component matters more than convenience in the schedule, especially in the second Diploma year when every subject has a live deadline.

faqs.question: What if you cannot find the right specialist for us?
faqs.answer: We will say so. Some combinations are genuinely thin: a specific Higher Level science close to a session, with a component deadline, at a particular time of day. The realistic options are moving the session slot to open a wider pool of tutors, running a short diagnostic block with a specialist and then weekly work with a strong generalist, or waiting for availability. We would rather give you one of those answers than substitute a generalist and let the mismatch emerge in week three of a term.

faqs.question: Can sessions work around a school day on this coast and around Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes. Students in Al Hamra Village with a campus inside the community are often home early, which makes a mid-afternoon session practical in a way it is not for families commuting from the city. Later slots to around 9pm work where a parent wants to be in the room. During Ramadan sessions move after Iftar and usually shorten to around 45 minutes, which holds concentration better than a full hour at the wrong time. Plan that shift before the month starts rather than rescheduling week by week.

They do not differ in how many people in this emirate have taught your child's Higher Level subject to an examination class, and that is the number a tutoring decision turns on. So send us the subject, the level, the live component and one piece of marked work, and take the free trial lesson before you commit to anything. Lessons here are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. If we cannot match the specialism properly, we will tell you that instead.

intro.heading: The Diploma is a calendar problem before it is a teaching problem
paragraphs: Al Mamourah sits in the Ras Al Khaimah city area, close to Al Qusaidat and the older residential districts behind the creek. Secondary students here travel out to the emirate's private schools, most of which cluster around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra Village and Mina Al Arab. The practical consequence is that a weekday already contains two journeys before any studying starts, and the realistic window for a session opens around five in the evening rather than straight after the last lesson.

That is the small version of the problem. The large version is sequencing. The Diploma runs on a chain of deadlines that the school sets and the family discovers late: subject and level confirmation, the Extended Essay research question, the first Extended Essay draft, the reflection sessions, the Theory of Knowledge essay title, the Internal Assessment drafts for six separate subjects, Creativity, Activity and Service completion, mock papers, predicted grades, and then the May session itself. Miss the order and a student spends Year 13 doing Year 12's work.

Private schools in Ras Al Khaimah answer to the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which regulates private education here and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. What it does not do is publish your child's internal Diploma deadlines, because those belong to the school. So the first useful action on this page is not booking a tutor; it is asking the Diploma coordinator for the internal deadline list in writing, which almost nobody does and which changes every conversation afterwards.

IB Gram matches Al Mamourah students to Diploma subject specialists and delivers every lesson one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address, and home visits are a service we run in India only. In a northern emirate where a Higher Level cohort can number a dozen students, a specialist chosen for the subject beats a generalist chosen for proximity, and that trade is the reason the format is what it is.

The sections below give you the two years as a backwards table, the internal deadlines that genuinely bite, what a term of support costs in AED with the publisher named, how Ramadan and the UAE school calendar move the revision window, how the Diploma calendar collides with university application deadlines, and what the options are if the May results disappoint. Read the first table, mark where your child is, and the next decision usually becomes obvious.

One honest caveat about dates. This page publishes no specific IB exam or results date. The board's own site is the only authority for those and it should be read there or confirmed with your child's Diploma coordinator, because a tutoring page quoting an IB date is a page a parent might plan a flight around. Cambridge and Pearson dates are a different matter and are cited below with their sources, since those boards publish them openly.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mamou.programmesIntro: Al Mamourah families meet the IB in three forms, and each has a different calendar shape. The Diploma is the one with hard external deadlines; the two below it are where the habits that survive the Diploma are built.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across Standard and Higher Level plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment marked by the school against published criteria and moderated externally, so a meaningful share of the final grade is settled before any exam paper is opened. The core components have their own deadlines that run independently of subject teaching.
programmes.countryNote: Ras Al Khaimah Diploma candidates sit the May session, like the rest of the UAE. The internal deadlines are set by your school and are the ones that control the plan: Extended Essay research question and drafts, reflection sessions, Theory of Knowledge title and essay, and six Internal Assessment submissions. Ask the coordinator for all of them at the start of Year 12 rather than discovering them one at a time.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment across eight subject groups, each reported on a one-to-eight scale rather than as a percentage, ending in the Personal Project. The Personal Project is the first time most students manage a long piece of work against a deadline they own, which makes it a rehearsal for the Extended Essay rather than a box to tick.
programmes.countryNote: An MYP student in Ras Al Khaimah moving into the Diploma faces the steepest jump in mathematics and the sciences, where Diploma teaching assumes algebraic fluency the MYP does not require. Caught in Year 11, that is eight to twelve weeks of work over a summer. Caught in the first Diploma report, it competes with six new subjects for the same evenings.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led and transdisciplinary, with no external examinations. The relevant feature for a Diploma-minded parent is the exhibition at the end, which asks a young student to plan and present independent work. Families who treat that as practice rather than performance tend to find the Personal Project and Extended Essay less alarming later.
programmes.countryNote: PYP provision in Ras Al Khaimah is limited compared with Dubai, so families in Al Mamourah often start in another curriculum and transfer in. A transfer at Year 6 or Year 7 is straightforward; a transfer into Year 11 or the first Diploma year is not, and the gap that needs closing is in independent written work rather than in subject content.

programmes.name: IGCSE as the route into the Diploma
programmes.description: Most Ras Al Khaimah students reach the Diploma through Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE rather than through the MYP. Extended tier in mathematics and the sciences is effectively the entry requirement for Higher Level in those subjects, and the grades out of Year 11 set the ceiling on the Diploma subject choice.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit Cambridge in the June and November series; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Those four windows matter to a Diploma plan because a November resit sits inside the first Diploma term and competes with it for the student's attention.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mamou.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Ras Al Khaimah families most often ask about, with the component that carries the calendar risk named in each case. The deadline problem and the content problem are usually different problems.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration deadline tends to arrive while Paper 3 content is still being taught at Higher Level, so students who leave the topic choice late end up writing an exploration about material they have not yet mastered. Choosing the topic early, even provisionally, removes most of that collision.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-heavy and calculator-assumed throughout. The exploration suits this course well because real data is easy to find, but students lose reflection marks by presenting the data rather than interrogating the model's fit. The deadline risk is low; the criterion risk is in reflection.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The scientific investigation is assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each. Design has to be settled before data collection, which means the highest-value session of the whole component happens weeks before any draft exists.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty propagation is examinable, routinely under-taught and quick to fix, which makes it the best value target in a short block. Paper 2 rewards algebraic rearrangement before substitution, a habit that has to be built rather than explained.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume disguises the real issue, which is command-term discipline in six and eight-mark questions. The investigation design deadline is the one that creeps up, because biology investigations need growing time or sampling time that the calendar does not forgive.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the written assignments are scheduled by the school, which means they land in the middle of other subjects' deadline weeks. Students who choose their global issue and extracts early buy themselves a calmer Year 13 regardless of ability.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries at eight hundred words each, drawn from published articles, with their own internal dates. The commonest failure is leaving all three to the same fortnight, which produces three rushed diagrams and no evaluation worth marking.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The project depends on access to an organisation and real information, so the practical constraint is other people's response times rather than the student's writing speed. Starting the approach early is worth more than starting the writing early.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The historical investigation runs to around two thousand two hundred words and depends on sources chosen before the question is finalised. Students who pick the question first and hunt sources afterwards usually have to change the question, losing a fortnight.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: The experimental study requires an ethical design and a replicable method, both of which must clear the school's internal approval before data collection. That approval step is the deadline nobody warns students about, and it sits early.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The solution requires a genuine client and a working artefact, so the dependency is a third party again. Scope is the trap: students design something ambitious in Year 12 and spend Year 13 trying to finish it instead of documenting it properly.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: The comparative study, process portfolio and exhibition accumulate across both years rather than arriving as a single deadline. Nothing can be caught up in a final term, which makes this the subject where calendar discipline matters most and is least often applied.

regions.name: Al Mamourah

regions.name: Al Nakheel
