regions.name: Al Hamra Village
regions.note: Coastal community roughly thirty minutes south and the emirate's main route into IB programmes. Diploma families in Al Mamourah are most often attached to this cluster, with the longest standard commute in RAK.

regions.name: Mina Al Arab

sections.heading: What an Al Mamourah family is really asking for
paragraphs: The phrase home tutor carries a logistics wish inside it. A family in Al Mamourah has already done two journeys to Al Nakheel or Al Hamra Village and back, and the idea of a third is unappealing. So the search is about removing travel rather than about a particular teaching format, and the honest answer has to deal with both halves of that.

In-home tutoring is a real market in the UAE and it carries a real premium. Published UAE rate surveys put in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180-500 per hour including the visit, against roughly AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The gap is the journey. In Ras Al Khaimah, paying that gap narrows the available pool rather than widening it, because the people who can reach Al Mamourah on a Tuesday evening are a short list and the people who have taught Diploma Chemistry at Higher Level are a different list.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one and live over video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, and that is a deliberate model rather than a gap in coverage. What it buys an Al Mamourah family is a tutor matched to the subject and level your child is actually sitting, available in the evening window that exists after the school run, with a written record of every session and no travel on either side.

The free trial lesson happens before any payment and runs on your child's own material, so the first session is evidence rather than a description. If the specialist your child needs is not available this month, you will be told that rather than offered somebody adjacent, which matters more in a Diploma year than in any other because the hours are finite and visible.

sections.heading: The Diploma, counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: This is the table that should be on the fridge of every Diploma household in Ras Al Khaimah and almost never is. Read forwards, the two years look spacious. Read backwards from the final paper, the sequence turns out to be tight, and the two terms that feel least urgent, the first two, are the ones carrying the work that cannot be redone. Every assessed component in the list below has a date set by your school, and once passed it is passed.

The windows in the middle column are approximate on purpose, because schools set their internal dates differently and this page publishes no specific IB session date. What is consistent is the ordering and the relative distance. The Extended Essay research question has to be settled long before anyone feels ready to settle it; the Internal Assessments cluster in Year 13's first half and collide with each other; and the mock window is the last point at which an external signal arrives in time to act on.

The right-hand column is the one to use. It names what should already be true at each stage, which turns an anxious feeling into a checklist. A family in Al Mamourah who reads this in the first term of Year 12 is in an excellent position. A family reading it in the second term of Year 13 should stop reading at the mock row and plan the final block, because the earlier rows are now history and treating them otherwise wastes the time that remains.

One structural point about the Diploma that the table makes visible: the core components are the only part of the programme where a student can lose marks through administration rather than through ability. A strong candidate who submits an Extended Essay late, or who misses a reflection session, loses points that no amount of subject knowledge recovers. Calendar discipline is therefore not an organisational nicety; it is a grade component.

sections.heading: The internal deadline is the real deadline
paragraphs: Parents hear about the IB's deadlines and plan around them. The dates that actually govern a Ras Al Khaimah student's life are the school's, and they sit earlier, sometimes much earlier, because the school needs time to mark internally, moderate, and upload. A school asking for a final Internal Assessment weeks ahead of the board's own window is not being difficult; it is building in the time its own process needs.

This produces a predictable failure. A student works to a date they have heard mentioned, submits something close to it, and is told the school deadline passed a fortnight ago. Marks are capped or the draft is submitted unfinished. The fix is purely administrative: at the start of Year 12, ask the Diploma coordinator for every internal date in writing, in one list, and put them on a single calendar alongside the family's travel plans.

The second half of the fix is spacing. Six Internal Assessments plus the Extended Essay plus the Theory of Knowledge essay cannot be distributed evenly by the school, because each subject sets its own rhythm. So they bunch, and the bunching is visible months in advance once the list exists. A student who moves one investigation design forward by three weeks because the calendar shows two landing together has done more for their Diploma than a term of extra teaching would.

A tutor's role in this is narrow and useful. The tutor works to your school's dates rather than to a generic plan, finishes a core component block two weeks before the internal deadline so the student does the final edit themselves, and names in each session note which deadline the week's work belongs to. That last detail sounds trivial and is the thing that keeps a plan alive across eighteen months.

sections.heading: What a term of Diploma support costs in this market
paragraphs: Take the monthly figure first, because that is the number a household plans around. UAE rate surveys put a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240-600 a month for budget tutoring, AED 600-1,200 for a mid-market qualified tutor, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Advertised packages in this market include online bundles from around AED 799 a month for eight sessions, and in-home bundles at AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour visits.

Converted to hours, the bands run as follows. Budget online and university-student tutors advertise from roughly AED 45-150, with one platform publishing from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150-300, with one UAE agency publishing International GCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists run AED 200-450 and above, with a UK agency quoting AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 500-650, with one provider publishing AED 650.

Every figure above belongs to the survey or provider that published it. None is an IB Gram price, and nothing on this page is a quote. What we do publish is the model: one-to-one, delivered online, with a free trial lesson before any payment and no card needed to book it. Ask for a quote and it arrives with the session length, the subject and the level attached, because an hourly rate detached from those three things means very little.

The useful comparison for an Al Mamourah family is total block cost against a named target, not hourly rate against hourly rate. Ten sessions at a specialist rate aimed at one Internal Assessment criterion is a smaller and better-defined sum than two years of a cheap weekly slot with no endpoint. Ask any prospective tutor for the number of sessions, the target, and the evidence that will show whether it worked.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the UAE calendar and when revision actually happens
paragraphs: A revision plan written without the UAE school calendar on the desk is a plan that will break. School days shorten during Ramadan, the useful study window moves to the late evening, and the weeks around Eid are effectively unavailable for new learning. None of that is a problem if the plan knows about it; all of it is a problem if the plan assumed twelve even weeks and got nine uneven ones.

The practical adjustments are small. Sessions move to a post-Iftar slot, which works because lessons are delivered online and there is no travel to schedule around prayer times or the family meal. Content-heavy teaching moves out of the Ramadan weeks and into the weeks either side, while the Ramadan sessions carry lighter work: past-paper sections, mark-scheme reading, criteria checks on a draft. The student keeps momentum without being asked to learn new material on a short night's sleep.

The same logic applies to the other fixed interruptions. Mid-term breaks, the National Day period, and family travel over the winter are all visible in advance, and a plan that absorbs them in October is a plan that survives March. Al Mamourah families who travel for part of the summer have an additional advantage with online delivery: the session runs from wherever the family is, so a four-week trip does not become a four-week gap.

One thing worth protecting deliberately. The fortnight immediately before the first paper should contain no new content and no new commitments, Ramadan or otherwise. Students who are still being taught in that window arrive at the first paper tired and uncertain, and the marks that teaching might have added are smaller than the marks the fatigue removes.

sections.heading: Where the Diploma calendar collides with university applications
paragraphs: Year 13 contains two calendars running at once and most families notice only in October. The Diploma calendar wants Internal Assessment drafts and mock preparation. The application calendar wants predicted grades, personal statements, essays, references and sometimes admissions tests. They peak within weeks of each other, and the student is the single resource both are drawing on.

Predicted grades are the hinge. They are issued by the school, they depend heavily on mock performance, and they determine which offers are realistic. A student whose mock sits two grades below the prediction they need is not short of time in May; they are short of evidence in November. That makes the term before predictions the highest-leverage point in the whole two years for a short, focused intervention in a single weak subject.

For UAE university routes there is a separate thread. The Ministry of Education equivalency process has its own documentary requirements and its own timing, and it is not something a tutoring service performs or guarantees. The British-track rule is published: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from those five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. For the IB there is no points figure published here, because none has been read on the Ministry's own site.

The sequencing advice is simple and rarely followed. Start the documentary work early, while the Diploma calendar is still light, rather than in the term where every deadline lands at once. Verify current requirements with the Ministry of Education or the emirate attestation authority directly, since they are the only authority on their own process, and no tutoring page should be the source you plan a university application around.

sections.heading: If the results disappoint: what the calendar still allows
paragraphs: A disappointing result arrives with a shorter decision window than families expect, and the options are sequenced rather than simultaneous. First comes reading the result properly, subject by subject and component by component where the school can release that detail, because the pattern decides everything that follows. A single weak component with a clear cause is a different situation from an even spread of low marks across a subject.

Then come the formal routes, each with its own window. An enquiry about results is a short-window option run by the school with the board, suitable where a mark sits just under a boundary. A retake in a later session is a longer commitment and sits in the middle of whatever the student starts next. A revised university plan may be faster and better than either, and is the option families consider last when it often deserves to be considered first.

For IGCSE siblings the equivalent arithmetic is clearer because the boards publish it. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE centres, and Pearson International GCSE runs in May/June and November, so a weak result in one series has a defined next window. The November 2026 Pearson timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those past dates show the rhythm; the live official timetable is the only version to plan from.

What a tutor contributes at this stage is diagnosis rather than reassurance. A marked script or a component breakdown, read against the published criteria or mark scheme, tells you whether five months of focused work would change the outcome or whether the sensible move is a different route. That is a conversation worth having in the first week after results rather than the fourth, because several of the windows close quickly.
bullets: Read the result component by component before choosing a route

sections.heading: Who may legally tutor in the UAE, and the one question to ask
paragraphs: The permit question takes one sentence to ask and most families never ask it. Private tuition in the UAE operates under a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation and granted free of charge for two years. So the question to any prospective tutor is whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and a straight answer is a reasonable expectation.

The eligible categories are wider than most parents assume: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service listing covers issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system, with no fee listed and a two-working-day completion time.

Two cautions attach. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and the ministry has not published the amounts, so a specific figure quoted to you has been invented by whoever quoted it. And the permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, which is the same position ADEK takes in its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi.

None of this amounts to an endorsement of anybody. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. A service that uses a regulator's name as an adjective about itself is making a claim it should be asked to evidence with a permit number.

sections.heading: The honesty line on the Extended Essay and Internal Assessments
paragraphs: This has to be stated rather than assumed, because services in this market sell finished Internal Assessments at a published price and they appear in the same search results as this page. The boundary here is firm: a tutor explains the criteria, works through published exemplars, questions whether a research question or an investigation design can carry the required depth, and reads the student's own draft to name which criterion is under-served.

What the tutor does not do is produce the work. Nobody here writes, finishes or edits to completion an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay. Submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice under the board's rules, and the penalty falls on the candidate rather than on whoever was paid, two years after the decision was taken. No fee arrangement compensates for a withheld Diploma.

There is a parallel rule about materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson. They are cited and linked here rather than reproduced or supplied, because redistribution is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure as well. A service offering a bundle of mark schemes as a selling point is offering something it does not own.

The practical effect on a core-component block is that it finishes two weeks before the school's internal deadline. The student does the final edit, in their own words, having been told clearly which criterion needs more. That is both the compliant arrangement and the better one, because a student who has made the final decisions can defend the work in a reflection session, and a student who has not cannot.

process.title: Send the internal deadline list
process.description: Before anything else, ask your child's Diploma coordinator for every internal date in writing: Extended Essay drafts and reflections, Theory of Knowledge title and essay, and the six Internal Assessment deadlines. That list is what a plan is built from, and most families have never seen it in one place.

process.title: Name the subject, the level and the component
process.description: Chemistry Higher Level is not one problem. A weak Paper 2 and an investigation stuck at the design stage need different people and different work. Tell us the subject, the level, and which component is actually behind, then send the marked script or the current draft.

process.title: Free trial lesson on your own material
process.description: A real lesson rather than a consultation call, run on a question your child got wrong or a draft paragraph that is not working. No payment and no card are needed to book it, and you are welcome to watch. What you are judging is how the tutor handles being stuck.

process.title: A plan written backwards
process.description: You get the sequence in writing, dated from your school's deadlines rather than from today: which weeks cover which topics, which sessions address which criterion, and when the block stops. Core-component blocks are planned to finish two weeks early by default.

process.title: Session notes tied to a deadline
process.description: Each note says what was covered, what was set, and which deadline the week's work belongs to. Over eighteen months that last detail is what keeps a long plan from quietly drifting, and it gives you something concrete to check rather than an impression to trust.

process.title: A clear answer when nobody is free
process.description: For a thinly taught Higher Level subject there may be no specialist available this month. You will be told so and given a date or an alternative plan. In a Diploma year a clear no is worth more than a quiet substitution that costs six weeks to discover.

whyPoints.title: The calendar is the plan
whyPoints.description: Every plan here is written back from your school's internal deadlines and the May session rather than forward from the day you enquire. That ordering is the whole difference between support that lands where it matters and a weekly slot that runs for two years without a target.

whyPoints.title: Core components treated as components
whyPoints.description: The Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay and six Internal Assessments carry marks and hard dates, and they are the part of the Diploma where a strong student can lose points to administration. They get their own blocks here rather than being squeezed into subject lessons.

whyPoints.title: Rates printed with their publisher
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page names the survey or provider that published it and is presented as the market, not as our price. Three of six ranking pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote US dollars, which UAE families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: A specialist, not the nearest available person
whyPoints.description: In an emirate where a Higher Level cohort can number a dozen students, matching by subject and level beats matching by distance. Delivering online is what makes that possible, and it is why the format is stated plainly instead of being discovered after payment.

whyPoints.title: No IB dates invented on this page
whyPoints.description: The IB's own site is the only authority for session and results dates, so none are published here. Cambridge and Pearson dates are cited with their sources, and the past ones keep their year because that is what makes them checkable.

whyPoints.title: A published boundary on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Teaching, criteria, exemplars and feedback on the student's own work. No writing or finishing of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay, because the malpractice penalty falls on the candidate and the line belongs in public rather than in terms.

faqs.question: Will a tutor actually come to our villa in Al Mamourah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run in India only. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one and live over video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. In-home tutoring does exist in the Ras Al Khaimah market at published rates of roughly AED 180-500 per hour including travel, against roughly AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor. In this emirate the premium mainly narrows the pool of available teachers, which is the opposite of what a family paying extra expects.

faqs.question: Which internal Diploma deadlines should I be asking the school about?
faqs.answer: All of them, in writing, at the start of Year 12. The list should include the Extended Essay subject and supervisor allocation, the research question deadline, each draft deadline, the reflection session dates, the Theory of Knowledge title and essay deadlines, and the draft and final dates for all six Internal Assessments. Schools set these earlier than the board's own windows because they need time to mark and moderate. Once you have the list on one calendar, the weeks where deadlines bunch become visible months ahead.

faqs.question: When does the Extended Essay work actually need to start?
faqs.answer: Earlier than it feels reasonable to start. The subject and supervisor are usually allocated around eighteen months before the final papers, and the research question should be settled within a few months of that, because a question that is too broad produces a first draft nobody can rescue. The single most valuable session on the component happens before any writing, mapping the intended argument against four thousand words until the question is narrow enough to answer in that space properly.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change a revision timetable in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: School days shorten and the useful study window moves to the late evening, so sessions commonly shift to a post-Iftar slot. Because lessons are delivered online there is no travel to arrange around prayer times or the family meal. The practical adjustment is to move content-heavy teaching out of the Ramadan weeks and into the weeks either side, keeping lighter work inside them: timed paper sections, mark-scheme reading, a criteria check on a draft. Families who plan this a month ahead lose almost no sessions.

faqs.question: My child's mock result is far below the predicted grade. What now?
faqs.answer: Read the mock component by component rather than as a single number, because the pattern decides the plan. A strong Paper 1 beside a weak Paper 2 points at timing or algebraic rearrangement under pressure, which responds quickly. An even spread of low marks points at content coverage, which takes longer. The term before predicted grades are issued is the highest-leverage moment in the whole Diploma for a short focused block, because predictions rest on mock evidence rather than on potential.

faqs.question: Is fortnightly enough for a Higher Level subject across two years?
faqs.answer: For maintenance, usually yes. A fortnightly slot exists to stop a subject drifting between report cards, which is where most Diploma damage accumulates without anybody noticing. It is not enough to close a gap that already exists, and it is not enough in the final term, where the pattern should step up to weekly paper work. Families who run fortnightly from early in Year 12 generally buy fewer total sessions than families who start weekly in the last six months.

faqs.question: Can the tutor work to my child's own school deadlines rather than a generic plan?
faqs.answer: That is the default here, and it is why we ask for the internal deadline list before the first session. A plan written against your school's dates will put Extended Essay planning in the weeks your school wants a draft and investigation design in the weeks your school requires approval. A generic Diploma schedule ignores the fact that two Ras Al Khaimah schools running the same programme can set their internal dates months apart from each other.

faqs.question: Does a Higher Level cohort of twelve students matter to my child's chances?
faqs.answer: It does not change the grade boundaries, which are set externally, and it does not mean the teaching is weak. What it changes is the margin for specialism. In a cohort that size, one teacher may cover several Diploma courses, and the hardest Higher Level content gets whatever attention a crowded timetable allows. That is arithmetic rather than anybody's failing, and it is the clearest practical reason an online specialist adds something in a northern emirate that it would add less of in Dubai.

faqs.question: What exactly may a tutor do with an Internal Assessment draft?
faqs.answer: Explain each criterion, work through published exemplars, question whether the design or topic can carry the required depth, and read the student's own draft to say which criterion is under-served. What a tutor must not do is supply sentences, rewrite the argument, or edit a draft to a finished state. Submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice and the penalty falls on the candidate. Blocks here finish two weeks before the internal deadline so the student makes the final decisions.

faqs.question: Do we need to worry about equivalency while the Diploma is still running?
faqs.answer: Start the documentary work early rather than in the term when every Diploma deadline lands at once, but do not treat it as a tutoring matter. Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process with its own requirements and timing, and no tutoring service performs it or guarantees an outcome from it. The published British-track rule asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match a Diploma specialist for Al Mamourah?
faqs.answer: For mathematics, the three sciences, English and economics, usually within a few days. For a thinly taught Higher Level subject it can take longer, and if nobody suitable is free you will be told that and offered a date rather than placed with somebody adjacent to the subject. In a Diploma year, six sessions spent discovering a mismatch are six weeks that do not come back, so a clear answer about availability is worth more than a fast one.

faqs.question: Can sessions run while we are travelling over the summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is one of the practical advantages of delivering lessons over video. The session runs from wherever the family is, so a four-week trip does not become a four-week gap in a plan that has deadlines waiting at the other end. The one thing worth agreeing in advance is the time zone the sessions will run in, because a slot that works on Gulf Standard Time may land awkwardly elsewhere and an awkward slot quietly becomes a cancelled one.

faqs.question: Who is legally allowed to give private lessons in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Anyone holding the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Tutoring without the permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and the ministry has published no amounts, so any figure quoted to you is invented.

faqs.question: Is it a good idea to pay my child's own Diploma teacher for extra lessons?
faqs.answer: It is the arrangement to avoid. The MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Beyond the rules it is poor practice on its own terms: the person marking your child's Internal Assessment should not also be paid to prepare it. An independent specialist gives you a second, unconflicted read.

faqs.question: What should the last fortnight before the papers contain?
faqs.answer: Timed past papers, mark-scheme reading, and nothing new. If a content gap surfaces in that window it gets a note and a two-minute recap rather than a lesson, because reopening material late reliably costs more marks than it recovers in a tired student. Blocks here are designed to end two weeks before the first paper for exactly this reason, so the final fortnight belongs to the student rather than to anybody's timetable.

faqs.question: How do we tell whether the tuition is working?
faqs.answer: Compare a marked script with a marked script. A diagnostic paper at the start and a comparable paper eight sessions later, both marked against the published scheme, give you component-level movement instead of an impression. On a core component the measure is the criterion band rather than a paper mark. The session notes tell you what was set and whether it was done, and if the work was done and nothing has moved, the match is wrong and should change.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mamou.closingHeading: Get the deadline list, then build the plan
ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mamou.closingBody: The most useful thing an Al Mamourah family can do this week costs nothing: ask your child's Diploma coordinator for every internal deadline in writing, in one list. Send it to us with the subject, the level and the component that is behind, and you will get a plan written backwards from those dates rather than forward from today. The trial lesson is free, runs on your child's own material, and you are welcome to watch it. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time, and we will tell you before you book if the specialist you need is not free this month.

intro.heading: The honest answer to the question you are actually asking
paragraphs: Al Marjan Island is a set of reclaimed islands reaching into the Gulf off the Ras Al Khaimah coast, heavily weighted towards apartments, serviced residences and resort development. There is no school on the island itself, so the school run goes inland or down the coast, and visitor access is more involved than anywhere else in the emirate. All of which matters for logistics and none of which answers the question a parent is actually typing.

That question is specific: is there anybody reachable who has taught Higher Level Chemistry, or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or Economics at Standard Level, to an examination class? Not somebody who studied it. Somebody who has taught it, knows what the criteria reward and can name them. Every page competing for this search implies the answer is yes for every subject. None of them publishes a coverage limit. Across the competitor pages researched for the UAE clusters, not one discloses a subject or level it cannot cover, and several route enquiries to telephone numbers outside the UAE without saying so.

The truthful answer has three parts. For most Standard Level subjects and for the common Higher Level ones, coverage online is good and a match usually takes days rather than weeks. For a small number of combinations - a narrow Higher Level option close to a session, or an unusual language - coverage is thin and the honest response is a conditional yes or a no. And locally, inside Ras Al Khaimah, for Higher Level sciences and mathematics, the pool is genuinely small, because the emirate has a comparatively modest private-school sector and the few experienced teachers in it are usually committed in the evenings.

This page therefore does something uncommon: it publishes the coverage picture, the fallback options when a specialist is not available, and a method for testing whether anyone's claimed expertise is real. That last part is useful whoever you end up hiring, including if it is not us. Ten minutes of the right questions separates a Diploma specialist from a capable graduate who has read the syllabus, and the questions are not difficult. It is also the part of this page we would keep if we could keep only one.

On delivery, because the URL says home tutor: IB Gram teaches Al Marjan Island students one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not place a tutor at a UAE address, and in-person visiting is a service we run only in India. On an island with involved access and no school of its own, that removes the logistics problem entirely. It also means the coverage question is answered from a national pool rather than from whoever is willing to cross the causeway at five o'clock.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-marja.programmesIntro: Coverage differs by programme as well as by subject, and it is worth knowing which part of the IB you are actually asking about before you ask anyone whether they can help.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, no external examinations, reported against learning outcomes with an Exhibition in the final year. Coverage here is not a specialist question at all: what a primary student needs is reading fluency, number fact recall and the ability to work independently for twenty minutes, and a good general primary teacher provides it. Anyone claiming a scarce specialism at this stage is overselling.
programmes.countryNote: Families on Al Marjan Island with primary-age children face the longest school run in the emirate, which argues for keeping any additional support at home and short. Two twenty-minute sessions a week work better at this age than one long one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-assessed against descriptors A to D with a Personal Project in the final year. Coverage is comfortable across the main subject groups because the content depth is moderate and the skills are transferable. Where it genuinely narrows is the Personal Project, which benefits from somebody who has supervised one rather than from a subject teacher.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Ras Al Khaimah family moves between a Middle Years school and an IGCSE school, the two sequence topics differently and real content gaps appear in maths and science. A single diagnostic session finds them; a summer usually closes them.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, usually three at Higher Level, scored out of 45, with written papers plus an internally assessed component in each subject marked against lettered criteria. This is where coverage becomes a real question, because the combination of subject, level and live component narrows the pool quickly. A Higher Level science with an investigation at planning stage needs a different person from a Standard Level revision request.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, with November available where offered. This page carries no specific IB examination or results date, because the IB's own site cannot be checked automatically; the coordinator's internal deadline sheet is the operative calendar.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma courses alongside a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Coverage for the Diploma courses taken within it is the same as for the Diploma itself. The reflective project is the thinnest area in the whole IB for tutoring supply, simply because far fewer people have supervised one.
programmes.countryNote: Where a school in the northern emirates offers this programme, confirm which components are internally and which externally assessed before planning support, because the balance differs from the Diploma and changes what is worth buying.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-marja.subjectsIntro: Here is the coverage picture subject by subject, stated as plainly as we can. Where it is thin, that is the honest position rather than a negotiating one.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Standard Level coverage is good and matches are quick. Higher Level is narrower, because the course is demanding and fewer tutors have taught it to completion. Ask a candidate what the Exploration criteria reward and whether they have supervised one; the answer separates teachers from graduates immediately.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Reasonable coverage at both levels, though fewer tutors have taught the Higher Level statistics content in depth than claim to. The useful test is asking how they would handle a modelling question where the technology does the computation and the marks sit in the interpretation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Standard Level coverage is good. Higher Level is one of the two thinnest areas in the whole Diploma for tutoring supply, and locally in Ras Al Khaimah it is close to absent. Investigation coaching at Higher Level narrows it further, because it requires someone who knows the criteria rather than the chemistry.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The other thin area at Higher Level. Uncertainty propagation and error analysis are the skills that matter and the ones most often absent in a candidate who has studied physics rather than taught it. Ask how they would teach propagating an uncertainty through a multiplication; a specialist answers in a sentence.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Good coverage at both levels, and the easiest of the three sciences to match quickly. The quality variable is investigation coaching: narrowing a research question until the variation is controllable is a skill distinct from knowing biology, and it is the one worth testing for.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Solid coverage, with one caveat: set texts vary by school and cohort, so a tutor's familiarity with the course does not mean familiarity with your child's texts. That is usually fine, because the assessed skill is analysis rather than content, but establish it rather than assuming.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Good coverage at both levels and quick to match. The differentiator is the internally assessed commentary work spread across the course, which needs a tutor who schedules rather than crams. Ask how they would sequence the commentaries against the school's other deadlines.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Reasonable coverage. The Higher Level research-based component with its own word limit and criteria is the narrower part, and the test is whether a candidate can describe what distinguishes a mid-band response from an upper-band one in that component specifically.

subjects.name: Languages other than English
subjects.description: The thinnest category overall, and genuinely so. Coverage for the most commonly taught languages is workable; for less common ones it is limited and the honest answer is often a conditional yes dependent on timing, or a no. We would rather say that than place a native speaker with no assessment knowledge.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Coverage depends on the Extended Essay's subject area rather than on the essay as a task. Theory of Knowledge support is reasonably available and uneven in quality, because arguing about knowledge is easy and teaching a student to answer a prescribed title is not.

sections.heading: Coverage and fallback, published rather than implied
paragraphs: This table is the reason the page exists. It states, by subject group and level, how coverage actually looks, roughly how long a match takes, and what happens when nobody suitable is free. No competitor page researched across the ten UAE query clusters discloses a coverage limit of any kind, which means a parent cannot tell the difference between a provider with deep coverage and one that says yes to everything and works it out afterwards.

Read it with one thing in mind: the limiting factor is almost never the subject alone. It is the combination of subject, level, live component and time slot. Higher Level Chemistry with an investigation at planning stage, needed at 7pm on a Tuesday, is a much narrower request than Standard Level Chemistry revision at any time. Families who can flex the slot usually widen the pool more than families who can flex the subject, which is not obvious until somebody says it.

The fallback column is the part worth reading twice, because it describes what honest providers do and most do not describe at all. A diagnostic block with a specialist followed by weekly work with a strong generalist is a real option that works, provided the family knows that is what they have bought. The same arrangement sold as a specialist throughout is a misrepresentation, and it is common.

Where the honest answer is no, we say no. That costs us a booking and saves a family a term. The alternative - placing a capable graduate who has read the syllabus with a Higher Level candidate eight weeks from a session - produces a mismatch that becomes obvious in week three, by which point the weeks are gone and so is the money.

sections.heading: How to test a claim of expertise in ten minutes
paragraphs: Whoever you hire, including if it is not us, this is the most useful ten minutes you will spend. The aim is to distinguish somebody who has taught a Diploma subject to an examination class from somebody who studied it well and has read the guide. Both will sound competent in a general conversation about the subject. Only one of them will answer these questions crisply.

The questions work because they ask about assessment rather than about content. A graduate who got a 7 in Higher Level Chemistry knows chemistry. They may have no idea what the investigation criteria reward, what distinguishes a mid-band evaluation from an upper-band one, or why an uncontrolled variable caps later criteria regardless of the write-up. A teacher knows those things because they have marked them, repeatedly, and watched moderation adjust them.

Ask them with the expectation of a short answer. A specialist names criteria, describes a common failure, and gives an example from experience. A non-specialist generalises, talks about engagement and confidence, or asks you what the school has said. Neither answer is dishonest; they describe different people, and only one of them is what a Higher Level candidate needs eight weeks out.

One further test, the cheapest of all: send a piece of your child's marked work before you book anything, and ask what it shows. A specialist comes back with two or three specific things and what they imply. A generalist comes back with encouragement. The free trial lesson is the same test at greater length, and the thing to watch in it is whether the tutor diagnoses before explaining and whether your child does most of the talking.

sections.heading: The red flags in this particular market
paragraphs: The tutoring market serving UAE families contains a number of practices that are worth recognising, because several of them appear on pages currently ranking for exactly this search. None of what follows is speculation; each item was observed on a live competitor page during research in October 2026, and each is either a regulatory exposure, a consumer-protection problem, or a straightforward misrepresentation.

The most serious is the sale of completed assessed work. One site in this market advertises finished Internal Assessments at a published price. That is an academic-honesty breach, and its consequences fall on the student rather than on the seller: submitted work must be the student's own, and a malpractice finding can end a Diploma. Any provider willing to sell that is telling you what they think of the student's interests.

The second is claimed regulator approval. Phrases implying that a tutoring service is approved, accredited or licensed by an education authority are the most dangerous available on these pages, because the specific permits involved are issued to institutions with premises and are verifiable. A tutoring platform that does not hold one and implies it does is making a claim a parent can check and should.

The others are quieter. Self-asserted star ratings in page markup that do not match anything countable. Prices quoted in US dollars to families who transact in dirhams, or no price at all - three of the six main pages in this cluster publish no figure, and one refuses to answer its own pricing question in its own FAQ. Telephone numbers outside the UAE presented as the local contact route. And statistics with no sample size, date or method attached: percentages of students, median scores, satisfaction figures. The table below lists what to look for and what it indicates.

sections.heading: Who is legally permitted to tutor your child, and how to check
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated, which is a better situation than the vagueness most pages leave parents with. The route is a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. The eligible categories are deliberately wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

The ministry lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are, in the ministry's own words, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any figure circulating online should be treated as unverified, and we will not repeat one here.

Two practical points follow. Because the permit is free and takes two working days, there is no cost or administrative excuse for not holding one, which makes it a fair and easy question to ask. And a tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: it requires an educational services permit from the relevant authority, with initial approval first and annual renewal. Nobody should describe themselves as regulator-approved on the strength of an individual tuition permit.

Our own position, stated plainly: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson, and occupies no office in the UAE. There is also a conduct dimension worth knowing: in Abu Dhabi the education department's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit carries its own code of conduct. Whatever the local rule, your child's own classroom teacher is the wrong person to hire privately.

sections.heading: Why the local pool is thin, in terms we can actually support
paragraphs: It is worth being precise about this rather than gesturing at it, because the reason matters for what a family should do. Ras Al Khaimah is a northern emirate with its own education regulator and a private-school sector concentrated around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab. A Diploma subject taught at Higher Level in a small number of settings produces a small number of teachers with experience of it, and a fraction of those take private work after a full teaching day.

Compare that with Dubai, where the private school sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for a share of enrolment and seven further private schools, including three International Baccalaureate schools, opening for the 2026-27 intake. The arithmetic of supply is simply different: a subject taught in many settings produces many experienced teachers, and some of them are free on a Tuesday evening.

This is not a judgement about Ras Al Khaimah's schools, several of which are long-established and well regarded. It is a statement about numbers, and it has one practical consequence: in this emirate, remote one-to-one is not a convenience or a cost saving. For Higher Level sciences and mathematics it is the difference between a specialist and whoever is available.

It also explains why coverage transparency matters more here than it would in Dubai. A family in a large market who hires a mismatch can replace them easily. A family on Al Marjan Island who hires the only locally available person has no second option, which is precisely why they deserve to know in advance whether that person has taught the course or studied it.

sections.heading: What we do when we cannot match you
paragraphs: Saying no is the part of this business nobody writes about, so here is how it works. If a request is for a subject, level, component and time slot we cannot cover with someone who has genuinely taught it, we tell you at the enquiry stage rather than after a trial lesson. The message names what is thin and why, which is usually the combination rather than the subject on its own.

Then we offer the real alternatives, described accurately. A different session slot often opens a materially wider pool, and families who can move an hour frequently solve the problem by moving an hour. Where that does not work, a diagnostic block with a specialist followed by weekly delivery by a strong generalist against the specialist's written plan is a genuine option, and we describe it in exactly those terms rather than as a specialist arrangement. Where neither works, the answer is to wait or to look elsewhere, and we say which.

We also tell you when you do not need what you are asking for. A family requesting a term of weekly Higher Level support for a problem that is two sessions of command-term work does not need the term, and selling it to them would be easy. The diagnosis from a marked script usually settles this in ten minutes, which is why we ask for the script before quoting anything.

None of this is generosity; it is the only version of this business that survives contact with a small market. In an emirate where families talk to each other and the alternatives are few, a mismatch sold as a match costs more than the booking was worth. The free trial lesson exists for the same reason: it is a test you run on us, with no card details taken and no obligation afterwards.

sections.heading: What a good first month looks like from here
paragraphs: Assume a match exists and has been made. A first month that is working looks specific rather than pleasant. In week one the tutor has produced a written diagnosis from the student's own marked work, naming two or three things costing marks and what the following sessions will do about each. If week one ended with a general impression and a plan to cover the syllabus, something has already gone wrong.

By week two or three the student should be doing most of the talking and most of the writing, with the tutor questioning rather than explaining. The single most reliable predictor of a wasted term is a tutor who lectures competently for fifty minutes while a student nods. It feels like value and produces almost nothing, because the only thing that moves marks is the student attempting, failing and being corrected.

By the end of the month there should be a piece of evidence: a timed section, a narrowed research question, a redrafted paragraph that now does what the criteria ask. One concrete artefact beats four weeks of positive reports. And there should be a review conversation, short, against the target that was written down at the start, with a real decision about whether to continue.

If the answer is no, say it early. The only thing wasted by changing a tutor at week three is three weeks; the cost of changing at week twelve is a term. In a market this size we would rather be told at week three and keep the relationship than discover at week twelve that a family quietly stopped booking. That is also why we publish the coverage table above: the conversations that go badly are nearly always the ones that started with a yes that should have been a no.

process.description: It is the cheapest test of a provider that exists. Ask what it shows. A specialist comes back with two or three specific observations and what they imply; a generalist comes back with encouragement. Run that test on us before you run it on anyone else.

process.description: One 45 to 60-minute one-to-one session over live video, no card details, no obligation. Watch whether the tutor diagnoses before explaining and whether your child talks. Those two signals predict the term better than any credential on a profile.

process.description: One concrete artefact and a short conversation against the written target. If nothing moved, change the plan or the tutor now rather than in the spring. Three weeks is a cheap loss; a term is not, and in a small emirate it is also hard to recover from.

faqs.question: Is there actually anyone in Ras Al Khaimah who teaches Higher Level Chemistry privately?
faqs.answer: Locally, very few, and that is the honest answer. The emirate has a comparatively small private-school sector concentrated around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab, so a Higher Level subject taught in a handful of settings produces a handful of experienced teachers, most of them committed in the evenings. Online the picture is better but still narrower than for Standard Level, particularly close to a session or where investigation coaching is needed. We publish that in the coverage table rather than discovering it with you after a trial lesson.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a tutor has really taught my child's subject?
faqs.answer: Ask four questions and listen for specificity. Which criteria is the Internal Assessment marked against, and roughly what is each worth? Where do students in this subject lose the most marks? How would you narrow this research question? Have you taught this subject at this level to a final-year class, and when? A teacher answers each in a sentence or two with examples. Someone who studied the subject well will generalise, talk about confidence and engagement, or ask what the school has said.

faqs.question: What happens if you cannot find the right tutor for us?
faqs.answer: We say so at the enquiry stage and name the constraint, which is usually the combination of level, component and time slot rather than the subject alone. Then we offer the real alternatives: a different session slot, which often opens a materially wider pool, or a diagnostic block with a specialist followed by weekly delivery by a strong generalist against the specialist's written plan. If neither works, the answer is to wait or look elsewhere, and we will say which rather than placing a mismatch.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects are hardest to find a specialist for?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Chemistry and Higher Level Physics are the two thinnest in the sciences, with Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches close behind. Less commonly taught languages are the thinnest category overall, and for some of them the honest answer is no rather than a conditional yes. Biology, Economics, Business Management and English A are comfortable at both levels. The Career-related Programme's reflective project is thinner than any subject, simply because very few people have supervised one.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need a UAE permit to teach my child online?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is free of charge, valid for two years, with a stated completion time of two working days, and it covers school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Because it costs nothing, there is no excuse for not holding one, which makes it a reasonable question to ask any provider.

faqs.question: Why should I trust a page that tells me what it cannot do?
faqs.answer: Because the alternative is a page that says yes to everything, and in a small emirate the cost of that falls on you. A family in a large market who hires a mismatch replaces them next week. A family on Al Marjan Island who hires the only available person has no second option, so the value of knowing in advance is much higher here. Publishing the limits also makes the positive claims checkable, which is the only way a claim about teaching experience means anything.

faqs.question: Can we change tutors if the first match does not work?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you should say so early rather than waiting politely. The only thing lost by changing at week three is three weeks; changing at week twelve costs a term. What we ask is a reason, because sometimes the problem is the plan rather than the person, and a new tutor following the same wrong plan changes nothing. Bring the marked evidence from the first month to that conversation and it usually becomes obvious within minutes which of the two it was.

faqs.question: What should the first session actually deliver?
faqs.answer: A written diagnosis from your child's own marked work, naming two or three specific things costing marks and what the next sessions will do about each. Not a syllabus overview, not a get-to-know-you hour, and not a lecture on the topic you named in your enquiry. If the tutor accepted your diagnosis instead of making their own, the rest of the block will be built on it, and the commonest reason a term produces nothing is that the wrong problem was being solved throughout.

faqs.question: Are online sessions workable from an apartment on Al Marjan Island?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the practical advantages here are larger than elsewhere in the emirate. There is no school on the island, visitor access is the most involved in Ras Al Khaimah, and the school run is the longest, so an arrangement that requires someone to arrive at a fixed hour degrades quickly. A live video session needs a usable connection, a quiet surface and a device the student can write on or alongside. Sessions also continue unchanged while a family travels, which households here do more than most.

faqs.question: Should we hire our child's own teacher privately if they offer?
faqs.answer: No. In Abu Dhabi the education department's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries its own code of conduct. Whatever the rule in a given emirate, the arrangement puts a teacher in the position of being paid by one family while assessing their child alongside others, which is bad for everyone including the teacher. Hire somebody with no connection to the school and no role in the student's assessment.

faqs.question: How long does a match normally take?
faqs.answer: For Standard Level subjects and the common Higher Level ones, usually a few days. For Higher Level Chemistry, Physics or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, often a week or more, and longer close to a session when the few available specialists are fully booked. Flexibility on the time slot shortens it more than anything else a family can offer. If a provider promises a specialist in any subject within twenty-four hours, ask what they mean by specialist, because the arithmetic of supply does not support it.

faqs.question: Why do some tutoring sites not publish any prices?
faqs.answer: It is a pattern in this market rather than an accident. Of the main pages researched for these searches, three publish no AED figure at all, one refuses to answer its own pricing question in its own FAQ, and two quote US dollars at families who transact in dirhams. Published market rates exist and are easy to cite: qualified online subject tutors run roughly AED 150-300 an hour, and in-home visits roughly AED 180-500 on tables read in October 2026. Ask any provider for an AED figure in writing before booking.

faqs.question: What should I make of a five-star rating on a tutoring site?
faqs.answer: Very little unless it is backed by countable, attributable reviews that match what the page's markup claims. Pages in this market publish ratings that contradict themselves within a single page, and self-asserted review markup is against Google's structured-data policy and a consumer-protection exposure as a commercial representation. Judge instead on things you can verify: whether the tutor can name the criteria, what they say about your child's marked script, and what the first month produced. Those are harder to fake than a number.

faqs.question: Can you help with the Extended Essay if the subject area is unusual?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the determining factor is the subject area rather than the essay as a task. Supervision support for an essay in a mainstream subject is comfortable to cover; a narrow area may not be, and the honest answer then is no rather than a generalist pretending otherwise. What is coverable in almost every case is the process: narrowing the research question, planning the reading, and responding to the student's own drafts against the criteria. The writing itself remains entirely the student's own work.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nakhe.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here teach IB Diploma subjects at Higher and Standard Level, and Middle Years Programme subjects where a student is heading into the Diploma. Each is matched to the course and the level rather than to a district, with evening availability shown in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Two districts, one school run, and the comparison worth making
paragraphs: Al Nakheel is the commercial centre of Ras Al Khaimah, and it is where most of the emirate's independent tutors actually live. Khuzam, inland and a short drive south, is where one of the main British curriculum campuses sits. A Diploma family in Al Nakheel is therefore in an unusual position: the local tutor supply is on their doorstep, and the school their child attends almost certainly is not. That combination produces a specific set of questions, and this page answers them in order.

The first question is whether the district matters at all. For logistics it does. A child at a Khuzam campus finishing at a quarter past three reaches an Al Nakheel flat somewhere around four, and a child travelling to the Al Hamra coast reaches it later. That decides whether a session can start at five or has to start at six, how many evenings a week are realistic, and whether Saturday morning is a better slot than any weekday at all. Those are real constraints and they belong in the plan.

For the academic answer it does not matter in the slightest, and that is the argument this page makes in the middle. The marks in a Higher Level chemistry paper are lost in the same places whether the student lives in Al Nakheel, Al Uraibi, Khuzam or Al Dhait. The mathematics exploration is marked against the same five criteria. The extended essay has the same four-thousand-word ceiling. What changes with the postcode is who can physically reach you, which is a constraint on supply and not a feature of the teaching.

This is where the honest statement belongs. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in Ras Al Khaimah or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons here are one-to-one online tuition over live video, with a shared whiteboard, annotated work and a recording afterwards. Because the delivery is remote, your district stops filtering the shortlist, and a student in Al Nakheel can work with whoever has actually taught Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level rather than whoever is twenty minutes away.

What follows is deliberately concrete. A district-by-district comparison of what the school day does to an evening. The Higher and Standard Level weightings, because most families know the labels and not the percentages. The two mathematics courses and which one a degree route expects. The exploration criteria, letter by letter, with the marks attached, which nobody else in this search publishes. The word limits across the Diploma core. And the boundary a tutor may not cross with any of it. None of it requires you to contact anybody to be useful, which is the test we would apply to any page selling something.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nakhe.programmesIntro: Al Nakheel households sit across the full IB continuum because the city centre feeds several campuses. Each programme below is described by what it actually demands of a student, with a note on what that means for a family living in the city rather than next to the school.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units, an inquiry stance and no external examinations, finishing with the exhibition in the final year. Reading fluency and secure number facts are the two things that predict everything afterwards, and they are also the two things an inquiry framework does not report on directly.
programmes.countryNote: City-centre families often have the shortest school run at this age and the longest later, because primary provision is closer than the Diploma campuses. That makes the primary years the cheapest and easiest time to establish a weekly routine, and it is the stage most households skip.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years, eight subject groups, and four criteria per subject each marked out of eight. A grade is a judgement against descriptors rather than a percentage, which is why a 5 feels alarming and is not. The personal project in the final year is the first piece of genuinely independent work most students meet.
programmes.countryNote: The decision that matters in Al Nakheel is the one at the end of the programme: Diploma at an international campus, or Year 10 and 11 IGCSE at a British one. The two routes have different commutes from the city centre, and families often choose on travel and then discover the academic consequences later.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the extended essay, theory of knowledge and creativity-activity-service. The second year is where the external papers bite and the first is where the internal assessments are either started properly or left too late. Both halves need different kinds of support.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma is where the local tutor supply in this emirate runs out fastest. A Higher Level mathematics or chemistry teacher within a short drive of Al Nakheel may not exist in a given year, and the usual local substitute is a subject graduate who has never taught the course. Those are not the same product.

programmes.name: IB Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma courses combined with a career-related study and a reflective project, for students who want depth in two or three academic subjects rather than six. Less common in the northern emirates, and worth knowing about because it is sometimes a better fit than a Diploma a student is struggling to carry.
programmes.countryNote: Where a school offers it, the Career-related Programme changes the support question from breadth to depth: two or three subjects need proper attention rather than six needing maintenance. For a family budgeting an evening a week, that is a materially easier problem.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nakhe.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Al Nakheel families ask about, with the specific place marks are lost in each. The level matters more than the subject name: Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra homework, and the weightings in the next section show why.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Higher Level, Paper 3 is an extended investigation requiring sustained reasoning rather than recall, and proof technique separates the top grades. At Standard Level the losses are usually mechanical: algebraic slips and unfinished method lines that forfeit marks a correct answer would have earned.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with heavy graphical calculator use. Marks go missing where a model is chosen without justification and where a conclusion is stated without returning to the context the question set up. Both are technique repairs rather than content gaps.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level depth exposes weak algebra immediately, and the data-analysis questions reward a trained habit of checking units, uncertainties and significant figures. Pairing physics with mathematics under one tutor usually saves a family a whole second arrangement.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics and organic mechanisms carry the Higher Level grade. In the internal assessment the marks are lost in evaluation far more often than in method, because students describe what went wrong without quantifying how much it mattered.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Wide content and unforgiving terminology. The common and expensive error is buying content hours when the real failure is command-term reading: a student who explains where the paper asked them to evaluate will sit mid-band whatever they know.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the evaluation half of extended answers decide the grade. The internal assessment commentaries need a tutor who will question an article choice rather than hand one over, which is a boundary worth checking before you book.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the stimulus is the grade. Students who respond to weak marks by learning more theory score the same again, and one properly marked paper makes that visible in about ten minutes.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the unseen analysis in Paper 1 are both learnable techniques with a long practice tail. Higher Level adds the essay, with its own word limit, and that is where structure rather than reading matters most.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Knowing studies is necessary and not sufficient. Marks sit in deploying a named study as evidence for one specific argument, and students who revise by summarising studies tend to plateau exactly where that stops working.

subjects.name: Theory of knowledge and the extended essay
subjects.description: Supervised rather than taught. The essay is capped at 4,000 words and the theory of knowledge essay at 1,600, and the support is interrogation of the student's own drafting. The writing belongs to the candidate throughout, with no exceptions.

The academic content of a Diploma subject does not change across them, and the middle of this page explains why.

regions.note: Inland, built around a British curriculum campus, and roughly fifteen minutes from the city centre outside peak. A child at that campus can reach an Al Nakheel flat by about four o'clock, which makes a five o'clock session realistic.

sections.heading: Al Nakheel against Khuzam: what the school day does to the evening
paragraphs: This is the comparison families here actually run, and it is worth doing with numbers rather than impressions. A Khuzam campus and a city-centre address are about fifteen minutes apart outside peak traffic, which means a child finishing at a quarter past three is home shortly after four and a five o'clock session is comfortable. The same child travelling to the Al Hamra coast is not home before five, and a five o'clock start is fiction.

That difference changes the plan rather than the teaching. A family with an early return can run two weekday sessions; a family with a long commute is better off with one longer weekend block, because a tired child at six-thirty on a Tuesday produces an hour of poor work that still costs an hour of money. Choosing the slot honestly is one of the few free improvements available to any tutoring arrangement, and it is almost never discussed.

The second column of the table is the one that surprises people. Across every district in this comparison, the subjects families ask for are nearly identical, the loss patterns are identical, and the scarcity of Higher Level specialists is identical. The districts differ in travel time and in rent. They do not differ in what a Diploma student needs from a teacher, which is the whole reason a remote arrangement makes the postcode irrelevant rather than inconvenient. A parent who has just moved from Al Uraibi to Al Dhait has changed their commute and changed nothing about which teacher their child needs, and the comparison table is really a timetable tool rather than a shortlist.

sections.heading: Higher Level is not Standard Level with more homework
paragraphs: Most families know the labels and very few know the percentages, which matters because the percentages are where tutoring time should be aimed. Higher Level courses carry more teaching hours, more content and, in several subjects, an additional paper that does not exist at Standard Level. A student taking three Higher Level subjects is carrying three extra papers as well as three deeper syllabuses, and the extra papers are weighted heavily enough to decide a grade on their own.

The practical consequence is that a Higher Level student and a Standard Level student in the same subject need different sessions, not different amounts of the same session. Standard Level work is usually about securing method marks and avoiding mechanical loss. Higher Level work is about sustained reasoning across a longer problem, and about the specific demands of the additional component, which rewards practice at that component rather than general revision of the subject.

A note on where exact figures belong. Component weightings are published by the IB for each subject in its own guide, and they change between syllabus cycles, so the right move is to read your child's current subject guide or ask their teacher rather than trust a general table on any tutoring page. What the table below does instead is show the shape of the difference and what each kind of component asks a student to do, which is stable across cycles and is what a plan is built on.

sections.heading: The mathematics route decision, taken two years too late
paragraphs: The single most consequential choice an Al Nakheel Diploma family makes is which mathematics course and at which level, and it is usually made on the basis of which one sounds easier. Analysis and Approaches is the proof-and-calculus route; Applications and Interpretation is the modelling-and-statistics route with heavier technology use. Both exist at Higher and Standard Level, and both are respectable courses. They are not interchangeable for the degree a student is aiming at.

The problem is timing. The choice is made at the end of the Middle Years Programme or Year 11, and its consequences surface when university entry requirements are read eighteen months later. Engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics courses commonly expect the analysis route at Higher Level; design, business, psychology and some social sciences are generally content with the applications route. Requirements vary by university and by year, so the only safe method is to read the published entry requirements for the specific courses on your child's list, including the UAE universities.

Where a tutor genuinely helps is before the decision rather than after it. An hour spent on a diagnostic of algebraic fluency and willingness to work with abstraction tells you more than a term of worrying. Students who find proof satisfying and algebra tolerable belong on the analysis route; students who are quick with data, context and modelling and who dislike abstraction will do better and score higher on applications. Choosing against the grain and then paying for tutoring to survive it is the expensive way round.

sections.heading: The mathematics exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Nobody in this search cluster publishes a single assessment criterion by letter, which is strange, because this is the part of the Diploma where families most often lose marks they could have kept. The mathematics exploration is marked out of twenty across five criteria, and the marks are not distributed the way students assume. Criterion E, the use of mathematics, carries six of the twenty. Presentation and mathematical communication carry four each. Personal engagement and reflection carry three each.

Read that distribution and the usual failure becomes obvious. Students pour effort into the mathematics, which is right, and then lose the eight marks available for communication and presentation by submitting something structured as a stream of working with no narrative. Reflection is the most neglected three marks in the Diploma: it asks for genuine consideration of what the result means and what the limitations were, and most first drafts have none of it at all.

What a tutor may do with this is precisely bounded and worth stating. Explaining what a criterion rewards is teaching. Reading a draft the student has written and saying that criterion D is currently unaddressed is feedback. Writing the reflection, restructuring the document, or supplying text for the student to insert is none of those things, and submitted work that is not the candidate's own is malpractice under the IB's academic honesty rules, with the consequence falling on the student. The criteria themselves live in the current subject guide and should be read there.
