sections.heading: The Diploma core, counted in words and deadlines
paragraphs: The core pieces are where Al Nakheel families most often ask for help late, and they are also the pieces with hard limits that make planning possible. The extended essay is capped at four thousand words. The theory of knowledge essay is capped at one thousand six hundred. The theory of knowledge exhibition commentary runs to nine hundred and fifty. Those ceilings are published by the IB and they are the single most useful planning facts in the Diploma, because a word count converts directly into a number of drafting weeks.

The deadlines, by contrast, are not the IB's. Your school sets internal submission dates months ahead of anything the board requires, in order to leave time for supervision, feedback and upload. That is why a tutoring plan has to be built from your own school's calendar rather than from a general timetable, and why booking core supervision in the autumn works and booking it in April does not. A tutor arriving after the school's internal deadline cannot help with the thing you are paying them for.

One further caution specific to this page. We do not publish IB examination or results dates anywhere on this site, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and we will not state a date we cannot verify from the source. Your child's IB coordinator holds the authoritative version for their session, and they are the only person who should be giving you one. Anything else on a tutoring page is a guess dressed as information, and a date a parent acts on is the worst possible thing to guess about.

sections.heading: The postcode changes the logistics and nothing else
paragraphs: Here is the claim this page has been building towards. Every item in the four tables above is identical for a student in Al Nakheel, a student in Khuzam and a student on Al Marjan Island. Criterion E is worth six marks everywhere. The extended essay ceiling is four thousand words everywhere. Higher Level additional papers exist regardless of which district a family rents in. The academic problem is national, or rather international, and it is not local at all.

What is local is supply, and this is where the northern emirates differ sharply from Dubai. The private-school set in Ras Al Khaimah is small and concentrated in a few districts, so the number of people within driving distance of Al Nakheel who have actually taught Higher Level chemistry or Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is small in any given year. Insisting on proximity therefore does not get you a better teacher; it gets you a shorter list, at a higher rate, because travel is unpaid time that returns to you in the hourly figure.

The conclusion is unglamorous. Use your district to decide when the session happens, because the school run genuinely constrains that. Do not use it to decide who teaches, because distance carries no information about whether somebody has taught your child's course. For an Al Nakheel family that reframing is worth more than any negotiation on rate, and it is the reason our delivery here is one-to-one over live video rather than a drive we would have to charge you for.

sections.heading: Online, in-home and group study compared for a city-centre family
paragraphs: Families in Al Nakheel have genuine alternatives, and a page that pretended otherwise would not be useful. There are tuition centres in the city, there are independent tutors living a few streets away, and there are study groups formed inside a school year cohort. Each earns its place in a different situation, and the comparison below is written to be fair to all of them rather than to arrive somewhere predetermined.

A centre buys structure and company, which is the right purchase for a student who works better with others in the room and needs the week shaped for them. An independent local tutor buys presence, which matters to some younger students in a way no video call replicates. A study group costs nothing and is excellent for working through past papers, provided somebody in it actually knows the mark scheme. None of those three reliably buys a Higher Level specialist in this emirate, and that is the gap.

Online one-to-one buys the specialist and the schedule flexibility, and gives up the physical presence. It also removes the failure mode nobody prices in: the session that does not happen. Across a thirty-week year, a physical arrangement loses sessions to traffic, weather, illness on either side and school events, and each loss is either money or an argument. A remote slot that must move moves by ninety minutes and still happens, and session count is a larger lever on a Diploma grade than hourly rate.

sections.heading: What a tutor may not touch, and why we say so on the page
paragraphs: There is an open market in this region for finished coursework, priced in four figures, and a family comparing options deserves to know that it exists and what it costs the student rather than the buyer. The IB's academic honesty rules make submitted work that is not the candidate's own a malpractice matter, and malpractice findings fall on the candidate. No price turns that into a sensible purchase, and no tutoring arrangement should blur it.

The workable boundary is easy to state and easy to check. A tutor explains what a criterion rewards, questions a research question, points at a paragraph and says the claim in it is unsupported, demonstrates how a source should be handled, and marks a draft against published criteria. A tutor does not write a student's internal assessment, does not draft their extended essay and does not edit a piece to completion. Feedback belongs in conversation and in annotation, never in the submitted file.

The same boundary applies to materials, and it is worth a sentence because some providers advertise the opposite as a feature. Subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB. A tutor can work through them with a student and can point you to the official page; reproducing them as downloads is copyright infringement. If a provider's main selling point is a library of other people's documents, they are offering something they have no right to give you.

sections.heading: Starting from Al Nakheel, and what the first month looks like
paragraphs: The useful first message contains the subject, the level, the school and the year, and ideally the thing that triggered the search. A mock result two grades below a prediction is a different problem from a student who has never been comfortable in the subject, and the first session should be designed around which one it is. Families who send that detail are matched in days; families who send a general worry spend a fortnight discovering it.

The first session is a diagnosis rather than a lesson. Your child attempts real questions at the right level while the tutor watches and says little, and the session ends with three statements: where marks are being lost, what connects the losses, and roughly how many sessions that implies. It is free, it is taken with the tutor who would actually teach, and nothing is owed if the match is wrong. A trial used as a sales meeting with teaching attached establishes nothing.

After that, a written plan with a session range on it, a fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time that survives the Khuzam or Al Hamra commute, and a review at four weeks that asks whether the diagnosis held. If the subject turns out to need six sessions rather than a term, we will say so, and the slot can move to the next subject. The point of a plan with a number on it is that reality can be checked against it, which an open-ended arrangement makes impossible.

process.title: Tell us the course and the level
process.description: Subject, Higher or Standard Level, school, year group and what prompted the enquiry. For a Diploma student the level is the critical detail, because a Higher Level course carries components that do not exist at Standard Level and needs a tutor who has taught them.

process.title: Hear the coverage position before clearing an evening
process.description: We say whether a tutor who has taught that exact course at that level is free this term, free at a different time, or not free at all. The last answer is given rather than hidden, because a Higher Level student placed with a generalist loses a term before anyone admits it.

process.title: A free diagnostic trial with the proposed tutor
process.description: One session, no payment beforehand, spent on real questions at the correct level. It ends with a loss pattern, the cause connecting the losses and an estimated session range. If the match is wrong you say so and nothing is owed.

process.title: A plan built on your school's calendar
process.description: Internal assessment deadlines are set by your school months before the board needs anything, so the plan is written around those dates rather than a generic timetable. Core supervision is booked a term ahead because drafting season is crowded everywhere.

process.title: A slot that survives the school run
process.description: One fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, chosen against the actual commute from Khuzam or the coast rather than against an optimistic estimate. Where the drive makes weekday evenings unworkable, a Saturday block replaces two tired weekday hours.

process.title: Review, then stop when it is finished
process.description: A review at four weeks and another at the mock results. Each asks whether to continue, step up, switch subject or stop. A provider who never proposes stopping is not reviewing anything, and continuing past the papers costs money and achieves nothing.

faqs.question: Can an IB home tutor in Al Nakheel actually come to our apartment?
faqs.answer: Local independent tutors in the city do offer that, and the published UAE market for in-home one-to-one runs around AED 180 to 500 an hour across sources including Bestimate's 2026 table. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India. Our lessons for Al Nakheel families are one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard and a recording afterwards. The trade is a person in the room against a tutor who has actually taught your child's course at the right level.

faqs.question: Is Diploma tutoring in Al Nakheel different from Diploma tutoring in Khuzam?
faqs.answer: Logistically yes, academically no. A Khuzam child is home by about four and can start at five; an Al Nakheel child travelling to the Al Hamra coast is not home before five and should probably take a Saturday block instead. What does not change is the content: the same criteria, the same component structures, the same places marks are lost. Treat the district as a scheduling fact and the specification as the matching fact, and the comparison resolves itself quickly.

faqs.question: How many marks is each mathematics exploration criterion worth?
faqs.answer: Twenty marks in total across five criteria. Use of mathematics carries six, presentation carries four, mathematical communication carries four, personal engagement carries three and reflection carries three. The distribution explains the usual failure: students work hard on the mathematics and lose the eight marks available for structure and notation, and reflection is frequently missing from a first draft entirely. Read the criteria in your child's current subject guide, because wording and allocations are set there and can change between syllabus cycles.

faqs.question: How long is the extended essay allowed to be?
faqs.answer: Four thousand words is the published maximum, and the theory of knowledge essay is capped at one thousand six hundred with the exhibition commentary at nine hundred and fifty. Those ceilings are the most useful planning numbers in the Diploma, because a word count converts straight into drafting weeks. The submission date, though, is your school's rather than the board's: schools set internal deadlines months early to allow for supervision and upload, which is why core support booked in the autumn works and the same support booked in April does not.

faqs.question: Which mathematics course should a student in Al Nakheel choose?
faqs.answer: It depends on the degree route and on how the student thinks, not on which sounds easier. Analysis and Approaches is algebra, calculus, proof and abstraction, and is commonly expected at Higher Level for engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics courses. Applications and Interpretation is modelling, statistics and heavy calculator use, and suits business, design, psychology and several social sciences. Requirements differ by university and by year, so read the published entry requirements for the specific courses on the list, including UAE universities.

faqs.question: What are the IB exam dates for the session our child is sitting?
faqs.answer: We will not tell you, and no tutoring page should. The IB's own website blocks automated checking, so nothing on this site states a Diploma examination or results date, and an unverified date is exactly the kind of error a parent acts on. Your child's IB coordinator holds the authoritative timetable for their session and is the only correct source. Cambridge and Pearson dates are different: those are published and checkable, and where we quote one we give the source and the exact historical day.

faqs.question: Why is it so hard to find a Higher Level specialist near the city centre?
faqs.answer: Because the private-school set in Ras Al Khaimah is small and concentrated in a handful of districts, so the pool of people who have taught Higher Level chemistry or Analysis and Approaches within driving distance of Al Nakheel is genuinely thin in any given year. The usual local substitute is a graduate in the subject who has never taught the Diploma, which is a different product at the same price. Removing distance from the match is the only way to widen that pool meaningfully.

faqs.question: Does a tuition centre in the city do the same job?
faqs.answer: It does a different job well. A centre buys structure, company and a shaped week, and for a student who works better with others in the room that is the right purchase. What a group class cannot buy here is a specialist in your child's exact course and level, because the economics of a centre depend on filling a room rather than on matching a syllabus. If the problem is a specific loss pattern in a Higher Level component, a group rate is cheap money spent on the wrong thing.

faqs.question: Our son has three Higher Level subjects and is drowning. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: With one subject, chosen on evidence rather than on which feels worst. Get one marked paper from each of the three and look for a shared cause, because three failing subjects usually have one: command-term reading, timed-paper pacing, or algebra that collapses under pressure. Fix the shared cause inside one subject with a tutor who knows the component, and the other two improve without being bought. Opening three slots at once gives each subject an hour a week and finishes none of them.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help with the internal assessment, and where is the line?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a firm boundary. A tutor explains what each criterion rewards, questions a research question, reads a draft the student has written and says that a claim is unsupported or that reflection is missing. A tutor does not write the internal assessment, does not draft the extended essay and does not edit a piece to completion. Submitted work that is not the candidate's own is malpractice under the IB's academic honesty rules and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the person who was paid.

faqs.question: Can you send us past papers and mark schemes to work from?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider who offers to is offering something they have no right to give. Subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, and reproducing them as downloads is copyright infringement. What a tutor can do is work through them with your child inside a session and point you at the official page so you can obtain them properly, usually through the school. A library of other people's documents is a selling point we have deliberately given up.

faqs.question: Which regulator oversees our school here, and does it affect tutoring?
faqs.answer: Private schools in Ras Al Khaimah answer to the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which the UAE government's information service describes as regulating private education here, and which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. It affects your calendar and your paperwork rather than your choice of tutor. It also does not endorse anybody: IB Gram holds no approval from that authority or any other, and a tutoring company implying otherwise is making a claim it cannot support.

faqs.question: Is a Saturday session better than a weekday one for a commuting family?
faqs.answer: Often, and it is under-used. A child who gets home at five, eats and then sits down at half past six produces an hour of tired work that costs a full hour of money. One longer Saturday block instead of two weekday sessions gives you a fresher student, room for a full timed paper under exam conditions, and marking in the same sitting. It also survives school events and late buses, which quietly remove several weekday sessions from every school year.

faqs.question: What should we be measuring by the fourth week of Diploma sessions?
faqs.answer: By a shrinking topic list and by marks on timed work, not by how the sessions feel. Agree at the start what will be measured: which topics come off the list, what a timed paper scores in week one against week eight, and whether the specific losses named in the diagnosis have stopped. Review formally at four weeks and again at the mock results. If nothing has moved by the second review, the diagnosis was wrong or the match is wrong, and both are fixable if you are looking.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not right for our child?
faqs.answer: You say so, inside the first few weeks, and we change the match without you buying the term again. The free trial exists precisely to make that conversation happen before money is involved rather than after, and it is taken with the tutor who would actually teach rather than with a coordinator. Ask any provider in this market the same question before the first invoice. A business whose pricing depends on you not asking it has told you something useful about everything else.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nakhe.closingHeading: Use the district for the timetable and the specification for the tutor
ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nakhe.closingBody: The comparison between Al Nakheel and Khuzam, or Al Nakheel and the coast, is worth running once: it tells you whether a session can start at five, at six, or only on a Saturday. After that it has nothing left to tell you, because criterion E is worth six marks in every district and the extended essay ceiling is four thousand words in all of them. Send us the subject, the level, the school and the year, and your child sits a free trial lesson with a tutor who has taught that course, one-to-one over live video, at a Gulf Standard Time slot that survives the school run.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-qusai.tutorsIntro: Al Qusaidat students are matched with specialists in the components families rarely think to book: a Group 3 subject, a language A oral, a Theory of Knowledge essay. The grid below lists what is most often requested from Ras Al Khaimah.

intro.heading: The components nobody books, and where the points are
paragraphs: A Diploma total is built from six subject grades and three core points, and tutoring spend in this market is concentrated almost entirely on two of the six groups. Mathematics and the sciences absorb nearly every enquiry, which leaves Group 3, the languages and the entire core receiving no external attention at all. Those are not minor components. A Group 3 subject is a seventh of the subject total, a language A grade is another seventh, and the core carries points of its own.

The imbalance has a cause. Science and mathematics problems feel technical and therefore solvable by a specialist, while an Economics commentary or a Theory of Knowledge essay feels like something a student either can or cannot do. That is not true. Each of those components has published criteria, a recognisable set of failure modes, and a technique that can be taught in a small number of sessions. They are, if anything, more responsive than a missing content sequence in Chemistry.

Al Qusaidat is an established residential district north-east of the creek in Ras Al Khaimah, with family housing and a reasonable run into the city's school cluster, which makes a 4:45pm session realistic on most school days. The housing matters here in a practical sense: an Individual Oral needs rehearsal space and an Extended Essay needs sustained quiet, both of which are easier in this district than in the old-town towers.

Delivery is stated plainly. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For the components on this page the format is well suited: a draft on a shared screen with criterion descriptors beside it, annotated live, and the annotated copy kept by the student afterwards.

Two cautions. Component structures, criteria and point allocations are given here because they are what makes the page useful, but IB documents are revised and this page reproduces none of them: confirm every figure against the subject guide and the assessment information your school issues. And no IB exam or results date appears anywhere, because the board's own site returns an error to automated checking and nothing in this project has been verified from the IB itself.

Nothing here is a claim about outcomes. No tutor can promise a grade, because boundaries are set after a series on the basis of that series' papers. What a specialist changes in these components is the precision of the student's own work, which is a smaller claim and one the student can see happening. It is also why the sessions described here are counted in small numbers rather than in terms: a criterion that has been unaddressed for a year can be addressed in an afternoon once somebody has pointed at the wording, and the student who has seen that done once tends to do it unaided afterwards.

programmes.description: The three components with no subject teacher and, in most timetables, no dedicated lesson in which the work is produced. ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-qusai.subjectsIntro: This grid leads with Group 3 and the languages, because those are the subjects where families in this emirate are least likely to have arranged any support at all.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram marks are the most available on the paper and the most reliably dropped: axes unlabelled, the shift not shown, the new equilibrium unmarked. Higher Level adds quantitative questions. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries built on recent articles, which must be collected as they appear.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A tool described earns almost nothing; the same tool applied to the case stimulus earns well. Higher Level adds the pre-released case study, published far enough ahead that structured early reading is worth more here than in any other subject on the timetable.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Marks come from naming studies precisely and using them as evidence rather than as illustration. Students lose heavily on evaluation, where a list of criticisms scores far below a ranked argument about which limitation actually undermines the conclusion.

subjects.name: Global Politics and History
subjects.description: Both reward supported judgement on the specific claim in the question rather than an account of everything known. The commonest failure is a narrative answer to an analytical question, which can be corrected in a handful of timed essays.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is a guided analysis of an unseen text and rewards argument about how the text constructs meaning. The Individual Oral needs a global issue chosen early and two extracts that genuinely support it. Higher Level adds an essay needing a single line of argument.

subjects.name: English A: Literature
subjects.description: Similar components with a literary focus, and the same recurring loss: the student writes about what a work says rather than how it works. The comparative essay rewards a point-by-point structure rather than a work-by-work tour.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Language A assesses analysis and extended writing at native level; language B assesses reading comprehension, writing to a specified text type and a spoken component. Home speakers in a language B course lose marks on register and convention rather than on vocabulary.

subjects.name: Mathematics and the sciences
subjects.description: Covered in detail elsewhere, and still the subjects most families book first. Worth noting that their internal assessments are judged against criteria in the same way the Group 3 components are, which is the skill this page is really about.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Two assessed tasks: an essay responding to a prescribed title and an exhibition built around objects and a prompt. Both reward precision over breadth, and both are routinely attempted without anybody having read the assessment instrument.

sections.heading: Group 3 papers, component by component
paragraphs: Group 3 subjects share a structural feature that explains most of the marks lost in them: the examination rewards the use of material rather than the possession of it. A student can know an entire Economics course and score in the middle bands, because every question asked them to do something with the knowledge and they explained it instead.

In Economics the doing is mostly diagrammatic and quantitative. Diagram marks are available in large numbers and are dropped by students who draw a shape they recognise without labelling the axes, showing the shift, or marking the new equilibrium. Higher Level adds calculation, and the internal assessment is a set of commentaries, each built on a genuinely recent article, each with a word limit that is enforced rather than indicative.

In Business Management the doing is application to the case stimulus. A reproduced tool scores almost nothing; the same tool built from the specific business in front of the student scores well. The Higher Level pre-released case study is the clearest example of an available advantage nobody takes, because it is published far enough ahead that structured early reading is possible and most students read it in the final fortnight.

In Psychology, History and Global Politics the doing is argument supported by named evidence. A study cited precisely is worth considerably more than a study gestured at, and evaluation written as a ranked claim about which limitation actually undermines a conclusion is worth more than a list of criticisms. Each of those is a technique rather than a body of knowledge, which is why a handful of timed essays with proper marking moves these subjects faster than the same hours spent revising content.

sections.heading: Language A and language B: what each component rewards
paragraphs: Language subjects are carried by every Diploma student and tutored by almost none of them, which is the single clearest imbalance in this market. They are also responsive, because the losses are structural rather than linguistic and structure can be taught.

In language A, whether Language and Literature or Literature, the recurring failure is writing about content instead of construction. Paper 1 presents an unseen text and asks for a guided analysis, and the marks go to an argument about how the text produces its effect: structure, voice, register, imagery, what is withheld. A student who paraphrases the text accurately has described something the examiner has already read. The Higher Level essay wants a single line of argument developed through a work rather than a tour of its features.

In language B the components are different and the failure is register. A home speaker placed in a language B course frequently has more vocabulary than the course requires and loses marks because a formal letter was written in the voice of a message to a friend, or because a blog entry ignored the conventions of a blog. The text type is prescribed and assessed, and that is an instruction rather than a suggestion.

Both have spoken components and both are routinely under-rehearsed, which is largely a housing problem rather than a motivation problem: rehearsing aloud needs a room. Al Qusaidat's family housing makes that easier than the old-town towers, and it is worth using deliberately, because a spoken component rehearsed three times against the criteria is a different performance from one attempted cold.

sections.heading: The Individual Oral: the component with the least guidance
paragraphs: Every Diploma language A student sits an Individual Oral and almost none of them is taught how. The component asks a student to explore a global issue through two extracts, one from a work in translation and one from a work originally written in the language of study, and to hold a sustained spoken argument about it. The marks are allocated against published criteria, and the single decision that determines most of them is taken weeks before the recording.

That decision is the pairing. A global issue has to be genuinely explored by both extracts, which means the extracts must do work rather than merely mention a theme. Students routinely choose extracts they enjoyed and then construct an issue backwards from them, which produces an oral where the issue is asserted at the start, not examined in the middle, and reasserted at the end. A specialist can see that in ten minutes and the student usually cannot.

The second determinant is structure under time pressure. A sustained spoken argument needs a shape the student can hold without notes: issue, first extract as evidence, second extract as development or contrast, and a conclusion that says something the extracts have earned. Rehearsing that shape three times against the criteria changes the performance substantially, and it is rehearsal rather than content work.

The third is practical. Rehearsing aloud needs a room where a teenager is willing to speak at normal volume, which in a shared flat is a real obstacle and in Al Qusaidat's family housing usually is not. Families who treat the oral as a scheduled rehearsal rather than a thing that happens on the day see a different outcome, and it costs two or three sessions rather than a term.

sections.heading: The Extended Essay: what a good question looks like by subject
paragraphs: The Extended Essay is 4,000 words of independent research assessed against named criteria, and its ceiling is set by the research question rather than by the writing. A question that cannot be answered inside the limit produces an essay that will not cut without losing its argument, which is why students arrive at 5,000 words and cannot see a route back.

A good question looks different in each subject, and this is the part students are least often shown. In a science it has a measurable relationship and a feasible method with equipment that actually exists. In Economics it has a specific market, a defined period and data that can be obtained. In History it has a bounded period and a defensible claim rather than a topic. In a language A essay it has a text or pair of texts and an argument about construction rather than content. In Mathematics it has an area of mathematics to develop rather than a phenomenon to describe.

The failures are also subject-specific and recognisable. A science essay whose method needs equipment the school does not have. An Economics essay about a whole economy over a decade. A History essay titled with a period rather than a claim. A language essay about a theme across four novels. A Mathematics essay about an interesting real-world situation with no mathematics in it. Every one of those is visible to a specialist in a single conversation and invisible to a student until they are 3,000 words in.

The legitimate support is therefore narrow and early: testing the question, reviewing feasibility, explaining what each named criterion demands, and giving written feedback on drafts the student has written. The school provides the supervisor. A tutor must never write, redraft or complete the essay, nor supply text for the student to paste in. Confirm the criteria and the word limit against the current Extended Essay guidance your school issues.

sections.heading: Theory of Knowledge: two tasks, two techniques
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge is assessed through two tasks and most students prepare for one of them. The essay responds to a prescribed title set by the IB and is externally assessed. The exhibition asks a student to select objects and link them to a prompt, with a written commentary, and is internally assessed. They reward different things and are routinely attempted without anybody having read the assessment instrument for either.

The essay fails in a predictable way: breadth instead of argument. A student gestures at four knowledge claims, mentions several areas of knowledge, offers two examples that illustrate nothing in particular, and concludes that the question is complex. The marks are available for one line of argument developed properly, with examples that do specific work and a genuine counterposition taken seriously rather than dismissed in a clause. Choosing which title to answer is itself a decision worth a session, because the titles are not equally tractable for a given student.

The exhibition fails differently: objects chosen for interest rather than for argument. Each object has to connect to the prompt specifically and the commentary has to make that connection explicit, in the prompt's own terms. A beautiful object with a loose connection scores below a mundane object with a precise one, which is counterintuitive to students and easy to correct once it is said.

Both tasks also contribute to the Diploma total through the combination with the Extended Essay, which is why neglecting them is more expensive than it looks. Confirm the current arrangements and allocations with your Theory of Knowledge teacher or coordinator, because this page reproduces no IB document and the arrangements are revised.

sections.heading: CAS: not graded, still a requirement
paragraphs: Creativity, Activity, Service is not graded and is a completion requirement, which is a combination that produces a specific kind of trouble: it has no marks to chase and it can stop a Diploma being awarded. In most households it is remembered in the final term, which is the worst time to discover that evidence or reflections are missing.

In Ras Al Khaimah there is an additional practical dimension. The emirate has fewer organised opportunities than Dubai, and a student looking for a service activity or a sustained creative commitment in the final year may find the options thin. Students who start in Grade 11, when the choice is wider and the pressure lower, generally finish without incident; students who start late are negotiating with organisations while coursework deadlines are landing.

This is explicitly not a tutoring task. A tutor cannot and should not produce reflections, complete a portfolio or manufacture evidence, and any provider offering to do so is offering to put a Diploma at risk. What is appropriate is to name it as a household calendar item in Grade 11 and to check, once a term, that the record is current.

The reason it belongs on a page about overlooked components is that it is the most overlooked of all, and unlike a weak essay it is not a matter of degree. A component that is simply not completed does not produce a lower grade; it produces a problem that has to be resolved with the school, usually under time pressure, and it is entirely avoidable with a calendar reminder.
bullets: Not graded, but a completion requirement with real consequences.

sections.heading: How the Diploma total is assembled
paragraphs: Families frequently plan around subject grades without a clear picture of how they combine, which makes it hard to judge where effort is worth spending. The structure is simple enough to state and worth knowing in Grade 11 rather than in the spring of Grade 12.

Six subjects each contribute a grade on a seven-point scale, giving a maximum of 42 from subjects. The Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay combination contributes up to a further three points, taking the maximum to 45. There are also requirements beyond the points total, including conditions about minimum grades and completion of the core, which is why a student can have a sufficient total and still have a problem. The specific conditions are published by the IB and administered by the school, and they should be confirmed with the coordinator rather than taken from any tutoring page.

Two planning consequences follow. First, the core is not decoration: points from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay combination are worth the same as points gained anywhere else, and they are available from components almost nobody tutors. Second, a single weak subject can matter disproportionately if it falls below a condition rather than merely below expectations, which is a question for the coordinator and not something to guess at.

A final honesty note. This page publishes no equivalency points figure for the IB, because the source used for the British and American tracks in this project does not state one, and an unverified threshold on a page like this would be a liability rather than a help. Confirm the IB position with the Ministry of Education or your emirate's attestation channel.

sections.heading: Honesty, materials and the permit
paragraphs: A page this far into assessed components owes a clear boundary. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain each assessment criterion and what its descriptors demand, help narrow a research question or test whether a global issue and its extracts genuinely fit, review a method for feasibility and ethics, and give written feedback on a draft the student has already written.

A tutor must never write, redraft or complete an Internal Assessment, a Mathematics exploration, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or exhibition commentary, a CAS reflection or any assessed work, and must not supply text, data or diagrams for submission. A page found during research for this project sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is an academic integrity breach and an IB malpractice trigger, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on whoever sold it.

On materials: no tutor should reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables, assessment instruments or subject guides as downloads. The official source should be referenced and linked instead, which is why this page carries no attachments and repeatedly asks readers to confirm structures and allocations against the documents their own school issues.

The last boundary is who may teach, and in a market this thin it decides who is even available for the components above. Eligibility for the permit is wide, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, which is why the person capable of coaching a Language A oral in Al Qusaidat may be an undergraduate rather than a career tutor. That is a permitted arrangement and not a disqualifying one. The permit itself is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, created by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE's own service page listing no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published there is no amount to repeat here. On our own standing: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from the Department of Knowledge, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no tutor can promise a grade, least of all on the core, where three points turn on two pieces of writing.

process.title: Name the component, not the subject
process.description: An enquiry that says Economics Paper 1 diagrams, or the Individual Oral, or the Theory of Knowledge essay, can be answered properly. One that says Economics takes a session to narrow. Bring the relevant subject guide or assessment information if you have it.

process.title: Take the free diagnostic session
process.description: The first session is a diagnosis with no card details taken. For the components on this page that usually means reading one piece of the student's own work against the published criteria and naming which criterion is unaddressed, which is faster and more specific than a general assessment.

process.title: Test the central decision before any writing
process.description: The Extended Essay question, the pairing of global issue and extracts, the choice of prescribed title, the objects for the exhibition. Each of those caps a component before a word is written, and each is visible to a specialist in a single conversation.

process.title: Schedule the rehearsals
process.description: Spoken components are under-rehearsed mostly because rehearsing aloud needs a room. Al Qusaidat's family housing usually provides one, so put three rehearsals in the calendar against the criteria rather than treating the oral as a thing that happens on the day.

process.title: Put CAS on the household calendar in Grade 11
process.description: It is not a tutoring task and no provider should touch it, but it is a completion requirement and the local options are thinner than in Dubai. A termly check that the record is current prevents the one problem that cannot be fixed by working harder.

whyPoints.title: The components nobody else covers
whyPoints.description: Group 3, the languages and the core receive almost no tutoring attention in this market, and they carry a large share of a Diploma total. Each has published criteria and recognisable failure modes, which makes them more responsive than a missing content sequence.

whyPoints.title: The decision before the drafting
whyPoints.description: An Extended Essay question, a global issue and its extracts, a prescribed title, a set of exhibition objects: each sets a ceiling before any writing happens. Testing them early is the highest-value hour available in the core.

whyPoints.title: Criteria open beside the draft
whyPoints.description: Work is marked against the published descriptors with the descriptors visible, so the student reads what the band demands rather than a general comment about quality. The annotated draft is theirs to keep.

whyPoints.title: Rehearsal treated as a scheduled task
whyPoints.description: Spoken components are under-prepared largely because rehearsing aloud needs a room. Three rehearsals against the criteria changes the performance substantially, and it costs sessions rather than a term.

whyPoints.title: Figures given with a caveat, never reproduced
whyPoints.description: Structures and allocations appear because they make the page useful, with an instruction to confirm them against the documents your school issues. No IB document is reproduced here and no unverified IB date is published anywhere.

whyPoints.title: Stated limits, including on CAS
whyPoints.description: Explaining criteria, testing decisions and feeding back on the student's own draft: yes. Producing any part of assessed work, including a CAS reflection: never, at any price or any deadline.

faqs.question: Which IB components do Al Qusaidat families most often leave untutored?
faqs.answer: Group 3, the languages and the entire core. Nearly every enquiry in this market concerns mathematics or a science, which leaves Economics, Business Management, Psychology, History, language A and the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay components receiving no external attention at all. Those are not minor: a Group 3 subject is a seventh of the subject total, a language A grade is another seventh, and the core contributes points of its own on top.

faqs.question: Why does my child score mid-band in Economics despite knowing the course?
faqs.answer: Because the paper rewards using the material rather than possessing it. Diagram marks are available in large numbers and are dropped by students who draw a recognisable shape without labelling the axes, showing the shift, or marking the new equilibrium. Higher Level adds calculation, where the same pattern appears: a correct figure with no working earns a fraction of what it should. Both are mechanical fixes and both apply across every topic in the course.

faqs.question: What is the best use of the Higher Level Business pre-released case study?
faqs.answer: Structured reading, started as soon as it is published rather than in the final fortnight. The pre-release is the clearest example in the Diploma of an available advantage almost nobody takes: the material is known in advance, so the work is building a map of the organisation, its context and the tools that will plausibly apply, rather than meeting it cold. Students who read it early and annotate it deliberately are preparing for a different examination from those who do not.

faqs.question: How should an Individual Oral extract be chosen?
faqs.answer: By whether it does work for the global issue, not by whether the student enjoyed it. The component asks for a global issue explored through two extracts, and most students choose extracts they liked and then construct an issue backwards, which produces an oral where the issue is asserted at the beginning, never examined in the middle, and reasserted at the end. A specialist can see that in ten minutes. Test the pairing weeks before the recording, because it decides most of the marks.

faqs.question: How many times should a spoken component be rehearsed?
faqs.answer: Three, against the published criteria, with specific feedback on structure rather than on confidence. A sustained spoken argument needs a shape the student can hold without notes: the issue, the first extract as evidence, the second as development or contrast, and a conclusion the extracts have earned. The practical obstacle is usually a room rather than willingness, and Al Qusaidat's family housing generally provides one where the old-town towers do not.

faqs.question: Why do home speakers lose marks in a language B course?
faqs.answer: On register and text type rather than on vocabulary. A language B writing task is prescribed: a formal letter, a report, a blog entry, each with conventions that are assessed. A student with more vocabulary than the course requires frequently writes fluently in the wrong voice, which costs marks that fluency cannot recover. The correction is mechanical: identify the text type, list its conventions, and rewrite one piece to deliver them. It transfers immediately.

faqs.question: What makes an Extended Essay question workable?
faqs.answer: That it can be answered inside 4,000 words, and the test differs by subject. A science question needs a measurable relationship and a method feasible with available equipment. An Economics question needs a specific market, a defined period and obtainable data. A History question needs a bounded period and a defensible claim rather than a topic. A Mathematics question needs mathematics to develop. A language question needs an argument about construction rather than a theme traced across several works.

faqs.question: My child's Extended Essay is over the word limit. What now?
faqs.answer: The problem is almost always the question rather than the prose. A question too broad to answer inside 4,000 words produces an essay that cannot be cut without losing its argument, which is why a student at 5,000 words cannot see a route back. The work is narrowing the question and rebuilding the structure around the narrower version. A tutor may do that narrowing, explain what each criterion demands and feed back on drafts; a tutor may never rewrite the essay.

faqs.question: How is Theory of Knowledge actually assessed?
faqs.answer: Through two tasks. An essay responding to a prescribed title set by the IB, which is externally assessed, and an exhibition in which the student links objects to a prompt with a written commentary, which is internally assessed. They reward different things and are routinely attempted without anybody having read the assessment instrument for either. Confirm the current arrangements and allocations with your Theory of Knowledge teacher, because this page reproduces no IB document.

faqs.question: Why do TOK essays score below what students expect?
faqs.answer: Breadth instead of argument. The familiar pattern is four knowledge claims gestured at, several areas of knowledge mentioned, two examples that illustrate nothing in particular, and a conclusion that the question is complex. The marks are available for one line of argument developed properly, with examples that do specific work and a counterposition taken seriously rather than dismissed in a clause. Choosing which prescribed title to answer is itself worth a session, because the titles are not equally tractable.

faqs.question: How should an Al Qusaidat student pick their three exhibition objects?
faqs.answer: A specific connection to the prompt, stated explicitly in the prompt's own terms. Students choose objects for interest and leave the link loose, which inverts the scoring: a mundane object with a precise connection outscores a striking object with a vague one. The correction is to write the connection first, in one sentence, and only keep the object if that sentence is convincing. That is counterintuitive to most students and easy to fix once it has been said out loud.

faqs.question: Is CAS something a tutor can help with?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider offering to produce reflections, complete a portfolio or manufacture evidence is offering to put a Diploma at risk. CAS is not graded but it is a completion requirement, which is the combination that causes trouble: no marks to chase and real consequences if it is incomplete. In this emirate the local options are thinner than in Dubai, so starting in Grade 11 matters. Treat it as a household calendar item with a termly check.

faqs.question: How is the Diploma total put together?
faqs.answer: Six subjects each contribute a grade on a seven-point scale, giving a maximum of 42 from subjects, and the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay combination contributes up to a further three, taking the maximum to 45. There are also conditions beyond the total, including requirements about minimum grades and completion of the core, which is why a sufficient total can still come with a problem. Confirm the specific conditions with your coordinator rather than with any tutoring page.

faqs.question: Will you tell me the IB score the Ministry requires for equivalency?
faqs.answer: Not one that this page will publish. The source used for the British and American tracks in this project states the figures for those routes but publishes no IB points threshold, and an unverified number here would be a liability rather than a help, particularly since one competitor page in this market already publishes an incorrect subject count for the British track. Confirm the IB position with the Ministry of Education or your emirate's attestation channel directly.

faqs.question: Can a Group 3 subject really improve in a few sessions?
faqs.answer: More reliably than a missing content sequence in a science, yes, because the losses are techniques rather than knowledge. Labelling a diagram fully, quoting the extract figure, applying a tool to the case in front of the student, citing a study precisely, ranking limitations instead of listing them: each of those is learnable in a handful of timed pieces with proper marking, and each applies across every topic in the course rather than to one of them.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-qusai.closingHeading: Bring the component, and the guide if you have it
ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-qusai.closingBody: If your child is in the Diploma in Al Qusaidat and the marks are going somewhere nobody is looking, the quickest route to an answer is to bring one piece of their own work and the relevant criteria. The first session is free, no card details are taken, and the tutor will name which criterion is unaddressed rather than offering a general view of the writing. Where the component has a central decision still open, an Extended Essay question, a global issue, a prescribed title, that is the hour worth spending first. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-julphar.tutorsIntro: Julphar families are matched with Diploma subject specialists who will take a short, reliably held slot rather than a long one that keeps collapsing, because in dense central housing the constraint is quiet time rather than available time.

intro.heading: Central, dense, and short of one specific thing
paragraphs: Julphar is the old quarter of Ras Al Khaimah, built around the creek and the historic port, with towers, older apartment stock and the shortest journeys in the emirate. A family here is minutes from the city school cluster rather than half an hour, which removes the problem most pages about tutoring in the Northern Emirates spend their time on.

What it does not remove is the one constraint nobody writes about. A Diploma session needs forty-five uninterrupted minutes with a screen, a pen and a paper, and in a central apartment with siblings and a shared living room that is a scarcer resource than an hour on a clock. Families in Al Hamra or Mina Al Arab have longer drives and more rooms; Julphar has shorter drives and fewer. Both are real trade-offs and only one of them is ever mentioned.

So this page is a set of comparisons, but not the obvious ones. Julphar against the master-planned coastal communities, on the trade that actually differs. A private tutor against the school's own support, because the overlap is larger than most families assume and paying twice for the same thing is common. One weekly hour against a short intensive block, which is the decision that moves a Diploma grade most. And the three Higher Levels against each other, because support spread evenly across all three usually achieves less than the same hours concentrated on one.

Delivery is stated plainly. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The phrase in this page's address is what parents search, and the honest answer for Julphar is that an online slot is easier to protect in dense housing than a visitor is, because a short session can be moved to a bedroom and a visitor cannot.

Rates quoted are the published market, attributed to the provider that published them and dated October 2026. Regulatory statements come from federal and emirate sources. No IB exam or results date appears, because the IB's own site returns an error to automated checking and nothing in this project has been verified from the board itself.

What this page does not do is pretend Julphar is disadvantaged. It is the best-connected part of the emirate and that is a genuine advantage. The point is simply that the scarce input here is a quiet room, and a plan built around that works better than one built around a drive time nobody in Julphar has to make. A cancelled or interrupted session is worse than a missed one, because it consumes the slot, the fee and the student's goodwill while producing nothing, and it is the commonest reason a plan that looked sensible in September has quietly stopped by November.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external papers and no fixed deadlines. The useful work is mechanics: number bonds, written method, reading stamina, explaining an answer in a sentence. A twenty-five or thirty-minute session is sufficient, which makes this the stage least affected by a shortage of quiet space.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, with strands inside each criterion. Marks are lost to an unaddressed strand rather than a misunderstood topic, and the repair is reading the strand wording against a draft, which needs attention more than it needs a long block.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, with an internally assessed component in every subject. The final year needs full papers under timed conditions, which is the one requirement that genuinely conflicts with a crowded flat.
programmes.countryNote: The practical answer for Julphar is to separate the two kinds of work: short weekday sessions at home for diagnosis and technique, and full papers sat somewhere quieter, which for many families means the school library or a weekend morning before the household wakes.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-julphar.subjectsIntro: The Diploma subjects most often requested from Ras Al Khaimah, with a note on how much uninterrupted time each one's work actually needs.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Non-calculator technique is the usual gap and it responds to short frequent sets rather than long sessions, which suits a Julphar weekday. Full Paper 1 practice needs a longer quiet block and belongs at the weekend.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Interpretation of calculator output is the recurring loss, which is conversational work and fits a short slot well. Higher Level graph theory and matrices arrive late and need sustained attention.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry responds to ninety-second drills done frequently; data questions need a paper and a mark scheme. Both fit forty-five minutes. The internal assessment needs planning time rather than quiet time.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Graph and unit discipline is quick, diagnosable work. Full papers are where pacing shows up, and pacing is the one thing that cannot be assessed in a short session at all.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Long-answer sequencing is the main loss and is repaired by rewriting existing answers, which is ideal short-slot work. Content volume means revision itself needs longer blocks elsewhere in the week.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram discipline is fast to fix in a short session. The three internal assessment commentaries need article collection across weeks, which is a habit rather than a session.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Timed case questions fit a forty-five-minute slot almost exactly. The Higher Level pre-released case study rewards reading spread over weeks, which needs no quiet room at all.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided analysis improves through rewriting one paragraph at a time, which is short-slot work. The Individual Oral needs rehearsal space, which is the hardest thing to find in a shared flat.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Both are narrowing problems before they are writing problems, and narrowing is a conversation. A single well-aimed short session on the research question is worth more than several on drafting.

sections.heading: Julphar against the coastal communities
paragraphs: The comparison families in Ras Al Khaimah actually make is between the old town and the newer master-planned communities, and it is usually framed as a housing decision. For tutoring it resolves into two variables that pull in opposite directions: journey length and available quiet space.

Julphar wins decisively on journeys. Sitting around the creek inside the city's school and commercial cluster, it offers the shortest school runs in the emirate, which means an earlier session, less chance of a cancelled evening and no travel premium if an in-home arrangement is ever considered. Al Hamra Village and Mina Al Arab sit at the other end: longer drives, later starts, and an in-home visit that is barely viable at all.

The coastal communities win on space. Villa and townhouse housing offers a room that can be closed, which is what a ninety-minute timed paper requires. Julphar's older apartment stock typically does not, and a Diploma student in the final year needs full papers more than they need anything else. That is the honest trade: Julphar makes short sessions easy and long ones hard; the coast does the reverse.

The planning consequence is different in each place rather than better in one. A Julphar family should build a plan from short, reliably held weekday sessions and find one longer quiet window a week somewhere else, which for many students means the school library or an early weekend morning. A coastal family should do the opposite: fewer, longer sessions at home, accepting that a weekday evening slot will sometimes lose to traffic.

sections.heading: What apartment living actually changes
paragraphs: This deserves its own section because it is the most practical thing on the page and the thing no competitor in this market mentions at all. A tutoring arrangement in a crowded flat fails for physical reasons long before it fails for academic ones.

The requirements are specific. A video session needs a surface, a device, a stable connection, and a space where nobody walks through or talks for forty-five minutes. A full timed paper needs the same for ninety minutes, plus the discipline of not being interrupted even once, because an interruption at minute fifty invalidates the pacing data the paper was meant to produce. In Julphar's older towers, with siblings and a shared living room, neither of those is automatically available.

The solutions are unglamorous and they work. Agree in week one which room is used and what the rest of the household does during the session, rather than negotiating it weekly. Pick a time when the flat is naturally quietest, which in many households is earlier than the obvious slot rather than later. Use headphones, which converts a shared room into a workable one for a conversational session even if not for a timed paper. And find one external venue for the long sittings: the school library, a relative's home, or an early weekend morning before anybody else is awake.

The reason this matters more than it sounds is that a cancelled or interrupted session is worse than a missed one, because it consumes the slot, the fee and the student's goodwill while producing nothing. A household that solves the room problem in week one keeps far more of its term than one that improvises.

sections.heading: A private tutor against the school's own support
paragraphs: Families routinely pay for something their school already provides, and in a small emirate where schools often run clinics and after-hours sessions the overlap can be substantial. Before buying anything, it is worth establishing what is already available, because the two kinds of support are genuinely different and the differences are the basis for a sensible division of labour.

A school knows the internal deadline calendar, sets the mocks, supervises the Extended Essay, and has the student's whole record in front of it. It cannot usually offer one-to-one time at length, cannot choose the teacher the student works best with, and in a small cohort may have only one person who teaches a particular Higher Level option. A private tutor can offer sustained one-to-one attention, a second experienced reading of a piece of work, and a specialist in a subject the school teaches with one teacher, but has no authority over deadlines, no access to the student's full record unless the family shares it, and no role in supervision.

The division that works is therefore straightforward. The school owns deadlines, supervision and the internal record. The tutor owns diagnosis, technique and sustained practice on specific components. Where a family is uncertain, the test is whether the task requires authority or attention: authority tasks belong to the school and attention tasks belong to a tutor.

Asking the school what it provides also produces a second benefit. A school that runs a weekly subject clinic has effectively supplied a free version of exactly the service a family was about to buy, and a family that knows about it can spend the money on something the school cannot do instead.

sections.heading: One weekly hour against a short intensive block
paragraphs: This is the choice that changes a Diploma outcome more than any other spending decision, and most families make it by default rather than by comparison. A year of weekly hours and an eight-week intensive block cost broadly similar amounts and do entirely different jobs.

The weekly hour is cumulative. It works where a topic sequence has broken down and has to be rebuilt, because rebuilding needs regular contact and spaced return to the same material. It is the right purchase in the first year of a course, in a subject that is genuinely weak, and it should step down to fortnightly once the diagnosed gap closes.

The intensive block is conversional. It works where the knowledge is already present and the marks are not being earned: timed questions marked against a published scheme, with an error log grouped by cause, over four to eight weeks. It changes technique quickly, it cannot build two years of missing content, and it has to be placed deliberately rather than bought when a family happens to panic.

The commonest expensive mistake is to buy the weekly hour for a technique problem, which means paying for a year to fix something an eight-week block would have fixed. The second commonest is to buy the block for a content problem, which produces a frustrated student and the conclusion that tutoring does not work. A diagnosis distinguishes them in a single session, which is the whole argument for doing it first.

sections.heading: Triaging the three Higher Levels
paragraphs: A Diploma student carries three Higher Level subjects and a household rarely has the capacity to support all three. Spreading the available hours evenly across them feels fair and is usually the least effective allocation, because the three subjects are almost never in the same condition.

A better allocation starts from three questions per subject. Is the problem content or technique, since technique responds in weeks and content takes a term. How much of the grade is still movable, which depends on how much of the course remains and where the internal component stands. And what does the subject do for the student's post-16 plan, because a subject carrying an offer requirement is worth more marginal effort than one that does not.

Run those three questions across three subjects and a clear ranking usually appears. The typical outcome is that one subject gets a weekly slot because its content needs rebuilding, one gets a short block later because its problem is technique, and one gets nothing beyond the school's own provision because it is already secure or because nothing depends on it. That is a rational allocation and it is almost never what a household arrives intending to buy.

The table sets out the triage. It is deliberately a framework rather than a recommendation, because the answer depends on the specific student, and the point is to make the decision explicit rather than letting it default to whichever subject produced the most recent bad mark.
