sections.heading: What a parent should do, and what a tutor should
paragraphs: A useful comparison that almost never appears: of the things that improve a Diploma outcome, some need a subject specialist and some need a parent, and confusing the two produces either an over-involved household or an outsourced one.

The parent tasks are logistical and motivational rather than academic, and they are the ones nobody else can do. Protecting the slot so that it is not the first thing cancelled. Settling the room and the household's rules for it. Collecting the school's deadline calendar in September. Noticing whether work happens between sessions, which is the single biggest determinant of whether tuition achieves anything. And asking, occasionally, whether the recurring error causes have changed, which is the only honest progress measure available.

The tutor tasks are the ones that need subject knowledge: diagnosing whether a loss is content, method, command term or timing; teaching the content where it is genuinely missing; marking work against the published scheme rather than an answer key; explaining what a criterion descriptor actually demands; and testing whether a coursework decision can reach the upper bands at all.

The failure modes are symmetrical. A parent who takes on academic judgement ends up arguing with a teenager about chemistry, which damages both the relationship and the chemistry. A household that outsources the logistical half finds the slot quietly dissolving in the autumn of the final year, and then concludes that the tutor was ineffective. Dividing the list explicitly, in week one, prevents both.
bullets: Parent: protect the slot, settle the room, collect the deadline calendar.
Parent: notice whether work happens between sessions; nothing matters more.
Tutor: diagnose the cause, teach the content, mark to the scheme, explain the criteria.
Neither: arguing about subject content across a dinner table.

sections.heading: Comparing this term with last term, honestly
paragraphs: The last comparison is the one that tells a family whether to continue, and it is almost always made against the wrong measure. A grade on a report is a poor progress signal: it moves for reasons that have nothing to do with tutoring, it arrives too late to act on, and in a small cohort it reflects the cohort as much as the student.

The honest measure is the error log. If the recurring causes in marked work have changed, something is working. If the same causes keep appearing term after term, the plan has not landed regardless of what the grade did. That is a factual conversation rather than an anxious one, and it is available every fortnight rather than once a term.

A second measure worth using is pacing, because it is objective and easy to track. Time one question at the start of a block and the same style of question eight weeks later. A student who is faster at the same accuracy is genuinely improving, whatever the next report says. A student whose speed has not moved after eight weeks of timed practice has a specific problem that needs naming rather than more hours.

The third is the step-down test. A provider that never proposes reducing frequency is managing revenue rather than marks. The point of a weekly slot is to stop needing it, and the honest end state of a successful arrangement is fortnightly contact, then none until the next pressure point. If that conversation has never been raised after two terms, raise it.
bullets: Measure whether the recurring error causes have changed, not what the grade did.
Track pacing: same accuracy, faster, is real improvement.
A good plan proposes its own step down.
Two terms with no step-down conversation is a signal worth acting on.

sections.heading: Honesty, materials and the permit
paragraphs: A tutor may teach the subject content, explain each assessment criterion and command term, mark work against the published scheme, test whether a coursework topic or method is viable, and give written feedback on a draft the student has already written. That is the whole of the legitimate service and it is a substantial service.

A tutor must never write, redraft or complete an Internal Assessment, a Mathematics exploration, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or any assessed coursework, and must not supply text, data or diagrams for submission. A page found during research for this project sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, and the consequence of buying one falls on the student rather than on whoever sold it. In a small emirate, where cohorts are tiny and work is read closely, that is a practical risk as well as a principled one.

On materials: no tutor should reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads. The official source should be referenced and linked instead, which is why this page carries no attachments and asks readers to confirm mark allocations against the subject guide their own school issues.

Julphar hires by word of mouth far more than by search, which makes one question easy to skip entirely: whether the tutor a neighbour recommends holds a permit. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so anybody quoting you an amount for it has invented the amount. The permit in question is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, which makes two working days the entire cost of being on the right side of it. Eligibility covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. As for us, IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from the Department of Knowledge, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no tutor can promise a grade, whichever of the two shapes compared above a family ends up buying.

process.title: Settle the room before the schedule
process.description: In Julphar the scarce input is forty-five uninterrupted minutes rather than a free hour. Decide which room is used, what the rest of the household does during the session, and where the ninety-minute papers will be sat, before anything is booked.

process.title: Ask the school what it already provides
process.description: Subject clinics, after-hours sessions, library access and coursework supervision all reduce what needs buying. A school running a weekly clinic has already supplied a free version of part of the service, which frees the budget for something the school cannot do.

process.title: Take the free diagnostic session
process.description: The first session is a diagnosis with no card details taken. It classifies lost marks into content, method, command term and timing, which is what decides whether the right purchase is a weekly slot or a short block. You keep the written summary either way.

process.title: Triage the three Higher Levels explicitly
process.description: Run three questions across each subject: content or technique, how much is still movable, and whether an offer depends on the grade. The usual outcome is one weekly slot, one later block and one left to the school, which is rarely what a household arrives intending to buy.

process.title: Review against the error log, then step down
process.description: Progress is whether the recurring causes change, not what the next report says. Once a diagnosed gap closes, weekly work moves to fortnightly or stops until the next pressure point, and that conversation should come from us rather than from you.

whyPoints.title: The constraint nobody else names
whyPoints.description: Julphar has the shortest journeys in the emirate and the least spare room, so a plan built around short reliably held sessions works where one built around long ambitious ones collapses. No competitor page in this market mentions the room at all.

whyPoints.title: The overlap with school support surfaced
whyPoints.description: Schools own deadlines, supervision and the internal record; tutors own diagnosis, technique and sustained practice. Asking what the school already provides frequently saves a family from paying twice for the same thing.

whyPoints.title: Weekly against intensive, compared rather than sold
whyPoints.description: A year of weekly hours and an eight-week block cost similar amounts and do different jobs. Buying the wrong one is the most expensive ordinary mistake in this market, and a single diagnostic session distinguishes them.

whyPoints.title: Three Higher Levels triaged, not treated equally
whyPoints.description: Even allocation across three subjects feels fair and usually achieves least. Content before technique, movable before settled, and offer-carrying before incidental is a rational order that households rarely arrive with.

whyPoints.title: A progress measure that is not a grade
whyPoints.description: Whether the recurring error causes have changed, and whether pacing has improved at the same accuracy. Both are available every fortnight, unlike a report, and both are factual rather than anxious.

whyPoints.title: Limits stated, including ours
whyPoints.description: No part of assessed work produced. No syllabus documents or mark schemes as downloads. No promised grades, no self-published ratings, and no claim of approval from the Department of Knowledge or any awarding body.

faqs.question: Is living in Julphar an advantage or a disadvantage for tutoring?
faqs.answer: Both, on different axes. Julphar sits inside the city's school cluster, so journeys are the shortest in the emirate, sessions can start earlier and fewer evenings are lost. What it lacks is spare quiet space: a Diploma session needs forty-five uninterrupted minutes and a full timed paper needs ninety, and older apartment stock with siblings and a shared living room does not supply either automatically. The coastal communities have the exact inverse problem.

faqs.question: Where should a Julphar student sit a full past paper?
faqs.answer: Somewhere other than a busy flat, because an interruption at minute fifty destroys the pacing information the paper was meant to produce. The options that work in practice are the school library, a relative's home, or an early weekend morning before the rest of the household is awake. Plan the venue as deliberately as the time: a full paper is the only thing that tests pacing and the decision about which question to leave.

faqs.question: How do I stop a session being interrupted in a shared flat?
faqs.answer: Settle it in week one rather than negotiating weekly. Agree which room is used, what everyone else does for those forty-five minutes, and which hour the flat is naturally quietest, which is often earlier than the obvious slot. Headphones turn a shared room into a workable space for conversational work, though not for a timed paper. Households that fix this in week one keep far more of their term than those that improvise it.

faqs.question: What does my child's school already provide that I might be paying for twice?
faqs.answer: Ask directly, because in this emirate schools often run more than families realise: subject clinics, after-hours sessions, library access during study periods, and formal Extended Essay supervision. A school running a weekly clinic has already supplied a free version of part of what you were about to buy. That frees the budget for the things a school genuinely cannot offer, such as sustained one-to-one time or a second experienced reading of internal work.

faqs.question: Should I buy a weekly hour or an eight-week block?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the diagnosis, and the two cost broadly similar amounts while doing different jobs. A weekly hour rebuilds a broken topic sequence, because rebuilding needs regular spaced return to the same material. An eight-week block converts knowledge already present into marks through timed practice marked against a published scheme. Buying the weekly hour for a technique problem means paying for a year to fix something eight weeks would have fixed.

faqs.question: How should I decide which Higher Level subject to support?
faqs.answer: Run three questions across all three. Is the problem content or technique, since technique responds in weeks and content takes a term. How much of the grade is still movable, given how much course remains and where the internal component stands. And does a post-16 offer depend on this particular grade. The usual rational outcome is one weekly slot, one later block, and one left to the school, which is rarely the even split households arrive intending.

faqs.question: What should a parent do, and what should be left to the tutor?
faqs.answer: Parents own the logistics and the motivation: protecting the slot, settling the room, collecting the school's deadline calendar in September, and noticing whether work happens between sessions, which matters more than anything else. Tutors own the academic judgement: diagnosing the cause of lost marks, teaching content, marking to the published scheme and explaining what a criterion descriptor demands. A parent who takes on academic judgement ends up arguing about chemistry with a teenager.

faqs.question: Without waiting for a report, how can I tell the sessions are landing?
faqs.answer: Watch the recurring error causes rather than the next report. If the causes appearing in marked work have changed, something is working; if the same ones keep appearing term after term, the plan has not landed regardless of the grade. A second objective measure is pacing: time one question at the start of a block and the same style of question eight weeks later, and faster at the same accuracy is real improvement, whatever the report says.

faqs.question: At what point should a Julphar family stop paying for weekly sessions?
faqs.answer: Sooner than most arrangements do. The purpose of a weekly slot is to stop needing it, so the honest end state is fortnightly contact and then none until the next pressure point. A provider that has never proposed reducing the frequency after two terms is managing its revenue rather than your child's marks. If that conversation has not come from the provider, raise it, and expect a specific answer about what would have to be true to step down.

faqs.question: Is an in-home tutor more practical in Julphar than elsewhere in RAK?
faqs.answer: More practical, yes, because Julphar is the best-connected part of the emirate and the travel premium is lowest here. Less useful than it sounds, though, for two reasons: a visitor needs the same quiet room an online session does and cannot be moved to a bedroom at short notice, and the shorter journey does not change who has actually taught your child's Higher Level option. Published rates run AED 150 to 300 online against AED 180 to 500 in-home, read October 2026.

faqs.question: Can a 45-minute session really do anything useful at Diploma level?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided it is built around a finishable task rather than a whole paper. One question group attempted under time, then marked against the published scheme in the same sitting with the student reading the marker's wording, takes thirty to forty minutes and produces a specific named reason a mark was lost. Four of those a month is a diagnosis. What forty-five minutes cannot do is test pacing across a complete paper, which is why the long sitting belongs elsewhere.

faqs.question: We have two children in a Julphar flat. Can both have sessions?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, but consecutively rather than simultaneously, because two video lessons at once need two quiet spaces and older apartment stock rarely offers them. Consecutive slots, for example 4:15pm and 5:15pm, concentrate the week's disruption into one evening and need only one quiet room at a time. That arrangement also tends to survive the term, where two simultaneous sessions in a shared living room usually do not.

faqs.question: Does my child need a tutor if the school has only one teacher for the subject?
faqs.answer: That is precisely the situation where external support adds most, and it is common in this emirate. A sole subject teacher has no colleague to moderate against on whether a piece of internal work is where it should be, and the student has no second experienced reading available locally. The value is calibration rather than remediation: somebody who has taught the same component to other cohorts saying whether the work is on track.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest useful thing a Julphar family can buy?
faqs.answer: A diagnosis, because it is free here and because almost all of the avoidable spending in this market comes from buying hours against an undiagnosed problem. One session that establishes whether the losses are content, method, command term or timing redirects everything after it, and it frequently reveals that the right purchase is an eight-week block later rather than a weekly slot now. You keep the written summary whether or not anything else is booked.

faqs.question: Why does this page talk about rooms rather than about teaching?
faqs.answer: Because in dense central housing the room is what decides whether the teaching happens. A cancelled or interrupted session is worse than a missed one: it consumes the slot, the fee and the student's goodwill while producing nothing, and it is the commonest reason a plan that looked sensible in September has quietly stopped by November. No competitor page in this market mentions it, which is a reasonable indication that none of them has run a plan from an old-town apartment.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-julphar.closingHeading: Fix the room, then book the diagnosis
ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-julphar.closingBody: For a Julphar household the first two decisions are physical rather than academic: which room a session happens in, and where the ninety-minute papers will be sat. Settle those, ask the school what support it already provides, and then take a free diagnostic session with no card details taken. The written summary will say whether the right purchase is a weekly slot now or a short block later, and which of three Higher Levels should get the hours. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, in forty-five-minute slots that can actually be kept.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-khuzam.tutorsIntro: Khuzam families are matched with Diploma subject specialists who commit to a slot for a term rather than to a single session, because in this emirate continuity with one tutor is harder to replace than anywhere else in the country.

intro.heading: In Ras Al Khaimah, timing is the scarce resource
paragraphs: Most pages about tutoring treat time as a convenience question and price as the real one. In Ras Al Khaimah the ranking is reversed. The private-school set here is small and concentrated around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab, the Diploma cohort inside it is smaller again, and the number of teachers in the emirate who have actually taught a particular Higher Level option is often in single figures. When supply is that thin, the question is not what a tutor costs but whether anybody suitable is free in the window you need.

Khuzam sits inland in Ras Al Khaimah city, a residential district of villas and family housing with a straightforward drive into the city's school cluster. That makes the school run manageable. It does not change the supply problem: a student in Khuzam sitting Chemistry at Higher Level is not short of roads, they are short of people who have taught that syllabus.

Capacity also moves through the year. A specialist who is free in September is frequently committed by February, because the same teachers cannot teach more hours and demand rises as a series approaches. That makes the booking calendar as important as the revision calendar, and it is the single most actionable thing on this page: in this emirate, early is not a virtue, it is availability.

Delivery is stated plainly. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The phrase in this page's address is what parents search, and it is answered honestly: what in-home tuition is quoted at in this market, what the travel premium consists of, and why removing the radius matters more here than in Dubai, where a school might have three teachers on the same course.

On dates, the page is deliberately restrained. No IB exam or results date appears, because the IB's own site returns an error to automated checking and nothing in this project has been verified from the board itself. What is safe to state is that UAE schools sit the May session and that a November session exists as an alternative route, and that every specific date should come from your school's Diploma coordinator or from ibo.org.

What follows is a plan rather than a pitch: the Grade 11 year term by term, the three core components that have no lesson slot, a capacity calendar for scarce subjects, how a schedule works when the specialist is in a different time zone, what the emirate's own regulator actually approves, and the boundaries that apply to coursework. Market rates appear once, attributed to the providers that published them and dated October 2026, because a family here still deserves a number to judge a quote against even when the real problem is supply.
bullets: Ras Al Khaimah's private schools are regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge.
That authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, not just inspection outcomes.
Specialist capacity in this emirate is tightest in the spring and loosest in September.
The Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS have no timetabled lesson, which is why they slip.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-khuzam.programmesIntro: Three IB stages reach Khuzam households, and the planning problem is different at each because only one of them has a fixed external endpoint.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external papers and no deadlines, which makes the calendar forgiving and the foundations easy to neglect. The work that pays off later is mechanics: number bonds, written method, reading stamina, explaining an answer in a sentence. None of it is urgent and all of it is expensive to repair at Diploma level.
programmes.countryNote: In a small emirate the primary cohort is tight-knit and a child's position inside it says little about national standing. An external view once a year, rather than weekly tuition, is usually the right purchase at this stage in Ras Al Khaimah.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, assessed through tasks spread across the year rather than through an examination window. The marks reward process, so a student who produces correct answers without justification loses the same marks repeatedly until somebody shows them the strand wording.
programmes.countryNote: MYP is where Diploma habits are formed. A Khuzam student who learns in Year 9 that 'explain' demands a mechanism arrives in Grade 11 with an advantage that no amount of Grade 12 revision replaces, and at a time when specialist capacity is easy to book.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, with an internally assessed component in every subject running on school-set deadlines. The deadlines cluster in one autumn, and the papers sit in the spring, which makes the whole thing a sequencing exercise.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the emirate's scarcity bites hardest. A Khuzam student may be one of very few in Ras Al Khaimah on a particular Higher Level option, with one teacher locally who knows the course and no second opinion available inside the emirate at all.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-khuzam.subjectsIntro: The Diploma subjects most often requested from Ras Al Khaimah, with a note on how scarce each one is locally, because scarcity is what determines when you need to book.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Standard Level is the most widely taught Diploma course in the emirate; Higher Level is not. Paper 1 is taken without a calculator and is where fluent calculator users lose a grade's worth of marks on hand algebra.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led. Higher Level adds graph theory and matrices, usually taught late, so a student behind in autumn faces new content and revision together. Locally scarce at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the losses, with data questions catching students who state a trend without its cause. One of the hardest subjects to source locally at Higher Level in this emirate.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Unit errors, gradients read instead of calculated, explanations written as equations. Technique responds quickly to timed practice, which makes a short booked block effective even late. Very scarce locally.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Naming a process earns a mark, ordering its stages earns the rest. Statistics questions catch students who have never calculated a standard deviation by hand. More widely taught locally than Chemistry or Physics.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram marks are the most available and most commonly dropped. The commentaries need recent articles collected as they appear. Among the scarcest Diploma subjects in the Northern Emirates.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the case stimulus is the whole paper. Higher Level adds the pre-released case study, published far enough ahead that early structured reading is unusually valuable.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 rewards argument about how a text works rather than summary. The Individual Oral needs a global issue chosen early. Reasonable local supply, with the widest quality spread of any subject.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic A
subjects.description: Language B assesses reading, writing to a specified text type and a spoken component. Home speakers lose marks on register and text-type convention rather than vocabulary. Strongest local supply in the emirate.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The essay answers a prescribed title against named criteria and rewards one developed line of argument. Breadth is the standard failure, and the component has no lesson slot in most timetables.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-khuzam.regionsIntro: What differs across these communities is the drive to the school cluster and how late a session realistically starts. The supply problem is the same everywhere in the emirate.

regions.name: Khuzam
regions.note: Inland residential district of Ras Al Khaimah city, with villa housing and a short drive to the city school cluster. Family houses mean a quiet room for a full timed paper is usually available.

regions.name: Al Nakheel
regions.note: Central district and the heart of the emirate's school and commercial cluster. The shortest school runs in Ras Al Khaimah, so an earlier slot is available if a student works better before dinner.

regions.name: Al Dhait
regions.note: Large residential area south of the city with substantial villa housing. Slightly longer runs than Khuzam and a 5:00pm start is the realistic earliest for most households.

regions.name: Al Hamra Village
regions.note: Coastal master-planned community towards the south of the emirate, with its own school presence. The drive into the city cluster is long enough that an in-home evening visit becomes impractical.

regions.name: Mina Al Arab
regions.note: Waterfront community with a mix of villas and apartments. Families here are generally further from the city school cluster, which lengthens the school run and compresses the evening.

regions.name: Julphar
regions.note: Older quarter around the historic port and the towers on the creek. Dense and central, with short runs but apartment living, so a quiet room needs planning rather than assuming.

regions.name: Al Qusaidat
regions.note: Established residential district north-east of the creek. Reasonable runs into the city cluster and a 4:45pm start holds on most days of the school week.

modes.title: A term-long reserved slot

In an emirate where a suitable specialist may be the only one available, holding a reserved slot across a term is worth more than any price difference, because the alternative to continuity here is not a cheaper tutor but no tutor.

modes.description: A short intensive aimed at one thing: the Grade 12 coursework cluster, the mock window, or the weeks before the papers. Because capacity is scarce, the block is reserved on the calendar at the start of the year rather than requested when it is needed.
bullets: Two or three sessions a week across four to eight weeks

modes.title: Core-component coaching

sections.heading: Why timing matters more here than in Dubai
paragraphs: A family in Dubai looking for a Higher Level Chemistry tutor is choosing between candidates. A family in Khuzam is often establishing whether one exists. That difference changes every subsequent decision, and it is the reason this page is organised around a calendar rather than around a price list.

The arithmetic is straightforward. The emirate's private-school set is small and concentrated around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab. The proportion of those schools running the full Diploma is smaller again. Inside each Diploma school, a particular Higher Level option may be taught by one teacher, and that teacher is frequently the person least able to tutor the students who need them: in Abu Dhabi the regulator's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid tuition of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that bars the same. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the current policy document and should be verified against it, but the pattern across sources is consistent.

What follows is a capacity problem rather than a pricing one. Independent tutors who do cover these subjects are typically covering them for several students across several emirates, and their diaries fill as a series approaches. A family that enquires in February is competing for the hours left over; a family that enquires in September is choosing from an open diary.

Removing the geography removes the binding constraint. Teaching over live video means the question stops being who lives within reach of Khuzam and becomes who teaches this course, which is a much larger set. But it does not remove the capacity question, because good specialists in any location still fill up. Early booking is the one lever available to every family here, and it costs nothing.

sections.heading: Grade 11 is the year the Diploma is decided
paragraphs: Families almost universally treat Grade 12 as the year that matters, and in terms of attention that is correct. In terms of leverage it is wrong. By the time Grade 12 begins, the subject and level choices are fixed, the content foundations are either built or missing, the coursework topics are either viable or not, and predicted grades are about to be generated from work already done.

Grade 11 autumn has two jobs: establishing whether the three Higher Levels chosen are the right three, and building content while nothing else competes for attention. A change of level made in the first term is routine; the same change made a year later is disruptive and sometimes impossible. This is also the period when specialist capacity is easiest to book, which makes it the cheapest term in the course in every sense.

Grade 11 spring has one job that matters more than all the others: choosing coursework topics and research questions that will actually work. A Mathematics exploration on a topic with no mathematics to develop, a science investigation whose method will not generate analysable data, an Extended Essay question too broad to answer inside 4,000 words: each of those caps a grade before a word is written, and each is visible to a specialist in a single session.

The table sets out the two Grade 11 terms and the summer that follows, with what each should deliver. The point is not that Grade 12 does not matter. It is that Grade 12 can only execute decisions Grade 11 made.

sections.heading: Three components with no lesson slot
paragraphs: The Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and CAS share one structural feature that explains almost all of the trouble they cause: none of them has a timetabled lesson in which the work gets done. Subject content arrives with a teacher, a room and a period. The core arrives with a deadline.

The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent piece whose fate is decided by the research question. A question that is too broad produces an essay that cannot be cut without losing its argument, which is why students arrive at 5,000 words and cannot see a way back. The narrowing has to happen before the writing, and it is a conversation rather than a revision exercise. The school provides a supervisor; a tutor's legitimate role is explaining what each named criterion demands and giving written feedback on drafts the student has written.

The Theory of Knowledge essay responds to a prescribed title and rewards one line of argument developed properly, with examples that do specific work. The standard failure is breadth: four knowledge claims gestured at, several areas of knowledge mentioned, nothing actually argued. Because there is no content to revise, students often do not know what preparation would even look like, which makes this the component where a single well-aimed session changes most.

CAS is not graded but it is a completion requirement, and in a small emirate with fewer organised opportunities it can become a genuine administrative problem late in the course. It belongs on the household's calendar in Grade 11, not in the final term.

sections.heading: The capacity calendar for scarce subjects
paragraphs: This is the section a family in Khuzam actually needs and no competitor page in this market publishes: not what tutoring costs, but when the person you want is likely to be free. Capacity in specialist Diploma subjects follows a predictable annual cycle, and planning around it is free.

September and October are the loosest months. New enquiries have not yet arrived in volume, students have not yet had a disappointing assessment, and tutors are building a term. A reserved weekly slot agreed in September usually holds for the whole year, which is worth more in this emirate than a marginally better rate.

November through January tightens as autumn reports land and coursework deadlines bite, with the heaviest pressure on core-component support because every Grade 12 in the country is writing at once. February onwards is the tightest period of the year for Higher Level sciences and Mathematics, which is precisely when most families start looking. By the final weeks before a series, availability for a scarce subject is largely whatever was not booked earlier.

It is a planning aid rather than a promise: availability depends on real diaries, and where no specialist is free in the window you need, the honest answer is to say so rather than to offer a generalist. sections.heading: Scheduling when the specialist is not in the emirate
paragraphs: If the whole argument of this page is that the right teacher is probably not in Ras Al Khaimah, the practical question is how a weekly session with somebody elsewhere actually works. The answer is less exotic than it sounds, but it has to be set up deliberately rather than assumed.

Everything is scheduled on Gulf Standard Time and written down in that time zone, which removes the single most common cause of missed sessions. For a tutor in a nearby time zone an afternoon slot in Khuzam is an afternoon slot for them too; for a tutor further west, a Khuzam evening is their morning, which can actually be more reliable than a local tutor's end-of-day. The thing to establish in week one is the tutor's own fixed commitments, so the slot sits in a stable part of their week rather than a flexible one.

The second thing to settle is what happens around holidays, because school calendars differ between countries. A tutor whose own region has a break in a week that is a normal school week in Ras Al Khaimah should say so at the start of term, and the plan should absorb it rather than discover it. Ramadan works the same way in reverse: sessions move to post-Iftar timing for the month, which an online booking handles easily.

The third is continuity. In a thin market the value of a reserved slot with a named tutor is high, so the arrangement should be termly rather than session by session, with a written handover if a change becomes necessary. A tutor who disappears mid-term is a much bigger problem in Khuzam than in Dubai, because the replacement pool nearby is close to empty.
bullets: Write every slot down in Gulf Standard Time, in both diaries.
Ask the tutor for their own fixed commitments and holiday weeks at the start of term.

sections.heading: Who regulates your school here, and what they approve
paragraphs: Parents arriving in Ras Al Khaimah from Dubai often look for a KHDA inspection report on a local school and find nothing, because KHDA's remit stops at the Dubai border. Private schools in this emirate are regulated by the Department of Knowledge, which the UAE government's own portal describes as regulating private education in the emirate.

The scope is wider than inspection. Ras Al Khaimah's authority, like Sharjah's, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That means the programme a school offers and the fees it charges have both been through the emirate authority, which is a useful thing for a parent to know when asking whether an offering is what it claims to be. The complete regulator map for UAE private schools is KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

None of that gives a tutoring provider any standing, and this page claims none. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from the Department of Knowledge, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai would need a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, renewed annually with the request at least 30 days before expiry; an individual tutor needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Neither is a badge a matching platform can wear.

What a family can reasonably verify is the school's latest inspection outcome, requested directly, and the tutor's permit position, asked for in one sentence. Both are ordinary questions and both should get ordinary answers.

sections.heading: Results, the alternative session, and the fortnight after
paragraphs: The calendar does not end with the papers, and the fortnight after results is where families in a small emirate are most exposed, because there is often nobody locally to ask. Three options exist and they have different deadlines, so identifying which applies matters more than reacting quickly.

The first is an enquiry upon results, where the school asks the board to review a mark. That is a school process with its own deadline and criteria, and the right question for the Diploma coordinator is whether the component profile makes a review plausible rather than whether the overall result was disappointing. The second is a retake in a later session. The third is to accept the result, which is frequently the correct answer and almost never presented as one.

The deciding input in all three cases is the component breakdown: marks by paper and by internal component. A shortfall concentrated in one paper is a different problem from a shortfall spread across every component, and only the first is reliably closed by a short block of technique work. Asking for that breakdown before making any decision is the step most families skip.

On dates, the same restraint applies as elsewhere on this page. UAE schools sit the May session and a November session exists as an alternative route, but no IB date here has been verified from the board, so none is published. Ask your Diploma coordinator about entry routes and deadlines, and tell any receiving institution about timing before relying on it.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, materials and the permit
paragraphs: Three boundaries, stated before they are needed rather than after. The first is academic. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain each assessment criterion and what its descriptors demand, help narrow a research question, review a method for feasibility and ethics, and give written feedback on a draft the student has already written.

A tutor must never write, redraft or complete an Internal Assessment, a Mathematics exploration, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or any assessed coursework, and must not supply text, data or diagrams for a student to submit. A page found during research for this project sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is an academic integrity breach and an IB malpractice trigger, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on whoever sold it. In a small emirate, where a cohort is tiny and work is read closely, this matters practically as well as in principle.

The second boundary is materials. No tutor should reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads. The official source should be referenced and linked instead, which is why this page carries no attachments and asks readers to confirm weightings against the guide their own school issues.

The third is who may tutor. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so none is quoted. No tutor can promise a grade either, because boundaries are set after a series on the basis of that series' papers.

faqs.question: Is there actually a Higher Level Diploma specialist available in Khuzam?
faqs.answer: Often not locally, and it is better to hear that at the start. The emirate's private-school set is small, the proportion running the full Diploma is smaller, and a given Higher Level option may be taught by one teacher in a school, who is frequently the person least able to tutor the students who need them. Removing the radius is what changes the answer: teaching over live video turns the question from who lives near Khuzam into who teaches this course.

faqs.question: When should a Ras Al Khaimah family book a Diploma tutor?
faqs.answer: September, for the year. Specialist capacity follows a predictable cycle: loose in September and October while tutors are building a term, tightening from November as autumn reports land and coursework bites, and tightest from February onwards for Higher Level sciences and Mathematics, which is exactly when most families start looking. A reserved weekly slot agreed early usually holds for the whole year, and in a thin market that is worth more than a marginally better rate.

faqs.question: Why is Grade 11 more important than Grade 12 for planning?
faqs.answer: Because Grade 12 can only execute decisions Grade 11 made. By the time the final year begins, subject and level choices are fixed, content foundations are built or missing, coursework topics are viable or not, and predicted grades are about to be generated from work already done. A level change in the first term of Grade 11 is routine; the same change a year later is disruptive and sometimes impossible. Grade 11 is also when specialist capacity is easiest to reserve.

faqs.question: Which Diploma components have no timetabled lesson?
faqs.answer: The Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and CAS. Subject content arrives with a teacher, a room and a period; those three arrive with a deadline and nothing else. That structural fact explains most of the trouble they cause, and it is why they need booked blocks of their own in Grade 11 rather than whatever attention is left in the final term. The school supplies a supervisor for the Extended Essay; a tutor's role is narrower and is set out on this page.

faqs.question: How does a weekly session with a tutor outside the emirate work?
faqs.answer: Everything is scheduled and written down in Gulf Standard Time in both diaries, which removes the commonest cause of missed sessions. In week one, ask the tutor for their own fixed commitments and holiday weeks, because school calendars differ between countries and a break the tutor's region takes may be a normal school week in Ras Al Khaimah. Book termly with a named tutor rather than session by session, and expect a written handover if a change becomes necessary.

faqs.question: Who regulates private schools in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: The emirate's Department of Knowledge, which regulates private education here and, like Sharjah's authority, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods rather than only inspecting. That is wider than many parents assume, and it means both the programme a school offers and the fees it charges have been through the emirate authority. A parent arriving from Dubai should note that KHDA reports do not cover schools here; request the school's latest inspection outcome directly.

faqs.question: What caps a Mathematics exploration grade before it is written?
faqs.answer: The topic. The exploration is marked across five criteria totalling 20 marks, with use of mathematics carrying the largest single allocation, so a well-written piece on a subject with nothing to develop mathematically cannot reach the upper bands however it is polished. A specialist can test viability in one session, which is why that check belongs in Grade 11 spring. The student chooses, writes and develops every part of the work themselves; a tutor tests the plan and feeds back on drafts.

faqs.question: Why does my child's Extended Essay keep growing past 4,000 words?
faqs.answer: Because the research question is too broad, almost always. A question that cannot be answered inside the limit produces an essay that will not cut without losing its argument, which is why a student at 5,000 words cannot see a way back. The work is narrowing the question and then rebuilding the structure around the narrower version, and it belongs before the writing. A tutor may do that narrowing work and give written feedback on drafts; a tutor may never rewrite the essay.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying more for an in-home tutor if one is available in RAK?
faqs.answer: It buys physical presence, which genuinely helps a younger or easily distracted student, and the premium is real: a qualified subject tutor working online is advertised at AED 150 to 300 an hour, while in-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent tutors, read October 2026. In this emirate the harder problem is that the in-home pool for a scarce Higher Level subject may be empty regardless of what a family is willing to pay.

faqs.question: What if nobody in Ras Al Khaimah covers my child's Higher Level option?
faqs.answer: You get told, rather than handed a generalist. The honest position in Ras Al Khaimah is that supply for rare Higher Level options is thin and sometimes nil in a given window. Where that happens the options are a later start date, a different format such as a short booked block closer to the series, or a recommendation to look elsewhere. Concealing a coverage gap costs a family a term, which is a worse outcome than losing an enquiry.

faqs.question: How should we use the summer between Grade 11 and Grade 12?
faqs.answer: For one named job, in three or four weeks with two sessions a week, finishing before term starts. The usual target is the content gap identified in Grade 11 spring, or settling a coursework topic and method so the autumn cluster begins with a viable plan rather than a blank page. What does not work is running a full programme through July and August: a student who studies all summer arrives in September already tired, which costs more than the gap would have.

faqs.question: Why will you not print a May session date for a Khuzam student?
faqs.answer: Because none has been verified. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB exam or results date in this project is confirmed from the board, and publishing an unverified date that a family builds a revision schedule around would be worse than publishing none. What is safe to state is that UAE schools sit the May session and that a November session exists as an alternative route. Take every specific date from your Diploma coordinator or from ibo.org.

faqs.question: What should we ask for in the fortnight after Diploma results?
faqs.answer: The component breakdown first: marks by paper and by internal component. A shortfall concentrated in one paper is a different problem from one spread across every component, and only the first is reliably closed by a short block of technique work. Then ask the coordinator whether the profile makes an enquiry upon results plausible, which is a school process with its own deadline and criteria. Accepting the result is often the right answer and is almost never offered as one.

faqs.question: Does my child's tutor need a UAE permit if they teach from abroad?
faqs.answer: The permit framework applies to private tutoring in the UAE, and the honest position is that a family should ask the provider directly what basis their tutors work on rather than assume. For tutors inside the country, the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can tuition raise a predicted grade that has already been issued?
faqs.answer: No, and that is worth knowing a year earlier than most families learn it. Predictions are issued in the autumn of Grade 12 and reflect work already completed, so tuition bought afterwards cannot change the prediction, only the final result. The window in which predictions are actually earned is Grade 11 and the spring that follows it. That is the strongest argument available for light, early, well-targeted work rather than a heavy intervention in the term the applications are written.

intro.heading: Where Diploma marks actually go missing, and why it is rarely the topic a parent names
paragraphs: A parent in Mina Al Arab who asks for help with Chemistry is usually right that something is wrong and usually wrong about what. The named problem is a topic. The actual problem, in the overwhelming majority of marked scripts, is one of four things: a command term misread, a conclusion that does not follow from the data presented, working omitted on a question where method marks were available, or an answer that was correct in substance and not in the language the criteria pay for. None of those is fixed by re-teaching a topic.

That is why this page is written from the assessment rather than from the service. A Diploma subject is a defined set of components with published weightings, assessed against published criteria, with command terms that have specified meanings. All of that is readable in advance. A student who has read it is competing on different terms from one who has not, and most students have not, because nobody sat down with them and the subject guide in the first year. The subject guide your school holds is the authoritative document, and almost no family has opened it.

Take the simplest example. A question beginning explain requires a causal link; one beginning describe does not; one beginning evaluate requires a judgement supported by both sides. A student who answers all three the same way will lose the same marks in every paper in every subject for two years. It is a two-session fix with a mark scheme open, and it is worth more than a term of content revision. Of the competitor pages researched for these UAE searches, none sets out a single command term or a single assessment criterion.

The Internal Assessment is the second large reservoir of recoverable marks. Every Diploma subject has one, each is marked against lettered criteria with stated maximum marks, and the moderation process is conservative. Students who choose a question too broad to control, collect data before thinking about the analysis, or write first and read the criteria afterwards produce work that reads perfectly well and scores in the middle. Narrowing a research question is the single highest-value hour a Diploma tutor can spend. It is also the part of the Diploma a tutor can help with soonest, because the planning stage has no deadline pressure attached to it yet.

A word on how this is delivered, because the URL says home tutor. IB Gram teaches Mina Al Arab students one-to-one over live video, on a shared screen, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not place a tutor at a UAE address, and in-person visiting is a service we run only in India. For syllabus work that format is genuinely better rather than merely acceptable: the student's own script, the published criteria and the mark scheme can all be open at once, annotated by both people, and the annotations survive the session.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-mina-al-.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes are relevant to a Mina Al Arab household, and the assessment logic changes at each step. Here is what each one measures and the skill it leaves underdeveloped.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led with no external examinations, reported against learning outcomes and finishing with an Exhibition. The strengths it builds are question-forming and collaboration; the gap it leaves is written fluency under time constraint. Tutoring at this stage, where it is needed at all, is about reading speed, number fact recall and sustained independent working rather than about any curriculum content.
programmes.countryNote: Mina Al Arab families with primary-age children generally have short school runs along the coast road. The useful question at this stage is whether the child can read a question, plan an answer and finish it unaided, because the Middle Years Programme assumes all three from Year 7.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against criteria A to D with published descriptors, plus a Personal Project in the final year. Criterion-based assessment is excellent training for the Diploma's internal components and poor training for its written papers, because almost nothing in the Middle Years Programme is a timed external examination. The Personal Project is the first real experience of a self-scoped task with a distant deadline.
programmes.countryNote: Where a student moves between a Middle Years school and an IGCSE school on this coast, topic sequencing differs and genuine content gaps open in maths and science. Those gaps are findable in a single diagnostic session and generally closeable over a summer.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, usually three at Higher Level, scored out of 45. Each subject carries written papers with published weightings and an internally assessed component marked against lettered criteria. The core adds Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay at a 4,000-word limit, and Creativity, Activity, Service. Higher Level courses carry additional topics and, in several subjects, an extra paper.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, with November available where a school offers it. This page publishes no specific IB examination or results date, since the IB's own site cannot be checked automatically; the coordinator's internal deadline sheet is the calendar a plan should follow.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-home-tutor-in-mina-al-.subjectsIntro: Subject by subject, here is the component that decides the grade and the specific place marks are lost. This is the level of detail a parent should expect from anyone claiming to be a Diploma specialist.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the most lost marks at Higher Level. Calculation questions usually fail on units and significant figures rather than on method. In the Internal Assessment, the commonest loss is an investigation with one poorly controlled variable, which caps the analysis and evaluation criteria no matter how careful the write-up.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields and circular motion are the content separators; uncertainty propagation is the technical one. Students lose marks by quoting a result to more figures than the data supports and by describing a method without identifying control variables. Both appear in the papers and in the Internal Assessment, which makes them double-value work.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Terminology precision is what the mark scheme pays for: active transport against a concentration gradient, not simply movement. Extended-response questions reward structure over volume. In the Internal Assessment, an ambitious question with uncontrollable variation scores lower than a narrow one executed cleanly, every time.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic speed decides the Higher Level grade more than any single topic. Marks are lost by omitting working on multi-step questions where method marks exist, and by answers left in a form the question did not ask for. The Exploration needs genuine mathematics rather than an application with mathematics attached.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling, with heavy legitimate use of technology. The recurring loss is interpretation: a correct calculation followed by no statement of what it means in context. Examiners reward the sentence that answers the question, and students routinely stop one line too early.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysis of how a text works on a reader, across literary and non-literary material, with an Individual Oral recorded in a school window. Marks are lost to description of content rather than discussion of technique and effect, and to essays that assert without quoting. At Higher Level the additional essay carries its own internal deadlines.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides the analysis marks: an unlabelled axis or a curve shifted the wrong way loses them regardless of the prose. The top band requires evaluation that weighs competing effects and reaches a supported judgement. Internally assessed commentary work is spread across the course and needs scheduling.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The discipline is selecting one correct tool and applying it to the stimulus, not listing several. Marks are lost to general commentary about a company where the question asked for application to the data provided. Higher Level candidates meet a research-based component with its own word limit and criteria.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Systems thinking and terminology carry more weight than students expect from a subject often chosen as a dual option. The recurring loss is a general example offered where a named case study was required, which is a habit rather than a knowledge gap and takes about two sessions to correct.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay on a prescribed title plus an exhibition, both assessed against published criteria. Students lose marks by writing about knowledge in general rather than answering the title, and by offering examples that illustrate nothing in particular. The teachable skill is building an argument that a counter-position could actually challenge.

regions.name: Al Nakheel

modes.title: Subject teaching, weekly
modes.description: One or two hours a week on the syllabus itself, sequenced from the school's scheme of work and running slightly ahead of it. Suited to a genuine content gap at Higher Level, where the additional topics are the usual culprits. Judged on the student's own performance in timed questions on those topics, not on how the sessions felt.

The work is criteria literacy, question narrowing and feedback on the student's own draft. The tutor asks questions and points out where a conclusion is unsupported; the student writes every word of it.

modes.description: The format for a student whose understanding is sound and whose marks are not. sections.heading: Diploma assessment structure, and where the weight sits
paragraphs: Before any teaching, a student should be able to say what each component of their subject is worth. Surprisingly few can, and the consequence is predictable: effort distributed by preference rather than by weighting. A student who enjoys practical work and dislikes extended writing will happily spend twenty hours on an investigation worth a fifth of the grade and four on the paper worth nearly half of it.

The exact weightings differ by subject and by level, and the authoritative source is the subject guide your school holds, so the right move is to read that rather than a summary. What generalises is the shape. There are externally assessed written papers carrying the large majority of the marks, and one internally assessed component carrying a meaningful minority. Higher Level courses typically add an extra paper or an extended component, which is where the difference in workload between Higher and Standard Level actually appears.

The planning consequence is straightforward arithmetic. If a component is worth a fifth of a subject and a student is losing a third of its available marks, that is a recoverable chunk of the subject grade sitting in one place, usually fixable with criteria work rather than content teaching. If the same student is losing a tenth of the marks across the written papers, the recovery is larger in absolute terms but slower, because paper performance moves with technique and volume rather than with a single intervention.

The table below sets out the generic structure with the specific failure modes attached to each part. It is deliberately not a weightings table, because publishing per-subject percentages from memory would be exactly the kind of unsourced precision this project avoids. Take the numbers from the subject guide; take the failure modes from here.

sections.heading: Command terms, and the marks they quietly decide
paragraphs: IB questions are built on command terms with specified meanings, and the mark scheme pays for the thing the term demands rather than for everything the student knows. This is the most reliable source of recoverable marks in the entire Diploma, and it is invisible on a report card because it shows up as consistent underperformance rather than as a named weakness.

The pattern in a marked script is distinctive. The student scores well on recall questions, loses marks on extended responses, and the comments say things like needs more depth or did not answer the question. What has actually happened is a mismatch: the question asked for a judgement and received a description, or asked for a causal mechanism and received a list. The content was there; the required operation was not performed.

Correcting it is fast, because it is a reading habit rather than knowledge. The exercise is to take twenty real question stems from past papers across the student's subjects, identify the command term in each, say aloud what the answer must therefore contain, and only then write one. Two sessions of that changes how a student reads every paper they sit afterwards, in every subject, for the rest of the Diploma.

The table below covers the terms that cause the most trouble. It is worth noting what is not in it: terms whose meanings students usually get right, such as state and calculate. The problem is concentrated in the middle band, where the terms look like synonyms and are not.

sections.heading: The Internal Assessment, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an internally assessed component marked by the school against the IB's published criteria and then moderated. The criteria are lettered, each carries a stated maximum, and together they are a substantial share of the subject grade. A student who writes against the criteria is working with information. A student who writes a good piece of work and hopes it fits is gambling, and the moderation process is not generous to gamblers.

This is the single widest uncontested gap in this search market. Across the competitor pages researched for the UAE clusters, not one names a single assessment criterion by letter with its mark allocation. Parents are told Internal Assessment support is offered; nobody tells them what the work is marked on, which means families cannot distinguish a tutor who knows the component from one who has heard of it. Ask a prospective tutor to name the criteria for your child's subject. The answer settles it.

The sequence that works is counterintuitive to most students. Read the criteria first and translate each into a question the finished piece must answer. Then narrow the research question until the investigation is genuinely controllable with the equipment, the time and the sample available. Then collect. Only then write. Students who write first and map to the criteria afterwards produce work that reads well and lands mid-range, and no amount of editing afterwards recovers the structural marks.

The boundary needs stating because this market needs it stated. A tutor may explain the criteria, ask questions about the plan, point out where a conclusion exceeds the data, and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not write a section, rewrite prose, supply data or edit to completion. Nobody at IB Gram will. A site currently ranking on these searches advertises completed Internal Assessments for sale at a published price; that is an academic-honesty breach whose consequences fall on the student rather than on the seller.

sections.heading: Chemistry at Higher Level: the three places the grade is decided
paragraphs: Higher Level Chemistry rewards three things disproportionately, and a student who is solid in all three rarely has a grade problem. The first is calculation discipline. Mole arithmetic, concentration, yields and energetics all involve multi-step work where units and significant figures carry marks of their own. Students lose these marks while understanding the chemistry perfectly, which is maddening and entirely fixable.

The second is equilibrium and energetics as a conceptual pair. Questions here ask for reasoning about why a system responds as it does, which means the command term is almost always explain or predict rather than state. A student who has memorised the direction a system shifts without the reasoning will answer correctly and score partially, because the mark scheme pays for the mechanism.

The third is organic chemistry, which is best treated as pattern recognition rather than memorisation. Once a student can read a functional group and predict a reaction type with a reason, the subject becomes considerably smaller than it looks. Students who attempt to memorise reactions individually find the volume overwhelming and never reach the point where the patterns do the work for them.

The Internal Assessment in Chemistry has its own characteristic failure, and it is a planning one. An investigation with an uncontrolled variable - temperature drift, concentration prepared imprecisely, a timing method with large human error - caps the analysis and evaluation criteria however carefully the write-up is produced. The fix is an hour spent on the method before anything is measured, which is why Internal Assessment coaching belongs in the first Diploma year rather than in the second.

sections.heading: Physics, uncertainty, and the marks nobody mentions
paragraphs: Physics at Diploma level contains a technical skill that barely appears at IGCSE and carries marks in every part of the course: handling uncertainty. Propagating an uncertainty through a calculation, quoting a result to a defensible number of figures, drawing error bars, judging whether a gradient is consistent with a prediction. A student who cannot do these things loses marks in the written papers and in the Internal Assessment simultaneously.

That double exposure makes it unusually good value for tutoring. Six focused sessions on uncertainty and data handling will show up in two separate places in the grade, which is rarely true of a content topic. It is also a skill that can be taught cleanly, because it is procedural: there are rules, they are learnable, and practice on real data makes them automatic.

The content separators are different. Fields, circular motion and the Higher Level additional topics carry the heaviest losses, partly because they are conceptually demanding and partly because they are taught late and therefore revised least. A revision plan that starts at the beginning of the syllabus and works forwards will reach them exhausted. Starting with the Higher Level material and working backwards is usually the better sequence.

The third recurring loss is method description. A question asking how an experiment would be carried out is marked on precision: what is varied, what is controlled, what is measured and how, with enough detail that someone else could repeat it. Students write a summary and lose marks they would never lose in conversation, because they know the answer and do not know that the answer has to be specified.

sections.heading: Mathematics: the Exploration, and the paper skills it does not build
paragraphs: The mathematics Exploration is the subject's internally assessed component, and it is the piece of Diploma work most often misunderstood. It asks for the student's own mathematics on a topic of their choice, marked against lettered criteria. The characteristic failure is choosing an application and attaching mathematics to it rather than choosing mathematics and finding an application, which produces a readable document with insufficient mathematical content to score in the upper bands.

A second failure is scope. An Exploration that attempts a large question needs more mathematics than a student at this level can deploy properly, and the write-up thins out exactly where the criteria want depth. A narrow question explored thoroughly, with the student's own working visible and reflected upon, scores better than an ambitious one surveyed. Narrowing is therefore the first and most valuable conversation.

What the Exploration does not build is paper technique, and the two are easy to confuse because both say mathematics. Paper performance at Higher Level turns on algebraic speed, on showing method where method marks exist, and on answering in the form the question requested. A student can produce an excellent Exploration and still lose a grade on the papers, which is why a plan should treat them as two separate pieces of work with two separate blocks.

The route question sits underneath all of this. Analysis and Approaches is algebra-heavy and proof-oriented; Applications and Interpretation is statistics-led and technology-heavy. Both are rigorous and neither is the soft option. Where a student has arrived in the wrong one, the decision is far easier early in the first Diploma year than later, and a diagnostic block with a specialist is a cheap way to make it on evidence rather than on impression.

sections.heading: Past-paper work, done so that it actually teaches something
paragraphs: Most students do past papers and most past-paper practice is wasted. The waste has a consistent shape: the paper is done untimed, marked generously or not at all, and then put away without anything being extracted from it. The student feels diligent and learns nothing, which is the worst possible combination because it consumes the hours that could have produced improvement.

Done properly, past-paper work is the most informative activity in a revision plan. The conditions have to be real, including timing, because pacing is one of the most common losses and it is invisible in untimed practice. The marking has to be against the published scheme, because the point is to learn what the scheme pays for rather than what seems reasonable. And the output has to be a list: which questions lost marks, what the mark scheme wanted, and what that implies for the next session.

The second discipline is selection. Working chronologically through every available paper is a poor use of time, because the student spends most of it on questions they can already do. Better to select by topic and question type against the diagnosed weaknesses, do those under time, and only then sit complete papers in the final weeks when stamina and pacing become the targets.

The third is annotation that survives. A mark scheme comparison is only useful if the student can revisit it, which is one practical advantage of working on a shared screen: the annotated script, the scheme and the notes stay together and can be reopened in the next session. A paper marked on paper in someone's living room generally disappears into a folder, and with it the only record of what the session established.

process.title: Name the subject, the level and the component
process.description: Higher Level Chemistry, second term of the first Diploma year, Internal Assessment at planning stage is a brief that selects a specialist. Needs help with science selects nobody. The level and the live component together determine who is worth putting in front of your child.

process.title: Send one marked script, not a summary of it
process.description: The marked paper shows in minutes whether marks went to command terms, method omission, calculation discipline or genuine content gaps. Those four need different work, and the script is the only reliable way to tell them apart. It costs nothing to send.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the script on screen
process.description: One 45 to 60-minute one-to-one session over live video, no card details, no obligation. The test to apply is whether the tutor works from the evidence in front of them and whether they can name the criteria or the command terms without looking them up.

process.title: Agree a block with a measurable target
process.description: Six to eight sessions, a named target such as uncertainty handling or evaluation-band writing, and a stated way to check it. Open-ended weekly bookings cannot be judged, which is why they continue. Blocks with targets can be judged, repeated or stopped.

process.title: Measure on timed questions in the weak area
process.description: At the end of the block, the student sits timed questions in the diagnosed area and the result is compared against the start. If nothing has moved, the plan or the match was wrong and both are fixable. We would rather be told at week three than at week twelve.

whyPoints.description: Not one competitor page researched across these UAE clusters names a single assessment criterion by letter. We will tell you which criteria your child's Internal Assessment is marked against and where the marks usually go missing in that subject.

whyPoints.description: Explanation of criteria, questions about the plan, feedback on the student's own draft. No writing, no rewriting, no supplied data, no editing to completion.
